It is therefore your concern, dearest son in Christ, to persist firmly in the good purpose which you have begun, and diligently to work for those things which you know concern the honor and advantage of your holy mother, the Roman Church, and of ourselves. [Col. 0136B]

Given at Asti, on the Ides of April.

XCIX. He confirms the possessions and rights of the church of Saint Frigdianus of Lucca. (Year 1132, 16 April.) [Col. 0136C]

[*Bullarium Lateranense*, 10.]

C. To [Gualterius, archbishop of Ravenna], he makes these things known: “We have crossed the Alps; we celebrated the Resurrection of the Lord at Asti [Note: [Col. 0135D] 10 April.]; thence, at the request of the people of Novara, we proceeded to their city and consecrated their greater church.” He urges him to meet him at Pavia [Note: [Col. 0135D] This letter, wrongly attributed to Calixtus II, is without doubt to be referred to Innocent II, Jaffé.]. (Year 1132, 17 April.)

[Amadesi, *Chronotaxis of the Bishops of Ravenna*, III, 121.]

CI. He confirms the possessions and privileges of the church of Blessed Alexander of Bergamo. (Year 1132, 31 May.)

[Lupus, *Codex diplomaticus Bergomatis*, II, p. 963.]

[Col. 0136D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons PETER, provost, and the brethren serving the Lord in the church of Blessed Alexander of Bergamo, present and future, in perpetual remembrance.

The authority of our office exhorts us to take care of all churches and, with the Lord’s help, beneficially to provide for their peace and welfare. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, graciously admitting your petitions, we have judged that the church of Blessed Alexander, in which you devote yourselves to divine service, should be fortified by a privilege of the Apostolic See, following the example of our predecessor Pope Paschal, of faithful memory. We decree that whatever possessions or goods now belong to it lawfully and canonically, or may in the future be obtained, by God’s favor, through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, your own lawful acquisition, or other reasonable means, shall be preserved for you unimpaired and secure in perpetuity. Among these we have judged that the following should be expressly named: namely, the grant of tithes made to your church’s provost by Adelbert, bishop of Bergamo, of good memory, as is contained in the writings of that bishop and of the canons of the blessed martyrs Alexander and Vincent, so that those tithes may accrue perpetually to the use of the brethren; also the churches of Licina, Lemene, and Villa, while preserving in them the right and due reverence of the diocesan bishop. Furthermore, we also confirm by apostolic authority the good usages and reasonable customs confirmed for you by our predecessor Pope Honorius, of pious memory.

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb your church, take away its possessions or retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations. Rather, let all things be preserved intact for the benefit of your use. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing the text of this our constitution, attempts rashly to act against it, and after a second or third warning does not correct his offence by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the rank of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the final judgment let him be subject to strict punishment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen. [Cols. 0137A–C]

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Ubertus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement, have subscribed. I, Goselmus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia, have subscribed. I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Romanus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George, have subscribed. [Col. 0137D]

Given at Piacenza through the hand of Almeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Kalends of June, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1133 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Innocent II, pope.

CII. He receives the monastery of Saint Savior at Pavia under the protection of the holy Roman Church and confirms its goods. (Year 1132, 3 June.)

[Margarini, *Bullarium Casinense*, vol. II, p. 142.]

[Col. 0138A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ JOHN, abbot of the venerable monastery called that of the Lord Savior, situated near Pavia, and to his successors to be regularly appointed, for ever.

The care of the pastoral office has been entrusted to us by God for this purpose: that we should provide with particular concern for the peace and welfare of all churches, and fortify them by the authority of the Apostolic See lest they be harassed by the troubles caused by wicked persons. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord John, abbot, assenting to your reasonable requests, we receive under the guardianship of Blessed Peter and the protection of the Apostolic See the monastery of the Lord Savior, over which by God’s favor you preside, together with all that pertains to it, following the example of our predecessors of happy memory—John, Benedict, Paschal, and Calixtus, Roman pontiffs. That monastery, renewed by the Empress Augusta Adelaide and enriched by her generosity and donations, we fortify by the text of this our privilege. We decree that whatever goods; urban or rural estates, cultivated or uncultivated; possessions, furnishings, or ornaments which it now lawfully and legitimately possesses, having been bestowed on the monastery by the aforesaid Augusta or by other faithful persons from their own right, or which it may hereafter acquire by God’s favor through grants of pontiffs, generosity of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful titles, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors.

When you, the present abbot of that place, or any of your successors die, no one may be set over it by any craft of deceit or by force, except one whom the brethren, by common consent or by the judgment of the sounder part, in the fear of God and according to the Rule of Blessed Benedict, decide should be elected. The one elected, moreover, shall be consecrated by the Roman pontiff. You may receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and the ordinations of your monks or canons who are to be promoted to sacred orders, from whichever bishop you prefer, provided that he is Catholic and enjoys the favor of the Apostolic See. Moreover, we permit baptism to be celebrated in those churches belonging to the monastery in which it is established that it has been celebrated up to this time. We forbid any bishop, without the abbot’s consent, to celebrate public masses in the monastery itself or to hold stations or perform any ordinations there. We further grant you the tithes of the revenues of the aforesaid monastery, to be held without opposition from any bishop or his ministers.

No person whatsoever, therefore, may rashly disturb the above-named monastery, take away its possessions, retain things taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations. Rather, let all things be kept whole for the unrestricted benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted. Moreover, adding this clause to the present document, we decree that the aforesaid monastery shall remain under the jurisdiction or power of no person, but shall be free from every yoke and subject to the holy Roman and Apostolic See alone. We further enact that the use of the dalmatic, sandals, and gloves is granted to you and your successors according to the statutes of our predecessors. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing the text of this our constitution, attempts rashly to act against it, and after a second or third warning does not make amendment by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the rank of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and at the final judgment let him be subject to strict punishment. But upon all who preserve what is right for that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen. [Cols. 0138B–0139B]

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Ubertus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement, have subscribed. [Col. 0139C] I, Anselm, priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed. I, Cosmas, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia, have subscribed. I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Dominic, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed.

Given at Piacenza through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, [Col. 0139D] on the third day before the Nones of June, in the twentieth indiction, in the year 1133 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Innocent II, pope.

CIII. He receives the church of Novara under his protection and confirms the possessions of Bishop Litifred and his successors. (Year 1132, 25 June.)

[Ughelli, *Italia sacra*, IV, 704.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother LITIFRED, bishop of Novara, and to his successors canonically appointed, for ever.

Set by the Lord’s ordinance upon the eminent watchtower of the Apostolic See, we are obliged by the office entrusted to us to love our brother bishops and to preserve their proper rights to the churches entrusted to them by God. Therefore, dearest brother in Christ Litifred, bishop of the church of Novara, beneficially providing for the church whose care has been entrusted to you by God, we decree that whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and lawfully possesses shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have added the following to be expressly named: namely, the abbey of Saint Lawrence; the abbey of Saint Bartholomew in the suburb of Novara; the abbey of Saint Savior of Casale; the abbey of Saint Silanus of Romagnano; the chapel of Saint Nazarius; the chapel of All Saints and Saint Savior; the chapel of Saint Matthew; the chapel of Saint Andrew; and the chapel of Saint Stephen.

Outside the city: the parish church of Saint Albinus of Mortara with its parish and seven chapels—namely those of Saint Lawrence, Saint Julius, Saint Gaudentius, Saint Victor, Saint Quiricus, Saint Michael, and Saint Peter—in which the bishop of Novara is acknowledged to have episcopal right. In Campo Lato: the parish church of Saint Peter; the church of Saint Gaudentius; the church of Saint Majolus; the church of Alexander; the church of Berredo; and the chapel of Saint Nazarius. The parish church of Vigevano with its chapels; the parish church of Cassiolo; the church of Ceredano and that of Gravalona; the church of Camari; and the churches of Romentino and Galiate. The parish church of Oleggio with its chapels; the parish church of Dulciago with its chapels; the new and old church of Saint Julius; the parish church of Varallo with its chapels; the parish church of Gattico with its chapels; the parish church of Gaudiano with its chapels; the parish church of Saint Julius with its chapels; the parish church of Vemenia with its chapels; the parish church of Baveno with its chapels; the chapel of Saint Angel and Saint Remigius; the parish church of Intro with its chapels; the parish church of Mergotio with its chapels; and the parish church of Oxula with its appurtenances. All churches which are in the valley of Sicida. The parish church of Grinasco and the chapels of Romagnano; the parish church of Agamio with its appurtenances, and that of Seciano with its appurtenances; the parish church of Xuno with its chapels; the parish church of Quiregio; the parish church of Petroro, with its monastery and chapels; the parish church of Casale, its castle, and the village of that same Casale; the parish church of Arcamariano with its chapels; the church of Monticelli; and the parish church of Vespolate with its chapels.

Furthermore, whatever churches the church of Novara possesses within or outside the city, or may hereafter acquire by God’s favor through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, we decree shall remain secure and inviolate for you in perpetuity. We also forbid anyone, without the assent or free will of you or your successors, and with due reverence to the Apostolic See, to presume to found a church in the bishopric of Novara. [Cols. 0140A–D]

No person whatsoever, therefore, may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations. Rather, let all things be preserved in their entirety for the unrestricted benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing the text of this our constitution, attempts rashly to act against it, and after a second or third warning does not make amendment by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the rank of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and at the final judgment let him be subject to strict punishment. But upon all who preserve what is right for that church, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. [Col. 0141A]

[Col. 0141B] I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Ubertus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement, have subscribed. I, Anselm, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed. I, Jomelsus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia, have subscribed. I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Romanus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. [Col. 0141C] I, Stephen, cardinal deacon of Saint Lucy in Orpheus, have subscribed. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George, have subscribed.

Given at Piacenza through the hand of Alimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Kalends of July, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1133 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Innocent II, pope.

CIV. He confirms the goods of the canons of the church of Novara. (Year 1132, 25 June.)

[Ughelli, *ibid.*, p. 706.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons, the canons of the church of Novara, present and future, for ever. [Col. 0141D]

Placed, through the ordinance of divine clemency, upon the eminent watchtower of the Apostolic See, we ought to love honorable persons with paternal charity; and we wish diligently to provide lest they or their goods be harassed by the troubles of wicked persons. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, moved by the prayers of our venerable brother Litifred, your bishop, we have judged that your reasonable petitions should be granted. We decree that whatever possessions or goods you now possess lawfully and canonically, or may hereafter acquire by God’s favor through grants of pontiffs, gifts of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you in perpetuity. Among these we have added the following to be expressly named:

In the city of Novara, the church of Saint Ambrose; at Trecate, the churches of Saint Cassian, Saint Michael, and Saint Ambrose; at Veura, the church of Saint Gaudentius with all its tithes and one *mansus*; at Matheo, the church of Saint Martin with all its tithes and one *mansus*; at Insarno, the church of Saint Damian with all its tithes and one *mansus*; at Matheo, the church of Saint Martin with all its tithes and eight *mansi*, and the jurisdiction of the entire village; at Corte Nuova, the church of Saint Michael with all its tithes, six *mansi*, and the jurisdiction of the whole village; at Quartaria, the church of Saint Majolus with all its tithes, six *mansi*, and the jurisdiction of the whole village; at Quartaria, the church of Saint Majolus with all its tithes, lands, and jurisdiction of the entire village; at Baceno, the church of Saint Gaudentius with the possessions of the house of Tertiana; the tithe of Tredaci with ten *mansi*; the tithe of Romentino; the tithe of Galiate; the tithe of Cameri; the tithe of Pernate; the tithe of Berzini; the tithe of Camiliani and Aguniati; the tithe of Oblati; the tithe of Novasse with all lands belonging to that same estate; the tithe of Gondiana with the possessions which it holds in that village; the tithe of Granotio; the tithe of Monticelli and twenty *modii* of rent; the tithe of Guilengi with the possessions which you hold there; and the tithe of Sociaco and the *mansi* which you have there.

The castle of Nomenonio with the entire jurisdiction of the village, its tithes, and twenty *mansi*; the tithe of Paliate with twelve *mansi*; two *mansi* at Terdobiato; one *mansus* at Vespolate; one *mansus* at Nibbiola; two *mansi* at Garbagna; two *mansi* at Stodegarda; one *mansus* at Casulino, with fifteen *solidi* of rent in old Milanese money and fifteen *modii* of grain; two parts of the castle of Mositi with the chapel of Saint Stephen, its jurisdiction, toll, honor, and twelve *mansi*; one *mansus* at Gargarengo; one *mansus* at Landiola; one *mansus* and a mill at Silavengo; one *mansus* at Carpiniano with the jurisdiction of that *mansus*; one *mansus* at Agaimo; one *mansus* at Siciano, with male and female servants and a rent of six *solidi*; at Fara, one *mansus*; one fourth part of the jurisdiction of Cisti with three and a half *mansi*; at Caltiniaca, three *mansi* and one mill; at Dulciago, three *mansi* with the jurisdiction of those *mansi*; at Mommo, six *mansi* and a mill; at Albo, one *mansus* with its jurisdiction; at Pramoxello, one fishery; another fishery near the castle of the Lord; at Maxeria, a rent of forty denarii in old Milanese money; Canatum and Oglon, with their fisheries, olive-groves, and female servants.

To these we add the tithes and other possessions which you have in the city of Novara; and we likewise confirm for you the settlement of the dispute concerning the obedience and reverence owed by the clergy of Saint Gaudentius, and the services for the dead, which was being contested between them and the clergy of that church. It was rightly made by Richard, bishop of Novara, of good memory; confirmed by the aforesaid brother Litifred, your bishop; and strengthened by our predecessor Pope Honorius, of holy memory. We decree, therefore, that no person may harass you concerning those things which we have confirmed to your whole body by the text of this present writing, or inflict upon you any rash diminution. Rather, let all things be preserved entire for the benefit of your use. If any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing the text of this our constitution, attempts rashly to act against it and, after a second or third warning, does not make amendment by fitting satisfaction, let him be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer, and at the final judgment let him be subject to strict punishment. But upon all of you who preserve what is right, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal recompense. [Cols. 0142A–0143B]

Sealed and subscribed as follows:

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Ubertus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement, have subscribed. I, Anselm, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed. I, [lacuna], cardinal priest of Saint Cecilia, have subscribed. I, [lacuna]. I, Romanus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, [Col. 0143C] have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Stephen, cardinal deacon of Saint Lucy in Orfea, have subscribed. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed.

Given at Piacenza through the hand of Aymeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Kalends of July, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1133 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Innocent II, pope.

CV. To the canons of Saint Alexander of Bergamo, he grants certain churches belonging to the Apostolic See. (Year 1132, 28 June.)

[Lupus, *Codex diplomaticus Bergomatis*, II, 966.]

[Col. 0143D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons P[ETER], provost, and the canons of the church of Blessed Alexander of Bergamo: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Those who are shown to be more faithful and devoted sons of Blessed Peter ought to be loved by the Apostolic See and assisted more generously in their needs. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, taking account of the zeal of your devotion, we have entrusted to your charity the churches of the Holy Trinity, Saint Savior, Saint Michael in Virgis, and Saint Eusebius, which are known to belong especially to the right of Blessed Peter. [Col. 0144A] It is therefore your concern to persist in obedience to, and love for, the Apostolic See in such a way that you may deserve faithfully to retain its favor; and that the same churches may by no means deteriorate under your custody, but may, with the Lord’s help, be restored to a better condition.

Given at Piacenza, on the fourth day before the Kalends of July.

CVI. He confirms the church of Aquileia as metropolitan of sixteen bishoprics and grants Patriarch Peregrinus the use of the pallium, *rationale*, *naccus*, and cross. (Year 1132, 29 June.)

[Ughelli, *Italia sacra*, vol. V, col. 62.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother PEREGRINUS, patriarch of Aquileia, [Col. 0144B] and to his successors canonically appointed, for ever.

The adorned house of the Lord, clothed about with variety, has columns, some placed in the highest splendor, others situated in the middle, and others set in the lowest place. For the holy Roman Church, which received primacy from the Savior himself through Blessed Peter, established some of its servants as bishops, to preside over the clergy and exercise care of souls for the peoples; others as archbishops, to lay the hand of consecration upon bishops and, exercising metropolitan power by giving law, to hold councils; and others as primates, who were subject to the Roman pontiff alone and possessed primacy over archbishops and provinces.

Therefore, beloved brother in Christ, Peregrinus, patriarch of Aquileia, to you, and through you to the holy church of Aquileia, over which you are known, by God’s authority, to preside, we grant metropolitan authority over sixteen bishoprics: Pula, Trieste, Poreč, Petena, Emona, Concordia, Treviso, Ceneda, Belluno, Feltre, Padua, Vicenza, Trent, Mantua, Verona, and Como. We also judge should be confirmed for you and your successors the abbeys of Ossiach, Möchling [*Mosicensem*, uncertain], Rosazzo, Beligna, Sesto, Pirano, and Saint Mary at the Organ. We confirm for you and your successors the use of the pallium, the *rationale*, and the *naccus*, granted by our predecessors to your predecessors for the dignity of that church, on those days specified in the privileges of your church. Wherever you go, moreover, by the authority of Blessed Peter and of ourselves we grant you and your successors permission to have the cross borne before you. We likewise confirm, by the sanction of this present decree, the county, march, and duchy granted to your church by royal or imperial privileges. [Cols. 0144C–D]

We also decree that whatever possessions and goods the church of Aquileia now justly and lawfully possesses, or may hereafter acquire by God’s favor, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you, saving in all things the right and due reverence of the holy Roman Church. We decree, therefore, that no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations. Rather, let all things be preserved intact for the unrestricted benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing the text of this our constitution, attempts rashly to act against it and, after a second or third warning, does not make amendment by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the rank of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and at the final judgment let him be subject to strict punishment. But upon all who preserve what is right for that church, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen. [Cols. 0145A–B]

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Ubertus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement, have subscribed. I, Anselm, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed. I, Sozilinus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia, have subscribed. I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Romanus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary [Col. 0145C] in Portico, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Stephen, cardinal deacon of Saint Lucy in Orphea, have subscribed. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.

Issued at Piacenza through the hand of Aimeric, deacon cardinal of the holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the third day before the Kalends of July, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1132 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third year of the pontificate of Pope Innocent II.

S. N. I, Peter the notary, wrote this exactly as I saw it in the privilege, adding or omitting neither word nor syllable.

### CVII. To A[tto], prior of the church of St. Fridianus at Lucca.  
*(30 June 1132.)*

[Baluze, *Miscellanies*, IV, 589.]

[Col. 0145D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ A., prior of St. Fridianus: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Heavenly things must be preferred to lowly things, celestial to earthly, eternal to temporal, and immortal to mortal things. For the discerning providence of almighty God has established us not as shepherds of cattle, but has chosen us as guardians of souls. Therefore, lest the souls of the faithful perish altogether, if there are in your parish persons publicly guilty of crimes or incest, you are to approach the bishop of Lucca or the archpriest, so that he may impose penance upon them according to ecclesiastical discipline. But if, when invited by you on this matter a second or third time, they disdain to comply, by apostolic authority we grant you leave to impose penance upon them.

Given at Piacenza, on the second day before the Kalends of July.

### CVIII. He confirms all the goods and privileges of the monastery of St. Sixtus in the diocese of Piacenza.  
*(14 July 1132.)*

[Cocquelines, vol. II, p. 214.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to ODDO, abbot of the venerable monastery of St. Sixtus, situated at Piacenza, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

[Col. 0146B] The care of the universal Church has been entrusted to us by God, the provider of all good things, in order that we may cherish religious persons and strive by every means to promote religion pleasing to God. For no service is ever acceptably offered to God unless, proceeding from the root of charity, it is preserved in the purity of religion.

Moved, therefore, by this concern for charity, our predecessors of blessed memory, the Roman pontiffs Paschal and Calixtus, wishing to restore religion in the monastery of St. Sixtus at Piacenza, where it had for a long time already declined, established there men of the monastic order in place of women living there without religious discipline, at the prayers and counsel of wise and religious men, and especially of Countess Matilda of illustrious memory. And they placed you, beloved son in Christ, Oddo, over them as abbot by apostolic authority, to restore in that place the order of monastic discipline according to the Rule of St. Benedict.

[Col. 0146C] We therefore, following in the footsteps of those same predecessors of ours, confirm by the force of this present writing the provision or arrangement made by them and secured by privilege, and decree that it be observed inviolate in times to come. We revoke and annul the document which, while our predecessor Pope Calixtus of blessed memory was in the regions of Gaul, is known to have been fraudulently obtained by the nuns of that place.

We decree that the place itself and all things belonging to it shall be preserved under the guardianship and protection of the Apostolic See, free from the molestations of any assailants, as is known to have been established by our predecessors, the Roman pontiffs. We further decree that all estates or possessions which Empress Angelberga, foundress of that monastery, is known to have bestowed upon it, and likewise any other goods, villages, households, dependent cells, or churches which the same abbey now justly and lawfully possesses, or may hereafter acquire, God granting, by grants of pontiffs, gifts of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors.

[Col. 0146D] Among these we have appended the following, to be specified by their proper names: at Piacenza, in the hospice, the church of St. Peter; the church of St. Martin at Burte; the church of St. Brigid; the church of St. Andrew outside the Milan Gate; the church of St. Mary at the head of the Trebbia; the church of St. Peter; at Centoria, the church of St. Bartholomew; at Scopora, two chapels; at Castronovo, the church of St. Michael and the church of St. Bartholomew; at Wardastalla, the church of St. Peter, the church of St. George, the church of St. Martin, and the church of St. Bartholomew; at Luciaria, the church of St. George with its chapels; at Curte Nova, the church of St. Lawrence; and in Campo Miliario, the church of St. Peter.

[Col. 0147A] Therefore let no person whatsoever presume rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; rather, let all be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted.

Upon your death, now abbot of that place, or that of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it through any fraudulent device or violence, save one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall deem fit to elect from their own community, if a suitable person can be found, according to the fear of God and the Rule of St. Benedict. But if no such person is found in the same monastery for the administration of the abbacy, he shall be chosen from the monastery of Casa Dei, so long as the discipline of the monastic order shall, God granting, flourish there. The elected person, however, shall be blessed by the Roman pontiff.

[Col. 0147B] Whatever further liberty or dignity our predecessors granted to the aforementioned monastery through authoritative charters of privilege, we also grant by the authority of this present privilege, and decree that it be held valid for times to come. Moreover, since that monastery has been entrusted to you for good governance, its possessions and goods shall remain wholly in your power; likewise, the chaplains of its church shall be subject to you.

If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this charter of our decree, shall rashly act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make suitable satisfaction, let that person lose the dignity of rank and office; let that person know that he or she is liable before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let that person be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let that person be subject to strict vengeance at the final judgment.

[Col. 0147D] But upon all who preserve what is just for that place may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ rest, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.

Given at Cremona through the hand of Aymeric, deacon cardinal of the holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the second day before the Ides of July, in the tenth indiction [read: twelfth], in the year 1133 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II [read: fourth].

### CIX. He confirms all goods, rights, and privileges of St. Antoninus the martyr in the city of Piacenza.  
*(15 July 1132.)*

[Cocquelines, II, p. 215.]

[Col. 0148A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son AZO, provost of the church of St. Antoninus the martyr, situated in the city of Piacenza, and to his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

The authority of our office exhorts us to concern ourselves with the condition of churches and, with the Lord’s help, to provide beneficially for their peace and welfare. For it is recognized as worthy and fitting to integrity that we who have been raised to the governance of churches should take care to defend them from the malice of wicked people.

[Col. 0148B] Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Provost Azo, granting assent to your just petitions, we fortify by the privilege of the Apostolic See the church of Blessed Antoninus the martyr, over which, by God’s authority, you preside. We decree that whatever estates, possessions, or goods, whether in churches or in other property, have been granted to that church by the bishops of the church of Piacenza or by other faithful people of God, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors.

Among these we have thought proper to specify by name: namely, the church of Blessed Mary at Curtina, situated near the church of the martyrs Saints Antoninus and Victor, together with the rights and customs which you appear now justly to possess in that church: that is, on all feasts of Mary you shall have one-third of the candles, and there you shall appoint priests and clerics in accordance with God’s will. You, however, the canons in your church, out of reverence for Blessed Antoninus the martyr, with whose most sacred body that place was formerly adorned, shall visit the said chapel every year on the Purification of Blessed Mary.

[Col. 0148C] In the territory of Plectula, the church of St. Antoninus the martyr, with its whole share, endowment, and offerings of the entire year, as it is known to have been granted to you in exchange by Dionysius, bishop of Piacenza of good memory, for the church of St. Syrus. In that church you shall have free power to appoint ministers according to God’s will.

At Gragnano, the chapel of St. Michael, with its entire endowment and the offerings of the whole year, granted to your church by our venerable brother Arduino, bishop of Piacenza, on these terms: that you shall have free power to appoint and remove clerics in that chapel, and to present them in due course to the bishop of Piacenza for promotion to sacred orders. The priest of that place, however, shall receive chrism and holy oil from the parish church of Tunense; when summoned to litanies and baptism there, he shall go without any opposition, while the right and reverence due to your church in all other matters remain preserved.

[Col. 0149A] Further, we decree that all other liberties and reasonable customs granted to your church by the bishops of Piacenza shall remain peacefully and unimpaired to you in future times. If you or your clerics perceive that you are being burdened, you may freely appeal to the Apostolic See, which is accustomed to aid the oppressed.

We decree that the goods and possessions which you may hereafter acquire, with God’s help, by grants of pontiffs, gifts of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and intact to you, without prejudice, of course, to the right and reverence due to the diocesan bishop.

Therefore let no person whatsoever presume rashly to disturb the aforementioned church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; rather, let all be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted.

[Col. 0149B] If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this charter of our decree, shall rashly act against it, and, after a second or third warning, does not make appropriate satisfaction, let that person lose the dignity of rank and office; let that person know that he or she is liable before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let that person be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let that person be subject to strict vengeance at the final judgment.

But upon all who preserve what is just for that church may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ rest, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.  
I, William, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed.  
I, Anselm, priest cardinal of the title of St. Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed.  
I, John, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed.  
I, Peter, bishop of Pavia, have subscribed.  
I, Joselmus, priest cardinal of the title of St. Cecilia, have subscribed.  
I, Lucas, priest cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed.  
[Col. 0149D] I, Romanus, deacon cardinal of the title of St. Mary in Portico, have subscribed.  
I, Otto, deacon cardinal of St. George, have subscribed.  
I, Guido, deacon cardinal of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed.

Given at Cremona through the hand of Aimeric, deacon cardinal of the holy Roman Church and likewise chancellor, on the Ides of July, in the tenth indiction [read: eleventh], in the year 1133 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Pope Innocent II.

### CX. He informs Henry, king of the English, that he has instructed Archbishop Hugh of Rouen to comply with his will concerning certain abbots; but he urges him not to permit abbots to be acephalous. He commends Archbishop Hugh.  
*(15 July 1132.)*

[Mansi, *Councils*, XXI, 424.]

[Col. 0150A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his dearest son in Christ HENRY, illustrious and glorious king of the English: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Just as we love your person with sincere charity, so we are ready, insofar as we can rightly do so before God, to take pains in matters which we recognize to concern your honor.

[Col. 0150B] We have instructed and advised our venerable brother Hugh, archbishop of Rouen, by our letters, that he should comply with your will concerning those abbots of whom Your Serenity has informed us. Yet the more highly the providence of divine mercy has adorned your person with honor, wisdom, and wealth, the more it has made you accountable to itself and bound you more closely to its service.

It is therefore expedient that, in the kingdom or duchy entrusted to you by divine ordinance, wrongful customs be cut away in your time; and, the roots of vices having been cut off, every good thing be planted through the zeal of your nobility, with the Lord cooperating. Otherwise, abbots and other clerics will be unable either to render acceptable service to God or to provide for the salvation of their souls; indeed, they will be considered *acephali*, that is, “without a head,” unless they are subject with due humility to their bishops and prelates [lacuna].

[Col. 0150C] Your prudence must therefore take care that, living wholly freely and without a yoke, they do not become inflated with pride, incur the ruin of their souls, and cause this—God forbid!—to be imputed to you before the presence of the heavenly Judge.

It belongs also to your excellence and prudence to love and honor the aforesaid brother of ours, Archbishop Hugh—a man indeed so eminent and prudent, in whose religious devotion and wisdom the holy Church of God rejoices—and not permit him to be troubled by any molestations.

Given at Cremona, on the Ides of July.

### CXI. To Hugh, Archbishop of Rouen—he exhorts him to yield something of ecclesiastical right to the king.  
*(July 1132.)*

[Mansi, *Councils*, XXI, 426.]

[Col. 0150D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his dearest brother HUGH, archbishop of Rouen: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Your brotherhood, as we believe, does not fail to know how concessions ought to be made to kings and princes of lands, through whose power and justice the Church of God and the Christian people are protected. But our dearest son Henry, king of the English, as we have learned, has become greatly angered with you because, contrary to his custom and that of the other dukes of Normandy, you have received profession and obedience from certain abbots.

[Col. 0151A] Although this was indeed just, and commanded to us in the Council of Reims, nevertheless, for love of him we ought at times to relax the strictness of justice and, for the present, comply with his will. For we believe, as has been communicated to our ears, and as we have instructed him by our letters, that if you yield to him in what concerns the honor and right of the church of Rouen, you will henceforth obtain the fullness of his favor.

We therefore request and command your brotherhood to comply with his will concerning those abbots, and, if you have bound any of the abbots, to absolve him.

### CXII. Privilege for the monastery of Tilieto.  
*(26 July 1132.)*

[Moriondi, *Monumenta Aquensia*, vol. I, col. 48.]

[Col. 0151B]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son OPIZZO, abbot of the monastery of Blessed Mary the Virgin and of the Holy Cross at Civitacula, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

The care of the universal Church has been entrusted to us by God, provider of all good things, in order that we may cherish religious persons and strive by every means to promote religion pleasing to God. For no service is more gratefully rendered to God unless, proceeding from the root of charity, it has been preserved from the corruption of religion.

[Col. 0151C] Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Opizzo, moved by the prayers of our venerable brother Azo, bishop of Acqui, and of his brother, the illustrious man Anselm, marquis, we graciously grant his just petitions. We fortify with the protection of the Apostolic See the monastery of Blessed Mary, Mother of the Lord, and of the Holy Cross—founded, as is known, in the diocese of Acqui by that same marquis, his mother, and also his brothers, sons, and wives—which you govern by God’s authority.

First, we decree that the monastic order according to the Rule of Blessed Benedict and the religious form of the brethren of the Cistercian monastery shall remain there inviolate in times to come. The goods and possessions which are known now justly and canonically to belong to that place, or which it may hereafter acquire, through God’s providence, by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to it and to its successors—namely, whatever is known to have been bestowed upon the monastery in the place called Boschus, or elsewhere, by the aforesaid marquis or by other faithful people of God.

[Col. 0151D] We further decree that neither the marquises nor anyone from the regions adjacent to that place, on the pretext of peace or war, or of the royal *fodrum* [provisioning levy], shall presume to oppress or trouble the monks or lay brothers dwelling there in their persons or goods, demand anything from them, or inflict any violence upon them. We establish the same thing by apostolic authority concerning the vineyards near the castle of Varaggio.

No one shall dare to demand or receive from you tithes from the produce which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, nor from your animals. We forbid any bishop, abbot, or other person to presume to receive or retain your monks or lay brothers without your free permission after they have made profession in your monastery. Rather, as violators of their profession, they shall be compelled to return to that place.

[Col. 0152A] We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; rather, let all be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, without prejudice, of course, to the right and due reverence of the bishop of Acqui.

If any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this charter of our decree, shall rashly act against it, and, when warned a second or third time, does not make suitable satisfaction, let that person lose the dignity of rank and office; let that person know that he or she is liable before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let that person be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let that person be subject to strict vengeance at the final judgment.

[Col. 0152B] But upon all who preserve what is just for that place may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ rest, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

[Col. 0152C] I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church.  
I, William, bishop of Palestrina.  
I, Ubertus, priest cardinal of the title of St. Lawrence in Lucina.  
I, Lucas, priest cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul.  
I, Romanus, deacon cardinal of St. Mary in Portico.  
I, Gregory, deacon cardinal of Saints Sergius and Bacchus.  
I, W., deacon cardinal of St. Mary in Via Lata.  
I, Otto, deacon cardinal of St. George at the Golden Veil.  
I, Guido, deacon cardinal of Saints Cosmas and Damian.

[Col. 0152D] Given at Brescia through the hand of Aymeric, deacon cardinal of the holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the seventh day before the Kalends of August, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1132 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CXIII. He takes the monastery of Leno under protection and confirms its privileges and possessions.  
*(26 July 1132.)*

[Zaccaria, *On the Abbey of Leno*, p. 114.]

### CXIV. Privilege for the canons of the church of St. Mary at Piacenza.  
*(29 July 1132.)*

[Cocquelines, vol. II, p. 216.]

[Col. 0153A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons in Christ JOHN, provost, and the canons of Blessed Mary, the mother church of Piacenza, both present and future, in perpetuity.

The authority of our office exhorts us to concern ourselves with the condition of churches and, with the Lord’s help, to provide beneficially for their peace and welfare. For it is recognized as worthy and fitting to integrity that we who have been raised to the governance of churches should defend them from the malice of wicked people and fortify them with the patronage of Blessed Peter and the Apostolic See.

[Col. 0153B] Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously grant your reasonable petitions and strengthen by the charter of this present privilege the church of Blessed Mary at Piacenza, in which you devote yourselves to divine service. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same church now justly and lawfully possesses, or may hereafter acquire, God granting, through grants of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors.

Among these we have appended the following to be noted by their proper names: namely, the parish church of Carmiano with its chapels; the parish church of Septima with its chapels; the parish church of Pomaria with its chapels; the parish church of Verdeto with its chapels; the parish church of Montisalto with its chapels; the parish church of Cassiano with its chapels; the parish church of Viculi with its chapels; and the parish church of St. George with five chapels—two at Paderna, one in Judaea, another at Castroziano, and another at Glariola.

[Col. 0153C] Also the chapels in the city: namely, St. Euphemia, St. Gervasius, St. Protasius, St. Peter of the Forum, St. Julian, St. Martin of the Forum, St. Dominic, St. Alexander, St. Martin of the Borough, St. Vincent, St. Stephen, Saints John and Paul, St. Zeno, St. Faustinus, St. Michael, St. Agatha, and St. Mary of Sperone. The priests of all these are customarily bound to baptize and catechize in your greater church on Holy Saturday.

We likewise confirm to you the tithes of the entire city and of the aforesaid parish churches, except the tithe rights of the parish church of Verdeto; further, the castle of Monte Regio, the castle of Cassino, half the castle of Gosolengo, half the castle of Viculi, and the castle of Carmiano.

[Col. 0153D] Moreover, by this present decree we establish that no bishop may impose upon your church, its persons, or its goods any exaction contrary to ancient custom and liberty.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforementioned church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with reckless vexations; rather, let all be preserved in their integrity for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted.

[Col. 0154A] If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this charter of our decree, shall rashly act against it, and, when warned a second or third time, does not make suitable satisfaction, let that person lose the dignity of rank and office; let that person know that he or she is liable before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let that person be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let that person be subject to strict vengeance at the final judgment.

But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ rest, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, may find the rewards of eternal peace. [Col. 0154B] Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.  
I, William, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed.  
I, Ubertus, priest cardinal of the title of St. Clement, have subscribed.  
I, Anselm, priest cardinal of the title of St. Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed.  
I, Lucas, priest cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed.  
I, Romanus, deacon cardinal of the title of St. Mary in Portico, have subscribed.  
I, Gregory, deacon cardinal of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed.  
[Col. 0154C] I, Guido, deacon cardinal of St. Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed.  
I, Otto, deacon cardinal of St. George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.  
I, Guido, deacon cardinal of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed.

Given at Brescia through the hand of Aymeric, deacon cardinal of the holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the fourth day before the Kalends of August, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1133 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CXV. Privilege for the monastery of Saints Faustinus and Jovita in the diocese of Brescia, of the Cassinese order.  
*(10 August 1132.)*

[Cocquelines, vol. II, p. 217.]

[Col. 0154D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son ALBERT, abbot of the monastery of Saints Faustinus and Jovita, situated in the suburb of Brescia, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

The care of the universal Church has been entrusted to us by God, provider of all good things, so that we may cherish religious persons and, providing beneficially for their peace and welfare with the Lord’s help, support with the protection of the Apostolic See the churches in which they serve. The monastery of the blessed martyrs Faustinus and Jovita, founded by our brother of good memory Rambert, formerly bishop of Brescia, and enriched with his goods and possessions, is rightly held in the highest honor and reverence among both ecclesiastical and secular persons because of the bodily presence of those martyrs.

[Col. 0155A] Hence our predecessors of blessed memory, the Roman pontiffs Stephen and Calixtus, loved that place in a special manner and confirmed it by their apostolic writings. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Albert, granting assent to your reasonable petitions, we fortify by the privilege of the Apostolic See the aforesaid monastery of the holy martyrs Faustinus and Jovita, over which, by God’s authority, you are known to preside. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and lawfully possesses, or may hereafter acquire, God granting, by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors.

[Col. 0155B] Among these we append the following to be specified by their proper names: the Church of All Saints, built in the castle of the aforesaid city; the church of St. Mary at Vergnano with its appurtenances; at Curticella, the church of St. Michael and that of St. Zeno, together with everything belonging to your monastery at Flumicello; the church of St. Mary at Mezzane; the church of St. Stephen, together with everything which you justly possess at Sale; the hospice of Denno with the property belonging to it; whatever the same monastery justly possesses in its vicinity, together with the hospice and the things belonging to it; the *braida* called St. Faustinus’s, with its mills and other buildings erected there, and the chapel of St. Dominic; the *braida* called Campus-Malxus; the castle of Turbola with the church of St. Andrew within the castle and, outside it, two other churches, namely those of St. Martin and St. Cassian; the estate of Buenni with its castle and chapel of St. Faustinus; half the castle of Vulpini, with the church of St. Stephen within the castle and the church of St. Gervasius outside it.

[Col. 0155C] At Cimmo, the church of St. Faustinus and whatever else you appear peacefully to hold there; the rent or *fictum* which every inhabitant of Asula, collectively and individually, has granted to be paid to your monastery; and whatever is known to belong to your monastery, in the present tenth indiction, at Calcinado, Curticelle, Yse, Pisonge, Batisino, the place of St. Vigilius, Monticello, Provenze, Gussago, Rivatica, Carpenedo, Remedello, and Ponte Carolo.

We also confirm for you by apostolic authority what was granted and confirmed in writing by our aforesaid brother Bishop Rambert for the use of the brethren of that monastery: namely, that you shall have power and permission to take wood from Mount Denno in such quantity as suffices for your needs. We also confirm to you the tithes of your possessions which up to this time you appear to have possessed justly and peacefully, to hold and possess.

[Col. 0156A] Therefore let no person whatsoever presume to disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; rather, let all be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the annual payment of one pound of silver to the church of Brescia.

Upon your death, now abbot of that place, or that of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it through any fraudulent device or violence, except one whom the brethren, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall deem fit to elect according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict.

[Col. 0156B] If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this charter of our decree, shall rashly act against it, and, when warned a second or third time, does not make suitable satisfaction, let that person lose the dignity of rank and office; let that person know that he or she is liable before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let that person be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let that person be subject to strict vengeance at the final judgment.

But upon all who preserve what is just for that place may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ rest, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.  
I, Rodulphus, bishop of Orte, have subscribed.  
I, Ubertus, priest cardinal of the title of St. Clement, have subscribed.  
[Col. 0156C] I, Anselm, priest cardinal of the title of St. Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed.  
I, Lucas, priest cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed.  
I, Gregory, deacon cardinal of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed.  
I, Guido, deacon cardinal of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed.

Given at Brescia through the hand of Aymeric, deacon cardinal of the holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the fourth day before the Ides of August, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1133 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CXVI. Privilege for the nunnery of St. Julia, in the diocese of Brescia, of the Cassinese order.  
*(30 August 1132.)*

[Cocquelines, II, p. 218.]

[Col. 0156D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughter in Christ CONSTANTIA, abbess of the monastery of our Lord and Savior and of St. Julia, virgin and martyr, which is called “New” and was founded in the city of Brescia, and to her sisters, both present and future, in perpetuity.

By authority of the Apostolic See, in which, by the Lord’s disposition, we have been established, we are bound to all Churches—and especially to those known to belong to the right and lordship of blessed Peter—to defend them from the attacks of wicked men and to cherish them beneath the pious bosom of the holy Roman Church. Therefore, dearest daughter in Christ, Constance, abbess, granting with due kindness our assent to your reasonable petitions, we strengthen by the privilege of the Apostolic See the monastery of blessed Julia, virgin and martyr, committed, by the Lord’s grant, to your care, which is known to have been built within the city of Brescia by Queen Ansa of noble memory.

We decree that whatever estates, possessions, or goods the same monastery now justly and lawfully possesses through the generosity of the aforesaid queen, or through the grants of emperors of illustrious memory who assumed the government of the realm after her, or through gifts bestowed by other faithful persons; and whatever it may hereafter obtain, by God’s favor, through the concession of pontiffs, the liberality of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you, your sisters, and those who succeed you in the same religious life. We append the following, to be recorded by their proper names:

Namely, Sirmione, with its two churches, those of our Lord the Savior and of Saint Vitus the martyr; Cervanica, with the church of Saint Julia the martyr; Nubelaria, with the church of Saint Lawrence; Berciago, with the two churches of Saint Zeno and Saint Stephen; the village of Maghone, with the church of Saint Alexander; Timolina, with the church of Saint Julia; Barbada, with the church of Saint Mary; Alfiano, with the church of Saint Julia; Monticello, with the church of Saint Mary; Voce, with the churches of Saint Peter and Saint Lawrence; Calvatone, with the churches of Saint Mary and Saint Julia; Scandolaria, with the church of Saint Michael; Ciconiaria, with the church of Saint Mary; Gosenago, with the church of Saint Martin the Confessor; Miliarina, with the church of Saint Julia; and Sermida.

Moreover, we likewise confirm to you whatever other courts, villages, castles, churches, and all things belong to the same monastery. By this present decree we also ordain that the aforesaid monastery, fortified by the protection of the Apostolic See and royal defense, shall never be subjected to the authority or jurisdiction of any other person, so that no priest may presume to celebrate there the solemnities of Mass unless invited by the abbess of that place.

Therefore let no person whatsoever presume rashly to disturb the aforesaid convent, remove its possessions, retain things removed, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; rather, let all things be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted. Upon the death of you, the abbess of that place, or of any woman who succeeds you in the same governance, no one shall be placed over it by any craft of deceit or violence, except the woman whom the sisters by common consent, or the sounder part of the sisters’ counsel, shall deem to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict.

We grant the abbess of the same place permission to build churches in honor of God and, wherever she wishes upon the lands of the aforesaid monastery, to establish a market and castles for the benefit of that monastery. Nor may any bishop, duke, margrave, count, viscount, or person great or small presume to exercise jurisdiction or render judgment in any place belonging to the monastery, or hold any plea without the abbess’s permission; nor may they alienate its spiritual or temporal property in any way, inflict injury upon it, or dare to exact fodrum, lodging-duty, river-toll, provisions, or any other public services.

Moreover, we confirm to you the tithes of the produce of your labor which you cultivate at your own expense, and jurisdiction over the servants and free persons belonging to your convent. You may receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and the ordination of the abbess, nuns, or your clerics who are to be advanced to holy orders, or anything belonging to the sacred mystery, from whichever Catholic bishops you prefer, provided that they grant these things to you freely and without any perversity or reproach; as is known to have been granted to your monastery, in consideration of the frailty of the female sex, by our predecessors of blessed memory, Paul and Calixtus, Roman pontiffs.

If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this charter of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and after a second or third admonition does not make suitable amends, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honor, know himself or herself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of this place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.  
I, William, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed.  
I, Ubert, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement, have subscribed.  
[Col. 0158D] I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed.  
I, Romanus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed.  
I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed.  
I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed.  
I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed.  
I, Oddo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.

Given at Brescia through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Kalends of September, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1133 of the Incarnation of the Lord, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of Pope Innocent II. [Col. 0159A]

### CXVII. Privilege for the Church of Saint Peter of Guastalla. (A.D. 1132, September 7.)

[AFFO, *History of Guastalla*, I, 333.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons JOHN, archpriest, and the brethren of the Church of Saint Peter situated in the district of Guastalla, present and future, forever.

The equity of justice and reason teaches that one who desires his own commands to be observed by his successors should preserve the enactments established by the will of his predecessor. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, assenting to your just wishes, we receive under the guardianship and protection of the Apostolic See and our own protection your Church, which was elevated to the status of a parish church of Capella by our predecessor Pope Gregory V of blessed memory, and fortified by the protection of the privilege of his successor Pope Paschal of holy memory; and we commend it to the patronage of Saint Peter.

We decree that whatever possessions, tithes, or goods this Church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter obtain by God’s favor through grants of pontiffs, the liberality of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you. We grant you full liberty to receive chrism and holy oil, the ordination of clerics, and consecrations of churches from whatever Catholic bishop you wish. Furthermore, we decree that no one may presume to build a church within the bounds of your parish, unless it is to be subject to you, without your permission; while in all things preserving the authority of the Apostolic See and the venerable dignity of the above-mentioned parish church.

We also decree that the chapels of Saint Bartholomew, Saint George, and Saint Martin, belonging by right to your church and confirmed to you by our aforesaid predecessors, shall remain forever subject to you. Therefore, no archbishop, bishop, abbot, duke, margrave, count, captain, judge, gastald, nor indeed any person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid Church, remove its possessions, retain things removed, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations. Rather, let all things be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted.

If therefore any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this charter of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and after a second or third admonition does not make suitable amends, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honor, know himself or herself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve what is right for this place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. [Col. 0160A]

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.  
I, William, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed.  
I, Romanus, cardinal of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed.  
I, Ubert, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement, have subscribed.  
I, Oddo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.

Given at Saint Benedict’s through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Ides of September, in the tenth indiction, in the third year of the pontificate of Pope Innocent II, in the year 1133 of the Incarnation of the Lord.

### CXVIII. He confirms to the Church of Saint Frigdianus of Lucca the Church of Saint Savior, granted by Landulf, bishop of Ferrara. (A.D. 1132, October 5.)

[*Lateran Bullarium*, 11.]

[Col. 0160B]

### CXIX. He decrees that the monks of the monastery of Saint George Major, received under the protection of the Apostolic See, shall henceforth elect as abbot whomever they judge suitable. (A.D. 1132, October 7.)

[CORNELIUS, *Churches of Venice*, vol. VIII, p. 218.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son TRIBUNE, abbot of the monastery of Saint George situated in the Venetian region, and to his successors regularly appointed, forever.

The authority of our office exhorts us to labor for the condition of the Churches in our charge and, with the Lord’s help, to provide wisely for their peace and advantage. For it is recognized to be fitting, honorable, and proper that we, who have been assumed to govern the Churches, should protect them from the wickedness of evil men and defend or fortify them by the patronage of the Apostolic See.

Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Tribune, we have considered it right to assent with due kindness to your reasonable requests, and we strengthen by the privilege of the holy Roman Church the monastery of blessed George, over which, by God’s grace, you are known to preside. By the charter of this present writing, we decree by apostolic authority that this place shall be preserved forever free under the guardianship and protection of blessed Peter. Neither patriarch, bishop, nor ecclesiastical or secular person may presume to compel you or your unwilling successors to attend a council; to absolve or receive persons excommunicated, expelled, or fugitive against you or your monks; or, without the consent of you and your successors, to promote anyone to orders.

Moreover, whatever possessions or goods the same monastery now justly and lawfully possesses anywhere, or may hereafter acquire by the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and the ordination of monks who are to be promoted to holy orders from the diocesan bishop, provided that he enjoys the favor and communion of the Apostolic See and is willing to provide these things freely and without improper exaction. Otherwise, for receiving these same sacraments, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you choose; strengthened by the authority of the Apostolic See, he shall grant what is requested.

Upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed over it by any craft of deceit or violence except the person whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of their counsel, elect according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict. We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforementioned convent, remove its possessions, retain things removed, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; rather, let all things be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted.

As acknowledgment of this liberty received from the Roman Church, you shall annually pay two gold coins to the Lateran palace. If any patriarch, archbishop, bishop, ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing this charter of our constitution, rashly attempts to act against it, and after a second or third admonition does not make suitable amends, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honor, know himself or herself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be excluded from the most holy body and blood of God and our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of this place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.  
I, Walter, archbishop of Ravenna, have subscribed.  
I, William, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed.  
I, Romanus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed.  
I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed.  
I, Oddo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.

Given at Nonantola through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the Nones of October, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1133 of the Incarnation of the Lord, and in the third year of the pontificate of Pope Innocent II. [Col. 0161D]

### CXX. He confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of Nonantola. (A.D. 1132, October 12.)

[MURATORI, *Italian Antiquities*, vol. V, p. 429.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ ILDEPRAND, abbot of the monastery of Nonantola, and to his successors living there according to the Rule, forever: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Although by the authority and benevolence of the Apostolic See we are bound to all Churches and ecclesiastical persons, it is especially fitting that we provide more earnestly for those Churches which, being especially attached to blessed Peter and the holy Roman Church, we ought to love with closer charity by defending them from the attacks of wicked men. For it is fitting and honorably proper that we who have been assumed to govern the Churches should, with the Lord’s help, make prudent provision for their peace and advantage.

Accordingly, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Ildeprand, we have deemed it right to assent with due kindness to your reasonable petitions, and, following the example of our predecessors of blessed memory—Leo, Alexander, Paschal, and Calixtus, Roman pontiffs—we strengthen by the privilege of the Apostolic See the monastery of blessed Sylvester at Nonantola, over which, by God’s grace, you are known to preside, and which was offered to blessed Peter by Astulf, king of the Lombards and founder of the place.

We decree that whatever estates, possessions, or goods the same monastery now justly and lawfully possesses shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. We append the following, to be recorded by their proper names: the castle of Nonantola itself; the Old Castle; Galianum; Cathinianum; Fananum; Lixanum; Sclopinum; Samonum; Campilium; Maranum; Pratum Albinum; the monastery of Saint Lucy, with its churches and appurtenances; the church of the Most Holy Trinity of Savino; Manzolino; Ravali; Rastellino; Saint Mary of Grumolo; Spinalberti; Solaria; Roncalia; Camorana; Curtile Siccum; the castle of Pollacci; Trecentula; Bondeno; Nogaria; the castle of Cella; and Marzalia with their appurtenances.

Furthermore, we confirm in perpetuity to your monastery the castle of Cellula, the court of Ragusa, and the castle of Theobald, with all the freehold estates which Margrave Boniface acquired and possessed in that county of Ferrara—property which Countess Matilda is known recently to have given you out of the offering which she had made to Saint Peter and the Roman Church—subject, namely, to an annual payment of one gold coin. We also confirm: in the city of Pavia, the church of Saint Quiricus; in Piacenza, the church of Saint Sylvester; in Monticello, the church of Saint George; in Cremona, the church of Saint Sylvester, the church of the Holy Cross, and the church of Saint Benedict; in the territory of Parma, the church of Saint Sylvester; in the suburb of Vicenza, the church of Saint Sylvester; in Libertino, the church of Saint Sylvester; at Monselice, the church of Saint Daniel with all belonging to it; and in the city of Treviso, the church of Saint Mary and Saint Fusca, with its liberty, chapels, and all that belongs to it.

Nor may the bishop of Modena, any bishop, prince, or ecclesiastical or secular person whatsoever inflict any burden on the aforesaid monastery, its dependent cells or churches, or its other possessions; impose exactions; or summon or hold a judicial hearing or conference contrary to the will of the abbot and brethren. Upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed over it by any craft of deceit or violence, except the person whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, foresee as to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict; that person shall come to be consecrated by the head of the Apostolic See.

You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and ordinations of monks who are to be advanced to holy orders, as well as of clerics belonging to the monastery, its cells, or churches, from whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, provided that he enjoys the favor and communion of the Apostolic See and is willing to provide these things freely and without improper exaction. For we permit no bishop, against the abbot’s will, to perform ordinations in the monastery or its cells or churches; celebrate public Masses; claim their tithes; procure by deception a rescript concerning the monastery or its property; or obtain such a rescript by any means for any person.
