But because your sentence seems far too lenient, we add this decree: in whatsoever places the aforesaid bloodthirsty men are present, no divine offices are to be celebrated there; and if anyone, remaining in the world, should attempt to support or shelter those sacrilegious killers of clerics, disturbers of the heavenly college, and shedders of the Lord’s blood, let him be struck by the sentence of anathema. [Col. 0215A]

In addition we decree that, because, through the impious wickedness and dreadful frenzy of their parents, clerics ought neither to acquire nor retain ecclesiastical benefice—for such things must be acquired, and once acquired retained, not by price, violence, terror, or the savage wickedness of blood-relations, but only through merit—both Theobald Noterius and others who have acquired or retained benefices by this most evil method, without prejudice, indeed, to the reverence due to the apostolic see, shall be deprived of ecclesiastical benefices. And because iniquity abounds, every care must be taken that clerics hereafter fear no human being; and, so that in welcome tranquillity they may be able to devote themselves to divine service, we extend to them apostolic assistance more generously.

## CLXV. He confirms the possessions and rights of the Church of Mortara, consecrated by himself. (Year 1134.)

[*Bullarium Lateranense*, 12.]

[Col. 0215B]

## CLXVI. He receives the monastery of Huysburg under his protection. (Year 1135, 8 January.)

[*Neue Mittheilungen aus dem Gebiete historisch-antiquarischer Forschungen*, IV, I, 9.]

## CLXVII. He confirms the possessions and privileges of the abbey of St Peter of the Golden Valley. (Year 1135, 8 January.)

[*Gallia Christiana vetus*, vol. IV, p. 114.]

[Col. 0215C] Innocent, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son GEOFFREY, abbot of St Peter of the Golden Valley, and to the brothers professing the canonical life in the same church, both present and future, in perpetuity.

Whenever a request is made of us which is known to accord with reason and propriety, it is fitting that we grant it willingly and offer fitting support to the desires of petitioners, so that faithful and devout devotion may obtain a prompt result. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, through the intervention of our venerable brother William, bishop of Poitiers, a wise and honourable man, proved in Catholic life, we gladly admit your petitions. Following the example of our predecessor of blessed memory, Pope Paschal, we have judged that the church of blessed Peter, in which you devote yourselves to divine office, should be fortified by the protection of the apostolic see.

First, indeed, we decree that the canonical order known to have been instituted in the same place shall be preserved there perpetually and inviolate according to the Rule of St Augustine. We forbid anyone, after having made profession, to possess anything as private property or to leave the cloister without the permission of the provost or congregation. We place both you and all that belongs to you under the protection of the apostolic see. We therefore decree that you and your successors who remain in the same religious profession shall possess in perpetuity all that you are at present known lawfully to possess: namely, in the district of Poitou, the churches of St Paul of [Col. 0216A] Hydriac, St Martin of Achai, St Hatarius of Borno, St Martin of Gemelles, St Peter of Solobria, St Mary of Toxoneries, St Martin of Loon, St Michael of Crum, St Mary of Masconia, St Eparchius of Germund, St Mary Magdalene of Pristiniac, and St Benedict of Boxeria; the church of St Varentius; St Mary Magdalene of Thouercia; St Paul of Bosco; St Stephen of Amaillo; the church of St Lupus and St Pancras; St Martin of Salis; the church of Bocaico; also the churches of the holy martyrs Gervasius and Protasius of Silvax; the church of St Saturninus of Loberchai; the church of St Hilary of Tolon; the church of the Holy Cross of Borellia; the church of St Mary of Galcis; St Mary of the houses of Iterius; and the church of St Hilary of Mazoil, granted to you by our venerable brothers Peter and William, bishops of Poitiers.

Likewise, in the district of Anjou, the church of St Peter of Dompno Petro and St Albinus of Torcanuo, which our brother of blessed memory Rainald, bishop of Anjou, and Geoffrey, his predecessor, granted to your church. [Col. 0216B]

We decree, therefore, that it shall be lawful for no person rashly to disturb your church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved intact, to the full benefit of those for whose support and government they were granted. If, however, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowingly acting against this charter of our constitution, should rashly attempt [Col. 0216C] to violate it, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not correct the matter by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the injustice committed; let him be cut off from the most holy body and blood of God and Lord, our Redeemer Jesus Christ; and let him be subject to severe vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of the same church may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, William, bishop of Palestrina. I, Matthew, bishop of Albano. [Col. 0216D] I, Gerard, cardinal-priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Anselm, priest-cardinal of the title of St Lawrence in Lucina. I, Luciferedus, priest of the title of Vestina. I, Lucas, priest of the title of Saints John and Paul. I, Guido, unworthy priest. I, Aro, priest of the title of St Anastasia. I, Gregory, cardinal-deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Guido, cardinal-deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, cardinal-deacon of St Adrian.

Given at Pisa through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal-deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the sixth day before the Ides [Col. 0217A] of January [8 January], in the twelfth indiction, in the year 1138 of the Lord’s Incarnation. [Note: [Col. 0217D] The chronological indicators are corrupt.] In the fifth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## CLXVIII. Bull confirming the privileges of the monastery of Scheningen. (Year 1135, 28 January.)

[FALKE, *Codex Traditionum Corbeiensium*, p. 761.]

Innocent, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GOTTSCHALK, provost, and the brothers professing the canonical life in the Church of Blessed Lawrence at Scheningen, both present and future, in perpetuity.

The authority of our office exhorts us to love religious men with brotherly charity and to strengthen with the protection of the apostolic see those arrangements which we find reasonably established by our brothers. You have informed us that our brother Reinhard, bishop of Halberstadt, of blessed memory, removed from the place of Scheningen certain nuns who had previously lived there wickedly: since they produced no fruit there, whether spiritual or temporal, but rather, living without rule or discipline, wandered hither and thither through various lands. For the benefit of the persons concerned and because of their evil conduct, after consulting his brethren he removed them from that place and decreed that regular canons should be established there.

But because that place was unsuitable for establishing the brothers’ offices, our said brother judged, by sounder counsel, that the cloister itself should be transferred from [Col. 0217C] its former place to a certain manor which he possessed in the village of Scheningen, with a view to usefulness; while making provision that the old church, with all belonging to it, should remain under the authority of the same brothers and continue under their perpetual dominion and administration.

We therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, assenting to your reasonable desires, confirm by apostolic authority what is known to have been done in this matter by the aforesaid Bishop Reinhard of blessed memory, our brother, and decree that it shall remain ratified for future times. We also decree that the canonical order known to have been instituted in your church according to the Rule of blessed Augustine shall, with the Lord’s help, be observed there inviolate.

Moreover, whatever goods and possessions [Col. 0217D] you now justly and canonically possess, and whatever you may be able to acquire in the future through grants of bishops, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, we place under the protection of the apostolic see and decree that they shall remain secure and unimpaired to you forever. We further forbid any of your brothers, after making profession in that place, to leave your church and transfer to another place without the free permission of the provost and brothers; nor may any bishop, abbot, prior, or other person presume to retain him. Rather, as a violator of his own [Col. 0218A] possession, he shall be compelled to return to his proper place. Furthermore, you shall be free to receive secular brothers who come and desire to join your community, provided that they have first sought permission from their own bishops or prelates.

When you, the present provost of the place, or any of your successors die, no one shall be placed over it by any artifice of fraud or violence, except one whom the common consent, or the party of the brothers possessing sounder judgment, shall provide to be elected according to the fear of God, from your own community or, if necessary, from another of the same profession, according to the Rule of blessed Augustine. Let no person whatsoever, therefore, presume to harass your church by rash vexations or exactions, to take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or oppress it with any troubles; but let all things be kept entire and unimpaired for the benefit of those for whose government and support they were granted, saving always the right and reverence due to the bishop of Halberstadt. [Col. 0218B]

If in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowingly acting against this charter of our constitution, should rashly attempt to violate it, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not correct his offence by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the injustice committed; let him be cut off from the most holy body and blood of God and Lord, our Redeemer Jesus Christ; and let him be subject to severe vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of the same church may there be the peace of our Lord [Col. 0218C] Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, William, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed. I, Matthew, bishop of Albano, have subscribed. I, Lucas, priest-cardinal of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Gerard, priest-cardinal of the title of the Most Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal-deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal-deacon of St Adrian, have subscribed.

Given at Pisa through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal-deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Kalends of February [28 January], [Col. 0218D] in the twelfth indiction, in the year 1135 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the fifth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## CLXIX. He confirms the privilege of the church in the village of Roncaglia, built by the bishop of Piacenza and granted to the canons of St Antoninus. (Year 1135, 13 March.)

[COCQUELINES, II, p. 223.]

Innocent, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son AZO, priest-cardinal of the holy Roman Church and provost of Blessed Antoninus of Piacenza, and to the brothers devoted to divine service in the same Church, [Col. 0219A] both present and future, in perpetuity.

Care for venerable places admonishes us to consider diligently their tranquillity and welfare, so that those who serve in ecclesiastical ministries may also be cherished by the desired protection of ecclesiastical guardianship. Your charity, beloved son in the Lord Azo, priest-cardinal, has informed us that our venerable brother Arduin, bishop of the city of Piacenza, granted you and the brothers of the Church of Blessed Antoninus permission to build in your village called Roncaglia, upon the estate of Blessed Antoninus, a church in honour of . . . , having made provision for this reason: because men and women were said frequently to have passed from this life, owing to the absence of a priest, without participation in the body and blood of the Lord.

The [Col. 0219B] same brother of ours granted to you and your successors, in perpetual right, the administration and ordering of that place. He added also that those who should resolve to put on the religious habit and serve God in the same place should be presented, at a suitable time, by the provost of the Church of St Antoninus—or, if he be absent, by his brothers—to the bishop of Piacenza for the reception of sacred orders. If a clerk or priest of the same place must be corrected because of faults, he shall be corrected by suitable and regular discipline by the same provost or his brothers. But if, though often warned, he should appear incorrigible, he shall be deprived by them of the benefice and residence of that place as useless and disobedient. The priest of the aforesaid place shall receive oil and chrism from the mother church. [Col. 0219C] He shall by no means presume to usurp the tithes belonging to the parish church of Sparovaria. Moreover, if anyone from the same village should wish to show devotion in any matters assigned to the same parish church, he shall by no means hinder this. In all other respects, the church now being built by you from its foundations in the aforesaid village of Roncaglia shall belong wholly and freely to the Church of Blessed Antoninus, so that no archpriest shall know that he has any right of authority in spiritual or temporal matters.

Therefore, since we wish those things which are established by us to remain unimpaired, so also we ought to confirm the good acts of our brothers. We graciously grant your requests and strengthen by apostolic authority what was established in this matter by our aforesaid brother Bishop Arduin; and we decree that it shall remain ratified in future times, as it is known to have been established in the written instrument of our same brother. [Col. 0219D] Let no person therefore presume rashly to disturb the aforesaid Church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with reckless vexations; but let all things be kept intact, to the full benefit of those for whose government and support they were granted.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowingly acting against this charter of our constitution, should rashly attempt to violate it, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make amends by suitable satisfaction, [Col. 0220A] let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the injustice committed; let him be cut off from the most holy body and blood of God and Lord, our Redeemer Jesus Christ; and let him be subject to severe vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of the same Church may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Matthew, bishop of Albano, have subscribed. I, Gerard, priest-cardinal of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Anselm, priest-cardinal of the title of St [Col. 0220B] Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed. I, Lictifred, priest-cardinal of the title of Vestina, have subscribed. I, Lucas, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Guido, unworthy priest, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal-deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal-deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal-deacon of St Adrian, have subscribed. I, Vasallus, cardinal-deacon of St Eustace, have subscribed.

Given at Pisa through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal-deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Ides [Col. 0220C] of March [13 March], in the twelfth indiction (read: thirteenth), in the year 1135 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the sixth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## CLXX. He grants to the Church of St Fridianus at Lucca a hospice and the church of St John. (Year 1135, 3 April.)

[*Bullarium Lateranense*, 14.]

## CLXXI. He confirms the possessions of the abbey of Heylissemiensis, to be built by Rainer. (Year 1135, 3 May.)

[MIRAEUS, *Opera diplomatica*, IV, p. 9.]

Innocent, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son RAINER. [Note: [Col. 0219D] Rainer of Zetrud, a nobleman and founder of this abbey, brought the first religious there in 1130 from the abbey of Floreffe in the county of Namur.] Greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0220D] A ready assent should be given to religious desires, so that faithful devotion may obtain a prompt result. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord Rainer, since, in order to obtain pardon for your sins, you have built, upon your own allod called Upper Heylichshain, a church in honour of Mary, holy Mother of God, so that almighty God may be served there according to the Rule of blessed Augustine and the religious observance of the brothers of Floreffe, we commend your purpose and desire in the Lord and exhort you in every way to carry it out more earnestly.

We graciously grant your just requests and decree by this present charter that the canonical order shall be preserved in the aforesaid church in perpetuity. We also decree that the possessions and goods bestowed upon that church by you or other religious men, or which by the Lord’s favour may hereafter be offered, shall remain secure and unimpaired to the brothers who serve the Lord there. [Col. 0221A]

Let no person whatsoever therefore presume to break or alter the aforesaid order in the aforementioned church, to disturb it by rash presumption, to take away or diminish its goods, or to harass it with any troubles, saving always the reverence due to the diocesan bishop.

But if anyone should dare or rashly attempt to oppose this our constitution, unless he makes suitable satisfaction, let him know that he will incur the indignation of the blessed apostles Peter [Col. 0221B] and Paul.

Given at Pisa, on the fifth day before the Nones of May [3 May], in the year 1135 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the sixth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## CLXXII. He confirms “the Order of St Augustine at the Church of Prémontré, on the fifth day before the Nones of May.” (Year 1135.)

[Continuation of Cosmas by the monks of Sázava, under the year 1135, in Pertz, *Monumenta Germaniae Historica, Scriptores*, IX, 158 (*Patrologia*, vol. CLXVI).]

## CLXXIII. He restores to the Church of St Fridianus at Lucca a parish seized by the monks of St George. (Year 1135, 21 May.)

[*Bullarium Lateranense*, 15.]

[Col. 0221C]

## CLXXIV. To Hubert, bishop, and the canons of Lucca. (Year 1135, 24 May.)

[BALUZE, *Miscellanea*, IV, 589.]

Innocent, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother Hu. [HUBERT], bishop, and to the canons of Lucca, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting that whoever strives to oppose apostolic commands should lie prostrated by grief over his own ruin. Furthermore, for the purpose of rendering justice to the brothers of St Fridianus, we have repeatedly summoned the monks of St George at Lucca to our presence. Yet they neither appeared before us nor gave the aforesaid brothers the satisfaction which they owed. For this offence we pronounced against them a sentence of interdict. But they, as sons of disobedience, did not observe the interdict at all. Therefore, after consulting our brothers, we bound those same monks by the bond of anathema. Accordingly, we command your charity to announce the same sentence throughout your diocese and to renew it every Sunday in your Church for the humiliation of those monks.

Given at Pisa, on the ninth day before the Kalends of June [24 May].

## CLXXV. He confirms certain possessions of the Church of Bonn. (Year 1135, 26 May.)

[GUNTHER, *Codex diplomaticus Rheno-Mosellanus*, I, 217.]

[Col. 0222A]

Innocent, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GERARD, provost, and the canons of the Church of Bonn, and to their successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

Placed in the chair of blessed Peter by divine disposing mercy, we ought to establish what makes for the Church’s peace and beneficially provide for the tranquillity and welfare of venerable places. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously grant your reasonable requests and, by this present written charter, confirm to you the allod which you are known to have acquired for 230 marks by purchase from the noblemen Gerard of Lon and Heribert of Saphra, with the assent of their wives and children: it lies near Bonn, in the village called Entenic, with vineyards, fields, woods, and serfs belonging to it. [Col. 0222B]

We also decree that the hide which you reasonably hold from the Church of Siegburg in the village called Remerstorf under a certain agreement shall remain secure and unimpaired to you forever; and we decree that all these things shall enjoy the freedom owed to them and shall remain free and undisturbed from every secular exaction. We decree, therefore, that neither your successors nor any person may alienate anything from the aforesaid acquired or to-be-acquired possessions, or [Col. 0222C] from those things which the Church of Bonn now freely and canonically possesses, or grant them in fief; but that all things shall be preserved intact for your benefit.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowingly acting against this charter of our constitution, should rashly attempt to violate it, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make amends by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the injustice committed; let him be cut off from the most holy body and blood of God and Lord, our Redeemer Jesus Christ; and let him be subject to severe vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of the same place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal [Col. 0222D] peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, William, bishop of Palestrina. I, Matthew, bishop of Albano. I, Gerard, priest-cardinal of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Lucas, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul. I, Guido, unworthy priest.

Given at Pisa, through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal-deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Kalends of June [26 May], in the thirteenth indiction, in the year 1135 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the sixth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## CLXXVI. Privilege for the abbey of Vendôme. (Year 1135, 26 May.)

[LAUNOY, *Opera*, III, I, 397.]

[Col. 0223A]

Innocent, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ FRAYMUND, abbot of the monastery of Vendôme, and to his successors to be appointed according to the Rule in perpetuity.

With all Churches and ecclesiastical persons we are debtors by reason of the authority and benevolence of the apostolic see; yet it is fitting that we provide more attentively for the peace and welfare of those which, without doubt, are more especially joined and belong to blessed Peter. It is therefore proper that, for the monastery of Vendôme, over which, dearest son in the Lord Raymond, abbot, you are known, by God’s authorizing grace, to preside, we should keep watch with so much greater paternal solicitude because, through the offering of Geoffrey, count of Anjou, of illustrious memory, and Agnes, countess of Poitou, that place is known to pertain to the right and lordship of the holy Roman Church. Therefore we graciously assent to your just petitions and, after the example of our predecessors, strengthen the aforesaid monastery of Vendôme by the privilege of the apostolic see.

Accordingly, just as the aforesaid founders vowed, we decree that this same monastery shall always remain under the protection and liberty of the holy Roman Church, free and released from every dependence upon other persons. We further decree that whatever possessions and goods, offered by the founders of that place itself or by other God-fearing persons and confirmed by the authority of our predecessors, the same monastery now possesses in whatever places, we confirm to you and your successors for ever by the tenor of this present writing. Among these we have appended the following, to be noted by their proper names: the church of St George on the island of Oléron, together with a great part of that island; the church of Blessed Mary of the castle of Oléron; the church of St Nicholas of Oléron; the church of Blessed Mary of Surgères; the church of the Holy Sepulchre at Beaugency; the parish church of St Clement of Crédon, with all churches contained within the bounds of that parish; the church of Adreio; the church of St Saturninus situated upon the Loire; the church of St Peter of Mont-Faulet; [Col. 0223D] the church of Carcere—namely, those of blessed Nicholas and Vincent and of St Mary—which, in the diocese of Le Mans, Hildebert, bishop of that place, granted to your monastery with the consent of the illustrious Geoffrey of Mayenne. In the diocese of Angers: the church of St Mary of Castellis; the church of St Mary of Cosma; the church of St Mary of Broco; the church of St Peter of Villeriis; and the church of St Hippolytus and St Germanus of Aretiacum.

We also confirm to you whatever Robert of Montcontour gave to the monastery of Vendôme and his son Bertran afterwards granted: the church of Blessed John which is upon the Loire. We also grant to you and your successors the church of Blessed Prisca with cardinal dignity. We likewise confirm to you the mitre, dalmatic, sandals, and every other insignia of cardinal dignity. Moreover, whatever possession, dignity, or immunity has been granted to that monastery by the apostolic see, or may hereafter be offered through the generosity of kings or princes or by the offerings of the faithful, we decree shall remain whole and unimpaired to you for ever.

Neither you nor any of your successors shall be compelled to go to a council at which the pope is not personally present. Nor may anyone excommunicate or lay an interdict upon churches subject to your monastery, wherever they may be, except for manifest offences which the abbot and monks of that place, having been admonished by the bishops themselves, have scorned to amend. If anyone should wish to bring suit against you or your successors concerning any matters, neither you nor your successors shall answer in any way [Col. 0224B] until you have consulted the Roman pontiff, whose the monastery itself and the monastery’s property are known to be. Whatever, therefore, shall be alienated or decided concerning those properties without the judgment of the Roman pontiff shall be void.

Furthermore, we decree that the counts of Anjou, Poitou, and Vendôme shall at all times be helpers and defenders of that place for the honour of the apostolic see. None of them shall impose any levy or customary due upon the property of the monastery of Vendôme, nor presume to claim anything therein, except protection alone, which they have promised to provide for the honour of the apostolic see. Upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed there through any craft of intrigue or violence, except one whom the brethren, by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, shall judge ought to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict; yet not without the testimony of three abbots considered the more religious in neighbouring places. The abbot-elect shall be blessed by the bishop of Chartres, or by whichever Catholic bishop he chooses, without any profession or exaction of any kind.

We further command that in both the monastery of Vendôme and the church of St Saviour near the walls of Angers, no person but the pope alone may exercise any power or lordship, or excommunicate or impose an interdict, even should the territory of Chartres or of Angers happen to be excommunicated for any offences; nevertheless, they shall not knowingly receive persons who have been excommunicated. We also decree that no person whatsoever may disturb the often-mentioned monastery, take away its possessions, retain possessions taken away, diminish them, or harass it with rash vexations; rather, let all things be preserved whole for the benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, and be useful for every purpose. If, therefore, in future any archbishop, bishop, emperor, king, prince, duke, count, viscount, judge, or any powerful or powerless person, knowing this page of our privilege, should attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make due amendment by appropriate satisfaction, let that person lose the dignity of his power and office; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment of the wrong committed; let him be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let him be subject at the last judgment to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Thus signed:

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, bishop of Palestrina. I, Antheus, bishop of Albano. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. [Col. 0225B] I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Vasallus, cardinal deacon of St Eustace. I, Lictefridus, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina. I, Chrysogonus, cardinal deacon of St Mary in Portico. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Anselm, cardinal priest of the title of St Lawrence in Lucina. I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul. I, Martin, cardinal priest of the title of St Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Guido, unworthy priest. [Col. 0225C] I, Axo, cardinal priest of the title of St Anastasia.

Given at Pisa, through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, the seventh day before the Kalends of June, in the twelfth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1135, in the sixth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

It follows in a circular figure:

**HELP US, O GOD OF OUR SALVATION. ST PETER. ST PAUL. POPE INNOCENT THE SECOND.**

## CLXXVII. Privilege for the Church of Selva Munda.  
*(A.D. 1135, 28 May.)*

*[Annales Camaldulenses, III, p. 242.]*

In 1135, while Innocent was still staying with the Pisans, as is read in the old summaries of Fontebuono, he confirmed by apostolic authority [Col. 0225D] the permission granted by his predecessor Pope Leo IX to the brethren of Selva Munda: namely, to build their monastery for safer habitation; to possess by his authority donations and offerings, both for the living and for the dead; and to receive tithes from their own goods by gift of the apostolic see. They had abandoned their first monastery, said to have been built in the county of Arezzo by a nobleman, Griffo, and founded through his devotion. For religious reasons he had placed one of his daughters over it and had joined religious women to her. But, moved by his daughter’s misconduct, he took away that monastery and converted it to the use of men, granting it liberty. [Col. 0226A] When wars arose between the son of the aforesaid Griffo and his nephews, the brethren of the said place were compelled to abandon their first monastery and build a new one under the permission obtained from the supreme pontiff. Pope Innocent confirmed that permission by God’s authority and commanded it to be observed for ever.

All the cardinals subscribed.

Given at Pisa, in the year of the Lord 1135, the fifth day before the Kalends of June, in the sixth year of the pontificate of Lord Innocent.

## CLXXVIII. He exhorts the archbishops and bishops established throughout the German kingdom to observe the privilege of the Roman Church: “that major causes be referred to examination by the apostolic see and that all oppressed persons may appeal to it without fear.”  
*(A.D. 1135, 30 May.)*

*[THEINER, Critical Investigations, p. 207.]*

[Col. 0226B]

INNOCENT, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers, the archbishops and bishops established throughout the German kingdom: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Then peace and charity mutually embrace one another, and sincere affection remains unbreakable in reciprocal love, if, according to the order of the divine dispensation and the distinct ranks of the Church, inferiors show reverence to superiors and those set above bestow diligence upon inferiors. But ecclesiastical order is thrown into confusion if inferiors presume upon unlawful acts through rashness, or if those presiding attempt what has not been granted under the laxity of impunity. For the structure of the human body and of the divine fellowship remains unharmed if shepherds keep watch over [Col. 0226C] the flock and desire rather to feed than to condemn [read: “rule”] among the clergy, and if subjects choose humbly to obey rather than insolently recoil from subjection.

Therefore, lest either part should overturn the ordering of this dispensation, blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, was appointed by the Lord at the head of the Church, so that through himself and his successors he might strengthen the brethren, correct errors, and render to each his due. Hence it has also been promulgated as a general law of the Church that major causes are to be referred to examination by the apostolic see, and that all oppressed persons may appeal to it without fear. For the holy Roman Church has reserved to itself this privilege of appeal. No one is ignorant how necessary the practice of appeal is, since it corrects both the injustice and the incompetence of judges. Once an appeal has been lodged, all things shall remain in their existing state, and nothing shall be altered until a decision concerning the appeal has been pronounced by the person to whom the appeal has been made.

Moreover, what appears blameworthy in laymen is criminal in clerics. Indeed, according to imperial enactments, if ordinary judges judge that appeals should be rejected, they are fined thirty pounds of gold; and their assessors and officials are fined an equal amount unless they have publicly resisted and objected in clear entries of record. How great a punishment, then, ought to be inflicted upon an ecclesiastical judge who rejects the teaching of his mother, the holy Roman Church, and strives to violate the privilege of blessed Peter—making himself equal to Jesus Christ and ascending above the seat of the apostles—he who has the force of justice ready to avenge every disobedience [Col. 0227A] cannot fail to know.

We therefore exhort your brotherhood in the Lord: as you desire that your own dignity be kept inviolate by the apostolic see, so be gentle toward your subjects, and henceforth do not attempt in any respect to lessen or violate the prerogative of hearing. Otherwise, we shall not be judged negligent, lukewarm, or guilty before the Lord for allowing such a grave transgression to go unpunished. For by the office of the apostolate a necessity has been imposed upon us by God: while honourably providing for the greater persons, we must beneficially care for the lesser without injury.

Given at Pisa, the third day before the Kalends of June.

## CLXXIX. Privilege for the monastery of Nobiliacum.  
*(A.D. 1135, 2 June.)*

*[DUCHESNE, History of the House of Béthune.]*

[Col. 0227B]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son WALTER, abbot of the monastery of Nobiliacum, and to his successors regularly appointed for ever.

[lacuna]

We also confirm the land situated near the sea, which William, advocate of Béthune, with the consent of Count Thierry of Flanders, gave to that church in exchange for Reschesburg, etc.

Given at Pisa through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, the fourth day before the Nones of June, in the thirteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1136, in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## CLXXX. The privileges and liberties of the abbey of St Peter on Mount Blandin, of the Order of St Benedict, are confirmed.  
*(A.D. 1135, 2 June.)*

*[MIRAEUS, Diplomatic Works, IV, p. 10.]*

[Col. 0227C]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son GILBERT, abbot of the monastery of Blandin, and to his successors for ever.

It is fitting for apostolic authority to cherish religious persons and to protect their places by pious guardianship, and to lighten and relieve whatever burdens them, so that, through the grace of the consolation granted, they may be more ready in God’s service.

For this reason we receive the aforesaid monastery of Blandin especially under the dominion and protection of blessed Peter alone and of ourselves, [Col. 0227D] and decree that it shall remain so for ever. By apostolic authority we establish that henceforth no bishop may presume in any way to diminish anything from the revenues, goods, estates, or villages of that monastery; make any intrusions there; place a cathedra there; confer orders there; establish a commune; hold a *placitum* (court); or exercise any power of command, unless invited by the abbot and brethren of that place. We wholly prohibit public masses or stations from being held in that monastery by a bishop, and prohibit a bishop from frequently coming there, unless called by the abbot and brethren.

We decree that the altars now canonically possessed by the same monastery [Col. 0228A] shall be free from every personal benefice, and that no exaction whatsoever shall be demanded in respect of them by bishops or their ministers on any pretext; nor shall they be subjected to inquiry except by canonical judgment, while in all things the canonical right of the diocesan bishop is preserved.

Moreover, we confirm inviolably that priests who are to minister at those altars shall first be elected by the abbot and his church, and shall thereafter be presented to the bishop, archdeacon, or dean, from whom they shall receive the cure of souls. But they shall render the abbot due obedience in matters belonging to the monastery. We also decree that, excepting those who have been ordained to their own titles, you may remove priests from your churches if they are insufficiently qualified and, with the consent of the diocesan bishop, appoint qualified persons in their place; and [Col. 0228B] that no one may anoint your sick parishioner with oil, take him outside the parish, or bury him when dead without your consent.

You may also excommunicate for notorious crimes; and those excommunicated shall be regarded as excommunicated by the bishop and his ministers, and shall by no means be absolved except by you. We declare your estates situated in Gaul free from every tithe except that on crops; and we confirm to you and your church the land that is formed by the sea’s alluvion adjoining your own land. Nor shall anyone ever have leave, without the abbot’s consent, to remove a monk from your monastery in order to promote him to an ecclesiastical order or for any other cause.

Accordingly, we establish that these decrees of constitution are to be observed by the authority of God and our own with perpetual stability [Col. 0228C] and without any opposition, and that they may not be changed by anyone upon any pretext. Peace and blessing be upon the observer; upon the non-observer, unless he comes to his senses, perpetual curse.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, William, bishop of Palestrina. I, Matthew, bishop of Albano. I, Guido, unworthy priest. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Lucas, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul.

Given at Pisa through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman [Col. 0228D] Church, the fourth day before the Nones of June, in the thirteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1136, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## CLXXXI. To Henry, bishop of the Leuci.—He confirms the agreement made between him and Frederick, count of Toul.  
*(A.D. 1135, 6 June.)*

*[MANSI, Councils, XXI, 419.]*

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, bishop of the Leuci, and to his successors canonically promoted for ever.

[Col. 0229A] As we ought, by the moderation of ecclesiastical discipline, to correct unreasonable enactments of our brethren, so likewise it is fitting that we confirm their good deeds. Therefore, venerable brother Henry, bishop, we confirm by this present writing, and decree to remain valid in future times, the peace and agreement made at Rutila in the parish of Trier, after many wars, labours, and expenses, between you and the nobleman Frederick, count of Toul, in the presence of our venerable brethren Altwin, bishop of Santa Rufina and then legate of the apostolic see; Albero, archbishop of Trier; and his suffragans—namely Stephen, bishop of Metz, and Albero, bishop of Verdun—as well as other noble princes: namely Simon, duke; Adelaide, duchess, his wife; Renaud, count of Bar; Walter of Cundricourt; Odo of Melaino; [Col. 0229B] and Peter of Bressejo.

That is: concerning the hospitality or customary due which the aforesaid Count Frederick was striving unjustly to appropriate for himself from the provision of the brethren of the Church of Toul, he shall henceforth dare to claim nothing as owed to him. Nevertheless, if the aforesaid count should wish to lodge at Visceriacum in the provision of the brethren twice yearly with only seven or ten knights, this shall not be denied him; but the brethren of that place shall support him and shall not trouble him concerning it, provided that he receives hospitality in the brethren’s manner; provided that, if he wishes it to be provided by the administration of ministeriales, he imposes no exaction in that village, either personally or through others. But if he presumes to transgress or violate this, the aforesaid brethren may obtain justice from him on that account.

Furthermore, should it ever be necessary and the same count request it from the dean or provost, a third lodging shall be given to him once yearly in the provision of the brethren, again with only seven or ten knights. But if necessity should arise and he is unable to obtain the lodging through either the dean or the provost, let him receive that lodging through the hands of the ministeriales and accept with thanksgiving the suitable service provided to him. If the count acts otherwise than as written above, violates the approved agreement made before the aforesaid bishops and princes, exercises any exaction or violence in the villages [Col. 0229D] of the aforesaid brethren, or fails to receive through the hands of the ministeriales the aforesaid services, borne by the canons and determined in the manner stated: let him entirely lose the lodgings that he received not by debt or justice but through the brethren’s forbearance. This arrangement may continue only so long as he observes the friendship owed to the brethren.

We therefore decree that neither the aforesaid count nor any person may rashly harass you, your successors, the Church of Toul, or its canons on this account, or exact from you or them anything beyond what has been stated. Rather, let him be content with the established lodgings, and henceforth let the Church of Toul and its canons remain free and undisturbed from his harassment. If anyone knowingly and rashly attempts to act against this page of our confirmation, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not correct his offence by appropriate satisfaction, let him incur the loss of his power and office and be separated from the most sacred body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ. But those who observe it shall obtain the grace of almighty God and of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Pisa through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, the seventh day before the Ides of June, in the eighth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1136, in the sixth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## CLXXXII. He assigns the church of John at Vico to the canons of Blessed Mary of Piacenza, subject to an annual payment to the apostolic see.  
*(A.D. 1135, 7 June.)*

*[COCQUELINES, II, p. 228.]*

[Col. 0230B]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son JOHN, provost of the church of Blessed Mary of Piacenza, and to his successors regularly appointed for ever.

By the administration of the office entrusted to us by God, we are compelled diligently to attend to maintaining the condition of God’s Churches in the strength of their soundness, and carefully to provide lest, through any circumstance, integrity and religion should altogether perish in places where they have been accustomed to flourish. For the church of St [Col. 0230C] John of Vico, situated within the limits of the diocese of Piacenza and especially belonging to the right and lordship of blessed Peter, has, because of sins, been greatly diminished and has suffered very great loss both in temporal and spiritual matters. But you, beloved son in the Lord John, provost, coming to the apostolic see, humbly petitioned us for the grant of that church.

Therefore, having confidence in Christ because of your religious character and zealous care, we entrust that church to you and your successors, and through you to the Church of Piacenza, for its improvement: namely, that the goods and possessions of that place which have been alienated may be recovered through your diligence; that those held may be preserved; and that an honourable service may be daily rendered to the Lord there by a community of regulars. If, however—which we do not desire—you should fall away from the favour of the apostolic see, or should not observe what has been imposed upon you concerning that church, that place, with all its possessions, movable, immovable, and animate, shall return without hindrance to the right, lordship, and free disposal of the holy Roman Church. As a sign that the aforesaid place belongs to blessed Peter and the holy Roman Church, you shall pay half an ounce of gold annually to the Lateran palace. Let no person whatsoever, therefore, henceforth harass you in this matter or impose any burden upon you. If anyone should presume, through rash boldness, to attempt this, let him know that he shall incur the indignation of the blessed [Col. 0231A] apostles Peter and Paul and of ourselves. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, William, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Anselm, cardinal priest of the title of St Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed. I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Martin, cardinal priest of the title of St Stephen on the Caelian Hill, have subscribed. I, Azo, cardinal priest of the title of St Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints [Col. 0231B] Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Stephen, cardinal deacon of St Lucy in Orphea, have subscribed. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of St George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of St Adrian, have subscribed. I, Boethius, cardinal deacon of St Vitus, have subscribed. I, Vasallus, cardinal deacon of St Eustace, have subscribed.

Given at Pisa through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, the seventh [Col. 0231C] day before the Ides of June, in the thirteenth indiction [read: fourteenth], in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1136, in the seventh year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## CLXXXIII. Bull for the abbey of Joncels.  
*(A.D. 1135, 8 June.)*

*[Gallia Christiana, VI, Instrumenta, 135.]*

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son BERENGER, abbot of the monastery of Blessed Peter of Joncels, and to his successors regularly appointed for ever.

Although, by the apostolic office entrusted to us by God, we are debtors to all Churches and ecclesiastical persons, it is fitting that we devote more zealous care to those which are known to belong more especially to the right of blessed Peter. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord Berenger, abbot, we graciously assent to your just petitions and, after the example of our predecessors Gregory VII and Paschal II, Roman pontiffs of revered memory, receive the monastery of blessed Peter at Joncels under the guardianship and protection of the apostolic see and strengthen it by this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and lawfully possesses, or may in future be able to acquire by God’s favour through the grant of pontiffs, the liberality of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among them we have appended the following to be noted by their proper names: [Col. 0232A] in the village of Joncels itself, the churches of St Felix, St Michael, and St Saturninus; in the diocese of Béziers, the church of St John of Silias; the church of St Peter of Rovinac; the church of St Martin of Avena; the church of St Mary of Altiniac; the church of St Dalmatius of Telnodaz; the church of the Saviour of Rocca Rotunda; the church of St Nicholas; the church of St Saturninus of Canaonas; the church of St Bartholomew of Arnosia; the church of St Julian of Fellinas; the church of St Peter of Dransthilag; the church of St Mary of Anisa; the church of St Stephen of Diano; the church of St Uricus of Bezet; the church of St Mary of Frangolia; the church of St Peter of Bruculo; the church of the Saviour of Podio; and the church of St Susanna of Barzac. In the diocese of Rodez [Col. 0232B]: the church of St Martin of Canals; the church of St Julian of Moleiras; the church of St Christopher of Druria; and the church of St Mary of Tauriaco. In the diocese of Agde: the church of St Mary of Nataliono and the church of St Cecilia of Lopiano. In the diocese of Lodève: the church of St Mary of Pruneto.

We grant and confirm to you in perpetuity, to hold and possess freely and without anyone’s contradiction, the tithes and other rights which until this time you have held quietly and lawfully; and by apostolic authority we decree that neither bishop nor any other person shall inflict upon you any diminution or violence concerning them. On the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed there through any artifice of intrigue or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of their counsel, shall judge ought to be elected from the same community, if a suitable person is found, according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict. If no person suitable to exercise this government can be found in that monastery, the aforesaid brethren may elect an abbot for themselves from another monastery. The abbot-elect shall be consecrated by the diocesan bishop, if he is willing to perform this without misconduct or any exaction; otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by the authority of the apostolic see, shall grant what is requested.

We have also judged it proper to add in this present chapter that the monastery itself, and its abbots and monks, shall be secure from all harassment of secular service and free from every burden of worldly oppression, serving the Lord in holy life and the observance of religion. If any bishop or any ecclesiastical or secular person should presume to burden your monastery in property or persons, the abbot and brethren of that place may freely appeal to the apostolic see. Let no person whatsoever therefore rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, remove its possessions, retain possessions removed, diminish them, or assign them to other places under a pretence of pious causes; rather, let all things be preserved whole for the benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, and be useful for every purpose. As a token [Col. 0233A] of this liberty received from the Roman Church, you shall pay one bezant each year to us and our successors. If any king, emperor, duke, count, prince, or ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not amend by appropriate satisfaction, let him lose the dignity of his power and office; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment of the wrong committed; let him be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject to strict vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of the aforesaid monastery may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action [Col. 0233B] and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Chrysogonus, cardinal deacon of St Mary in Portico, have subscribed.

Given at Pisa through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, the sixth day before the Ides of June, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1135, in the thirteenth indiction, in the sixth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## CLXXXIV. Privilege for the abbey of Maillezais.  
*(A.D. 1135, 9 June.)*

*[ARCÈRE, History of La Rochelle, vol. II, documentary proofs, p. 669.]*

[Col. 0233C]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son TEBALD, abbot of the monastery of St Peter of Maillezais, and to his successors regularly appointed for ever.

Although, by the authority and benevolence of the apostolic see, we are debtors to all churches and ecclesiastical persons, it is fitting that we provide more attentively for, and defend from the attacks of wicked persons with a closer love, those which undoubtedly adhere more especially to blessed Peter and the holy Roman Church. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord Tebald, abbot, we graciously assent to your petitions and strengthen and confirm by this present writing to you and your successors regularly appointed the monastery of Maillezais over which, by God’s authorizing grace, you are known to preside. Following the tenor of the privileges of our holy predecessors of blessed memory—Sergius, Alexander, Urban, Paschal, Calixtus, and Gelasius, Roman pontiffs—we establish by apostolic authority in this present instrument of our privilege that whatever the same monastery now possesses, or may hereafter canonically acquire through the grant of pontiffs, the liberality of princes, or the offerings of the faithful, and whatever is shown to have been confirmed to your predecessors by the protection of the privileges of our aforesaid predecessors, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors.

Moreover, so that your monastery [Col. 0234A] of Maillezais, established under the protection and jurisdiction of the holy Roman Church, which by God’s aid we serve, may not be subject to the dominion of any other church’s right, we forbid every priest of any church to exercise in it any authority whatever, except the head of this apostolic see; so strictly that, unless invited by the abbot, he may not even presume to celebrate the solemnities of Mass. You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and ordinations of monks to be promoted to sacred orders from the bishop of Poitiers, provided that he has the favour and communion of the apostolic see and is willing to supply them freely and without misconduct, with every exaction set aside. Otherwise you may receive such sacraments and consecration from whichever Catholic bishop you prefer.

It is therefore your duty, beloved in Christ, zealously to establish the institutions of regular discipline, so that, the freer you are from secular disturbances, the more fully and diligently you may endeavour with all the powers of soul and mind to please God. As a token of this liberty received from the Roman Church, you shall pay twenty shillings of current money annually to the Lateran palace.

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb that monastery, take away its possessions, retain possessions taken away, diminish them, or harass it with rash vexations; rather, let all things be preserved whole for the benefit of those for whose support they were granted, and be useful for every purpose. If any ecclesiastical or secular person [Col. 0234C] should hereafter, knowing this page of our constitution, rashly attempt to act against it, and, after a second or third warning, does not make due amendment by appropriate satisfaction, let that person lose the dignity of office and honour and be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at Pisa, through the hand of Aimeric, deacon cardinal and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the fifth Ides of June, in the thirteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1136 [Col. 0234D], and in the sixth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

CLXXXV. Privilege for the monastery of St Michael of Hugthoven. (10 June 1135.)

[SCHOEPFLIN, *Alsatian Diplomatic Documents*, vol. I, p. 208.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son CONRAD, abbot of the monastery of St Michael, situated in the place called Vosagus, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

[Col. 0235A] A desire shown to concern the religious purpose and the salvation of souls ought, by the Lord’s authority, to be fulfilled without delay. Therefore, for this reason, we receive under the protection of the chief of the Apostles and under our own protection, and strengthen by the page of this present privilege, the monastery built in honour of St Michael and all the heavenly powers in the diocese of Strasbourg, in the wood called Vosagus beside the river Scheram, by Count Werner of good memory, and offered by him to St Peter. We decree that all which that place now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means under God’s provision, acquire, shall remain firm and inviolate in perpetuity for you, beloved [Col. 0235B] son in the Lord, Abbot Conrad, and your successors.

Among these we append the following, to be recorded by their proper names: namely, the fields, woods, and meadows adjoining in that valley; serfs, female slaves, and fishing rights as far as Ludenbach; and the chapel of Rugnisbach with its appurtenances. We confirm to you, for holding and possession, the timber granted you by the same count from his demesne forest, necessary for the work of the monastery, the workshops of the cloister, and the needs of the brethren. We further add that, if that same forest bears fruit, you shall likewise receive a tenth part of it, according to the grant of that same man.

Likewise, the estate at Fleresheim, granted to you by Count Adelbert of Hadesburc [Col. 0235C] and his wife Judinta, together with the renunciation of the church situated there. The estate at Heidolfesheim, with its serfs and ban, which you appear to possess through the gift of the illustrious Count Folmar, son of the aforesaid Werner, and of his wife Helliga. Likewise the estate at Egensheim, given by Berlint, sister of the same count; and the estate at Taleheim. The estate at Eureseim [Note: [Col. 0235D] Ebersheim is meant, from which the monastery of Novientum is called Ebersheim Munster.]; the estate at Tambach. Likewise, the estate which you appear to possess in Luteringia, at Geheresdorf, through the gift of Count Luttold and his wife Adeleheid. One entire forest tract and two half-tracts; two mills; a half ban for selling wine; and a quarter share of the market. Likewise, an estate at Brachalfingen [Note: [Col. 0236D] Perhaps modern Brechlingen.], another at Banesdorf, and another at Herebrehteswile; three whole churches and one half church. [Col. 0235D] Likewise, the estate in the aforesaid village given by the priest Donatus and his brother Rainard, with male and female serfs; and the church of that village, given by Count Conrad and Count Erimann with his wife Agnes.

On the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it by any violence, except the person whom all the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall elect according to the fear of God and the Rule of St Benedict. The elected person shall be consecrated by the bishop of Strasbourg, if he is Catholic, enjoys the favour of the Apostolic See, and is willing to confer it upon you without corruption or exaction. Otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall confer that consecration upon you.

[Col. 0236A] We also decree that burial in the place itself shall be free, so that no one may hinder the devotion and final will of those who determine to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated. The advocate of the place shall not be appointed through any violence, but by the common will of the abbot and chapter. If he should burden your monastery beyond what is just, you shall be free to choose another, as seems best to you.

Moreover, the monastery itself, with its appurtenances, shall be [Col. 0236B] secure, sacred, and free from the jurisdiction of the bishop of Strasbourg and from every exaction imposed by him. As a token of this liberty received from the Roman Church, you shall annually pay one Byzantine gold coin to us and our successors.

We therefore decree that absolutely no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any molestations; rather, all things shall be preserved whole for the complete benefit of the uses for which they were granted, namely, the governance and support of those concerned. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, after a second or third warning, should fail to make suitable amends, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and rank and be cut off from the most sacred [Col. 0236C] body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ. But let all who preserve the rights of that place have the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, William, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed. I, Gregory, deacon cardinal of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Matthew, bishop of Albano, have subscribed. I, Stephen, deacon cardinal of St Lucy in [Col. 0236D] Orphen, have subscribed. I, Anselm, cardinal priest, have subscribed. I, Theodwin, bishop of Santa Rufina, have subscribed. I, Odo, deacon cardinal of St George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Azo, cardinal priest of the title of St Anastasia, have subscribed.

Given at Pisa, through the hand of Aimeric, deacon cardinal and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the fourth Ides of June, in the thirteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1135, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

CLXXXVI. Bull raising the priory of St Peter of Nant to the rank of an abbey, uniting several churches to it. (13 June 1135.)

[*Gallia Christiana*, I, Documents, 61.]

[Col. 0237A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son RAYMOND, abbot of the monastery of Blessed Peter of Nant, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

The authority of the Apostolic See urges us to cherish religious persons and to foster their places, especially those which belong to the men of St Peter, in the bosom of the holy Roman Church, and with paternal affection to provide that religion may increase and be preserved in them. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot, [Col. 0237B] we have judged that your desire, which is shown to concern the religious purpose and the salvation of souls, ought by God’s authority to be fulfilled without delay: namely, that the church of Blessed Peter of Nant—which, thanks be to God, has greatly increased through your diligence both in temporal and spiritual matters—shall henceforth, in accordance with your petition, be established as an abbey rather than a priory. And, so that it may remain an abbey inviolably in the future, we enact this by the present decree.

We receive it, as belonging to the right and property of Blessed Peter, under the guardianship and protection of the Apostolic See and strengthen it by the page of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and lawfully possesses, or may hereafter, by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity [Col. 0237C] of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means under the Lord’s provision, acquire, shall remain firm and inviolate for you and your successors.

Among these we have appended the following to be recorded by their proper names: in the village of Nant, the church of St Stephen and the church of St James; in Larzac, the church of St Saviour, the church of St Mary of Cuneis, the church of St Stephen of Cantobrio, the church of St Mary Magdalene of Lechiciis, the church of St Martin of Vicano, the church of St Michael of Robiaco, the church of the Holy Sepulchre of Algua, the church of St Christopher of Cubertoirata, the church of St Mary of Luc, the church of St Mary of Celcleras, and the church of St John of Brolio. In the [Col. 0237D] diocese of Nîmes: the church of St Mary of Durbia, the church of St Gerald of Rupefolio, the church of St John of Vallegarinta, the church of St Mary of Treve, and the church of St Peter of Revenh.

Furthermore, upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed there through any cunning of usurpation or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren in counsel, shall determine ought to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of St Benedict. The elected person shall be consecrated by the diocesan bishop, if he is Catholic and willing to grant this without corruption or any exaction; otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what is requested.

[Col. 0238A] We also determine that burial in the place itself shall be free, so that no one may stand in the way [read: *obsistat*, “oppose”] of the devotion and final will of those who determine to be buried there, unless they have been excommunicated, while the right of the mother church is nevertheless preserved. Therefore, no bishop, and no person great or small whatsoever, may [printed *facit*; read *vacet*, “be at liberty”] rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations. Rather, all things shall be preserved intact for the benefit of your use and that of the brethren and poor.

As a token that that monastery belongs to the right of Blessed Peter, you shall annually pay two Byzantine gold coins to us and our successors. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, after a second or third warning, should fail to make suitable amends, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and rank, be cut off from the most sacred [Col. 0238B] body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer, and at the last judgement be subject to strict vengeance. But let all who preserve the rights of that place have the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. [Col. 0238C] I, William, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed. I, Guy, bishop of Tivoli, have subscribed. I, Gerard, cardinal priest, have subscribed. I, Litusens, cardinal priest, have subscribed. I, Luke, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Anthony, cardinal priest, have subscribed. I, Gregory, deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Chrysogonus, deacon cardinal, have subscribed.

Given at Pisa, through the hand of Aymeric, deacon cardinal and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the Ides of June, in the thirteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation eleven hundred [Col. 0238D], and in the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II. [The year is incomplete in the supplied text.]

CLXXXVII. At the request of Bishop Goslen of Soissons, he confirms to Marmoutier the church of Saints Rufinus and Valerius at Bazoches. (16 June 1135.)

[MABILLON, *Annals of the Order of St Benedict*, VI, 671.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son ODO, abbot of Marmoutier, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

Whenever a request is made of us which is known to accord with reason and propriety, it teaches us gladly to grant it and to furnish suitable [Col. 0239A] support for petitioners’ desires. And just as we desire that what we establish remain firm and inviolate, so likewise we ought to strengthen by Apostolic authority those arrangements which we find have been made by our brethren through reasonable care.

Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Odo, providing for the interests of Marmoutier and assenting to the petitions of our venerable brother Goslen, bishop of Soissons, we grant to you, and through you to Blessed Martin, the church of Bazoches, consecrated in honour of the blessed martyrs Rufinus and Valerius, which the same bishop, with the consent of his chapter, granted to you, together with all things belonging to that church, to possess and hold in perpetuity. There remain preserved, however, the arrangements reasonably established between you and that bishop concerning the prior of Bazoches and the church of St Theobald, and confirmed by your mutual [Col. 0239B] writings.

Therefore no person may henceforth harass Blessed Martin’s Marmoutier on account of this our confirmation, or bring upon you or your successors any trouble or opposition concerning the aforesaid church of Bazoches and all things belonging to it. If anyone, however, with rash boldness attempts to act against this our constitution, and, after a second or third warning, fails to correct the offence by worthy satisfaction, let that person suffer the loss of the dignity of office and rank, and be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ. But those who observe it shall obtain the favour of almighty God, of the blessed Apostles Peter and Paul, and of us. Amen, [Col. 0239C] amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, [subscription mark]. I, William, bishop of Palestrina, [subscription mark]. I, Guy, bishop of Tivoli, [subscription mark]. I, Luke, priest [of Saints] John and Paul, [subscription mark]. I, Guy, unworthy priest, [subscription mark]. I, Azo, cardinal priest of the title of St Anastasia, [subscription mark].

Given at Pisa, through the hand of Aimeric, deacon cardinal and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of July, in the fourteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1136, in the sixth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

CLXXXVIII. (17 June 1135.)

[*Gallia Christiana*, XII, Documents, 260.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, [Col. 0239D] to his beloved daughters in Christ, HELOISE and the other sisters dedicated to divine service in the oratory of the Holy Trinity, situated in the district of Troyes, in the parish of Quincey, above the river Arducon, both present and future, in perpetuity.

“Whenever that,” etc., as in the privilege of 28 November 1131, no. 70 above. We further decree that you shall not be compelled to leave the monastery in order to receive blessing and consecration; nor may the bishop or any other person presume, on account of the election of an abbess or for any other reason, to inflict upon you any burden or molestation. “Therefore no person,” etc. As a token of this liberty received from the Roman Church, you shall annually pay [Col. 0240A] one gold obol to the Lateran palace. “If therefore anyone,” etc.

Given at Pisa, through the hand of Aimeric, deacon cardinal and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of July, in the thirteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1136, in the sixth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

CLXXXIX. He informs the clergy of the Church of Milan that Tetald of Medolaco has been excommunicated for harassing the church of Virgis. (18 June 1135.)

[LUPUS, *Diplomatic Codex of Bergamo*, II, 989.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons T., archpriest; A., archdeacon; A., vicedominus; An. of Rode; Na., primicerius; Ste., archpriest; and the other clergy of the Church of Milan, Catholic men: greeting and Apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0240B] We do not wish your charity to be unaware that, because of the excessive harassment and plunder which Tetald of Medolaco has often inflicted upon the church of Virgis, which belongs to the right of Blessed Peter, and has not ceased to inflict, we have bound him by the bond of excommunication. Therefore we command and order your whole body to avoid him completely as an excommunicated person and to drive him from your territories.

Given at Pisa, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of July.

CXC. He informs Bishop Gregory, clergy, and people of Bergamo that he has settled the controversy between the canons of St Vincent and St Alexander. (18 June 1135.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia Sacra*, IV, 455.]

[Col. 0240C]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother GREGORY, bishop, and to his beloved sons, the clergy and people of Bergamo: greeting and Apostolic blessing.

We make known to your charity that, after many labours and difficulties which we have often endured in order to quiet the dispute long agitated between the canons of St Vincent and St Alexander, we have at length, God being favourable, settled that controversy. Therefore we command and order you to put an end to the wars and hostilities, and to observe without contradiction what has been established by us concerning this matter. Moreover, under the attestation of anathema, we command your whole body, upon receiving these letters, to remove from there the *Bettefredum* [meaning uncertain] which, as we have learned, you erected in the bell-tower of St Vincent because of the same discord; and henceforth to maintain peace and concord.

Given at Pisa, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of July.

CXCI. Privilege for the monastery of the Holy Cross at Donauwörth. (19 June 1135.)

[COCQUELINES, vol. II, 230.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ DIETRICH, abbot of the monastery of the Holy Cross of Werd, and to his successors regularly appointed.

As we have learned from the acts of our predecessor Pope Leo IX of holy memory, a nobleman named Mangold of Werde once built a monastery in his castle out of devotion. Offering it to Blessed Peter, chief of the Apostles, he caused it to be consecrated in honour of the holy and life-giving Cross through the hands of that Roman pontiff, and established there women religious to serve God.

[Col. 0241A] It then happened that, after that monastery had been broken up and devastated through the agency of wicked men, another Mangold, son of the nobleman just mentioned, obtained from the Apostolic See permission to transfer the same monastery to another place. Accordingly, he founded a church on level ground beside the castle itself and assigned women religious there to God’s service. When these women had declined both in religious discipline and in number, a third Mangold humbly approached our predecessor Pope Paschal of illustrious memory and requested that, after the women religious had been removed, monks be placed in the same location. The Roman pontiff graciously assented to his petition and directed by his letters Gebhard, formerly bishop of Constance and then legate of the Apostolic See, to take monks from the cell of St Blasius and place them in that monastery. When the aforesaid bishop had done this, that place greatly increased, thanks be to God, both in temporal and spiritual matters.

Therefore, beloved son Abbot Dietrich, you have humbly asked us to strengthen by a privilege of the Apostolic See that monastery over which, by God’s authority, you preside.
