We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations [Col. 0268B]; but let all things remain intact, etc.

Given at Pisa through the hand of Almericus, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, 20 February, the twelfth indiction, in the year 1136 of the Lord’s Incarnation, the sixth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

CCXX. To Gregory, bishop of Bergamo. (1136, 28 February.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, IV, 456.]

INNOCENT, etc., to his venerable brother GREGORY, bishop of Bergamo, etc.

There is no doubt that we settled in our presence the controversy hitherto conducted between the canons of the holy martyrs Vincent and Alexander. Yet the canons of St Vincent, desiring, as we have learned, to be wiser than is fitting [Col. 0268C], quibble over the words of our decision and twist them to their own understanding and will. Nor content with this, they have transferred the places in choir established from ancient times. But this change is known not to have been wrought by the right hand of the Most High.

We therefore command and direct your brotherhood that, both concerning the places in choir or at table—every removal having been eliminated—and concerning peace, incense, and other matters, you shall cause what we have decreed to be observed inviolably. Nor shall you permit such subtleties or quibbles to be further introduced against our decision. With regard also to the rendering of fealties, penances, chaplains, places in the choir, synod, or the bishop’s table [Col. 0268D], etc., or the other chapters contained in our privilege, sit among them as so equitable an arbiter that the canons of St Alexander shall have no ground on which they ought justly to complain against you.

Given at Pisa, 28 February.

CCXXI. To Peter the Venerable, abbot of Cluny.—Confirmation of the church of Rochabovecourt. (1136, 13 March.)

[MANSI, Councils, XXI, 411.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ PETER, abbot of Cluny, and to his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

A good and diligent householder rejoices greatly [Col. 0269A] when he sees his vineyard, which he has leased out, being cultivated by husbandmen with watchful care and being cleared alike of thistles and brambles. His joy is certainly increased by a more delightful gladness if that same vineyard, through regular propagation, begins to extend across a wide expanse. By a corresponding reasoning, therefore, we believe it especially pleasing to God if the religious community dedicated to God at the monastery of Cluny both adorns diverse churches, instructs the minds of very many persons in regular discipline, and kindles them with faith which works through love. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Peter, abbot of Cluny, mindful of the devotion which you, together with the church entrusted to you, have always shown toward the Apostolic See, and of the honor and service which you rendered to us effectively and faithfully, especially in the time of schism: we not only confirm to you and to your successors, but also, in confirming it, bestow by apostolic authority, the church [Col. 0269B] of Rochebeaucourt, which, with the approval of its clergy, was canonically given by our venerable brother William, bishop of Périgueux, to Abbot Pons, your predecessor, and through him to the church of Cluny, and was solemnly confirmed by our predecessor Pope Calixtus of blessed memory, as his privilege attests; so that the Cluniac order may flourish there in perpetuity, to the praise of God—for which it was especially instituted—and to the honor of the most holy Roman Church, to which it is wholly devoted. We decree that no person may presume rashly to disturb that church, or to take away, diminish, or harass by any vexations the goods which it now lawfully possesses or may hereafter, by God’s favor, reasonably acquire through lawful means. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly [Col. 0269C] violates this page of our constitution, etc.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, William, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Guy, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian, have subscribed. I, Vassalus, cardinal deacon of Saint Eustachius, have subscribed. I, Hubaldus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed. I, Anselm, cardinal priest, have subscribed. [Col. 0269D] I, Littifredus, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina, have subscribed. I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed.

Given at Pisa through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the second Ides of March, in the fourteenth indiction, in the year 1136 of the Lord’s Incarnation, the seventh year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## CCXXII. To the same. — Confirmation of Mont-Desiderius.  
*(A.D. 1136, March 13.)*

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 1412.]

It is composed in precisely the same words as the preceding document, down to “and kindles them with faith which works through love.” Then:

With this intention, indeed, we also confirm to you and to your successors in perpetuity the church of Mont-Desiderius [perhaps *Montisdesideriensis* rather than *Montisderiensis*], canonically and devoutly conferred upon the monastery of Cluny by our venerable brothers Guarin, bishop [Col. 0270A] of Amiens, and Simon, bishop of Noyon, with all its appurtenances; this being granted also by our dearest son Louis, illustrious and glorious king of the Franks, by Raynald, archbishop of Rheims, and by Ralph of Péronne, who humbly entreated the Apostolic See for its confirmation. We decree that absolutely no person may rashly disturb that church or take away, diminish, or harass by any vexations the goods which it now lawfully possesses or may hereafter, by God’s favor, acquire through lawful means. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly violates this [Col. 0270B] page of our constitution, etc.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, William, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed. I, Anselm, cardinal priest, have subscribed. I, Luitfredus, cardinal priest, have subscribed. I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Guy, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian, have subscribed. I, Vassalus, cardinal deacon of Saint Eustachius, have subscribed. I, Hubaldus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed.

Given at Pisa through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the third Ides of March, in the fourteenth indiction, in the year 1136 of the Lord’s [Col. 0270C] Incarnation, the seventh year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## CCXXIII. Privilege for the Church of Nice.  
*(A.D. 1136, March 29.)*

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, IV, 1110.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother PETER, bishop of Nice, and to his successors canonically promoted in perpetuity.

The authority of our office exhorts us to labor for the condition of churches and, with the Lord’s help, to provide beneficially for their peace and welfare. For it is recognized as worthy and fitting to our office that we, who have been taken up for the governance of churches, should protect them from the malice [Col. 0270D] of wicked persons, fortify them by the patronage of Blessed Peter and of the Apostolic See, and strengthen by the privilege of the Holy Roman Church the Church of Nice, over which, by God’s appointment, you are known to preside. We decree that the canonical order, which by your praiseworthy effort and God’s grace has been established in the Church of Nice according to the rule of Blessed Augustine, shall be inviolably observed there in future times; and that, when the clerics presently serving the Lord in it die, no one shall replace them unless he is a canon who has professed the regular life. Moreover, when you, now bishop of that place, die, no one except a regular bishop shall be appointed there, one who may, with the Lord’s help, be able both to preside over and to benefit that church.

We also decree that whatever goods and possessions that church [Col. 0271A] now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, with the Lord’s permission, acquire by grants of popes, gifts of kings and princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall be preserved to you and to your successors in perpetuity, secure and undiminished. Among these we have added the following, to be recorded by their proper names: namely, the church of Saint Mary of Clansio; the church of Saint Lawrence of Illontia; the church of Saint Mary of Pila; the church of Saint Thecla; the castle called Drapum; the church of Saint Mary of Villa Vetus; the monastery of Saint Pontius, together with the churches belonging to it, which are recognized lawfully to belong to it within the diocese of Nice as episcopal property; the church of Saint Mary of Olivo; and the church of Saint Hospitius.

Therefore no person may infringe, alter, or overthrow on any pretext that which has been done by you concerning the institution of the aforesaid church and confirmed by us, nor take away its possessions, retain its abbeys, or harass it with any troubles; rather, all things shall always be preserved for the benefit of every use of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly [Col. 0271B] attempts to oppose or rashly contravene this page of our constitution, having been warned a second and a third time, and does not correct his offense by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ; and let him be subject at the final judgment to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve its rights for that church may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, William, bishop of Palestrina. I, Hubaldus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, Chrysogonus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Anselm, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina. I, Lutefredus, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina. I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and [Col. 0271D] Paul.

Given at Pisa through the hand of Almeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Kalends of April, in the fifteenth indiction, in the year 1137 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and the seventh year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## CCXXIV. To Alvisus, bishop of Arras.  
*(A.D. 1136, March 29.)*

[BALUZE, *Miscellanies*, II, 165.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother ALVISUS, bishop of Arras, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Giving manifold thanks to your brotherhood for your devotion and solicitude concerning ourselves and the holy Roman Church, [Col. 0272A] we greet your beloved person by apostolic letters and inform you, as a special son of Blessed Peter, that by God’s favor we and our brethren are well. Moreover, we have granted your requests on behalf of the abbots of Hasnon and Montreuil and of No., the archdeacon, who did not come when summoned to the council. Although, according to the decrees of the holy Fathers, we ought to exact punishment on this account, nevertheless, imitating the gentleness of the Apostolic See, we have judged that this should be forgiven them out of regard for you; and we absolve the aforesaid archdeacon and abbots from the sentence of interdict. Exercise the same solicitude also concerning the other abbots known not to have come when called to the council. Further, because Sydrac, summoned by your brotherhood [Col. 0272B] to appear before us, did not come, we shall, with God as our author, hold valid whatever your prudence canonically decrees concerning his case. Furthermore, sympathizing with your devotion, we have remitted the canons of Condé to our venerable brother Renold, archbishop of Rheims, so that, by his judgment, the controversy between you and them may by God’s favor be concluded.

Given at Pisa, on the fourth day before the Kalends of April.

## CCXXV. Privilege for the Camaldolese Congregation.  
*(A.D. 1136, April 22.)*

[*Annals of Camaldoli*, vol. III, col. 353.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons AZO, prior of Camaldoli, and his brethren, [Col. 0272C] both present and future, in perpetuity.

The incomprehensible and ineffable mercy of divine power has established us in the administration of the Apostolic See for this purpose of providence: that we should strive to exercise a fatherly care concerning all churches. For the holy Roman Church, which retains the primacy over all churches granted to it by God, ought, as a diligent and devout mother, to provide for each church with constant vigilance. It is fitting, therefore, that churches and venerable places—especially those known to serve almighty God in the habit of true religion—should receive the honor of a more special prerogative and be strengthened by the protection of apostolic authority.

Accordingly, following in the footsteps of our predecessor Pope Honorius of good memory and assenting to your petitions, beloved sons [Col. 0272D] in the Lord, we decree by this present ordinance that the hermitage of Camaldoli shall remain in its condition and in the vigor of its religious observance for all future time, and that the order of monastic observance established throughout your congregation shall not be altered by the insolence of any person or by any superstition. We further add that, after making monastic profession, none of the brethren of your congregation may leave without the permission of the prior and the reasonable consent of the brethren. If anyone presumes to depart and, having been warned a second and third time, refuses to return, we subject him to the sentence of excommunication until he makes suitable satisfaction.

Moreover, we forbid any bishop, without canonical examination, to interdict the divine office in churches governed by brethren of your congregation. Further, during a general interdict of a city or parish, with doors closed and diocesan persons not admitted, the monks of your churches shall in no way be forbidden to celebrate the divine offices. Whoever may travel to any place in the service of the servants of God dwelling in the hermitage of Camaldoli shall suffer absolutely no molestation either going, returning, or remaining. Moreover, whatever goods and possessions you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter, by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, acquire by God’s favor, shall remain secure and undiminished to you and to your successors [Col. 0273B] remaining in the same religious life, [Col. 0273B] in perpetuity.

Among these we have added the following to be recorded by their proper names: namely, the church of Saint Donatus, called Fons Bonus, with its hospital and all its goods; the monastery of Saint Mary in Poplena; the monastery of Saint Peter in Luco; the monastery of Saint Saviour near the city of Florence; the monastery of Montismuri; the monastery of Saint Peter in Cerreto; the monastery of Saint Mary in Polliciano; the monastery of Saint Peter in Fontiniano; the monastery of Saint Justus in Volterra; the monastery of Saint Mary in Morrena; the monastery of Saint Fridianus; the monastery of Saint Michael within the city of Pisa; the monastery of Saint Savinus in [Col. 0273C] the territory of that city; the monastery of Saint Stephen in Cintoria; the monastery of Saint Saviour in Cantignano; the monastery of Saint Peter in Puteoli; the monastery of Saint Saviour in Silvamunda; the monastery of Saint Mary in Aguano; the monastery of Saint Peter in Rota; the monastery of Saint Saviour of the Berardingi; the monastery of Saint Vigilius in the borough of Siena; the monastery of Saint Peter on the living mountain of Amiata, without prejudice to the proper custom of that place; the monastery of Saint Quiricus in Rosa; the monastery of Saint Savinus in Chio; the hermitage of Fleri with its monastery; the monastery of Saint Virianus; the monastery of Saint Bartholomew in Anglari.

In the diocese of Castello: the abbey of Dezane, without prejudice to the right of the Church of Castello; the monastery of Saint Mary at the crossroads; the hermitage of Saint Peter in Lajolo; the monastery of Saint Mary in the Island; the monastery of Saint Mary at the lake; the monastery of Saint Angel near the castle of Britti; the monastery of Saint Christina in the same estate. In the March of Camerino: the monastery of Saint George; the monastery of Saint Martin in Accole, with the church called Heremite. On the island of Sardinia: the monastery of the Holy Trinity; at Saccari, the church of Saint Eugenia in Samanar; the church of Saint Michael and Saint Lawrence in Vanari; the church of Saint Mary, Saint John, and Saint Simeon in Salvenero; the church of Saint Nicholas in Trulla; the church of Saint Peter in Scano; the church of Saint Paul in Cotroniano; the monastery of Saint Bartholomew of Anglari, with its castle and all [Col. 0274A] its appurtenances; and the castle of Montorio with all its appurtenances.

In the city of Pisa: the monastery of Saint Zeno, with the right of the Roman Church wholly preserved; the estate of Montione, which you bought from the abbot of Saint Flora, and the church of that estate; the estate of Modionas, which you bought from Henry the provost and the other canons, as is contained in your charters, and the church of that estate with its tithe; the tithe of the estate of Largnano, and of the estate of Agna, and the church of that estate.

Therefore we decree that absolutely no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid hermitage and your congregation, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass them with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole, to benefit in every way the use of the religious brethren and the poor. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts rashly to contravene this page of our constitution, having been warned a second and third time, and does not correct his offense by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know that he is guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject at the final judgment to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve their rights for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

[Col. 0274C] I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church.

**HELP US, O GOD, OUR SAVIOUR.**

I, William, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed. I, Maurus, bishop of Arezzo, have subscribed. I, Anselm, cardinal priest, have subscribed. I, Lictifredus, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina, have subscribed. I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Wido, unworthy priest, have subscribed. I, Azo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. [Col. 0274D] I, Guy, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian, have subscribed. I, Boethius, cardinal deacon of Saints Vitus and Modestus, have subscribed. I, Vassalus, cardinal deacon of Saint Eustachius, have subscribed. I, Hubaldus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed.

Given at Pisa through the hand of Aymeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the tenth day before the Kalends of May, in the thirteenth indiction, in the year 1137 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and the seventh year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## CCXXVI. He congratulates Lothair, emperor of the Romans, on the defeat of Frederick, duke of Swabia. He urges him to act so that he may “obtain Davidic empire and Solomonic kingdom.”  
*(Read Pisa instead of Pavia.) (A.D. 1136, April 24.)*

[SCHLOSSER AND BERCHT, *Archive*, II, 370.]

[Col. 0275A]

## CCXXVII. Privilege, or confirmatory bull, for the Church of Rohr.  
*(A.D. 1136, April 24.)*

[*Monumenta Boica*, vol. XVI, p. 102.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son BRUNO, provost, and to the brethren gathered in the Church of Rohr who profess the canonical life, both future and present, in perpetuity.

[Col. 0275B] The authority of our office exhorts us to cherish religious places and to foster them with the support of a desired petition. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your petitions, receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves the Church of Rohr, in which you devote yourselves to the divine office, and strengthen it by the page of this present writing. We decree that the canonical order according to the rule of Blessed Augustine shall be inviolably observed in the same place for all future time. Furthermore, whatever goods and possessions you may, by the grant of our venerable brother Henry, bishop of Regensburg, the generosity of princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, acquire through God’s favor, shall remain secure and undiminished to you in perpetuity.

Therefore we decree that no person may lawfully [Col. 0275C] rashly disturb your aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; rather, all things shall be preserved whole for the benefit of the uses of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If indeed in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts rashly to contravene this page of our constitution, having been warned a second and third time, and does not correct his presumption by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know that he is guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most holy body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject [Col. 0275D] at the final judgment to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve their rights for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, William, bishop of Palestrina. I, Guy, bishop of Tivoli. I, Wido, unworthy priest.

Given at Pisa through the hand of Almeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the eighth day before the Kalends of May, in the thirteenth indiction, in the year 1136 of the Lord’s Incarnation, the seventh year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## CCXXVIII. Privilege for the Monastery of Laureacum.  
*(A.D. 1136, April 24.)*

[PETRUS, *Suevia ecclesiastica*, p. 537.]

[Col. 0276A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son GRAFDON, abbot of the monastery called Laureacum, situated in the diocese of Augsburg, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

Whenever requests are made to us concerning religion and the ornament of honorable conduct, we ought not delay in granting them, lest we appear to defer good desires which should rather be encouraged. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Grafdo, we have judged that your just petitions should be granted. We receive under the guardianship and protection of the Apostolic See, and fortify by the patronage of the prince of the apostles, the monastery [Col. 0276B] called Laureacum, which the illustrious Duke Frederick, following the will and desire of his father, who had founded it on his own allodial estate, offered to Blessed Peter under an annual payment of one gold coin.

By the page of this present writing, therefore, we decree that the monastic order shall be inviolably observed in that monastery in future times according to the Rule of Blessed Benedict. Whatever goods or possessions are known to have been collected for that place by its founders or by other faithful servants of God, and whatever it may hereafter, by grants of popes, generosity of kings, dukes, or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, acquire through God’s favor, shall remain secure and undiminished to you and to your successors.

In order that the brethren who at any time are devoted to divine service in that monastery may be supported from the goods of the place, we prohibit by apostolic authority any abbot or any ecclesiastical or secular person whatever from taking away, selling, granting in fief, or presuming in any way to alienate the possessions and goods of the aforesaid place. When you, the present abbot of that place, or any of your successors die, no one shall be appointed there through any cunning of fraud or by violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, in the fear of God and according to the Rule of Blessed Benedict, shall judge fit to elect.

You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars [Col. 0276D] or churches, the abbot’s blessing, and ordinations of your monks or clerics who are to be promoted to sacred orders from the diocesan bishop, provided that he is Catholic, enjoys the favor of the Roman Church, and is willing to provide these things freely and without any improper exaction. Otherwise, you shall approach whatever Catholic bishop you prefer; supported by our authority, he shall grant what is requested.

Therefore we decree that no bishop, advocate, or their officials, nor any ecclesiastical person, may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole for you. [Col. 0277A] We likewise decree that the burial-place of that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the final will of those who choose to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated, without prejudice to the right of the mother church. We also confirm to you the tithes which you lawfully possess and have possessed peacefully and quietly until this time. As a token of this liberty received from the Roman Church, and that the same place belongs to the jurisdiction of Blessed Peter, you shall pay one bezant yearly to us and to our successors.

If anyone, therefore, with rash daring attempts to oppose this our constitution, and, having been warned a second and third time, does not make amends by suitable satisfaction, let him be cut off from the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ and be subject at the final judgment to strict [Col. 0277B] vengeance. But upon those who observe it may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, William, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed. I, Guy, bishop of Tivoli, have subscribed. I, Littifredus, cardinal priest of Saint Justina, have subscribed. I, Lucas, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Wido, unworthy priest, have subscribed. I, Azo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and [Col. 0277C] Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Guy, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian, have subscribed. I, Hubaldus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed. I, Chrysogonus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed.

Given at Pisa through the hand of Almeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the eighth day before the Kalends of May, in the fourteenth indiction, in the year 1136 of the Lord’s Incarnation, the seventh year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## CCXXIX. He confirms the discipline and goods of the monastery of Saint Paul at Verdun.  
*(A.D. 1136, April 24.)*

[D. CALMET, *History of Lorraine*, II, documents, p. CCCX.]

[Col. 0277D]

INNOCENT, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son ROGER, abbot of the monastery of Saint Paul situated in the suburb of Verdun, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

Although by the office of the apostolate entrusted to us by God we are debtors to all ecclesiastical persons, we ought nevertheless to apply ourselves with a more earnest zeal of charity to those whom we know to serve the Lord in the habit of true religion. Therefore, beloved son in Christ, Abbot Roger, we graciously assent to your petitions and strengthen by the privilege [Col. 0278A] of the Apostolic See the monastery of Blessed Paul, over which, by God’s appointment, you are known to preside. We decree that what was done by our venerable brother Albero, bishop of Verdun, concerning the institution of that place because of the insolence of brethren formerly dwelling there, and approved by our most beloved brother Albero, archbishop of Trier, shall remain valid and unshaken by our authority for all time: namely, that the canonical order, according to the rule and norm of Blessed Augustine and the institution of the brethren of Prémontré, shall be inviolably observed in that place, and that through them due service shall be rendered to the divine majesty.

We also decree that whatever goods and possessions the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, through grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful causes, acquire by God’s favor, shall be preserved secure and undiminished to you and to your successors. Therefore no person whatsoever may disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any troubles; rather, all things shall be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of the uses of those for whose governance and support they were granted, the right of the diocesan bishop being preserved. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts rashly to contravene this page of our constitution, having been warned a second or third time, and does not correct his offense by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know that he is guilty before divine [Col. 0278C] judgment of the perpetual iniquity; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ; and let him be subject at the final judgment to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve their rights for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at Pisa on the eighth day before the Kalends of May, in the fourteenth indiction, in the year 1137 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and the sixth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## CCXXX. He confirms the cemetery of the monastery of Celta Paulina.  
*(A.D. 1136, April 26.)*

[MULDNER, *Historical Account of the Cemetery Chapel of the Holy Cross*, p. 59, on the testimony of Schultes, *Diplomatic Directory*, I, 317.]

[Col. 0278D]

## CCXXXI. To Raynald, archbishop of Rheims. — That he should grant to the people requesting him his archdeacon, elected archbishop of Bourges.  
*(A.D. 1136, May 12.)*

[PEZ, *Treasury of Anecdotes*, VI, I, 310.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother R., archbishop, and to the chapter of Rheims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is characteristic of the good of charity to rejoice in the advancement of others as in one’s own. He who presents himself as a helper of good works is also a sharer in their reward. [Col. 0279A] Therefore, because the clergy and people of Bourges, deprived of the comfort of a pastor, have elected our dearest son, Master [magistrum?] A., archdeacon of the Church of Rheims, as their archbishop, it is fitting for all of you to rejoice, since by the gift of divine grace you have deserved to have such a person, one whom they seek with great earnestness and supreme desire for the governance of so glorious and noble a church. Accordingly, by apostolic letters we command you, requesting as we command and commanding as we request, to release the person of the same elect to the Church of Bourges in the name of the Lord, and to ensure that the desire of those who have chosen him for their father and archbishop is laudably fulfilled.

Given at Pisa, on the fourth Ides of May.

## CCXXXII. To Master A., archdeacon of Rheims. — That he should obey God, who calls him to the archbishopric of Bourges.  
*(A.D. 1136, May.)*

[PEZ, in the place cited above.]

[Col. 0279B]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son, Master A., archdeacon of Rheims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The faithful and wise steward does [not] place in a napkin the talent which he receives from the Lord to be given out to money-changers, but rather labors with unremitting zeal and the greatest diligence, so that he may restore to his Lord the money entrusted to him with multiplied profit. [Col. 0279C] For this purpose the supreme shepherd, our Lord Jesus Christ, as the authority of the Gospel testifies, said for the third time to Blessed Peter, when he confessed for the third time that he loved his Master: “Feed my sheep” (John XVII, 21). From this it follows that the one who loves feeds, and the one who does not love does not feed. Therefore, if the Son of God came forth from the secret place of the Father into our public world in order to furnish us with the pastures of eternal blessedness, no one pleasing to God ought to prefer his own quiet to the welfare of his neighbors.

Moreover, dearest son in Christ, we wish you to know that the noble and glorious Church of Bourges, deprived of a bishop’s comfort, has chosen your person as its pastor and archbishop. The Lord calls you; Christ invites you to cherish the children of that aforesaid church, entrusted to you by his grace, and more fully to form them in saving disciplines. We also, therefore, whose special concern is to provide for the whole Church of God and to lend aid and counsel to good undertakings, confirm the election made of you. By apostolic authority, for the remission of sins, we enjoin, request, and command you to undertake, every objection and excuse being set aside, both a ministry so pleasing to God and a work so glorious, so that, by divine grace cooperating and your own effort striving, the prerogative of the aforesaid church may be kept intact and provision made beneficially for the people.

## CCXXXIII. Privilege for the Church of Saint Aubert at Cambrai.  
*(A.D. 1136, May 31.)*

[LE GLAY, *Glossary*, p. 39.]

[Col. 0280A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GALTER, abbot, and the sons of the Church of Saint Aubert situated in the city of Cambrai, and to their successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

The authority of our office exhorts us to be zealous for the condition of the Churches and, with the Lord’s aid, to provide beneficially for their peace and welfare. For it is recognized as worthy and consonant with propriety that we, who have been raised to the governance of the Churches, should both defend them from the malice of wicked men and fortify them by the protection of blessed Peter and of the Apostolic See. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we grant assent to your petitions and confirm by the authority of this present document the Church of Saint Aubert, in which you are devoted to divine service, decreeing that whatever goods and possessions that same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter be able reasonably to acquire, by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, through the Lord’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: namely, the Church of Saint Vedast, situated in the city of Cambrai, with many *mansi*; and five brewing-houses (*cambae*) grinding at your mill which you possess in the city; and three ovens; and, from the Salt Gate as far as the road of Saint Remigius, on the left-hand side, whatever you possess in water, fish, lands, and lodgings; one oven; one brewing-house, with its grinding-right; and your *mansus*, with streams flowing within and without, together with the entire district; likewise the entire village called Tillet, with all its appurtenances; the altar-right of Vinciacum, with all its dependencies, namely Lesden, Liegiscurch, and Scurviler, and one mill, one oven, one brewing-house, and everything belonging to the aforesaid altar-right; the altar-right of Vilers Renardi; and the land which the three brothers Hugh, Wibald, and Elbert gave in that same village from Haistaldi Pratum; and whatever right they possessed in the village called Berilgias and at Dehereeias, which they bestowed upon the aforesaid church; the altar-right of Goeio; the altar-right of Silviniacum; the altar-right of Otvilers; the Church of Saint Aubert, with its altar-right, in the village called Andra, with one *mansus* and arable land; the altar-right of the village called Saint Vedast; and a quarter of the allod at Albertiis; the allod which Robert of Bello Manso gave at Fontanas.

In the district of Hainaut: the church with its altar-right at Siccis Avesnis, with fifty *mansi*, arable land, and woodland; likewise the altar-right of Thiens; the altar-right of Maheng; the altar-right of Sausoith; the altar-right of Ivurio, with the dependency of Ramocurth.

> **Note: [Col. 0279D] Altar-right of Ivurio with the dependency of Ramocurth.** From this one may conclude that near Iwuy there existed [Col. 0280D] a village or hamlet called Ramecourt or Ramocourt, sufficiently substantial to constitute a [Col. 0281C] dependency of the parish of Iwuy. What was the precise location of Ramecourt? This we cannot determine; but perhaps traces of it might be found in the plain separating Iwuy from Villers-en-Cauchie. Carpentier, III, 206, cites a Margaret of Ramecourt, married in the fourteenth century to Jean de Beaumont, who belonged to a patrician family of Cambrai.

The altar-right of Riva, in which the Church of Saint Mary has a share; the altar-right of the village called Strada, whose *sonegia* is twelve denarii.

> **Note: [Col. 0281C] Altar-right of the village of Strada.** There are so many places called Estrées that we do not know to which one this refers; moreover, the list of benefices to which the abbot of Saint-Aubert had the right of presentation contains no designation resembling this one.

The altar-right of Barastra with its dependencies Haplencurth and Rahiercurth.

> **Note: [Col. 0281C] Altar-right of Barastra with its dependencies Haplencurth and Rahiercurth.** Barastre was noted under charter 15. The two dependencies named here are Haplincourt—now in the Pas-de-Calais, canton of Bertincourt, formerly Artois, deanery of Beaumez—and Ruyaulcourt, with the same topographical classification. [Col. 0281D] Haplincourt, having been made a parish, remained in the abbot of Saint-Aubert’s right of presentation; but the benefice of Ruyaulcourt belonged to the cathedral chapter.

The altar-right of Chaum, with its dependency Provilla.

> **Note: [Col. 0281D] Chaum with its dependency Provilla.** Quéant and Pronville in Artois, deanery of Beaumetz, whose benefices were indeed in the abbot of Saint-Aubert’s right of presentation.

The altar-right of Gahuncurth; the chapel at Vitriacum, with arable land.

> **Note: [Col. 0281D] The chapel at Vitriacum.** The abbot of Saint-Aubert appointed to the castle chapel of Vitry, now the chief town of a canton in the Pas-de-Calais, on the Scarpe, a place famous under the Merovingian kings. See Gregory of Tours, edition of Messrs. Guadet and Taranne, vol. IV, pp. 52, 169, and 501. In this *History of the Franks*, Vitry is always called *Victoriacum*.

The altar-right of Gavera.

> **Note: [Col. 0281D] Altar-right of Gavera.** Gavre or Gaver, on the Scheldt, 12 kilometres from Gaud, belonged before 1559 to the diocese of Cambrai and the deanery of Aalst. [Col. 0282C] The benefice was always conferred by the abbot of Saint-Aubert.

The altar-right of Aesna, with its dependencies, namely Houlcurt and Grandi Ponte.

> **Note: [Col. 0282C] Altar-right of Aesna with the dependencies Houlcurth and Grandi Ponte.** Esne, canton of Clary; Haucourt, the same canton. Grand-Pont is now only a hamlet between Esne and Lesdain. *Naviam*: Naves; *Scaldeuvrium*: Escaudœuvres. *Guennecurth* is doubtless the same as Galhuncurt, explained above, p. 164. *Ramelias*: Ramillies, canton of Cambrai-West.

Of the wax which the priests of the greater archdeaconry bring on the day of Pentecost, a sixth part shall be assigned to the aforesaid church, both now and from ancient times. At Naviam, thirteen *mansi*; at Scaldeuvrium, two *mansi* and arable land, together with the tithe of that land; at Guennecurth, the allod which Gunhard gave; at Ramelias, five *mansi* and half of the allod which you possess there; at Chementias, *mansi* and an allod.

> **Note: [Col. 0282C] At Chementias.** This name, which elsewhere is written *Chimeniae* or *Kimneiae*, evidently designates a place in the neighbourhood of Boistrancourt and Cattenières, as is sufficiently indicated by the following passage from a bull of Eugenius III dated 1145: “The chapel of Busteronis Curte, with its house; likewise the tithe of Oilard Corbellus, with the tithe of the precen­torship of Saint Gaugericus, from the road of Cambrai at Boisteronis Curtis as far as Besen, and from Chimneis as far as Castinières.” I can see in this region no hamlet [Col. 0282D] or farm recalling this designation, except perhaps the estate of Chantemelle, situated at roughly equal distance from Cattenières and Boistrancourt.

At Reiglencurth, one *mansus* and arable land; at Meevrias, three fields; at Blahercurth, *mansi*; at Seherias, two parts of four *mansi* from the allod which the knight Osto gave; the allod of the village called Manullo, with land, woodland, and everything belonging to that village; at Locheneias, four *mansi* of free allod, and another allod which Doda, wife of Engerannus, and Alaisa, wife of Robert, gave; at Fontanas Fagalae, the allod which Robert of Pulchro Manso gave, with everything belonging to it.

> **Note: [Col. 0282D] Reiglencurth.** Raillencourt, canton of Cambrai-West. *Metvrias*: Moeuvres, canton of Marcoing. *Blahercurth*: Blécourt, canton of Cambrai-West. *Seherias*: perhaps one should read *Deherias*, Deheries, already mentioned above. *Manullo* and *Lochenieas* are uncertain names.

At Arras, in Strata, one brewing-house which Robert the priest, son of Thamardus, gave, with the permission and confirmation of Alvisus, bishop of that city.

> **Note: [Col. 0282D] At Arras in Strata.** The term *Strata* designates a particular section of the city of Arras called l’Estrée, doubtless because it was crossed by one of those great Roman roads known as the chaussées Brunehaut; one of the parishes of that city was called Saint-Jean-en-Lestrée.

At Bantheneias, [Col. 0282A] two *mansi* and arable land; at Roseth in the district of Vermandois, an allod; at Belveverth, property yielding every year three solidi in the currency of Cambrai; likewise the land in the precinct of the church, where the brothers’ garden and workshops are, which Burcardus, bishop of that city, granted and confirmed, and which the aforesaid church shall freely possess with its whole district.

You shall also receive, without contradiction, chrism and the oil of the sick and of catechumens from the Church of Cambrai, according to your ancient and reasonable customs. Therefore let no person whatsoever be permitted to disturb the aforesaid Church of Blessed Aubert, to take away or diminish its possessions, or to harass it with any vexations; but let all things be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of the uses for which they were granted, saving, nevertheless, the due justice and reverence owed to the diocesan.

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to contravene it, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not amend the wrong by appropriate satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honour, recognize himself or herself answerable before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be excluded from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and at the final judgment be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that church may there rest the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at Pisa through the hand of Emeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor, on the second day before the Kalends of June, in the fourteenth indiction, in the year 1137 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the seventh year of the pontificate of Pope Innocent II.

## CCXXXIV. To Alvisus, Bishop of Arras.  
*(A.D. 1136, 1 June.)*

[BALUZE, *Miscellanies*, II, 164.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother ALVISUS, bishop of Arras: greeting and the apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0283B] We have received the letters of your brotherhood with due kindness; and, by apostolic dispensation, we have released our beloved son Nicholas, bishop-elect of Cambrai, who has not yet received sacred orders, both because of the Church’s need and out of regard for your affection and that of the others who more urgently interceded with us on his behalf. It therefore belongs to you, according to the prudence bestowed upon you by God, to labour effectively for the service and advantage of the holy Roman Church, as we confidently expect from you as its devoted son.

Given at Pisa, on the Kalends of June.

## CCXXXV. Privilege for the Abbey of Balneum.  
*(A.D. 1136, 11 June.)*

[*Annals of Camaldoli*, III, col. 311.]

[Col. 0283C]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons JOHN, archpriest, and the canons of Balneum, present and future, for ever.

The authority of our office exhorts us to be zealous for the condition of the Churches and, with the Lord’s help, beneficially to provide for their peace and welfare. For some time ago, beloved son in the Lord John, archpriest, you repeatedly complained to us concerning the injuries and oppressions which, you said, were inflicted upon the Church of Balneum entrusted to you. Among the other burdens which you laid before us, you made grave complaint against the abbot of Trivium, asserting [Col. 0283D] that he was violently taking from the Church of Balneum twelve chapels, together with their tithes, the offerings of both living and dead, and the remaining parochial right.

Accordingly, we sent our messenger into your region, to investigate the matter carefully and to summon both you and the aforesaid abbot sufficiently in advance to appear before us on the first Kalends of May to plead the cause. At that appointed time both parties appeared before us. The aforesaid abbot produced in support of his case a certain document in the name of our predecessor Pope Paschal. On examining it more closely, we discovered plainly that it was suspicious and forged, because certain erasures were found in it, and names had been altered and written in place of others. Yet it is clearer than daylight both from the authorities of the holy canons and from the general custom of the Church [Col. 0284A] that every chapel ought to be subject to its own mother-church and render to it account for tithes and other things belonging to parochial right, since it is manifest that this same mother-church is situated within the estate of blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, and belongs to his dominion by proprietary right.

Having heard the allegations of both sides, we and our brethren thought fit to issue a definitive judgment upon this dispute. But the abbot, wishing to prolong the case and seek an evasion, asked for a longer adjournment, promising that at whatever date we should prescribe he would appear fully prepared for the case and bring certain instruments which he had left at home. Not wishing to appear to act precipitately, [Col. 0284B] we gave him an adjournment until the octave of Saint Martin, directing that in the meantime, with respect to that church—which he acknowledged to belong by right to blessed Peter—he should pay in good faith the portions, offerings, and tithes of those chapels.

At the appointed time the abbot returned to us and produced an old volume in which we could find nothing relevant to the advantage of his cause. When repeatedly questioned by us, he further answered that the aforesaid chapels were situated within the parishes of that same mother-church, adding that the ministers of those chapels were accustomed every year to visit that mother-church with a litany and offerings, and that both the same mother-church, the chapels, and the whole estate of the territory of Balneum belong by right to Saint Peter.

Therefore, having considered the authority of the holy canons and taken counsel with our brethren and with many wise archbishops, abbots, and others who were present, since the aforesaid abbot cannot produce any authentic instrument concerning his acquisition of them, we restore and grant by judgment to you, beloved son in the Lord John, archpriest, and through you to the Church of Balneum, all the tithes of the aforesaid chapels—whose names are these: Saint Saviour, Saint Nicholas, Saint Paul, Saint Apollinaris, Saint Martin, Saint Paternianus, Saint Hilary, Saint Flora, Saint Margaret, Saint Andrew, Saint Blaise, and Saint Angel—and all their parochial right. Thus [Col. 0284D] you shall henceforth possess in these chapels the same authority which you exercise in the others subject to the aforesaid mother-church: namely, to appoint or remove priests, prohibit them from office, restore them to office, and receive the portions due from the offerings of both living and dead, together with any other things belonging to the mother church and to your office. We further grant you authority, according to the institutions of the holy canons, to regulate and administer all tithes collected at any time from the estates of the aforesaid chapels by parishioners, or received from the whole territory of Balneum.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may molest the Church of Balneum in these matters, take away its possessions, retain things taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; rather, all shall be preserved for its beneficial use in their entirety. Moreover, we prohibit any ecclesiastical or secular person from receiving or possessing, without the consent of that same mother-church, in the aforesaid chapels situated within the territory of Balneum, tithes, offerings, or other things belonging to the administration or property of the mother Church of Balneum. If anyone knowingly attempts to oppose this constitution of ours and, having been warned a second or third time, does not correct that presumption by suitable satisfaction, let that person incur the loss of the dignity of office and honour, be excluded from the most sacred Body and Blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, and at the final judgment be subject to severe vengeance.

[Col. 0285B] But upon all who preserve the rights of that Church may there rest the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.

## CCXXXVI. He grants Henry, Patriarch of Grado, the use of the pallium and of the cross borne before him, and confirms the Church’s possessions.  
*(A.D. 1136, 12 June.)*

[UGHELLI, *Italia Sacra*, V, 1120.]

[Col. 0286A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, patriarch of Grado, and to his successors canonically appointed for ever.

The full honour due to the Apostolic See and to the Roman pontiffs is preserved when the dignity conferred upon all Churches is safeguarded. And just as, even with grace favouring us, we ought to confer on no one more than that person deserves, so likewise no one ought, through the prompting of ambition, to diminish what belongs to another by right. Therefore, the greater the prerogative by which you are known to be exalted, the more diligently you should attend to this: that in correcting your subjects reason may have greater force with you than power, and that the good may find you a gentle corrector and the wicked a merciful one. Love persons; pursue vices. Otherwise, if you should choose to act differently, correction may turn into cruelty, and you may destroy what you desire to amend. Thus you must cut away a wound without ulcerating what is healthy, lest, if you apply the iron more deeply than the matter requires, it harm the one whom you hasten to help. Let each element, therefore, be tempered by the other, so that the good may have, in love, something to fear, and the wicked, in fear, something to love.

Accordingly, venerable brother Henry, patriarch, we graciously assent to your requests and fortify by the protection of this present document the Church of Grado, over which, by God’s authority, you are known to preside. Following the authority of our predecessors Pelagius, Alexander, and Urban II, and especially maintaining the tenor of that constitution which our most holy predecessor Leo IX confirmed both by synodal judgment and by a charter of privilege, we grant to you and to your canonically appointed successors patriarchal dignity and confirm the governance of the Church of Grado within those boundaries alone which are known to have been established for that Church by the aforesaid predecessors.

We also grant that a cross may be borne before you, except when you are at Rome or in the presence and company of the Roman pontiff. From the generosity of the Apostolic See we also grant to your brotherhood the pallium, the fullness of the pontifical office, which you are to use within your church at the solemn celebration of Mass on those days on which we do not doubt your predecessors used it: at the Nativity of the Lord, Epiphany, the three feasts of Saint Mary, the Lord’s Supper, Holy Saturday, the Resurrection of the Lord, the Ascension, Pentecost, the Nativity of Saint John the Baptist and of all the Apostles, the feasts of Saint Mark, the protomartyr Stephen, Saint Lawrence, and Saint Maximus, the solemnity of All Saints, and the principal feasts of your church; likewise at the consecration of churches, bishops, and other clergy, and on the anniversary of your own consecration.

We further decree that whatever goods or possessions the Church of Grado now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. We freely confirm to you and your successors churches given to the Church of Grado by religious men and situated in the parishes of that province, so that no bishop, without your consent, may celebrate consecrations in them or forbid divine offices to priests serving the Lord in those places, so long as they remain there. We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever, etc. If anyone hereafter, etc. But upon all, etc. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.  
I, William, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed.

## CCXXXIX. To Gregory, Bishop of Bergamo.  
*(A.D. 1136, 24 July.)*

[UGHELLI, *Italia Sacra*, IV, 455.]

[Col. 0287D]

INNOCENT, etc., to his venerable brother GREGORY, bishop of Bergamo: greeting and the apostolic blessing.

Disputes and controversies are prolonged without end if what has been adjudged is not put into effect. Therefore, by apostolic letters, we command and direct your brotherhood that, as you desire to retain the favour of blessed Peter and of ourselves, putting aside all lukewarmness, you shall cause the judgment which we rendered in the case of Saint Vincent and Saint Alexander to be observed without challenge. If the canons of Saint Vincent should refuse obedience, let the force of justice not grow weak: exclude the disobedient from entering the churches, [Col. 0288A] and forbid the celebration of divine offices in their churches.

Given at Pisa, on the ninth day before the Kalends of August.

## CCXL. Privilege for the Church of Blessed Mary of Reno.  
*(A.D. 1136, 27 August.)*

[SAVIOLI, *Bolognese Annals*, I, Appendix, p. 193.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GUIDO, prior, and the brethren professing the regular life in the Church of Blessed Mary of Reno, present and future, for ever.

Whenever a request is made to us that is recognized to accord with reason and propriety, it is fitting that we gladly grant it and afford appropriate support to the petitioners’ wishes. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your reasonable petitions and fortify by the privilege of the Apostolic See the Church of Blessed Mary in which you are devoted to divine service. We decree that the canonical order, which is known to have been established in your church according to the Rule of blessed Augustine, shall be preserved there inviolably for all future time.

Moreover, whatever possessions or goods that same church now justly and canonically possesses, and whatever it may hereafter be able to acquire, through the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, through the Lord’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Further, since, according to the testimony of Holy Scripture, [Col. 0288C] tithes are revenues for needy souls, and religious persons who are accustomed to live by others’ alms or beneficence ought not to suffer burdens upon their own goods, we decree that no one shall dare to demand or receive tithes from you on the produce which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or on your means of sustenance (*nutrimenta*). You may also receive for conversion clerics or laypeople fleeing the world, provided that they are bound by no obligation, and retain them in your community according to the rule of canonical institution.

Let no person, therefore, dare rashly to disturb the same church, take away its possessions, retain things taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations. Rather, let all things be preserved intact for the benefit of the uses for which they were granted, saving nevertheless the due reverence owed to the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to contravene it and, having been warned a second or third time, does not amend the wrong by appropriate satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honour, recognize himself or herself answerable before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be excluded from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and at the final judgment be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there rest the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action [Col. 0289A] and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.  
I, William, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed.  
I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed.  
I, Anselm, cardinal priest, have subscribed.  
I, Littifredus, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina, have subscribed.  
I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed.
