Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb your monastery, remove its possessions, retain those removed, diminish them, or harass it with any molestations; but that all things shall be preserved whole for the benefit of those for whose support and governance [Col. 0317C] they were granted. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person shall hereafter knowingly attempt with rash audacity to contravene this page of our grant, after a second or third warning, unless he makes suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know that he is answerable before divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be excluded from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve their rights to the aforesaid monastery, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

[Col. 0317D] I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Theodewinus, bishop of Santa Rufina. I, Drogo, bishop of Ostia. I, Albert, bishop of Albano. I, Anselm, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina. I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of the title of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Chrysogonus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico.

[Col. 0318A] Given at Pisa through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of March, in the fourteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1136, in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II. [Note: [Col. 0317D] The chronological data are corrupt.]

CCLXVII. Privilege for the Church of Orange. (Year 1137, February 25.)

[Gallia Christiana, I, Instrument 132.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother William, bishop of Orange, and to his successors to be canonically promoted [read: appointed].

Established by the Lord upon the chair of blessed Peter, we ought to love our brother bishops [Col. 0318B] and foster under the protection of the Apostolic See the places entrusted to them. Therefore, venerable brother William, bishop, we grant our assent to your petitions and strengthen, by the page of this present writing, the Church of Orange, over which you preside by God’s authority. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, through grants of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, by the Lord’s working, acquire, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors for ever.

Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: namely, the church of Saint Florentius, with the cemetery and the village [Col. 0318C] called Claustrum, situated within that cemetery; with the marsh; the enclosed field which the countess of Orange, with the consent of her son Raimbald, granted to Blessed Florentius; with its tithes and other possessions; the church of Blessed Eutropius, with tithes of the whole territory of Cadarossa and its possessions; the church of Saint Peter with its tithes and possessions; the churches of Montdragon, Séguret, and Jonquières, with their tithes and possessions; [the churches] of Mornas, Sérignan, Grapontis, Saint-Julian, Derbucio, Guarda, Travaillan, Camaret, Vellaiga, Vacqueyras, Albuna, Durban, Balmes, Albagnano, and Jonqueriis, with their tithes and possessions; and the tithes of Sarriano and of Podio-d’Icardo [Col. 0318D], of Saint-Privat, Causianis, Gausianis, and Aselano; and the church of Saint Genesius with its appurtenances; and all other things which the fraternity of your venerable brother predecessors, the bishops, recovered from the hands of occupiers.

We likewise confirm to you all that the aforesaid church appears to possess through you or through your feudal dependants. Following also the example of our predecessor Pope Calixtus of blessed memory, we decree by apostolic authority that in the aforesaid Church of Orange the episcopal seat shall remain for all future time without objection from the bishop of Tricastin or anyone else. [Col. 0319A] Likewise, that place shall possess its own episcopal parish, in which you and your successors shall have free authority to ordain clerics, consecrate churches and oratories, and administer the other functions belonging to the episcopal office.

Furthermore, we confirm as to be held and possessed peacefully and without any harassment by the aforesaid Church of Orange the boundaries of the parish of Orange, which, by order of the same predecessor of ours, are shown to have been established by your predecessor Berengar, bishop of good memory, in the presence of Atto, formerly archbishop of Arles, and his suffragans, through the testimony of witnesses and documentary charters; and which, at Rome, with Pons, bishop of Tricastin, present, after the reasons on both sides had been diligently investigated by that same Roman pontiff, were approved in the presence of bishops and cardinals. Namely: from the bridge of Abolena, along the royal road running between the two mountains as far as Diganum; and from that bridge, as the water of the Lez rises toward the south, as far as the boundaries of the bishopric of Vaison. [Col. 0319B]

Moreover, let the provisions of the holy canons determine the due portion of tithes and of all offerings made in churches for the living and the dead. Therefore, venerable brother bishop, we prohibit anyone from usurping from you the fourth part of the tithes that belongs to you. Likewise, we decree that no one may presume improperly to appropriate for personal use the revenues of the church that do not belong to him.

[Col. 0319C] Therefore no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid Church of Orange, remove its possessions, retain those removed, diminish them, or harass it with molestations of any kind; but that all things shall be preserved whole for the benefit of those for whose support and governance they were granted. If anyone hereafter knowingly attempts rashly to contravene this page of our constitution, after a second or third warning, unless he makes suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know that he is answerable before divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be excluded from the most sacred Body and Blood of our Lord Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve for that place [Col. 0319D] what belongs to it, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of their action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Angelus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence, have subscribed. I, Litafredus, priest, have subscribed. I, Lucas, priest of the title of Saints John and Paul. Marton, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen. I, Guido, unworthy priest. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca. [Col. 0320A] I, Bernard, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Chrisologus [read: Chrysogonus]. I, Theodevitus, bishop of Santa Rufina. I, Drogo, bishop of Ostia. I, Albert, bishop of Albano. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of the title of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Guiguo, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian. I, Ulbordus, cardinal of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, Chrysogonus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Ivo, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary.

Given at Pisa through the hand of Aymeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Kalends of March, in the fifteenth indiction, [Col. 0320B] in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1137, in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent.

CCLXVIII. To Petronilla, abbess of Fontevraud. (Year 1137, February 28.)

[Pavillon, *Life of Robert of Arbrissel*, p. 627.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughter in Christ Petronilla and her sisters, present and future, in perpetuity.

What accords with reason and is known to accord with honour, it is fitting for us willingly to grant and to bestow appropriate support upon the desires of petitioners. Therefore, beloved daughters in Christ, we graciously assent to your just petitions and strengthen by the page of this present writing, under the protection of the Apostolic See, the monastery [Col. 0320C] of Blessed Mary of Fontevraud, in which you are dedicated to divine service, together with all that pertains to it. We decree that whatever goods and possessions that aforesaid monastery now justly and lawfully possesses, or may hereafter reasonably acquire through grants of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, or offerings of the faithful, shall remain secure and unimpaired both to you and to those who shall regularly succeed you in that same governance.

Among these we have added the following for specification by their proper names: namely, the church of Saint Quentin of Fontaines, with all revenues, possessions, and appurtenances; Haute-Bruyère [Col. 0320D] with its appurtenances, vineyards, and other goods bestowed upon your church by Count Amolmic; the alms or gift granted to you by Count Robert, namely, ten marks of silver to be paid to you each year, etc. Moreover, that you may serve the Lord more peacefully, and that your sacred community may in no way be hindered by the frequent coming and going of people and may thereby be more devoted to this very end, we altogether prohibit by this present writing that any dwellings whatsoever be established around your monastery, and that anyone presume to build or consecrate a church near you, whereby the peace and religious life of your monastery might be disturbed, etc.

Given at Pisa through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Kalends of March, in the fifteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1137.

CCLXIX. At the request of Archbishop Hubert, he confirms the possessions of the Church of Saint Mary of Pisa. (Year 1137, March 5.)

[Ughelli, *Italia sacra*, III, 388.]

[Col. 0321A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HUBERT, archbishop of Pisa, and to his successors to be canonically appointed in perpetuity.

The Church of Pisa, a special daughter of the holy Roman Church, has from ancient times been prompt and devoted in serving blessed Peter and the Roman pontiffs. We have ourselves proved this by manifest indications in our own person, and, during the pressing necessity of the Church, above all our other supporters, we have experienced through certain proofs in fact the devotion [Col. 0321B] of the clergy and people of the city of Pisa. To this is added your own closeness to us, beloved and venerable brother Hubert, archbishop, whom, by a special prerogative, we have graciously granted from the bosom of the Apostolic See to govern the Church of Blessed Mary ever Virgin, over which you preside by God’s authority, and whom we have adorned, as it were with the hands of blessed Peter himself, with the mitre of archiepiscopal dignity.

For all these reasons, we judge that the same house of the aforesaid Mother of God is worthy of greater favour and benevolence, and we strengthen it, with all that pertains to it, by the page of this present writing. First, indeed, we decree that you shall have the authority, in accordance with the enactments of the holy canons, to arrange the tithes of the bishopric of Pisa that belong to it; to ordain worthy persons [Col. 0321C] in the episcopal see and in the aforesaid church of the Mother of God according to the sanctions of the canons; to establish canons there; canonically to correct what requires correction there; and likewise to administer your other parish churches or chapels.

We also decree that whatever possessions and goods the aforesaid church of Blessed Mary now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, through grants of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, with the Lord’s favour, acquire, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and to your successors for ever. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: namely, the castle of Cucilla; the castle and estate of [Col. 0321D] Locenthana; the castle and estate of Saint Lucia; the castle and estate of Monte Calvo; three parts of the castle and hill of Ripasticaria; nine fourteenths of the castle and estate of Bellora and Boccello; a fifth part of the castle of Segalare; two parts of the castle and estate of Plumbino; the judicial fine and fodrum (a provisioning levy) of Vada; the judicial fine and fodrum (a provisioning levy) of Zasignana; the castle and estate of Gari; half the castle and estate of Ceule; half the castle and estate of Lucagnano; the judicial fine and fodrum (a provisioning levy) of Buti; the judicial fine and fodrum (a provisioning levy) of Vico; the estate of Plentina; the judicial fine and fodrum (a provisioning levy) of Saint John of Vena; new and old Sanfa; the episcopal castle of Calche with its estate; the estate of Papiana with its appurtenances; the estate of Avane with its morlo [reading uncertain], cattle-yard, and other appurtenances; the mound from [Col. 0322A] Arno to the pond from the land of the sons of Dodo, and from Castagnolo to the sea, and from the raised place to the sea; one third situated in the pond; the castle and estate of Livorno; the castle and estate of Uriliano, situated near Chiesina; half the castle and estate of Callirile; the castle and estate of Riojacco; and the land of Ubertinga.

Furthermore, we confirm to the aforesaid church of the Mother of God, and no less to its successors, the parish churches belonging to it: namely, the parish church of Calcinaria with the chapel of Saint Angel of Travalda, the chapel of Rupida with the chapel of Planthule, and all other chapels belonging to that parish church; the parish church of Buti with the chapel of Saint Mark of Submonte, with all its other chapels; the parish church of Vico Ausurissole with all its other chapels; the parish church of Saint John of Vena with [Col. 0322B] all its chapels; the parish church of Cassina with all its chapels; the parish church of Saint Cassian with all its chapels; the parish church of Saint Julia with all its chapels; the parish church of Saint Lawrence of the estate with all its chapels; the parish church of Calci with all its chapels; the parish church of Asciano with all its chapels; the parish church of Massazuculi with the chapel of Saint Agatha and Clatri, the chapel of Saint Prosper of Bozzano, and the chapel of Balbano, with all its other chapels; the parish church of Avone with, etc.; the parish church of Pugnano with the chapel of Lajano, with, etc.; the parish church of Rujuno; the parish church of Arena; the church of Saint Nicholas of Patino; the parish church of Livorno; the parish church of Larzenta with, etc.; the parish church of Limone with, etc.; the parish church of Saint Lawrence of Patha with, etc.; the parish church of Saint Angel with, etc.; the parish church of Pomaria and Monte [Col. 0322C] Vaso, with all its chapels; the parish church of Rosignano with, etc.; the parish church of Vada with, etc.; the parish church of Ripabella with the church of Saint Perpetua, the territory of the church of Saint Cassian of Molazzano, and all other chapels belonging to that parish church.

Moreover, so that nothing may be lacking to you for the complete security and confirmation of all these things, we establish for you by apostolic authority, saving of course the right of blessed Peter and the holy Roman Church, everything which belongs by right of ownership to the aforesaid Church of Pisa in the territories of the aforesaid parish churches, or within the boundaries of the following parish churches: namely, the parish church of Trajana, the parish church of Miliana, the parish church of Tripallo, the parish church of Gello in Colline, the parish church of Bibone, and the parish church of Pararini.

[Col. 0322D] Therefore no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid Church of Pisa or remove its possessions. If anyone, therefore, etc.; but upon all, etc. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Theodewinus, bishop of Santa Rufina, have subscribed. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Anselm, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence, have subscribed. I, Gotifredus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint . . ., have subscribed. I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Ivo, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Aquiro, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian, have subscribed. [Col. 0323A] I, Ubaldus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed. I, Chrysogonus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Bernard, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus, have subscribed.

Given at Campiglio through the hand of Americ, cardinal deacon of the holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Nones of March, in the fifteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1138, in the ninth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

CCLXX. To Didacus, bishop of Compostela. (Year 1137, March 10?)

[Flórez, *España sagrada*, XX, 584.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother DIDACUS, archbishop of Compostela, greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0323B] The entire Roman curia and the faithful of our Church have humbly entreated the Apostolic See on behalf of the bearer of this letter, our common son and cleric Aria. We therefore diligently accede to their petitions and send apostolic letters to your fraternity on his behalf, requesting and commanding that you receive him kindly and, for the reverence of blessed Peter and of ourselves, grant him without delay an ecclesiastical benefice with a prebend in the Church of Compostela.

Given at the castle of Bibione, on the sixth day before the Ides of March [i.e. after the Kalends].

CCLXXI. He directs Adalbert, archbishop of Mainz, to protect the household of the monastery of Saint Emmeram of Regensburg against the knight Sigebotus. (Year 1137, March 26.)

[Pez, *Thesaurus Anecdotorum*, I, III, 136.]

[Col. 0323C]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother A., archbishop of Mainz, legate of the Apostolic See, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Gerhard, the bearer of this letter, coming to us complained against the knight Sigebotus that, although he and his kinsmen belong to the household of Blessed Emmeram, that same Sigebotus is attempting to claim them as his own serfs. Therefore, by these apostolic letters, we request and command your fraternity to maintain the aforesaid Gerhard and his kinsmen in their right against the vexations of that same Sigebotus. And if that same Sigebotus should presume to burden them contrary to justice, pronounce due sentence [Col. 0323D] against him.

Given at Viterbo, on the seventh day before the Kalends of April.

CCLXXII. Privilege for the Church of London. (Year 1137, April 8.)

[Rymer, *Foedera, Conventiones, Litterae inter Reges Angliae et Alios*, vol. I, p. 14.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son NORMAN, prior of Christ Church situated within the walls of the city of London, and to his brethren, present and future, in perpetuity.

It accords with the clemency of the Apostolic See to love religious persons with paternal affection and to foster the places entrusted to them under the protection of desired defence. [Col. 0324A] Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your reasonable petitions and strengthen under the patronage of the Apostolic See the church of Christ, in which you are dedicated to divine service.

For we decree that whatever possessions and goods the same church now justly and lawfully possesses, or may hereafter, through grants of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, with the Lord’s favour, acquire, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and to your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: namely, two parts of the revenue from the city of Exeter; the land of Lectuna, which Simon de Molins and his wife Adelina bestowed upon that place for the sake of divine mercy; the land and [Col. 0324B] *soke* of the Anglischecnihte-Gylde (“Guild of English knights”); the church of Bix with its revenues; and the church of Tottenham. Furthermore, whatever churches or lands, outside or within the city of London, have reasonably been bestowed upon you by God’s faithful, or may hereafter be offered, we confirm to you and, through you, to that church by apostolic authority.

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb that church, remove its possessions, retain those removed, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole for the benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving of course the due reverence owed to the diocesan bishop.

[Col. 0324C] If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person shall hereafter knowingly attempt rashly to contravene this page of our constitution, after a second or third warning, unless he makes suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him be excluded from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer; and at the last judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance.

But upon all who preserve the rights of that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Theodewinus, bishop, have subscribed. [Col. 0324D] I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Drogo, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Anselm, cardinal priest, have subscribed. I, Albert, bishop of Albano, have subscribed. I, Hubaldus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed. I, Chrysogonus, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Godefredus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Lucas, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Martin, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen, have subscribed. [Col. 0325A] I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca, have subscribed. I, Bernard, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus, have subscribed.

Given at Viterbo through the hand of Almeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the sixth day before the Ides of April, in the fifteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1137, in the seventh year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

CCLXXIII. Privilege for the hospital of Roncesvalles. Year 1137, May 6.

[Oihenart, *Notitia utriusque Vasconiae, tum Iberiae, tum Aquitaniae*, p. 95.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to all the faithful to whom these letters shall come, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The honour and reverence bestowed upon pious places [Col. 0325B] are without doubt offered to almighty God. For alms—whose meaning is “the work of our God”—if weighed with careful consideration, are not a gift but a loan; and what is ministered to Christ’s poor assists its author in the present age and brings him in the future the reward of eternal recompense. With this intention, our venerable brother Sancho, bishop of Pamplona, in the place called Roncesvalles, built out of devotion a house for receiving the poor and pilgrims, and a church in honour of blessed Mary. We have received it, honourably endowed by that brother of ours and by other devout men, under the protection of blessed Peter the apostle and of ourselves, and have strengthened it with all its goods [Col. 0325C] by apostolic privilege.

Therefore we request and command your charity, and enjoin it upon you for the remission of sins, that you grant appropriate assistance from the gifts bestowed upon you by God for the support of that place. Know that we bestow upon all its benefactors the grace of the entire apostolic blessing, and that we subject those who presume to harass so venerable a place to the sentence of fitting punishment.

Given in the territory of Anagni, on the second day before the Nones of May.

CCLXXIV. He sends letters “to all monasteries adjoining the Church of Cassino” that they are not to obey Rainald, the elected abbot of Cassino, or the brethren. (Year 1137, May.)

[Peter, *Chronicle of the Monastery of Cassino*, book IV, chapter 108 (*Patrologia*, vol. CLXXIII).]

[Col. 0325D]

CCLXXV. To the monks of Morchbach. (Year 1137, June 11.)

[Hund, *Metropolis Salisburgensis*, III, p. 440.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons in Christ, the provost and brethren of the church of Morchbach, greeting and apostolic blessing.

According to the apostolic saying, we ought to attend not only to what is useful to ourselves, but to what is useful to many, that they may be saved; and from our abundance we ought to supply the want of the needy. Moreover, as has been made known to us, the church of Blessed Peter of Undenstorff [Col. 0326A] considers it expedient to have a provost from your community. Therefore, by apostolic letters, we request, command, and direct your whole community that you grant to the brethren of that place one of your brethren whom that church shall request for its governance, and that you by no means hinder their good purpose.

Given at Bari, on the fourth day before the Nones of July.

CCLXXVI. To Walter, bishop of Augsburg.—He directs him to refrain from inflicting molestations upon the monastery of Benediktbeuern, since it is a royal monastery. (Year 1137, June 11.)

[Pez, *Thesaurus Anecdotorum*, III, III, 633, from a Tegernsee manuscript of the twelfth century.]

[Col. 0326B] INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother W., bishop of Augsburg, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our faithful son E., abbot of Benediktbeuern, coming to us asserted that he had suffered many grievances from your fraternity, both because of his deposition and because of the sentence of anathema imposed upon him. Moreover, our glorious son L., the emperor, declares that the abbey of Benediktbeuern is royal, and that this has been recognized by his court, adjudged by the sentence of the princes, and confirmed by imperial privilege.

Therefore we command and enjoin upon your brotherhood that, either personally or through a subordinate, you inflict no further injury or molestation upon the aforesaid abbot or his brethren; rather, permit them to live in peace and serve God. For we do not wish what is known to have been adjudged, after the case had been heard, by the judgment of the princes in the imperial court to be altered, but to be held valid—namely, concerning the estate on which that monastery is situated.

Given at Bari, 3 Ides of July [read: June].

CCLXXVII. To the monks of Benediktbeuern, commanding them, after Abbot Engelschalk has been released from the bond of excommunication, to render him reverence and obedience as their prelate and master. (A.D. 1137, June 15.)

[PEZ, ibid., p. 631.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the monks of Buron Monastery, greeting and apostolic blessing.

As Holy Scripture testifies, he offers acceptable service to the Lord who drives adversity away from the afflicted. Therefore, when our son E., your abbot, came to us and declared that he had suffered many wrongs from our brother W., bishop of Augsburg, both on account of his deposition and on account of the sentence of anathema imposed upon him, we compassionated his oppressions with paternal affection. There is added to this that our glorious son Lothair, the emperor, declares the abbey of Buron to be royal, and asserts that this has been acknowledged in his court, adjudged by the judgment of the princes, and confirmed by an imperial privilege.

Therefore we, whose special concern it is to provide more diligently for the peace of venerable places, command and enjoin upon our brother W., bishop of Augsburg, that he henceforth inflict no injury or molestation upon your aforesaid abbot in goods or even in person, but rather permit both you and him to live in peace and serve God. For we do not wish what has reasonably been adjudged, after the case was heard, by the judgment of the princes in the imperial court—namely, concerning the estate on which the same monastery is situated—to be altered, but to be held valid.

Nor should it escape your notice that we have released your aforesaid abbot from the bond of the above-mentioned excommunication; and we command and enjoin that you render him obedience and reverence as to a prelate and master.

Given at Bari, 17 Kalends of July.

CCLXXVIII. At the request of Abbot Chunrad, he confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of the Savior and St Boniface at Fulda. (A.D. 1137, June 21.)

[DRONKE, *Codex diplomaticus Fuldensis*, 387.]

[Col. 0327B]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son CHUNRAD, abbot of the monastery of our Lord Jesus Christ the Savior and of Saint Boniface, situated beside the bank of the river called Fulda, and to his successors to be regularly appointed in perpetuity.

Although, by the office of the apostolate and benevolence entrusted to us by God, we are debtors to all Churches and ecclesiastical persons, it especially befits us to devote ourselves with more earnest zeal of charity to those which are known to belong, by right and property, to the Apostolic See by a special prerogative. Nor is there doubt that, if we graciously assent to the petitions of our brethren, we shall without doubt find the Lord favorable to our own desires. For this reason, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Chunrad, we grant due and kindly assent to your requests, and strengthen by the privilege of the Apostolic See the monastery of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ and of Boniface, over which, by God’s authority, you preside; first establishing that whatever possessions and whatever goods that venerable place now justly and lawfully holds, or may in future, by God’s favor, acquire through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: namely, the monastery of Saint Andrew the Apostle, called *Exajulum*, situated at Rome beside the church of the holy Mother of God and ever-Virgin Mary called *ad Praesepe*; granted by our predecessor Pope Leo of blessed memory, out of affection, to your predecessor, the religious abbot Hecbert, together with all its heated chambers, dwellings, wine-cellars, and kitchen; with vineyards, gardens, and various kinds of fruit trees; with courtyard, well, and entrance through the great gate from the public road; and generally with everything, both within and outside the city, that justly and rightly belongs to the same monastery.

We also forbid every priest of any Church to usurp for himself any lordship or authority in your same monastery, with the sole exception of our Apostolic See. Nor may the bishop in whose diocese the monastery is situated celebrate the solemnities of Mass there unless invited by the abbot of that place. Furthermore, we decree that the gifts, offerings, and tithes of the faithful shall remain forever firm and inviolate for the same monastery, without opposition from any person. Moreover, we prohibit any woman ever to presume to enter there; and no one may at any time hold a court there or in its other places, nor compel servants or tenants to perform any service for that place, except one whom the abbot has permitted to do so for the benefit of the same venerable house.

Upon the death of you, the present abbot of the place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed over it by any cunning of intrusion or by force, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall, in the fear of God and according to the Rule of Blessed Benedict, provide to be elected. The person elected, however, shall be blessed only by the Roman pontiff.

We further establish that, at suitable times, information shall be given to our ecclesiastical solicitude as to how the monastic order is being directed according to regular observance among the brethren entrusted to your government, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Chunrad, and how fitting concord is being maintained among them by ecclesiastical diligence, lest perhaps—God forbid—under the pretext of this privilege your intention and course of uprightness should in any respect be turned aside from the standard of justice.

Moreover, dearest son, we grant you authority, by our apostolic authority, to preach the word of God; and we grant that both you and your successors shall hold precedence before the other abbots of Gaul or Germany in every place and assembly where you are present. Following the example of our predecessors, we also grant you, by the kindness of the Apostolic See, the use of the dalmatic and sandals in solemn Masses. And, that your devotion toward Blessed Peter and toward ourselves may increase more fully, as an indication of the closer familiarity in which we desire to cherish you in the bosom of the Apostolic See, we grant to you and your successors the right to use the mitre and ring.

If the abbot of the aforesaid monastery should perhaps be accused of any crime, he shall be subject only to the judgment of the Roman See. We have also judged it fitting to add generally to this our ordinance that whatever is known to have been granted to the same Fulda monastery by the authority of our predecessors, kings, or emperors shall remain supported in perpetuity by the authority of the present privilege.

Therefore let no person whatsoever be permitted rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, to take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations. Rather, let all things be kept intact, to benefit in every way the uses of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing this page of our constitution, should presume rashly to act against it, after being warned a second and third time, unless he makes amends by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of the Lord God, our Redeemer Jesus Christ; and let him be subject, at the last judgment, to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that monastery may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

(Signature.) I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. (Bene valete.)

I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian.

Given at Bari through the hand of Luke, cardinal priest, acting in place of Lord Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, 11 Kalends of July, in the fifteenth indiction, in the year 1137 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

CCLXXIX. Concerning the reverence owed to the canons of the Holy Sepulchre. (A.D. 1137, July 18.)

[DE ROZIÈRE, *Cartulaire du Saint-Sépulcre*, p. 5.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brethren F[ULCHER], archbishop of Tyre; JO[HN], bishop of Acre; B[ERNARD], bishop of Sidon; and B[ALDWIN], bishop of Beirut, suffragans of the Church of Tyre: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Then is charity rightly ordered in the Church of the Lord, according to that saying of sacred Scripture, when subjects render obedience and reverence to their prelates, and prelates show themselves not as lording it over the clergy but rather as gentle and benevolent. For if in secular affairs each person’s right and proper rank must be preserved, much more must no confusion be introduced into ecclesiastical arrangements.

For this reason, we exhort your brotherhood in the Lord and, by apostolic authority, command and enjoin that you show due reverence to our venerable brother William, patriarch of Jerusalem, and take care likewise to honor him as befits so great a man. For one who knows himself to be set over others ought not to take it ill that another is set over himself.

Given in the territory of Potenza, 15 Kalends of August.

CCLXXX. To Peter, abbot of Cluny. (A.D. 1137, July 20.)

[*Bibliotheca Cluniacensis*, p. 765.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son PETER, abbot of the Cluniacs: greeting and apostolic blessing.

For the concern and diligence which we have learned that you display toward us and the affairs of Blessed Peter, we give thanks to almighty God and to your devotion. Blessed, therefore, is the Lord God of Israel, who has visited and made redemption for his people. He has also deigned so greatly to magnify his mercy toward us, and has made our journey so prosperous, that from the city of Rome as far as Bari scarcely any city or castle remains which is not subject and obedient to Blessed Peter and to us.

In this we rejoice to see the ancient miracles of the divine hand shining forth: the more Holy Church is seen to be struck beneath the hammer of tribulation, the more highly she is raised up [or: exalted]; and, after the manner of spices, the more she is crushed by blows, the more widely she pours out the fragrance of sweetness.

Indeed, it would have been desirable to us if, as you informed us by letter, we could have had the presence of your person, so that even thus our labors by day and night might, by God’s favor, be relieved. But since the heat of summer, the unwholesomeness of the air, and the frailty of your constitution do not permit this at all, we exhort your charity in the Lord that, setting these matters aside, together with the sacred community of Cluny you persist in the customary prayers, that he may bring to a happy consummation the favor which our Creator has willed thus far to show us; and that, moved by your prayers and those of other religious persons, he may now impose the desired end upon the long sufferings of his bride and of the Christian people, worn down beneath the yoke of that Sicilian tyrant. This, indeed, as we trust in his mercy, will quickly be accomplished.

Furthermore, greeting the aforesaid community through you in the Lord, we commend ourselves and our brethren to your prayers and theirs.

Given in the territory of Potenza, 13 Kalends of August.

CCLXXXI. Bull for Aldo, first abbot of Châtillon. (A.D. 1137, September 20.)

[*Gallia Christiana*, IV, Instruments, p. 170.]

[Col. 0330C]

INNOCENT, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son ALDO, abbot of Saint Mary of Châtillon, and to his successors, etc.

What has been established in the church of the Blessed Mother of God through the grace that inspires it, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Aldo, is acceptable to us; and for this reason we have thought it right to admonish your charity that, after the manner of a good husbandman, you should diligently cultivate the vineyard of the supreme householder entrusted to you, and strive according to your strength to improve it. Since, however, at the exhortation of our fellow-brethren Guillaume, formerly bishop of Langres, and Bernard, abbot of Clairvaux, it has been instituted in the church of Blessed Mary that, when its secular canons die, only regular canons shall be appointed in their place, we likewise approve this; establishing that, upon the death of the secular canons now known to be among you, no one shall be substituted for them except a canon professing the regular life.

We also decree that whatever possessions that place now canonically holds, or may later acquire through grants of pontiffs or gifts of kings and princes, shall remain firm to you and your successors. Let no one therefore, etc.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Drogo, bishop of Ostia. I, Gerard, cardinal of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Anselin, cardinal priest. I, Luke, cardinal priest. I, Martin, cardinal priest. I, Guido, cardinal deacon. I, Chrysogonus, cardinal deacon. I, Ivo, cardinal deacon.

Given at San Germano through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, 12 Kalends of October, in the first indiction, in the year 1138, and in the eighth year of the pontificate of Innocent II.

CCLXXXII. To William, lord of Montpellier.—He asks him, as a special son of the Roman Church, to labor effectively for its honor and advantage, receiving a return from him when time and circumstances require. (A.D. 1137, September 21.)

[D. BOUQUET, *Recueil*, XV, 393.]

[Col. 0331B]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ WILLIAM of Montpellier: greeting and apostolic blessing.

As a mother cannot forget her infant, so neither ought the Roman pontiff to forget the son of his mother; rather, as far as he can and knows how, he ought to cherish him with maternal services. Therefore, having great confidence in your proven devotion, we command by apostolic letters, requesting you, that you labor effectively for whatever you know concerns the honor and benefit of Blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, as his special son; knowing that, when time or circumstance requires, we shall, by God’s favor, do the same in matters concerning you or your friends.

Furthermore, let your belovedness know that we are well through God’s grace, and that we wish the same for you.

Given at San Germano, 11 Kalends of October.

CCLXXXIII. He affirms to Albero, archbishop of Trier, and his successors the primacy of Belgic Gaul. (A.D. 1137, October 1.)

[GUNTHER, *Codex diplomaticus Rheno-Mosellanus*, I, 226.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother ALBERO, archbishop of Trier, and to his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

The distinction and glory of individual Churches, together with the prerogative of every ecclesiastical person, redound to the dignity of apostolic majesty, to the praise and exaltation of the Holy Roman Church. For the Church of Trier, thanks be to God, has from long ago shone gloriously among the other provinces of the German kingdom and has been distinguished by the highest nobility. And you, dearest brother in Christ, Archbishop Albero, have lived so honorably from the first flower of youth, have served the Apostolic See so manfully, and, since assuming the governance of the Church of Trier, have shown yourself so much more powerful and exalted, that you have become a stronger wall for the house of the Lord.

Accordingly, inflamed with affection both for you and for the Church entrusted to you, following in the footsteps of our predecessors John XIII, Benedict VII, Leo IX, and Victor II, Roman pontiffs of holy memory, we strengthen by apostolic authority the dignities granted by them to the Church of Trier and confirmed by imperial charters; and, by this page of the present writing, we confirm to you the primacy of Belgic Gaul in this manner. We establish that whenever a priest, deacon, subdeacon, or any ordinary legate is sent from our chief and Apostolic See for ecclesiastical utility or for holding a synod into Gaul, Belgica, or Germany, you and your successors shall hold precedence among the other bishops after that apostolic legate. But if a legate of the Roman Church is absent, you shall nevertheless have the power and permission, after the emperor or king, to sit, pronounce sentence, and issue synodal judgment.

We also decree, in accordance with what was established in the sacred Council of Chalcedon and renewed by us in general councils, that no king, emperor, advocate, ecclesiastical person, or secular person may seize or plunder the goods of deceased archbishops, priests, or other clerics of the Church of Trier; rather, those goods shall be freely preserved for the use of their successor in accordance with the arrangement of the steward and clergy.

Moreover, out of reverence for the Church of Trier and regard for your person, we too grant you by apostolic authority what was granted by our predecessors of apostolic memory to the archbishops of Trier: the right to ride with a *naccus* [term uncertain] at the stations, and to have the cross borne before you everywhere.

Among all these things, we grant to you and your successors, and confirm by apostolic authority, both generally and specifically, everything that appears to belong to the aforesaid Church of Trier, within the city and outside it: namely, churches with all things belonging to them, whether of regular canons, monks, or virgins, which belong or ought to belong to it by written grants or charters of kings, emperors, or founders of those places; and whatever else, in whatever manner and wherever, that venerable Church possesses or ought to possess.

Therefore let no person whatsoever rashly disturb your person, that of your successors, or the Church of Trier in respect of this our grant; nor take away, diminish, or harass your goods by any vexations. Rather, let all be preserved intact for the benefit of yourselves and the poor. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing this page of our constitution, should presume rashly to oppose it, then, after a second and third warning, unless he makes fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor, cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and Lord, our Redeemer Jesus Christ, and subjected at the last judgment to strict vengeance. But upon those who preserve it may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Drogo, bishop of Ostia. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Luke, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul. I, Chrysogonus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico.

Given in the Roman territory through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the Kalends of October, in the first indiction, in the year 1137 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

CCLXXXIV. He appoints Adalbero, archbishop of Trier, legate of the Holy See throughout the archdioceses of Trier, Mainz, Cologne, Salzburg, Bremen, and Magdeburg. (A.D. 1137, October 2.)

[HONTHEIM, *Historia Trevirensis diplomatica*, I, 536.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brethren the archbishops and bishops, and to his beloved sons all abbots, clergy, princes, and people established throughout the provinces of Trier, Mainz, Cologne, Salzburg, Bremen, and Magdeburg: greeting and apostolic blessing.

According to the teaching of the Doctor of the Gentiles, the blessed Apostle Paul, we are debtors, by the office of the apostolate imposed upon us by God, not only to the wise but also to the foolish, and not only to those nearby but also to those far away; since the bonds of Blessed Peter have been entrusted to us, and the care of all Churches situated throughout the regions of the world rests upon us. Thus, those matters which, because of distance or the multiplicity of causes, we cannot settle by our own presence, we may, with the Lord as author, carry out through the vicars of the Apostolic See.

For this reason we have taken our venerable brother Adalbero, archbishop of Trier—a man indeed wise, discerning, and proven in ecclesiastical necessities from early youth—into a share of our solicitude, and have appointed him legate of the Apostolic See in your regions. Therefore we command you and, by the authority of this letter, enjoin that you not find it burdensome to render obedience and reverence to that our brother and to assemble at his summons for the holding of synodal meetings, so that, supported by your counsel and assistance, he may correct what requires correction and, with the Lord’s help, establish what is right.

Given in the Roman territory, on the sixth Nones of October.

[Note: [Col. 0333D] Balderic explains the occasion for this prerogative granted to Albero as follows in the *Life of Albero*: “Albero set out on the Italian expedition with King Lothair with one hundred knights according to the estimate, but in truth with sixty-seven; and after Roger, king of Sicily, had been driven from the confines of Apulia, which he had occupied, and Apulia had been given to Duke Rainulf, and the royal rights of Blessed Peter had been recovered, the emperor, as he was returning, happened in the Trentine valley to fall into the common fate of mortals. The lord archbishop himself, however, was honored by Lord Pope Innocent with the office of legate.” It is clear that all this must be assigned to the year 1137 from the time of Lothair’s death, who ceased to live in this year, on 4 December.]

CCLXXXV. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Mary of Salzburg. (A.D. 1137, October 2.)

[SCHATEN, *Annales Paderbornenses*, I, p. 747.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the monks of the monastery of Sualenberg, present and future, in perpetuity.

The most holy Roman Church, which through Blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, has obtained primacy over all Churches, has mercifully been accustomed to assist all who need his support. For it is fitting that we, who have been taken up for the governance of souls, should protect them both from the wickedness of evil men and fortify them with the patronage of Blessed Peter.

Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we grant assent to your desires and strengthen by this present page of writing the monastery of Sualenberg, founded by the nobleman Widekind in honor of the Blessed Mother of God, and offered by him from devotion, with the counsel and assent of our glorious son Lothair Augustus, emperor of the Romans, and of our brother Adalbert, archbishop of Mainz of good memory, to the governance of the Church of Paderborn. We establish that whatever possessions and goods this place now canonically holds through the gift of our brother Bernard, bishop of Paderborn, or of Widekind himself, and whatever may reasonably be offered to that venerable place by grants of pontiffs, gifts of emperors or princes, or gifts of any faithful persons, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you forever.

Upon the death of you, abbot of the same place, no one shall be placed over it by any craft of intrusion or by force, except one whom the brethren of that monastery by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall, in the fear of God and according to the Rule of Blessed Benedict, provide to be elected. We utterly forbid the appointment there of an advocate except through the election and provision of the abbot and brethren.

Therefore we decree that no one whatsoever may rashly disturb your monastery, take away its possessions, retain possessions taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any molestations; but let all things be preserved intact for your beneficial use. If, however—God forbid—the advocate who at the time holds office in your monastery should prove useless, you may substitute another suitable person in his place, for the honor and benefit of your house. If the bishop in whose diocese your monastery is situated should rashly wish to burden you in any matter, you shall have free power to flee for aid to your mother, the Roman Church, since you stand under her special protection.

If anyone, therefore, in the future, knowing this page of our constitution, should presume rashly to oppose it, then, after a second and third warning, unless he corrects his presumption by fitting satisfaction, let him suffer the loss of his power and honor, be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and Lord, our Redeemer Jesus Christ, and be subject at the last judgment to strict vengeance. But those who preserve for that place what belongs to it shall receive the grace of almighty God and of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Drogo, bishop of Ostia. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian. I, Anselm, cardinal priest. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Chrysogonus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Luke, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul. I, Martin, cardinal priest of Saint Stephen.

Given in the Roman territory through the hand of Innocent, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the sixth Nones of October, in the year 1137 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first indiction, and in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

CCLXXXVI. At the request of Archbishop Conrad, he confirms the boundary between the archbishopric of Magdeburg and the bishopric of Meissen. (A.D. 1137, October 2.)

[DREYHAUPT, *Pagus Neletici*, I, 30.]

CCLXXXVII. At the request of Margrave Chunrad, he receives under protection the convent of Saint John at Gerbstedt and confirms its privileges. (A.D. 1137, October 3.)

[Col. 0335D] [KREYZIG, *Beiträge*, II, 349.]

CCLXXXVIII. He entrusts the church of Saint Pantaleon to the Church of Saint Fridianus at Lucca, and confirms its tithes from the estate of Loveto in the county of Ferrara. (A.D. 1137, November 1.)

[*Bullarium Lateranense*, 17.]

CCLXXXIX. To A., archpriest, and the brethren of the church of Saint Martin at Lucca: he announces that he has entrusted the church of Saint Pantaleon to the brethren of the church of Saint Fridianus. (A.D. 1137, November 1.)

[BALUZE, *Miscellanea*, IV, 589.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons A., archdeacon; A., archpriest; and the other canons of the Church of Blessed Martin at Lucca: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Compassionating with paternal affection the prolonged destitution of the Church of Saint Pantaleon, we have thought fit to come to its aid and make salutary provision for it. Therefore, after consultation with our brethren, we have entrusted that place, by apostolic dispensation, to our beloved sons J. [Jerome], prior, and the brethren of the Church of Saint Fridianus, for the restoration of religious observance and the improvement of the place, so long, namely, as religious life and canonical order flourish among those brethren. This is on condition, however, that they receive the ordinations of clerics and other ecclesiastical sacraments from your bishop, if he is Catholic, enjoys the favor of the Apostolic See, and is willing to confer them without abuse or exaction.

Therefore we command and enjoin that neither you nor any subordinate inflict any molestation upon the said prior and his brethren in this matter, but instead permit them to serve God there quietly and peacefully.

Given at Rome, on the Kalends of November.

CCXC. To B., chaplain of the church of Saint Julian. (A.D. 1131, November 1.)

[BALUZE, ibid., p. 590.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to B., chaplain of the Church of Saint Julian: greeting and apostolic blessing.

By this present writing we command you to obey our beloved son J., prior, and the brethren of the Church of Saint Fridianus, since the Church of Saint Pantaleon has been entrusted to them by us. If you disdain to obey them, know that we have given them leave to remove you from it and to order that place for the honor of God and the welfare of the Church.

Given at Rome, on the Kalends of November.

CCXCI. He confirms to the monastery of Saint Blaise in the Black Forest the cell of Wislikon. (A.D. 1137, November 28.)

[HERGOTT, *Genealogia Habsburgica*, II, p. 157.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son BERTHOLD, abbot of the monastery of Saint Blaise in the Black Forest, and to his successors and brethren to be regularly advanced in perpetuity.

[Col. 0336D]

It is fitting to accede to just and reasonable desires, and it is known to be pleasing to the divine will. For God has set us over the Catholic Church so that we may strive to advance all the faithful generally, but especially those of the household of holy religion, by teaching, example, and authority alike.

Let it therefore be known to all, present . . . how certain noblemen, namely Alger and Adalbero, built a cell on their estate, commonly called Wyslikon, situated in the district of Thurgau, and, for the sake of religion, granted it to God and Saint Blaise as a perpetual inheritance with all its appurtenances: houses, fields, meadows, roads, waters, watercourses, exits and revenues, woods, pastures and common pastures, cultivated and uncultivated land, acquisitions and property to be acquired, and every right that can be spoken or named . . . together with every benefit that can arise or be conceived, and with full common rights in the pastures and common pastures of the surrounding villages—namely Bebikon, Lenginanch, Shnesanch, Medendorf, Siglistorf, Rumiken, and Meliken.

Done lawfully in the monastery of Saint Blaise, in the presence of Rustein, venerable abbot of that place, and many nobles, whose names are these: Reinhard and his brother Walther of Goesenstein; Theoderic of Roetelein; Diethelm of Eun; Bernhard, son of Bil., of Misacho; Bern of Altwise; Volker of Legnach; Hiltibold of Turchin; Diethelnius of Helwile.

In the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1114, six days before the Kalends of January, Friday.

Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, graciously assenting to your requests and also to the prayers of Ulrich, bishop of Constance, and Duke Conrad, advocate of the monastery of Saint Blaise, especially for the good of prosperity, peace, and concord, we confirm to you the same cell, with every right named above, by authority of the Apostolic See. We add this admonition: that the inhabitants of the aforesaid cell are to burden the people of the named villages only in grain and fodder; but in all other respects we acknowledge for them, by apostolic authority, complete and full common rights.

We also will that the exchange made in respect of the withholding of the tithes which were to be paid from that place to the church of Shnesanch shall be established with perpetual firmness. To the same cell we likewise grant, in the name of the Lord, the unrestricted right of baptism and burial.

We establish that no prior other than one whom the abbot judges useful and suitable shall preside over that place; and we establish the same concerning the advocate. Greater matters—namely, the granting of perpetual benefices, the transfer of estates, and similar matters—are reserved to the abbot’s judgment.

Under the full force of this constitution we also will your other cells—namely Ochsenhusen, Berowa, Witnowa, and Burglon—to be included; and we will both these and the churches through which your monks celebrate the divine offices for the people to be free and exempt from diocesan jurisdiction and every exaction.

We also recognize the decree of Pope Honorius II of good memory: namely, that no bishop or legate of the Apostolic See may, without a special authorization of the supreme pontiff, lawfully place your places or monks under interdict or excommunicate them.

If anyone should be opposed in word or deed to this privilege of our authority, unless he makes worthy amendment, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor, excluded from participation in the body and blood of the Lord and from communion with the faithful, and, by authority of the apostles Peter and Paul, subjected to eternal condemnation with Judas in his betrayal of our Lord Jesus Christ. But upon all who piously preserve these things may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, eternal salvation, and rest for their souls. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Gregory, cardinal of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian. I, Chrysogonus, cardinal deacon of Saint Praxedes. I, Ivo, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Aquiro.

Given at Rome through the hand of Luke, cardinal-priest, acting in place of Lord Aimeric, cardinal-deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Kalends of December, in the first indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1138, in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## CCXCII. Privilege for the monastery of St Blaise.  
*(29 November 1137.)*

[GERBERT, *History of the Black Forest*, III, 70.]

[Col. 0338B]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son BERTHOLD, abbot of the monastery of St Blaise in the Black Forest, and to his successors, present and future, in perpetuity.

A desire shown to concern the purpose of religious life and the salvation of souls ought, by God’s authorization, to be fulfilled without delay. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, assenting to your desires, we confirm by the privilege of the Apostolic See the monastery built by brothers of your community on the estate which the noblemen Hawinus, Adhelbert, and Chunradus, with the consent of the late illustrious Duke Welf, gave from devotion to the monastery of St Blaise in the Black Forest, at the place commonly called Ochsenhusen, [Col. 0338C] situated in the district of Ramechgowe, in the county of Bozze.

[Note: At [Col. 0337D], in charter 59 of the *Traditions of St Gall*, it is read that Lanthert and Huito offered to the monastery of St Gall their serfs whom they possessed in the district of Ramockewi: “Done in the village called Louphaim,” [Col. 0338D] on the right bank of the Rotham River, which below Ehingen flows into the Danube. Moreover, the county here called that of Bozze is called the county of Arnulf in Herrgott’s charter, vol. I, p. 58.]

We decree that whatever possessions and goods—in male and female serfs, building-sites, buildings, revenues and returns, fields, acquired or to be acquired, meadows, pastures, waters and watercourses, mills, fisheries, woods, and other appurtenances—which it now canonically possesses, or may hereafter obtain, with the Lord’s help, through grants of popes, gifts of kings, emperors, or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and inviolate to you in perpetuity.

Provided, however, that the same monastery shall at all times remain subject to the community of St Blaise and that, according to its rule or order, the divine office shall be celebrated there, as is known to have been instituted from its very foundation. We also decree that no abbot, powerful person, or any person whatsoever may rashly disturb, seize, retain after seizure, diminish, or harass by any annoyance the property belonging to the aforesaid church of Ochsenhusen; but that all shall be preserved whole for the benefit in every respect of those for whose governance and support they were granted.

We further ordain that no one shall preside as prior over that place [Col. 0339A] except the person whom the abbot of St Blaise shall decide is to be appointed. Concerning the advocate, we likewise decree that, should he prove unsuitable, another suitable person shall be substituted for him at the discretion of the same abbot; and at no time shall any other of those called lesser advocates be maintained there.

If any wish to come there for conversion, the prior or brothers may not receive them into their fellowship without the permission of the abbot of St Blaise. More important affairs—for example, the alteration of buildings, the canonical granting of benefices, and similar matters—shall be reserved to the direction and judgment of the aforesaid abbot.

But if anyone should oppose this our disposition, unless he suitably corrects his offense, he shall be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor and shall be cut off from the most sacred [Col. 0339B] body and blood of God and our Lord Jesus Christ. Those, however, who observe these provisions, through the merits of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul, shall receive from the Lord, the rewarder of all good things, the rewards of eternal life. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church.  
I, Gregory, cardinal-deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus.  
I, Guido, cardinal-deacon of St Adrian.  
I, Grysogonus, cardinal-deacon of St Mary in Portico.  
I, Ivo, cardinal-deacon of St Mary in Aquiro.

Given at Rome through the hand of Luke, cardinal-priest, acting in place of Lord Aimeric, cardinal-deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, [Col. 0339C] on the third day before the Kalends of December, in the first indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1137, in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

[Note: From this it is evident that Innocent had already sometimes begun the indiction before Christmas or the New Year.]

## CCXCIII. He confirms the foundation of the canonry of Klosterneuburg, made by St Leopold, Margrave of Austria, and receives that canonry into the protection of the Apostolic See, etc.  
*(30 November 1137.)*

[PEZ, *Thesaurus Anecdotorum*, VI, I, 322.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons HARTMANN, provost, and the brothers in the cell of St Mary of Neuburg, situated in the diocese of Passau, who profess the canonical life, [Col. 0339D] present and future, in perpetuity.

Although by the office entrusted to us we are debtors to all churches and ecclesiastical persons, we ought nevertheless to devote more earnest care to those whom we know to strive more ardently for the service of almighty God and the observance of regular order. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests; and we receive under the guardianship and protection of the prince of the apostles himself the church of Holy Mary, Mother of God, offered to the blessed apostle Peter, in which you are occupied in divine service, and confirm it by the privilege of the Apostolic See.

[Col. 0340A] First, we decree that the canonical order known to have been established in that place according to the Rule of blessed Augustine shall be preserved there in perpetuity in future times. We also ratify by this present document the goods and possessions which the same church now reasonably possesses, or may hereafter obtain, with the Lord’s help, by grants of popes, gifts of emperors or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means; and in particular the tithes of the adjoining parish of Neuburg, canonically transferred by our brother Reimar, bishop of Passau.

When you, the provost of the same place, or any of your successors dies, no one shall be placed over it by any trickery or force; but only the person whom the brothers by common consent, [Col. 0340B] or the sounder part of the brothers’ counsel, shall judge ought to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Augustine, with the canonical right and reverence due to the diocesan bishop preserved.

You shall receive ecclesiastical sacraments from the diocesan bishop, provided that he is Catholic, enjoys the grace and communion of the Apostolic See, and is willing to administer them to you freely and without any improper condition. Otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what is requested.

Further, assenting to the devout request of your community, we decree by this present ordinance that no advocate of the aforesaid church shall be appointed except from the house and lineage [Col. 0340C] of our beloved son Margrave Leopold, though chosen at your own discretion; provided that no burden or exaction is imposed upon that place for his protection. If he proves unsuitable to the aforesaid church and, after a second or third warning, fails to amend, you and your successors may remove him from such administration and substitute another suitable person.

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, seize its possessions, retain them after seizure, diminish them, or harass it by any annoyance. Rather, all shall be preserved whole for the benefit in every respect of those for whose governance and support they were granted. As a token of this liberty received from the Roman [Col. 0340D] Church, you shall pay one Byzantine coin annually to us and our successors.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowingly acting against this text of our constitution, rashly attempts to contravene it, then, after a second or third warning, if he has not made suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the wrong committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and at the final judgment let him be subject to strict punishment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord [Col. 0341A] Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action, and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.  
I, Anselm, cardinal-priest, have subscribed.  
I, Gregory, cardinal-deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed.  
I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed.

## CCXCIV. To Albero, bishop of Liège. — He announces that he has promoted Arnulf to be abbot of Gembloux and bestowed upon him the gift of blessing, etc.  
*(18 December 1137.)*

[Gallia Christiana, III, Documents 127.]

[Col. 0341B] INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother ALBERO, bishop, and to the chapter of Liège, and likewise to all the monks and people of Gembloux: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The authority of our office urges us to provide with fatherly concern both for those far away and for those close at hand. Therefore we have received with due kindness our beloved son Arnulf, the elect of the monastery of Gembloux, when he came to us; and, at your request, we have promoted him as abbot by our own hands, as it were by the hands of blessed Peter, and, with the due reverence of the church of Liège preserved, have bestowed on him the grace of blessing.

Accordingly, when we send him back to you with the accompanying letters and the favor of the Apostolic See, receive him reverently and install him honorably in the seat of the aforesaid monastery. Since, beloved brother Bishop Albero, our aforesaid son Arnulf has been constituted abbot there, with your consenting support, for the reform of religion in that place, it is fitting that you provide him with counsel and aid in recovering the possessions and property of the monastery of Gembloux which the abbots of that place have disposed of by sale or other alienation without the common consent of its chapter, and that you cause them to be restored to him.

We order that the secular houses recently built in the courtyard of the same monastery and beneath the brothers’ dormitory, which are greatly harmful to religious life, be wholly demolished. If their founders prove contemptuous, do not delay to restrain them by canonical censure.

Furthermore, we command your charity diligently to admonish Count Godfrey of Namur, his son Henry, and Ebaldo of Florennes, their accomplices, who in peacetime on a Friday burned the borough of Gembloux together with the church of St Saviour and plundered and destroyed the villages and estates of that monastery, that they restore what they have taken from the abbot and brothers of the aforesaid place and make satisfaction for the injuries. If this has not been done within forty days after you receive these letters, administer due justice upon them without delay.

Moreover, brother bishop, we command you not to allow the aforesaid abbot to be harassed by the concubine of the late cleric Baldwin concerning the church of St Saviour; instead, cause the revenues received from it since his death, [Col. 0342A] and those of the future, to be rendered in full to that abbot.

Given at Rome, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of January.

## CCXCV. To the archbishops of Reims, Sens, and Tours, whom he admonishes to be gentle and to leave those unjustly oppressed free to appeal to the Apostolic See.  
*(1130–1138.)*

[PEZ, *Thesaurus Anecdotorum*, VI, I, 308.]

INNOCENT Pope II, to R. [REYNALD], archbishop of Reims; H., archbishop of Sens; H. [HUGH], archbishop of Tours; and their suffragan bishops.

Peace and charity then embrace one another reciprocally, and sincerity remains unbroken in mutual affection, when, in accordance with the order of divine dispensation and the distinct ranks of the Church, those of lower rank render reverence to their superiors and those of greater rank devote care to their inferiors. But ecclesiastical order is confused if inferiors rashly presume unlawful things, or if rulers attempt unauthorized acts under a remiss impunity.

For the fabric of the human body and of the divine fellowship remains unimpaired if shepherds keep watch over the flock, seek rather to feed than to dominate the clergy, and subjects prefer to obey humbly rather than insolently to withdraw from subjection. Therefore, lest either part overturn the ordering of the heavenly dispensation, Peter, prince of the apostles, was appointed by the Lord at the head of the Church, that through himself and his successors he might strengthen the brethren, correct errors, [Col. 0342C] and render to each his due rights.

Hence it has also been promulgated by the general law of the Church that greater cases are to be referred to the examination of the Apostolic See and that those oppressed may appeal to it fearlessly; in this matter the holy Roman Church has reserved to itself the privilege of appeal. No one is ignorant how necessary the use of appeal is, since it corrects the injustice and ignorance of judges. Once an appeal has been lodged, all matters shall remain in their existing condition, and nothing shall be changed until a judgment on the appeal has been pronounced by the person to whom appeal has been made.

Moreover, what is blameworthy in laypeople seems criminal in clerics. Indeed, according to the imperial enactments, if ordinary judges decide that appeals are to be rejected, they are fined thirty pounds [Col. 0342D] of gold, and their assessors and officials are fined the same amount unless they have publicly opposed the decision and clearly objected in proper proceedings [perhaps *actis*, “records/proceedings”]. How severe, therefore, must be the punishment of an ecclesiastical judge who rejects the teaching of his mother, the holy Roman Church, and strives to infringe the privilege of blessed Peter, making himself equal to Jesus Christ and ascending above the see of the apostles—the force of justice, which stands ready to avenge every disobedience, does not fail to know.

We therefore exhort your brotherhood in the Lord: as you desire that your dignity be preserved inviolate by the Apostolic See, so be gentle toward your subjects, and henceforth do not attempt in any respect to diminish or infringe the prerogative of hearing appeals. Otherwise, before the [Col. 0343A] Lord we shall be judged negligent, lukewarm, or guilty for allowing such a grave offense to go unpunished. For by the office of the apostolate a necessity has been imposed upon us by God: while providing honorably for greater persons, we must care beneficially, without injury, for lesser ones.

I, Guido, cardinal-deacon of St Adrian, have subscribed.  
I, Drogo, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed.  
I, Bazifredus, cardinal-priest of the title of Vestina, have subscribed.  
I, Luke, cardinal-priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed.  
I, Martin, cardinal-priest of the title of St Stephen on the Caelian Hill, have subscribed.  
I, Chrysogonus, cardinal-deacon of St Mary in Portico, have subscribed.

Given at Rome through the hand of Luke, cardinal-priest, acting in place of Lord Aimeric, cardinal-deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Kalends of December, [Col. 0343B] in the first indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1137, in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## CCXCVI. Privilege for the monastery of Porta, of the Cistercian Order. — No one is to hunt within the district of the monastery.  
*(13 January 1138.)*

[COCQUELINES, II, 233.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son ADELbert, abbot of Porta, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

The petition of a pious will ought to be fulfilled in deed, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth worthily [Col. 0343C] and the requested benefit may unquestionably acquire force. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Adelbert, we gladly assent to your reasonable petitions. By this present document we decree that in the monastery of Porta, over which by God’s authority you are known to preside, the monastic Order instituted there according to the Rule of blessed Benedict and the observance of the Cistercian brothers shall be inviolably observed in all future time.

We also confirm the exchange reasonably made by our venerable brother Udo, bishop of Neuburg, with you and your brothers: namely, the place of Porta, with all its appurtenances, granted to you by that bishop by title of exchange in return for the place of Smolna, where you had previously served the Lord; provided that the same place of Smolna, with all its appurtenances, shall pass to the jurisdiction and use of the aforesaid bishop.

We further decree that whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and reasonably possesses, or may hereafter obtain, with the Lord’s help, by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and inviolate to you and your successors. In order that you may serve almighty God more peacefully, we have thought fit to forbid by this present document any cleric or layperson within your boundaries to dare to engage in hunting or devote attention to similar frivolities.
