We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever [Col. 0344A] may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, seize its possessions, retain them after seizure, diminish them, or harass it by any vexation; rather, all shall be preserved whole for the benefit in every respect of those for whose governance and support they were granted, with the due reverence owed to the diocesan bishop preserved.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts rashly to contravene this text of our constitution and, after a second or third warning, does not correct the offense by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honor, recognize himself or herself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and our Lord Jesus Christ, and be subject at the final judgment [Col. 0344B] to strict punishment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church.  
I, Peter, cardinal-priest of the title of St Susanna, have subscribed.  
I, Gregory, cardinal-deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus.  
I, Gerard, cardinal-priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem.  
I, Guido, cardinal-deacon of St Mary in Portico.

[Col. 0344C] Given at Rome through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal-deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the Ides of January, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1137, in the seventh year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## CCXCVII. To A., archdeacon, and A., archpriest, of the church of Lucca.  
*(23 January 1138.)*

[BALUZE, *Miscellanies*, IV, 590.]

INNOCENT, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons A., archdeacon, and A., archpriest of the church of Lucca: greeting and apostolic blessing.

You do not doubt that the care of all churches, and especially of those which belong by right to blessed Peter, pertains to the Roman pontiff by a particular prerogative. We are astonished, however, that, as we have learned, the priests Manfred and Alberic, together with Lambert and Capellus, canons of your church, are wickedly opposing the arrangement which we made concerning the church of St Pantaleon, with the right of St Martin preserved. Since they abuse our patience and seek to kick against the goad, we command and order you strictly to admonish these canons to desist from such harassment and not to presume to inflict any annoyance, either personally or through another person acting under them, upon our beloved sons J., prior, and the brothers of St Fridian, to whom we entrusted that church.

If, within fifteen days after you receive these present letters, the aforesaid [Col. 0345A] canons do not obey your admonitions, from that time we suspend them from their offices and charge you to observe that sentence firmly.

Given at Rome, on the tenth day before the Kalends of February.

## CCXCVIII. To the same persons.  
*(23 January 1138.)*

[BALUZE, ibid.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons A., archdeacon, and A., archpriest of the church of Lucca: greeting and apostolic blessing.

As canonical authority attests, the Apostolic See has the right to judge concerning every church and to dispose matters as it decrees. Therefore we command your affection, with an order, that on the pretext of those oaths which are said to have been made more for the ruin than for the welfare of the church of St Pantaleon, you do not allow injury or molestation to be inflicted upon our beloved sons J., prior, and the canons of St Fridian. If those who made those oaths as unlawfully as imprudently wish to persist in their obstinacy, we shall not be able to refrain from administering full justice with respect to them.

Given at Rome, on the tenth day before the Kalends of February.

## CCXCIX. He informs Jerome, prior, and the brothers of the church of St Fridian at Lucca concerning the preceding two letters.  
*(23 January 1138.)*

[BALUZE, ibid., p. 591.]

[Col. 0345C] INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Jerome, prior, and the brothers of the church of St Fridian: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We are greatly troubled by the harassment which you endure from any of your opponents concerning the church of St Pantaleon. Accordingly, we have ordered the archdeacon and archpriest of Lucca that, unless the priest Manfred and the others who oppose you in this matter cease from such an attack within fifteen days after receiving our letters, they shall then be suspended from their offices until they make satisfaction. Concerning those also who made those unlawful and imprudent oaths, unless they repent, we shall, with the Lord’s authorization, administer full justice. Henceforth we earnestly commend ourselves and our brothers [Col. 0345D] to your prayers.

Given at Rome, on the tenth day before the Kalends of February.

## CCC. To certain priests and canons of the church of St Martin at Lucca.  
*(January 1138.)*

[BALUZE, as above, p. 590.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to MANFRED and ALBERIC, priests, and likewise to LAMBERT, CAPELLUS, and HENRY, canons of the church of St Martin: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It has come to our ears that you oppose the arrangement which we made concerning the church of St Pantaleon by entrusting it to the canons of St Fridian. Therefore, by apostolic authority, we command and order you [Col. 0346A] in no way to harass the aforesaid brothers further concerning the same matter, but rather to observe without challenge what we have decreed concerning it; otherwise, know that punishment will be exacted upon you as despisers of the decrees of the Apostolic See.

## CCCI. The canons of Cheminon adopt the Cistercian observance.  
*(17 February 1138.)*

[Gallia Christiana, X, Documents 1127.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son STEPHEN, abbot of the monastery of Trois-Fontaines, and to his successors regularly appointed, in perpetuity.

[Col. 0346B] We render praises and thanks to almighty God because He has made the name and manner of life of the brothers of Clairvaux so renowned and conspicuous in various parts of the world that, through their praiseworthy . . . ., religious men themselves also desire to become more religious and strive, according to the Psalmist’s saying, to go “from strength to strength.”

This pleases us, and we confirm it by apostolic authority: the canons of Cheminon have transferred themselves and their place to the monastery of Trois-Fontaines and have resolved henceforth to live under your care and instruction. Since God, being immutable and eternal, does not approve changeable hearts, and with Him there is no change nor shadow of variation, we likewise decree that the aforesaid canons, present or future, shall in no way be permitted at any time to withdraw themselves from your subjection or, on any pretext, to raise their heel against you. Rather, the same place with its appurtenances and the persons then serving the Lord there shall be subject and obedient to you, just as abbeys established according to the Cistercian Rule obey their head.

The annual payment to us and our successors of twelve coins of Châlons is nevertheless reserved. We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb you or your successors concerning this our confirmation or cause you any opposition on that account. But if anyone rashly attempts to contravene this present constitution, [Col. 0346D] then, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his presumption by suitable satisfaction, let him be subject to excommunication. Those who observe it, however, shall obtain the grace of almighty God and of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, etc.

Given at Rome through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal-deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of March, in the first indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1140, in the ninth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## CCCII. Concerning the obedience owed to the patriarch of Jerusalem.  
*(6 March 1138.)*

[ROZIÈRE, *Cartulary of the Holy Sepulchre*, p. 5.]

[Col. 0347A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers F[ULCHER], archbishop of Tyre; R[AIMOND], bishop of Tortosa; G[ERARD], bishop of Tripoli; H . . . ., bishop of Gibelet; B[ALDWIN], bishop of Beirut; B[ERNARD], bishop of Sidon; and JOHN, bishop of Acre: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We do not wish you, brothers, to be ignorant that, if anyone desires above all to please the Lord on earth, he must humbly obey apostolic commands. For assuredly anyone who strives to oppose the commands of blessed Peter or his successors is unworthy of the priesthood. Whoever endeavors to despise or nullify the injunctions or institutions of the Roman Church, which is the first and mother of all churches, shuts to himself the entrance of heaven after death and becomes contemptible while living on earth. For from the abundance of apostolic discipline each church both receives its own dignity and preserves its authority.

Therefore, by apostolic letters, we command and order you to render to our brother W[illiam], patriarch of Jerusalem, as your primate and patriarch, the due submission and obedience, all opposition set aside. The same was also enjoined by our predecessor of blessed memory, Pope Honorius, upon G[William], archbishop of Tyre, [the predecessor] of you, venerable brother F[ulcher], archbishop: namely, [Col. 0347C] submission and obedience. If you prove contemptuous, we shall administer canonical justice upon you.

Given at Rome, on the second day before the Nones of March.

## CCCIII. To John, abbot of St George. — On the reform of the convent of St Gangolf.  
*(12 March 1138.)*

[NEUGART, *Codex Diplomaticus Alemannicus*, II, 70, from the archive of St George.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son JOHN, abbot of St George: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Because, son, as we know and have learned, our predecessor Honorius of happy memory was so intent and diligent upon reforming the religious life [Col. 0347D] of the church of St Gangolf at Ordechdal that, at the persistent request and petition of Count Peter, advocate of that church, and of his wife Ita and their only son Reginald, he strove wholly to reform the religious observance of that church, long fallen into decay, according to the observance of the Rule of St Benedict. Therefore it ought now likewise to possess the support and benevolence of our authority in this matter.

[Note: Alternatively Crouchtal or Kraufthal, in the confines of Lower Alsace, in the diocese of Strasbourg; in Latin, Claustriacum. It was a convent, at the beginning of the twelfth century dedicated to the memory of St Mark by its founder Folmar the Younger, count of Metz, and entrusted to the care of his brother Theocer, abbot of St George in the Black Forest (Meurissius, *History of the Bishops of Metz*, book III, p. 390). Pope Julius III in 1550 united it, along with the monastery of Lixheim, to the College of Wisdom at Heidelberg under Frederick, Count Palatine. The ruins of the old abbey church are still visible in the village of Kraufthal, a possession of the Duke of Zweibrücken.]

[Note: Peter of Luxembourg in Lower Alsace was the son of Frederick, count of Montion, and Agnes of Savoy, and nephew through his brother of Theoderic, count of Montbéliard. See the notice concerning the foundation of the convent of St John in Alsace, 1127, in *Gallia Christiana*, vol. V, Documents, p. 479; Schoepflin, *Alsatian Diplomatic Records*, vol. I, p. 204; Grandidier, *History of Alsace*, supporting documents, no. 608.]

Let it therefore be known to all, future and present, that in this matter, wholly following in his footsteps, we approve, uphold, and confirm his authority in every respect. And therefore we now command what he commanded, decree what he decreed, and establish that all of it shall henceforth remain valid in every respect.

We understand that the reform of that church was accomplished and completed in the following manner and order: Bishop Stephen of Metz, together with his people and clergy, piously consented to it and further gave counsel and aid; and, for the peace of that church, he wholly abstained from the consecration of its abbess itself. Likewise the aforesaid Peter wholly abstained from the election of that abbess and from her investiture, which had been granted to him by hereditary right; he freely transferred everything to God and blessed George and henceforth entrusted it in perpetuity to the will and discretion of the abbot of St George.

Nor is it unknown that the venerable Hatticha, then abbess of that monastery, firmly gave her support in bringing these measures to completion and most devoutly, gratefully, and voluntarily gave her assent out of piety and humility. Thus the church now accepts as a rule through her that if any abbess in future, acting irregularly and with stiff neck, in the manner of secular monasteries, should refuse to submit to that obedience, exposing the goods or estates of the monastery incautiously, she shall be removed at the pleasure of the aforesaid abbot without hope of reinstatement, and another, selected by him in her place, shall be duly received.

[Note: After Hatticha, Agnes governed in 1187; Gertrude of Utzenheim in 1487; Margaret Bartold of Kiuspach in 1546. From the papers of D. Grandidier, author of the *Ecclesiastical History of Strasbourg*.]

What, therefore, as we have said, we know to have been done and established then by our predecessor, we now command, by divine, apostolic, and our own authority, to be maintained perpetually and firmly observed. Commanding, we order it; and by these present letters we specially entrust to you and your successors the supreme governance of that church and the care of souls. To prevent anyone from opposing this commission or presuming in any manner to be its opponent, we not only forbid this under threat of divine and apostolic excommunication, [Col. 0348D] but also subject to divine and apostolic excommunication anyone found to have violated it.

Given at Rome, on the fourth day before the Ides of March.

## CCCIV. Privilege for the monastery of St Martin of Laon.  
*(21 March 1138.)*

[LE PAIGE, *Bibliotheca Praemonstratensis*, p. 450.]

[Col. 0349A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Walter, abbot, and the canons of the church of St Martin, situated in the suburb of Laon, and to their successors there dedicated to divine service, in perpetuity.

For this purpose, the care of the universal Church has been entrusted to us by God, the disposer of all good things: that we may love religious persons and strive by every means to promote religion pleasing to God. For no service is ever rendered acceptably to God unless, proceeding from the root of charity, it has flowed forth from that very fountain of religion. With this consideration, therefore, beloved son in the Lord Walter, abbot, we graciously grant assent to your just petitions; and we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and the safeguarding of the apostolic see the church of Saint Martin over which, by God’s ordinance, you are known to preside, and strengthen it by the authority of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future, God favouring, acquire through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for ever to you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: namely, the vineyards which the church itself possesses at Tiriniacum, Jovia, Mont Antel, Ursellus, Cryptae, and Mont Laon [Col. 0349B–C]; likewise the estates, lands, and cottages which it has at Avains, Verciniacum, Bruris, Makigni, Pomeretum, Morolgis, Vele, Salmunceum, Villa Mariae, and Vorgia. We also confirm the cultivated land called Monstrata, granted to that church by the gift of Geoffrey, with the consent of our dearest son Louis, king of the French, of illustrious memory; the cultivated land of Sormunt; the ovens of Moncel and Verciniacum; the mill called Croslet; a mill-site at Chivy; and another mill-site at Paranni. Further, the estates of Diona, Couerci, Taran, Remicurte, Floricurte, Pusello, and Biauvoir; and one half of the mills of Anisiacum, as these have been confirmed to you by our venerable brother Bartholomew, bishop of Laon [Col. 0349C–D].

We further decree that henceforth none of you or of your successors shall presume, through any rashness, to impair or alter the form and observance of the Rule and the prerogative of religious life which are now observed in the church of Prémontré; rather, each of you, imploring divine assistance, shall labour more diligently that your order may advance from good to better. None of the brethren who have promised stability and obedience in that place may depart; and no one shall dare to retain one who has departed except with letters of commendation. We further ordain that the land lying before the gates of your church as far as the church of Saint Stephen shall, for the peace of the brethren, as hitherto, remain for ever free of every inhabitant.

We also decree that no person may expel from their places brethren who have departed from that church, nor may anyone receive your fugitives; rather, by our authority, we grant you leave to excommunicate those same fugitives. Moreover, so that the integrity of your order may be inviolably maintained both among prelates and among subjects, we decree that, if any abbot who has gone forth from your church departs from the order and custom of the monastery of Laon, the abbot of the said monastery shall admonish him twice or three times concerning his correction. If he appears incorrigible, the diocesan bishop, in the presence and with the testimony of the abbot of Saint Martin, shall without any delay depose the transgressor against his order. The bishop shall return the deposed man to the church of Blessed Martin and shall immediately appoint another suitable man in his place, by the canonical election of the brethren [Col. 0350A–B].

We also grant that the burial-ground of the same place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and final wish of those who have resolved to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated, saving the rights of parish priests. Therefore let no one whatsoever presume to disturb rashly the aforesaid church, to take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with reckless vexations; but let all things be preserved entire for the benefit, in every respect, of those for whose support and governance they have been granted.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this decree of ours, should rashly attempt to act against it, after a second or third warning, unless he has made amends by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know that he stands guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who maintain the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Almeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of April, in the first indiction, in the year 1137 of the Lord’s Incarnation [Col. 0350C–D], and in the ninth year of the pontificate of Lord Innocent II, pope.

### CCCV. To Hugh, Abbot of Prémontré.  
*(Year 1138, 21 March.)*

[LE PAIGE, *Bibliotheca Praemonstratensis*, p. 421.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons HUGH of the Church of Prémontré, and the other abbots and religious men of the same profession: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Just as things once consecrated to God cannot return to secular uses, so those who have vowed to serve God in your places and have bound themselves by the bond of profession cannot transfer to other places without the permission of their prelate. Therefore no bishop, abbot, or prior may receive your professed canons or lay brothers without the free permission of their prelate [Col. 0350D–0351A]. By apostolic authority we likewise prohibit anyone from rashly attempting to retain against your will any persons of your profession. Furthermore, we grant you authority to bind your fugitives under sentence of excommunication until, upon returning, they make satisfaction.

Given at the Lateran, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of April.

### CCCVI. He confirms the possessions of the canons of the Church of Saint Marianus at Gubbio.  
*(Year 1138, 23 March.)*

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, I, 636.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons BENEDICT, provost, and his brethren serving in the church of the cathedral see of Blessed Marianus in the city of Gubbio, present and future, for ever.

A petition of pious intention ought to be fulfilled by a corresponding effect, so that faithful devotion may shine forth commendably and the benefit sought may undoubtedly gain force. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your petitions and strengthen by the document of apostolic privilege the church of Blessed Marianus, in which you are devoted to divine service. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that place now canonically possesses, or may in future, through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, by the Lord’s favour, acquire, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you for ever. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: namely, the parish church of Saint John of the City; the parish church of Saint Mary Serrata; the parish church of Lisciano; the parish church of Saint Mary of Gadiano, with the parish church of Saint Donatus and Saint Virianus; the parish church of Saint Gervasius; and the estate of Lavari, with all other churches and goods belonging to the aforesaid church [Col. 0351B–C].

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid Church of Blessed Marianus, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or trouble it by any vexations whatsoever; but let all things be preserved entire for the benefit, in every respect, of those for whose governance and support they have been granted. If therefore anyone, etc. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have confirmed this with my own hand. I, Peter, cardinal priest of Saint Susanna. I, Bernard, cardinal priest of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Anselm, cardinal priest of Saint Lawrence in Lucina. I, Martin, cardinal priest of Saint Stephen. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint George. I, Guy, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Guy, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian. I, Boethius, cardinal deacon of Saints Vitus and Modestus [Col. 0351D–0352A]. I, Ivo, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Aquiro. I, G. G., cardinal of Saint Angelo. I, Gerard, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Domnica.

Given at the Lateran through the hands of Aimeric, cardinal chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the tenth day before the Kalends of April, in the first indiction, in the year 1137 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the ninth year of the pontificate of Lord Innocent II, pope.

### CCCVII. Privilege concerning churches subject to the Bishop of Paris, etc.  
*(Year 1138, 26 March.)*

[Gallia Christiana, VII, *Instrumenta*, 57.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother STEPHEN, bishop of Paris, and his successors canonically appointed for ever.

[Col. 0352B] The more renowned the noble and glorious Church of Paris is because it is established in the seat of the king of the French, and the more devoted you, venerable brother Stephen, bishop, show yourself by manifest proofs in love and reverence toward blessed Peter and the holy Roman Church, the more readily do we grant the desired assistance in those matters known to concern the honour and benefit of both. Therefore, dearest brother Stephen, assenting to your reasonable petitions, we strengthen for you and your successors, and through you for the Church of Paris, by the privilege of apostolic protection, whatever the Church of Paris now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future, God favouring, acquire by grants of pontiffs, generosity of kings, gifts of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful titles.

Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: namely, the church of Saint Marcellus; the church of Saint Clodoald, with its estate and all appurtenances; the church of Saint Germanus of Auxerre; the church of Saint Eligius; and also the church of Campelli, with its prebends and three parishes, namely Saint Medericus, the Chapel, and the lands belonging to that church—saving, of course, the annual payment to the Church of Sens of a rent of two solidi in the currency current in that land, namely that used in those regions. These aforesaid churches are known to belong to the right and property of the bishop of Paris [Col. 0352B–C].

We also confirm episcopal jurisdiction in the following abbeys and their parishes and all parishioners: namely, in the abbey of Lagny, the abbey of Saint-Maur-des-Fossés, the abbey of Saint Magloire, the abbey of Saint Victor, the abbey of the Valley of Saint Mary, the abbey of Sarneya, the abbey of nuns—that is, Montmartre—and Kala; and further, in the church of Argenteuil.

Moreover, we likewise confirm for you the pact and agreement made between you and our dearest son Louis, king of the French, of illustrious memory, concerning a place situated in the suburb of Paris called Campellus: namely, that one third of the whole revenue of the ditch of that land, whether from rent, purchases, profits, or any other means by which anything may arise from it, shall be paid without any diminution to you and your successors; but the remaining shares shall be rendered to the royal fisc [Col. 0352D–0353A]. And when a provost of the king is appointed over this matter, he shall swear fealty to you and your successors, and yours shall swear fealty to the king and his heirs; and neither, without the other, shall receive or dispose of anything from that land.

We also decree that if any canon of the Church of Paris is promoted to the dignity of a bishopric, his prebend shall freely return to the Church of Paris. We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb you or your successors concerning this confirmation of ours, or take away the possessions of the Church of Paris, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass them by any molestations. But if in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this decree of ours, should rashly attempt to act against it, after a second or third warning, unless he has corrected his presumption by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know that he stands guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of the Lord, our Redeemer Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance [Col. 0353A–B]. But upon all who maintain the rights of that place and church may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, etc.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Aymeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Kalends of April, in the first indiction, in the year 1137 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Innocent II, pope [Col. 0353B–C].

### CCCVIII. Privilege for the Abbey of Alba Ripa.  
*(Year 1138, 27 March.)*

[Gallia Christiana, IV, *Instrumenta*, 169.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his most reverend son in Christ RAINBALD, abbot of the monastery of Alba Ripa, and his successors regularly appointed for ever.

Placed by the Lord’s ordering upon the watchtower of the apostolic see, we ought to love and cherish religious persons with all the greater fatherly affection because we trust that, by their prayers, we shall be assisted with fitting support in carrying out the office of apostleship entrusted to us and shall share in the eternal blessing to come. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord Rainbald, abbot, at the request of our dearest son Bernard, abbot of Clairvaux—through whose religious life and prudence countless benefits have come from the Lord to the holy Church—[lacuna] we graciously assent to your desires and strengthen by the authority of this present document the monastery of Alba Ripa over which, by God’s ordinance, you preside.

We decree that whatever possessions and goods that place now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future, by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, through the Lord’s favour, acquire, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify by name: namely, whatever, out of devotion, was bestowed for the use of the monastery of Alba Ripa by Wilenco, bishop of Langres, of blessed memory, through the hand of the aforesaid abbot of Clairvaux, in the places noted below: Solongereth, Campo Alerii, Ambrariae, Aula, Arcufractum, Rachese, Quince, Morethangiae, and Crille [Col. 0353D–0354A]. This gift is known to have been made not only from what the aforesaid bishop possessed there in his own property and lordship, but also from whatever you could justly acquire from the lands held from him by others under feudal title or in any other manner.

Further, we likewise confirm what the same bishop bestowed upon you, apart from the aforesaid places, throughout all his other surrounding lands: that is, all necessities, freely and without charge, for the use of yourselves, your houses, and your animals—whether grasses, waters, woods, acorns, or any other things; food or drink, honey, hunting, and all other similar things—to be taken or found by you, all your people, or your hired servants. We likewise ratify by similar sanction a similar gift made to you by the nobleman Rainald of Grance. We add the donation which the distinguished man Ebalus, count of Sauz, and Rainald of Grance are known to have made to you from what they possessed within the aforesaid boundaries. And, outside those places, if any things from their property and lordship are necessary for the use of yourselves, your people, or your animals, let them remain secure and inviolate to you [Col. 0354B–C].

Therefore no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery concerning this decree of ours, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any molestations; but let all things be preserved entire for your benefit in every respect. If anyone knowingly attempts to oppose this decree of ours, after a second or third warning, unless he suitably corrects his presumption, let him be subject to excommunication. But those who preserve these provisions shall obtain the grace of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul. Amen, amen, amen.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the sixth day before the Kalends of April, in the first indiction, in the year 1138 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the ninth year of the pontificate of Lord Innocent II, pope [Col. 0354C–D].

### CCCIX. To all the faithful dwelling in the realm of Constantinople.  
*(Year 1138, 28 March.)*

[Eugène de ROZIÈRES, *Cartulaire du Saint-Sépulcre*, p. 86.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to all Latin faithful of God who are in the army of the king of Constantinople or dwell in his land: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0355A] Just as one who makes himself a helper in honourable works shares in the reward, so one who gives assistance to a wicked deed cannot be free from guilt; for equal punishment embraces those who act and those who consent. Catholic and God-fearing men, both from regions beyond the mountains and from Italy, are known to have laboured greatly for the liberation of the Eastern Church and the cleansing of God’s sanctuary, exposing themselves to the diverse dangers of sea and land. At last, by the co-operation of divine grace and not without the shedding of much human blood, it was freed from the servitude and domination of unbelievers and brought under Christian power.

But now, as we have learned, the king of Constantinople, who separates himself from the unity of the Church and is disobedient to blessed Peter, keeper of the keys of heaven, who is prince of the apostles and, after Christ, head and foundation of the Church, is striving to occupy Antioch and the other neighbouring cities and subject them to his domination. Therefore, because it is our duty to gather all the faithful back to the bosom of their mother Church and to prohibit unlawful acts, we ask, admonish, and command all of you, and enjoin this upon you for the remission of sins: if the aforesaid king should presume to occupy or attack the said Antioch or other places held by faithful Christians, you are in every way to withdraw yourselves from his company and service and not give him aid or counsel in so presumptuous an invasion; otherwise, know that you share in his condemnation [Col. 0355A–B].

Given at the Lateran, on the fifth day before the Kalends of April [Col. 0355C].

### CCCX. He transfers the episcopal see of the Church of Roselle to Grosseto.  
*(Year 1138, 9 April.)*

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, X, 268.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother ROLLAND, bishop of Grosseto, and his successors canonically appointed, in perpetual remembrance.

The most holy Roman Church, head and teacher of all Churches, was divinely established by our very Saviour Jesus Christ. Just as, by the special privilege conferred upon it from heaven, it has power, where necessity requires, to establish new bishoprics, so likewise it can unite two into one, divide one into two, and transfer episcopal sees suffering oppression or violence through any tyrannical cruelty to other, safer places. Indeed, blessed Augustine, the distinguished doctor and ruler of the holy Church, allows this to be done for specified reasons: namely, the ferocity of persecutors, difficulty of places, or association with wicked persons. Our predecessors also, who lived in various ages, frequently permitted this same transfer within one and the same diocese to other, more fortified places.

With this dispensation in view, venerable brother Rolland, bishop, because the Church of Roselle is assailed and harassed by the attacks of many robbers dwelling around it, and the people of that place have, through the exigency of sins, been reduced to great desolation and fewness, after taking counsel with our brethren we transfer by apostolic authority the dignity of the episcopal see hitherto held in that city to the city of Grosseto. By the decree of this present privilege we ordain that the same place shall henceforth be adorned with the supreme dignity of an episcopal see [Col. 0355D–0356A].

Therefore no person whatsoever may rashly disturb you or your successors concerning this decree of ours, or alter anything in these matters. Rather, may the city of Grosseto enjoy for ever the dignity of an episcopal see; and may obedience and reverence be humbly rendered to it as to the mother church by all clerics and laity of the diocese of Roselle. If in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this disposition of ours, should rashly attempt to act against it, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his presumption by suitable satisfaction, let him suffer the loss of his power and honour; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of the Lord, our Redeemer Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance.

We further decree that no prejudice shall, by reason of this grant of ours, be inflicted upon privileges granted by the apostolic see to monasteries or other pious places. But upon all who maintain the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen [Col. 0356A–C].

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna, have subscribed. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Anselm, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed. I, Luke, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Martin, cardinal priest of Saint Stephen, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Odo, cardinal deacon at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Guy, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Guy, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian, have subscribed. I, Chrysogonus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Angelo, have subscribed. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in Carcere, have subscribed [Col. 0356C–0357A].

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aymeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Ides of April, in the first indiction, in the year 1138 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the ninth year of the pontificate of Lord Innocent II, pope.

### CCCXI. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Martin of the Fields.  
*(Year 1138, 11 April.)*

[MARRIER, *Historia S. Martini de Campis*, p. 379.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons THEOBALD, prior, and the brethren of the monastery of Blessed Martin in the Fields, present and future, regularly appointed for ever.

[Col. 0357B] With willing mind we strengthen by the protection of the apostolic see those things which are conferred upon pious and religious places by the generosity of bishops and kings. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we confirm, for you and your successors and through you for the monastery of Saint Martin in perpetuity, by this present document, the church of Old Crecy, with its precinct and all its appurtenances, which was bestowed upon you in pious devotion by our venerable brother Burchard, bishop of Meaux, and subsequently confirmed by his successor Manasses. We decree that no person whatsoever may infringe or alter this gift, or rashly act against this confirmation of ours. If anyone should attempt this in audacious presumption, let him incur the wrath of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul [Col. 0357B–C].

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Almeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Ides of April, in the first indiction, in the year 1138 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the ninth year of the pontificate of Lord Innocent II, pope.

### CCCXII. Privilege for the nunnery of Saint Alexander at Parma.  
*(Year 1138, 12 April.)*

[AFFO, *Storia della città di Parma*, II, p. 348, from the archive of the monastery of Saint Alexander at Parma.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughter in Christ AGNES, abbess of the monastery of Blessed Alexander situated within the city of Parma, and to her sisters, present and future, regularly appointed in that place for ever.

Although by the office entrusted to us we must exercise solicitude for all churches and religious places, it is fitting that we be especially zealous for those known to adhere more particularly to blessed Peter and to belong to his right. Therefore, beloved daughter in the Lord Agnes, abbess, we graciously assent to the reasonable petitions of you and your sisters, and receive under the guardianship and protection of the apostolic see the monastery of Blessed Alexander, in which you are devoted to divine service and which indeed belongs to the right of blessed Peter. We strengthen it by the patronage of the apostolic see.

We decree that whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and lawfully possesses, or may in future acquire through grants of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for ever to you, those succeeding you, and through you to that monastery. Among these we have added the following to be recorded by their proper names: within the city of Parma, the church of Blessed Bartholomew with all its appurtenances; at Fabrario, the church of Saint Andrew with all that belongs to it and with its demesne; the lands or possessions which you have at Foligaria; at Fodico, the church of Blessed James with its appurtenances; and at Belena, the church of Blessed Lawrence with all its appurtenances [Col. 0357D–0358A].

We also confirm whatever you possess in lands, vineyards, and houses at Melajanum and Colornium; and, near the same city of Parma, whatever you possess at Meletolum, Baganzola Valeria, and Vicugibuli in lands, vineyards, houses, and demesnes. At Vigorcolum, one enclosed vineyard with other lands and dependent tenants. We likewise confirm whatever you possess at Julinianum and Purpurano, whether in lands and vineyards or in dependent tenants, houses, and other things. By this present document we secure to you what you possess at Vigattuli, Marturani, the basilica of Nola, Moliole, Castello Nuovo, Feline, Vigodemeri, Traversedula, Purilio, Berotto, Cadecomazi, and Noceto, in lands, vineyards, and other things [Col. 0358A–B].

No one shall presume to exact from you a tithe of the labour which you cultivate at your own expense. You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and the ordination of clerics to be promoted to holy orders from the diocesan bishop, provided that he is Catholic, enjoys the favour of the apostolic see, and is willing to supply these things freely and without any improper exaction. Otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer; supported by our authority, he shall grant what is requested.

Upon the death of you, the present abbess of the same place, or of whichever sister succeeds you in the governance of the abbey, no person shall be set over it through any artifice of subreption or violence, except one whom the sisters of that place, or the sounder part of them, elect according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict [Col. 0358C–D]. Furthermore, we decree that the burial-ground of that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and final wish of those who resolve to be buried there, unless they happen to be excommunicated.

Therefore no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but let all things be preserved entire for the benefit in every respect of those for whose governance and support they have been granted. As a token of the liberty received from the Roman Church and that the same monastery belongs to the right of blessed Peter, you shall pay one Byzantine gold coin yearly to us and our successors.

If in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this decree of ours, should rashly attempt to act against it, after a second or third warning, unless he makes suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know that he stands guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of the Lord, our Redeemer Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who maintain the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen [Col. 0358D–0359A].

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Bernard, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Anselm, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed. I, Luke, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Baldwin, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Mary “Fountain of Oil,” have subscribed. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Guy, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Guy, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian, have subscribed. I, Chrysogonus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Hubald, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed. I, Ivo, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Lauro, have subscribed. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in Carcere, have subscribed [Col. 0359A–C].

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Almeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Ides of April, in the first indiction, in the year 1138 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the ninth year of the pontificate of Lord Innocent II, pope.

A lead bull is appended.

### CCCXIII. He confirms the order of Premonstratensian canons in the monastery of Vilthim and its goods, and grants many privileges.  
*(Year 1138, 30 April.)*

[HUGO, *Annales Praemonstratenses*, vol. II, p. 686.]

[Col. 0359D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son MARQUARD, provost of Vilthim, and his successors canonically appointed, in perpetual remembrance.

The care of venerable places admonishes us to give thoughtful consideration to their peace and welfare. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Provost Marquard, we assent to your reasonable petitions and confirm by the present page the Church of Vilthinen, over which, by God’s authorizing, you are known to preside. First, indeed, we decree that the canonical order established there according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine and the observance of the Premonstratensian brethren shall be preserved there inviolate for all time.

[Col. 0360A] We further decree that whatever possessions and goods that same Church now canonically possesses, or may in the future, God being propitious, acquire by grants of popes, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Moreover, we add that whatever goods, whether churches, tithes, or other possessions, our brother Reginbert, bishop of Brixen, has conferred for the use of the canons of the aforesaid church, or whatever may hereafter be bestowed by his successors through their devotion, no bishop succeeding them shall presume to diminish or take away any part thereof.

And so that the provost and brethren of the same place may be freer to devote themselves to the service of almighty God, [Col. 0360B] we decree that henceforth you shall be free and undisturbed from every exaction of temporal things. Upon the death of yourself, now provost of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it by any craft of surreptitiousness or violence, save one whom the brethren of that place, by common consent and the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel shall, according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Augustine, provide to be elected.

You shall receive chrism, holy oil, the consecration of altars or churches, and the ordination of clerics to be promoted to sacred orders from the diocesan bishop, provided that he is Catholic and enjoys the favor and communion of the Apostolic See, and is willing to provide these things without perversity or exaction. Otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic prelate [Col. 0360C] you prefer; supported, indeed, by our authority, he shall grant what is requested.

Therefore let no bishop, nor any person whatever, have the right to disturb the aforesaid Church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but let all things be preserved whole, to benefit your use and that of the poor. We also decree that the burial-ground of that place shall be altogether free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who have resolved to be buried there, unless they happen to be excommunicated.

If, therefore, anyone should rashly attempt to oppose this our constitution, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not correct his presumption by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power [Col. 0360D] and honor; let him know himself to be guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and our Lord, Jesus Christ the Redeemer; and let him be subject, at the last judgment, to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ rest, so that here they may receive the fruit of good works and, before the strict Judge, etc., may obtain [their reward]. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aimeric, deacon-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Kalends of May, in the first indiction, in the year 1138 of the Incarnation of the Lord, and in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CCCXIV. To Conrad, Archbishop of the Church of Salzburg.  
*(In the year 1138, April 30.)*

[HANSISIUS, *Germania sacra*, II, p. 948.]

[Col. 0361A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to our venerable brother CONRAD, archbishop of the Church of Salzburg, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have graciously received the letter sent to us by your brotherhood on behalf of our brother Reinbert, bishop of Brixen. Although an unfavorable report concerning him had reached us, nevertheless, out of charity alone and reverence for your person, we dealt with him rather in apostolic gentleness than in the rigor of justice, and meanwhile sent him back to the seat [Col. 0361B] of his church with the favor of the Holy Roman Church and with our support.

Accordingly, we have thought fit to admonish your brotherhood that, since the ordering of the Church of Brixen especially rests upon you, you should show yourself so diligent and zealous toward that same brother of ours that, with the Lord’s assistance, matters there may be directed in such a way that no loss due to neglect can be imputed either to us or to you.

But concerning the repose or release which you requested from the Apostolic See, we cannot grant your request. Rather, for the remission of your sins we enjoin upon you that you watch over your flock as a good shepherd, and strive to preserve the obedience once undertaken, so that with the Apostle you may be able to say: “I have fought a hard contest, I have completed the course, I have kept the faith”; and, when [Col. 0361C] the Prince of Shepherds appears, you may receive from him an unfading crown. Be solicitous, as you know how, concerning the service of the Church.

Given at the Lateran, the second day before the Kalends of May . . . . . *(The remainder cannot be read.)*

### CCCXV. To Baldwin, Archbishop of Pisa.—He grants various privileges.  
*(In the year 1138, May 1.)*

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, III, 389.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother BALDWIN, archbishop of Pisa, and to his successors canonically promoted, in perpetuity.

Then honor is kept whole for the Apostolic See and the Roman pontiffs when each Church’s own dignity is preserved. For the customary kindness and prudent humility of the Roman Church makes those whom it finds to be devoted and gentle sons more closely bound to itself—some by dignities and honors, others by the prerogative of familiarity and affection. For it is just and reasonable that to the devotion of those whose benefits and services we recall having received, we should take care to respond with willing minds, not in equal measure or equal amount, but through the benevolence of abundant grace.

Therefore, since from the discord and war existing between the cities of Pisa and Genoa there have arisen many slaughters of men and innumerable captivities of Christians, we—whose particular concern it is to provide with solicitude for the salvation of all, both spiritual and temporal—have, for the good of peace and in compensation for bishoprics which, indeed, we learned had been granted in the island of Corsica to the Church of Pisa by our predecessors the Roman pontiffs, received from your predecessor, our brother of good memory the archbishop, two bishoprics in the judicature of Gallura, namely Galtellinensis and Civitatensis. We grant and subject to metropolitan jurisdiction the bishopric of Populonia, together with these two, to you and your successors, and through you to the Church of Pisa; and we have declared you invested with the honor of primacy over the province of Torres. We likewise confirm by the present page the legation of Sardinia, granted by our predecessor Pope Urban to your predecessors, to you and your successors.

Finally, so that the city of Pisa, which through heavenly favor has frequently gained victory over the enemies [Col. 0362B] of the Christian name and subdued many of their cities, may be honored more highly, we grant you and your successors permission to use a white horse with a white *nocco* [uncertain ceremonial covering or ornament] in processions, and to carry the cross—that is, the banner of the Lord—through the provinces subject to you. We also grant your brotherhood the use of the pallium, so that you may enjoy it according to the custom of the Church of Pisa, and at the consecrations of the three bishops in Corsica—namely, of Aleria, Ajaccio, and Sagone—and of the aforesaid two in Sardinia and of the bishop of Populonia, whose metropolitan you are.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts rashly to infringe the page of this our constitution, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not correct the matter by suitable amendment, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power or honor, let him or her be guilty, etc., and cut off from the most sacred, etc. But upon all who preserve the rights of that Church, etc., may they, etc., and before the strict Judge find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.

### CCCXVI. To Oprand, Abbot of Valle Alta.—He confirms to this monastery all goods given by Bishop Gregory and secures them by the privilege of the Apostolic See.  
*(In the year 1138, May 5.)*

[LUPUS, *Codex diplomaticus Bergomensis*, II, 1015, from the archive of the same abbey.]

[Col. 0363B]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son OPRAND, abbot of the monastery of Valle Alta, situated in the parish of Bergamo, and to his successors regularly appointed, in perpetuity.

The care of venerable places admonishes us to think diligently concerning their peace. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Oprand, we graciously assent to the justice of this desire and confirm, by the force of the present privilege, the monastery of Saint Benedict situated in Alta Valle, over which, by God’s authorizing, you are known to preside. We decree that whatever possessions and goods have been canonically conferred upon the aforesaid monastery by our venerable brother Gregory, bishop of Bergamo, with the counsel and assent of his brethren, as well as of the advocate and other worthy men—whether meadows, woods, fields, waters, watercourses, with the uses of lands and streams, or anything else—or may hereafter be lawfully given by him or other faithful servants of God, shall be preserved [Col. 0363C] and remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors, according to the boundaries or adjoining properties contained in the written instrument of that same brother of ours, Bishop Gregory—namely, etc.

Upon the death of yourself, now abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it by any craft of surreptitiousness or violence, except one whom the brethren, [Col. 0363D] by common consent or by the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, shall, according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict, provide to be elected. The person elected shall be blessed and ordained by the bishop of Bergamo who is then in office; and your monastery shall remain under the patronage and protection [Col. 0364A] of that bishop. Therefore let no one, etc.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.  
I, Gerard, priest-cardinal of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed.  
I, Lucas, cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed.

[Col. 0364B] Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aimeric, deacon-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Nones of May, in the first indiction, in the year 1138 of the Incarnation of the Lord, and in the ninth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CCCXVII. He assigns in perpetuity to the canons of Blessed Peter the churches of the holy martyrs John and Paul, Saint Martin, Saint Stephen Major, and Saint Stephen Minor, together with one half of the offerings and goods belonging to certain altars and sacred buildings.  
*(In the year 1138, May 23.)*

[*Bullarium Vaticanum* I, p. 46.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the canons of Saints John and Paul, Saint Martin, Saint Stephen Major, and [Col. 0364C] Saint Stephen Minor, appointed to the service of the church of Blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, both present and future, in perpetuity.

> **Note:** [Col. 0363D] Adrian IV, in a bull issued in 1158 on the fourth day before the Ides of February and to be printed below, calls them “the canons of the basilica of the prince of the apostles and rectors of the four monasteries of Saints John and Paul, Saint Martin, Saint Stephen Major, and Saint Stephen Minor.” In the present diploma Innocent II calls them the canons of these monasteries appointed to the service of the Vatican basilica. The reason for this designation is entirely clear to those who examine the above-mentioned constitutions of Pope Leo IX.

It is evident to all worshippers of the Christian faith that Blessed Peter was established by our Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ himself, as prince of the apostles, and that by heavenly privilege power to bind and loose souls was entrusted to him. Thus it is said to him: “You are Peter, and upon this rock I shall build my Church, and I shall give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven; and whatever you bind on earth shall be bound also in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth shall be loosed also in heaven.” And again: “If you love me, Simon Peter, feed my sheep.”

Therefore we, although unworthy, [Col. 0364D] who are vicars of that same keeper of the keys of heaven and sit in his place in the holy Church of God, ought to cherish under our protection the special ministers and patrimonies of the Apostolic See, and defend them from the attacks of wicked men.

> **Note:** [Col. 0363D] Ancient records sufficiently show that the bishops of Rome formerly called themselves vicars of Saint Peter; [Col. 0364D] several examples occur in this collection of diplomas. Although the supreme pontiffs clearly understood themselves truly to be Saint Peter’s heirs and successors in the highest dignity, nevertheless they firmly believed that the prince of the apostles himself lives perpetually in the Roman Church, to which he poured forth almost his entire teaching together with his blood; that he sits in the same chair, guides the helm of the whole Church, and has never abandoned its governance. Therefore they wished to be regarded as, as it were, vicars, lending him their service. See Peter Constantine, nos. 12 ff., preface to the *Letters of the Roman Pontiffs*.

Accordingly, [Col. 0365A] beloved sons in the Lord, we grant due assent to your petitions with fitting kindness and confirm by the present page the most sacred churches of the blessed martyrs John and Paul, Saint Martin, Saint Stephen Major, and Saint Stephen Minor, assigned for your use and support. We decree that whatever possessions and goods canonically belong to these venerable places, or which you may in the future, God being propitious, acquire by grants of popes, the generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you in perpetuity. Among these we have thought fit expressly to name:

the half of the offerings [Col. 0365B] of the altar of Saint Mary, and of all the possessions, goods, revenues, and houses belonging to the same church of Saint Mary in the Tower;

> **Note:** [Col. 0365C] The eminent Pietro Moretti conjectures that Innocent II consoled by this privilege the ministers of the Vatican basilica, who had suffered much through the cruelty and rapacity of the antipope Anacletus—who plundered the exceedingly rich treasury of the Vatican church, as may be seen in Baronius under the year 1120—part I of *Lucubrations on Priests*, section 5, § 1. Moreover, after Peter Mallius, the Roman canon, Innocent’s distinguished service to the Basilica of Saint Peter was celebrated in the description of that basilica, title 54, where, as a memorial of grateful feeling toward the supreme pontiff, he inserted these words: “He [Innocent II] also drew up a privilege in which he granted to the canons of the Basilica of Blessed Peter one half of all the ministrations of all the altars which are in the church of Blessed Peter and of Saint Mary in the Tower, except the altar of Pope Saint Leo IX.”

also, the half of the offerings of the altar of Saint Gregory and of all things belonging to it;

> **Note:** [Col. 0365D] Gregory IV built an oratory and altar in honor of his predecessor Saint Gregory the Great and transferred to it the remains of that most holy bishop, as the *Liber pontificalis* under Gregory IV and John the Deacon, book IV of the *Life of Saint Gregory I*, chapter 80, relate. That oratory may be seen at the south side of the old basilica in Alpharanus’s ground-plan, no. 85. Concerning offerings customarily made at Saint Gregory’s altar, it is worthy of note that Anastasius, in his account of Benedict III, relates that certain Englishmen who had gone to Rome placed a silver tablet in the oratory of Blessed Pope Gregory built near the Basilica of Saint Peter. There was another, older altar of Saint Gregory I, which Leo III, according to his biographer, covered in the purest gilded silver.  

the half of the offerings of the church of Saint John and of all things belonging to it;

> **Note:** [Col. 0366C] Alpharanus’s plan, no. 30, shows the oratory of Saint John situated on the north side of the old basilica. The Roman canon mentions it in title 41, and gives title 34 the heading: “Concerning the church of Saint John at the Fonts.” Pope Symmachus, most generous toward the Basilica of Saint Peter, made two oratories, one of Saint John the Baptist and one of Saint John the Evangelist; in their confession he placed silver arches and chambers with an income of thirty pounds. These are the words of the *Liber pontificalis* under Symmachus.

the half of the offerings of the church of Saint Petronilla and of all things belonging to it.

> **Note:** [Col. 0366D] This was a splendid church dedicated by Pope Paul I to God, best and greatest, in the name of and with the relics of that holy virgin. Several princes and kings of Gaul, and especially Roman bishops, as may be seen in Anastasius the Librarian, enriched it with very many gifts. Adrian I attached this sacred building to the monastery of Saint Stephen Major, as Vegio attests, book IV, no. 114. Alpharanus accurately delineated it in his ground-plan, letter d; and all who have treated more fully of the Vatican Basilica of Saint Peter have illustrated it in their commentaries.

We therefore decree that absolutely no one may rashly disturb the aforesaid churches regarding these things or any others, take away their possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or wear them down by reckless vexations; but let all things be preserved whole, for every sort of benefit to your use in perpetuity.

If anyone indeed should presume rashly to oppose this our constitution, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not correct his presumption by fitting amendment, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself to be guilty before the divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and [Col. 0366A] blood of God and our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer; and let him be subject at the last judgment to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ rest, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.  
I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed.  
I, Guido, bishop of Tivoli, have subscribed.  
I, Gerard, priest-cardinal of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed.  
I, Anselm, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed.  
I, Lictifred, priest-cardinal of the title of Vestina [Col. 0366B]—that is, Saint Vitalis—have subscribed.  
I, Lucas, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed.  
I, Martin, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Stephen, have subscribed.  
I, Stancius, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Sabina, have subscribed.  
I, Gregory, deacon-cardinal of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed.

> **Note:** [Col. 0366D] The church or deaconry of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, of which Innocent III speaks in letter 102, book II, in Baluze, formerly stood by the Arch of Septimius Severus near the Capitol.

I, Oddo, deacon-cardinal of Saint George, have subscribed.  
I, Guido, deacon-cardinal of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed.  
I, Guido, deacon-cardinal of Saint Adrian, have subscribed.  
I, Boethius, deacon-cardinal of Saints Vitus and Modestus, have subscribed.

I, Grisogonus, deacon-cardinal of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed.  
I, G. G., deacon-cardinal of Saint Angelo, have subscribed.

> **Note:** [Col. 0366D] Namely Gregory de Papa, or de Papareschi, nephew of Innocent II through his brother; he was created deacon-cardinal of Saint Angelo in 1134 or 1135. Consult Ciaconius, *Lives of the Roman Pontiffs and Cardinals*, vol. I, col. 992.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aimeric, deacon-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman [Col. 0367A] Church, on the tenth day before the Kalends of June, in the first indiction, in the year 1138 of the Incarnation of the Lord, and in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CCCXVIII. At the request of Bishop Benedict, he confirms the boundaries of the bishopric of Foligno and the possessions of its Church.  
*(In the year 1138, June 11.)*

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, I, 693.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother BENEDICT, bishop of Foligno, and to his successors canonically appointed, greeting in perpetuity.

The incomprehensible and ineffable mercy of divine power has placed us, by this dispensation of providence, in the administration of the Apostolic See, so that [Col. 0367B] we may endeavor to exercise fatherly care for all churches. Therefore, venerable brother in Christ, Bishop Benedict, we assent with due kindness to your just petition and secure with the privilege of the Apostolic See the Church of Foligno, over which, by God’s authorizing, you are known to preside. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that Church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, God being propitious, acquire by reasonable means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors.

We also decree that all the boundaries of the diocese, as possessed by your predecessors down to the present day, shall be preserved wholly intact for you and your successors in perpetuity. The first side [Col. 0367C] runs from the Timia to the Dead River; the second side, from the Dead River to Palumbus’s spring, and from Saint Stephen’s at the Cross of Saint Martin to Cerreto, and to the stream of Fojano as far as the stream called Griscus. The third side reaches from that Griscus through Corniale of Vaccagna as far as the slope of Mars, thence to the hill of Jupiter, and descends directly as far as the Cross of Saint Maurus. On the fourth side, toward the *dona* [uncertain reading] near Spello, it reaches the aforesaid River Timia.

Moreover, we confirm to you and to the Church of Saint Felician of Foligno the parish church of Saint John of Foroflumini with its churches; the parish church of Saint John of Filecto with its churches; the parish church of Saint Felician of Butino; the parish church of Saint Mary Nova; the parish church of Saint Mary of Foligno with their churches and possessions; [Col. 0367D] the parish church of Saint Valentine; the parish church of Rovelleta; the parish church of Saint Mary of the Rock; the parish church of Saint Mary of Fellonica with their possessions and churches; the parish church of Cassignano; the parish church of Porcarella; and the parish church of Saint Andrew of Orbe, with their churches and appurtenances.

Furthermore, we decree that the castle of Landolina with its estate, the monastery of Saint Peter with its possessions, and the church of Saint Mary of Rignano with all its appurtenances shall always remain under the lordship of you and your successors. We further decree that the canonry of Saint Felician, with all its appurtenances and churches, shall remain under our jurisdiction [Col. 0368A] in such a way that no provost and no canon may be appointed there without the bishop’s assent. A prebend from the canonry shall also be assigned to the bishop whenever he does not wish to dine with the brethren in the refectory.

We likewise decree that the monastery of the Savior, the church of Saint . . . ., the church of Saint Constantius, the church of Saint Abundius, the church of Saint Herculius, and all the churches of the city shall remain under your disposition and ordering according to the ordinances of the sacred canons. In addition, we decree that the church of Saint Christina, the church of Saint Peter of Rotondo, and the canonry of Saint Paternian, with all their appurtenances; the monastery of Saint Stephen; the monastery of Salvino; Saint Martin of Murro; Saint Angelo of Rosaja with all their appurtenances; and the canonries of Saint Martin, Saint Andrew, [Col. 0368B] and Saint Lucy, with all their appurtenances and churches—as likewise all other churches of the bishopric of Foligno—shall remain under our disposition and ordering.

We confirm to you and your successors in perpetuity the revenues from the market, gates, bridges, city roads, and the bishop’s castle, namely that of Saint Felician, just as the Church of Foligno has possessed them hitherto by ancient right and through the generosity of royal liberality. We also confirm in perpetuity to your jurisdiction: the field called Saint Mary’s Field; the field of Pissinale; the field of Uccellano; the field of Vaccaria; the field of Saint Abundius of Filecto; Frigidus Field; the field of Gualdo; all the land of Berard, son of Rico; all the land which Count Acto, son of Lupo, gave to the Church of Saint Felician; and all the land [Col. 0368C] at Spello and Colle. We likewise confirm the bed of the River Topino near the city, to be held in your jurisdiction perpetually; all mills already built there or which may be built in the future; all buildings that will be erected there; and all male and female slaves and free persons belonging to the Church, who shall always remain in the possession of you or your successors. Therefore we decree, etc. If anyone therefore, etc. But upon all, etc. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church.  
Gregory, priest-cardinal of the title of the Holy Apostles, has subscribed.  
Peter, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Susanna, has subscribed.  
Peter, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Marcellus, has subscribed.  
Gerard, priest-cardinal of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem, has subscribed.  
[Col. 0368D] Anselm, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, has subscribed.  
Lucas, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul, has subscribed.  
Gregory, deacon-cardinal of Saints Sergius, has subscribed.  
Guido, deacon-cardinal of Saint Adrian, has subscribed.  
Oddo, deacon-cardinal of Saint George at the Golden Veil, has subscribed.  
Guido, deacon-cardinal of Saints Cosmas and Damian, has subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aimeric, deacon-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Ides of June, in the first indiction, in the year 1138 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

> **Note:** [Col. 0367D] In this diploma, reader, observe that the boundaries of the diocese of Foligno formerly extended more broadly, since they included Saint Mary of Pistia and the Castle of Pignano, which at the present time acknowledge only the jurisdiction of Nocera. [Col. 0368D]

### CCCXIX. To Alvisus, Bishop of Arras.—He announces that he has referred his dispute with the abbot of Saint Vedast to Hugh, Archbishop of Rouen, and other bishops for decision.  
*(In the year 1138, July 3.)*

[BALUZE, *Miscellanea*, II, 164.]

[Col. 0369A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother ALVISUS, bishop of Arras, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have received the complaint which your brotherhood set before us against the abbot of Saint Vedast, and we are greatly troubled by his very presumptuous transgressions. Since we do not permit the crime of simony and so many other grave offenses which he is said to have committed within the Church against religious persons to remain unexamined, we have committed these matters for examination and determination to our venerable brothers Hugh, archbishop of Rouen, Goslenus, bishop of Soissons, Milo, [Col. 0369B] bishop of Thérouanne, and Geoffrey, bishop of Châlons.

For our part, we intend to love and honor your person and the Church entrusted to you, and we do not wish to fail you in justice. We desire that your devotion may rejoice and give thanks to God, because the filth of schism has been driven from the city and the peace of the Holy Roman Church restored by divine providence.

Given at Albano, the fifth day before the Nones of July.

### CCCXX. To the archbishops, bishops, abbots, clergy, princes, and people established throughout the provinces of Trier, Mainz, Cologne, Magdeburg, and Bremen: he announces that Albero, Archbishop of Trier, has been appointed legate of the Apostolic See, and commands them to obey him.  
*(In the year 1138, July 17.)*

[GUNTHER, *Codex diplomaticus Rheno-Mosellanus*, I, 229.]

[Col. 0369C]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brothers the archbishops and bishops, and to his beloved sons all abbots, clergy, princes, and people established throughout the provinces of Trier, Mainz, Cologne, Magdeburg, and Bremen, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The authority and administration of the Church of God, and the care of the Christian people, were entrusted by heavenly privilege by our Savior the Lord Jesus Christ himself to Blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, and to his vicars. For to him the Lord said especially: “When you have turned again, strengthen your brethren” (Luke 22); and: [Col. 0369D] “Whatever you bind on earth shall be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven” (Matthew 16).

With this purpose in view, we who, though unworthy, are established in the Apostolic See and exercise the office of that same keeper of the keys of heaven, desire to provide beneficially for our brethren both near and far, so that, for those to whom we cannot show our own presence, we may minister through our agents the nourishment of life. For this reason, we have associated with our share of responsibility our venerable brother A., archbishop of Trier, a man certainly wise, discerning, and tested from his earliest years in ecclesiastical necessities; and we have appointed him legate of the Apostolic See in your regions. [Col. 0370A] Therefore, by the authority of the present document, we command and enjoin you to render obedience and reverence to that same brother of ours and to assemble, when he summons you, for the holding of synodal councils, so that, relying on your counsel and help, he may be able, with the Lord’s assistance, to correct what requires correction and establish what is right.

Given at Albano, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of August.

### CCCXXI. To William, Patriarch of Jerusalem.—Concerning the diocese of Tyre.  
*(In the year 1138, July 17.)*

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 394.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to WILLIAM, patriarch of Jerusalem, greeting and [Col. 0370B] apostolic blessing.

The more greatly the kindness of heavenly bounty has exalted the Church of Jerusalem in your times, the more fitting it is that your person should be more humane toward its brethren and honor with mutual love those who render you obedience. Therefore we command your brotherhood to love and honor, from consideration of brotherly affection, our venerable brother Fulcher, archbishop of Tyre, who obeys you by command of the Holy Roman Church. Carefully ensure that you impose no burden upon him, nor that under pretext of this subjection—which is in fact bestowed upon you and the Church of Jerusalem by the favor of the Apostolic See—the noble and renowned Church of Tyre suffer any loss in its rights or [Col. 0370C] dignity.
