For it is unworthy that the honor which would be rendered to it by Antioch if it obeyed Antioch should be withheld by you or your successors.

Given at Albano, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of August.

### CCCXXII. He receives the Church of the Holy Sepulchre at Jerusalem under his protection and confirms its possessions.  
*(In the year 1138, July 26.)*

[Eugène DE ROZIÈRE, *Cartulary of the Holy Sepulchre*, p. 22.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons PETER, prior, and the brethren professing the canonical life in the church of the Holy Sepulchre, both present and future, in perpetuity.

If the gentleness and generosity of the holy Roman Church ought to furnish fitting aid to all Christians, it is much more fitting that it should bestow this more abundantly upon those who lead the religious life and appear to cleave more closely to almighty God. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, since you have resolved to live according to the Rule of blessed Augustine, and, worshipping in the place where the Lord’s feet stood, you serve in regular observance at his glorious tomb, in which he rested bodily for three days, and at the other most holy places where the Redeemer of the world endured bonds, scourges, the disgrace of the cross, wounds, and death for our salvation, we judge you worthy of greater goodwill and favor and desire to cherish you with paternal affection.

Accordingly, granting due and kindly assent to your petitions, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter the most sacred church of the Holy Sepulchre, in which, diligently attending to divine worship, you continually recall with the eyes of faith the Lord’s Passion and the triumph of his most victorious cross, and also your persons; and we fortify you by the authority of this present document. We decree that all which that church now canonically possesses, and whatever has been justly bestowed upon that place by men of distinguished memory—Duke Godfrey and each King Baldwin, Arnulf, and the other patriarchs—or shall hereafter be reasonably bestowed by patriarchs or other faithful servants of God, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you forever. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names:

namely, the church of the Holy Sepulchre at [Col. 0371B] Brindisi, with its appurtenances; likewise the church situated outside the castle of Barletta, in the honor and name of the same Sepulchre, on the southern side beside the public roads, one of which leads to Canosa and the other to Salpi, with all its appurtenances; likewise the church of the Holy Sepulchre outside the walls of the city of Troia, with all its appurtenances; and the church situated in the suburb of Benevento in honor of blessed Theodore.

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid place or your persons, or take away, diminish, or harass with any molestations the possessions of your church; but that all things be preserved whole for you, to be of use for yourselves and for Christ’s poor, without prejudice, however, to the canonical right and reverence due to the patriarch of Jerusalem. If any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing the text of this our constitution, shall presume rashly to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his presumption by suitable satisfaction, let him incur the loss of his authority and rank and be subject to excommunication. But let those who preserve these things obtain the favor of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.  
I, Giles, bishop of Tusculum, have subscribed.  
I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Apostles, have subscribed.  
[Col. 0371D] I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed.  
I, Anselm, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed.  
I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed.  
I, Ivo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Damaso, have subscribed.  
I, Vassallus, cardinal deacon of Saint Eustace, have subscribed.  
I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Angelo, have subscribed.

Given at Albano, through the hand of Aymeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Kalends of August [26 July], in the first indiction, in the year 1138 of the Lord’s Incarnation [Col. 0372A], and in the ninth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CCCXXIII. On the subjection owed by the Church of Tyre to the Church of Jerusalem.  
*(A.D. 1138, 28 July.)*

[Eug. de Rozière, *Cartulaire du Saint-Sépulcre*, p. 4.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother F[ULCHERO], archbishop of Tyre: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The ordering and administration of the whole Church of God which sojourns on earth has been entrusted to blessed Peter, keeper of the keys of heaven, and to his vicars. Hence it has always been lawful, and always will be lawful, for him, according to the nature of the matter and the time, to divide bishoprics, unite those divided, transfer the rights of kingdoms, establish new metropolitan sees, and assign the subjection of metropolitans to primates according to the moderation of his judgment.

We therefore, following in the footsteps of our predecessors, the Roman pontiffs, decree that the Church of Tyre, which was formerly subject to Antioch, shall be subject to Jerusalem; and by letters and by word of mouth we command you to obey our venerable brother W[illiam], patriarch, as your primate. We therefore forbid the patriarch of Antioch, on this ground, to presume to promulgate against your person a sentence of interdict or excommunication. If he should presume to attempt this, let it be held void and not deserve the name of a sentence; nor may your fraternity inflict any injury or burden upon the patriarch of Jerusalem. [Col. 0372C]

Given at Albano, on the fifth day before the Kalends of August [28 July].

### CCCXXIV. Privilege for the abbey of Sept-Fontaines.  
*(A.D. 1138, 10 November.)*

[Hugo, *Annales Praemonstratenses*, II, p. 495.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son JOHN, abbot of Sept-Fontaines, and to his successors regularly professed, forever.

It befits the clemency of the Apostolic See to lend an ear to the prayers of religious persons and to provide beneficially for their peace and welfare. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot John, we graciously assent to your desires and confirm, by the authority of this present document, the monastery of Sept-Fontaines over which, by God’s gift, you preside. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that venerable place now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter obtain, God willing, by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: namely, from the gift of John of Runiac, Lambert and Hugh his sons, Raeir of Fanon, James, Hugh [lacuna].

Moreover, we confirm by this present decree to your church the mill, court, and workshops necessary for their use, together with the other things mentioned above, which were confirmed to you by our aforesaid Archbishop Rainald. We further add that the canonical order established in the same church according to the Rule of blessed Augustine and the institution of our brother of good memory, Archbishop Norbert, shall be preserved there perpetually in future times. We also decree that no brother of that church, after making profession there, may transfer to another church without your consent and that of the chapter of that place; nor may anyone receive or retain such a fugitive. If, when summoned and canonically warned, he refuses to return, the abbot shall have authority to pronounce canonical sentence against him.

We altogether forbid tithes to be exacted from you on the produce which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense. You shall, however, receive ecclesiastical sacraments from the diocesan bishop, provided that he is Catholic, enjoys the favor and communion of the Apostolic See, and is willing to administer them to you without corruption or exaction. Otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what is requested.

Therefore let no person presume rashly to disturb your present church, take away its possessions, retain things taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any molestations; but let all things be preserved whole for you, to be useful to those for whose governance and sustenance they were granted. If anyone knowingly presumes, with rash audacity, to oppose this our constitution, then, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his presumption by fitting amendment, let him be subject to excommunication. But let those who preserve these things obtain the favor of almighty God and of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul. Amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, etc.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Lucas, cardinal priest acting in place of Lord Aymeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Ides of November [10 November], in the first indiction, in the year 1138 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CCCXXV. He confirms the discipline and rules of the regular canons established throughout the bishopric of Halberstadt.  
*(A.D. 1138, 14 November.)*

[Schöttgen and Kreysig, *Diplomatarium*, II, 696.]

[Col. 0373D]

### CCCXXVI. He receives under protection the convent of Saint Mary at Lamspringe and confirms its privileges and possessions.  
*(A.D. 1138, 14 November.)*

[Koken, *Beiträge zur niedersächsischen Geschichte*, I, 171.]

### CCCXXVII. Privilege for the Church of Hamersleben.  
*(A.D. 1138, 14 November.)*

[Leukfeld, *Antiquitates Katelenburgenses*, vol. I, p. 85.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, [Col. 0374A] to his beloved son THIETMAR, provost—namely, of Hamersleben—and to all the prelates of regular canons established throughout the bishopric of Halberstadt, present and future, forever.

A pious request ought to be fulfilled by the effect that follows the will, so that faithful devotion may shine forth commendably and the benefit requested may assuredly acquire force. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, favorably assenting to your just petitions, we receive under the guardianship and protection of the Apostolic See the churches over which you appear to preside, together with the possessions and goods belonging to them, and confirm them by this present privilege. We decree that whatever possessions or goods—in churches, cultivated or uncultivated lands, vineyards, meadows, common rights (*banni*), mills, woods, pastures, or other things—you now justly and lawfully possess, or may hereafter acquire, with the Lord’s help, by grants of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and, through you, to those same churches.

We further decree that the canonical order which is known to have been established in those churches according to the Rule of blessed Augustine, or which shall, God willing, be established in others, shall be inviolably preserved forever in future times. In these places, indeed, the order or discipline of regular life is to be observed under a stricter rule or discernment, so that, while the profession of canonical life remains intact, the brethren may have freedom not to fall to lower things but always to ascend to more perfect ones.

No canon, after making profession, may lawfully leave your churches and transfer elsewhere, whether from fickleness or for the observance of a stricter life, without the free permission of his provost and chapter. Nor may any bishop, abbot, or prior dare retain one who departs. If any disturbance or discord arises among brethren of your profession, the provosts of the congregations of your brethren shall assemble together; through their effort and diligence, the controversy which has arisen among them shall, if possible, be settled. Otherwise, recourse shall be had to the bishop. If peace cannot be restored even through him, the matter shall be brought as quickly as possible before the Roman pontiff.

Furthermore, to secure your perpetual peace and tranquillity, we decree that, if any ecclesiastical or secular person wishes to burden you or your churches concerning these chapters or other matters, you may avail yourselves of the remedy of appeal. We also wish the provosts of your congregations to meet every year on the Feast of the Exaltation of the Holy Cross, so that, if anything concerning your order needs correction, it may there be decided, with the Lord’s aid, by common counsel. The person entrusted with convening and managing such an assembly shall be chosen jointly. Whatever is there enacted for the correction or improvement of your order shall be observed without contradiction by those subject to it.

Moreover, brethren from your cloisters who have been made provosts in other churches, or shall hereafter be so appointed, if they err in their own conduct, in religious life, or in canonical order, or prove negligent toward their subjects, shall answer and make satisfaction for such offences to the provosts of the cloisters from which they were taken. And if perhaps those brethren are deposed from that office by judgment, or wish to resign it, they shall return to the cloister from which they came and remain in their former obedience.

Further, the provosts and brethren of your profession, who desire to have not a dissimilar but a religious pastor, shall have liberty, without any contradiction, to take part in the election of bishops. Congregations of nuns, whether they have abbesses or not, shall customarily obey the discipline and instruction of men of your profession, proven in life, for the correction of their life and conduct. On the death of any of your provosts, no one shall be appointed in his place except the person whom the surviving provosts decide, by common counsel or by the counsel of the sounder part, ought to be elected. No provost, whether living or dying, may dare to appoint another in his own place.

Secular canons shall likewise not be free to inflict injuries or molestations upon those who, for God’s sake, have chosen poverty in the world and despised riches. If any of them presumes to attempt this, he shall be more severely corrected by his bishop. And since scandals and persecutions frequently arise, by which servants of God are often afflicted and compelled to leave their places, should such events occur, you may carry your movable goods with you and use them in the places where you are. You may also avoid in the sacraments priests who publicly keep concubines or are incontinent, and those convicted or confessed of the Simoniacal heresy, and have no communion with them in these matters.

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb you or your churches in respect of these our constitutions, take away your goods or possessions, retain things taken away, diminish them, or harass you with reckless vexations; but that all things be preserved whole, to be of every benefit for the use of those for whose sustenance and governance they were granted. If in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing the text of this our constitution, shall presume rashly to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his offence by fitting satisfaction, let him lose the dignity of his authority and rank; let him know that he stands guilty before divine judgment for the wrong committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ; and at the final judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all your churches that preserve their rights may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good works and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church.  
I, Gerhard, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem.  
I, Anselm, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina.  
[Col. 0376A] I, Martin, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill.  
I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus.  
I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian.  
I, Christopher, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Humeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of December [14 November], in the second indiction, in the year 1138 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CCCXXVIII. He confirms the discipline, privileges, and possessions of the monastery of Saint John at Halberstadt.  
*(A.D. 1138, 19 November.)*

[Jaffé, *Regesta pontificum Romanorum*, p. 583, with this notice: “In the Magdeburg archive. From Pertz’s papers.”]

[Col. 0376B]

### CCCXXIX. He confirms the judgment of Bishop Atto by which the consuls of Pistoia, despoilers of Church property, had been excommunicated.  
*(A.D. 1138, 4 December.)*

[Zacharia, *Anecdota medii aevi*, p. 211.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to A., venerable brother and bishop, and to his beloved sons, the clergy of Pistoia: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Concerning the injury which, we have learned, has been inflicted upon your clergy and Church by the Pistoiese, we sympathize with your charity with due affection; and both in this and in other matters, as is expedient for you, we wish to offer counsel and aid as to most beloved brothers. Therefore we hold valid the sentence pronounced by our predecessor of blessed memory, Pope Paschal, against the assailants of your Church and its goods; and, by the Lord’s authority, we confirm the sentence which you have already pronounced, or shall hereafter canonically pronounce, against your citizens for so great a presumption and sacrilege.

Given at Rome, on the second day before the Nones of December [4 December].

### CCCXXX. He urges the clergy of Pisa, Pistoia, Florence, Fiesole, Lucca, Volterra, and Siena to publish and enforce the sentence of excommunication pronounced against the consuls of Pistoia.  
*(A.D. 1138, 4 December.)*

[Zacharia, *ibid.*]

[Col. 0376D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the faithful bishops, abbots, clerics, and laymen established throughout the dioceses of Pisa, Pistoia, Florence, Fiesole, Lucca, Volterra, and Siena: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It has been reported to your ears that the consuls of Pistoia have sinned most grievously against their mother Church and, setting aside reverence for God, have stripped her of her treasures. For this reason our venerable brother A., bishop of the same place, has pronounced sentence against them. Therefore, since, according to the saying of Holy Scripture, a brother helping a brother is like a fortified and strong city, and since we ought to regard the evils of our neighbors as our own, we command and enjoin you to stand manfully with our same brother and the clergy of Pistoia in this matter, and throughout your dioceses to observe and firmly cause to be observed the sentence which that bishop has already pronounced, or shall hereafter canonically promulgate, against those sacrilegious men.

Given at Rome, on the second day before the Nones of December [4 December].

### CCCXXXI. Privilege for the church called Gratia Dei.  
*(A.D. 1138, 8 December.)*

[Ludewig, *Reliquiae Manuscriptorum*, XI, 545.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son HENRY, provost of the church called Gratia Dei, and to his brethren, present and future, in perpetual remembrance.

[Col. 0377B] It is fitting for us to grant assent to pious vows and to hear religious men in their requests, since the more frail we are, the more [lacuna] by their prayers. Nor is there doubt that, if we graciously assent to their petitions, we find almighty God favorable in our necessities. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, assenting to your desires, we confirm by the privilege of the Apostolic See the church called Gratia Dei, in which you are occupied with divine service. We decree that the canonical order established there according to the Rule of blessed Augustine and the form handed down by our brother of blessed memory, Norbert, archbishop of Magdeburg, shall in that church be preserved inviolate in future times.

We also decree that no brother, after making profession in your church, may transfer to another place without the permission of the superior and brethren; nor may anyone dare retain one who departs. If such a person, after a second or third warning from his superior, refuses to return, the provost then in office shall have authority to pronounce canonical sentence against him. Since brethren living the common life ought to be maintained by the alms and benefactions of others, we likewise decree that no one may dare exact from you tithes from the produce which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or even from your livestock; nor may anyone ever compel you to pay them.

We further add that all the goods granted to you by our aforesaid brother Norbert, archbishop, and confirmed in writing by his venerable successor Conrad, as well as whatever you now justly and canonically possess or may hereafter obtain, God willing, by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you forever.

Upon the death of you, the present provost of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over that place through any contrivance of deception or violence, except the person whom the brethren, by common consent or by the counsel of the sounder part, shall elect for themselves according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Augustine. Nor shall they be compelled to receive as father or superior a cleric of another profession; rather, they shall freely and harmoniously elect, and make their own provost, one whom they judge tested in conduct and learning within that canonical life and suitable for the office.

That provost shall enjoy the privilege of such freedom granted to him by our venerable brother Archbishop Conrad: namely, that he shall not be burdened by the pastor of the Church of Magdeburg with oppressive exactions on the pretext of any military expedition or other service. But if councils of the holy Fathers are held, when summoned he shall attend and render due honor and reverence to the archbishop.

Therefore no person whatsoever may rashly disturb that same church, take away its possessions, retain things taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but let all things be preserved whole, to be of every benefit for the use of those for whose governance and sustenance they were granted. If anyone hereafter attempts to act against this our constitution, then, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his offence by fitting satisfaction, let him incur the indignation of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul, and be subject to excommunication. But upon those preserving to that place what belongs to it, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good works and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Lucas, cardinal priest acting in place of Lord Almeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the sixth day before the Ides of December [8 December], in the second indiction, in the year 1138 of the Lord’s Incarnation [Col. 0378C], and in the ninth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CCCXXXII. Privilege for the canons of the Church of Porto.  
*(A.D. 1138, 17 December.)*

[Fantuzzi, *Monumenta Ravennatia*, II, p. 117.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son JOHN, prior of the church of Saint Mary in Porto, and to his successors canonically appointed, forever.

It befits apostolic dignity to grant assent to just vows and to hear with kindly ears the prayers of religious persons. Nor is there doubt that, if we graciously support the petitions of God’s servants, we find the Lord merciful in our necessities; so that, just as by divine providence we are called Fathers among God’s people, we may also deserve, through affection expressed in action, beneficially to preside over the faithful.

Therefore, although we ought to provide generally for all ecclesiastical persons, we ought nevertheless to be more diligently concerned for those who are known to devote themselves with greater zeal to the service of almighty God and to shine by a stricter religious observance and uprightness of conduct. With this purpose, beloved son in the Lord, Prior John, we grant due and kindly assent to the petitions of your devotion and confirm by the authority of this present privilege the church of blessed Mary, Mother of God, over which, by God’s gift, you are known to preside, with all its appurtenances.

We decree that whatever possessions or goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, with the Lord’s help, by grants of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors forever. You may receive into conversion in your congregation clerics fleeing from the secular world, without opposition or harassment from any bishop or provost. Nor may any bishop or provost dare prevent you from admitting into your community, by your own act, laypersons from any parishes for conversion to regular discipline, unless they are bound by some legal obligations.

No brother of the same church may, after making profession among you, leave your cloister or house for any reason without the permission of the prior of the church or without the common permission of the community. If any professed cleric or layman leaves your cloister or house and, when warned, refuses to return, the prior of that church then in office shall, by apostolic authority, have power to suspend him from his offices and excommunicate him. No bishop or abbot may presume to receive or retain anyone suspended, interdicted, or excommunicated. We grant all these things to you by apostolic authority, so long as the rule of canonical order, by the Lord’s favor, remains vigorous among you.

Moreover, by our concession you may regularly confer clerical tonsure in your place upon those who wish through regular profession to live the regular life. You may receive the ordinations of your clerics from whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, whenever the Church of Ravenna lacks a bishop or when its bishop is known not to be Catholic. No bishop or episcopal official may dare demand from you tithes of the produce which you gather anywhere by your own labor and expense. We also decree that burial in your sacred places shall be entirely free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated.

In addition, by the authority of this present privilege we decree that your aforesaid church, together with all that belongs to it wherever situated, shall be exempt from every extraordinary public burden. Thus, whenever the archbishop of Ravenna, any other bishop in whose diocese you have a church or possession, or—upon the death of the archbishop—the clerics or laymen of the same church must travel to the Roman pontiff or emperor on any business, they may not dare make any levy upon you from the property of that church in silver, horses, or any other expenses, nor ever impose any burden there by lodging.

Furthermore, if war breaks out and the citizens of Ravenna, or of other cities, or the people of other places make a levy for soldiers, for fortifying a city, or for a castle, we likewise command that your aforesaid church shall be exempt from every exaction. Graciously assenting also to your just petitions, we confirm Aquimolum, with its redemption-right and adjacent lands, outside the gate of Saint Lawrence at Ravenna, where you have constructed a mill beside the bridge which is seen to stand over the water flowing before that gate, on the upper and outer side of the same bridge. It belongs to the right of blessed Peter, subject to an annual payment by your church to us and our successors of one denarius in Luccan currency. Whatever, moreover, has been bestowed upon your church by our venerable brother Walter, archbishop of Ravenna, for the sake of divine mercy, we confirm to you by the authority of this present document.

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away or diminish its possessions, or harass it with any vexations; but let all things be preserved whole, to be of every benefit for the use of those for whose governance and sustenance they were granted. If any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing the text of this our constitution, shall presume rashly to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he makes suitable satisfaction, let him lose the dignity of his authority and rank; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the wrong committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and at the final judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good works and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.  
I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed.  
I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of the Apostles, have subscribed.  
I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus, have subscribed.  
I, Crescentius, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Marcellinus and Peter, have subscribed.  
I, Comes, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Eudoxia, have subscribed.  
I, Anselm, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed.  
I, Guido, unworthy priest of the holy Roman Church, have subscribed.  
I, Gripho, cardinal priest of the title of the Shepherd, have subscribed.  
I, Jero, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Lawrence and Damasus, have subscribed.  
I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.  
I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed.  
I, Vassallus, cardinal deacon of Saint Eustace, have subscribed.  
I, Hubaldus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed.  
I, Grisogonus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed.  
I, Gerard, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Domnica, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Lucas, cardinal priest acting in place of Lord Aymeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of January [17 December], in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1138 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the ninth year of the pontificate of Pope Innocent II.

### CCCXXXIII. Privilege for the abbey of Floreffe, of the Premonstratensian Order.  
*(A.D. 1138, 21 December.)*

[Miraeus, *Opera diplomatica*, IV, 11.]

[Col. 0381A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son GERLAND, abbot of Floreffe, and to his successors canonically instituted, forever.

It befits apostolic dignity to grant assent to just vows and to hear with kindly ears the prayers of religious persons. With this purpose, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Gerland, we grant due and kindly assent to the petitions of your devotion, and we confirm by the authority of this present privilege the church of Floreffe, over which, by God’s gift, you are known to preside, together with all its appurtenances.

[Col. 0381C]

Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: the estate of Meillinga; the estate of Herlemont, with sixty *bonnuaria* and its tithe; the freehold at the chapel; likewise, at that same chapel, the land of Folorin and the land of Arnulf, which you hold from the Church of Lobbes at a rent of two denarii; the estate of Serevilla and half its tithe; and the land which you hold in the valley of Colombine from Walter of Villers, at a rent of seven solidi and four denarii; also a mill on the River Sambre, in the freehold called Avulois, half of which you hold from Gerard the cleric and his brother Godescalc of Morelmeis, at a rent of two solidi, while the other two parts you hold from the church of Blessed Foillan at Fosses and from a certain nobleman Hugh, at a rent of two solidi.

[Col. 0381D]

Likewise, the two mills of Vangir, one at a rent of two solidi and the other rent-free; and the land which you hold from Hugh Multon on this side of the Sambre in your parish; also the estate of Vervis; half the freehold of Timeon; moreover, the hospital house in the town of Wanze, with all its appurtenances, given to blessed Peter by Countess Emissende at an annual payment of one gold piece. Likewise, the tithe and endowment wherever adjoining the church of Floreffe, together with its resident tenants and the other things subject to that possession; also the parish house and the head-tax of the household, which is placed upon the altar; the dependent churches, namely Saint Lawrence of Sartho, Saint Martin of Jodïou, Saint Gertrude of Floreffiolo, and another church of Blessed Martin; likewise the count’s chapel with all its appurtenances, which, together with the aforesaid church of Blessed Mary, were given by Godfrey, Count of Namur. Further, half of Ardenella, thirty *bonnuaria* at Sartum Bernardi, and a third part of the *postula* [reading uncertain].

Likewise we have decreed that you shall not be compelled to give tithes to anyone from the produce which you gather by your own hands or at your own expense, or from your livestock. No one shall dare to alter your order and purpose of living canonically according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine and the institution of the Church of Prémontré, or impose upon you the order of another profession.

[Col. 0382A]

Moreover, none of your brethren who have promised stability and obedience may depart without the permission of their own abbot and chapter; nor may anyone dare retain one who has departed. Likewise, let your church not cease its services because of a general interdict imposed upon the parish, provided only that those known to be interdicted or excommunicated are not admitted.

Furthermore, by apostolic authority we confirm to you the liberty of your church, defined by a privilege of Alexander, Bishop of Liège, and strengthened by the consent of his church: namely, that, just as the parish itself, so also the parish priest shall be subject to the hand of the abbot alone, free from synod and council and from every jurisdiction whatever of archdeacon and dean; nor shall the dean come there except together with the archdeacon.

[Col. 0382B]

You shall also receive chrism, oil, consecrations of altars and churches, and ordinations of clerics from the diocesan bishop, if he possesses the favour of the Apostolic See and is willing to supply them to you freely and without any exaction. Otherwise, receive the same from any Catholic bishop who, supported by our authority, grants what is requested.

Therefore we decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb you or the aforesaid church of Floreffe contrary to this our constitution, or to take away its goods or possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass them with any molestations; but let all be preserved intact, for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted.

[Col. 0382C]

But if anyone, by rash presumption, should presume to act contrary to this our decree, after a second or third warning, unless he correct his offence by suitable satisfaction, let him incur the indignation of Almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul, and be subject to excommunication. But those who preserve these things shall obtain the favour of God and of our Lord Redeemer, and of those same apostles. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Henry, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of January [21 December], in the first indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1138, in the ninth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CCCXXXIV. He confirms the foundation and privileges of the Abbey of Vicogne, of the Premonstratensian religious order, near Valenciennes.  
*(A.D. 1138, 21 December.)*

[Miraeus, *Opera diplomatica*, vol. IV, p. 12.]

[Col. 0382D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son GUARIN, abbot of Casa Dei, in the wood called Vicogne, and to his successors to be canonically appointed in perpetuity.

Whenever something is requested of us which is recognized to accord with reason and propriety, it befits us to grant it willingly and to furnish suitable support to the desires of petitioners.

[Col. 0383A]

Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Guarin, we graciously assent to your just petitions and strengthen by the authority of this present writing the church of Casa Dei, over which, by God’s appointment, you preside, together with all things belonging to it. We decree that whatever possessions or goods that venerable place now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s favour, shall remain secure and inviolate for you and your successors.

Among these, we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: Tiliois, Maisnil, Belmunt, and Hatinies. Furthermore, no one shall dare alter your order and purpose of living canonically according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine and the institution of the Church of Prémontré, or impose upon you the order of another profession.

[Col. 0383B]

Moreover, none of your brethren who have promised stability and obedience may depart without the permission of their own abbot and chapter, nor may anyone presume to retain one who has departed.

If anyone canonically summoned refuses to return, the abbot shall have authority to pronounce sentence against him. Nor shall your church cease divine worship because of a general interdict imposed upon the parish; rather, with excommunicated persons excluded, it shall celebrate the divine offices. Likewise, we decree that you shall not be compelled to give tithes to anyone from the produce which you gather by your own hands or at your own expense, or from your livestock.

[Col. 0383C]

Since, indeed, it more and more befits us to provide for your peace, and since we desire you to be assiduous in divine offices, we likewise decree that neither you, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Guarin, nor any of your successors, may presume to leave, unless perhaps summoned to a synod or upon other business.

Therefore let no person whatsoever rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its goods or possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass them by any molestations; but let all be preserved intact, to benefit in every way those for whose governance and support they were granted. But if anyone, by rash presumption, should presume to act contrary to this our decree, after a second or third warning, unless he correct his offence by suitable amendment,

[Col. 0383D]

let him incur the indignation of Almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul, and be subject to excommunication. But those who preserve these things shall obtain the favour of God and of our Lord Redeemer, and of those same apostles. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Luke, cardinal priest, acting in place of Lord Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of January [21 December], in the first indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1138, in the ninth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CCCXXXV. He receives the Church of Prémontré under the protection of Blessed Peter.  
*(A.D. 1138, 21 December.)*

[Hugo, *Annales Praemonstratenses*, I, p. 11.]

[Col. 0384A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son HUGH, abbot of Prémontré, and to his successors to be canonically appointed in perpetuity.

To grant assent to just requests and to hear with kindly ears the prayers of religious persons is fitting to the apostolic dignity. Nor is there doubt that, if we graciously respond to the petitions of God’s servants, we find the Lord merciful toward our own needs; so that, just as by divine providence we are called fathers among God’s people, we may also deserve, through the effective accomplishment of our work, profitably to preside over the faithful.

[Col. 0384B]

Although we ought generally to provide for all ecclesiastical persons, we ought nevertheless to be solicitous with more earnest care for those whom it is evident are intent with greater zeal upon the service of Almighty God and shine forth through a stricter religious life and upright conduct. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Hugh, we grant due assent to the petitions of your devotion, and by the authority of this present privilege strengthen the Church of Prémontré, over which, by God’s appointment, you preside, together with all things belonging to it. We decree that whatever possessions or goods that venerable place now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, through grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes,

[Col. 0384C]

offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through God’s favour, shall remain secure and inviolate for you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names—and, at the intervention of our venerable brethren Bartholomew, Bishop of Laon, and Simon, Bishop of Noyon, to confirm to your monastery—the enclosure of the valley of Prémontré, as it is contained in your writings and defined by fixed boundaries, free from every exaction, whether of land-tax, tithe, or rent; the estate of Fontenelles, with its fishpond and two parts of the mills below it, and its other appurtenances; the estate of Merlin with its vineyards; the estate of Roseries with its dependencies and appurtenances; the estate of Vercigny

[Col. 0384D]

with its appurtenances; the estate of Souppy with the mills below it on the river called the Aisne, and its other dependencies and appurtenances; two parts of the tithe of Chavus. At Valavergni, ten *modii* of wine from the tithe of that same town; the tithe with the land-tax of Vrevin and the land of Concivilla, excepting two *modii* which must be paid from it to the church of Blessed Mary at Nogent; also the fishpond and mill beside that same town, just as Ingelrannus, son of Thomas of Marle, had held them in his lordship in the aforesaid two towns. The rents of Poilly; the mill of Rochis; the mill of Proisel; the mill of Achery; the mill of Cortun; the mill of Cenceny; the wine-dues of Bourguignon; the land of Carreni;

[Col. 0385A]

two parts of the mill of Aquila; the vineyards of Brovencourt, Ursignicourt, Brummont, Lizy, Valavrigny, Montarcenne, and Montbavin; the vineyards of Coucy Castle and Coucivilla; the wine-dues and vineyards of Novavilla in the diocese of Soissons; in the suburb of the city, an estate and site, wine-press, and vineyards. At Pomerias, wine-dues; the money-rents of the castle of Brana and the town of Branella; the estate of Biucy with vineyards and its other appurtenances; the mill of Rupibus beneath that same town; the estate of Clamecy with wine-press, vineyards, and other appurtenances. At Sorny, two wine-presses, vineyards, and other revenues; the estate of Tenselva with its appurtenances; the estate of Luilly; and half a mill with its other appurtenances. At Bethencourt, wine-dues and other revenues.

[Col. 0385B]

At Pinon, a certain rent, a third of the small tithe of Atrium, a sixth part of a certain mill, and the tithe which Josbert held there; the chapel and estate of Rosel, with mill, fishpond, wine-press, vineyards, and all its appurtenances. On the hill of Trosly, one estate, and another in the valley, with lands, vineyards, and other appurtenances; and part of the village with its dependencies, which Andrew of Boldimento gave to you, just as he held it in his own lordship; and certain other things offered by other faithful servants of God; the estate of Bincy with its appurtenances; the estate of Allechi and two parts of the tithe, vineyards with their other appurtenances. At Cauny, rent and wine-dues. In the town called Pont-Saint-Médard, a fourth part of the tithe. At Margival, half

[Col. 0385C]

a mill, and half the chestnut-groves at Vausaillon. In the diocese of Noyon, the altar and estate of Bonolio with their appurtenances; the estate of Bolmont; the estate of Calveni; the freehold of Germaines; the estate of Montisel; the estate of Thory; the estate of Landricourt. And in the suburb of Noyon, land, vineyards, and meadows; an estate with the things belonging to it. The mills of Despeville and half the tithe of that same town. Two parts of the tithe of Destoily. A sixth part of the tithe of Duri; the mills of Offois and two parts of the tithe of that same town; a third part of the tithe of Grecy; half the site of a certain mill at Dinisa and half the tithe of that same town; two parts of the tithe of Saint Radegund; two parts of the tithe of Calveni; a third

[Col. 0385D]

part of the tithe of Caullaincourt; two parts of the tithe of Gricourt; three parts of half the tithe of Leherives; a third part of the tithe of Lancy; the tithe of Kivres; a third at Omencourt; a third of Liencourt and of Curcy; three *jugera* at Greum; the free chapel of Saint Nicholas at Saint-Quentin; the estate of the freeholds with its dependencies; the estate of Voïana with its appurtenances; the estate of Hanopiis in freehold, with the tithe; two parts of the tithe of Bechincourt; two parts of the tithe of Cartigny; the entire tithe of Falvi, excepting the small tithe; a fourth part of Aldeni; the mills of Escauly with their appurtenances; the mills of Hamel; and the site of a certain mill at Pieton.

[Col. 0386A]

We have also considered, in accordance with humanity, and by this present decree, to remain in force forever, have decreed: the sisters who, through the labour of our brother of blessed memory Norbert, Archbishop of Magdeburg, and through your exhortation, came to the service of Almighty God and offered themselves to the Lord, shall now and always, without anyone’s objection, receive from the goods of your church what is necessary for temporal support. No small part of those goods is known to have come to that place through them.

Likewise, we decree that you shall not be compelled to give tithes to anyone from the produce which you gather by your own hands and at your own expense; nor shall it be lawful for any bishop, on any pretext, to prohibit divine offices in your church. If, however, a general interdict is imposed in the diocese, then, with excommunicated persons excluded

[Col. 0386B]

and the doors closed, you shall nevertheless celebrate the divine offices.

Moreover, you shall receive the ordinations of canons, consecrations of altars or churches, and the other ecclesiastical sacraments from the Bishop of Laon, if he is Catholic and enjoys the favour and communion of the Apostolic See. Otherwise, you shall approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what is requested.

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass them with any molestations; but let all be preserved intact for you, to benefit in every way those for whose governance and support they were granted. But if anyone

[Col. 0386C]

knowingly, by rash presumption, should presume to act contrary to this our constitution, after a second or third warning, unless he correct his presumption by suitable satisfaction, let him be subject to excommunication. But those who preserve these things shall obtain the favour of Almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Luke, cardinal priest, acting in place of Lord Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of January [21 December], in the second indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1138, in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CCCXXXVI. He grants Premonstratensian monasteries immunity from tithes.  
*(A.D. 1138, 21 December.)*

[Lepaige, *Bibliotheca Praemonstratensis*, p. 624.]

[Col. 0386D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the abbots, provosts, and remaining brethren and professed members of the Premonstratensian Order, both present and future, in perpetuity.

Divine Law has ordained that tithes are to be paid by the people to priests and Levites. But no reason permits bishops or any ecclesiastical or secular persons to receive tithes from canons or clerics living the common life, from their own labours or from their livestock; as Blessed Gregory the Great, the eminent teacher, testifies and says:

> “What are we to say concerning those who live the common life, in respect of giving alms and offering hospitality, when they ought to distribute in pious causes everything that remains over?”

[Col. 0387A]

Wherefore, by this present writing we decree and by apostolic authority establish that no bishop and no ecclesiastical or secular person shall have leave to demand from you tithes from the produce which you gather by your own hands and at your own expense, or indeed from your livestock, nor to disturb your peace on any pretext. Rather, freed from vexations and exactions of this sort, you may devote yourselves with untroubled minds to divine service by day and night. But if anyone, by rash presumption, should attempt to act contrary to this, and does not amend his presumption by suitable satisfaction,

[Col. 0387B]

let him incur the indignation of Almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of January [21 December].

### CCCXXXVII. Privilege for the Premonstratensian Order.  
*(A.D. 1138, 21 December.)*

[Le Paige, *Bibliotheca Praemonstratensis*, p. 624.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the abbots and provosts of the Premonstratensian Order and its professed members: greeting and apostolic blessing.

He who, by the ordering mercy of God, merits to hold the place of a shepherd must diligently think not only of his own salvation but also of the salvation of his brethren.

[Col. 0387C]

He is certain that, just as he will receive from the Lord reward and blessing for the good works both of himself and of those entrusted to him, so conversely, if—God forbid!—he himself has gone astray or has permitted his subjects to deviate from the right path, he will incur a sentence of condemnation. He must also perform the office of a physician, cherishing what he knows should be nourished and cutting away with the iron of discernment what he sees ought to be amputated.

With this purpose, we decree that if any abbot of your order and profession, whether of the Church of Prémontré or of another place, should—may God avert it!—be detected in a crime, or appear altogether useless in office, you shall have, by our concession and with the common counsel of all of you, or even of the greater and sounder part, free authority to depose such a person and appoint another in his place.

[Col. 0387D]

Given at the Lateran, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of January [21 December].

### CCCXXXVIII. He confirms the goods of the Church of Belleval.  
*(A.D. 1138, 21 December.)*

[Hugo, *Annales Praemonstratenses*, I, p. 205.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son PHILIP, abbot of Belleval, and to his brethren, both present and future, in perpetuity.

A devout request should be fulfilled in its result, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth commendably and the benefit sought may undoubtedly gain effect. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your reasonable requests,

[Col. 0388A]

and confirm by the privilege of the Apostolic See to you and, through you, to your monastery, whatever the faithful of God, especially our venerable brother of blessed memory Rainald, Archbishop of the Church of Reims, have in devout piety and reasonably bestowed upon you in churches, houses, woods, waters or watercourses, cultivated and uncultivated lands, and have confirmed to you by his charter.

Among these we have added the following, to be specified by their proper names: namely, the place itself called Aureavallis, granted to you and your successors with all its appurtenances—cultivated and uncultivated lands, meadows, woods, and waters—by our venerable brother Albero, Bishop of Verdun, with the common consent and counsel of his church, and with the assent and at the request of Counts Rainald of Bar and Henry of Grandpré. Also the possession called Anement, situated upon the River Meuse, which, through the hand of the aforesaid our brother Archbishop Rainald, you bought from Hugh of Reims, of the Jewish quarter, and his son Ernald for seven pounds in denarii;

[Col. 0388B]

and for which you also gave Hugh of Duzey sixty solidi. By the aforesaid title of sale and purchase, the same place with all its appurtenances—namely, cultivated and uncultivated lands, meadows, woods, and waters—was delivered to you by them. The mills which, by the grant and conveyance of the aforesaid our brother, you constructed upon the Meuse. Also the stagnant water called Ramus; the land which William Manses, with the assent of his brethren, gave to you; and the land granted to you by Holdiard and her husband Roger, and by their brothers, sisters, and nephews with their own persons. The place called Crisseium, given to you and your church for love of God by Adelaide of Grandpré, her son John, and her brethren, with all its appurtenances—namely cultivated and uncultivated lands, meadows, mill-sites on the Aisne, and such use of fishing and woodland as is necessary for building and fuel.

Furthermore, no one shall presume to demand from you the tithes which our beloved son Ursus, abbot of the monastery of Saint-Denis at Reims, granted to your church at a rent of three solidi in Reims coin, payable every year. We moreover confirm to you the land, fishery, and meadows given to you by Elias of Burgo; and by this present writing we make secure to you the land called Wamel, with all its appurtenances,

[Col. 0388D]

cultivated and uncultivated lands, meadows, woods, and waters.

Moreover, no one shall presume to demand from you tithes of the produce which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or impose any exaction upon your church. Nor shall it be lawful for any person whatsoever rashly to disturb your church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass them with any vexations; rather, let all be preserved intact for the benefit of you and the poor.

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this text of our constitution, should attempt rashly to act contrary to it, after a second or third warning, unless he makes suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and office, and know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and our Lord Jesus Christ, and be subject at the last judgment to strict retribution.

[Col. 0389A]

But upon all who preserve the rights of that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Luke, cardinal priest, acting in place of Lord Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of January [21 December], in the second indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation

[Col. 0389B]

1139, in the ninth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CCCXXXIX. Privilege for the Monastery of Saint Nicholas of Clairfont.  
*(A.D. 1138, 21 December.)*

[Hugo, *ibid.*, p. 402.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son GERARD, abbot of Saint Nicholas of Clairfont, and to his successors to be canonically appointed in perpetuity.

A devout request ought to be fostered by earnest support, so that both the sincerity of devotion may shine forth commendably and the benefit sought may undoubtedly gain effect. Therefore, at the intervention of our venerable brethren Bartholomew, Bishop of Laon, and Nicholas, Bishop of Cambrai,

[Col. 0389C]

we grant paternal assent to your just petitions, beloved son in Christ, Abbot Gerard, and strengthen by the authority of this present writing the church of Saint Nicholas of Clairfont, over which, by the Lord’s appointment, you preside, with all its appurtenances.

First, indeed, we decree that the canonical order according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine and the institution of the brethren of Prémontré shall be permanently and inviolably observed in that church in future times. We also decree that none of the brethren of that church, after making profession there, shall have leave, without your consent and that of the chapter of the place itself, to transfer to another church; nor may anyone receive or retain one who thus transfers. And if such a person, when summoned and canonically warned, refuses to withdraw, the abbot shall have authority to pronounce canonical sentence against him.

[Col. 0389D]

If a general interdict is imposed in the place where your church is situated, then, with excommunicated persons excluded and the doors closed, it shall be lawful to celebrate the divine offices.

We decree for the future that whatever possessions or goods the Church of Saint Nicholas now canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s favour, shall remain secure and inviolate for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names:

[Col. 0390A]

Namely, in the diocese of Laon: the abbey itself of Clairfont with every tithe and land-tax of the lands adjoining you, namely from the spring of Emelim through the newly cleared lands of Rebo, Albert, and Danser, as far as the road of Rosbais (Roubais); and, on the other side, from the ditches of Montimbre through the beautiful oak as far as the dry Sumer. Also the land of Bray, the length of which is known to extend from the boundary of the land of Clairfont as far as the land of Boucoy (Boucoy), and its breadth between the two streams, Bray and Gerbais. Further, beyond the stream of Bray, two ploughlands of land—all of which lie within the parish of Wimiis (now Vimis). In the parish of Lusoir, all the land between Bray and Gerbais, given by Gibard surnamed Boverius. Also all the land

[Col. 0390B]

between Bray and Sumer belonging to the territory of Lusoir, from the land of Geregnies (Gerenies) as far as the territory of Voemiis, given by Rabodo, his wife Bruna, and their children. For this land, twelve denarii are to be paid annually for its whole tithe, both of agriculture and of animal-rearing, to the church of Saint Peter at Buciliacum, to which the altar of Lusoir belongs; two solidi to the church of Saint Michael; and twelve [denarii] in Valenciennes currency to the priest of Lusoir.

In the parish of Sorbais, the freehold given by Gerard and Godfrey, sons of Hugh Malvais, with the assent of their mother and brethren. In the diocese of Cambrai, the land formerly called Malus Rivus (“Bad Stream”), but now Pulcher Rivus (“Fair Stream”; now Beautron), for the tenure of which ten solidi in Valenciennes currency are paid annually to the heirs,

[Col. 0390C]

and for its entire tithe, both major and minor, ten solidi of the same currency are paid annually to the church of Saint Michael. Also, two cultivated fields of Heresiae (Lersy) and Marcella, free from every rent; likewise the land of Marcella at a rent of two Valenciennes solidi, and two cultivated fields, one at Heresiae and the other beside Plancha, at a rent of four denarii.

Since brethren who live the common life ought to live from the beneficence and alms of others, we decree that you shall not be compelled to give tithes to anyone from the produce which you gather by your own hands and at your own expense. Moreover, you shall receive the ordinations of clerics, the consecrations of altars or churches, and the other ecclesiastical

[Col. 0390D]

sacraments from the Bishop of Laon, provided that he is Catholic, enjoys the favour and communion of the Apostolic See, and is willing to provide them to you without wrongdoing or exaction. Otherwise, you shall approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what you have requested.

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass them with any molestations; but let all be preserved intact for you, to benefit those for whose governance and support they were granted. But if anyone knowingly, by rash presumption, should presume to act contrary to this our constitution, after a second or third warning, unless he correct his presumption

[Col. 0391A]

by suitable amendment, let him be subject to excommunication. But those who preserve these things shall obtain the blessing of Almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul, and eternal life. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given through the hands of Lueporus, cardinal, acting in place of Lord Emeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of January [21 December], in the eleventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1138, in the ninth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CCCXL. He confirms the possessions and privileges of the Monastery of Saint Nicholas of Sept-Fontaines (diocese of Langres).  
*(A.D. 1138, 21 December.)*

[Hugo, *Annales Praemonstratenses*, II, p. 487.]

[Col. 0391B]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son BESCELIN, abbot of Saint Nicholas of Sept-Fontaines, and to his successors canonically professing, in perpetuity.

Whenever a request is made of us which is recognized to accord with reason and propriety, it is fitting that we grant it with willing mind and give appropriate assent to the desires of those who ask. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Bescelin, we graciously accede to your just petitions, and by the present page of writing we strengthen the church of Saint Nicholas of Seven Springs, over which, by God’s authority, you preside, together with all that belongs to it; decreeing that whatever possessions, whatever goods, that place now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future be able to acquire, God being favorable, by grant of popes, generosity of kings or princes, offering of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to set down expressly the following: namely, whatever you possess from the allod of Villers, whether cultivated or uncultivated lands, together with all appurtenances and rights of use. Also what you hold within the bounds of Roseriis, Andelo, and Brualcurt: namely pasture necessary for your horses, cows, pigs, sheep, and any other animals, both in woods and elsewhere.

Moreover, we grant to you, to hold and possess freely and absolutely, everything which the brothers of that place have justly and canonically acquired, or may hereafter acquire, within the bounds of Andelo from men of Bartholomew of Nojant holding a fief from him by his grant. [Col. 0391C–D] Furthermore, we likewise confirm to you the place called Frangesvaul, with all its appurtenances, cultivated and uncultivated lands, meadows, waters, and woods, as our brother Wileneus, bishop of Langres, of good memory, granted and confirmed it in writing to your whole community.

We likewise confirm to you the place of Seven Springs itself, together with Francavalle, which Abbot Radulf of the church of Saint Peter of Monte, with the consent of his brothers, granted you freely, for the preservation of charity and humility, under an annual rent of one gold coin—or, in the fourth year, a Byzantine coin—to be paid to his church on the feast of Saint Peter; and likewise the fraternal custom hitherto observed at the funerals of the dead, to be kept for ever hereafter. [Col. 0392A] Moreover, we add that the abbot of Seven Springs for the time being shall henceforth receive none of the brothers of the church of Blessed Peter in that place, after profession and obedience have been made, without the common consent of the brothers of that church of Blessed Peter. The abbot of Saint Peter shall likewise keep this same rule toward you unimpaired.

Since those who live the common life ought to live from the alms and beneficence of others, we decree that you shall not be compelled to render tithes to anyone from the produce which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or from your livestock. No one shall dare to alter your canonical order and manner of life according to the Rule of blessed Augustine and the institution of the Church of Prémontré, or impose upon you the order of another profession.

Nor may any of your brothers who have promised stability and obedience depart without the permission of their own abbot and chapter; nor shall anyone dare retain one who departs. If, having been canonically summoned, he scorns to return, the abbot shall have authority to pronounce sentence against him. Nor shall your church be closed because of a general interdict of the parish; rather, with excommunicated or interdicted persons excluded, you may celebrate the divine offices. [Col. 0392B]

Likewise we decree that neither you, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Bescelin, nor any of your successors, shall presume to depart, unless summoned to a synod or on other business. [Col. 0392C] Therefore let no person whatsoever be permitted to disturb rashly the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it by any other vexations; rather, let all things be preserved whole and unimpaired, to be of every benefit for the use of those for whose support and governance they were granted.

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowingly opposing this page of our constitution, attempts rashly to act against it, then, having been warned a second or third time, unless he makes amends by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment of the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let him be subject to strict vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Lucas, cardinal priest, acting in the place of Lord Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of January [21 December], in the first indiction, in the year 1138 of the Lord’s Incarnation, [Col. 0393A] and in the ninth year of the pontificate of Pope Innocent II.

### CCCXLI. To Manasses, Bishop of Meaux. (Year 1138.)

[Duplessis, *Histoire de Meaux*, book II, p. 33.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother MANASSES, bishop of Meaux, and to his successors canonically promoted, for ever.

The care of the government entrusted to us admonishes us, by the Lord’s ordering, to apply attentive concern and vigilance to every individual, so that no confusion may be introduced in ecclesiastical arrangements, but rather that each person’s right and proper dignity may be preserved. For this reason, venerable brother Bishop Manasses, considering your devotion toward the Apostolic See, we grant due assent with kindness to your desires; and by the present page of privilege we strengthen the Church of Meaux, over which, by God’s authority, you preside. We confirm to you and your successors the episcopal right which your predecessors are known to have held in all abbeys, monasteries, and churches situated within the bishopric of Meaux. Therefore let no person whatsoever be permitted rashly to trouble you or your successors concerning this our confirmation, or thereby inflict upon you any diminution or opposition, etc. [Col. 0393B]

Given at the Lateran, in the year 1138 of the Lord’s Incarnation.

### CCCXLII. To Walter, Bishop of Augsburg.—He urges him to receive Abbot Engelscalc of Benediktbeuern and his brothers into favor and communion. (Year 1138.)

[Pez, *Thesaurus Anecdotorum*, III, III, p. 633.]

[Col. 0393C]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother W., bishop of Augsburg, greeting and the apostolic blessing.

Let your brotherhood know that E., abbot of the monastery of Beuern, and his fellow brother O., when they visited the Apostolic See in the past year, were released by our command from the sentence by which they had been bound. Therefore, by apostolic letters we command you—and in commanding, enjoin you—to receive them into ecclesiastical communion, setting aside all evasion; and henceforth neither trouble the aforesaid monastery in its goods or persons, nor allow it to be troubled by anyone.

It pains us, moreover, that you did not show our letters the reverence that was fitting, and that, after receiving the apostolic letters, you harassed those brothers. Therefore, in commanding, we enjoin you to bring back to their place, or freely permit to return, the brothers who departed from that monastery because of your harassment. [Col. 0393D]

### CCCXLII bis. Privilege for the Premonstratensian Order. (29 December 1138.)

[Le Paige, *Bibliotheca Praemonstratensis*, I, p. 624.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brothers archbishops and bishops, and to the beloved sons abbots, provosts, and priors to whom these letters shall come, greeting and the apostolic blessing.

He cannot seem to be inflamed by the love of brotherly charity who presumptuously inflicts upon his neighbor what he does not wish done to himself. Moreover, the more anyone is adorned with greater dignity and office, and the more he desires to be called and to be religious, the more carefully must he ensure that nothing irregular or less than canonical may be found in his actions; rather, that his works may shine before men and that the almighty Lord may be praised through his good endeavors.

For this reason we command your brotherhood and, by apostolic authority, enjoin that you receive none of the lay brothers (*conversi*) or other brothers of the Premonstratensian order after they have made profession in their own house and promised obedience, without the permission of their prelate. If any of them, contrary to this our prohibition, takes refuge with you, restore that same fugitive to his own abbot—or, as the text reads, “to the fugitive” (*vel transfugo*)—without objection or harassment. If you prove contemptuous, know that you will incur the indignation of the Apostolic See. [Col. 0394A–B]

Given at the Lateran, on the fourth day before the Kalends of January [29 December].

### CCCXLIII. To Stephen, Bishop of Autun.—He appoints Al. abbot of Vézelay. (1131–1139, 27 January.)

[Mansi, *Concilia*, XXI, 402.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother STEPHEN, bishop of Autun, greeting [Col. 0394C] and the apostolic blessing.

As your brotherhood knows, because of the absence of its shepherd the monastery of Vézelay has suffered the greatest loss, both in temporal and spiritual matters. Therefore, lest that monastery be harassed longer on this account, we have given our beloved son Al., subprior of Cluny, to the monks of that place as abbot. We therefore command your brotherhood to lay upon him, in our stead, the hand of blessing.

Given on the sixth day before the Kalends of February [27 January].

### CCCXLIV. To Gregory, Bishop of Bergamo. (1138–1139, 9 April.)

[Lupus, *Codex diplomaticus Bergomensis*, II, p. 1018.]

[Col. 0394D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother G[REGORY], bishop of Bergamo, greeting and the apostolic blessing.

We do not believe that your brotherhood is unaware that, grieving with paternal affection over the dispute conducted between the clerics of Saint Vincent and Saint Alexander, we settled it after oaths had been received and confirmed the settlement by the authority of our writing. Since, as we have learned, certain disturbers of peace and concord neglect to observe our command concerning this matter through their quibbles, we command and enjoin you by these present letters to ensure that our command concerning the seat at table, and the sentence given by us between them concerning the fealty of the clerics and other matters, be observed without resistance.

But if the canons of Saint Vincent, through endeavors of wrongful intent, should refuse altogether to receive fealties from the clerics of that bishopric and should withdraw from the table, you are to provide in these and other matters in such wise that the clerics of Saint Alexander do not henceforth lose the ancient custom which, in our presence, they proved by witnesses and obtained through our sentence. Donations, sales, alienations, and any invasions of the goods of the Church of Bergamo, made by the intruder Arnulf or in his time, have been annulled and voided by our predecessors and by us. Therefore we do not wish Arnulf’s time to be counted toward prescription in these matters. [Col. 0395A]

Given at the Lateran, on the fifth day before the Ides of April [9 April].

### CCCXLV. He informs the canons of the Church of Saint Alexander of Bergamo of the preceding letter. (1138–1139.)

[Lupus, *ibid.*, p. 1018.]

[Col. 0395B]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the canons of Saint Alexander, greeting and the apostolic blessing.

To settle the dispute which was being conducted between you and the canons of Saint Vincent, we labored with paternal affection and, after receiving oaths, imposed a proper conclusion. Therefore know that it is grievous to us that, as we have learned, they neglect to observe what we decreed concerning this matter and strive to impede it by certain quibbles of words. Accordingly, we have enjoined upon your venerable brother G[regory], your bishop, with a command that he ensure the irreversible observance of our command concerning the seat at table and of the sentence given by us between you and them concerning the fealty of the clerics and other matters.

If those canons, through efforts of wrongful intent, refuse to receive fealties from the clerics of that bishopric and withdraw from the table, he is to make provision for you in these and other matters so that you do not henceforth lose the ancient custom which, in our presence, you proved by approved witnesses and obtained through our sentence. [Col. 0395C]

### CCCXLVI. Privilege for the Church of Saint John at Madalharstorf. (7 January 1139.)

[*Monumenta Boica*, XV, p. 269.]

[Col. 0395D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son EPPON, abbot of the monastery of Madalharstorf, situated in the bishopric of Regensburg in honor of Blessed John the Evangelist, and to his successors regularly appointed, for ever.

The care of the universal Church has been entrusted to us by God, the provider of all good things, in order that we may love religious persons and endeavor in every way to advance religion pleasing to God. For no service is ever rendered acceptably to God unless it proceeds from the root of charity and is preserved in the purity of religion. For this purpose of charity, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Eppo, graciously acceding to your reasonable requests, we receive under the guardianship and protection of the Apostolic See, and strengthen by this present privilege, the monastery of Blessed John the Evangelist over which, by God’s authority, you preside—a monastery known to have been founded in pious devotion by a certain Henry and his son Ernest—with all its appurtenances.

First, we decree that the monastic order according to the Rule of blessed Benedict shall be observed there inviolably for all future time. We also confirm by this writing, and decree to remain unimpaired for ever, the freedom conferred upon that monastery by Lothar of revered memory or by other ecclesiastical or secular persons, and likewise the exchange made between you and the monastery of nuns at Regensburg for the redemption of the rent. [Col. 0396A–B] Furthermore, whatever possessions or goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter be able to acquire through the grant of popes, the generosity of kings and princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, the Lord granting it, shall remain firm and whole for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to name expressly:
