the estate in the village of Stainkirchen, with fields, woods, meadows, and the mill situated there; the estate with a mill in the village of Ettiusdorff, together with its appurtenances; Ruesdorff, Hader, Ascholtzausem with their appurtenances; Ketenpeunt, Reiut, Prinpach, Pnechausen with its chapel and other appurtenances; Harselpach; Puech with its appurtenances; Perchaim with its mill; Hard with its chapel and other appurtenances; Chleping, Sitiching, Penning, Puecha, Wernsing, Taching with three vineyards, Grietzpach, Stainbach, Kafftn with their appurtenances; Mangolting with its mill; two estates at Teyting; a vineyard at Weng; and a vineyard at Watempach. [Col. 0396B–C]

In the bishopric of Passau: five vineyards at Marquard’s crossing; one vineyard at Sikchendorff; Trasemstorff; Schlichendorff; Grindorff, with their appurtenances and male and female serfs inhabiting that same estate, granted to your monastery by the noblewoman Leukarda for the love of God.

Moreover, we decree that no one shall presume to demand tithes from you from the land of your monastery, from newly cleared lands, or from other produce which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense. No bishop may impose upon you or your church labor-services or other new exactions contrary to monastic peace and religion. We also decree that the burial-place of that site shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who have resolved to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated.

When you, the present abbot of that place, die, no one shall be placed there by any cunning of deceit or violence, except one whom the brothers, by common consent or by the counsel of the sounder part, elect according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict. You and your church may also choose an advocate and henceforth retain him for carrying out the affairs of that place. [Col. 0396D–0397A]

If anyone, after making profession in your monastery, flees from it and, having been warned a second or third time, scorns to return to your cloister, you may excommunicate him; and no bishop, abbot, or prior may dare retain an excommunicated person. Therefore let no person whatsoever be permitted rashly to disturb that monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but let all things be preserved intact, for the benefit of you and the poor—saving, of course, the right and reverence due to the Church of Bamberg, to which that monastery, with all its appurtenances, is known to have been assigned and subjected through your efforts and petition, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Eppo.

If any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowingly opposing this page of our constitution, attempts rashly to act against it, then, having been warned a second or third time, unless he makes amends by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment of the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most holy body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let him be subject to strict vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen. [Col. 0397B]

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Ides of January [7 January], in the second indiction, in the year 1139 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the ninth year of the pontificate of Pope Innocent II. [Col. 0397C]

### CCCXLVII. Privilege for the Monastery of Saint Mary of Biburg. (7 January 1139.)

[Hund, *Metropolis Salisburgensis*, II, p. 205.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son EBERHARD, abbot of Saint Mary of Biburg, [Col. 0397D] and to his successors regularly appointed, for ever.

Placed, by the Lord’s ordering, on the seat of justice, it is fitting for us to provide beneficially for the peace and welfare of churches, so that, just as by the grace of God we are called fathers in name, so we may likewise be proved such in deed. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Eberhard, acceding to the just desires of you and your brothers, we receive under the guardianship of blessed Peter and our protection the church of the blessed Mother and Virgin Mary of Biburg, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of the Apostolic See.

First, we decree that the religious observance established in your church according to the Rule of blessed Benedict through the care and industry of Otto, bishop of Bamberg, shall be firmly observed there for all future time. Furthermore, whatever possessions or goods that place now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter be able to acquire, God being favorable, by grant of popes, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for ever for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to name expressly: Griezpach, Mozeinhoven, Pucha, Percha, Gubedum, Lobesingen; in Tangrintil, seven holdings from newly cleared land; and the church on the hill of Adallungestorff.

Moreover, we decree that no one shall dare demand tithes from you from the land of your monastery, from newly cleared lands, or from other produce [Col. 0398A–B] which you gather by your own hands or at your own expense.

No bishop may impose upon you or your church labor-services or other new exactions contrary to monastic peace and religion. Furthermore, we decree that the burial-place of that site shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who have resolved to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated. When you, the present abbot of that place, die, no one shall be placed there by any cunning of deceit or violence, except one whom the brothers, or the sounder part of the brothers’ counsel, shall judge to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict. You and your church may also choose an advocate and freely retain him to carry out the affairs of that place. [Col. 0398B–C]

Therefore let no person whatsoever be permitted rashly to trouble you or your church concerning this our constitution, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass them with reckless vexations; rather, let all things be preserved whole for the use and every benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowingly opposing this page of our constitution, attempts rashly to act against it, then, having been warned a second or third time, unless he corrects his offense by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his honor and power; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment of the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let him be subject to strict vengeance at the last judgment.

But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen. [Col. 0398C–D]

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Almeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Ides of January [7 January], in the second indiction, in the year 1139 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the ninth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CCCXLVIII. To Gerard of Tripoli, R. of Tortosa, and H. of Byblos, bishops.—Concerning the diocese of Tyre. (17 January 1139.)

[Mansi, *Concilia*, XXI, p. 395.]

[Col. 0399A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers GERARD, bishop of Tripoli; R., bishop of Tortosa; and H., bishop of Byblos, greeting and the apostolic blessing.

Your brotherhood ought to know that the condition of the Church shines forth more clearly when the ranks established in it are kept unimpaired and the reverence owed to every prelate is rendered without contention or contradiction. For each person among those who are subject ought to consider with what reverence and honor he must honor his prelates, if he has any. If these are unjustly and undeservedly withheld, the condition of unity will surely waver—a unity to which ecclesiastical teaching, in order to make it firmer, has brought all things by arranging them within itself with diligent consideration.

Therefore, lest the honor or dignity of your churches be diminished or nullified through contention or improper rebellion, we command and enjoin you by apostolic letters to render due obedience and reverence to our venerable brother Fulcher, archbishop of Tyre, as your metropolitan. By apostolic authority we restore you and your churches to the Church of Tyre, which is your metropolis, and likewise release you from the oath or fealty by which you are bound to the patriarch of Antioch. If you neglect to obey our commands and, within three months after receiving these letters, to return to the obedience of our aforesaid brother, we shall, God being the author, hold ratified the sentence which he canonically pronounces against you. [Col. 0399B–C]

Given at the Lateran, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of February [17 January].

### CCCXLIX. To Radulf, Patriarch of Antioch.—Concerning the diocese of Tyre. (17 January 1139.)

[Mansi, *Concilia*, XXI, p. 395.]

[Col. 0399D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother RADULF, patriarch of Antioch, greeting and the apostolic blessing.

The institutions of the holy canons provide that everyone should remain content within his own boundaries and should not encroach upon another’s rights. We are forbidden by both divine and human laws to do to our neighbors what we do not wish done to ourselves. Since this is so, we command your brotherhood not to prevent the suffragans of the Church of Tyre from rendering due obedience and reverence to their metropolitan, our venerable brother Archbishop Fulcher; otherwise, the canonical sanctions are violated when obedience is withheld from metropolitans by their suffragans. For we desire that each prelate and subject should retain his own right and proper order without contradiction. [Col. 0400A]

Given at the Lateran, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of February [17 January].

### CCCL. To Baldwin, Bishop of Beirut, Bernard, Bishop of Sidon, and John, Bishop of Ptolemais.—Concerning the diocese of Tyre. (17 January 1139.)

[Mansi, *Concilia*, XXI, p. 396.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers BALDWIN, bishop of Beirut; BERNARD, bishop of Sidon; and JOHN, bishop of Ptolemais, greeting and the apostolic blessing.

For this purpose the holy Fathers willed that there should be different ranks and orders in the Church: so that, while lesser persons render subjection and reverence to greater ones, unity might be formed from diversity and the administration of individual offices rightly conducted. But it grieves and greatly astonishes us that, although we had already long ago commanded you by apostolic letters to show obedience and reverence to our venerable brother Fulcher, archbishop of Tyre and your metropolitan, you have scorned to do so, alleging certain inadequate excuses and interpretations; whereas to resist is indeed like the sin of divination, and to refuse assent like the crime of idolatry (1 Kings 11). [Col. 0400B]

We therefore command you and again enjoin you by apostolic authority that, laying aside every excuse, you obey our same brother henceforth. Under pretext of the obedience which you owe to some primate, do not in any degree withhold from him the subjection and reverence owed to him as your metropolitan. If you prove further contemptuous, we shall, God being the author, hold ratified the sentence which that archbishop has pronounced or may pronounce canonically against you. But if, because you have obeyed our same brother, the patriarch of Jerusalem establishes anything against you, we decree that the same sentence lacks force and judge it to be of no effect. [Col. 0400C]

Given at the Lateran, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of February [17 January].

### CCCLI. To William, Patriarch of Jerusalem.—Concerning the diocese of Tyre. (17 January 1139.)

[Mansi, *Concilia*, XXI, p. 394.]

[Col. 0400D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother WILLIAM, patriarch of Jerusalem, greeting and the apostolic blessing.

The authority of the Gospel declares that the primacy of the whole Church and of ecclesiastical institution was granted by heavenly privilege to Blessed Peter, prince of the apostles. And below: We are astonished, however, that, although the Roman Church has labored so greatly for the liberation of the Eastern Church and, by shedding the blood of many sons, has stirred the hearts of both ecclesiastical and secular persons to its service, you have not taken care on this occasion to respond to your mother as is fitting.

For it had seemed too little to you that you had presumed to trouble our venerable brother Fulcher, archbishop of Tyre, when he came to the Roman Church, in the manner of his predecessors, to receive the pallium, unless you also showed yourself inhuman, difficult, and excessively harsh toward him as he returned from us. Thus you were unwilling either to restore to him the ancient dignity of the Church of Tyre or, within three months after receiving our letters, to render him justice, according to our command, concerning the injuries done to him, or concerning Caipha or Porphyra. Yet it is surely most unworthy that the honor which the Church of Antioch would render him, if it were obedient to him, should be withheld by you or your successors. Moreover, you are said to exercise power over his subjects in an excessive manner. [Col. 0401A]

Accordingly, by apostolic authority, we command and enjoin you—as you desire to be cherished by the pious efforts and assistance of your same mother, and as you desire to be helped by her protection in your necessities—to love and honor the aforesaid archbishop and presume to trouble him in nothing. Rather, do not delay, within forty days after receiving these present letters, to render him full justice in all matters concerning which he has lodged complaint with you; nor presume anything against his subjects contrary to the enactments of the canons. Otherwise, you should fear that we may withdraw both him and his suffragans from your obedience and keep them in our own hand. [Col. 0401B]

Given at the Lateran, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of January [17 December].

> **Note:** [Col. 0401D] Read: “the sixteenth day before the Kalends of February [17 January],” Jaffé.

### CCCLII. Privilege for the Church of Bamberg. (23 January 1139.)

[*Neue Mittheilungen*, I, IV, p. 15.]

[Col. 0401C]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother OTTO, bishop of Bamberg, and to his successors canonically appointed, for ever.

Placed, by the Lord’s ordering, upon the watchtower of the Apostolic See, it is fitting for us to exercise such care for the condition and peace of all churches that they may be defended against the wickedness of evil men by the protection of the most holy Roman and Apostolic Church, and that the things granted or to be granted to those churches under just titles may be possessed by them in firm and unshaken liberty.

Therefore we, whose special concern it is to admit and bring to effect the lawful petitions of those who ask, grant apostolic assent to your requests, venerable brother in Christ, Bishop Otto. We receive under the guardianship of blessed Peter and our protection, and strengthen by the privilege of the Apostolic See, the Church of Bamberg, over which, by God’s authority, you are known to preside, together with all its goods and appurtenances. We decree that whatever possessions, whatever goods, in abbeys, provostships, churches, villages, estates, cultivated or uncultivated lands, tithes, or any other things that church now justly and canonically possesses in its own bishopric or another’s—by exchange, purchase, grants of popes, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other means—or may reasonably be able hereafter to acquire, by the Lord’s favor, shall remain firm and unimpaired for ever to you and your successors and, through us, to the Church of Bamberg. [Col. 0401D–0402A]

Those things also which, through your care and industry, have been lawfully acquired for that church shall be preserved for it especially in inviolable and unshaken stability. Their names are as follows: Pruviningun, Entistorf, Mychelvelt, Voraugia, Uraha, Madelhartestorf, Biburch, Clunic, Reginerits Storf, Luncheim, Haholtisbrunne, Munstur, with the church of Blessed Sixtus and its other appurtenances; Viscera, Tocchelmhusen, Alterisbach, Vindeberge, Trosendorfs, Botenstein, Munirichsberch, Circhendorf, Gestenishusen, Cranaha, Bonaha, Rota, together with other things conferred on the aforesaid church by your brotherhood. [Col. 0402A–B]

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may dare rashly to trouble you or your successors concerning this our constitution, take away the possessions of your church, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass them by any vexations. Rather, let all things be preserved whole and remain in your power, for every benefit of both yourselves and that church.

If any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowingly opposing the tenor of this our constitution, attempts rashly to act against it, then, having been warned a second or third time, unless he duly corrects his offense, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment of the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ; and let him be subject to strict vengeance at the last judgment. [Col. 0402B–C]

But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Almeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the tenth day before the Kalends of February [23 January], in the second indiction, in the year 1139 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the ninth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II. [Col. 0402C–D]

### CCCLIII. He confirms the religious observance introduced by Saint Otto into his monasteries. (23 January 1139.)

[Ussermann, *Episcopatus Bambergensis*, Pr., p. 88.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother OTTO, bishop of Bamberg, and to his successors canonically appointed, greeting and the apostolic blessing.

Whenever something is requested of us that is recognized as consonant with religion and propriety, it is fitting that we grant it with a willing mind and afford suitable assistance, [Col. 0403A] so that faithful devotion may attain a swift result. Therefore, venerable brother Otto, bishop, we mercifully assent, out of the customary kindness of the Apostolic See, to the wishes of your petition. First, indeed, we decree that the rule of religious life which, through your diligence and with the Lord’s cooperation, has been established in the churches entrusted to you, shall be firmly preserved in them for all time. We further decree that no one shall be installed in those same churches through the depravity of simony, but that honorable persons—whose worthiness of character and condition commends them—shall be ordained there.

Moreover, in the monasteries which were either built long ago within your parish, or which you yourself have established out of devotion, or which you may be able to unite to your church by other just means, or which any of the faithful may henceforth, through divine inspiration, build within [Col. 0403B] your diocese, we decree that the order of sacred religion shall remain. Nor may anyone in any way alter the form of this institution, unless perhaps, by the Lord’s grant, he should wish to advance it to the prerogative of a better condition. Nor shall this be committed to the individual judgment of anyone; rather, we decree that it must be done by the counsel and consent of all the monasteries belonging to the diocese of Bamberg, or of their sounder part.

But if anyone should rashly attempt to oppose this our constitution, and, having been warned a second and a third time, should not correct his deed by suitable satisfaction, let him be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Redeemer Jesus Christ, and at the last judgment be subject to severe vengeance; while those who preserve for the same places the things that are just may obtain [Col. 0403C] the favor of almighty God, of the blessed Peter and Paul, and of us.

Given at the Lateran, 10 Kalends of February, indiction 2.

### CCCLIV. To Cardinal Azo.—Concerning the settlement of the dispute between the canons of the Greater Church and those of Saint Antoninus.  
*(A.D. 1139, January 25.)*

[CAMPI, *History of Piacenza*, I, p. 411.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son AZO, priest-cardinal of the holy Roman Church, and provost of Saint Antoninus of Piacenza, etc.

[Col. 0403D] Given at the Lateran, 8 Kalends of February, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1139, in the ninth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CCCLV. He confirms the goods and rights of the Abbey of Gengenbach.  
*(A.D. 1139, February 28.)*

[WURTWEIN, *Nova Subsidia diplomatica*, vol. VII, p. 107, from the autograph in the archive of the high choir of Strasbourg Cathedral.]

[Col. 0404A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son GODEFREY, abbot of the monastery at Gengenbach, situated in the district of Mortenang on the river Kinzig, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

A pious request of will ought to be fulfilled by a resulting effect, so that sincerity may shine forth praiseworthily and the benefit sought may unquestionably acquire strength. Therefore, beloved son in Christ, Abbot Godfrey, [Col. 0404B] we have thought fit mercifully to assent to your reasonable requests. We receive under the guardianship and protection of the Apostolic See the monastery of Gengenbach, over which, by the Lord’s authority, you preside. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and lawfully possesses, or may hereafter be able, by God’s favor, to acquire through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors forever. Among these, we have thought fit to record the following by their proper names: in Mortenang, Gengebac [Note: [Col. 0403D] Gongenbach.], Cella [Note: [Col. 0403D] Zell.], Steinach [Note: [Col. 0403D] Steinach.], Hademarsbach [Note: [Col. 0403D] Harmersbach.], [lacuna] [Note: [Col. 0403D] The names are erased in the autograph through age. The erased names may perhaps be supplied from another bull of Nicholas IV, A.D. 1287, for the Abbey of Gengenbach: Reichenbach, a fourth part of Gerolteshecke Castle.], Gerolstesbeke Castle, Norderaha [Note: [Col. 0403D] Nordrach.], with woods, waters, and all their appurtenances or dependencies; [Col. 0404C] Ichenheim [Note: [Col. 0403D] Ichenheim.], with the cell and all things belonging to it; Schopheim [Note: [Col. 0403D] It is called Ober Schopffen in the aforementioned bull of Nicholas IV.], Kinzdorff [Note: [Col. 0403D] Kinsdorff.], Linegizen [Note: [Col. 0403D] Linx.], [lacuna]; in Breisgau, Nuvershusen [Note: [Col. 0404D] Newershausen.]; in Alsace, Dancratesheim [Note: [Col. 0404D] Dangolsheim.], Westhusen [Note: [Col. 0404D] Westhusen.], Belhen [Note: [Col. 0404D] Behlenheim.], Durmingen [Note: [Col. 0404D] Durningen.], Franckenheim [Note: [Col. 0404D] Hoh-Franckenheim.], Batenesdorf [Note: [Col. 0404D] Bettendorff.]. In these villages of Alsace, moreover, as your predecessors are known to have done up to the present time, you and your successors may appoint an advocate, who shall endeavor to do those things which appear to concern the advantage and peace of your monastery.

We also confirm the wine-tithe granted to you by Ricgardis, formerly an illustrious queen; Kunegesheim [Note: [Col. 0404D] Kintheim.], Schervibre [Note: [Col. 0404D] Scherwibre.]; in Swabia, Rimigesdorf, Bessendorf, Urslingen, Villingen, Aschahabmorn-Stettein [Col. 0404D] [Note: [Col. 0404D] In the bull of Nicholas IV, A.D. 1287, the following are named: Rumeluisdorff, Urselingen, Villingen, and Gruemstaten; and they are said to be villages situated in Swabia and in the diocese of Constance.].

Upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any one of your successors, no one shall be placed over it by any cunning of fraud or by violence; but only the man whom the brothers, by common consent, or the sounder part of the brothers, shall elect according to the fear of God and the Rule of Saint Benedict. And, in order that you may be able to serve almighty God more peacefully, we confirm by the present written page the liberty granted to your monastery by the emperors: namely, that no judge, judicial authority, or any great or small person may dare impose any evil customs upon you or your brothers, or upon the monastery, churches, and villages belonging to it, or upon its inhabitants, whether free or servile, dwelling on the land of that monastery; nor may they harass them with exactions or unjust judgments.

[Col. 0405A] We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no one at all rashly to disturb the aforesaid place, or to seize its possessions, retain those seized, diminish them, or harass it with any annoyances; but that all things shall be preserved whole and unimpaired, serving in every way the benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should not make amendment by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honor, and know himself or herself to be answerable before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let that person be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of the Lord, our Redeemer Jesus Christ, and be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance.

But let the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ be upon all who preserve their rights for that place, [Col. 0405C] so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church.  
I, Aegidius, bishop of Tusculum.  
I, Theodwin, bishop of Saint Rufina.  
I, Peter, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Marcellus.  
I, Gerard, priest-cardinal of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem.  
I, An[...], priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina.  
I, Luke, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul.  
I, Chrysogonus, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Praxedes.  
I, Gregory, deacon-cardinal of Saints Sergius and [Col. 0405D] Bacchus.  
I, Otto, deacon-cardinal of Saint George at the Veil of Gold.  
I, Gerard, deacon-cardinal of Saint Mary in d[...].  
I, Hubald, deacon-cardinal of Saint Adrian.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Aimeric, deacon-cardinal and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Kalends of March, indiction 2, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1139, in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CCCLVI. Privilege for the monastery of Ringsted.  
*(A.D. 1139, March 1.)*

[TORKELIN, *Diplomatarium Arnaea-Magnæanum*, I, p. 8.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 0406A] son ORME, prior of the Church of Ringsted, and to his successors to be appointed.

Whenever something is requested of us which is recognized as consonant with reason and propriety, it is fitting that we grant it with a willing mind and provide suitable assistance for the desires of those who ask, so that faithful devotion may obtain a celebrated result. Therefore, beloved prior Orme in the Lord, we mercifully assent to your requests, receive under the protection of Saint Peter and our own the Church of Ringsted, over which, by God’s authority, you preside, and fortify it with all its appurtenances by the page of this privilege. We decree that the monastic order known to have been established there according to the Rule of the holy Fathers shall be preserved there inviolably for all future time.

Furthermore, whatever the same venerable place now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by God’s favor, be able to acquire through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings and princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. We also decree that no brother of the same place, after making profession among you, shall dare remove to another place without the permission of the prior and chapter; nor shall anyone presume to retain a departing brother. If, indeed, he has been summoned three times and refuses or scorns to return, the prior then in office shall have authority to pronounce canonical sentence against him.

[Col. 0406C] We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no one at all rashly to disturb your aforesaid church, or to take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any annoyances; but that all things shall be preserved whole for the benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving, of course, canonical justice and the reverence due to the diocesan bishop. If any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of his or her power and honor, know himself or herself answerable before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be excluded from the most holy body and blood of God and of the Lord, our Redeemer Jesus Christ, and be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance.

[Col. 0406D] But let the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ be upon all who preserve their rights for that place, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, with my own hand, subscribed.  
I, Aegidius, bishop of Tusculum, with my own hand, subscribed.  
I, BB., priest-cardinal of the title of the Apostles, with my own hand, subscribed.  
I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, with my own hand, subscribed.  
I, Guido, deacon-cardinal of Saints Cosmas and Damian beside the Temple of Romulus, with my own hand, subscribed.  
I, Crescentius, cardinal of the title of Saints Marcellinus and Peter, with my own hand, subscribed.  
[Col. 0407A] I, Comes, priest-cardinal of the title of Eudoxius, with my own hand, subscribed.  
I, Gripho, priest-cardinal of the title of Pastor, with my own hand, subscribed.  
I, Luke, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints Lawrence and Paul, with my own hand, subscribed.  
I, Chrysogonus, priest-cardinal of the title of Praxedes, with my own hand, subscribed.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Aimeric, deacon-cardinal and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the Kalends of March, indiction 2, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1139, in the ninth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CCCLVII. To Bernard, bishop of Segontia.  
*(A.D. 1139, March 6.)*

[LOPERRÁEZ, *Description of Osma*, III, p. 18.]

[Col. 0407B] INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother BERNARD, bishop of Segontia, and to his successors canonically instituted, in perpetuity.

The care of the office we have undertaken compels us to establish what concerns the peace of the churches and, with the Lord as author, to provide for their tranquillity. Nor is there any doubt that the office entrusted to us requires us so to weigh the decrees of the paternal canons that each Church may retain its rights and that what is regularly done by our brethren may be established with firm and unshaken stability. For this reason, venerable brother Bernard, bishop, we mercifully assent to your petitions. We confirm by apostolic authority, and decree to remain valid for all future time, the settlement of the dispute concerning the town of Soria, which was conducted between you and our brethren Michael, bishop of Tarazona, and Bertrand, bishop of Osma, and which was made [Col. 0407C] through the discernment of our beloved son Guido, deacon-cardinal of the holy Roman Church and then legate of the Apostolic See, with the counsel of the illustrious man Alfonso, king of the Spains, as well as of the archbishops, bishops, abbots, and other religious and wise men who had assembled at the Council of Burgos.

Namely: of those things which belonged to the Church of Segontia, the Church of Tarazona was to possess Calatayud, Borovia, Alcázar, with all the boundaries of the same towns; the greater church of Calatayud, with all its estates; and the estates which you are known to have bought there; the prosperous town of Olbega, which lies between Calatayud and the town of Daroca, called Salas, near Olbega. There were, however, reserved to the proprietary right of the Church of Segontia two castles: Deza, namely, between Calatayud and Almazán; and Fariza, between Calatayud and Medina.

To you, however, venerable brother Bernard, bishop in the Lord, it was granted that you should hold, from the right of the Church of Osma, Ayllón with all its boundaries and the estates which the bishop of that place possessed there; Aguilera; the castle of Galbe; half of the village called Liceras; Caracena with all its villages, with the two monasteries of Saint Saviour and Saint Mary of Tiermes; the king’s ford; Aguilera; Berlanga with all its boundaries and with the monastery of Saint Bandulus; Velamazán; and Barca. Furthermore, Almazán, [Col. 0408A] with all its boundaries, concerning which the bishop of Osma had made complaint. Moreover, it was granted to that same bishop of Osma to possess Soria entire, with all its boundaries—the subject of the dispute—and the monastery of Saint Mary of Bomaio, together with the royal tithes of the same town, which had belonged by right to the Church of Segontia. All these things, as they were established by that same son of ours, Guido, we strengthen by the safeguard of our favor.

Furthermore, whatever possessions and goods the Church of Segontia now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by the favor of the Lord, be able to acquire through grants of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: Medina, Molina, Saint Justus, Atienza, both Castejones with their appurtenances; and, from royal revenues, the tithes throughout the whole bishopric, saltworks, mills, and also the castle of Serón with all its boundaries.

[Col. 0408B] We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no one at all rashly to disturb the aforesaid Church of Segontia in respect of this our grant and confirmation, or to take away its possessions, retain those taken, diminish them, or harass it with any annoyances; but that all things shall be preserved whole, serving in every way the benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honor, know himself or herself answerable before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Redeemer Jesus Christ, and at the last judgment be subject to severe vengeance. But let the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ be upon all who preserve their rights for that place, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

HELP US, O GOD, OUR SAVIOUR.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, [Col. 0408D] have subscribed +.

### CCCLVIII. At the request of Ortlieb, bishop of Basel, he confirms the possessions of the monastery of Lucelle.  
*(A.D. 1139, March 18.—Fragment.)*

[BERNARDINI, *Epitome of the Deeds of Lucelle*, 24.]

[Col. 0409C]

### CCCLIX. Privilege for the monastery of Laach.  
*(A.D. 1139, March 23.)*

[GUNTHER, *Codex diplomaticus*, I, 241.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son GISELBERT, abbot of the monastery of Laach, situated in the parish of Trier, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

[Col. 0409D] We see that we have been placed, by the Lord’s ordering, upon the watchtower of the Apostolic See so that we may love religious persons and defend their places by favorable protection, lest they be troubled by the assaults of wicked people; so that, as by the ordering of divine mercy we are called Fathers in name, we may likewise be proved such in deed. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Giselbert, assenting to the just requests of you and your brethren, we receive under the guardianship and protection of the Apostolic See the monastery of Laach, over which, by the Lord’s authority, you preside, and fortify it by the page of this present writing.

First, indeed, we decree that the monastic order in the same place, according to the Rule of Saint Benedict and the observance of the monastery of Cluny, shall be preserved inviolably for all future time. Nor shall anyone, after making profession among you, have leave to transfer to another place, whether under the pretext of stricter or less strict religious observance, without the permission of the abbot and brothers; and no abbot or any other person shall dare retain one who departs. Moreover, we prohibit you and your successors, under penalty affecting your office, from giving any goods of the monastery to anyone as a benefice or applying to other uses things granted to you for the common benefit. Nor may anyone at any time dwell in the same monastery or around it, or build a house there to live in, except the monks assigned, or hereafter to be assigned, to the service of that place.

[Col. 0410B] Upon the death of you, the present abbot of the same place, or of any one of your successors, no one shall be placed over it by any fraud or violence, except the person whom the brothers, by common consent, or the sounder part of them, in accordance with the fear of God and the Rule of Saint Benedict, shall judge ought to be elected from the same community, or from another, if—God forbid—no suitable person is found among them.

You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and ordinations of monks or clerics who are to be promoted to sacred orders, from the diocesan bishop, provided that he is Catholic, possesses the favor of the Apostolic See, and is willing to provide these things freely and without any improper payment. Otherwise, you shall approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer; supported by our authority, he shall grant what is requested. We also grant that the burial place of that monastery shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and final will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated, saving the right of the mother church.

[Col. 0410C] Public masses or stations shall by no means be celebrated in the monastery by bishops without the consent of the abbot and brothers, lest any occasion for popular gatherings be afforded in the retreats of God’s servants. We further add that, in the event of a general interdict of the parish, the monastery itself shall not cease from divine offices; rather, with the doors closed and the excommunicated and interdicted excluded, the due offices shall be rendered there to almighty God.

Moreover, the advocate of the same monastery, whoever he may be at the time, shall presume nothing in that place beyond the constitution and written instrument of Counts Palatine Henry and Siegfried, founders of that place. [Col. 0410D] If he too should prove useless—God forbid—you may remove him and appoint another in his place.

We further decree that whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and lawfully possesses, or may hereafter, with God’s help, acquire through grants of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall stand confirmed to you forever by this present privilege and remain unimpaired. Among these, we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: first, the place itself called Laach, in which the same monastery is known to have been founded especially by the aforesaid noble Count Palatine Henry and his wife Adelheid, free from every secular right and authority; the church of Saint Dionysius at Kroth; also the village called Bella, Reida, Alchena, Willeberge, Kroth, and Beytendorp, with all their appurtenances, bestowed on you by the aforesaid Henry; four holdings at Kroth and Meylem in Brabant, given by Count Palatine Siegfried; one holding at Kroth, granted to you by the noble Count Palatine William and his mother Gertrude, with the consent of the knight Robert, who had held it from them in fief; the allod at the Moselle called Neuim, with its appurtenances, which Abbot Bertramn of Saint Arnulf of Metz, with the consent of our venerable brother Stephen, bishop of that city, and of his chapter, sold to your monastery for a suitable price, and for which that church is known to have acquired another, more advantageous estate.

[Col. 0411B] The allod at Evernaco, granted to you by the knight John and his wife Matilda; vineyards at Winningin and Leia, bestowed on you by Hunge and other faithful persons; at Andernach, Ludenstorp, and Hamersten, properties bestowed on you by Frederick, archbishop of Cologne, of revered memory; an estate at Wadenhem, granted by Embrico; the manor of Budenarde, granted to you by Henry and his brothers, and by Warner and his brothers; the fields and vineyards at Luzinc and Menedich; the allod at Pomero, granted to you by the knight Robert; the manor of Hardenhaga, with serfs and forests, granted to you by Meingod, Ernest, and Erlewin; a holding at Aldendrop, granted by Albert; likewise, the allod at Glensa, from the alms of Folcold; a holding at Wassenaco, given by the knight Embrico; two holdings at Werchenrede, from the alms of Count Hermann; vineyards at Cuchema and a holding at Wilre, given by Theoderic; vineyards at Mudhena; a holding granted by the knight Rudolf; and half a holding and half the lake, granted by Count Gerard.

[Col. 0411C] We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no one at all rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, or to take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall remain whole, serving the benefit of you and of the poor. If, therefore, any archbishop, bishop, king, prince of whatever rank, or any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honor, know himself or herself answerable before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of the Lord, our Redeemer Jesus Christ, and be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance.

But let the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ be upon all who preserve their rights for that place, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church.  
I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina.  
[Col. 0412A] I, Theodewin, bishop of Silva Candida.  
I, Gerard, priest-cardinal of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem.  
I, Luke, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul.  
I, Chrysogonus, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Praxedes.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Theoderic, deacon-cardinal and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, 10 Kalends of April, indiction 2, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1138, in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CCCLX. He fortifies Abbot Wikard of Pontigny and his monastery by the privilege of the Apostolic See.  
*(A.D. 1139, March 24.)*

[*Gallia Christiana*, XII, Instrument 111.]

[Col. 0412B]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son WIKARD, abbot of Pontigny, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

We render thanks to almighty God, whose mercy is better than lives, because He has adorned the monastery of Pontigny with such religious devotion and brilliance of integrity that not only neighboring places but also distant ones are worthily enlightened by the example of your way of life and are likewise instructed to pursue whatever is better. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Wikard, embracing your person in the arms of closer charity, we assent with due kindness to your desires and fortify by the privilege of the Apostolic See the monastery of Pontigny, over which, by God’s authority, you are known to preside. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same venerable and God-beloved place now canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by God’s favor, acquire through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: the lands of Dochiac and Creciac, which the canons of Saint Florentin granted to the monastery of Pontigny in perpetual right through the hand and written instrument of our brother Henry, archbishop of Sens; this grant was likewise approved by the abbot of Saint Germanus of Auxerre together with his chapter and confirmed in writing. Also the exchange of the land of Saint Martin of Chablis, situated in the parish of Ligny, for the land of Hugh of Merliniac and of Provost Humbald, situated in the territory of Chablis. We likewise confirm to you the grange of Chailly with all lands belonging to it, and whatever in the forest of Othe has been granted to that church or lawfully purchased by it.

[Col. 0413A] Therefore let no one at all presume to disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken, diminish them, or harass it with any annoyances; but let all things be preserved whole, serving in every way the benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted.

If any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowingly, should rashly attempt to act against this page of our constitution, and, having been warned a second or third time, should not correct his offense by suitable satisfaction, let that person suffer loss of power and honor and be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of the Lord, our Redeemer Jesus Christ. But those who preserve to that place what belongs to it may obtain the grace of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.  
[Col. 0413B] I, Theodewin, bishop of Silva Candida, subscribed.  
I, Anselm, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, subscribed.  
I, Luke, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul, subscribed.  
I, Guido, unworthy priest of the holy Roman Church, subscribed.  
I, Ivo, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Lawrence in Damaso, subscribed.

### CCCLXI. He receives the monastery of Saint Bartholomew (diocese of Penne) under protection and confirms its goods and rights.  
*(A.D. 1139, March 25.)*

[*Anecdota Ughelliana*, 391.]

[Col. 0413D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son JOHN, abbot of Saint Bartholomew, situated in the parish of Penne, and to his brethren regularly appointed in perpetuity.

The effect should follow a devout petition, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth worthily and the benefit sought may unquestionably take effect. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot John, granting assent to your just requests, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the monastery of Blessed Bartholomew, over which by divine authority you are known to preside, and strengthen it by the force of an apostolic privilege against the wickedness of evil men [Col. 0414A]. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, God granting it, by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: namely, the castle of Carpinetum; the castle of Fara, with its appurtenances; likewise the churches of St Vital, St Michael, St John, St Mary, St Peregrine, and St Nicholas of Vicolo; the church of St Mary at Sereneo; the churches of St Mary and St Felix at Catuniano, with their appurtenances; the church of St Christopher and St Mary at Genestrulo; the church of St Nicholas [Col. 0414B]; St Just of the castle of Occetano; the church of St Mary of Brituli; the church of St Lawrence of Fabrica; the church of John at Balneo; St Lawrence of Unicani; the church of St Mary in Plano; and St Mary in Cellulis, with its appurtenances.

You shall indeed receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars, and blessings of clerics from the diocesan bishop, provided that he is Catholic, enjoys the favour and communion of the Apostolic See, and is willing to confer these upon you freely and without improper dealing. Otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, that he may grant what you request.

Upon the death of yourself, the present abbot of that place, or of any one of your successors, no one shall be placed over it by any craft of fraud or violence, except the person whom the brothers by common consent, or the sounder party of the brothers, shall, according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict, provide to be elected [Col. 0414C], and who is always to be consecrated by the Roman pontiff. We also decree that burial in that place shall be entirely free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated.

Therefore let no person whatsoever presume rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with reckless vexations; but let all things be preserved entire for the benefit in every respect of those for whose support and governance they were granted. If anyone therefore in the future, etc. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. [Col. 0414D]  
I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed.  
I, Guido, bishop of Tivoli, have subscribed.  
I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed.
