But those who preserve these provisions shall obtain the blessing and grace of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul. Amen, amen, amen.

[Col. 0441A] I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. Fare well. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Ivo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Damaso, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Aymeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of May, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation one thousand one hundred and thirty-nine, in the second indiction, in the tenth year of the pontificate of lord Pope Innocent II.

### CCCLXXXIII. Privilege for the monastery of Saints Nicholas and Medard of Tournai.  
*(Year 1139, 14 April.)*

[COUSIN, *History of Tournai*, vol. II, p. 216.]

[Col. 0441B]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son OGER, abbot of the church of Saints Nicholas and Medard of Tournai, and to his successors canonically appointed, for ever.

Since we sit in the seat of justice, we must love our brethren with sincere charity and preserve each person’s rights by the privilege of our authority. In view of this consideration, therefore, beloved son Abbot Oger, we confirm to you and your successors that whatever the church of Saints Nicholas and Medard of Tournai now justly and canonically [Col. 0441C] possesses, or may in future acquire by grants of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other reasonable means, shall remain firm and unshaken to you.

Among these we have judged the following to be expressly named: dwellings within Tournai paying rent; arable lands around the city itself between the two streams, namely the Ries and the Mayry; land around the living spring; lands around the stream called Ries; land and tithe at Landast; the allod and rent-paying land at Castrecin; your tithe which you hold in that estate from the church of Saint Martin for a rent of two solidi; land beside Malbray; the tithe of animals on that land, which you hold from the church of Antoing for a rent of seven solidi; and an annual revenue of two measures of grain at Rosbais. We also confirm to you the order of blessed Augustine according to the custom of Saint Nicholas “of the arid gamantia” [reading uncertain], and the free election of your abbot.

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, claim for his own use those unjustly acquired, diminish them, or harass it with reckless vexations. Rather, all things shall be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose support and government they were granted, while in all things the right and reverence due to the diocesan bishop are preserved. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against [Col. 0442A] it, then, having been warned a second or third time, unless he corrects his offence by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ; and let him be subject, at the final judgment, to strict vengeance. But may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ be upon all who preserve the rights of that place, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Aimeric, chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of May, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1139, in the second indiction, in the tenth year of the pontificate of lord Pope Innocent II.

### CCCLXXXIV. He receives the hospital house of Tournai under his protection and confirms its possessions and privileges.  
*(Year 1139, 15 April.)*

[MIRAEUS, *Diplomatic Works*, II, p. 966.]

[Col. 0442B]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son GERARD, administrator of the hospital house of Tournai, and to his successors, for ever.

It accords with the clemency of the Apostolic See to provide by favourable protection for the defence of the poor. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Gerard, we graciously assent to your desires and receive under the guardianship of Saint Peter and of ourselves the hospital house which you administer and govern for the service of the poor and the glory of almighty God. We fortify it by the page of this present document, decreeing that whatever possessions and whatever goods that venerable place now lawfully possesses, or may in future acquire, the Lord being favourable, by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors.

Among these we have judged the following to be expressly named: namely, in the city of Tournai, the house of the poor and another house, which pay fixed annual revenues, and in addition one mill; in the district of Tournai, the altar-right of Warconio and one estate, with the lands belonging to it; in the district of Brabant, the altar-right of Velana and three estates, with the lands, woods, and meadows belonging to them; and one prebend [Col. 0442C–D] granted to you by our venerable brother Simon, bishop of Tournai, out of his devotion, so that, on the death of Dean Goter, it shall be received by a priest chosen by the chapter. That priest shall diligently serve the care of the poor; he shall take nothing from the hospital house itself, but his needs shall instead be provided from the prebend, and he shall perform the priestly office at the altar of Saint Mary.

If that priest—God forbid!—behaves too negligently toward Christ’s poor and, after admonition, refuses correction, he shall be removed, and another more useful man shall be appointed in his place through a new election of the chapter.

Also, after the senior citizens have been summoned to your chapter, a layman of good reputation shall be chosen as colleague to that priest [Col. 0443A], for the administration of temporal matters and for exercising the most diligent care toward the poor. We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid hospital house of ours, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it in any manner; but that all things shall be preserved intact, for the benefit in every way of the poor. If anyone should presume in rash audacity to attempt this, let him incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul, and be subject to excommunication. But those who preserve these provisions shall have forgiveness of their sins and shall obtain the blessing and grace of those same apostles. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church.

[Col. 0443B] Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of May, in the second indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1138, and in the ninth year of the pontificate of lord Pope Innocent II.

### CCCLXXXV. To Manfred of Mantua and Lothair of Vicenza, bishops.  
*(Year 1139, 16 April.)*

[TIRABOSCHI, *History of the Abbey of Nonantola*, II, p. 249, from Vatican manuscript parchment codex in quarto, no. 285, final verso page.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brethren M[ANFRED], bishop of Mantua, and L., bishop of Vicenza, greeting and apostolic blessing.

A serious dispute is being conducted between our beloved son Ild., abbot of Nonantola, and our brother T., bishop of Verona, concerning the parish church of Nogara and its chapels. We have judged this controversy to be entrusted to your discretion. Therefore, by apostolic letters we command your brotherhood, under obedience, to go together to the aforesaid place by the approaching Kalends of June; and if it is established that the monastery of Nonantola possessed the aforesaid churches and lost them without judgment, you shall restore it to possession of them. You shall nevertheless do this even if the aforesaid bishop does not appear when summoned by you.

[Col. 0443D] Given at the Lateran, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of May.

### CCCLXXXVI. To Theobald, bishop of Verona.  
*(Year 1139, 16 April.)*

[TIRABOSCHI, *History of Nonantola*, II, p. 249.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother T., bishop of Verona, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Concerning the dispute being conducted between you and our beloved son J., abbot of Nonantola, over the parish church of Nogara, we have directed our venerable brethren M[anfred], bishop of Mantua, and L., bishop of Vicenza, to go to the same place and, after hearing the arguments of both sides, in no way permit the same suit to remain undecided beyond the approaching Kalends of June [Col. 0444A]. By these present letters, therefore, we command your brotherhood that, when summoned by those same brethren of ours, you shall appear before them and firmly observe whatever they decide concerning this case.

Given at the Lateran, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of May.

### CCCLXXXVII. Privilege for the monastery of Kamp.  
*(Year 1139, 16 April.)*

[LA COMBLET, *Cartulary*, vol. I, p. 322.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son THEODERIC, abbot of the church of Kamp, and to his successors regularly appointed, for ever.

By the office of the apostolate entrusted to us by God, we are debtors both to those nearby and to those far away. Although we ought to honour and love all persons, and to preserve due justice for the churches entrusted to our brethren, we are especially bound to foster with more earnest affection those whom we know to have been made illustrious by God’s grace through greater uprightness of life and splendour of religious observance. For this reason, beloved son in the Lord, Theodoric, abbot of the Church of Kamp, we graciously assent to your petitions and fortify by the page of this present privilege the aforesaid monastery over which, by the Lord’s authority, you preside. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods that place now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future acquire, God being favourable, by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings, generosity of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other [Col. 0444B–C] just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors.

Among these we have judged the following to be expressly named: namely, the estate of Gumbreteseyme with its boundaries; Honepoul with its appurtenances; and Goterswicg with what belongs to it. We further enact that the monastic order established in that place according to the Rule of Blessed Benedict and the institution of the Cistercian chapter shall be preserved there inviolate for all future time. Moreover, we decree that your place shall be free from every secular servitude and exaction, and that it shall remain in the liberty in which Frederick, archbishop of blessed memory, established it. We forbid anyone to presume, on any pretext, to diminish the jurisdiction which that archbishop granted you in the adjacent woods, pastures, and waters out of devotion.

Nor may a bishop compel or summon you or your successors, against your will, to his business except perhaps to a synod. We further establish that, because of a general interdict imposed on the parish, your monastery shall not cease from divine offices; nor may any of your brethren, after making profession in that place, leave the cloister and transfer to another place, under pretext of a lesser or greater religious observance, without the licence of his superior. No bishop or abbot may presume to retain one who leaves; and if he has been canonically admonished and refuses to return, you shall have free power to pronounce canonical sentence against him. No one may dare to demand tithes from you [Col. 0444D–0445A] from uncultivated lands or from the maintenance of your livestock.

We therefore decree that no one may rashly disturb that monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with other reckless vexations. Rather, all things shall be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose government and support they were granted. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, having been warned a second or third time, if he does not make suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ; and let him be subject, at the final judgment, to strict vengeance. But may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ be upon all who preserve the rights of that place, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find in the future the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.

I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Angelo, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of May, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1139, in the second indiction, in the tenth year of the pontificate of lord Pope Innocent II.

### CCCLXXXVIII. Confirmation of the foundation of the abbey of Averbode, for whose governance and immunity certain decrees are established.  
*(Year 1139, 16 April.)*

[COCQUELINES, II, p. 243.]

[Col. 0445C]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son Abbot ANDREW of Saint Mary situated at Averbode, and to your successors canonically appointed, for ever.

The pious request of a will ought to be fulfilled by its consequent effect, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth commendably and the benefit sought may unquestionably acquire strength. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Andrew, we graciously assent to your petitions and receive under the protection of Saint Peter, and fortify by the page of this present privilege, the church of Saint Mary situated at Drebode [read: [Col. 0445D] Averbode], which the nobleman Count Arnulf and his associates founded in the sight of pious devotion and freely offered to almighty God for the remedy of their souls and for your support, from the boundary called Endeberghe as far as the boundary called Ubrepat, together with the surrounding pastures.

For we decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods that place now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future acquire, God being favourable, by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors.

[Col. 0446A] We further add that the same place shall remain free from every exaction, as is known to have been established by those same founders. It shall have no advocate except the bishop; and the canonical order, according to the Rule of Saint Augustine and the institution of the Church of Prémontré, shall be preserved there forever. We also decree that no brother, after making profession in that place, may transfer to another place without the permission of his superior. If he departs and, having been canonically warned, scorns to return, you shall nevertheless have authority to prohibit him from the divine offices; and no bishop or abbot shall dare to receive or retain one so prohibited. Indeed, we forbid tithes to be demanded from the produce which you cultivate by your own hands and at your own expense. [Col. 0446B] We likewise command that the same rule be observed concerning the increase of your animals.

Moreover, that you may remain more peacefully and freely in the service of Almighty God, by apostolic authority we forbid any bishop to compel or summon you unwillingly to his business, except perhaps to a synod. Furthermore, we grant that the burial-place of that house shall be entirely free, so that no one may obstruct the devotion and last will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated, while preserving, of course, the canonical right and due reverence of the mother church. Among the other possessions of the same place, we likewise confirm the church called Tessenderlon.

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb [Col. 0446C] that place, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any other disturbances; but that all shall be kept whole, to serve in every way the benefit of those for whose government and support they were granted. Should any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing this page of our constitution, rashly attempt to contravene it, after a second or third warning, unless he makes fitting satisfaction, let him lose the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself liable before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; and let him be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ.

But let those who preserve all these things obtain the blessing [Col. 0446D] and grace of Almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of May [16 April], in the second indiction, in the year 1139 of the Lord’s Incarnation, the tenth year of the pontificate of Pope Innocent II.

### CCCLXXXIX. Privilege for the monastery of Nonantola.  
*(Year 1139, 17 April.)*

[TIRABOSCHI, *History of Nonantola*, II, 247.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son ILDEBRAND, abbot of the monastery of St Sylvester [Col. 0447A] of Nonantola, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

Whoever desires to enter and dwell in the heavenly Jerusalem ought, according to the testimony of the Psalmist, diligently to direct his attention toward the things that make for peace. With this consideration, since many disputes and wars have hitherto existed between the Church of Nonantola and that of Modena, an agreement of this kind was formerly established at last for the good of peace between the inhabitants of the two places: namely, that, at the request of the abbot of Nonantola, the bishop of Modena should consecrate the church of the castle of Vetro with its chapels; the church of Sclopano with its chapels; the church of Fanano with its chapels; the church of Comurana with its chapels; the church of Trecentola with its chapels; and the church of Cortiola with its chapels; [Col. 0447B] and should ordain their clergy.

After this, however, peace not having been observed by the Modenese, Ribald, bishop of Modena, without consulting the abbot and against his will, consecrated one of the aforesaid churches by force. Thereupon, you, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Ildebrand, came to the council which, by the Lord’s guidance, we celebrated in the City, and complained before us against that bishop. When he appeared before us and our brethren and could not defend himself concerning the matters alleged, he received the following judgment: since it was established that this agreement had been made contrary to the privileges granted to the monastery of Nonantola by many Roman pontiffs, we decreed that it should have no force and held it wholly null and void, [Col. 0447C] commanding the bishop of Modena not to presume thereafter upon anything similar, but rather always and everywhere to allow your monastery peacefully to enjoy the liberty granted to it.

Therefore no person whatsoever may in any way harass you or your successors in these matters, infringe or alter this our constitution, or bring upon you any opposition on that account. But if anyone, with rash presumption, should dare to attempt this, unless he duly amends his offence, let him incur the indignation of Almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul, and be subject to excommunication . . . . *(The remainder is lacking.)*

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. [Col. 0447D] I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Azo, cardinal priest of the title of St Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of St Praxedes, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of the title of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of St George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Hubald, cardinal deacon of St Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman [Col. 0448A] Church, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of May [17 April], in the second indiction, in the year 1139 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the tenth year of the pontificate of Pope Innocent II.

I, Roger, notary of the Church of Nonantola, have written what I found written in the judgment of Lord Pope Innocent, adding or subtracting nothing.

### CCCXC. Privilege for the abbey of St Hubert, of the Order of St Benedict, in the Ardennes.  
*(Year 1139, 17 April.)*

[ROBAULX, *Chronicle of Saint-Hubert*, p. 335, from the archives of the abbey of St Hubert.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ GILLEBERT, abbot of the monastery of St Hubert in the Ardennes, and to his successors regularly [Col. 0448B] appointed there in perpetuity.

It befits the clemency of the Apostolic See to love religious men and cherish them in the bosom of maternal piety. For this reason, beloved Abbot Gillebert in the Lord, we graciously consent to your desires, receive into the protection of blessed Peter and our own the monastery of St Hubert, over which, by God’s appointment, you preside, and strengthen it by the page of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, through the gifts of the faithful or by any means whatsoever through the Lord’s favour, shall remain secure and undiminished to you and your successors.

And because the same monastery, as you yourself [Col. 0448C] have represented to us, frequently suffers various injuries from various plunderers, by authority of this Apostolic See we grant to you and your successors the power of binding and loosing. We confirm to the aforesaid monastery of St Hubert all that belongs to it: namely, fourteen chapels free from every episcopal exaction; also the cell of Ebernei Court with its appurtenances; the cell of St Theobald, situated in the castle of Porcino, with its appurtenances; Pirense with its appurtenances; the cell of Mollins with its appurtenances; the cell of Curien with its appurtenances; the cell of Sancey with its appurtenances; the cell of St Peter, with the chapel of St John in the castle of Bouillon and its other appurtenances; the church of Palatiolo, with its chapels and tithes; the church of Horto, with its chapel and rock [Col. 0448D] and its other appurtenances; the church of St Michael, and the hill and allod of Miruolo; the church of St Monon of Nassonia with all its appurtenances; the chapel of St Hubert at Liège; the church of Stawles; the church of Nirves; the church of Burs with its appurtenances; the church of Alvento with its appurtenances; the church of Bassayo with its appurtenances; and many other churches which it possesses—while preserving the right and due reverence of the diocesan bishops.

Moreover, we confirm to the aforesaid monastery the offerings of the faithful commonly called *cruces bannales* (“proclaimed crosses”); from the three deaneries, from the deanery of Graide, the offering of wax, or the obol of Liège currency itself; and cheeses made from the full milk of cows, sheep, and goats, [Col. 0449A] for one day from every house in each of the following villages: Maisin, Reduit, Vuscejae, Gusanvillae, Ocham, Palatioli, Offagne, Salsenrivi, Graides, Gedines, Loytres, likewise Loitres Borsines, Riennes, Willezies, Harnyes, Altifageti, Oyseis, Gembres, Bievre, Givet. The same shall be received from every house in the following villages of the deanery of Bohan: Wellin, Ham, Herpruviae, Bohanniae, Gimellae, Marlidee, Aye, Haverenne, Liceuriae, Mosbour, Burs, Telins, Waureliae, Tevins, Sernum, Villers, Jamblines, Wanlin, Frelo, Cotue, Mont-Saint-Pierre, Brumartin, Revoniae, Mont-Valcheri. The same shall be received from all villages of the deanery of Bastogne, with one loaf added from each house.

No abbot shall be rashly appointed [Col. 0449B] over the aforesaid monastery or established contrary to the sacred canons; rather, its abbot shall be the man whom the harmonious community shall choose freely according to the fear of God. We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb that monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or trouble it with rash vexations; but that all things shall be kept whole, to be of every benefit to the use of those for whose government and support they were granted.

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing this page of our constitution, rashly attempts to contravene it, after a second or third warning, unless he makes amends by fitting satisfaction, let him lose the dignity of his power and honour; [Col. 0449C] let him know himself liable before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance.

But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

+ I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul. I, Chrysogonus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint [Col. 0449D] Praxedes.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Aymeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of May [17 April], in the second indiction, in the year 1139 of the Lord’s Incarnation, the tenth year of the pontificate of Pope Innocent II.

### CCCXCI. Privilege for the Church of Lichfield in England.  
*(Year 1139, 18 April.)*

[*Monasticon Anglicanum*, III, p. 234.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the canons of the Church of Lichfield, present and future alike: greeting and apostolic blessing in Christ.

It befits the clemency of the Apostolic See to afford the aid of maternal protection to all who implore its patronage, so that, just as by the Lord’s ordering we are called fathers among the people of God, we may also be shown to be such by the performance of our works. For this reason, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously consent to your desires with paternal kindness and strengthen by the page of this present writing the Church of Lichfield, in which divine service is performed. We decree that the churches, tithes, possessions, and all goods which the aforesaid Church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means through God’s favour—and likewise all that has been conferred upon you by our venerable brother Roger, bishop of Coventry, in churches, tithes, [Col. 0450B] lands, and other possessions, or may hereafter be conferred by him through God’s favour—shall remain firm and undiminished to you forever.

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb that Church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations whatsoever; but that all things shall be kept whole, to serve in every way the benefit of those for whose government and support they were granted. If anyone with rash presumption should dare to attempt this, let him incur the indignation of Almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul and be subject to excommunication. But those who preserve these things shall obtain the blessing and grace of those same apostles and of ourselves. Amen, [Col. 0450C] amen, amen.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of May [18 April], in the second indiction, in the year 1139 of the Lord’s Incarnation, the tenth year of the pontificate of Pope Innocent II.

### CCCXCII. He informs Abbot Chuonrad and the monks of Fulda that Sturmi has been enrolled among the saints in the council.  
*(Year 1139, 19 April.)*

[MABILLON, *Acts of the Saints of the Order of St Benedict*, III, II, 284.]

INNOCENT, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son [Col. 0450D] CHUONRAD, abbot, and to the monks of the monastery of Fulda: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is most fitting and most worthy of every praise that those whom the King of kings and Lord of lords deigns to honour should receive devoted reverence from human beings. Therefore, having heard of the praiseworthy life of the blessed confessor Sturmi, having also learned in part of the miracles which the Lord works through his merits, and upon the testimony of our brethren who had come from the regions of Germany, in the plenary synod which by God’s grace has been assembled at the Lateran, after taking counsel with patriarchs, archbishops, bishops, and abbots, we have commanded that the same blessed man be honoured among the saints and elect; and that the day of his death be solemnly celebrated with joy. [Col. 0451A]

It is therefore your concern, dearest sons, to be so devoted to the observances of that confessor for the honour of Almighty God, and so to keep the venerable decrees of our mother, the Holy Roman Church, that your house may deserve praise and glory both with God and with men, and that your devotion may attain the rewards of eternal life.

Given at the Lateran, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of May [19 April].

### CCCXCIII. He settles the dispute concerning the tithes of the estate of the Church of St Maurice between Archbishop Chunrad of Magdeburg and Bishop Wiger of Brandenburg.  
*(Year 1139, 20 April.)*

[RIEDEL, *New Diplomatic Codex of Brandenburg*, I, VIII, p. 101.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother [Col. 0451B] CHUNRAD, archbishop of Magdeburg, and to his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

It is unfitting that discord should find a place among persons from whom the benefits of peace and concord ought to proceed. Therefore we have thought it right to commit to parchment and ink the agreement concerning the tithes of the estate of the church of Blessed Maurice, which is situated in the Church of Brandenburg, between our venerable brother Wiger, bishop of Brandenburg, and our beloved son Gerard, provost of Magdeburg, and his associates acting in your stead in that case, in our Lateran palace.

For it has been determined that you, venerable brother Chunrad, archbishop, and your brethren shall give and hand over to the bishop of Brandenburg and his church one hundred talents of Magdeburg currency and an equal number of *mansi* of land in the same bishopric, as our brother Bishop Anselm, Gerard, provost of Magdeburg, and Arnold, abbot of Berge, shall approve, for the sake of peace. [Col. 0451C] These *mansi* must be such that each one pays two solidi as rent, apart from other revenues, which shall nevertheless accrue to the use of the aforesaid bishop. Among these one hundred *mansi*, the village of Pecho shall be counted, with its woods, pastures, meadows, waters, and watercourses within the bounds of the same village. However, the rent of that village shall be assessed by trustworthy and God-fearing men, and, in accordance with a just calculation, deducted from the number of the aforesaid *mansi*.

In return for all these things, the bishop of Brandenburg shall make peace with you and your church, the controversy having been set aside, and shall wholly desist from the same dispute concerning the tithes of the cultivated or uncultivated estate of Blessed Maurice which you presently possess or hold in your own hand, venerable brother Chunrad, archbishop, whether you have granted them to other churches or your predecessors have granted them. [Col. 0451D] Therefore no person whatsoever may lawfully rashly disturb you or your successors concerning this constitution—while preserving the third part of the tithes due to parish priests—nor bring upon you any opposition or diminution, infringe it in any respect, or alter it.

But if anyone, with rash presumption, should dare to attempt this, after a second or third warning, unless he repairs his offence by fitting satisfaction, let him lose the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself liable before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be excluded from the most holy body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the last judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. But may those who preserve these things, through the merits of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul, deserve to obtain the grace of Almighty God and the rewards of eternal life. Amen. [Col. 0452A]

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Paul. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. [Col. 0452B] I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul. I, Chrysogonus, cardinal priest of the title of St Praxedes. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of St George. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian beside the temple of Romulus. I, . . . . cardinal deacon of St Eustace beside the temple of Agrippa. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of St Angelo. I, Gerard, deacon of St Mary in Dominica.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Almeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of May [20 April], in the second indiction, in the year 1139 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the tenth year of our pontificate as Lord Pope Innocent II. [Col. 0452C]

### CCCXCIV. He confirms the judgment rendered between Lanzo, abbot of St Michael, and Haduid, abbess of Juvigny, concerning the church of St Tyriacus.  
*(Year 1139, 20 April.)*

[BALUZE, *Miscellanies*, III, 69.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son LANZO, abbot of St Michael, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

We ought by paternal provision to establish those things which concern the peace of the Churches and wisely to provide for their tranquility and benefit. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Lanzo, we confirm by apostolic authority the settlement of the controversy between you and Haduid, abbess of Juvigny, concerning the church of Tyrcio, which was reasonably made in the presence of our venerable brethren—William, bishop of Palestrina, and Matthew, bishop of Albano, both of blessed memory; and John of Cremona, cardinal priest of the title of St Chrysogonus, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross, and Hubert, cardinal priest of the title of St Clement—before our assumption of the apostolic office. We decree that it shall remain valid and unshaken in future times, impose perpetual silence concerning this matter upon the same abbess and her successors, and decree by this present sanction, according to what was determined on this matter by those bishops and cardinals, that the aforesaid [Col. 0453A] abbess shall wholly desist from the claim which she brought against your monastery concerning the aforesaid church of Tyrcio, and that your monastery shall peacefully possess that place with its appurtenances.

Therefore no person may rashly disturb you or your successors concerning this our confirmation, or bring upon you any diminution or opposition on that account. But if anyone, with rash presumption, should dare to act contrary to these provisions, let him incur the indignation of Almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul, and be subject to excommunication until he repents of his presumption and makes fitting satisfaction. Amen, amen, amen.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman [Col. 0453B] Church, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of May [20 April], in the second indiction, in the year 1139 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CCCXCV. Bull confirming the replacement by Premonstratensians at the abbey of Pöhlde.  
*(Year 1139, 20 April.)*

[HUGO, *Premonstratensian Annals*, II, 386.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son CONRAD, provost of the Church of Pöhlde, and to your successors regularly promoted in perpetuity.

Whenever that which is recognized as belonging to reason is requested from us, it is fitting that we grant it willingly and confer the desired assistance. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Provost Conrad, we graciously consent to your requests and strengthen by the page of this present writing the Church of Pöhlde, over which by the Lord’s appointment you preside. First, indeed, we decree that the canonical order, known to have been instituted there according to the Rule of blessed Augustine and the form of religious life of Norbert, archbishop of Magdeburg, of revered memory, shall be preserved inviolate for all future time. [Col. 0453C]

Moreover, we confirm to you and your successors—and through us to the same church—the third part of the court of Palidum with all its revenues, fields, woods, pastures, fisheries, cultivated and uncultivated lands; and, in addition, whatever possessions and goods the same church now justly and lawfully possesses, bestowed by bishops, kings, princes, or other faithful of God, and may hereafter acquire through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings, generosity of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means through God’s favour, shall remain secure and undiminished to you and your successors. No one shall presume to demand from you tithes of the produce which you cultivate by your own hands and at your own expense, or of the increase of your animals. Nor may any layman take away or retain things belonging to the maintenance of the brethren. You shall have authority to receive and retain in your community secular clerics or laypersons fleeing the world to you, unless they are excommunicated or held in servile condition. [Col. 0454A]

But one received or retained, after making profession, shall not leave your cloister without the permission of the provost and brethren, nor transfer to another place under the pretext of any religious order. No bishop or abbot may retain such a person, but shall compel him, as a transgressor, to return to the place from which he departed. You shall have authority to excommunicate those who, having become apostates, return to the world. We also grant that the burial-place of that house shall be free, so that no one may obstruct the devotion and last will of those who determine to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated; while preserving in all things the reverence and right of the diocesan bishop.

We decree, therefore, that no bishop, cleric, layman, knight, or person whatsoever [Col. 0454B] may rashly disturb your aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be kept whole, to serve in every way the benefit of those for whose government and support they were granted. Should any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, rashly attempt to contravene it, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his offence by fitting satisfaction, let him lose the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself liable before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and at the last judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. [Col. 0454C] But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Gerhard, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Martin, cardinal priest of St Stephen on the Caelian Hill.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Henry, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of May [20 April], in the year 1138 of the Lord’s Incarnation, [Col. 0454D] in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CCCXCVI. Diploma declaring that the Church of Ferrara is a special daughter of the Roman Church and that its county is part of the patrimony of St Peter.  
*(Year 1139, 22 April.)*

[COCQUELINES, II, 244.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother GRYPHO, bishop of Ferrara, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

We see that, by the Lord’s ordering, we have been placed in the chair of the Apostolic See in order that we may bear the care of all churches, render to each its due, and preserve intact its right, especially in the case of those which belong to blessed Peter. Therefore, after the death of Landulf, bishop of the city of Ferrara, certain clerics and laypersons acting generally as representatives came into our presence and humbly entreated us to give a bishop to the Church of Ferrara according to the tenor of its privileges.

But because at that time our venerable brother G., archbishop of Ravenna, opposing them, asserted that the consecration of the bishop of Ferrara ought to be performed by himself, we ordered them both by letters and orally to come to the next synod with wise and discerning men, authentic documents, and other evidence [lacuna], so that then, with the Lord’s help, they might obtain justice, which [lacuna] is. Having therefore seen and carefully examined [Col. 0455B] the privileges and arguments both of the people of Ferrara and of the aforesaid complaining archbishop, we found the documents of the Ferrarese to prevail.

Having therefore taken counsel with our brother bishops and cardinals, we decreed that the bishop of Ferrara should be elected according to the tenor of the Ferrarese privileges and consecrated by the bishop of the Roman See; and we decreed that the Church of Ferrara should remain under the right and lordship of the Apostolic See. These matters having been accomplished, beloved son in the Lord, Grypho, we consecrate you bishop, invoking the grace of the Holy Spirit—you having been chosen from among our cardinals, a cardinal of our Holy Roman Church and archpriest of the title of St Pudentiana—and we confirm to you, for governing the flock of the Church of Ferrara, as a daughter of the Apostolic See, the estates and patrimonies of that same mother.

Namely, we confirm the Babylonian estate called Ferraria, with its twelve *fundi* (landholdings); to it we subject another eleven smaller estates with every obligation and service: that is, the estate and riverbank of Palatiolum with its twelve *fundi*; the estate of Constanciacus with its twelve *fundi*; likewise the estate of Quartisiana with its twelve *fundi*; and the entire estate of Donoro with its twelve *fundi*. [Col. 0455C] Likewise, the estate of Populare with its twelve *fundi*; moreover, the estate of Curulum and the estate of Salesta with their twenty-four *fundi*; and the estate of Senetica and Castilione likewise with their *fundi*.

We donate and convey, by this page of donation and transfer, these aforesaid estates, with everything belonging to their rights, from the lordship, right, and authority of this Holy Roman Church to the holy Church of Ferrara, so that from this hour onward it shall be lawful for you, dearest brother Bishop Grypho, and your successors, in each estate to appoint and consecrate churches with clerics, deacons, and priests. We decree in every respect that the Church of Ferrara, with its whole parish, shall forever be preserved in the right, lordship, and privilege of our Holy Roman Church of blessed Peter, whose patrimony it is; and that it shall always be under our jurisdiction, appointment, and consecration, so that whoever is elected, ordained, and consecrated there by us [Col. 0456A] shall exercise this honour and authority in their full integrity.

The boundaries and limits of the county of Ferrara are as follows. On the eastern side, on one side of the River Po, are our estate of Fiscalia and Veteraria; the boundary extends as far as the ditch of Bosso, crosses the River Sandalo to Pucilletum, crosses the River Gabiana by Luduria, encircles the large village and Madrasia, and reaches Maletum. From Maletum it proceeds beside Argile Ansianum through marshes and fisheries to Vitrica; crossing Vitrica, it comes to the Burana ditch, enters the Po, and descends westward to Ulmus Formosa, which is the fixed boundary between Romagna and Lombardy.

On the other side of the river, the boundaries likewise begin eastward at the hill of the boundary, which is the boundary [Col. 0456B] between our county of Ferrara and our other county of Comacchio; they extend through marshes and fisheries as far as the Fossato of Silvula, encircle the estate of Corneto and Longano, which belongs to our county of Ferrara, then descend westward through marshes and fisheries to the River Tartaro, and proceed to the River Po.

Indeed, we remove evil and oppressive customs from the inhabitants of the greater estate of Ferrara, provided nevertheless that, as they have been accustomed, each free person, as a head of household, shall annually pay one Venetian penny through their messenger toward the support of the Holy Roman Church. Of the rent, tribute, and toll from the riverbank, we grant one half, as a benefaction, for the common utility, improvement, or restoration of the aforesaid greater estate; the other half we reserve to ourselves. Likewise, we remit one half of the market toll to our aforesaid bishop.

We retain the general court in the lordship and authority of our Holy Roman Church, provided that, when our messenger administers justice once a year, it shall be observed by all for three days. But we exact no levy or *fodrum*, no evil or unjust service, payment, or customary due; rather, out of fear and love of God, we have remitted all such things to all inhabitants of that greater estate of our aforesaid holy Church of St George, and we subject to it the other smaller estates, as stated above, with all their [Col. 0456D] obligations.

If any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to contravene it, or should presume either to diminish the Church of Ferrara in the matters stated above or to take away from the Holy Apostolic See its rights in them, as set forth above, he shall pay to that Holy Apostolic See, as a penalty and composition, one hundred pounds of the finest gold. Unless he corrects by fitting satisfaction what he has wrongly presumed, let him lose the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself liable before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be excluded from the most holy body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the [Col. 0457A] last judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance.

But upon all who preserve the rights of these churches may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Anselm, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina. I, Lictifrid, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina. I, Ivo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence and Damasus. [Col. 0457B] I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul. I, Martin, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Azo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia. I, Boetius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement. I, Chrysogonus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Constantius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Theodewin, bishop of Saint Rufina. [Col. 0457C] I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Vassallo, cardinal deacon of Saint Eustace beside the temple of Agrippa. I, Ubald, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Angelo. I, Ubald, cardinal of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Gerhard, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Domnica. [Col. 0457D] I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in Carcere. I, Ubald, deacon of Saint Adrian.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aymeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the tenth day before the Kalends of May, in the second indiction, in the year 1139 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CCCXCVII. Privilege for the Church of Selbold. (Year 1139, April 25.)

[WENCK, *Hessian Territorial History*, II, charter 86.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 0458A] son LUTOLD, provost of Saint John the Baptist at Selbold, and to his successors canonically appointed for ever.

The authority of our office urges us to cherish religious places and to foster them under the protection of the Apostolic See. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord Lutold, we grant your just petitions and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the church of Saint John the Baptist, over which, by God’s authorisation, you preside; and we fortify it by the present document. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods that venerable place now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future, by the grant of pontiffs, the gifts of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God favouring, [Col. 0458B] acquire, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and to your successors.

Among these we have thought it proper to specify: the parish church at Selbold, with its appurtenances, lands, and tithes, on the condition, namely, that you shall answer for it to no person and to no bishop; vineyards in Alta Villa granted to you by Walther and Hartmann. Moreover, concerning the produce which you gather by your own hands and at your own expense, we absolutely forbid the exaction of tithes from you. We likewise forbid your brethren or conversi, after making profession, to leave the cloister or transfer themselves to another place without the permission of their superior or brethren. No bishop, abbot, ecclesiastical person, or secular person shall dare receive or retain those who depart. [Col. 0458C] If, after being admonished a second or third time, they disdain to return, you shall have authority to excommunicate them.

You shall receive the ordination of clerics, the consecration of churches or altars, and other ecclesiastical sacraments from the Archbishop of Mainz, if he is Catholic, enjoys the favour of the Apostolic See, and is willing to confer them graciously and without impropriety; otherwise, you may apply to whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what is requested. We further decree that, because of a general interdict, the aforesaid parish church shall not be deprived of divine worship; rather, with the doors closed and the excommunicated and interdicted excluded, you may celebrate the divine offices in a low voice. Nor shall you be compelled to pay tithes on the fodder of your animals.

[Col. 0458D] Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb your aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain possessions taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all shall be preserved entire, for the full benefit of the uses of those for whose governance they were granted. If anyone in future attempts to contravene this our decree, let that person be deprived of the dignity of authority and honour, be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, and be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance. But those who preserve these provisions shall obtain the grace of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul. As a token of the liberty received from the Roman [Col. 0459A] Church, you shall pay one Byzantine coin annually to us and our successors.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Berard, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul. I, Martin, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Azo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia. I, Chrysogonus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Angelo.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aimeric, [Col. 0459B] cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Kalends of May, in the year 1139 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CCCXCVIII. He confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of Saint Bertin at Sithiu, freed from the authority of the Cluniacs, imposing upon the monks an annual rent of one ounce of gold. (Year 1139, April 26.)

[Collection of Cartularies, III, 310.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son LEO, abbot of Saint Bertin, and to his successors regularly appointed for ever.

Those provisions instituted by the holy Fathers for the enduring benefit of churches or monasteries [Col. 0459C] ought not to be overthrown by any wrongdoing or disturbed by any change of times. And the greater the reverence shown by all churches to the Apostolic See, the more diligently ought we to be concerned for their protection and to provide attentively for their tranquillity. Therefore, beloved son in God, Abbot Leo, we have thought it proper to commit to parchment and ink for the memory of posterity the decision of the controversy long disputed between you and our beloved son Peter, abbot of Cluny, concerning the subjection which that abbot claimed for himself in your monastery.

Since that abbot and his brethren repeatedly complained before us of the withdrawal of subjection and [Col. 0459D] obedience which was denied him by the monastery of Saint Bertin, you were summoned to appear before us in answer. When, at the appointed time, you presented yourself before us, the aforesaid abbot neither came nor sent a representative, although, at your own inconvenience and expense, you had remained at our court until the time of the council and had waited a long while for the other party. That abbot nevertheless came to the council but declined to pursue the complaints for which a date between you had been fixed. Your belovedness, however, for that reason did not present yourself any less often for justice, both in the plenary synod and in the Lateran palace before us.

[Col. 0460A] Accordingly, after carefully inspecting the privileges of both parties and taking counsel with our brother bishops and cardinals, we follow with reasonable diligence the judgment pronounced in this matter by our predecessor Pope Paschal of holy memory, with the judgment of his brother bishops and cardinals, and confirmed by his successor Pope Calixtus of apostolic memory. The privileges which the Cluniacs asserted that they possessed from the Apostolic See concerning this matter having been annulled, justice so requiring, we release both you and your successors and brethren, and the monastery of Saint Bertin, from this suit and from subjection to the Cluniacs. We restore that monastery to its liberty; and, without prejudice to the right of the church or bishop of Thérouanne, decree that the same place shall remain perpetually under the jurisdiction and protection of the Roman Church alone.

We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods the said place now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future, by the grant of pontiffs, the gifts of kings, the liberality of princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God favouring, acquire, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought it proper to set forth in their own terms:

[Col. 0460B] In the parish of Thérouanne: the church of Saint Margaret; the church of Saint John; Saint Martin; the church of Harbela; the church of Petrenessa; and the church of Torbessem, free as of old from every episcopal due; the church of Broborg with its chapels; likewise, two sheaves of the tithe of newly cleared land, wherever it may accrue throughout the whole parish of Broborg, which extends to the boundaries of neighbouring parishes, and which Baldwin of Lille, count of Flanders, and his son Robert, and their successors, granted and confirmed to the church of Saint Bertin.

[Col. 0460C] The church of Archas with the same vill; the church of Popringhem with the same vill; the church of Steenkerka; the church of Bruxele; the church of Scales; the church of Bovrinkehem with their vills; the vill of Aldefort, of Ostresela, and of Rokestoir, with the land which the Church bought from Arnulf of Venti and other adjoining lands; the allod which Clarembald gave in the vill of Lustinghem; the church of Coeka and the church of Helcin with their vills, and a share of the church of Vualnas; the church of Locanes and Aquina; the church of Hunela with the same vill; the altar of Merchem, granted to you by the venerable Bishop John.

In the parish of Noyon: Canetekurt, that is, Calmunt. [Col. 0460D] In the parish of Tournai: the church of Rokeshem; the church of Hedinghem; the church of Westkerke; and the tithe of Clemeskerke; the church of Hitinghem; the church of Lisimega; the church of Snelguekerke; the church of Erninghem; the church of Bovenkerke. In the parish of Arras: the church of Vuerkin; the church of Salomones; the church of Hautay. In the territory of Furnes: an annual rent of forty pounds, which Charles gave for the soul of Count Baldwin; and the land of Buri, which your church is known to possess in the district of Beauvais.

In the parish of Boulogne: the church of Ferkena and the church of Gildestorp with their appurtenances; and we command that no exaction be levied from these by bishops or their officers on any pretext, saving the bishops’ annual revenues. [Col. 0461A] Also the church of Coclers, which Baldric, bishop of the church of Tournai, granted to Lambert, abbot of good memory, and to his successors to administer, together with the altar of Rusleta, free from every exaction except ten solidi of pence, payable annually from Rusleta to the bishop.

Also the whole area of the precinct lying on every side between your basilica and the middle course of the river Agnion, with the fisheries of Mera and Grath, Mardic and Stranguere, and Langha, and adjoining cultivated or uncultivated lands, as you have possessed them of old. Again, in the parish of Thérouanne: the church of Oxelara, the church of Vuarnestim, the church of Saint Mary called [Col. 0461B] Eggafrid’s chapel, and the church of Haveskerke.

We also grant that the appointment of the abbot in the monastery of Saint Silvin at Alciacum shall always be subject to your disposition, according to the custom of former times. We absolutely prohibit the bishop from holding public visitations in that monastery, and prohibit that bishop from coming there frequently unless summoned by the abbot and brethren. Upon the death of you, the present abbot of the same place, no one shall be placed there by any trick of usurpation or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall elect according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict.

Moreover, we decree that in all your parishes no one shall presume, without your consent, to build a church or monastery or to retain one already built; and no priest or cleric shall, without your grant, have leave to remain in your churches or chapels, or presume to celebrate divine offices in them. [Col. 0461C] As a token of this liberty received from the Roman Church, you shall annually pay an ounce of gold to us and our successors.

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the said monastery in respect of this our grant and confirmation, take away its possessions, retain possessions taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any other vexations; but that all shall be preserved entire, to the full benefit of the uses of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If in future any king, duke, margrave, prince, count, archbishop, bishop, or other ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this document of our constitution, attempts recklessly to contravene it, then, after a second or third warning, unless that person makes suitable satisfaction by amendment, let that person be deprived of the dignity of authority and honour, know that he or she is answerable before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance.

[Col. 0461D] But upon all who preserve the rights of that church may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and acquire hereafter the rewards of eternal blessedness. Amen, amen, amen.

[Col. 0462A] I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Haymeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the sixth day before the Kalends of May, in the second indiction, in the year 1139 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

HELP US, O GOD OF OUR SALVATION.

### CCCXCIX. He urges Bishop Milo, Archdeacons Philip and Milo, and the whole chapter of the Morini, as well as Count Thierry of Flanders, Countess Sibyl, and the barons established throughout Flanders, to defend the liberty of the monastery of Saint Bertin at Sithiu. (Year 1139, April 26.)

[Collection of Cartularies, III, 313.]

[Col. 0462B]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons MILO, bishop of Thérouanne, PHILIP and MILO, archdeacons, and the whole chapter of the Morini; and also to THEODERIC, illustrious count of Flanders, to Sibyl, countess, and to the barons established throughout Flanders: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We wish your belovedness to know that our dearest son Leo, abbot of Saint Bertin, appeared before us when summoned concerning the complaint brought against him by the abbot and monks of Cluny. Yet the aforesaid abbot postponed his arrival until the council and, on the appointed day, did not appear before us. Again, at the time of the council, although both abbots were present, the abbot of Cluny declined to pursue his complaints; whereas the abbot of Saint Bertin repeatedly presented himself for justice and judgment, both in the plenary synod and in our Lateran palace.

[Col. 0462C] Therefore, after taking counsel with our brother bishops and cardinals and carefully inspecting the privileges of both parties, we have wholly freed the monastery of Saint Bertin from subjection to the Cluniacs; and, without prejudice to the right of the bishop and church of Thérouanne, have decreed that it shall remain perpetually under the jurisdiction of the Holy Roman Church alone and enjoy its liberty. Since this is so, we command and, by commanding, enjoin your belovedness to love and honour the aforesaid monastery [Col. 0462D] and our beloved son Leo, abbot of that place, and to take care to uphold them in their right.

Given at the Lateran, on the sixth day before the Kalends of May.

### CD. He writes to William Castellan and to both the greater and lesser inhabitants of the town of Saint-Omer concerning the protection of the liberty of the monastery of Saint Bertin at Sithiu. (Year 1139, April.)

[See Iperius’s *Chronicle*, in MARTÈNE, *Thesaurus*, vol. III, 639.]

### CDI. He receives the Church of the Holy Sepulchre at Jerusalem into protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. (Year 1139, April 27.)

[Eugène DE ROZIÈRE, *Cartulary of the Holy Sepulchre*, 74.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable [Col. 0463A] brother WILLIAM, patriarch of Jerusalem, and to the canons of the Holy Sepulchre professing the regular life, both present and future, for ever.

By the office entrusted to us by God, we are debtors both to those near at hand and to those far away. Therefore we grant your petitions, receive the Church of the Holy Sepulchre under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, and fortify it by the present document. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods that place now justly and lawfully possesses, or may in future, by the grant of pontiffs, the gifts of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God favouring, acquire, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you for ever.

[Col. 0463B] Among these we have thought it proper to specify: the church situated outside the castle of Barletta, on the southern side, in the honour and name of the Holy Sepulchre, with all its appurtenances. The founders of that place built it, with the consent and will of Bisantius, archbishop of Trani, on the condition that in every year the brethren of that church should pay the mother church only one pound of incense. The church of the Holy Sepulchre at Brindisi; the church of Saint Lawrence outside the gate of that city, with its appurtenances; likewise the church of the Holy Sepulchre outside the walls of the city of Troia, which our brother William, bishop of that city, granted to you with all its appurtenances; the church in honour of blessed Theodore, situated in the suburb of Benevento, with all its appurtenances, which our predecessor Pope Calixtus of holy memory gave to the Church of the Holy Sepulchre; and the church of Saint Apollinaris outside Bari.

[Col. 0463C] We decree that the burial rights of those churches shall remain as free and undisturbed as you are known to have possessed them until now. You shall receive chrism, holy oil, the consecration of altars, and the ordination of clerics to be advanced to holy orders from the diocesan bishops, provided that they are Catholic, enjoy the favour and communion of the Apostolic See, and are willing to confer these things freely and without impropriety; otherwise, you may apply to whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what is requested.

[Col. 0463D] Therefore we decree that no archbishop, bishop, archdeacon, or any other person may rashly disturb the aforesaid churches, take away their possessions, retain possessions taken away, diminish them, or improperly impose any burden upon their rectors; but that all shall be preserved entire, for the full benefit of the uses of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this document of our constitution, attempts rashly to contravene it, let that person be deprived of the dignity of authority and honour, be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, and be subject at the last judgment to severe [Col. 0464A] vengeance. But those who preserve these provisions shall obtain the grace of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Azo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Ivo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence [Col. 0464B] and Damasus, have subscribed. I, Grisogonus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Kalends of May, in the second indiction, in the year 1139 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CDII. To Peter the Venerable, Abbot of Cluny.—Confirmation of certain Cluniac possessions. (Year 1139, April 28.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 412.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son PETER, abbot of Cluny, and to his successors regularly appointed [Col. 0464C] for ever.

Those whom almighty God makes conspicuous by fuller distinction and the splendour of religion ought especially to be honoured by the Apostolic See and fostered with suitable supports. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Peter, embracing your person with fatherly affection, we confirm to you and your successors the gift made into our hand in devotion by the illustrious William of Montpellier and to be conveyed through us to the monastery of Cluny; and we decree that it shall remain valid and inviolable in perpetuity to the monastery of Cluny. We decree that an oratory and cemetery shall be built in that place, and that any persons coming from anywhere who decide to be buried there shall not be hindered by anyone, unless they are bound by the bond of excommunication; the right of the mother church being, of course, preserved.

[Col. 0464D] We further decree that whatever may hereafter, God favouring, be granted to the brethren serving God in that place by the grant of pontiffs, the gifts of princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and inviolable both to you and to those brethren, present and future. Likewise, the monastery of Saint Gervais of Fos, which was once a priory of the monastery of Cluny but has now, through the insolence of certain persons, been converted into an abbey, shall be restored to the status and order of a priory and shall remain for ever, with all its appurtenances, under the jurisdiction and disposition of that monastery.

[Col. 0465A] Furthermore, so that the sacred monastery of Cluny may always receive increase from good to better, we decree that the monastery of Saints Domitian and Ragnebert shall remain perpetually under your right and disposition and that of your successors, as is known to have been established by our venerable brother Peter, archbishop of Lyons and legate of the Apostolic See, and confirmed by his document and seal. Therefore no one may lawfully rashly disturb the monastery of Cluny in respect of this our grant and confirmation, take away its possessions, retain possessions taken away, or diminish them; but all shall be preserved entire, to the full benefit of the uses of those for whose support and governance they were granted. If any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this document of our constitution [Col. 0465B], etc.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Gerald, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Theodewin, bishop of Saint Rufina, have subscribed. I, Anselm, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed. I, Littifred, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina, have subscribed. I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen, have subscribed. [Col. 0465C] I, Martin, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Kalends of May, in the second indiction, in the year 1138 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CDIII. To Walter, Abbot of Senones.—Confirmation of the possessions of the monastery of Saint Stephen. (Year 1139, April 28.)

[*Gallia Christiana*, XIII, *Instruments*, 498.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son WALTER, abbot of the monastery of Senones, and to his successors, etc. . . . .

For this reason, beloved son in the Lord Walter, abbot, we graciously grant the petitions of you and of our venerable brother Stephen, bishop of Metz. We strengthen by the protection of our favour the monastery of Saint Stephen, commonly called Le Monier, situated beside the castle of Danubrium, freely granted and established by that bishop’s gift for those who serve there for ever, consecrated through the intervention of the aforesaid bishop and other religious men by our brother Lethuin of Saint Rufina, then legate of the Apostolic See, and over which, by God’s authorisation, you preside, etc. We decree that whatever possessions, etc., shall remain firm to you and to your successors; among these we have thought it proper to specify in their own terms:

[Col. 0466A] A garden with meadow; your right of ban in the waters, woods, and pastures, as granted you by the bishop of good memory aforesaid; etc. The remission of twenty solidi for Varta of the castle of Danubrium; saltworks exempt from every payment of whatever kind; the remission of five solidi for the crane-shaped gallows situated above the well in the town of Metz; the church of Ramberti-villa, with its revenues and both greater and lesser tithes; the allod of Bossemont; and the fourth part of the church which a certain Siccard rendered to the same monastery into the hand of the bishop named above; and one quarter of the allod which the same Siccard, with his wife, lawfully gave to the same church at Fontiniac; the entire half of the whole allod which had belonged to Arnold of good memory, etc.

Pope Innocent II.

I, Gerard, cardinal priest of Holy Cross [Col. 0466B] in Jerusalem.

I, Lucas, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, and several other cardinals, etc.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Almeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Kalends of May, in the second indiction, in the year 1139, and in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CDIV. He confirms the goods and privileges of the Church of Lincoln. (Year 1139, April 28.)

[*Monasticon Anglicanum*, III, p. 269.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother ALEXANDER, bishop of Lincoln, and to his successors canonically appointed for ever.

[Col. 0466C] Although, by the office and benevolence of the apostolate entrusted to us by God, we are debtors to all churches and ecclesiastical persons, we ought nevertheless to provide with more earnest devotion of charity for those whom we know to be readier and more devoted in the service of blessed Peter and of ourselves. With this purpose, venerable brother Bishop Alexander, we grant your desires with fraternal kindness and fortify by the protection of this document the Church of Lincoln, whose government, by God’s authorisation, you administer. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods that place now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future, by the gifts of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just [Col. 0466D] means, God favouring, acquire, shall remain firm and unimpaired for ever to you and your successors and also to the canons of that church. Among these we have thought it proper to specify in their own terms:

Namely, the abbey of Eynsham with its tenements; Newark with its appurtenances and with royal jurisdiction over three wapentakes, which the kings of England granted to the Church; Stow with its appurtenances; Norton; Louth; Nareham; and the land which the aforesaid church has in Lincoln, namely Westgate with its appurtenances, both outside and within the walls of that city; and the land which King Stephen gave both to you and to your successors for building episcopal residences, with land assessed at twenty solidi for restoring those residences, on the southern side of the church, together with the church of Saint [Col. 0467A] Michael situated upon that land; the church of All Saints, with other churches of the aforesaid city; Asford; Holme with its appurtenances; the manor of Leicester, outside and inside the walls, where there are two churches with thirty-two burgesses’ dwellings; Banbury and Cropredy with its hundred and liberties; Dorchester with its hundred and liberties; and Thame and Middleton with its hundred and liberties; Kilsby with its appurtenances; Woburn with its appurtenances; Biggleswade; Spaldwick, which manor was given to the Church of Lincoln as compensation for a part of its diocese called Cambridgeshire, which is now the bishopric of Ely; and Bugden.

[Col. 0467B] We also confirm the liberty of the Church of Lincoln with its diocese: namely, Lincolnshire with all Lindsey; Northamptonshire with Rutland; Leicestershire; Oxfordshire; Buckinghamshire; Bedfordshire; Huntingdonshire; and the greater part of Hertfordshire.

We also confirm the lands which King Stephen granted in compensation to the aforesaid church and the canons serving God there for eighteen pounds of pence which the canons used to have, by royal grant, in the manors of Kirketon and Caster: namely, in Thorpe three carucates of land and seven bovates; in Pisehanc two carucates and five bovates of land, and two parts of one bovate; in Gillebi and in Warton seven bovates; and at Trent nine and a half bovates. Furthermore, Walton; the church of Aleberes [Col. 0467C] with its appurtenances; the church of Leighton; the church of Buckingham with its appurtenances; the church of Sutton with its appurtenances; the manor of Welton with its appurtenances; and the other ecclesiastical possessions of the canons of that church—we confirm them as firm to the aforesaid church and those canons.

We also confirm Leighton and the land of Bidefordstam, both within and outside the borough, with its liberties.
