We likewise confirm by apostolic authority for ever to you and your successors the remission of military service owed from the bishopric of Lincoln, which your predecessors customarily performed at Lincoln Castle. King Henry of glorious memory remitted to the Church of Lincoln, and to you and your successors, the service of a third knight; he granted that this service should instead be performed for your castle at Newark and confirmed this by his charter.

[Col. 0467D] Upon the death of you, venerable brother Bishop Alexander, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed over the Church of Lincoln by any trick of usurpation or violence, except one whom the clergy and people [Col. 0468A] by common consent, or the sounder part of the council, shall judge fit to elect according to the fear of God and the decrees of the holy canons. Furthermore, the liberty granted to that church by the illustrious Stephen, king of the English, we also strengthen in the name of our authority.

Among the other marks of that liberty we have thought it especially proper to insert in this decree that, at your death or that of your successors, while the episcopal see is vacant, no one whatsoever shall presume to usurp episcopal or ecclesiastical goods. Rather, all churches and their possessions shall remain in the free custody and power of the clergy, to be preserved for the use of the future bishop and the benefit of that church. Therefore no one at all may rashly disturb you or your church concerning this our constitution or confirmation, take away its possessions, retain possessions taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but all shall be preserved entire, for the full benefit of the uses of those for whose governance and support they were granted.

[Col. 0468B] If in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this document of our constitution, attempts rashly to contravene it, then, after a second or third warning, unless that person suitably amends the offence, let that person be deprived of the dignity of authority and honour, know that he or she is answerable before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and be subject at the last judgment to severe [Col. 0468C] vengeance.

But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Almeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Kalends of May, in the second indiction, in the year 1138 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CDV. He grants a bull to the monastery of Pfäfers. (Year 1139, April 29.)

[WEGELIN, *Regesta of Pfäfers*, p. 7.]

CDVI. To the clergy and people of Reims.—No new laws are to be instituted.  
[Note: [Col. 0467D] Through a singular mistake, this document in the white book of the chapter is found after the charter issued in 1198 by William of the White Hands, prohibiting the subjects of the chapter from forming a commune with the subjects of the archbishop. It is attributed to Innocent III and bears the title: “Confirmation by the pope of the same prohibition.” By a coincidence as singular as the error of which we [Col. 0468D] speak, the page on which Cocquault (vol. II, p. 426) reported this bull under the year 1140, and stated that the original was still preserved in the chapter treasury, has been torn away throughout the portion containing the citation of the text itself. Did the chapter wish to make the emancipated municipal body bear the anathema pronounced against an unsuccessful first attempt at emancipation, and by a fraud restore an initial [Col. 0469C] interest to an act which otherwise would have lost all [Col. 0469D] its relevance? We would find that difficult to believe, and we attribute the two facts just noted to ignorance and chance. Moreover, seventy years after Cocquault, Marlot (II, 330) listed this document under its true date.]. (A.D. 1139, April 30.)

[VARIN, *Archives administratives de Reims*, I, I, p. 300; Cartulary G of the chapter, fol. 2; White Book of the chapter, fol. 122.]

[Col. 0468D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 0469A] sons, the clergy and people of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Justice and reason require that the goods of any vacant see of the Church must not be rashly seized by anyone, but must be preserved in that condition and freedom in which they stood while the pastor was alive. Therefore, we command your whole community and order by apostolic authority that you introduce no new laws or customs whatsoever into the city of Reims; but rather leave it entirely in the condition and freedom in which it is known to have stood in the time of our brother of good memory, R., your archbishop. But if any persons presume to establish a commune in that city, we declare such an act void; and, under penalty of anathema, we prohibit by apostolic authority the establishment of such a commune among you. [Col. 0469B]

Given at the Lateran, on the second day before the Kalends of May [30 April].

CDVII. At the request of Peter, abbot of Cluny, he confirms the possessions of Romainmôtier. (A.D. 1139, April 30.)

[*Mémoires et documents de la Suisse romande*, vol. III, p. 581.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son PONTIUS [Note: [Col. 0469D] Ponce, prior of Romainmôtier, was already prior in 1135; he is then mentioned as a witness in a charter of the bishop of Lausanne for Guignes, prior of Payerne (see *Annales de l’abbaye du Lac de Joux*, p. 10).], and to the brethren of the monastery of Romainmôtier, present and future, greeting in the Lord.

As assent is not to be granted to those who seek what is unjust, so the petition of those desiring what is lawful ought not to be delayed. Accordingly, beloved son in the Lord, Prior Pontius, at your request and through the intervention of our beloved son Peter [Note: [Col. 0469D] Peter the Venerable, abbot of Cluny.], abbot of Cluny, we graciously accede to your petitions; and we fortify by the text of this present privilege the monastery of Romainmôtier, over which, by the Lord’s appointment, you preside. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the said monastery now justly and canonically possesses shall remain secure and inviolate to you and your successors. Among these we have thought it proper to state expressly the following: in the archbishopric of Besançon, the church of Bannens and the chapel of Saint Columba [Note: [Col. 0469D] Bannens and Sainte-Colombe in the arrondissement of Pontarlier.].

In the bishopric of Lausanne: the church of Béthusi [Note: [Col. 0469D] Béthusi near Lausanne.] with its appurtenances [Col. 0470A]; the church of Lully [Note: [Col. 0469D] Lully near Estavayer.] with its appurtenances; the chapel of the hospice of Orbe [Note: [Col. 0469D] Important monasteries formerly had hospices in the principal town of their vicinity, with attached chapels or churches. A few brethren [Col. 0470C] received there the prior, procurator, and religious [Col. 0470D] whom business or illness drew away from their solitude.]; the chapel of Gumoens; the obedience (*obedientia*) of the valley of Orbe, with its chapel [Note: [Col. 0470D] *Obedientia* does not mean patronage, but an obedience. An obedientiary was a religious who served a benefice by order of a superior. The obedientiary, always an ecclesiastic and sometimes entrusted with the care of souls, was subordinate to a higher establishment from which he derived his powers and which presented him for the ordinary’s canonical institution (note by M. Duvernois). In the present charter a chapel is mentioned at Vallorbes; in another of 1148 it is a church. The foundation of the priory of Vallorbes is doubtless later.]; the church of Mollens, with its chapels of Ballens and Torclens [Note: [Col. 0470D] Mollens, Ballens, and Torclens; the latter village has been destroyed.]; the church of Apples, with its appurtenances.

In the bishopric of Geneva: the church of Bursins, with its chapels of Bursinel and Gimel [Note: [Col. 0470D] Bursins, Bursinel, and Gimel, which soon ceased to be chapels.]; the church of Saint Eugendus [Note: [Col. 0470D] Saint-Oyens, not far from Gimel.].

Moreover, whatever the same place may hereafter acquire, by grants of popes, gifts of kings, liberality of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other reasonable means, with God’s favor, we likewise confirm to you and your successors with firm and unshaken stability. We decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery on account of this our grant and confirmation, or take away, retain when taken away, or diminish its possessions; but that all things be wholly preserved intact for the benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted. Should any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing this text of our constitution, rashly attempt to act against it, and, after a second or third warning, fail to make suitable satisfaction by proper amendment, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honor; let that person know himself or herself guilty before the divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let that person be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer; and at the last judgment let that person be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here [Col. 0470C] the fruit of good action and in the future obtain the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

Monogram.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Theodewin, bishop of Santa Rufina, have subscribed. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. [Col. 0471A] I, Bernard, cardinal-priest of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal-deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Otto, cardinal-deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Lucas, cardinal-priest of the two Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Martin, cardinal-priest of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill, have subscribed. I, Ivo, cardinal-priest of Saint Lawrence in Damaso, have subscribed. I, Boethius, cardinal-priest of Saint Clement, have subscribed. I, Brisagonus, cardinal-priest of Saint Praxedes, [Col. 0471B] have subscribed. I, Hubald, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal-deacon of Saint Angelo, have subscribed. I, Gerard, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Domnica, have subscribed. I, Octavian, cardinal-deacon of Saint Nicholas in Carcere, have subscribed.

Given at Latii, through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal-deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Kalends of May [30 April], in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1139, second indiction, in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

[Col. 0471C] (The lead seal of Innocent II is appended to it by a red silk cord.)

CDVIII. Bull for the monastery of Juncelles. (A.D. 1139, May 1.)

[*Gallia Christiana*, VI, documents, 136.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son WILLIAM, abbot of Saint Peter of Juncelles, and to his successors to be regularly appointed in perpetuity.

It befits apostolic dignity to end the controversies of litigants either by a definitive judgment or by agreement, and, lest disputes be prolonged without end, to provide with attentive vigilance that they may instead be brought to rest. With this end in view, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot William, we confirm by this present document the agreement made in our Lateran palace between you and the abbot of Psalmodi and his brethren, by the consent of both parties and through the reasonable efforts of our venerable brothers William, bishop of Nîmes, and Everard, bishop of Uzès, as well as the abbots Peter of Saint-Gilles and Peter of Marseille. We decree that it shall remain valid and unshaken in future times, imposing by this present decree perpetual silence upon the aforesaid abbot and his brethren regarding subjection or any other claims which they asserted in your monastery. We decree that whatever possessions and goods [Col. 0472A] the aforesaid monastery of Juncelles now justly and canonically possesses, or may thereafter acquire through grants of popes, the liberality of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, by the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and inviolate to you and your successors. Among these we have thought it proper to state expressly the following, etc., as in the bull of 1135, above no. 183.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal-deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the Kalends of May [1 May], second indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1139, in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II. [Note: [Col. 0471D] In the same archive there exist two other bulls of exactly the same style and tenor: one of Pope Lucius [Col. 0472D] III, to Abbot Deodatus, dated 1184; the other of Clement IV, dated 1267, to the monks of Juncelles.]

CDIX. He confirms the privileges of the clergy of Ferrara. (A.D. 1139, May 23.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, II, 535.]

[Col. 0472B]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son GUALFRED, archpriest of the church of Ferrara, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The most holy Roman Church, which received from the Lord the keys and rights of the kingdom of heaven, has always lent its ear to the prayers of those dear to it and has always shown the favor of love to its faithful. Therefore, beloved son Gualfred, archpriest, knowing that your fidelity will be beneficial to us and to the Holy Roman Church, and giving attentive consideration to the prayers offered for you by all the cardinals and the whole Roman curia, we lend an ear to your prayers and willingly and carefully examine your documents. Having examined and completed these matters, we approve whatever Bishop [Col. 0472C] Landulf has secured from laymen concerning ecclesiastical dues, tithes, and firstfruits: henceforth no member of the clergy of Ferrara is to be compelled to pay tithes or any revenues to any layperson from his patrimonies or ecclesiastical possessions. Whatever has been established by Bishop Landulf concerning solemn masses and the funerals of the dead in the city of Ferrara, we confirm to you and your successors. Whatever in the *mundiburdium*—the imperial protection—of Emperor Otto we have seen to be pleasing to you, we establish and decree: namely, that all clerics of the community of the city of Ferrara shall be exempt from every payment and wholly from every secular and lay service.

Moreover, we will that your person and the goods which you justly have [Col. 0472D] and hold, or may hereafter justly acquire by God’s favor, be under our protection, and be guarded, fortified, and defended by the Holy Roman Church. And if you should consider yourself burdened in any ecclesiastical or secular matter, you may freely appeal to the holy apostolic see. But if anyone, in rash presumption, should presume rashly to violate this our command, let that person incur indignation and be struck by the sword of the authority of the Holy Roman Church and of ourselves. Amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Theoderinus, bishop of Santa Rufina, have subscribed. [Col. 0473A] I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Gerard, cardinal-priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Anselm, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed. I, Lampredus, cardinal-priest of the title of Vestina, have subscribed. I, Ivo, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Damaso, have subscribed. I, Lucas, cardinal-priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Martin, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill, have subscribed. I, . . . cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Boethius, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Clement, have subscribed. I, Sanctius, cardinal of the title of Saint Sabina, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal-deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. [Col. 0473B] I, Otto, cardinal-deacon of the title of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Vassallo, cardinal-deacon of Saint Eustace beside the temple of Agrippa, have subscribed. I, Ubald, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Almeric, cardinal-deacon and chancellor, on the tenth day before the Kalends of June [23 May], second indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1139, in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

CDX. Privilege for the monastery of Fonte Avellana. (A.D. 1139, May 24.)

[*Annales Camaldulenses*, III, p. 382.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 0473C] son BENEDICT, prior of the hermitage of the Holy Cross of Fonte Avellana, and to his brethren, present and future, in perpetuity.

As no effect is to be granted to those who seek what is unjust, so the petition of those desiring what is lawful should not be deferred. Indeed, if we respond with kindly intent to the prayers of religious men, we shall doubtless find the merciful Lord favorable to our own needs. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Prior Benedict, we grant apostolic assent to the petitions of both you and your brethren, and fortify by the privilege of the apostolic see the church of the Holy Cross of Fonte Avellana, in which you are devoted to divine service. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same place now [Col. 0473D] justly and canonically possesses, or may in future acquire through grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, with the Lord’s aid, shall remain secure and inviolate to you.

Among these we have thought it proper to state expressly the following: in the city of Rimini, the church of Saint Sylvester with all its appurtenances; and the things which you are known to possess both within and outside the city of Pesaro. In the county of Fano, within the city, the church of Saint Saviour with all its appurtenances, and the things which you hold in the estate of Monte Maggiore; the church of Saint Martin of Exaltaria with all its appurtenances; the church of Saint Martin of Barti; and the church of Saint Sylvester of Ruico with their appurtenances.

[Col. 0474A] In the county of Senigallia, within the city, the church of Saint Bartholomew with palace, houses, and its other appurtenances. Outside the same city, the church of Saint Septimius, the parish church of Saint Erasmus, and the church of Saint Mary of Cerreniano, with all their dependencies and appurtenances; the estate of Fractula with its churches and all its appurtenances; the church of Saint Eleutherius on the estate of Castellari, with other churches and their appurtenances; the estate of Calcinaria with its appurtenances; the castle of Loreto with its churches and all its appurtenances; one half of the castle of Nosula with its churches and appurtenances.

In the county of Osimo, the church of Saint Lawrence with its appurtenances; the church of Saint Superantius of Cingulo, with the other churches and their appurtenances. In the bishopric [Col. 0474B] of Umana, the church of Saint Mary of Recanati with the other churches and their appurtenances; the church of Saint Sylvester near the castle of Guicardi with all its appurtenances. In the county of Ascoli, the church of Saint Hilary near the city with all its appurtenances. In the county of Fermo, the right which you have in the church of Saint Paternian near the castle of Saint John with all its appurtenances; the church of Saint Leonard of Volubrio with its churches and their appurtenances. In the county of Camerino, the church of Saint Domninus of Valentiana with its churches and appurtenances; the church of Saint Damian with the other churches near the castle of Saint Anatolia; the church of Saint Michael of Acquavivola; the church [Col. 0474C] of Saint Michael of Caniseiane with all their appurtenances.

In the city of Spoleto, the church of Saint Andrew with all its appurtenances, and the church of Saint Fabian of Trevi with its appurtenances. In the county of Nocera, the church of the Holy Cross of Slaviniano; the church of Saint Antoninus of Postiniane; the church of Saint Blaise of Balciano; the church of Saint Romanus of Gaphano; the church of Saint Prosper of Glo. . . . . with all their appurtenances; the right which you have in the parish church of Saint Mary of Gualdo, and in the churches of Saint Mary of Rotundo, Saint Stephen of Gardinasia, and Saint Lawrence of Lametula, with all their appurtenances; and the church of Collalto.

In the county of Gubbio, the monastery of Saint Andrew of the Island with its castles, villages, churches, and all appurtenances; [Col. 0474D] the monastery of Saint Bartholomew of Campo Regiano with its castles, churches, hamlets, and all appurtenances; the monastery of Saint Peter of Salajolo with its churches, villages, and all appurtenances; the church of Saint Apollinaris of Bartiano with all its appurtenances, both within and outside the city; the castle of Castellari with the churches of Saint Sylvester and Saint Christopher and their appurtenances; the right which you have in the church of Saint Lawrence of Postserra with all its appurtenances; the church of Saint John of Bottano with all its appurtenances; likewise, the right which you have in the church of Saint Marianus of Palcano with all its appurtenances; the monastery of Saint Habundus and the parish church [Col. 0475A] of Saint Angelo of Clandida with their churches and all their appurtenances; the castle . . . . . with its appurtenances; the castle of Ripalta with its church and all its appurtenances; the church of Saint Mary of Pondu with its appurtenances.

In the county of Cagli, the church of Saint Bartholomew of Freruleta with all its appurtenances; the monastery of Saint Angelo of Sorticulo with its churches and all its appurtenances; the castle of Torre and the hill of Benno with their churches and all their appurtenances; the whole possession of Guido Acto in Surclano and other places; the church of Saint Martin of Monte Aculeo with all its appurtenances; the castle of Monte Sicone with the church of Saint Angelo and all its appurtenances; the church of Saint Bartholomew and the church [Col. 0475B] of Saint Marcellus of Taruco; the church of Saint Christopher of Scotaneto; the church of Saint Paternian, with the right which you have in the parish church of Saint Flavian, with its appurtenances.

In the county of Urbino, the church of Saint Mary of Rancalesto; the church of Saint Mary of Spineto; the church of Saint Marianus of . . . . .; Saint Peter of Cruccicula with houses and dwellings within the city and its other appurtenances. In the county of Città di Castello, the castle of Monte Maggiore; the monastery of the Holy Cross in that same castle, with other churches, villages, and all its appurtenances; likewise houses and dwellings within the city, with their appurtenances. In the county of Perugia, in the suburb of the city, the church of Saint [Col. 0475C] Quiricus with all its appurtenances; the right which you have in the church of Pilo; the church of Saint Blandus of Rantello; and the church of Saint Martin of Mantiniano with all their appurtenances; the hermitage of Saint Saviour of Monte Albo, with its churches, villages, and all its appurtenances.

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb you or your Church in regard to this our constitution, or take away, retain when taken away, diminish, or in any manner harass its possessions; but that all things be preserved entire and perpetually inviolate for the benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing this text [Col. 0475D] of our constitution, rashly attempts to act against it and, after a second or third warning, does not make amendment by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honor; let that person know himself or herself guilty before the divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let that person be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer; and at the last judgment let that person be subject to strict vengeance. But upon those preserving what belongs to that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here [Col. 0476A] they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

HELP US, O GOD, OUR SAVIOUR.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Gerard, cardinal-priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Godfrey, cardinal of the title of Vestina, have subscribed. I, Martin, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill, have subscribed. I, Guido, priest of the Holy Roman Church, have subscribed. I, Otto, cardinal-deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.

[Col. 0476B] Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aymeric, cardinal-deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the ninth day before the Kalends of June [24 May], second indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1139, in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II. [Note: [Col. 0475D] This privilege was sealed with a certain lead papal bull attached by red silk, upon which bull were depicted two human heads; above the heads were these letters: S. PA. S. Pe; on the other side were other letters: INNOCENTIUS PP. II. [Col. 0476D] There follow the attestations and testimonies of three notaries, James Soriane, Peter John, and John Peter, who acknowledge that in 1178 they copied this diploma from the autograph, in the presence of Andrew, judge, who added his decree, and many others.]

CDXI. He sends the pallium to Gaudius, archbishop of Salona. (A.D. 1139, May 24.)

[FARLATI, *Illyricum sacrum*, III, p. 173.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother, the archbishop of Salona, greeting and apostolic blessing.

As the authority of Blessed Gregory attests, and the records of deeds both ancient and modern [Col. 0476C] declare, the examination and consecration of the archbishop of Salona belong by ancient institution especially to the Roman pontiff. Therefore you know that you committed a grave offense against the holy Roman Church and wished, in rash presumption, to render void the keys of blessed Peter, when, scorning the dignity of the apostolic see, you hastened to another province and attempted, contrary to ancient custom, to receive consecration from the archbishop of Esztergom. Although, therefore, you have gravely transgressed, although you have attempted to kick against the goad, nevertheless, because our beloved son Béla, king of Hungary, frequently interceded for you with the apostolic see by letters and messengers, we have at last yielded to his prayers. Through our beloved son Hubald, cardinal-deacon—a man [Col. 0476D] indeed upright and learned in letters—we send to your brotherhood the pallium, the fullness of the pontifical office, a sign of humility and justice, so that you may use it on those days which are contained in the authentic records of your Church.

It is therefore your concern to show yourself so devoted and humble in all things toward blessed Peter, to devote yourself so earnestly to his service and to obey apostolic commands, that you may be found more worthy of this favor and that we may rejoice in the zeal of your conduct. Moreover, we decree that the bishops established throughout [Col. 0477A] Dalmatia as suffragans, whom Salona enjoyed in its flourishing time, shall obey with all reverence the holy Church of Split, where rests the body of Saint Domnius, disciple of blessed Peter. We know that this Church is to be the sole metropolitan of all Dalmatia in the Church of Salona, in accordance with what we find in our decrees. Likewise, because in your letters you complained of suffragans refusing to come to the council of the holy metropolitan Church of Salona, we decree that no synod shall be celebrated anywhere else in Dalmatia except in your metropolitan church, and that there all the suffragans of the aforesaid Church of Salona shall be consecrated according to customary practice.

Given at the Lateran, on the ninth day before the Kalends of June [24 May].

CDXII. He confirms the privileges granted by Pope Paschal II to the monastery of Jesus of Nazareth (Montearagón).—“Given at Ferentino, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of July, in the ninth year of our pontificate.” (A.D. 1139, June.)

[AYNSA, *Fundación de Huesca*, p. 455.]

[Col. 0477B]

CDXIII. He writes to Milo, bishop of Thérouanne, and Alvisus, bishop of Arras, concerning the dissolution of the marriage of M., constable of the count of Flanders. (A.D. 1139, June 12.)

[BALUZE, *Miscellanea*, II, 165.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable [Col. 0477C] brothers MILO, bishop of Thérouanne, and ALVISUS, bishop of Arras, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It has been reported to us that an objection of kinship is raised between M., constable of the count of Flanders, and his wife. Therefore, by these present letters we command your brotherhood to investigate this matter diligently; and if the same kinship is established before you through sufficient and suitable witnesses, you are to separate that union in accordance with the enactments of the canons of the Fathers.

Given at Ferentino, on the second day before the Ides of June [12 June].

CDXIV. To M[anfred], bishop of Mantua, and L[othair], bishop of Vicenza. (A.D. 1139, July 2.)

[TIRABOSCHI, *Storia di Nonantola*, I, p. 249.]

[Col. 0477D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers M[ANFRED], bishop of Mantua, and L., bishop of Vicenza, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It troubles us that, as we have learned from your letters, the bishop of Verona, summoned before you in the matter of the parish church of Nogara, was unwilling either to obey our command or to appear for your judgment. Therefore, by apostolic letters we have commanded him to restore that same parish church to our beloved son J., abbot of Nonantola, without prejudice to the right of the Church of Verona. During the coming Lent he is also to present himself before us, [Col. 0478A] prepared to carry out whatever reason shall prescribe.

Given at San Germano, on the sixth day before the Nones of July [2 July].

CDXV. He exhorts the archbishops and bishops of Sardinia to protect the churches of the monastery of Cassino. (A.D. 1139, July 6.)

[GATTULA, *Historia Cassinensis*, Supplement, vol. I, p. 430.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers, the archbishops and bishops established throughout Sardinia, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We ought to display all the greater concern for the defense of the possessions of the monastery of Cassino [Col. 0478B] because the same place, together with all that belongs to it, is known to belong in a special manner to the right of blessed Peter. But what we cannot bring into effect through our own presence, we must take care to accomplish through our brother archbishops and bishops. Therefore, commanding and ordering by apostolic letters, we direct your brotherhood to take care, for reverence toward blessed Peter and toward ourselves, to cherish and protect the churches and other goods which Saint Benedict possesses in your dioceses, and to defend them against the molestations of wicked persons. You are to inflict no injury or diminution upon them, nor allow it to be inflicted by others. But if any persons presume to harass them, you shall do them full justice. [Col. 0478C] Moreover, if any of the faithful wish to confer any of their goods upon those venerable places, you must by no means presume to forbid or oppose it.

Given at San Germano, on the second day before the Nones of July [6 July].

CDXVI. To Roger, king of Sicily.—He confirms the royal title granted to him by Honorius. (A.D. 1139, July 27.)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 396.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his dearest son in Christ, ROGER, illustrious and glorious king of Sicily, and to his heirs, in perpetuity.

[Col. 0478D] Those whom the dispensation of divine counsel has chosen from on high for the government and welfare of the people, and has fittingly adorned with prudence, justice, and the splendor of other virtues, it is worthy and reasonable that the bride of Christ, the holy and apostolic Roman mother Church, should love with sincere affection and advance from high things to yet higher. Indeed, it has been proved by manifest evidence that Robert Guiscard, duke of Apulia, your predecessor, the valiant and faithful knight of blessed Peter of illustrious memory, manfully overcame the Church’s mighty and powerful enemies, leaving to his posterity a name worthy of remembrance and an example of virtue worthy of imitation.

Your father, Roger of illustrious memory, likewise, through the toils of war and military conflicts, a fearless [Col. 0479A] destroyer of the enemies of the Christian name and a zealous promoter of the Christian religion, as a good and devoted son rendered manifold services to his mother, the holy Roman Church. Therefore our predecessor, the religious and prudent Pope Honorius, seeing your nobility descended from the aforesaid lineage, hoping greatly in you, and believing you adorned with prudence, fortified by justice, and fit for governing the people, loved you greatly and advanced you to higher things.

We, therefore, following in his footsteps and placing hope and confidence in your power for the honor and benefit of the holy Church of God, grant and confirm by apostolic authority to Your Excellency the kingdom of Sicily—which, as is reported in ancient histories, was unquestionably a kingdom—granted to you by that same predecessor, with the full integrity of royal honor and dignity belonging to kings. We likewise fortify with the strength of our favor and grant to you the duchy of Apulia granted to you by him, together with the principality of Capua. And, so that you may be more strongly bound to the love and service of blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, and to us and our successors, we have thought fit to grant these same things—namely the kingdom of Sicily, the duchy of Apulia, and the principality of Capua—to your heirs who, unless prevented by us and our successors, shall render liege homage to us and our successors and, at a suitable time and in a place not dangerous but safe and advantageous to us and to them, swear the fidelity which you swore. With God’s favor, we shall uphold them in the things [Col. 0479C] granted. But if they should by chance fail in this, those same heirs of yours shall nevertheless retain without diminution what they held.

The annual payment (*census*), as established—namely, six hundred *scifati*—shall be rendered each year by you and your heirs to us and our successors, unless an impediment should intervene; but once you remove the impediment, it shall nevertheless be paid. It is therefore your concern, dearest son, to show yourself so devoted and humble toward the honor and service of your mother, the holy Roman Church, and to exert yourself so earnestly in her needs, that the apostolic see may rejoice in so devoted and glorious a son and rest secure in his love.

If any ecclesiastical or secular [Col. 0479D] power rashly attempts to oppose this our grant, until it restrains its presumption by satisfaction, let it incur the indignation of Almighty God and of His apostles, the blessed Peter and Paul; and until it comes to its senses, let it be struck by the sentence of anathema. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. Haimeric, cardinal-deacon of the Holy Roman Church.

Given in the territory of Mamanum, through the hand of Chancellor Haimeric, on the sixth day before the Kalends of August [27 July], second indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1139, in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

CDXVII. To the canons of the church of Saint Antoninus at Piacenza. (A.D. 1139, October 3.)

[CAMPI, *Della Historia di Piacenza*, I, p. 412.]

[Col. 0480A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the canons of Saint Antoninus at Piacenza, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Of the death of our most dearly beloved son Azo, priest-cardinal and your provost, we grieve all the more deeply because we loved his person more closely, and because by his death greater services have been withdrawn from the Holy Roman Church and from us. Yet since in such a matter the one consolation of the Savior remains to us, [Col. 0480B] we exhort your whole community in the Lord that you persevere in unity and concord, and, having invoked the grace of the Holy Spirit, elect as your provost a suitable person through whose diligence that church itself may, God favoring it, be rightly governed, and under whose rule you may be able to advance both spiritually and temporally. Know that we love your persons and your place with paternal affection and, wherever it is expedient, shall furnish you counsel and aid, with the Lord’s help.

Given at Rome, on the fifth day before the Nones of October [3 October].

## CDXVIII. Privilege for St. George of Prüfening. (20 October 1139.)

*[Monumenta Boica, vol. XIII, p. 164.]*

[Col. 0480C]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son ERBO, abbot of the monastery of Blessed George at Prüfening, and to his successors to be regularly appointed forever.

Just as no effect is to be granted to those who seek what is unjust, so the petition of those who desire what is lawful ought not to be delayed. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Erbo, we graciously assent to your just petitions, and receive under the guardianship and protection of the Apostolic See the monastery of Blessed George at Prüfening, over which, by the Lord’s authority, you are known to preside, [Col. 0480D] and we strengthen it by the protection of the present document. We decree that whatever goods and possessions have been justly and canonically bestowed upon your monastery by our brother Otto, bishop of Bamberg, of good memory, and by his successor Egilbert with the consent of their brethren, or may hereafter be conferred upon the same place, God favoring it, by their successors or by other faithful people of God in like manner, whether by succession of pontiffs, gifts of kings, generosity of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other reasonable means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors.

Among these, the following appear to require specification by their proper names: the church of Seambach; Hemburen with its appurtenances; Gebenbhac with its appurtenances; Oberdorf; the church of Neuwen kirchen; [Col. 0481A] Icenronte; Abach; Dietburgerout, with its appurtenances.

We further add that, in the churches situated upon the land of your monastery, you may choose worthy priests, who are to be presented by you to the bishop and, if they are suitable, are to receive from that bishop the care of souls; they shall answer to him concerning spiritual matters, but to you concerning temporal matters. Moreover, except for the Roman pontiff and his legate, we forbid anyone to have permission to pronounce a sentence of interdict or excommunication in your monastery. If, however, a general interdict is imposed in that land, then, after excluding from your church those who are excommunicated or under interdict, you may celebrate the offices in a low voice behind closed doors. Nevertheless, if your bishop, by the counsel and judgment of religious men, decrees that any of these things ought to be done, [Col. 0481B] he shall nonetheless retain the authority to carry it out.

Furthermore, by apostolic authority we forbid tithes to be exacted from you for the produce which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense. Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb your monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any molestations; but let all things be preserved whole for the benefit, in every way, of those for whose governance and support they were granted.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, having been admonished a second or third time, unless he makes suitable satisfaction, [Col. 0481C] let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself to be liable before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and at the final judgment let him be subject to strict punishment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Theodewin, bishop of Santa Rufina, have subscribed. [Col. 0481D] I, Anselm, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed. I, Vassallus, deacon-cardinal of Saint Eustace beside the Temple of Agrippa, have subscribed. I, Peter Castellanus, bishop, have subscribed. I, Lucas, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Octavian, deacon-cardinal of Saint Nicholas in Prison, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aimeric, deacon-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of November, in the third indiction, in the year 1139 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Innocent II, pope.

## CDXIX. Privilege for the monastery of St. Magnus. (20 October 1139.)

*[HUNDII, Metropolis Salisburgensis, III, p. 522.]*

[Col. 0482A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son GEBEHARD, administrator of the church called “at the Banks,” and to his successors to be regularly appointed forever.

A desire shown to concern the purpose of religious life and the salvation of souls ought fittingly to be granted by us with a willing mind, and suitable assistance ought to be given to the desires of petitioners, so that faithful devotion may obtain a swift result and the benefit sought may undoubtedly gain strength. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord Gebehard, we gladly assent to your reasonable [Col. 0482B] petitions, and receive under the guardianship and protection of the Apostolic See the church called “at the Banks,” over which, by the Lord’s authority, you preside, and we strengthen it by the page of the present document.

First, we decree that the canonical order known to have been established in that place according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine shall be preserved inviolate forever. We also decree that whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and lawfully possesses, or may hereafter acquire, with the Lord’s help, by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors.

Therefore no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid [Col. 0482C] church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but let all things be preserved whole for the benefit, in every way, of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, having been admonished a second or third time, unless he makes suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself to be liable before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and at the final judgment let him be subject to strict punishment. [Col. 0482D] But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Lucas, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Grysogonus, priest-cardinal of the title of Praxedes, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hands of Aymeric, deacon-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of November, in the third indiction, in the year 1139 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Innocent II, pope.

## CDXX. To Egilbert, bishop of Bamberg: grants the right to wear the pallium and have the cross borne before him; grants other privileges. (20 October 1139.)

*[USSERMANN, Episcopatus Bamberg., documentary appendix 91.]*

[Col. 0483A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother EGILBERT, bishop of Bamberg, and to his successors to be canonically appointed forever.

The words of the Lord’s address to Peter, prince of the apostles, declare that the office of teaching the whole of ecclesiastical discipline was especially entrusted to blessed Peter, the keeper of the keys of heaven: “If you love me, feed my sheep”; and elsewhere: “I have prayed for you, Peter, that your faith may not fail”; and: “When you have turned, [Col. 0483B] strengthen your brethren.” For this reason the most holy Roman Church, which by heavenly privilege holds primacy over all others and judges not only earthly but also heavenly matters, is accustomed likewise to adorn with diverse prerogatives her children, whom she fills with the nourishment of divine law in maternal affection, and in her customary clemency to confer due honor on her members.

Therefore, venerable brother Bishop Egilbert, since, with the Lord cooperating, we ourselves consecrated you bishop as though by the very hands of blessed Peter, we grant to your person the pallium—the fullness of the pontifical office, the sign of humility and justice—for the celebration of the sacred solemnities of Mass. You may use it within the church only, on the days contained in the present document: namely, on the Lord’s Supper; Easter; Pentecost; the Nativity of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ; the feast of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul; the solemnities of Saint Dionysius and Saint George, martyrs; the anniversary day of your consecration; dedications of churches; and solemn ordinations of clerics. [Col. 0483C]

We wish you in every respect to vindicate the character of this pallium, and, God favoring you, to conduct yourself in all things so that the good may experience you as a kindly corrector and the wicked as a compassionate one. In this correction you must observe this order: love persons and pursue vices, lest, if you should perhaps act otherwise, [Col. 0483D] correction turn into cruelty and you lose those whom you desire to amend. Thus you must cut away a wound without injuring what is sound, lest, if you apply the knife more deeply than the matter requires, you harm the person whom you hasten to benefit. Let gentleness in you likewise be prudent, not lax; let correction be careful, not harsh. Let each quality thus be tempered by the other, so that the good may have, through love, something to beware of, and the wicked, through fear, something to love. Therefore, dearest brother, if you carefully preserve this dignity of the pallium which you have received, you will possess inwardly what you are known to have received outwardly. May divine grace guard your brotherhood and always protect it from every adversity.

Moreover, because the possessions of the Church of Bamberg lie in various [Col. 0484A] bishoprics or parishes, and because certain bishops, as we have learned, have been negligent in restraining evildoers or disturbers of those possessions, we decree that, if those evildoers, after canonical warning, refuse to restore what they have taken and to desist from their presumption, and if the bishops in whose parishes they dwell prove negligent in correcting them, you may pronounce canonical sentence against them.

We likewise confirm to the Church of Bamberg the abbey called Munstar [Note: [Col. 0483D] Munchmünster in Bavaria], which was given to you by Lothair, emperor of good memory, together with the church of Blessed Sixtus and the other churches, villages, and all appurtenances belonging to it. We also grant you authority, under the authority of the Holy Roman Church, to organize, for the honor of God, the churches situated among the barbarians [Note: [Col. 0484D] namely, in Pomerania], which were converted [Col. 0484B] by our brother Otto, your predecessor of venerable memory, from the squalor of their former paganism to Christian standards and ecclesiastical discipline, until, God favoring them, they obtain a Catholic bishop of their own.

Further, as a token of greater intimacy and affection, we grant that a cross may be borne before you within the boundaries of the Church of Bamberg, while preserving, of course, the reverence due to the metropolitan see of Mainz. As a sign that the city of Bamberg belongs specially and properly to blessed Peter, you shall pay each year to us and our successors, as rent, one fine, properly equipped and caparisoned white horse, such as befits the Roman pontiff to ride in processions or at other times. [Col. 0484C]

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aimeric, deacon-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of November, in the third indiction, in the year 1139 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Innocent II, pope.

## CDXXI. Privilege for the church of St. Prosper at Bondeno. (23 October 1139.)

*[TIRABOSCHI, Memorie storiche Modenesi, III, p. 8, from the archive of the monastery of St. Prosper.]*

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son HUGH, archpriest of the church of Saint [Col. 0484D] Prosper at Bondeno, and to his successors to be regularly appointed forever.

A pious request should be fulfilled by a corresponding result, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth worthily and the benefit sought may undoubtedly gain strength. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Archpriest Hugh, granting just assent to your reasonable requests, we strengthen with the privilege of the Apostolic See the church of Blessed Prosper, over which, by the Lord’s authority, you are known to preside.

For we decree that whatever possessions . . . that church now justly and lawfully possesses, or may hereafter acquire, with the Lord’s help, by grants of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful . . . means, shall remain firm to you and your successors and . . . unimpaired. Among these we have added the following to be specified by their proper names: . . . near the acres; on the other side, one vineyard of Bondeno together with the dwelling . . . the holding of Turicli; half the holding of Ferrarius; a quarter of the holding of Domini . . . the holding of Bubulo; the Braida of Saint James with meadow . . . beside the church of St. Martin. [Col. 0485A]

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may . . . rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken . . . or harass it with vexations; but let all things be preserved whole for the benefit, in every way, of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, having been admonished a second or third time, unless he makes suitable satisfaction, [Col. 0485B] let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself to be liable before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ; and at the final judgment let him be subject to strict punishment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Peter Castellanus, bishop, have subscribed. [Col. 0485C] I, Gerard, priest-cardinal of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Anselm, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed. I, Lucas, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Grisogonus, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Praxedes, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Almeric, deacon-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the tenth day before the Kalends of November, in the third indiction, in the year 1139 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Innocent II, pope.

## CDXXII. Bull for settling the controversy between Manasses, bishop of Meaux, and Risendis, abbess of the monastery of Faremoutiers. (23 October 1139.)

*[DUPLESSIS, History of Meaux, II, p. 34.]*

[Col. 0485D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughter in Christ RISENDIS, abbess of the monastery of Faremoutiers, and to the sisters who shall regularly succeed her in the government of the abbey forever.

A controversy had arisen between our venerable brother Manasses, bishop of Meaux, and you, beloved daughter in Christ, Abbess Risendis. We entrusted its settlement to our venerable brothers Geoffrey, bishop of Châlons, and Hugh, bishop of Auxerre. Having called to their assistance religious and prudent men, they settled that controversy, as we affirm from their writings, etc. [Col. 0486A]

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aimeric, deacon-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the tenth day before the Kalends of November, in the third indiction, in the year 1139 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Innocent II, pope.

## CDXXIII. Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary at Bagnolo. (18 November 1139.)

*[GIULINI, Memorie di Milano, vol. V, p. 570.]*

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son BRUNO, abbot of the monastery of Saint Mary, situated in the village of Bagnolo in the territory of Milan, and to his successors to be regularly appointed forever.

[Col. 0486B]

If we receive with paternal kindness the prayers and desires of religious men, we undoubtedly find the merciful Lord favorable to our own needs. And although, by the office of the apostolate entrusted to us by God, we ought to provide beneficially for all churches spread far and wide throughout the world, we ought nevertheless to devote more eager concern to those which are under the jurisdiction of blessed Peter and which, because of sins, have been diminished in temporal and spiritual matters.

Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Bruno, we grant assent to your petitions, and by apostolic dispensation give to you and your successors the abbey of Cerreto, which belongs to the jurisdiction of blessed Peter, so that through you and your brethren honest conduct and religious life may be reformed there, and that place, receiving a welcome increase both temporally and spiritually, may be subject to the monastery of Clairvaux. [Col. 0486C]

We further decree that both that place itself and everything now belonging to it canonically and lawfully—lands, meadows, pastures, woods, waters, and all other cultivated or uncultivated things—or which it may hereafter acquire, God favoring it, by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. As a sign that the same abbey belongs to the jurisdiction of blessed Peter, each year you shall pay to us and our successors twelve coins of Milanese currency as rent.

That you may more safely and freely devote yourselves to the service of almighty God, we establish by apostolic authority that no one may presume to demand or receive from you tithes or first-fruits from the produce which you cultivate with your own hands. [Col. 0486D] Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any molestations; but let all things be preserved whole and unimpaired for the benefit, in every way, of those for whose support and governance they were granted.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, [Col. 0487A] then, having been admonished a second or third time, unless he corrects his offence by suitable amendment, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself to be liable before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and at the final judgment let him be subject to strict punishment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. [Col. 0487B] I, Theodewin, bishop of Santa Rufina, have subscribed. I, Albert, bishop of Albano, have subscribed. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Gerard, priest-cardinal of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Anselm, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed. I, Lucas, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Boethius, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Clement, have subscribed. I, Ivo, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Lawrence in Damaso, have subscribed. I, Otto, deacon-cardinal of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Guido, deacon-cardinal of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Octavian, deacon-cardinal of Saint Nicholas in Prison, have subscribed. [Col. 0487C]

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aimeric, deacon-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of December, in the third indiction, in the year 1139 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Innocent II, pope.

## CDXXIV. Takes the monastery of Reichenberg, near Goslar, under protection, and confirms its discipline and possessions. (25 November 1139.)

*[HEINECCIUS, Antiquities of Goslar, book II, p. 142.]*

[Col. 0487D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son GERHARD, provost of the church of Reichenberg, and to his brethren who profess the canonical life, both present and future, forever.

We ought readily to grant assent to religious desires, so that faithful devotion may obtain a swift result. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your petitions and strengthen by the protection of the present document the church of Reichenberg, in which you are devoted to divine service. We decree that the canonical order according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine [Col. 0488A] shall be preserved irrevocably in that place forever. We further add that, after having made profession there and assumed the religious habit, none of you may transfer to another place without the permission of his superior.

Moreover, whatever possessions and goods that venerable place now justly and lawfully possesses, or may hereafter acquire through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, the Lord providing, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you forever. Therefore no person whatsoever may rashly disturb your aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any molestations; [Col. 0488B] but let all things be preserved whole for the benefit, in every way, of those for whose governance and support they were granted.

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, having been admonished a second or third time, unless he corrects his offence by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself to be liable before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ; and at the final judgment let him be subject to divine punishment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the supreme Judge the rewards of eternal [Col. 0488C] peace. Amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of the Church of Faenza, have subscribed. I, Gerard, priest-cardinal of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Godfrey, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Vestina, have subscribed. I, Lucas, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Theodewin, bishop of Santa Rufina, have subscribed. I, Otto, deacon-cardinal of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Guido, deacon-cardinal of Saint Angelo, have subscribed. I, Octavian, deacon-cardinal of Saint Nicholas in [Col. 0488D] Prison, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hands of Almeric, deacon-cardinal and chancellor of the Apostolic See, in the third indiction, in the year 1138 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the ninth year of the pontificate of Lord Innocent II.

## CDXXV. Writes to the clergy and laity of the diocese of Hildesheim: “that no layperson may presume to appropriate, either during life or at death, the movable or immovable goods of the brethren of monasteries or of other clerics.” (27 November 1139.)

*[JAFFÉ, Regesta Pontificum Romanorum, p. 589, from the royal archive at Hanover.]*

## CDXXVI. Privilege for the convent of women at Quedlinburg. (11 December 1139.)

*[LEUCKFELD, Antiquities of Michaelstein, p. 20.]*

[Col. 0489A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughter in Christ BEATRICE, abbess of the monastery of Quedlinburg, and to all who shall regularly succeed her in the governance of that place, forever.

As the records of ancient deeds declare, the monastery of Quedlinburg was founded by King Henry of illustrious memory and, under an annual payment of one pound of silver to blessed Peter, was offered by its founder to that prince of the apostles. Likewise, our predecessors of holy memory—Agapetus, John, and Sylvester, Roman pontiffs—received that place [Col. 0489B] into the ownership and protection of the Apostolic See and fortified it with authentic documents.

Therefore we, whose special concern it is to defend with greater diligence the goods and possessions belonging especially to the Holy Roman Church, grant paternal assent to your petitions, beloved daughter in the Lord, Abbess Beatrice. We strengthen by the protection of the Apostolic See, following the example of those same predecessors of ours, the monastery of Quedlinburg, situated beside the river Bode, over which, by the Lord’s authority, you are known to preside. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that venerable place now justly and canonically possesses, whether churches, tithes, or other things, or may hereafter acquire, God favoring it, by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings, generosity of princes, [Col. 0489C] offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors.

We renew and absolutely prohibit any church or person, except the Roman pontiff, ever to subject that monastery to itself. Nor may any king at any time be permitted to grant that monastery as a benefice to any persons. When you, now abbess of that place, or any of the sisters who succeed you in the governance of the abbey, die, no one may be placed over it by any craft of intrigue or by force, except the woman whom the nuns of that monastery by common consent, or the sounder part of their counsel, shall, in the fear of God, determine to elect.

And as we decree that the aforesaid [Col. 0489D] monastery shall be subject to the Roman pontiff alone, so by the present decree we likewise enact concerning the persons both of clerics and laity, and all other matters generally belonging to that place and assigned to our service, what is known to have been established by the enactment of those same predecessors of ours. Likewise we decree that the cloister of Saint Mary on the Mount shall be ordered according to the Rule of Blessed Benedict, and that the cloister of Saint Wipert in the aforesaid place of Quedlinburg, as well as the cloister of Saint Nicholas at Winethusen, shall be ordered according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine.

Furthermore, we confirm to that place all that, from the goods of Burchard, once a knight but now a convert, you, beloved daughter in Christ, Abbess Beatrice, have bestowed in devotion upon the church of Saint Michael the Archangel, situated in the place called Saint Michael’s Rock, at his request and with his consent. [Col. 0490A] We further add that whoever shall choose to serve God there must live communally and according to rule, without private property. Whatever that place now lawfully possesses, or may hereafter acquire by reasonable means, we decree shall remain secure to you, provided that the same church shall remain under the monastery of Quedlinburg, as it has hitherto stood by right and arrangement.

We establish the same by the present document concerning the church of Saint John the Baptist situated at Quedlinburg and the hospice beside it for the reception of the poor. Nevertheless, a religious and wise priest shall be appointed there, who shall also have care of the poor; and, excepting excommunicated persons, anyone who wishes to be buried there shall by no means be forbidden, while preserving the right and reverence due to the mother church. [Col. 0490B]

Therefore no emperor, king, archbishop, bishop, prince, or person of any ecclesiastical or other rank may rashly disturb those monasteries, or the sisters or brethren serving the Lord there; take away their possessions; retain what has been taken; diminish them; or harass them with any molestations. Rather, let all things be preserved whole for your use, or for the use of your sisters or brethren. As a sign that the same place belongs to blessed Peter’s jurisdiction, each year you shall pay to us and our successors one pound of silver as rent.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, having been admonished a second or third time, unless he corrects his offence by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself to be liable before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and at the final judgment let him be subject to strict punishment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen. [Col. 0490C]

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Theodewin, bishop of Santa Rufina. I, Gerhard, priest-cardinal of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Lucas, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul. I, Chrysogonus, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Gregory, deacon-cardinal of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Guido, deacon-cardinal of Saints Cosmas and Damian. [Col. 0490D]

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Almeric, deacon-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Ides of December, [Col. 0491A] in the third indiction, in the year 1139 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Innocent II, pope.

## CDXXVII. Privilege for the monastery of Ravensburg. (11 December 1139.)

*[GUNTHER, Codex Diplomaticus Rheno-Mosellanus, I, p. 252.]*

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons WECELIN, provost, and his brethren professing the canonical life in the church of Ravensburg, forever.

We ought readily to grant assent to religious desires, so that faithful devotion may attain a speedy result. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously accede to your petitions; and, following the example of our predecessor Pope Honorius of holy memory, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves your persons and the church of Ravenghensburch, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the safeguard of this present writing. We decree that the canonical order, according to the Rule of blessed Augustine, shall be preserved in that place inviolate for all time.

Upon the death of you, the provost of that place, or of any one of your successors, no one shall be set over that church by any cunning of fraud or by force, but rather the person whom the brethren, by common consent—or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel—shall, in the fear of God, regularly judge to be elected. Moreover, the possessions and goods which you now justly and canonically possess through the generosity of the illustrious Count Bertolf, his wife Hadewic, or the offerings of other faithful persons, and whatever you may hereafter be able, by God’s bounty, to acquire by lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you, saving the right and reverence due to the diocesan bishop.

By the authority also of God, of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul, and of ourselves, we forbid anyone to usurp for himself the advocacy of the same monastery without the election of the provost and brethren. We further prohibit that advocate from daring to appoint a substitute advocate for himself in that place. The person elected shall not presume to exact any service from the canonical brethren or from their officials, nor to conduct his lawsuits and pleas within the enclosure and cloistral workshops. The archpriest shall not be permitted to hold a synod there without the consent of the canonical brethren; nor shall money be exacted from anyone at any future time for the redemption of the church.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may disturb your aforesaid church in any respect, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; rather, all things shall be preserved whole for you, to serve the benefit of yourselves and of the poor. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, shall rashly presume to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he makes suitable amends, let him lose the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and at the last judgment let him be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve their rights for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good works and, before the severe Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church.  
I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina.  
I, Albert, bishop of Albano.  
I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia.  
I, Gerard, cardinal priest of Holy Cross in Jerusalem.  
I, Intifred, cardinal priest of the title of Vellina.  
I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul.  
I, Grysogonus, cardinal priest of the title of Praxedes.  
[Col. 0492B] I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil.  
I, Gerard, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Domnica.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Ides of December, in the third indiction, in the year 1139 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CDXXVIII. Privilege for the Church of Ilbenstadt.  
*(A.D. 1139, 12 December.)*

[HUGO, *Annals of the Premonstratensian Order*, I, Preface, p. 662.]

[Col. 0492C] INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son ANTHONY, provost, and to the brethren professing the canonical life in the church of Eloffstadt, both present and future, for ever.

The care of the Catholic Church has been entrusted to us by God, the supreme shepherd, in order that we may love His servants with paternal affection and strive all the more by every means to foster their devotions, in proportion as they are known to adhere more fervently to ecclesiastical discipline and to the rules of the holy Fathers. Indeed, service will then be pleasing to almighty God if the salutary institution of holy places is preserved in purity of religion by the protection of the holy Roman Church.

Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Provost Anthony, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the guardianship and protection of the Apostolic See the church of Eloffstadt, over which, by God’s appointment, you preside; and we strengthen it by the page of this present document. We decree and confirm by apostolic authority that the canonical order according to the Rule of blessed Augustine shall there be preserved inviolate for all future time.

We likewise confirm to you, your successors, and the same church in perpetuity by this present privilege the permission granted you by the archbishop to preach throughout the whole province and to labour by every means for the salvation of souls in life and in death; and whatever other goods the same church now justly and lawfully possesses in allods, tithes, serfs, cultivated and uncultivated lands. Among these we have added the following by their proper names:

[Col. 0493A] the estate upon which the noble brothers Counts Gotefrid and Oddo built your church in honour of Mary, Mother of God, and of the apostles Peter and Paul, for the remission of their sins, together with the other possessions bestowed upon you by them; the allod of Dorcheim; the allod of Roda; the toll or ferry-charge which our beloved son Lothar, emperor of good memory, gave at Franchenword for the salvation of his soul; and the allod of Tutnendorff. Whatever else you may hereafter acquire, with the Lord’s aid, through grants of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or any other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors.

Upon the death of you, now provost of that place, or of any one of your successors, no one shall be put in charge there by any crafty fraud or violence, save the person whom the brethren by common consent—or the sounder part of their counsel—shall, in the fear of God and according to the Rule of blessed Augustine, judge fit to elect.

It shall also be lawful for you to receive into communion, in life and in death, clerics or laypersons fleeing the world or desiring to enter the ranks of your community, unless they are bound by excommunication or by the obligations of some condition. Nor shall any brother, after assuming the habit and making profession there, be permitted to depart from your fellowship without the common permission of the brethren; and no bishop, abbot, monk, or any person whatsoever shall dare, without the permission of the provost and brethren, to receive or retain one who departs.

[Col. 0493C] If such a fugitive, after a second or third warning, should perhaps scorn to repent, his superior shall have full authority to excommunicate him. In the churches which your church has established, or which, with God’s help, it shall establish in future times, due reverence shall be rendered to you according to the institution of your order. But if—God forbid!—the prelates of churches propagated from your community are found to be destroyers of religion, or otherwise to be of disgraceful life and evil conduct, they shall nevertheless be corrected according to the regular rule known to have been established for apostates or brethren of your congregations.

Furthermore, by apostolic authority we command that your house shall not be compelled to accept an advocate against the brethren’s will. If a general interdict is proclaimed in the province of Mainz, then, excluding those excommunicated and under interdict, you may freely celebrate the divine offices in the churches of your parish.

We therefore decree that no archbishop, bishop, archdeacon, ecclesiastical or secular person whatsoever may disturb your church, oppress it by exactions, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or weary it by any vexations; rather, all things shall be preserved whole, for the benefit in every respect of the needs of those for whose governance and support they were granted—saving, of course, the canonical right and reverence due to the archbishop of Mainz.

If any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this page of our constitution, shall rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he gives suitable satisfaction, let him lose the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and at the last judgment let him be subject to severe vengeance.
