But upon all who preserve their rights for that place, or serve the Lord there, may there be the peace of the Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good works and, before the severe Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church.  
I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina.  
[Col. 0494B] I, Theodewin, bishop of Saint Rufina.  
I, Albert, bishop of Albano.  
I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia.  
I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem.  
I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul.  
I, Chrisogonus, cardinal priest of the title of Praxedes.  
I, George, cardinal deacon of Saint Angelo.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Almeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Ides of December, in the second indiction, in the year 1139 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CDXXIX. He confirms to the monastery of Saint John at Kastenborn the possessions bestowed by Otto, formerly bishop of Halberstadt.  
*(A.D. 1139, 14 December.)*

[*Thuringia sacra*, p. 305.]

[Col. 0494C]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved brethren professing the canonical life in the church of Saint John the Evangelist at Caldebrunnen, both present and future, for perpetual remembrance.

As the authority of the sacred canons teaches, holy places may be transferred for three reasons. Our beloved son Otto, formerly bishop of Halberstadt, recognizing that two of these reasons applied to the church of Revenigne—namely, the unsuitability [Col. 0494D] of the site and the harassment of robbers—transferred and exchanged, with the common consent of his brethren, for the greater fruit of divine service, the estates bestowed upon the aforesaid church, moving them to Caldebrunnen.

We therefore, whose special concern it is reasonably to confirm what is done by our brethren and to foster pious desires with appropriate assistance, confirm by this present decree the same transfer, made for the aforesaid reasons, and decree that it shall remain valid in future times. Following also in the footsteps of our predecessors of holy memory, Calixtus and Honorius, we decree that the order of canonical life which you have professed in that church shall be observed there for ever; and we strengthen the same place, with all its appurtenances, by the protection of blessed Peter.

Moreover, whatever possessions and goods have been lawfully bestowed upon that place from their own right by the noblemen Hermann and Wicmann, or by any other faithful persons, and whatever may hereafter, by God’s bounty, be justly and canonically bestowed, shall always remain secure and inviolate to you and your successors.

No person, therefore, may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, or harass it by any rash vexations; rather, all things shall be preserved whole for the benefit in every respect of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the canonical reverence due to the bishop of Halberstadt.

Upon the death of the provost of that venerable place, no one shall be set over it by any cunning fraud or violence, except the person whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, shall choose according to God. If anyone, having learned the tenor of this decree, should rashly—God forbid!—attempt to oppose it, let him suffer the loss of his honour and office, or be punished by the penalty of excommunication, unless he corrects his presumption by worthy satisfaction. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, with my own hand.  
I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of the holy martyrs Sergius and Bacchus, with my own hand.  
I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, with my own hand.  
I, Theodewin, bishop of Saint Rufina, with my own hand.  
[Col. 0495C] I, Albert, bishop of Albano, with my own hand.  
I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, with my own hand.  
I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, with my own hand.  
I, Anselm, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, with my own hand.  
I, Lucas, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, with my own hand.  
I, Chrysogonus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes, with my own hand.  
I, Ivo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Damaso.

Given at the Lateran through the hands of Himeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of January, [Col. 0495D] in the third indiction, in the year 1139 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CDXXX. To Gerard, provost of Bonn.  
*(A.D. 1139, 16 December.)*

[GUNTHER, *Codex diplomaticus Rheno-Mosellanus*, I, p. 256.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son GERARD, provost of Bonn, and to his successors canonically instituted, for ever.

As the authority of the holy canons teaches, the oversight and ordering of churches belongs to the care of bishops. Because they cannot personally perform everything, archdeacons have been appointed, who, as it were the eyes of bishops, inspect all things, so that, once they have thoroughly ascertained the condition of churches, clergy, and people, matters requiring correction may be corrected, and matters requiring establishment may, by God’s help, be confirmed.

They also make representations to the bishop concerning the repair of diocesan churches; they investigate parishes and the ornaments and property of churches and parishes, and report to the bishop their affairs or the liberties of churches. Moreover, the transgressions of priests and others are reported by them to the same bishops. From all this it is plainly inferred that archdeacons ought, without anyone’s opposition, to visit parishes and to take care of the souls of the people dwelling there.

Accordingly, beloved son in the Lord, Provost Gerard, following in the footsteps of the holy Fathers and observing the general custom of the Church, we grant and confirm to you and your successors the permission and free authority, at fixed times, to visit and make circuits of the deaneries situated in your archdeaconry—namely Archoe and Zulphechoe—as you have hitherto been accustomed to do in the other two, namely Yflensis and Sibergensis.

[Col. 0496B] And because a new remedy must be applied to new diseases: if plunderers and wrongdoers against the church of Bonn, after warning, perhaps refuse to repent, and the archbishop, when requested, neglects to restrain them according to justice, then, after they have been summoned a second and third time and have not made satisfaction, your person shall have the authority to place them under interdict or excommunicate them.

We further decree that you shall retain the seat and place adjudged to you in equity by the church of Cologne, both in the choir of Saint Peter and in public processions or assemblies. It is therefore your concern to live honourably by God’s grace and to remain devoted to the holy Roman Church, your mother, so that you may be worthy of greater favour. But if anyone should rashly attempt to act against the tenor of this our constitution, unless he corrects his presumption by suitable satisfaction, let him incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul. But those who preserve these things shall obtain the grace of the same blessings. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church.  
I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of Holy [Col. 0496D] Cross in Jerusalem.  
I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul.  
I, Ivo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Damaso.  
I, Grisogonus, cardinal priest of the title of Praxedes.  
I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina.  
I, Teodin, bishop of Saint Rufina.  
I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia.  
I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus.  
I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian.  
[Col. 0497A] I, GG., cardinal deacon of Saint Angelo.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Almeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of January, in the year 1139 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CDXXXI. He confirms the privileges of the monastery of Saints Peter and Paul at Canterbury.  
*(A.D. 1139.)*

[Chronicle of W. Thorne, in TWYSDEN, *Historians of England*, II, p. 1800.]

### CDXXXII. To Louis, king of the Franks.  
*(A.D. 1139.)*

[BALUZE, *Miscellanea*, II, p. 165.]

[Col. 0497B] INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his dearest son in Christ, LOUIS, illustrious and glorious king of the Franks: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The farmer rejoices if a tree planted by him is firmly rooted and bears excellent fruit in due season. Therefore, dearest son, since, by the anointing of the Holy Spirit, you have been consecrated by the Lord as king through our hands, as through the hands of blessed Peter, we rejoice all the more gladly in your good deeds and successes; and we are all the more bitterly grieved if you act otherwise.

It does not become a king, when provoked by anger, to break out into unlawful words or oaths. Rather, he ought with great deliberation and careful balance to weigh his words and deeds and foresee the outcome of events. Whoever seeks to offend the most holy Roman Church, the mother Church, or to lessen her dignity, sets his mouth against heaven and incurs indignation from on high.

But because we love your person with sincere charity and paternal affection, we grant your requests; and, in compassion for the noble and renowned church of Rheims, we permit the canons of Rheims to elect as archbishop a suitable and honourable person, provided that he is not bound to the governance of a bishopric. We command that this be done, with the Holy Spirit cooperating, on the advice of our venerable brethren Geoffrey, bishop of Chartres and legate of the Apostolic See, Hugh, bishop of Auxerre, Gossen, bishop of Soissons, and Alvis, bishop of Arras.

[Col. 0497D] And because God has willed that you should be elected and anointed king so that you might defend His bride, namely the holy Church redeemed by His own blood, and preserve her liberty unimpaired, we command you by apostolic writings and impose it upon you for the remission of sins: disperse by royal power those perverse assemblies of the people of Rheims which they call *compagnias*; restore both the church and city to the condition and liberty in which they stood in the time of your father and our brother, Archbishop Rainold of distinguished memory, recently deceased; and cause the losses inflicted by the citizens upon the Church and ecclesiastical persons to be repaired for them. It is better for you that God should rejoice in you in this age as His defender than that, by failing to punish evil, you should experience Him as avenger in the age to come.

### CDXXXIII. He takes under protection the convent of Saints George and Pancras at Heklingen, and confirms its goods and rights.  
*(A.D. 1140, 10 January.)*

[ECCARD, *Genealogical History of the Princes of Upper Saxony*, p. 563.]

[Col. 0498A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughter in Christ IRMENGARD, abbess of the monastery of the holy martyrs George and Pancras at Kakelinge, and to the sisters who shall regularly succeed her in the government of the abbey, for ever.

Established by God’s ordering upon the watchtower of the Apostolic See, we ought so to apply the decrees of the Fathers’ canons that each person’s right may be preserved, and that to no one—so far as lies within our power—[the text is defective]; all the more it is fitting for us to be solicitous for their protection and to labour more attentively for their [Col. 0498B] peace and tranquillity.

Accordingly, beloved daughter in the Lord, Abbess Irmengard, we grant your wishes with paternal kindness; and we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and strengthen by the page of this present document, the monastery of Saints George and Pancras, over which, by God’s appointment, you preside. It was founded by the noble Count Bernard, enriched both by him and by his successors and counts, namely Theoderic and Helperic, and altered for the better with a like intention of devotion by Helperic’s sons, namely Margrave Chunrad and Bernard. We decree that the monastic order according to the Rule of blessed Benedict shall be preserved in that place inviolate for all time.

Moreover, whatever goods and possessions that monastery now canonically possesses from the gift of the aforesaid men or of other persons, and whatever it may hereafter, by God’s provision, acquire through grants of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and to the sisters succeeding you in the government of the abbey.

Upon the death of you, now abbess of that place, or of any sister succeeding you in the same office, no woman shall be put over it by any fraud or violence, except the one whom the sisters by common consent—or the sounder part of their counsel—shall elect according to the fear of God and the aforesaid Rule. We likewise decree that the same shall be observed in the case of the provost when one is to be elected.

No person, therefore, may rashly disturb your aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it by any molestations; rather, all things shall be preserved whole for the benefit of those for whose support they were granted.

If any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his presumption by suitable satisfaction, let him suffer the loss of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and at the last judgment [Col. 0499A] let him be subject to severe vengeance. But those who preserve these provisions shall obtain the blessing and grace of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church.  
I, Gregory, deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus.  
I, Theodoric, bishop of Saint Rufina.  
I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil.  
I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian.  
I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the church of Holy Cross in Jerusalem.  
I, Anselm, cardinal priest of the church of Saint [Col. 0499B] Lawrence in Lucina.  
I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the church of Saints John and Paul.  
I, Chrysogonus, cardinal priest of the church of Saint Praxedes.  
I, Ivo, cardinal priest of the church of Saints Lawrence and Damasus.  
I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia.  
I, Hubald, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Ides of January, in the third indiction, in the year 1139 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CDXXXIV. He confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of Saint Blaise.  
*(A.D. 1140, 21 January.)*

[NEUGART, *Codex diplomaticus Alemannicus*, II, p. 68.]

[Col. 0499C]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons B. [BERTHOLD], abbot, and the brethren of the monastery of Saint Blaise: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Although, by reason of the office of the apostolate entrusted to us by God, we ought generally to honour and love our brethren, bishops and abbots, and preserve for the churches entrusted to them their rights, we ought nevertheless to provide with more attentive care for those who are known to adhere more especially [Col. 0499D] to blessed Peter and the holy Roman Church.

For this reason we graciously assent to your desires, and we also, by apostolic authority, declare firm and ratify by this present writing the grant which our predecessor Honorius of blessed memory confirmed for you by the authority of his privilege.

> [Note: The bull of Honorius II, dated 28 March 1126, was published by Celsus Gerbert, *History of the Black Forest*, vol. III, p. 59.]

That is: you shall hold in perpetuity for your own use your churches and the tithes belonging to churches which you have or shall have, and which, with God’s consent, you may receive from laymen, without any opposition from bishops or others, while preserving episcopal reverence.

We have thought it proper to specify by their proper names the churches which that venerable place now possesses, together with the benefit of their tithes: the church of Nallingen,

> [Note: Nallingen in Württemberg.]

which was assigned by the nobleman Anshalm together with half the tithes; the church of Batimaringin,

> [Note: Bettmaringen in the Alpgau, district of Saint Blaise.]

which Arnold handed over to the monastery with half the tithes; the church of Sneisanc,

> [Note: Schneisingen in the Swiss part of the county of Baden.]

which Count Erlewin offered to the church of Saint Blaise with a half share of the tithes;

> [Note: See above, no. 824.]

and the churches of Berowe and Nunkilcha,

> [Note: Neukirch between Rottweil and Schömberg.]

which Gotefrid likewise bestowed with portions of the tithes.

In these your churches [Col. 0500B] and in the others which you possess, we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb your aforesaid monastery or molest it by any vexations. But if anyone, knowingly acting against the authority of this our confirmation, should rashly attempt to oppose it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his offence by suitable satisfaction, let him incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul. Amen.

Given at the Lateran, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of February, in the year 1137.

### CDXXXV. He confirms for the monastery of Saint Blaise the privileges bestowed by emperors and his predecessors, together with its dependent houses and churches.  
*(A.D. 1140, 21 January.)*

[NEUGART, *ibid.*, p. 68.]

[Col. 0500C]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son BERTOLD, abbot of the monastery of Saint Blaise, situated in the diocese of Constance, in the place called the Black Forest, and to his successors regularly appointed, for ever.

“Although, by reason of the office of the apostolate entrusted to us by God,” etc., as above in the bull of A.D. 1137. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Bertold, we assent with paternal kindness to your desires, and strengthen by the page of this present writing the monastery of blessed Blaise, over which, by God’s appointment, you are known to preside. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that venerable place now justly and canonically [Col. 0500D] possesses, or may hereafter acquire through grants of pontiffs, etc. Among these we have thought it proper to specify by their proper names:

namely, the dependent houses of Hochsenhusen,

> [Note: Now a celebrated Benedictine abbey in Swabia.]

Berowa,

> [Note: Berau, a convent with a provostship between the rivers Schlücht and Schwarzach in the Black Forest.]

Wittenowa,

> [Note: Witnau in Upper Breisgau, now in the district of Baden.]

Burgelun,

> [Note: Bürglen, a provostship there at Mount Blauen.]

with all their appurtenances; likewise the churches of Nunchilcha, Sneisanc, Birbomestorf,

> [Note: Birmenstorf on Mount Albis, between Lake Zurich and the river Reuss.]

Bathmaringin, and Griezheim,

> [Note: Griefsen in the Klettgau.]

with all their appurtenances; and also the dependent house of Wizelinhoven,

> [Note: Wissilighofen between the towns of Kaiserstuhl and Zurzach, now a provostship.]

with its appurtenances.

We also confirm the ordinance concerning the liberty and advocacy of your monastery made by Emperor Henry IV of good memory,

> [Note: A.D. 1125, 8 January; above, no. 845.]

and strengthened by our predecessor Calixtus of blessed memory by the privilege of his authority,

> [Note: A.D. 1120, 19 March, in Celsus Gerbert, *History of the Black Forest*, vol. III, p. 48; and 18 June 1120, above, no. 838.]

and fortified by our beloved son King Lothar through the force of his charter,

> [Note: A.D. 1126, 4 January, in P. Herrgott, *Codex of Proofs*, no. 206.]

and confirmed by Pope Honorius of holy memory through the deliberation of bishops and cardinals,

> [Note: In the same year, 28 March; *History of the Black Forest*, vol. III, p. 59.]

and approved by us in the Lateran Council.

> [Note: The Tenth General Lateran Council was convened in A.D. 1139, in April.]

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb your aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; rather, all things shall be preserved whole [Col. 0501B] for the benefit in every respect of those for whose governance and support they were granted. “If, therefore, any person,” etc. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed (*ss.*).  
I, Theodewin, bishop of Saint Rufina, have subscribed.  
I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed.  
I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed.  
I, Anselm, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed.  
I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed.  
I, Boetius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement, have subscribed.  
I, Ivo, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Lawrence and Damasus, have subscribed.  
[Col. 0501C] I, Grisogonus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes, have subscribed.  
I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed.  
I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.  
I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed.  
I, Uass., cardinal deacon of Saint Eustace, have subscribed.  
I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Angelo, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of February, in the third indiction, in the year 1140 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

> [Note: Nearly completed; for Innocent II was elected about the middle of February 1130.]

### CDXXXVI. He confirms the donation to the monastery of Reichenau, made by Duke Conrad of Zähringen, of a quarter share in the village of Oningen.  
*(A.D. 1140, 17 February.)*

[HERRGOTT, *Genealogy of the House of Habsburg*, II, p. 160.]

[Col. 0501D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son FRIDELOO, abbot of the monastery of Reichenau, and to his successors regularly appointed, for ever.

[Col. 0502A] By the office of the apostolate entrusted to us by God, we ought to take care of all churches; and whatever is bestowed upon them through the offerings or donations of the faithful, we ought to strengthen by apostolic protection. We wish to exercise this care more abundantly toward the monastery of Reichenau, because that place, together with its appurtenances, is known to belong more especially to the right of blessed Peter.

Accordingly, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Frideloo, favourably assenting to your requests, we confirm in perpetuity to you and your successors, and through you to the same monastery, and strengthen by this present privilege, the fourth part of the village of Oningin. It was piously bestowed upon the monastery of Reichenau by the illustrious Duke Chunrad of Zähringen with every right and jurisdiction which he himself possessed there by hereditary succession.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may henceforth trouble your church concerning this our confirmation or inflict upon you any injury concerning the aforesaid portion of the village. But if anyone should rashly attempt to invalidate or alter this donation or offering, then, after a second or third warning, unless he gives suitable satisfaction, let him lose the dignity of his power and honour, and remain subject to excommunication until he corrects his offence. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church.  
I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul.  
I, Theodwin, bishop of Saint Rufina.  
[Col. 0502C] I, Gotho, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church.  
I, Ivo, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Lawrence and Damasus.  
I, Grisogonus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of March, in the third indiction, in the year 1139 of the Lord’s Incarnation; in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CDXXXVII. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Mary of Berghe.  
*(A.D. 1140, 26 February.)*

[LACOMBLET, *Book of Charters*, I, p. 221.]

[Col. 0502D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son BERNON, abbot of the monastery of Saint Mary of Berghe, and to his successors regularly appointed, for ever.

The devout request of a willing purpose ought to be fulfilled with effect, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth commendably and the benefit requested may undoubtedly gain force. With this in view, beloved son in the Lord, Berno, abbot, [Col. 0503A] we graciously assent to your requests and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the monastery of Saint Mary of Berghe, over which, by God’s authorship, you preside; and we fortify it by the authority of this present document. We decree that whatever goods and whatever possessions that monastery now justly and lawfully possesses, or may in future be able to acquire, by grant of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s assistance, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: the estate of Berghe, bestowed upon the church by the illustrious Count Adolf of Cologne, out of his devotion, for founding and establishing religious life there; also the manor of Bochem [Col. 0503B] with its tithes; the land situated beside Bladesheim called Cameruost, with its tithes; the manor of Wanemala; a vineyard in the bishopric of Würzburg, situated on the mountain called Thaebog; one vineyard at Truensthorp (Dransdorf); and likewise a vineyard at Bagaracha with its tithes.

We further decree that you shall not be compelled to pay tithes from the labour which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or from the fodder of your animals. Let the monastic order which, according to the Rule of blessed Benedict and the institution of the Cistercian brothers, has by God’s grace been established in that monastery, be preserved there for all time. Moreover, so that you may more freely devote yourselves to the divine offices, we establish that [Col. 0503C] the abbot who at any time presides over the aforesaid monastery shall not be compelled to attend a synod or secular courts, except in a grave and evident necessity.

Therefore let no person whatsoever be permitted rashly to disturb your aforesaid monastery, to take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations whatsoever; but let all things be preserved whole for the benefit, in every way, of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this document of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless that person corrects the offence by fitting satisfaction, let that person be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer, and at the last [Col. 0503D] judgment be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Theodewin, bishop of Saint Rufina, have subscribed. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Anselm, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed. [Col. 0504A] I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in Carcere, have subscribed. I, Guido, unworthy priest of the Holy Roman Church, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Kalends of March [26 February], in the third indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1139, and in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CDXXXVIII. At the request of Bishop Godebald, he confirms the possessions of the Church of Meissen. (1140, 27 February.)

[JAFFÉ, *Regesta Romanorum pontificum*, p. 589, “from Pertz’s notes.”]

### CDXXXIX. He confirms the privileges and exemptions of Egmond Abbey, of Benedictine monks, and likewise of Rijnsburg Abbey, of noble nuns of the same order in Holland. (1140, 28 February.)

[MIRAEUS, *Opera diplomatica*, IV, p. 13.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son WALTER, abbot of the monastery of Egmond, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

[Col. 0504C] The nobleman Count Theodoric of Holland, setting out for Jerusalem, came into our presence. Among other matters which we discussed with him concerning the correction of morals and the ordering of his life, that illustrious man, both on his own behalf and on behalf of his mother Countess Petronilla, offered and transferred Egmond monastery, and likewise Rijnsburg monastery, by right of ownership to the blessed prince of the apostles, from devotion.

And therefore we, whose especial concern it is particularly to defend the rights of that same key-bearer of heaven, have received those venerable places into the ownership and protection of the Holy Roman Church and have secured them, with all their appurtenances, by the protection of this present document. [Col. 0504D]

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monasteries, take away their possessions, retain what has been taken away, or harass them by any vexations; but let all things be kept whole for the benefit in every way of those for whose support and governance they were granted.

Moreover, as a sign that these monasteries belong to the jurisdiction of blessed Peter, each year you and your successors shall pay to us and our successors, by way of census, four solidi in Freising currency.

If any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this document of our constitution, should [Col. 0505A] rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless that person corrects the offence by suitable satisfaction, let that person be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer, and at the last judgment be subject to severe vengeance.

But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen. Fare well.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. [Col. 0505B] I, Otto, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint George, have subscribed. I, Michael, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed. I, Albert, bishop of Albano, have subscribed. I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Albert, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, George, deacon of Saint Angelo, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aimeric Theodoric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the day before the Kalends of March [28 February], in the third indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation one thousand one hundred and thirty-nine, and in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent [Col. 0505C] II.

### CDXL. Privilege for the Church of Saint Gentian at Balgentiacum. (1140, 6 March.)

[*Gallia Christiana*, VIII, Instrumenta, 506, from the original.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son JOSCELIN, abbot of Saint Gentian of Balgentiacum, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

Among the other duties which arise for us from the care of the universal Church, it is fitting that we should provide more attentively for the peace of religious persons, because, the more frail we are, the more we need their prayers. With this in view, beloved abbot Joscelin in the Lord, [Col. 0505D] we graciously assent to your requests and confirm by the privilege of the Apostolic See the Church of Saint Gentian, over which, by God’s authorship, you are known to preside. First, indeed, we decree that the canonical order established in your church of the Blessed Mother of God and Saint Gentian according to the Rule of blessed Augustine shall be preserved there for all time. We also enact that whatever possessions and whatever goods that venerable place now justly and lawfully possesses, or may in future be able to acquire through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s assistance, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: the Church of Saint Firmin [Col. 0506A] with the tithe belonging to it, the parish of the whole town, and all cemeteries; likewise the chapel of Saint Nicholas and the chapel of Saint Lazarus; the Church of Saint Peter of Vosone, with tithe, land, and all that belongs to it; the Church of Saint Andrew of Darneto with all its appurtenances; also three arpents of vineyards in the same town; the Church of Saint Stephen of Marciliacum; the Church of Saint Sulpicius of Lalliacum; the Church of Saint Aignan of Boola; the Church of Saint John of Tovers and the chapel of Saint Martin, which is in the cemetery of that church; the Church of Saint Peter of Poliacum; the Church of Saint Peter of Villecerlo; the Church of Saint Leobinus of Pireto; the land of Feucis of Sisuinnai; the land of Melsdun; the land of Pireto above [Col. 0506B] the Malva; the land of Castris; the land of Villemani; the land of Taupennis; half of the mill of Porta; half of the mill of Tovers; the mill of Trusseth; the tithe of Chosel; and twenty solidi from the toll of Firmitas Neberti.

Upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, let no one be placed over it through any cunning of deception or violence, except the person whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, in the fear of God and according to the Rule of blessed Augustine, shall judge fit to elect; and let him be consecrated by the bishop of Orléans without any improper exaction.

We further add that, after making profession in your church, no brother may migrate to other places without your permission and that of the chapter; and no one may dare retain a departing brother. If he is summoned a second or third time and—God forbid—scorns to return, his superior shall have the power to pronounce canonical sentence against him. Nor may anyone, against your will, build new churches or oratories in your parishes, saving the authority and reverence of the Holy Roman Church. Therefore it concerns you, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Joscelin, with divine mercy aiding you, to live honourably and, should your brethren at any time commit offences, to correct them after taking counsel with your brethren. [Col. 0506C]

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may disturb your aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but let all things be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this document of our constitution, should presume rashly to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless that person corrects the offence by suitable satisfaction, let that person incur the indignation of almighty God, of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul, and of us; let that person be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and at the last judgment let that person be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action [Col. 0507A] and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Anselm, cardinal priest of Saint Lawrence in Lucina. I, Lictifred, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina. I, Lucas, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul. I, Guido, unworthy priest of the Holy Roman Church. I, Ivo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Damaso. [Col. 0507B] I, Chrysogonus, cardinal priest of Saint Praxedes. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Albert, bishop of Albano. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. I, Gregory, cardinal of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Vassallus, cardinal deacon of Saint Eustachius. I, …, priest, cardinal deacon of the Holy Roman Church. I, Goizo, cardinal deacon of the Holy Roman Church. I, Rainerius, cardinal deacon of the Holy Roman [Col. 0507C] Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Almeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the day before the Nones of March [6 March], in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1139, and in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CDXLI. Privilege for the Church of Saint Nicholas at Miseray. (1140, 3 April.)

[*Gallia Christiana*, II, Instrumenta, 59.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons in Christ GERALD, prior of Miseraicum, and his brethren, present and future, professing the religious life in that place, in perpetuity.

[Col. 0507D] He who cherishes religious persons and readily grants assent to their pious desires offers to the Lord a pleasing holocaust. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we assent with paternal kindness to your requests and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the Church of Blessed Nicholas of Miseraicum, in which you devote yourselves to divine service; and we have fortified it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods that venerable place now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future be able to acquire, by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through God’s favour, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you [Col. 0508A] and your successors.

We also enact that religious life shall flourish in that place for all future time. We further prohibit anyone whatsoever from exacting tithes from your labour, cultivated with your own hands or at your own expense, or from the produce of your animals. We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb your aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain offerings, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but let all things be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If anyone, therefore, should presume in future to contravene this our decree, let that person incur the indignation of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul [Col. 0508B] and be subject to excommunication. But let those who observe these provisions obtain the blessing and grace of almighty God and of those same apostles. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Theodwin, bishop of Saint Rufina. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Albert, bishop of Albano. I, Anselm, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. I, Chrysogonus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. [Col. 0508C] I, Rainerius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca. I, Griso, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Nicholas in Carcere.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Nones of April [3 April], in the third indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation one thousand one hundred and thirty-six [Note: [Col. 0507] Read “the fortieth year,” which corresponds to the eleventh year of Innocent II and to the third indiction.], and in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CDXLII. He confirms the possessions and rights of the canons of Verona. (1140, 16 April.—Fragment.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia Sacra*, V, 781.]

[Col. 0508D]

In the archive of the canons is found a diploma of Innocent II in favour of Gilbert, archpriest, and the other canons of the Church of Verona, drawn up in precisely the same words as the diploma of Callixtus II for the same persons.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of May [16 April], in the third indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1140, and in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

[Col. 0509A] I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Theodwin, bishop of Porto and Saint Rufina. I, Anselm, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina. I, Gotifred, cardinal priest of the title of Saint … . I, Chrysogonus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Presbyter of the title of Pastor, cardinal priest. I, W., cardinal priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus. I, Gozo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. [Col. 0509B] I, Gerard, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Dominica. I, Thomas, cardinal deacon of the Holy Roman Church.

### CDXLIII. He entrusts the Church of Saint Saviour in Mustolio to the Church of Saint Frigdianus at Lucca, on condition that twelve denarii of Luccan currency are paid yearly. (1140, 21 April.)

[*Bullarium Lateranense*, 18.]

### CDXLIV. He receives the Church of Saint Vincent at Bergamo into his protection and confirms its goods and rights. (1140, 29 April.)

[LUPUS, *Codex diplomaticus Bergomensis*, II, p. 1022.]

[Col. 0509C]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ALBERT, archpriest, and his brethren, present and future, living canonically in the Church of Saint Vincent at Bergamo, in perpetual remembrance.

The authority of the Apostolic See entrusted to us exhorts us to provide the aid of protection to places and persons which duly seek it with devotion. For, just as no effect ought to be granted to those who seek unjust things, so the petition of those asking for lawful and just things ought not to be delayed—especially that of those who delight to serve almighty God with uprightness of life and commendable moral conduct. [Col. 0509D] Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just and reasonable requests and receive under the guardianship and protection of the Apostolic See the Church of blessed Vincent the martyr, together with the community of your congregation and all that belongs to the same church; and we fortify it by the authority of this present document.

We establish that whatever possessions and whatever goods, in churches, towns, villages, tithes, revenues of markets, or other things, that church now justly and lawfully possesses, or may in future reasonably be able to acquire, through grants of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, with the Lord’s aid, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors for ever. [Col. 0510A] We therefore decree that, so long as you remain in the observance of canonical discipline, no person whatsoever may rashly disturb your church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it by burdensome forced services or rash vexations; but let all things be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted.

We further prohibit either a bishop or an archbishop, or any other person, from diverting the goods of your community to private uses, granting them to others as benefices, or alienating them in any other way from the brothers’ prebend or the common benefit. Leases, exchanges, or investitures of the aforesaid possessions [Col. 0510B] shall in no manner be carried out without the common counsel of the brethren, and no bishop or any persons whatsoever may usurp such a right, without prejudice, however, to the canonical reverence due to the Catholic bishops of Bergamo.

If, therefore, in future any archbishop, bishop, emperor, king, duke, prince, count, viscount, or any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this document of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless that person corrects the offence by suitable satisfaction, let that person forfeit the dignity of power and honour; let that person recognize himself or herself as guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let that person be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and at the last [Col. 0510C] judgment let that person be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Theodewind, bishop of Saint Rufina, have subscribed. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Anselm, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed. [Col. 0510D] I, Wido, unworthy priest of the Holy Roman Church, have subscribed. I, Ivo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Damaso, have subscribed. I, Chrysogonus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Callixtus, have subscribed. I, Presbit. (sic), cardinal priest of the title of Pastor, have subscribed. I, Goizo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of the title of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. [Col. 0511A] I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Vassallus, cardinal deacon of Saint Eustachius, have subscribed. I, Gerard, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Dominica, have subscribed. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in Carcere, have subscribed. I, Thomas, cardinal deacon of the Holy Roman Church, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of the Holy Roman Church, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Kalends of May [29 April], in the third indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation [Col. 0511B] 1140, and in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CDXLV. He receives into his protection the monastery of Saint Maximinus at Trier and confirms its possessions. (1140, 6 May.)

[HONTHEIM, *Historia Trevirensis diplomatica*, I, 543.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son SIGER, abbot of the monastery of Saint Maximinus, situated in the suburb of Trier, and to his successors regularly appointed.

The incomprehensible and ineffable mercy of divine power has established us in the administration of the Apostolic See by this plan of providence, so that we may strive to exercise paternal concern for all Churches. [Col. 0511C] For the Holy Roman Church, which retains the primacy over all Churches granted to it by God, ought, as a loving mother, to provide with unceasing vigilance for each Church. To her, indeed, as to their head and mother, all must have recourse, so that they may be nourished from her bosom, defended by her authority, and relieved from their oppressions.

It is fitting, therefore, that churches and venerable places—especially those belonging to the special right and particular ownership of the Holy Church, which, by God’s authorship, we serve—should receive the honour of a more special prerogative and be strengthened by the protection of apostolic authority. Accordingly, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Siger, graciously yielding to the just requests of you and your brethren, after the example of our predecessors of holy memory, Gregory, Agapetus, John; likewise John and Leo IX, Roman pontiffs, [Col. 0511D] we receive under the guardianship and protection of the Apostolic See the monastery of blessed Maximinus, over which, by the Lord’s authorship, you preside, and fortify it by the present privilege.

We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods, in churches, villages, lands cultivated or uncultivated, or other things, which that monastery now justly and lawfully possesses, or may in future be able to acquire through grants of pontiffs, generosity of kings, emperors, or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through God’s favour, shall remain firm and unimpaired for ever for you and your successors and for the brethren serving the Lord there from time to time. [Col. 0512A] Among these we have thought fit to record the following by their proper names: in the archbishopric of Trier, the villages, with churches, of Bescha, Willera, Drudelinga, Murmiringa, Mamhra, Daleheim, Frisinga, Tavena, Berga with its appurtenances, Emmelde, Luttrestharra, Billicha, Marchidictum with its appurtenances, Oldinga, Schitelinga, Mudeuurt, Mersche, Liniche with its appurtenances, Everlinga, Voela, Ham with its appurtenances in the district of Bidgowe, Ratersdorff, Buchstat, Frankingun, Ebbena, Metzrich, Stedeheim, Enselinga, Simonisvilla, Meisbreth, Kenne, Insula, Lonquich, Vallis with its appurtenances, Riola, Lorche, Poliche, Decima with its appurtenances, Martinivilla, Bumaga with its appurtenances, Budelbach, Lovena, Rivenacha, Gunderhausen [Col. 0512B] with its appurtenances, Prichena with its appurtenances; the church of Talefangh, the church of Remiche, the church of Wimerskirche, the church of Lunesdorff, the church of Cumiciaco, the church of Steinsele, the church of Schoneberga, and the church of Betresdorff.

In the archbishopric of Mainz: the Church of Saint Christopher with houses and small plots in that city; the church of Wyldenstein; the church of Gozoluesheim; the church of Albucha; the church of Winheim; the church of Flancheim; the church of Husun; likewise the villages of Suapeheim, Evernesheim, Briccenheim, Buckenheim, Esenheim, Apula with its appurtenances, Scheringesfeld, Mammeldal, and Siemera.

In the archbishopric of Cologne: Oxesheim with its church, Leccenic with its church, Buddelar, and Barwillere [Col. 0512C] with its church and appurtenances.

In the bishopric of Liège: Aselbrunna with its church, Curmeringa, and Fractura.

In the bishopric of Metz: in the city itself, houses with small plots, vineyards, and fields; the church of Theodonisvilla with five manses; Wilre with its church; the church of Lutzelkirche; Bisanga with its church and appurtenances; Wirtzkircha with its church; Tincheris, Vriulcurt, and Vkenishem. We likewise confirm to you the fishery of the River Rover and the fish-weir constructed in it.

Furthermore, we confirm to you the churches and other possessions belonging to the aforesaid abbey, with their tithes and endowments, and all royal tithes which our predecessor Pope Leo, of blessed memory, granted to your monastery for the use of guests, the poor, and pilgrims. [Col. 0512D] We also decree that the liberty bestowed on your monastery by Roman pontiffs and religious kings or emperors shall be preserved inviolate: namely, that the same place shall never be subject to any see or church, but shall remain under the right and protection of the Holy Roman Church and under the *mundiburdium*, or guardianship, of emperors, enjoying the liberty and immunity which that monastery is known to have possessed from Roman pontiffs and emperors.

No person of any rank, unless invited by you or by any one of your successors, may dare to order or carry out anything within the aforesaid monastery according to that person’s own will. Upon the death of you, abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, [Col. 0513A] let no one be placed over it by any cunning of deception or violence, except the person whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of their counsel, shall in the fear of God and according to the Rule of blessed Benedict judge fit to elect.

We also grant that burial in that place shall be free, so that no one may obstruct the devotion of those who resolve to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated. We therefore decree that no ecclesiastical or secular person whatsoever may rashly disturb your aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but let all things be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If, therefore, in [Col. 0513B] future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this document of our constitution, should attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless that person corrects the offence by suitable satisfaction, let that person forfeit the dignity of power and honour; let that person recognize himself or herself as guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let that person be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and at the last judgment let that person be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the supreme Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. [Col. 0513C] I, Anselm, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina. I, Chrysogonus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Ivo, cardinal priest of Saint Lawrence in Damaso. I, G. G., cardinal priest of the title of Saint Callixtus. I, Ribaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia. [Col. 0514A] I, Wido, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus. I, Presbyter, cardinal priest of the title of Pastor. I, Goizo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Theodewin, bishop of Saint Rufina. I, Alberius, bishop of Albano. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Vasallus, cardinal deacon of Saint Eustachius beside the Temple of Agrippa. I, Hubaldus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. [Col. 0514B] I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in Carcere. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of the Holy Roman Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Almeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Nones of May [6 May], in the third indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1140, and in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0513C] Balderic recounts in what manner the present bull was fraudulently obtained by the monks in the following passage of the *Life of Albero*: “At that time, when the Church of Saint Maximinus was vacant of a pastor, the monks chose as abbot a certain monk from the Church of Liège, brother of certain counsellors of the Count of Namur, for the purpose that the count might daily be more fiercely inflamed into his madness by their counsels. Taking him to Rome at great expense, against the archbishop’s will, they had Lord Pope Innocent bless him as abbot. The crowds marvelled at so sudden a reversal of affairs: namely, that the Roman Church should so grievously trouble such a man and so great a man—Albero—who had endured so many labours and so many dangers for her, who had so recently stood in such great favour with the Apostolic See, and who had so strongly opposed himself to King Lothar for Pope Innocent in the expedition mentioned above that the archbishop and the king had parted from one another not with serene expressions.

“Moreover, during this war between the archbishop and the Count of Namur, the brethren of the Church of Confluentes, Saint Florin’s, also began to harass him. For against his will they chose as provost the nobleman Lord Louis of Isenburg. Going to Rome with him at great expense, they brought back apostolic letters contrary to the will of the lord archbishop. When they offered them to the lord archbishop as he sat in synod, he cast them to the ground in agitation of mind. Consequently he was accused before Lord Pope Innocent, who summoned him for an appointed day; and when he did not appear on that day, he was suspended from episcopal office. All these evils came upon him at once; and from all of them the Lord delivered [Col. 0514D] him. For, coming to Rome, he secured the abbot of Saint Maximinus’s promise of obedience to him and his sworn fidelity, and he annulled the election of the men of Confluentes.”

Brower reads the oath of Abbot Siger, rendered to the archbishop, in a very ancient codex of the Gospels from the metropolitan library—which, alas, no longer exists today—in which were entered the obediences rendered to the archbishop by the individual abbots of the archdiocese of Trier. *Annals of Trier*, book XIV, no. 44:

“I, Seyher, abbot of Saint Maximinus, promise obedience to the see of the Church of Trier, and to you, Albero, by God’s grace archbishop of Trier, and to your Catholic successors for ever, without prejudice to the commitment of my order.”

Finally, in order that this result might be attained and that what had been fraudulently obtained might be revoked, Saint Bernard sent two letters to Pope Innocent—Bernard’s letters 179 and 180. That they were not without effect is demonstrated by the papal confirmation that followed on 20 December of this year.]

### CDXLVI. To Albero, Archbishop of Trier. He orders him to restore the monastery of Saint Maximinus to order. (1140, 8 May.)

[WURTVEIN, *Nova subsidia*, IX, p. 202.]

[Col. 0514C]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother ALBERO, archbishop of Trier and legate of the Apostolic See: greeting and apostolic blessing.

With fatherly affection we sympathize with your labors, and in whatever ways we can according to God, we willingly bestow help and counsel on you as our most beloved brother. [Note: [Col. 0515D] These letters of Innocent II point to the efforts expended by Archbishop Albero on behalf of the abbey of St. Maximin: it was badly unsettled through the incompetence of its domestic ruler, and needed to be bound by better regulations and, once internal discord had been removed, recalled to concord and peace.]

We wish you to know that we have caused the abbot of St. Maximin—[Note: [Col. 0515D] He was Gerard, according to an ancient writer: lavish with his own resources and prodigal of the sacred treasury, not content with turning St. Maximin’s extensive estates to profane uses, he squandered the goods of the monastery, openly dissipating its property and wealth, to the great disgrace of his life and profession.]—to be absolved, after receiving security that he would obey our commands concerning the matter for which he had been excommunicated. Having absolved him, we remit him to your discretion; and we command him orally that he render obedience and reverence to you, as to his own archbishop, with humility. It is therefore your responsibility to apply yourself diligently to restoring religious life in that monastery and to devote more earnest effort to the peace and tranquility of that place and of the brethren there serving the Lord. [Note: [Col. 0515D] In order that this Gerard might at last come to his senses, Albero admonished and opposed him more severely; but when he persisted in his obstinacy, he was deprived of his office and shortly thereafter departed this life (Chronicle of Spanheim).]

We did not approve the election which the clerics of St. Florin had made of the provost of Mainz, contrary to the decrees of the holy Fathers. Moreover, since, as we directed, Count Henry of Namur [Col. 0515B] has ravaged your bishopric with plundering and fire, by these present letters we command you strictly to admonish him, exercising ecclesiastical censure, to cease from harassing both your church and yourself, and to make satisfaction for the losses and injuries inflicted. We, however, shall, with God as author, hold valid the sentence which you canonically pronounce against him. [Note: [Col. 0516D] Henry, bishop of Namur, son of Waleran, who, having married the daughter of Conrad of Luxembourg through Albero’s mediation, held the county of that province and other benefices from the Church of Trier under the title of a feudal benefice. Forgetful of religion and eager for war, he invaded the Trier region as an enemy. After negotiations for peace with him had been undertaken, but unsuccessfully, and when it became evident that the count aimed at anything rather than peace, Albero finally resorted to force. Following the count’s own example, by small expeditions and generally frequent incursions he brought about such devastation that he left the count no opportunity to recover his breath (Browerus, *Annales Trevirenses*, vol. II, p. 39).]

Given at the Lateran, 8 May.

## CDXLVII. To Henry of Sens and Renaud of Reims, bishops, and Bernard, abbot of Clairvaux.—Concerning the condemnation of Abelard and Arnold of Brescia, their confinement in monasteries, and the burning of their books. (1140, 16 July.)

[Mansi, *Concilia*, XXI, 564.]

[Col. 0515C]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers HENRY, archbishop of Sens, and RENAUD, archbishop of Reims, and their suffragans, and to his dearest son in Christ BERNARD, abbot of Clairvaux: greeting and apostolic blessing.

As the Apostle testifies (Eph. 4), there is known to be one God and one faith, upon which, as upon an immovable foundation—besides which no one can lay another—the unviolated firmness of the Catholic Church rests. Hence Blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, deserved to hear, because of his outstanding confession of this faith: “You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build [Col. 0515D] my Church” (Matt. 16). By “rock” he plainly signifies the firmness of faith and the solidity of Catholic unity.

This indeed is the seamless tunic [Col. 0516A] of the Redeemer, over which the soldiers cast lots, but which they were wholly unable to divide. Against it the nations raged at the beginning, and the peoples devised vain things; the kings of the earth stood forth, and the princes assembled together as one. Yet the apostles, leaders of the Lord’s flock, and their successors, apostolic men, inflamed with the ardor of charity and zeal for righteousness, did not hesitate to defend the faith and to plant it in the hearts of peoples by the shedding of their own blood. At last, when the fury of persecutors had ceased, he commanded the winds, and there came to be a great calm in the Church.

But because the enemy of humankind always prowls about, seeking whom he may devour, he introduced the deceitful fraud of heretics in order to assail the sincerity of the faith. Against these, the true governors of the Churches [Col. 0516B] rose up manfully and condemned their depraved doctrines together with their authors. Thus, at the great Synod of Nicaea the heretic Arius was condemned. The Synod of Constantinople condemned the heretic Manichaeus [probably Macedonius] by a fitting sentence. At the Synod of Ephesus Nestorius received the deserved condemnation of his error. Likewise, the Synod of Chalcedon refuted the Nestorian and Eutychian heresies, together with Dioscorus and his accomplices, by a most just sentence.

Moreover, Marcian—although a layman, yet a most Christian emperor—inflamed with love for the Catholic faith, writing to our most holy predecessor Pope John, spoke among other things as follows against those who seek to profane the sacred mysteries:

> “Let no cleric, nor anyone of any other condition, henceforth attempt publicly to dispute concerning the Christian faith. For whoever endeavors to reopen and debate anew matters once judged and rightly determined does injury to the decision of the most reverend synod; and punishment shall not be lacking for the despisers of this law, as for sacrilegious persons. Therefore, if any cleric dares publicly to discuss religion, he shall be removed from the fellowship of the clergy.”

We grieve, however, because, as we have learned from the examination of your letters and from the articles of errors sent to us by your fraternity, in these last days, when perilous times are at hand, the pernicious teaching of Master Peter Abelard, and the heresies aforesaid, and other perverse doctrines opposed to the Catholic faith [Col. 0516D] have begun to spring up. Yet in this matter we are especially comforted and give thanks to almighty God, because in your regions he has raised up such sons in place of fathers [Col. 0517A] and has willed that, in the time of our apostolate, there should be in his Church such distinguished shepherds, who endeavor to oppose the slanders of the new heretic and to present to Christ, one husband, an undefiled bride, a chaste virgin.

Therefore we, who, though unworthy, are seen to sit in the chair of St. Peter—to whom the Lord said, “And you, when you have turned again, strengthen your brethren” (Luke 22)—having taken counsel with our brother cardinal-bishops, condemn, by the authority of the holy canons, the articles sent to us by your discretion and all the doctrines of that same Peter, together with their author; and we impose perpetual silence upon him as upon a heretic. We also decree that all followers and defenders of his error are to be separated from the fellowship of the faithful and bound by the bond of [Col. 0517B] excommunication.

Given at the Lateran, 21 July.

## CDXLVIII. To Samson of Reims and Henry of Sens, archbishops, and Bernard, abbot of Clairvaux.—Concerning the condemnation of Abelard and Arnold. (1140, 16 July.)

[Mansi, *Concilia*, XXI, 565.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers SAMSON, archbishop of Reims, and HENRY, archbishop of Sens, and to his dearest son in Christ BERNARD, abbot of Clairvaux: greeting and apostolic blessing.

By these present letters we command your fraternity [Col. 0517C] to have Peter Abelard and Arnold of Brescia, fabricators of perverse doctrine and assailants of the Catholic faith, confined separately in religious houses wherever you judge best, and to have their books of error burned wherever they may be found.

Given at the Lateran, 16 July.

Do not show these transcripts to anyone until the letters themselves have been presented to the archbishops at the approaching conference in Paris.

## CDXLIX. To Segnioretto, priest, and his companions serving the Lord in the chapel of St. Saviour. (1140, 20 September.)

[Baluz., *Miscellanea*, IV, 592.]

[Col. 0517D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons SEGNIORETTO, priest, and his companions serving the Lord in the chapel of St. Saviour at Mustolio: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have entrusted the chapel of St. Saviour, which belongs by right to Blessed Peter, with all its appurtenances, to Jeremiah, prior of St. Fridianus, and to his brethren. Therefore, by these present letters we command and, in commanding, enjoin you to render them obedience and reverence humbly and without any contradiction.

Given beyond the Tiber, 20 September.

## CDL. He receives the Church of Pomerania under his protection; orders the episcopal see to be in the city of Wollin; and confirms the Church’s property. (1140, 14 October.)

[Ludevig, *Scriptores rerum Germanicarum*, II, 535.]

[Col. 0518A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother ADELBERTO, bishop of the Pomeranians, and to his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

By the office of the apostolate entrusted to us by God, it is fitting that we provide with fatherly care for our brethren, whether near at hand or far away, and preserve their rights in the churches in which they are known to serve the Lord; so that, as by the Lord’s ordering we are called fathers in name, so we may likewise be proved such in deed. For this reason, venerable brother Adalbert, bishop, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves the Pomeranian Church entrusted to you, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that the episcopal see shall be established in perpetuity in the city of Wollin, in the church of Blessed Albert.

Further, whatever goods and possessions that Church now justly and lawfully possesses, or may in future acquire, God being favorable, through grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you [Col. 0518C] and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: the city of Wollin itself, with its market, tavern, and all its appurtenances; Dymin, Treboses, Chozk, Wollgast, Huzon, Grosswin, Piritz, and Stargard, with their villages and all their appurtenances; Stettin; Camin, with its tavern, market, and appurtenances; throughout all Pomerania as far as the River Leba, from every ploughman two measures of grain and five denarii as tithe; and the market called Si chem.

We therefore decree that neither king nor duke nor any person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid Church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; [Col. 0518D] but that all things be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they have been granted. If, in future, any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this document of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his offence by suitable satisfaction, let him suffer deprivation of his rank and authority; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity perpetrated; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let him be subject to strict punishment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action [Col. 0519A] and before the strict Judge find the rewards of eternal peace.

Given beyond the Tiber through the hand of Aymericus, cardinal-deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on 14 October, in the fourth indiction, in the year 1140 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Pope Innocent II.

## CDLI. At the request of Bishop Grimald, he confirms the possessions of the Church of Penne. (1140, 27 October.)

[Ughelli, *Italia sacra*, I, 1119.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother GRIMALD, bishop of Penne, and to his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

[Col. 0519B] As no effect is to be granted to those who request unjust things, so the petition of lawful claimants ought not to be delayed. Therefore, beloved brother in the Lord, Bishop Grimald, we have graciously received your reasonable prayers and strengthen, by the privilege of this present document, the church of Blessed Mary and of the glorious martyr and deacon of Christ, Maximus. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that Church now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future acquire, God being favorable, through grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to state by their proper names: [Col. 0519C] the city itself with all its appurtenances; namely, with the hamlets of Neto, Cese, and Casale; St. John of Cypresso; Mezu; the castle called Collis Altus; the village of Paternella; the church of St. Mary of Liciano, with its churches and all its appurtenances; the church of St. Peter of Laureto, with its churches and all its appurtenances; the church of St. Serotinus; the church of St. Saturianus at Colle Cortino; the church of St. Felix of Monte Silvano; the church of St. Michael and St. John; the church of St. Barbara in the city of St. Angelo, with the church of St. Angelo, St. Andrew, and St. Antimus; the church of St. Mary of Atria; the church of St. Mary of Moscufo; the church of St. Mary of Planella; the church of St. Mary of Cumulo; [Col. 0519D] the church of St. Mary in the city of Quana; the church of Blessed Mary of Catiniano; the church of St. Mary of Bistejo; the church of St. Peter at Penne; the church of St. Clement of Balbine; the church of St. Mary of Trevio; the church of St. George at Ornanum; the church of St. Rufina of Aquilano; the church of St. Angelo of Puteo; the church of St. Mary of Rubilia; the church of St. Lawrence of Fabrica; the church of St. Mary of Brittuli; the church of St. John in Balneo; and the church of St. Mary of Podio.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid Church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they have been granted. [Col. 0520A] If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this document of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he makes amends by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his authority and rank; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity perpetrated; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let him be subject to strict punishment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Gerald, cardinal-priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal of the title of the Shepherd, have subscribed. I, Guizo, cardinal-priest of St. Cecilia, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal-deacon of the title of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Octavian, cardinal-deacon of St. Nicholas in Carcere, have subscribed. I, Thomas, cardinal-deacon of the Holy Roman Church, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aymericus, cardinal-deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, 27 October, fourth indiction, in the year 1140 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## CDLII. With the pope’s approval, the nuns of Crisenon are freed from the dominion of Molesme. (1140, 1 November.)

[*Gallia Christiana*, XII, Instrumenta, 112.]

[Col. 0520C]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughter ADALINA, abbess of Crisenon, and to all the sisters of the same place: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Both from the report of the bearer of these letters and from the letters of our son G., the illustrious count of Nevers, we have learned, and have received favorably, that you and your house with its appurtenances have been wholly freed from the yoke and dominion of the monks of Molesme. Whatever has been provided and established by our beloved sons Hugh, of good memory, then bishop of Auxerre, [Col. 0520D] and G., illustrious count of Nevers—whether concerning your organization or a change of your disposition—according to the judgment of the venerable abbots Hugh of Pontigny, A. of Vézelay, and G. of Troyes, and G., prior of Clairvaux, to whom we entrusted the matter, we likewise will and hold ratified by apostolic authority.

As to the privilege which you have requested to be made on this matter: when we have examined the matter more fully and have seen the document concerning the settlement of that peace, you will obtain it without difficulty. We exhort you, most beloved daughters in Christ, by the obligation of our office, to take the greatest care lest, under the occasion of this liberty—God forbid!—you diminish your former religious observance in any respect. Rather, serving God with the utmost humility and submission, strive with every diligence that you may at last deserve to pass [Col. 0521A] to the freedom of the glory of the children of God.

Given at Rome, 1 November, in the year of the Lord 1140.

## CDLIII. He receives the monastery of St. James of Besse under his protection and confirms its goods and privileges, imposing on the monks an annual payment of one gold piece. (1140, 19 November.)

[Ughelli, *Italia sacra*, IV, 776.]
