INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son NICOLAS, abbot of the monastery of St. James of Bexia, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

[Col. 0521B] “Of apostolic governance,” etc., as far as “we may foster by our protection.” Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Nicholas, we graciously assent to your reasonable petitions and receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves the monastery over which, by God’s ordinance, you are known to preside; and we strengthen it by the protection of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions, etc., as far as “shall remain unimpaired.”

Among these we have thought fit to state by their proper names: namely, the church of St. Gratian, situated in the suburb of Vercelli, with the hospital for the poor; the land at Lateriano; at Tarto; at [lacuna]; at the hamlet of Ruffo; at Lebraria; and at Castello Nuovo, with all that pertains to that church and hospital; the church of St. Saviour in the borough; St. Agatha, with lands acquired in the plain of St. Agatha; [Col. 0521C] the church of St. Michael near Cerione; the church of St. Mary at Ronicenda; the church of St. Martin of Scala with its appurtenances; the church of St. Eusebius near the castle of Montisalto, with a hospital for the poor and everything belonging to the same church and hospital; also the lands which you possess at Carisio, Salutiola, Cerione, and in the district of Biella; the estate of Medieni; and the wood called Rovicenda.

Furthermore, no cleric or layperson whatsoever may presume to exact tithes from you upon the produce of your labors, which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or upon the fodder of your animals. Upon your death, etc., as far as “they shall jointly provide for the election, according to God and the Rule of St. Benedict,” saving the canonical right and [Col. 0521D] reverence due to the bishop of Vercelli.

We decree, therefore, that neither the bishop of Vercelli nor any person whatsoever may, etc., as far as “beneficial in every respect.” And let the monastery itself remain without contradiction in the liberty granted by Raynerius, bishop of Vercelli of good memory, founder of that monastery. As a token of this protection and liberty prescribed by the Apostolic See, pay annually to us and our successors one gold piece. If, therefore, in future, etc., as far as “let him be subject to strict punishment.” But upon all who preserve the rights of that place, etc., as far as “may they find the rewards of eternal peace.” Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Albert, bishop of Albano. [Col. 0522A] I, Gerard, cardinal-priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Chrysogonus, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Praxedes. I, Anselm, cardinal-priest of St. Lawrence in Lucina. I, Peter, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Pastor. I, Goizo, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Cecilia. I, Guido, unworthy priest of the Holy Roman Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Arimericus, cardinal-deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, 19 November, fourth indiction, in the year 1140 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## CDLIV. He receives the monastery of St. Paul in Carinthia under his protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. (1140, 24 November.)

[Col. 0522B] [Hormayr, *Archiv für Süddeutsche Geographie*, 1821, p. 238.]

## CDLV. Privilege for Moyenmoutier. (1140, 12 December.)

[Belhomme, *Histoire de Moyenmoutier*, p. 284.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son MILO, abbot of Moyenmoutier, and to his successors regularly appointed: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The care of the Catholic Church has been entrusted to us by God, the supreme shepherd, so that we may love with fatherly affection and be the more ready to incline to the devout petitions of those known to adhere more fervently to ecclesiastical disciplines and the Rules of the holy Fathers. [Col. 0522C] For then our service shall be acceptable to God, if the institutions and order of holy places are preserved in the purity of religious life through our protection.

Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Milo, we graciously assent to your reasonable petitions and receive under the guardianship of Blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery, in which, by God’s ordinance, you are known to serve; and we strengthen it by the text of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and lawfully possesses, or may in future acquire, God being favorable, through grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to record by their proper [Col. 0522D] names: the village belonging to the monastery itself, Moyenmoutier, with the other villages subject to it, namely Rua (Ravon), Werria (La Voivre), Visivallum (Veseval); the church of St. Peter at Scamnum (Pechone), with the estate acquired there; the village called Alba (Blamont); the church at Montiniacum (Montigny), and the estate which you hold there; the church at Guineix (Gugney), with its estate and the persons whom you hold there; the church at Erkelingis (Ersing), with its estate; the court of Montis (Mont-dit-Berg), with its appurtenances; at the court of Mantonis (Mantoncourt), the estate which belonged to Odo; the church at Serris (Serres), with what you have lawfully acquired; the church of Riclusicortis (Rechicourt); [Col. 0523A] the church at Corte (Gelacourt) and the chapel at Asteravalla (Aizerailles); the field and meadow which Hilfrid gave you in that same village; at Manceriolae (perhaps Mazerulles), an estate with woodland and a mill; the allod at Moyen (Moyen), which Draco and Robert granted to that monastery; and the allod which you have lawfully acquired from the church of St. Deodatus; the estate at Romoraldivilla (Remenoville) and the allod of Lord Garcirius; and at Barbonville the allod which the same Garsirus gave you; the allod which Widericus and Cono gave you; the possessions of Barbonville [Note: [Col. 0523D] Among the possessions of Barbonville may be included Hassonville and Lord Stephen, commonly called Domtaille, of which no special mention is made here.] at Manieriae (Magnières); the tithes of Avenigis and Croadis, which belonged to the benefice of Moyenmoutier itself; the church at Gevoniscurte (Givicourt), with its chapels; and the land which Simon of Paroya—now Paroye—gave you there; the exchange at Hunaldi Masnile (Hunamesnil); what you possess at Marsallum and Richecicortem (Marsal and Richecourt); and an allod at Lord Rosvinus—perhaps Lord Juvinus, Domgevin; the court of Welchercha (Veldkirch), with its appurtenances; the church of Blessed Maximin, with the chapels of Blessed Mary and St. Aper at Erguiseim (now Krautergersheim); at Tutelheim (Titelheim), nine holdings; at Hundenisheim (Hindesheim), the church of Blessed Peter the Apostle and an estate with its appurtenances; at Uthratisheim (Itersheim), the allod of Gerard and Hecelinus. At Startosheim (Storstheim), one holding. At Hergenseim (Krautergersheim), one holding. At Wirchensheim, four; and at [Col. 0523C] Biristet (perhaps Baar), one.

The church of St. Maurice in the village called Capella—perhaps La Chapelle above the Mortagne; the church at Alta Petra (Autrepierre) and the estate at Maleséivilla (Malzéville); the church of Echery, with its appurtenances; the cell of Bellevallis, with the churches and estates lawfully granted to it; the church at Raspatium (Repas); in the village of Moyenmoutier, the chapel of St. Aper; at the Seven Firs (Ban de Sapt), the chapel of St. Gregory; at Hurbacium (Hurbache), namely the chapels of St. Stephen, of the Holy Cross [Note: [Col. 0523D] This chapel of the Holy Cross is today called that of St. Gengulf, on account of that saint’s relics later placed in it.] and of St. Mary [Note: [Col. 0523D] This second chapel of the parish of Hurbache is situated in the hamlet called Vepria, commonly La Voivre.]; at Ormont (St. Jean d’Ormont); at Visivallum (Veseval), the chapel of St. Leodegar; at Dilonisvilla (Glonville), the church of St. Maurice with its chapels; at Busseriae (Bussières) [Note: [Col. 0524D] This is perhaps the more elevated place where they report that the mother church of Matexeio and Valesiis formerly stood; it is now called the Hermits of Bussières.] [Col. 0523D] the chapel of St. Remigius with the chapel of St. Giles; in the city of Strasbourg, one residence; at Abnieim, seven holdings of land; the court of Radavillaris (Raviller), with its dependent vineyards, meadows, and fields; at Bercheim, vineyards and courts, and the tithes of the demesne lands of the lord bishop of Toul; and the wood there given you by him. [Note: [Col. 0524D] Hence it is evident that, after losing through the judgment of Pope Innocent the principal court of Bercheim, the monks of Moyenmoutier still held there other smaller courts, as well as tithes and woodland.] At Rabaldivilare (Ribauville), Aresvingordos. At Castinoxe (Châtenoy), a court [Col. 0524A] with vineyards; the cell at Tanvillare (Tanviller) and the tithes of that allod; the church at Montis with its chapels—Mont, Moussey, and Thionville; and the church of Barbonville.

Furthermore, by apostolic authority we forbid any advocate, in the goods or judicial rights of that monastery, to receive anything beyond what has been established from ancient times, to impose upon them any new customs or exactions, or to appoint a subadvocate in his place. We therefore decree that neither the bishop himself, nor king, duke, prince, nor any person whatsoever may rashly disturb or burden the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it in any manner; but that all things be kept whole for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they have been granted. [Col. 0524B] If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this document of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his offence by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his authority and rank; let him acknowledge himself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity perpetrated; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let him be subject to strict punishment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

[Col. 0524C] I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Gerard, cardinal-priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Gregory, cardinal-deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Otto, cardinal-deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aimericus, cardinal-deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, 12 December, fourth indiction, in the year 1140 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## CDLVI. He confirms the goods and immunities of the monastery of Stivagium. (1140, 12 December.)

[Hugo, *Annales Praemonstratenses*, II, p. 540.]

[Col. 0524D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son HENRY, provost of Stivagium, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

To us the care of the Catholic Church has been entrusted by God, the supreme shepherd, so that we may love God’s servants with paternal affection and, all the more, strive by every means to foster their devotion [Col. 0525A], since they are known to adhere with greater fervour to ecclesiastical disciplines and to the Rules of the holy Fathers. For then will our service be pleasing to God, if, through our protection, the wholesome institution, discipline, and order of holy places are preserved in the purity of religious life. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Provost Henry, we graciously assent to your reasonable requests. We receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid monastery, over which by God’s providence you are known to preside, and strengthen it by the protection of this present writing; decreeing that whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future, by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes [Col. 0525B], the offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, God being favourable, be able to acquire, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to record by their proper names: the village belonging to that monastery itself, with the other villages subject to it—namely, Brehemont, with all the land from Lacavere to Bellummont, cultivated and uncultivated; and fifteen holdings at Mansuile, with all the land from Lastigie to Fossehe; together with another estate from Haldidvidis Ford to the Great Stream, including fishing in that stream; with the entire wood called Espasge; and fishing from Broken Rock to Haldidvidis Ford; and, moreover, a third part of the ban of Stivagium itself, in lands, meadows, woods, waters, and the pasture-rights for every kind of animal throughout [Col. 0525C] the whole ban.

Also the tithe of the whole of that ban, both of crops and of animals, together with the head-rent of persons dwelling throughout all Lorraine, both persons belonging to the monastery of Eleon and those belonging to Stivagium. Sindronisvilla, which Sendraas gave, with its tithe, its serfs, and the jurisdiction of that ban, with its boundary extending from the ford of the Moselle called St Peter’s Ford to the wood called Liwir, and beyond the field of St Quentin to the aforesaid Moselle, with fishing as far as Tornalli; the estate of Saberti-orti, with serfs and the jurisdiction of that ban.

The four quarter-units of land which you possess at Frovilla; the twelve which you possess in the freehold of Bassumpunt; the two quarter-units of land which you possess at Hennolvilla; the freehold [Col. 0525D] of Envas, with two woods and the jurisdiction of that ban, with serfs; the tithe of crofts (*croadae*) and enclosed fields (*ancingiae*), and of the cultivation of four oxen ploughing at the same place; and the orchard-land (*brol[i]*) which you have held freely from ancient times.

The court of Dunceres and its church, with the chapel subject to it in honour of St Mary; and eight quarter-units of land belong to the aforesaid court. The lesser rents of the four quarter-units amount to sixteen pence and twelve hens; and each of those four quarter-units owes, for carriage-service and grinding, three pence and four sheaves of the enclosed fields, and at the season of hay-cutting and harvest, a sickle; and they owe three allotments, amounting to six shillings [Col. 0526A]. Fifteen gardens owe five shillings, fifteen hens, and five eggs each. And the rents at Sefrevile, Roiville, Bereznil, and Nossoncour owe five shillings; and the estate of Jungeris, with serfs, woods, meadows, and the jurisdiction of the ban.

In Alsace, at Singolsem: the church in honour of blessed Peter, with every tithe, and the estate on which that church stands; and fifty-two *hoba[e]* in the same district. The church of Dispaglingis, with every tithe. At Farlivigis, the church with every tithe, and the church with tithes at Falves. At Andlan, the church of St Andrew with every tithe; the church of Stivagium, in which your religious house is situated.

The pastoral care of the souls, both clerics and laypeople, of the parish [Col. 0526B] churches with all their appurtenances: namely, the church of St Mary situated in the same place, with the chapel of St Michael at Belmunt; also the chapel of St Aper belonging to the church of Norpadi; the chapel of St Dionysius at Burguntia; the chapel of St Remigius; and the parish church of St Mary of Mosteriolum, with the chapel of St Martin at Nohenneis, together with their tithes and rents, and the tithe of Cretumville.

At Bellummont, fifteen holdings occupied in the churchyard; at the church of Norpadi, fifteen holdings in the churchyard; at Burguntia, fifteen holdings in the churchyard; at St Remigius, fifteen holdings in the churchyard. At Nohenneis, fifteen holdings in the churchyard assigned to the lighting of the church of St Mary. Likewise, synodal pleas and the jurisdiction [Col. 0526C] over laypeople, and the pastoral offices of those who receive churches from your hands; and the other matters which belong to you by the grant of Bruno, of holy recollection and pious memory, of the holy Church of Toul, who drew up and gave you a privilege concerning these matters.

> [Note: [Col. 0525D] Bruno, when he became pope under the name Leo IX, chose to be styled bishop of the Church of Toul. What the privilege issued by [Col. 0526D] Bruno, whether as bishop of Toul or as Roman pontiff, contained is unknown, since it has long ceased to exist in the archives of Stivagium, having, as is believed, been carried off to Andelacum.]

Moreover, by apostolic authority we forbid any advocate to take anything from the goods or peasantry of the monastery except with consent, or to impose upon them new customs or any exactions, or to appoint a sub-advocate in his place.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no bishop, king, duke, prince, or any person whatsoever rashly to disturb or burden the aforesaid monastery, or to take away, retain, diminish, or harass its possessions by any molestations; but that all shall be preserved whole [Col. 0526D], for the benefit in every respect of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, after a second or third warning, unless he correct his offence by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment of the iniquity he has perpetrated; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject to severe vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of this place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Sertin. I, Ivo, cardinal priest of the title of St Lawrence in Damaso. I, Chrysogonus, cardinal priest of the title of St Praxedes. I, G[—], cardinal priest of the title of St Callistus. I, Cono, cardinal priest of the title of St Cecilia. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius [Col. 0527B] and Bacchus. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of St George at the Golden Veil. I, Gerard, cardinal deacon of St Mary in Domnica. I, Octavian, cardinal of St Nicholas in Carcere. I, Thomas, cardinal deacon of the Holy Roman Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Henry, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the second Ides of December, in the third indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1140, in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## CDLVII. Confirms the introduction of Premonstratensian canons into the monastery of St Dionysius at Schefflaren.  
*(1140, 18 December.)*

[HUGO, *Annal. Praem.*, II, p. 483.]

[Col. 0527C]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son ENGELBERT, provost of the monastery of St Dionysius at Schefflaren, and to his brethren, present and future, regularly appointed in perpetuity.

It accords with the mercy of apostolic governance to choose religious persons and to strengthen their places with pious protection. For it is recognised as worthy and consistent with honour that we, who have been raised to the governance of churches, should both protect them from the malice of wicked people and foster them by the patronage of the apostolic see. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your reasonable requests [Col. 0527D], receive your monastery under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, and strengthen it by this present written instrument.

First, we decree that in your monastery the canonical order, according to the Rule of St Augustine and the institution of the Church of Prémontré, shall be preserved inviolably for all time. Moreover, whatever goods and possessions the same monastery now justly and lawfully possesses, whether through the gift of our venerable brother Otto, bishop of Freising, or of other faithful of Christ, or may in future be able to acquire through the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors [Col. 0528A].

We also enact that none professed in your monastery may, on any pretext, transfer to other places without the permission of the abbot and chapter; nor may anyone presume to receive or retain those who depart against your will. During a general interdict in that bishopric, we grant permission to celebrate the divine offices in a subdued voice and with closed doors, provided that no person under interdict or excommunication is admitted. Priests who are to be admitted in your churches shall be presented to the bishop: in spiritual matters they shall answer to him, but in temporal matters to you.

Furthermore, no cleric or layperson whatsoever may presume to demand from you tithes of the produce which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or of the increase of your animals [Col. 0528B]. You shall receive chrism, holy oil, the consecration of altars or churches, and the ordinations of clerics to be promoted to holy orders from the diocesan bishop, provided that he is Catholic, enjoys the favour and communion of the apostolic see, and is willing to provide these things freely and without any improper charge. Otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer; supported by our authority, he shall grant what is requested.

On your death, you who are now provost of that place, no one shall be set over it by any device of deceit or by force, except the person whom the brethren, by common consent and according to God and the Rule of St Augustine, judge should be chosen. We likewise decree that the burial-place of that house shall be free, so that no one may hinder the devotion and final wish of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated, without prejudice to the right of the mother church [Col. 0528C].

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away, retain, diminish, or harass its possessions by any vexations; but that everything shall be preserved whole, for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support it was granted. If any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, after a second or third warning, unless he correct his offence by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his honour and power [Col. 0528D]; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment of the iniquity he has perpetrated; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and our Lord Jesus Christ; and let him be subject to severe vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of this place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Albert, bishop of Attanum [Attanensis]. [Col. 0529A] I, Otto, cardinal deacon of St George at the Golden Veil. I, Anselm, cardinal priest of the title of St Lawrence in Lucina. I, Bernard, cardinal deacon of St Mary in Domnica. I, Ivo, cardinal priest of the title of St Lawrence in Damaso. I, Chrysogonus, cardinal priest of the title of St Pastor. I, Gorzo, cardinal priest of the title of St Cecilia. I, Aubald, cardinal deacon of St Mary in Via Lata. I, Thomas, cardinal deacon of the Holy Roman Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy [Col. 0529B] Roman Church, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of January, in the third indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1140, in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## CDLXVIII. Affirms to Archbishop Albero of Trier and his successors the grant of the monastery of St Maximin by King Conrad.  
*(1140, 20 December.)*

[HONTHEIM, *Hist. Trevir.*, I, 547.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother ADALBERO, archbishop of Trier and legate of the apostolic see, and to his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

Then does holy mother Church rejoice and exult when she bears and nourishes a son so full of faith, fortified by diligence and charity, who, filled with virtues by the splendour of the divine majesty, shines forth; and who appears glorious and worthy of reverence in the sight of the Roman pontiff, the most holy Roman Church, kings, princes, and peoples. Therefore, venerable brother in the Lord Adalbero, archbishop of Trier and legate of the apostolic see, inclined by your prayers and those of many religious persons interceding for you [Col. 0529C], and not unmindful of the devotion and services more generously rendered by your fraternity in the times of our predecessors of happy memory, Popes Paschal and Callistus, and in our own time, after consultation with our brethren, the bishops and cardinals, we confirm by apostolic authority to you and your successors, and strengthen by this present written instrument, that right which our dearest son Conrad, King of the Romans, or his predecessors, are known to have possessed in the abbey of St Maximin, and which has been granted or restored by that Conrad to you, and through you to the Church of Trier [Col. 0529D], saving in every respect the right of the Holy Roman Church, if it has any.

If anyone, knowing this page of our confirmation, should rashly attempt to act against it, unless he make fitting satisfaction, let him incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul. But those who preserve these things shall obtain the blessing of that same almighty God and of His aforesaid apostles. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of St George at the Golden Veil. [Col. 0530B] I, Vas[allus], cardinal deacon of St Eustachius. I, Hubald, cardinal deacon of St Mary in Via Lata. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Absalon, cardinal priest of the title of St Lawrence in Lucina. I, Guido, unworthy priest of the Holy Roman Church. I, Luc[—], cardinal priest of the title of St Lawrence in Damaso. I, Chrysogonus, cardinal priest of the title of St Praxedes. I, Ramerius, cardinal priest of the title of St Prisca. I, Gerzo, cardinal priest of St Cecilia. I, Hubald, cardinal deacon of St Adrian.

[Col. 0530C] Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of January, in the fourth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1140, in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

> [Note: [Col. 0529D] Zyllesius, in *Defens. abbat. S. Maxim.*, part II, section VII, §2, p. 99, objects to this bull:  
> 1. That its autograph has not been seen.  
> 2. That there survive original documents of supreme pontiffs contrary to it, especially a bull of Innocent II from this same year, 1140, which decrees that the monastery of St Maximin shall never be subjected to any see or church, but shall remain under the right and protection of the Holy Roman Church and under the *mundiburdium*, or protection, of the emperors, enjoying the liberty and immunity which the same monastery is known to have possessed from Roman pontiffs and emperors.  
> 3. That this pontifical bull for the archbishop is merely confirmatory of Conrad’s concession, and that, if the latter falls—as something merely recited—this one cannot stand.  
> 4. That in all papal confirmations customarily granted to newly elected abbots, the monastery of St Maximin is said to be immediately subject to the Holy See.  
> But how weakly all these arguments stand may readily be perceived from what precedes, especially since the bull of Innocent issued on 6 May of this year, obtained surreptitiously, offers little—indeed, no—obstacle and has been revoked by the present document once the facts became known.]

## CDLIX. Confirms the rights and exemptions of the newly founded monastery of Hemmerod.  
*(1140, 20 December.)*

[HONTHEIM, *ibid.*, 548.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son RANDULPH, abbot of the monastery of Claustrum, and to his brethren, present and future, regularly appointed in perpetuity.

Since without the worship of true religion neither the unity of charity can endure nor service pleasing to God be rendered [Col. 0530D], it is fitting for apostolic authority to love religious persons and to foster their places by the protection of the apostolic see. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Randulph, we graciously assent to your just requests, receive under the guardianship of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid monastery over which, by God’s providence, you preside [Col. 0531A], and strengthen it by this present privilege. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the aforesaid monastery now possesses, or may in future, through the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, with the Lord’s aid, be able to acquire, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Certainly, no cleric or layperson whatsoever may presume to demand from you tithes from the produce which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or from the increase of your animals. We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away [Col. 0531B], retain what has been taken away, diminish, or harass its possessions by any molestations; but that all shall be preserved whole, for the benefit in every respect of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, unless he correct his offence suitably, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment of the iniquity he has perpetrated; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject to severe vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of this venerable place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit [Col. 0531C] of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Albert, bishop of Albano. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Vasallus, cardinal deacon of St Eustachius. I, Ivo, cardinal priest of the title of St Lawrence in Damaso. I, Chrysogonus, cardinal priest of the title of St Praxedes. [Col. 0531D] I, G[—], cardinal priest of the title of St Callistus. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of the title of St Nicholas in Carcere. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of St Pastor. I, Guizo, cardinal priest of the title of St Cecilia.

Given at the Lateran through the hands of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of January, in the third indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1140, in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## CDLX. To Henry, bishop of Moravia, who wishes to convert pagans to the faith: he writes that the bishop should first come to Rome.  
*(About 12 April 1140.)*

[BOCZEK, *Codex diplom. Morav.*, I, p. 212.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable [Col. 0532A] brother HENRY, bishop of Moravia: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have received your fraternity’s letter graciously and rejoiced to be informed of your well-being. Yet, since from it we have learned of your intention to preach the word of the Lord to pagans and to convert them to the faith of Christ, it is necessary that you come to your mother, the holy Roman Church, so that, once the fruit expected from this has been understood, and having there received, by her authority, a method of teaching according to the doctrine of the universal Church, you may, with the Lord’s aid, accomplish what must be done.

Given at the Lateran, on the second Ides of April.

## CDLXI. To Hugh, abbot of the monastery of St Augustine at Canterbury.  
*(1139–1141, 20 November.)*

[*Rerum Anglicarum Scriptores*, II, p. 1801.]

[Col. 0532B]

INNOCENT, bishop, etc. . . . . .

We have received your letters and messengers with paternal kindness and carefully considered what you have reported to us. We wish indeed to love your monastery with special affection, as one existing under the guardianship and proprietorship of blessed Peter; to foster it in the liberty bestowed upon it by our predecessors and ourselves; and to restrain your disturbers by apostolic authority. It is therefore incumbent upon you, beloved sons in the Lord, that, just as your monastery was the beginning of religious life in England, so you should likewise laudably devote yourselves to the observance of the monastic profession [Col. 0532C], and take care to present yourselves before God and people in such a way that almighty God may be honoured by your conduct and the apostolic see may rejoice with maternal affection.

We also direct you to have made for our use a small hand-held Bible, such as befits the Roman pontiff. And because, beloved son in the Lord Hugh, we have learned that, on account of your relatives, the same monastery has suffered many losses and burdens, we command you, by this direction, to remove them from the lordship of the monastery’s manors, so that the place may be freed from such a burden and you may deserve not to incur any further reproach or sin from this source.

You shall also compel the monk Hubert, whom we have heard to be a disturber of the brethren and harmful to [Col. 0532D] that place, to return to his own monastery, namely St Andrew’s. You shall manage and conduct the affairs of that place by the counsel of the prior and brethren, not by the counsels of any outsiders; and, with the counsel of those brethren, you shall strive to make up the number which is said to have been diminished, from honourable and religious persons. You shall also firmly maintain and observe the commands contained in the authentic privileges of the apostolic see granted to the aforesaid monastery.

Moreover, should any adversity befall you or your brethren, it shall be your duty to have recourse to the Roman Church, the common mother of all, or to send those same brethren, so that both you and they may be supported by fitting consolations from us and relieved from their oppressions. We have, moreover, directed our brother Theobald, archbishop of Canterbury, under prohibition not further to exact from you the pound, shilling, and seven pence [Col. 0533A] demanded from you for the receipt of chrism and holy oil; and we likewise forbid you to pay it henceforth.

Given at the Lateran, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of December.

## CDLXII. To Theobald, archbishop of Canterbury: forbids him to inflict injuries on the monks of St Augustine or to exact from them “a pound, a shilling, and seven denarii for the provision of chrism and holy oil.”  
*(1139–1141, November.)*

[*Chronicle of W. Thorn*, in TWISDEN, *Hist. Anglic. Script.*, II, 1800.]

## CDLXIII. To Henry, bishop of Winchester: that he should protect the monastery of St Augustine at Canterbury.  
*(1139–1141, November.)*

[*Hist. Angl. Script.*, II, 1801.]

[Col. 0533B]

INNOCENT, bishop, etc. . . . .

We give the greatest thanks to your fraternity, because you have shown attentive concern for the things of blessed Peter and have stood by the abbot and brethren of the monastery of St Augustine at Canterbury as helper and protector in their needs. And because virtue consists not in beginning but in completing, we command your experience, both requesting and enjoining, that you uphold as usual the aforesaid monastery and the brethren serving the Lord there; that, out of reverence for blessed Peter and for ourselves, you permit no one to harass them by injuries or molestations; and that you take the utmost care [Col. 0533C] to furnish counsel and assistance in every respect, both with the king and with all others, as necessity requires. Thus you should strive to strengthen them in our stead, so that they may rejoice in their security and liberty, and we may be able to return fuller thanks for your care.

## CDLXIV. To Stephen, king of the English: that he should not allow the monastery of St Augustine at Canterbury to suffer injuries.  
*(1139–1141, November.)*

[As above.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, etc.

The more almighty God … and below, whence there is also laid upon you the obligation to love religious places and, from consideration of filial devotion, not to permit what belongs to blessed Peter to be harassed by any injuries or molestations [Col. 0533D]. For whoever deserves to have the same prince of the apostles as patron in heaven stands secure against adversaries on earth. Your kingdom can never be better established or enlarged than if you strive to honour churches and ecclesiastical persons. Therefore, we direct, request, and exhort your fraternity in the Lord that you do not trouble the monastery of St Augustine at Canterbury—which that holy man himself unquestionably offered to the prince of the apostles, and which Roman pontiffs and your predecessor Æthelbert, king of the English, endowed with liberty and fortified by their privileges—or permit it to be harassed by anyone. Rather, protect it against every external tumult of disturbances, so that those who serve God within it [Col. 0534A], rejoicing in their peace and liberty, may strive more earnestly to pour forth prayers to God for you and for the peace of your kingdom, and that we may thereby be able to give more abundant thanks to your serenity.

## CDLXV. Privilege granted to Humbert, bishop of Autun.  
*(1141, 21 January.)*

[D. PLANCHER, *Histoire de Bourgogne*, vol. I, *Preuves*, p. 41.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HUMBERT, bishop of Autun, and to his successors canonically appointed.

It is equitable and consistent with justice that we, who by the office of apostolate imposed upon us bear care for all churches [Col. 0534B], should preserve intact for each of them its own dignities and privileges. For it is worthy and reasonable that the noble and renowned Church of Autun, which has remained steadfast in the Catholic faith and obedience and in reverence for blessed Peter and the holy Roman Church, should enjoy its prerogative freely. Therefore, dearest brother in Christ, Humbert, bishop of Autun, whom we have adorned with the distinction of the pallium, graciously assenting to your reasonable petitions, we confirm by the privilege of this present writing, to you and through you to the Church of Autun, and to your successors for ever, whatever grants, churches, villages, towns, or goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may lawfully, with the Lord’s aid, acquire in the future.

Among these we have added the following, to be expressly named: the church of Blessed Mary and St Lazarus at Avalon, and the castle of Toilonius with all their appurtenances; the churches of Ulmo; the church of St Sabina; the church of St Mary of Borbon; and also the right which you have in the church—namely, at Rigny, Brion, and Sarri [Col. 0534C].

We also grant you freely and without opposition to correct what ought to be corrected and to arrange what ought to be arranged within your bishopric, according to the constitutions of the holy Fathers. Likewise we confirm to you the vicariate dignity which your predecessors are known to have held in the Church of Lyons down to these times. No primate or metropolitan, therefore, may presume to determine anything in your bishopric concerning matters belonging to your diocese without the consent of you or your suffragans [Col. 0534D]. For the apostolic see, which appoints primates, metropolitans, and bishops, has prescribed for each his own boundaries and limits.

Accordingly, numerous decrees of Roman pontiffs have preceded this and other provisions: namely, that if any metropolitan, without the presence of all his suffragans or the counsel of bishops, should wish to conduct or burden either their churches or other churches—not merely those which belong to his own diocese—he shall be strictly corrected by all, lest he dare in future to presume such things. And again, if any metropolitan bishop should attempt, without the counsel and will of all the suffragan bishops, to do anything beyond what pertains solely to his own diocese [Col. 0535A], he shall be subject to the peril of his rank, and what he has done shall be held null and void.

On the death of you or any bishop among your successors, no provost or layperson may presume to seize the episcopal residences or occupy any episcopal goods; instead, all shall be preserved for the succeeding bishop. Whoever presumes to attempt this shall know that he is subject to excommunication.

We have therefore decreed that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb that church, take away anything of its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish, or harass it by any vexations; but that all shall be preserved whole, for the benefit and advantage of you and of the poor. If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution [Col. 0535B], should rashly attempt to act against it, after a second or third warning, unless he make suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity he has perpetrated; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and our Lord Jesus Christ; and let him be subject to severe vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that church may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. [Col. 0535C] I, Chrysogonus, cardinal priest of St Praxedes. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of St Pastor. I, Boizo, cardinal priest of the title of St Cecilia. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Otto, cardinal deacon. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Gerard, cardinal deacon of St Mary in Domnica.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon of the holy Roman Church and …, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of February, in the fourth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation [Col. 0535D] 1140, in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Lord Innocent.

## CDLXVI. Confirms the possessions and privileges of the convent of St Mary at Minervium.  
*(1141, 28 January.)*

[GRADONICI, *Pont. Brix.*, 209.]

## CDLXVII. Privilege for the monastery of Baumburg.  
*(1141, 1 February.)*

[*Monumenta Boica*, vol. II, p. 186.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GOTSCHALK, provost of the church of Saint [name uncertain] at Baumburg, and his brethren, present [Col. 0536A] and future, regularly appointed in perpetuity.

To assent to the just desires of religious men, and willingly to grant their reasonable petitions, is urged upon the apostolic see, over which, by God’s bounty, we preside, by its authority and by the unity of fraternal charity. For this reason, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously receive your prayers and confirm to you and to your church the gift, reasonably made, of the church of Blessed Mary of Hawarteschirha, together with its tithes, villages, and estates, by our venerable brother Henry, bishop of Passau, at the request and with the consent of Wolfram, advocate of that village, and of his son Beringarius; Wolfram also freely resigning that same advocacy for the benefit of the aforesaid church of Saint Margaret. We decree that in the aforesaid church of Blessed Mary [Col. 0536B] the canonical order according to the Rule of blessed Augustine shall be observed inviolate for all time.

Moreover, whatever possessions and whatever goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by grant of popes, gift of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, by the Lord’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. We therefore decree that absolutely no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any other injuries; but that all things be preserved intact, for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and maintenance they were granted. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing the terms of this constitution of ours, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make amendment by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour, recognize himself or herself as answerable before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and at the final judgment be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Almeric, deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman [Col. 0536D] Church, on the Kalends of February, in the fourth indiction, in the year 1140 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

CDLXVIII. He secures for the monastery of Saint Mary of Lucedio an estate given by Rainerius, marquis of Montferrat. (1141, 3 March.)

[MORIONDI, *Monumenta Aquensia*, I, p. 52, from the original.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son RICHARD, abbot of the monastery of Saint Mary of Lucedio, and to his successors living there according to rule for ever.

The worship of true religion cannot be wholly observed without integrity. But when disputes and quarrels arise under the pretext of legal causes, the mind is troubled and the radiance and delight of inward contemplation are withdrawn. For this reason, because every effort must be made to provide peace and concord for religious persons, we approve, beloved son in the Lord Richard, abbot, the renunciation made by Otto, abbot of Saint Januarius, and his brethren, after many lawsuits and disputes, concerning the estate which Rainerius, marquis of Montferrat, of illustrious memory, gave out of pious devotion to Anselm, then bishop of Vercelli, confirming it to the monastery of Blessed Mary of Lucedio, over which, by God’s authority, you preside. We confirm to you and your successors, and through you to the aforesaid monastery of Blessed Mary for ever, that same possession together with the other goods which you now justly and lawfully possess or may hereafter reasonably acquire. We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may, etc.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Albert, bishop of Albano. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Anselm, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina. I, Guido, unworthy priest of the holy Roman Church. I, Stamius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina. I, Grisogonus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Ribaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia. I, Gorzo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. [Col. 0537C] I, Otto, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint George at the Veil of Gold. I, Vasallus, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Eustace. I, Ubaldus, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Adrian. I, Thomas, cardinal deacon of the holy Roman Church.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Almeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Nones of March, in the fourth indiction, in the year 1130 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the twelfth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

CDLXIX. He confirms to the monastery of Tournus the churches of Planésiac and Tresilliac, in the dioceses of Lyons and Clermont. (1141, 25 March.)

[COCQUELINES, II, p. 249.]

[Col. 0537D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son PETER, abbot of Tournus, and to his successors regularly appointed for ever.

The authority of the apostolic see entrusted to us urges us to extend the protection of guardianship to places and persons which duly invoke its assistance with devotion. For just as no effect is to be granted to those who seek unjust things, so the petition of those requesting what is lawful and just is not to be delayed, especially when they either appear devoutly to embrace religion and rejoice to serve the Lord under it, or rejoice to serve almighty God with an honourable life and praiseworthy ordering of conduct. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, we graciously assent to your reasonable petitions, and confirm to you and your successors, and through you to that monastery, the grants reasonably made to your monastery by our venerable brethren: namely, of the church of Planésiac by Hubert, archbishop of Besançon, and of the church of Tresilliac by Aymeric, bishop of Clermont. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods the aforesaid churches now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter acquire by grant of popes, gift of kings [Col. 0538B] or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God being favourable, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you for ever. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make amendment by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour, recognize himself or herself as answerable before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and at the final judgment be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve what is just for those same churches may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Chrysogonus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes, have subscribed. I, Rainerius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca, have subscribed. I, Guido, priest of the title of Saint Cecilia, have subscribed. I, Ubaldus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed. I, Ubaldus, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian, have subscribed.

[Col. 0538D] Given at the Lateran, through the hands of Aymeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the eighth day before the Kalends of April, in the third indiction, in the year 1141 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the twelfth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

[Note: [Col. 0537D] It should read “the eleventh”; for, according to Dionysian reckoning, the year 1141 corresponds to the year 1140 of the common era, as the third indiction indicates, which was counted only in this [Col. 0538D] year and corresponded to the eleventh year of Innocent’s pontificate.]

CDLXX. He receives the monastery of Aurea Vallis (diocese of Trier) under protection and confirms its goods. (1141, 12 April.)

[Dom CALMET, *History of Lorraine*, II, Proofs, p. CCCXX.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son CONSTANTINE, abbot of the monastery of Blessed [Col. 0539A] Mary of Aurea Vallis, and to his successors regularly appointed for ever.

It accords with the clemency of apostolic governance to cherish religious persons and fortify their places with pious protection. For it is recognized as worthy and fitting to honour that we who have been raised to the governance of churches should protect them from the malice of wicked persons and foster them by the patronage of the apostolic see. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord Constantine, we graciously assent to your reasonable petitions, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the above-mentioned monastery over which, by God’s authority, you are known to preside, and strengthen it by the protection of this document. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods that monastery now [Col. 0539B] justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by grant of popes, gift of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God being favourable, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Furthermore, no cleric or layman whatsoever may presume to exact tithes from you upon the produce of your lands which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or upon the sustenance of your animals. We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the said monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things be preserved intact, for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and maintenance they were granted. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make amendment by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour, recognize himself or herself as answerable before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and at the final judgment be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve what is just for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

[Col. 0539D] A little lower down, in a circular field, was written: “SAINT PETER, SAINT PAUL, INNOCENT P. II”; and around it: “HELP US, O GOD OUR SAVIOUR”; and at the side: “I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church”;

And a little lower:

I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Albert, bishop of Albano. I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Prison of Tullian. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. [Col. 0540A] I, Martin, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Boetius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Thomas, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina.

And still lower:

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Ides of April, in the fourth indiction, in the year 1141 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the twelfth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

CDLXXI. Privilege for the convent of Chiemsee. (1141, 19 April.)

[HONDIUS, *Metropolis of Salzburg*, II, p. 241.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughter MACHILDIS, abbess of Chiemsee, and to her sisters, present and future, regularly appointed for ever.

Since without the true worship of religion neither the unity of charity can endure nor service pleasing to God be offered, it is fitting for apostolic authority to cherish religious persons and fortify their places with pious protection. Therefore, beloved daughters in the Lord, we graciously assent to your reasonable petitions, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own that monastery of Blessed Mary, Mother of God, which is situated in the diocese of Salzburg, and strengthen it by the protection of this document. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by grant of popes, [Col. 0540C] gift of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God being favourable, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb, diminish, or harass the aforesaid monastery with any vexations; but that all things be preserved intact for your benefit and that of those for whose governance and maintenance they were granted. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make amendment by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour, recognize himself or herself as answerable before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and at the final judgment be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve what is just for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Albert, bishop of Albano. I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina. I, Gerhard, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. [Col. 0541A] I, Anselm, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina. I, Guido, unworthy priest of the holy Roman Church. I, Boetius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement. I, Ivo, cardinal priest of Saints Lawrence and Damasus. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Callixtus. I, Ribaldus, cardinal priest of Saint Anastasia. I, Goizo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of the Shepherds. I, Thomas, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and [Col. 0541B] Bacchus. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Veil of Gold. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Vassallus, cardinal deacon of Saint Eustace. I, Hubaldus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Prison. I, Hubaldus, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of May, in the fourth indiction, in the year 1141 of the Lord’s Incarnation, [Col. 0541C] and in the twelfth year of the pontificate of Pope Innocent II.

CDLXXII. He receives the convent of Saint Mary of Hédera under protection and confirms its possessions, at the request of Stephen, bishop of Paris. (1141, 30 April.)

[MABILLON, *Benedictine Annals*, VI, 675.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughter HILDIARDIS, abbess of the monastery of Saint Mary of Hédera, and to her sisters, present and future, regularly appointed for ever.

The care of the universal Church has been entrusted to us by God, the provider of all good things, for this purpose: that we should cherish religious persons and strive in every way to spread religion pleasing to God. For no service is ever pleasingly rendered to God unless, proceeding from the root of charity, it is preserved by purity of religion. Therefore all lovers of the Christian faith ought to cherish religion and more diligently foster venerable places together with the persons devoted to divine service, so that they may not be troubled by the vexations of wicked persons or wearied by oppressive exactions. Therefore, beloved daughters in the Lord, moved by the prayers of our venerable brother Stephen, bishop of Paris, we receive the aforesaid monastery under the protection of blessed Peter and our own and strengthen it by the privilege of this document. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods that [Col. 0542A] monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by grant of popes, gift of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God being favourable, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Furthermore, no cleric or layperson whatsoever may presume to exact tithes from you upon the produce of your lands which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or upon the sustenance of your animals. We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb your aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things be preserved intact for your benefit and for that of those for whose governance and maintenance they were granted. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make amendment by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour, recognize himself or herself as answerable before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and at the final judgment be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve what is just for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. [Col. 0542C] Amen, amen, amen.

In the round circle this saying is read: “HELP US, O GOD OUR SAVIOUR.”

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed. I, Martin, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill, have subscribed. I, Ivo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence of Damasus, have subscribed. I, Grizo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Veil [Col. 0542D] of Gold, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian beside the temple of Romulus, have subscribed. I, Imbaldus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed. I, Hubaldus, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of the holy Roman Church, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Kalends of May, in the third indiction, in the year 1141 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the twelfth year of the pontificate of Lord Innocent II.

CDLXXIII. He receives the Florentine convent of Saint Ambrose under protection and confirms its possessions. (1141, 4 May.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia Sacra*, III, 93.]

[Col. 0543A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughter CECILIA, abbess of the monastery of Saint Ambrose of Petra Plana, and to her sisters, present and future, regularly appointed to remain for ever.

“To this end, the universal Church,” etc., as far as “wearied.” Therefore, beloved daughters in the Lord, we graciously assent to your reasonable petitions and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the aforesaid monastery of blessed Ambrose, situated in the diocese of Florence, strengthening it by the protection of this document. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by grant of popes, gift of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God being favourable, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these, we have thought fit expressly to name the church of Saint Michael, situated at Palchito within the city of Florence, together with all its appurtenances, canonically granted to you by Godfrey, bishop of Florence, and confirmed by his own document, without prejudice to the canonical reverence due to the Church of Florence. We also grant you unrestricted authority to receive offerings, both for the living and for the dead, without anyone’s opposition. We likewise decree that its burial ground shall be free, so that no one may hinder those who decide to be buried there, unless they happen to be excommunicated, while preserving, nevertheless, the rights of the mother Church. We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb your aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things be preserved intact, for your benefit and for that of others for whose governance and maintenance they were granted. If any ecclesiastical person, etc. But upon all, etc. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. [Col. 0543D] I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Anselm, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed. I, Martin, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill, have subscribed. I, Boethius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement, have subscribed. I, Goizo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia, have subscribed. I, Thomas, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina, have subscribed. [Col. 0544A] I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Otho, cardinal deacon of Saint Gregory at the Veil of Gold, have subscribed. I, Vassallus, cardinal deacon of Saint Eustace, have subscribed. I, Ubaldus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Nicholas in the Prison, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Nones of May, in the fourth indiction, in the year 1141 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the twelfth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II, etc.

CDLXXIV. He receives the monastery of Saint Saviour at Venice under the protection of the apostolic see and decrees that the canonical order established there by Bonofilius shall remain for ever. (1141, 13 May.)

[CORNELIUS, *The Churches of Venice Illustrated*, vol. XIV, p. 92.]

[Col. 0544B]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons BONOFILIUS and his brethren, professing the canonical life in the church of Saint Saviour situated at Rialto, present and future, for ever.

The authority of the apostolic see entrusted to us urges us to extend the protection of guardianship to places and persons which duly invoke its assistance with devotion. For just as no effect is to be granted to those who seek unjust things, so the petition of those requesting what is lawful and just is not to be delayed, especially of those who appear devoutly to embrace religion and rejoice to serve the Lord under it. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously receive your reasonable prayers, receive the aforesaid church of Saint Saviour under the protection of blessed Peter and our own, and strengthen it by the privilege of this document. Since you have vowed to observe the canonical order and to live according to the Rule of blessed Augustine, we willingly assent to your vows and by apostolic authority decree that this same order shall remain inviolate in that church for all time. We decree [Col. 0544D] that whatever possessions and whatever goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter acquire by grant of popes, gift of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, by the Lord’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. We likewise confirm to you the share of tithes from your parishioners which belongs to your church according to the sacred canons and the constitutions of the holy Fathers. Furthermore, we forbid anyone, by any craft of surreptitiousness or by force, to be placed over that church unless the brethren of that place jointly, or the sounder part of their counsel, have canonically provided for that person to be elected.

[Col. 0545A] We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb you personally or that church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; nor may anyone unlawfully receive or retain that church’s parishioners, while preserving the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If anyone, knowingly, should rashly attempt to act against this page of our constitution and, having been warned a second or third time, does not amend the offence by worthy satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour and be subject to strict vengeance at the final judgment. But upon all who preserve what is just for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal [Col. 0545B] peace. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Anselm, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed. I, Martin, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill, have subscribed. I, Boetius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement, have subscribed. I, Rabaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia, have subscribed. [Col. 0545C] I, Goizo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia, have subscribed. I, Thomas, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina, have subscribed. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Veil of Gold, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Vassallus, cardinal deacon of Saint Eustace, have subscribed. I, Ubaldus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed.

[Note: [Col. 0545D] Mozzagrugnius gave Ubaldus as cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian; yet he ought to be called cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, as appears in the original.]

I, Hybaldus, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian, have subscribed.

[Note: [Col. 0546D] Hybadus, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian, was omitted by Mozzagrugnius.]

I, Guido, cardinal deacon of the holy Roman Church, [Col. 0545D] have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Ides of May, in the fourth indiction, in the year 1141 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the twelfth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

CDLXXV. He confirms the goods and status, together with its liberties, of the monastery of Saint Mary of Regia Vallis. (1141, 14 May.)

[HUGO, *Premonstratensian Annals*, II, 406.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 0546A] sons HERBERT, abbot of Regia Vallis, and his brethren, present and future, regularly appointed for ever.

The pastoral responsibility entrusted to us by God requires us to labour to preserve, with exact diligence, religion pleasing to God once it has been established. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, gladly assenting to your reasonable petitions, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the church of Blessed Mary, Mother of God and ever-virgin, of Regia Vallis, situated in the diocese of Toul, and strengthen it by the privilege of this document. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by grant of popes, gift of kings or princes, [Col. 0546B] offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God being favourable, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to specify in their own terms: namely, Regia Vallis itself with all its appurtenances; the vineyards of Lucey, the vineyards of Parney, the vineyards of Seroces, the vineyards of Fou, the land of Fracia; the valley of Bernaicuria and your portion of the adjoining village; Gauvillare with its altar and appurtenances; and the right of use, with a mill, in the beechwood of Commercy. Furthermore, no cleric or layperson whatsoever may presume to exact tithes from you upon the produce of your lands which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or upon the sustenance of your animals. We therefore decree that no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid [Col. 0546C] church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things be preserved intact, for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and maintenance they were granted. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make amendment by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour, recognize himself or herself as answerable before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and at the final judgment be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve what is just for that [Col. 0546D] place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Martin, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen. I, Goizo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Veil of Gold. I, Gerard, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Domnica. [Col. 0547A] I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Prison.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Ides of May, in the fourth indiction, in the year 1141 of the Lord’s Incarnation; and in the twelfth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

CDLXXVI. To the clergy and people of Poitiers—concerning the elect Grimoard. (1141, 20 May.)

[*Gallia Christiana*, II, 1174, in the text, from the manuscript codex of the Sainte-Chapelle at Bourges.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the canons, abbots, princes, clergy, and [Col. 0547B] people of Poitiers: greeting and apostolic blessing.

True obedience, the companion of humility, implants the other virtues in the mind and preserves them once implanted. For it alone possesses the merit of faith; without it a person is proved faithless, even though he or she appears faithful. Therefore, whoever presumes, while within the unity of the holy Church, to be disobedient to a prelate cannot have a share with God. You ought indeed to rejoice, because, as we have learned, after our venerable brother William, your bishop, entered upon the way of all flesh, a suitable and religious person has been established as bishop for you. Since he is rightly set over others whose life and conduct are judged acceptable before God, we piously command and enjoin upon all of you by apostolic letters that henceforth you obey him with humility and due obedience, and take care to comply with his salutary commands.

Given at the Lateran, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of June.

CDLXXVII. To G[rimoard], bishop-elect of Poitiers. (1141, May.)

[Ibid., col. 1175, from the same codex.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother G., bishop of Poitiers: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have learned that your person has been raised to the governance of the Church of Poitiers; and since one who wishes to preside over others ought greatly to demonstrate his life by conduct, we command and enjoin upon you by apostolic letters that you strive to exercise yourself worthily in matters pertaining to the episcopal office: “do the work of an evangelist; fulfil your ministry.” Love your subjects with paternal affection; and diligently provide, with watchful attention of mind, that the Church entrusted to you by God may be increased under your oversight both spiritually and temporally. Labour also, with all diligence, to recover the possessions and goods of that bishopric which are known to have been dissipated or unlawfully alienated.

CDLXXVIII. He receives the Church of the Holy Sepulchre of Jerusalem under protection and confirms its possessions. (1141, 21 June.)

[Eug. DE ROZIÈRE, *Cartulary of the Holy Sepulchre*, 24.]

[Col. 0548A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons PETER, prior, and the brethren professing the canonical life in the church of the Holy Sepulchre, present and future, for ever.
