If the gentleness and generosity of the holy Roman Church ought to afford suitable relief to Christians, it is much more fitting that it should bestow this more abundantly upon those who lead a religious life and appear to cleave more closely to the omnipotent Lord. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, since you have resolved to live according to the Rule of blessed Augustine [Col. 0548B], and in the place where the feet of the Lord stood, worshipping at his glorious tomb, in which he rested bodily for three days, and at the other most holy places where the Redeemer of the world endured for our salvation bonds, scourges, the disgrace of the cross, wounds, and death, you serve regularly as soldiers, we judge you worthy of greater goodwill and favor, and wish to cherish you with paternal affection. Accordingly, graciously acceding to your requests as is due, we take under the protection of blessed Peter and our own, and strengthen by the page of this present writing, the most holy church of the Holy Sepulchre—in which, intent upon divine service, you continually recall with the faith of eyewitnesses the Passion of the Lord and the triumph of the most victorious cross—as well as your persons; [Col. 0548C] decreeing that whatever possessions and goods that same church now canonically possesses; whatever has also been justly bestowed upon that place by men of distinguished memory—namely Duke Godfrey and both Kings Baldwin—as well as by Arnulf and other patriarchs; and whatever shall hereafter reasonably be conferred by patriarchs or other faithful people of God, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you forever. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names:

namely, the possessions which you have in Antioch and its territory, as they were lawfully granted to your church and confirmed in writing by Raymond, illustrious prince of the same city, and his wife Constance; the church of the Holy Sepulchre on Mount Peregrinus [Pilgrim Mountain] near Tripoli; [Col. 0548D] the church of Saint George with all its appurtenances; in the city of Tyre, the church of Saint Mary; in the territory of that city, the hamlet of Derina and the garden between the wall and the outer defensive wall; in the city of Acre, the church of the Holy Sepulchre; in the territory of that city, the church of Saint Mary of Mimas with all its appurtenances; in the city of Jaffa, the church of Saint Peter with all its appurtenances; the tithes of the city of Jerusalem and those which you have in the territory of that city; the altar offerings of the church of the Holy Sepulchre; in the diocese of Pavia, the castle of Cerret with all its dependencies—saving, of course, the rights of the bishops in whose parishes your churches are situated.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to contravene it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he makes suitable amends by satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and office; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the wrong committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let him be subject to stern vengeance at the final judgment. But upon all who preserve the just rights of that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed. [Col. 0549B] I, Anselm, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed. I, Martin, cardinal priest [of the title] of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill, have subscribed. I, Sancius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina, have subscribed. I, Boethius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement, have subscribed. I, Ivo, cardinal priest of Saint Lawrence, title of Damasus, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Calixtus, have subscribed. I, Ribald, cardinal priest of the title of Saint [Col. 0549C] Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Rainer, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca, have subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of the Shepherd, have subscribed. I, Goizo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia, have subscribed. I, Thomas, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina, have subscribed. I, Hubald, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. [Col. 0549D] I, Hubald, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed. I, Gerard, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Domnica, have subscribed. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in Carcere, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Baron, chaplain and scribe, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of July, in the fourth indiction, in the year 1141 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the twelfth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CDLXXIX. He takes the monastery of Saint Bartholomew at Fiesole under protection and confirms its possessions and rights.  
*(1141, September 22.)*

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, III, 243.]

[Col. 0550A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GREGORY, abbot of Saint Bartholomew, and his brethren, present and future, regularly established, forever.

It befits us willingly to grant a desire shown to concern the purpose of religion and the salvation of souls, and to afford fitting support to the wishes of petitioners. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests and take under the protection of blessed Peter and our own, and fortify by the privilege of this present writing, the monastery of blessed Bartholomew the apostle, [Col. 0550B] situated beside the mountain of the city of Fiesole, with all its appurtenances. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, God being favorable, through grants of popes, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names:

the monastery of Saint Saviour of Alena with the church of Saint Pontitus; the church of Saint Martin in Fugnano; at Campo Novoli, the church of Saint Martin with tithes and all its appurtenances and adjoining property; and whatever the aforesaid monastery is known to possess in the diocese of Bologna; at Capraia, one half of the church of Saint Christina; at Ripula, the church of Saint Saviour; the church of Saint Michael of Marene; at Ripalta, the church of Saint Andrew; the church of Saint Donatus of Fronzano; at Bivigliano, one half of the church of Saint Mary; the estate of Saint Domninus with all its tithes; the estate of Papiana with its appurtenances; and whatever it is known to possess in the parish church of Saint Donatus of Calenzano, with tithes and its appurtenances; likewise in the parish church of Saint Stephen of Campi, in the parish church of Saint Martin situated at Brozzi, [Col. 0550C] in the parish church of Saint Julian at Settimo, or within the parish church of Saint John of Signa, with tithes and all their appurtenances. Also the other villages and possessions which were granted to you by name in the privilege and donation of James, bishop of Fiesole, of good memory. [Col. 0550D]

We also prohibit and, by apostolic authority, forbid anyone whatsoever to alter the same monastery into another order or to transfer an episcopal see there without authorization from the Roman pontiff. Upon the death of the present abbot of the same place, no one shall be placed over it through any device or violence of subjection, except one whom the brethren of that place, by common assent or by the assent of the sounder part of the counsel, in the fear of God and according to the Rule of blessed Benedict, shall canonically determine ought to be elected. If he is a canon of the bishop of Fiesole and enjoys the favor and communion of the Apostolic See, and is willing to confer it freely and without any impropriety, he shall receive blessing from him. [Col. 0551A] Otherwise he may approach whichever bishop he prefers, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what is requested.

We also grant that the burial place of that house shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated, while preserving, nevertheless, the rights of the mother church. To the monastery of Saint Saviour of Alena, which is known to be subject to the same monastery of Saint Bartholomew, we grant free burial, as it is also known to have possessed it hitherto. Moreover, we grant to you and to your monastery of Saint Saviour, for the use of the poor, the tithes of the labor of your hands. Furthermore, we forbid any person whatsoever to prohibit divine office in the same monastery or in the monastery of Saint Saviour, [Col. 0551B] except the Roman pontiff or his legate, or to impose undue exactions or harass them with any unjust molestations by rash presumption.

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may, etc.; if anyone therefore, etc.; but upon all, etc. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Martin, cardinal priest of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill, have subscribed. I, Manfred, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina, have subscribed. [Col. 0551C] I, Boethius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement, have subscribed. I, Guido, priest of Saint Lawrence, title of Damasus, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Nicholas in Carcere, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Apollinaris, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Baron, chaplain and scribe, on the tenth day before the Kalends of October, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1141 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the twelfth year of the pontificate of Lord Innocent II.

### CDLXXX. Bull of Innocent II confirming the goods and possessions of the church of Trunchin.  
*(1141, September 22.)*

[HUGO, *Ann. Praem.*, II, p. 608.]

[Col. 0551D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GOZWIN, abbot of Trunchin, and his brethren to be regularly established, in perpetual remembrance.

The care of the pastoral office has been entrusted to us by God for this purpose: that, God being pleased, we may labor by every means to establish religion and, once established, preserve it through increased diligence. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, moved by the prayers of our venerable brother Simon, bishop of Noyon, we graciously assent to your just requests and take under the protection of blessed Peter and our own, and fortify by the protection of this present writing, the church of Saint Mary of Trunchin, in which you are devoted to divine service. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire through grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: [Col. 0552A]

namely, the estates and villages of Landenghem, Voclar, Petengem, Astinem, Salenghem, Verrebronch, Hulst, and Hulsterlo; uncultivated land beside Belsalam; the estate called Stabulum; Burste; the orchard lying beside the same church; and all the dwellings situated between that orchard and the courtyard, which Ywanus bestowed upon the aforesaid church, together with every tithe of his revenues both in the same village and throughout all Waasland.

[Col. 0552B] You may also at all times celebrate divine offices behind closed doors and with excommunicated or interdicted persons excluded, unless there has been manifest fault on the part of the abbot or brethren of that house. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to contravene it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he makes suitable amends by satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and office; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the wrong committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let him be subject to stern vengeance at the final judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here [Col. 0552C] they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. I, Bernard, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina. I, Boethius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement. I, Ivo, cardinal priest of Saint Lawrence, title of Damasus. [Col. 0552D] I, GG., cardinal priest of the title of Calixtus. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of the holy Roman Church. I, Reinerius, cardinal priest of the title of Prisca.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Baron, chaplain and scribe, on the tenth day before the Kalends of October, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1141 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the twelfth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CDLXXXI. To William, lord of Montpellier.—He sympathizes with the tribulations and hardships which William suffered from his disloyal men, and promises him his aid and counsel.  
*(1141, October 5.)*

[D. BOUQUET, *Recueil*, XV, p. 402.]

Innocent, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ William, lord of Montpellier, greeting and apostolic blessing. [Col. 0553A]

We have received your letters and messengers with due kindness, and we sympathize with paternal affection in the tribulations and hardships which you suffer from your disloyal men, [Note: [Col. 0553D] In the chronicle of the old city one reads: “In the year 1141, the men of Montpellier drove William of Montpellier of the Ville out, and he went to Latat, and the battle lasted two years. The count of Barcelona recovered the town by siege, and then ten beans were worth one denier. The count of Barcelona built the tower of Latat.” Gariel renders these words into Latin in the same place: “In the year 1141 the men of Montpellier expelled William of Montpellier, their lord, from his city; [Col. 0554D] he withdrew to Latat. From this a war lasting two years arose, through which the count of Barcelona (Raymond Berengar IV) recovered the city by siege, subdued by such famine that ten beans cost one denier. The count of Barcelona built the tower of Latat.”] since we love your person with true charity in the Lord as a Catholic prince and a special son of blessed Peter, and willingly bestow aid and counsel in those matters in which we are able to do so according to God. You, however, since the testing furnace proves the righteous as gold, act manfully, let your heart be strengthened, and wait for the Lord; for he restrains the winds and stills the sea.

Given at the Lateran, on the third day before the Nones of October.

### CDLXXXII. He takes the hospital of Saint Blaise near Monza under protection and confirms its possessions.  
*(1141, October 15.)*

[GIULINI, *Memorie di Mil.*, vol. V, p. 576.]

[Col. 0553B]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son ADAM, master of the hospital at Saint Blaise near Monza, and to his brethren, present and future, canonically appointed, forever.

We have been advanced, by the Lord’s disposition, to the governance of the Apostolic See in order that we may be bound to assent to pious vows and incline our ears to just petitions. Therefore, beloved son Adam in the Lord, considering your commendable devotion, we receive with paternal kindness and fortify by the page of this present writing the aforesaid hospital [Col. 0553C] which, together with all its dependencies, by the assent and counsel of Arnold, John, and the other neighbors of that place, you offer to blessed Peter and to us, subject to an annual payment to us and our successors of six denarii in old Milanese currency. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same hospital now justly and lawfully possesses, or may hereafter acquire by reasonable means, God being favorable, shall remain secure and unimpaired to that hospital and to the poor.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to contravene it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he makes suitable amends by satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and office; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the wrong committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let him be subject to stern vengeance at the final judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place, [Col. 0554A] may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

In the circle: **HELP US, O GOD OUR SAVIOUR.**

In the monogram: **Fare well.**

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Hubald, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of the holy Roman Church, have subscribed.

[Col. 0554B] Given at the Lateran through the hand of Baron, chaplain and scribe, on the Ides of October, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1141 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the twelfth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CDLXXXIII. To the monks of Marchiennes.—He declares the censures of A., bishop of Arras, void and orders them to proceed to the election of an abbot.  
*(1141, November 1.)*

[MARTENE, *Ampl. Collect.*, I, 719, from a Marchiennes manuscript.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his most beloved sons the monks of Marchiennes, greeting and apostolic blessing. [Col. 0554C]

We sympathize with due concern over the injuries and oppressions which, from your letters and from the report of your brethren John and Andrew, who appeared before us, we have learned were inflicted upon you by our brother A., [Note: [Col. 0554D] Alvisus, who was elected bishop of Arras in 1131 from being abbot of Anchin; to him Saint Bernard’s Letter 327 is extant.] bishop of Arras. As beloved sons of ours, we willingly grant you, so far as we are able according to God, aid and assistance. Therefore, because the aforesaid our brother entirely obstructed your election, jointly celebrated in accordance with the Rule of blessed Benedict and with the tenor of the privileges of our predecessor Pope Calixtus of good memory and of ourselves; and because, as a further manifestation of his malice, he presumed, after an appeal had been made to the Apostolic See, to prohibit your monastery from [Col. 0554D] divine offices, we have judged that interdict void and by apostolic authority command you to celebrate divine offices. If he is known to have made any alteration or enactment in the same monastery or in places belonging to it after the appeal to the Apostolic See, [Col. 0555A] we annul the whole of it and command that everything be restored to the state in which it is known to have been at the time of the appeal. And we command you that, in accordance with the Rule of blessed Benedict and the privileges of the Apostolic See, you elect as your abbot, by the common assent or by the assent of the sounder part, a religious and suitable person, by whose prudence and religious character that monastery may, with the Lord’s help, prosper both temporally and spiritually.

Given at the Lateran, on the Kalends of November.

### CDLXXXIV. To A. [Alvisus], bishop of Arras.—He rebukes him for having harassed the monks of Marchiennes.  
*(1141, November.)*

[MARTENE, ibid., col. 720, from the same manuscript.]

[Col. 0555B]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother A., bishop of Arras, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We are astonished and grieved at the injuries, oppressions, losses, and many other burdens which, we have learned, have been inflicted by your brotherhood upon the monastery and brethren of Marchiennes. These things are indeed greatly contrary to your order and religious profession, and are shown to be opposed to the provisions made by blessed Gregory concerning monasteries and religious places. For, as they assert, their abbot was compelled by your oppressive acts to leave the monastery itself; and when they, in accordance with the Rule of blessed Benedict and the privilege of our predecessors [Col. 0555C] and of ourselves, elected an abbot, namely a religious and honorable person, you, disregarding the decrees of the Apostolic See, harassed them in every way on this account. To add to the measure of your malice, you presumed, contrary to an appeal made to the Apostolic See, to prohibit the aforesaid monastery from divine offices. How severely such presumption ought to be punished is shown by the judgment of blessed Gregory, who says:

> “Nothing concerning one who has fled to the bosom of the holy Roman Church and implored its assistance shall be decided before an order has been issued by the authority of that same Church, which has so imparted its functions to other churches that they have been called to share its solicitude, but not the fullness of its power. [Col. 0555D] Yet if—what we do not suppose—anyone should presume otherwise, let him be removed from clerical office and judged by all to be guilty against apostolic authority.”

And because we cannot allow contempt for blessed Peter and the holy Roman Church to go unpunished, by this present writing we command and order you entirely to leave the aforesaid monastery and brethren in peace and not to presume to hinder them in any respect, whether personally or through others. Concerning your contempt for the holy Roman Church and for ourselves, and many other matters reported to our ears in unfavorable rumor about your person, you are to come before us on the next Sunday on which is read, “I am the good shepherd,” to answer.

### CDLXXXV. Privilege for the canonical church of Saint Mary at Parma.  
*(1141, November 7.)*

[AFFO, *Storia di Parmi*, II, p. 350, from the archive of the chapter of Parma, twelfth century, no. XXXI.]

[Col. 0556A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son BONIZO, archpriest, and to the other canons of the Church of Parma, present and future, canonically appointed, forever.

The principle of equity and justice urges us to confer upon the Church enduring security for its property and defenses of unshaken strength. For it is not fitting that clerics called to the Lord’s portion should be troubled by the perverse vexations of evil men or wearied by the rash harassment of anyone whatever; [Col. 0556B] likewise, estates dedicated to the uses of heavenly mysteries ought to endure no forced services of the powerful and nothing extraordinary. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, through the intervention of our beloved son Master Hubald, cardinal deacon, we graciously assent to your just requests and take under the protection of blessed Peter and our own, and fortify by the privilege of this present writing, the canonical church of blessed Mary, Mother of God and ever-Virgin, at Parma, with all its movable and immovable goods. We decree that whatever possessions and goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter acquire, God being favorable, by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings [Col. 0556C] of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names:

the monastery of Saint Quentin with the church of Saint Mary of the Plain and the other things legally belonging to it; the church of Saint Christina; the church of Saint Nicholas and the church of Saint Antoninus; the parish church of Saint Pancras with the church of Saint Nicholas and its hospice beside the Taro, and with the church of Saint Anastasius within the city and the other things belonging to that parish church; the parish church of Saint Martin with tithes; the parish church of Saint Prosper with tithes; the parish church of Purpurano with its chapels; the parish church of Molandriano; the parish church of Saint Callianus with tithes; the chapel of Vilignano; [Col. 0556D] the chapel of Marano; the chapel of Meletulo; the chapel of Ballone; the chapel of Corviaco, situated within the castle; the chapel of Barca; the chapel of Marzaliis; the chapel of Azano; the chapel of Lower Vallera; the chapel of Travagnano; the chapel of Terentio; the chapel of Saint Secundus; the chapel of Pizzo; the chapel of Palazione; the chapel of Vico Longo; the chapel of Sala; the right which you have in the chapel of Saint Gorgius of Prati, in the chapel of Ponticello, and in the chapel of Vico Pauli; the chapel of Ulmo; the chapel of Calerno with its hospital; the chapel of Saint Lawrence of Meletula, together with all things legally belonging to the aforesaid parish churches and chapels; the tithes of all inhabitants in that city and its suburbs, as you have lawfully possessed them down to [Col. 0557A] the present time according to the division of the parish churches; and your share of the offerings made on the vigil and feast of Saint Domninus of Borgo and on the Assumption of Blessed Mary in the parish church of Corniglio.

We decree, therefore, that no ecclesiastical or secular person whatsoever may rashly disturb that canonical church, or take away, retain, diminish, or subject to any exactions you see fit [*quibuslibet videbitis exactionibus*, apparently corrupt] your goods or possessions; rather, let all be preserved intact and wholly devoted to the use of those for whose governance and support they were granted, while preserving the canonical reverence due to your bishop. As a token of the protection received from the Apostolic See, moreover, you shall pay to us and our successors each year one gold bezant.

If, therefore, in the future anyone, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to contravene it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he makes suitable amends by satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and office; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the wrong committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let him be subject to stern vengeance at the final judgment. But upon all who preserve the just rights of that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. [Col. 0557C] I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed. I, Stantius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina, have subscribed. I, Gibert, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Calixtus, have subscribed. I, Rainer, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca, have subscribed. I, Goyzo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia, have subscribed. I, Thomas, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina, have subscribed. I, Hubald, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of the holy Roman Church, [Col. 0557D] have subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Baron, chaplain and scribe, on the seventh day before the Ides of November, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1141 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the twelfth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

A lead bull is appended.

### CDLXXXVI. Privilege for the church of Freising.  
*(1141, November 20.)*

[*Monumenta Boica*, IX, p. 24.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother OTTO, bishop of Freising, and to his successors canonically appointed, forever. [Col. 0558A]

By the office of apostleship entrusted to us by God, we ought to love our brother bishops and preserve their rights for the churches committed to them by God. Therefore, beloved brother Otto, bishop in the Lord, we graciously admit your reasonable requests and fortify, under the protection of blessed Peter and our own and by the protection of this present writing, your person together with the church committed to you by God. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, the Lord being favorable, through grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you [Col. 0558B] and your successors.

We also enact that, in whatever diocese monasteries or churches have been built upon land of the church of Freising, priests shall be appointed in them with your assent and counsel. We confirm to you and to the church committed to you the rights of your church which our venerable brother Conrad, archbishop of Salzburg, has acknowledged and established by the authority of his writing. We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb that church, or take away, retain after taking, diminish, or alienate its tithes, goods, and possessions, or harass it with any molestations; rather, let all be preserved intact for the benefit of you and your successors. Moreover, because advocates are appointed for the defense [Col. 0558C] of the church, we wholly forbid the advocates of that church to presume to inflict any burden upon that house or upon property belonging to it, or to exact from them anything beyond their right.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to contravene it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he makes suitable amends by satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and office; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the wrong committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let him be subject to stern vengeance at the final judgment. But upon all who preserve the just rights of that place, [Col. 0558D] may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace.

Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Gregory, deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Baron, chaplain and scribe, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of December, in the fifth indiction, in the year **1144** of the Lord’s Incarnation [as printed], and in the twelfth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### CDLXXXVII. Privilege for the monastery of Wezzinbrunn.  
*(1141, November 20.)*

[*Monumenta Boica*, vol. VII, p. 380.]

[Col. 0559A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons WATTO, abbot of Wezzenbrunn, and his brethren, present and future, regularly appointed, forever.

The care of the universal Church has been entrusted to us by God, the provider of all good things, so that we may cherish religious persons and their churches, and, lest they suffer loss of their property through the attacks of wicked men, it is fitting that we provide for them through the protection of apostolic authority. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously grant your just petitions with paternal kindness [Col. 0559B], receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the monastery of Wezzinbrunn, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that the monastic order known to have been established in that monastery according to the Rule of blessed Benedict shall be observed there inviolate for all future time.

Moreover, whatever possessions and whatever goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, God being gracious, through the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought it proper to specify by their own names: namely, two [Col. 0559C] parts of the tithe of Risbach, as these were reasonably granted to you and confirmed by his writing by our venerable brother Henry, bishop of Regensburg; and the following estates: Achselswanc, Pansingen, Piberbach, Waltenberc, Wolmutsahe, Gutingen, Gezines, Izenes.

We also decree that no one shall dare to usurp or receive from anyone else the advocacy of that place, except the person whom the abbot and brethren shall jointly deem fit to elect according to the fear of God and the advantage of the monastery itself. Likewise, in the churches known to belong by right to your monastery, priests shall be appointed with your consent and counsel, as has been decreed in general councils.

Furthermore, concerning the tithes granted to your church by our brothers Wolfgang [Col. 0559D], bishop of Regensburg, and Ulrich, bishop of Augsburg, their successors shall by no rash presumption be permitted to harass you or inflict any vexation upon you. Concerning also the land of your monastery, and newly cultivated land, or the other produce which you gather by your own hands and at your own expense, we prohibit by apostolic authority the exaction of tithes from you, in accordance with what has been decreed by us in general councils.

Nor shall any of your brethren, after making profession in that monastery, be permitted to depart from it or transfer to other places without the leave of the abbot or brethren; and no bishop or abbot shall dare receive or retain one who departs. In addition, by the present decree we establish that no bishop shall have leave to impose upon you or your church forced services [angariae, compulsory labor-services], [Col. 0560A] or other exactions contrary to monastic peace and advantage.

Furthermore, we decree that the burial-place of that location shall be entirely free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and final will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated. Therefore no king, duke, margrave, or other person shall be permitted rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery contrary to this our constitution, or to take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass them by any vexations; rather, let all things be preserved whole, for your use and benefit in every respect.

But if anyone, knowingly, should rashly attempt to act against this page of our decree, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make fitting amends for his offense, [Col. 0560B] let him incur the indignation of almighty God and of His apostles, blessed Peter and Paul, and be subject to excommunication. But may those who preserve these provisions obtain the blessing and favor of those same apostles. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of Saint Cross in Jerusalem. I, Ivo, cardinal priest of Saints Lawrence and Damasus.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Baro, chaplain and scribe, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of December, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1141 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the twelfth year of the pontificate of lord Pope Innocent II.

CDLXXXVIII. He receives the monastery of Marchiennes under protection and confirms its goods and privileges. (Year 1141, December 1.)

[BUZELIM, *Gallo-Flandria sacra et profana*, Part I, p. 346.]

[Col. 0560C]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the monks of Marchiennes, present and future, regularly appointed in succession, in perpetual remembrance.

The authority of our office admonishes us to cherish religious places and sustain them with the fitting support of consolation. For this reason, beloved sons in the Lord, we grant your just petitions our paternal [Col. 0560D] consent, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the monastery of Marchiennes, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods the aforesaid monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, God being gracious, through the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors, etc.

For afterward it enumerates at greatest length the possessions, tithes, and altars subject to Marchiennes, to all of which it finally adds the following:

We decree that all these things shall remain under the immunity of customary freedom, so that the brethren may be able to render the services due to almighty [Col. 0561A] God. Adding further, we decree that no one whatsoever may place the aforesaid monastery and the church of Hamage under interdict from divine offices without manifest and proven fault. Nor shall anyone be imposed as abbot there through any craft of surreptitiousness or violence; rather, it shall be lawful for you, by common counsel or by the counsel of the sounder part, according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict, to elect an abbot without anyone’s opposition.

You may obtain chrism, holy oil, the consecration of altars or churches, the blessing of the abbot, and the ordination of your monks or clerics who are to be promoted to sacred orders, from the diocesan bishop, provided that he is Catholic, enjoys the favor and communion of the Apostolic See, [Col. 0561B] and is willing to provide these things freely and without any impropriety. Otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer; strengthened by our authority, he shall grant what you request.

We also grant that the burial-place of that location shall be free, so that no one may oppose any persons deciding to be buried there, unless they happen to be excommunicated. We therefore decree that no person whatsoever shall be permitted rashly to disturb that monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it by any annoyances; rather, all shall be preserved whole and unimpaired, for the use and benefit in every respect of those for whose governance and support they were granted.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular [Col. 0561C] person, knowingly, should rashly attempt to act against this page of our constitution, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to correct the offense by fitting satisfaction, let that person lose the dignity of office and honor, recognize himself or herself as guilty before the divine judgment of the iniquity committed, be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and be subject at the final judgment to strict vengeance. But may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ be upon all who preserve the rights of that place, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given through the hand of Baro, chaplain and scribe, on the Kalends of December, in the fifth indiction, in the year [Col. 0561D] 1141 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the twelfth year of the pontificate of lord Pope Innocent II.

CDLXXXIX. He confirms the judgment of Conrad III, king of the Romans, rendered for the monastery of Saint Blaise against the bishop of Basel. (Year 1141, December 6.)

[NEUGART, *Codex diplomaticus Alemannicus*, II, 74.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons G. [Note: [Col. 0561] Read: Gunther, who succeeded Berthold, who died on the fifth day before the Nones of August in this year. See *Historia Silvae Nigrae*, vol. I, p. 385.], abbot, and the monks of Saint Blaise, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Agreements entered into for the good of peace and the tranquility of churches, according to the moderation of equity and justice, ought to be strengthened by the protection of the Apostolic See and established in their stability, so that they cannot in the future be impaired by any opposition [Col. 0562A]. Therefore we strengthen by apostolic authority, and decree shall remain ratified and unshaken, the agreement reasonably made between you and the Church of Basel, through our dearest son Conrad, illustrious king of the Romans, concerning the dispute over the subjection and advocacy of your monastery, and confirmed on this account by documents and witnesses.

But if anyone, knowingly, should rashly attempt to act against this page of our confirmation, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to correct the offense by fitting satisfaction, let him incur the indignation of almighty God and of His apostles, blessed Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, on the eighth day before the Ides of December.

CDXC. To Gregory, bishop of Bergamo. (Year 1141, December 13.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, IV, 459.]

[Col. 0562B]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother GREGORY, bishop of Bergamo, and his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

Placed by the Lord’s ordering upon the lofty watchtower of the Apostolic See, we are bound by the office entrusted to us to cherish our brothers, the bishops, and to preserve the rights of the churches committed to them by God. Therefore, beloved brother G., bishop of Bergamo, providing with paternal [Col. 0562C] concern for the church whose care has been committed to you by God, we decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter reasonably acquire through the Lord’s generosity, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. The canons of Saint Vincent, present and future, shall render canonical and due obedience to you and your successors, and shall not withdraw it on the pretext of a privilege obtained from the Apostolic See. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person, etc. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, subscribe. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, subscribe. I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina, subscribe. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cross in Jerusalem [Col. 0562D], subscribe. I, Guido, unworthy priest of the Holy Roman Church, subscribe. I, Suasinus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen, subscribe. I, Boethius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement, subscribe. I, Ivo, cardinal priest of Saint Lawrence in Damaso, subscribe. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Calixtus, subscribe. I, Gratian, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina, subscribe. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, subscribe. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, subscribe. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, subscribe. I, Hubald, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, subscribe. I, Gerard, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Domnica, subscribe. [Col. 0563A] I, Peter, deacon of Saint Mary in Aquiro, subscribe.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Baro, chaplain and scribe, on the Ides of December, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1141 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the twelfth year of the pontificate of lord Pope Innocent II.

CDXCI. He receives the church of Saint Mary of Zaragoza under protection and confirms the goods of its canons. (Year 1141, December 15.)

[ARRUEGO, *Catedral episcopal de Zaragoza*, p. 792.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons PETER, prior, and the canons of the church of Saint Mary in the city of Zaragoza, present and future, regularly appointed in succession, in perpetuity.

[Col. 0563B] The care of the universal Church has been entrusted to us so that we may cherish religious persons and strive by every means to foster religion pleasing to God. For no service is ever rendered acceptably to God unless, proceeding from the root of charity, it has been preserved in the purity of religion. Accordingly, moved by this regard for charity and by the prayers of our venerable brother Bernard, your bishop, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid church of Mary, Mother of God and ever Virgin, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing.

First, we decree that the canonical order known to have been instituted in that church by our aforesaid brother according to the Rule of blessed Augustine shall be preserved there inviolate for all [Col. 0563C] time. Moreover, whatever possessions and whatever goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, God being gracious, through the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever shall be permitted rashly to disturb the aforesaid church, take away its goods or possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it by any annoyances; rather, all things shall be preserved whole for the use and benefit in every respect of those for whose governance and support they were granted, without prejudice to the canonical right and reverence due to the bishop of Zaragoza [Col. 0563D].

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowingly, should rashly attempt to act against this page of our constitution, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to amend the offense by fitting satisfaction, let that person abstain from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and be subject at the final judgment to strict vengeance. But may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ be upon all who preserve the rights of that place, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. [Col. 0564A] I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cross in Jerusalem. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint Gregory [read: George] at the Golden Veil. I, Guido, unworthy priest of the Holy Roman Church. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Ivo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Damaso. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Baro, chaplain and scribe, on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of January, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1141 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the twelfth year of the pontificate of lord [Col. 0564B] Pope Innocent II.

CDXCII. To Henry, bishop of Moravia, desiring to preach to the pagans of Prussia, he grants permission to bear the cross before him. (About the year 1141, January 31.)

[BOCZER, *Codex diplomaticus Moraviae*, I, p. 212.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, bishop of Moravia, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is not fitting for a bishop appointed to feed the Lord’s flock to leave his own sheep hungry and provide fodder for strangers. Yet if you desire to preach the word of the Lord to the pagans of Prussia and convert them to the faith of Christ, and judge that fruit will thereby accrue to the Church [Col. 0564C] of God, you must first appoint within the bishopric committed to you by God honorable and prudent persons who may correct what needs correcting, establish what must be established for the honor of God, and supply the food of life to the sheep committed to you by God. Thereafter, if you recognize so great a labor as beneficial to the Church of God, strive, with the Lord’s help, to accomplish this holy work.

We also grant your brotherhood leave to bear before yourself, in that people’s land, the cross in remembrance of the Lord’s Passion and for the conversion of Christ’s enemies. But once you have proclaimed the word of the Lord to that people, do not delay to return to the people committed to you.

Given at the Lateran, on the second day before the Kalends of February.

CDXCIII. To Henry, bishop of Moravia, he grants permission to preach to the pagans in Prussia, provided that he does not neglect to reform his rebellious people. (About the year 1141, April 1.)

[BOCZEK, *Codex diplomaticus*, I, p. 213.]

[Col. 0564D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, bishop of Moravia, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Those who hold the governance of the pastoral office in the Church of God and are set over the governance of others ought carefully to consider that they must render an account to the supreme Judge not only for their own transgressions but also for those of their subjects. Therefore, although, dearest brother in Christ, the people committed to you by God are stiff-necked and [Col. 0565A] rebellious and disobedient toward you, it seems to us highly necessary for you to labor more earnestly for their salvation and admonition, and, insofar as you can, recall them to the way of uprightness.

For it is written: “Cry aloud; do not cease; lift up your voice like a trumpet.” And again it is written: “If, when I say to the wicked, ‘You shall surely die,’ you do not announce it to him or speak, so that he may turn from his wicked way and live, that wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but I shall require his blood from your hand. But if you announce it to the wicked man and he is not converted from his iniquity, he shall die; but you have delivered your own soul.” Paul likewise says to the Ephesians: “Today my hands are clean from the blood of all of you; for I did not shrink from [Col. 0565B] declaring to you the whole counsel of God.”

Thus he would not have been clean from their blood if he had been unwilling to announce God’s counsel to them; for when a pastor is unwilling to rebuke offenders, he undoubtedly kills them by keeping silence. Therefore, even if—God forbid!—they should refuse to be converted by your admonitions, they themselves shall die in their impiety, but you shall be delivered from their death.

But if it seems useful to your judgment to go to the pagans of whom you informed us, and proclaim to them the word of God and the Christian faith, it is pleasing to us, provided that you do not neglect to return as soon as possible to the people committed to you.

Given at the Lateran, on the Kalends of April.

CDXCIV. He rebukes the clergy of the bishopric of Olomouc for celebrating divine offices contrary to their bishop’s prohibition, and admonishes them to obedience and reverence toward their bishop. (About the year 1141, April 1.)

[BOCZEK, *Codex diplomaticus*, vol. I, p. 214.]

[Col. 0565C]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the abbots, canons, and clerics established throughout the bishopric of Olomouc.

That we by no means greet you with the favor of blessed Peter and of ourselves is to be attributed not to our severity but rather to your disobedience and presumption. For we hear—to our great grief—that you have broken out into such madness that, contrary to the prohibition of our venerable brother Henry, your bishop, you presume to celebrate divine offices, receive those whom he has excommunicated, and do not at all fear to share with them in ecclesiastical sacraments, [Col. 0565D] which belong to God. How execrable this is, and how contrary to the salvation of your souls, the decrees of the holy Fathers plainly declare.

For Pope Calixtus says, among other things: “Let no one receive persons excommunicated by priests, nor communicate with them in prayer, food, drink, or counsel, nor say ‘hail’ to them; for whoever knowingly communicates with excommunicated persons in these or other prohibited matters shall himself also be subject, according to the institution of the apostles, to a like excommunication.” Therefore clerics and laypeople should abstain from such persons if they do not wish to suffer the same penalty.

Likewise, from the Council of Carthage: “Whoever communicates or prays with an excommunicated person, if he is a layman, shall be excommunicated; [Col. 0566A] if a cleric, he shall be deposed.”

Since these things are so, through apostolic writings we admonish and, in admonishing, command all of you to make worthy satisfaction to our aforesaid brother, your bishop, for such great offenses, and with all devotion humbly return to his obedience and reverence. Otherwise, whatever sentence of excommunication or deposition he shall pronounce against you in canonical equity, we shall confirm by the authority of blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, and by our own authority.

Given at the Lateran, on the Kalends of April.

CDXCV. To the priests Raymond, Rusticus, and Baro. (Year 1138–1142, March 14.)

[BALUZ, *Miscellanea*, IV, 591.]

[Col. 0566B]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the priests RAYMOND, RUSTICUS, and BARO, greeting and apostolic blessing.

You do not doubt that we committed the church of Saint P. to our beloved sons J., prior, and the brethren of the church of Saint Fridian, in order to restore religious observance in that place. Therefore, by apostolic authority, we command and strictly enjoin you to observe without objection what we have done in this matter, and neither to remain in that church nor in any place belonging to it without the leave of those brethren. If you should prove resistant, and do not repent of such [Col. 0566C] obstinacy within fifteen days after receiving this letter, from that time onward we prohibit the divine office to you.

Given at the Lateran, on the second day before the Ides of March.

CDXCVI. He exhorts Count Roboto to restore a certain estate to the church of Bamberg. (Year 1138–1142, November 24.)

[A mention of this letter occurs in LANG, *Regesta*, I, 158.]

CDXCVII. To the knights and worthy men of Nogara. (Year 1138–1142, November 25.)

[MURATORI, *Antiquitates Italicae*, II, 179.]

[Col. 0566D] INNOCENT, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the knights and worthy men of Nogara, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It has come to our ears that you have cleared the forest of Nogara, which Countess Matilda held from the monastery of Nonantola under an annual payment and, before her death, restored to that monastery, and that you cultivate it for your own benefit. Since it is exceedingly dangerous to diminish or withhold the rights of churches, through this present writing we command and strictly enjoin you to pay in full to the brethren of the aforesaid monastery their due from the produce which you cultivate there.

Given at the Lateran, on the seventh day before the Kalends of December.

CDXCVIII. He orders A[lbero], archbishop of Trier, to excommunicate the abbot of Saint Maximin for embezzlement and simony. (Year 1138–1142, December 5.)

[A mention of this privilege occurs in JAFFÉ, *Regesta Romanorum pontificum*, p. 592.]

[Col. 0567A]

CDXCIX. He forbids the alienation of the goods of the monastery of Münchmünster. (Year 1138–1142, December 5.)

[LANG, *Regesta*, I, 132.]

He exhorts Margrave D. D. to restore what was taken from the monastery of Blessed Peter [Münchmünster]. (Year 1138–1142, December 8.)

[LUDEWIG, *Scriptores rerum Germanicarum*, vol. I, p. 580.]

[Col. 0567B]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ D. [DIETPOLD], margrave, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Whoever desires to please God should assist and support religious men devoted to divine service, according to the means granted to him by God, and offer them help and counsel in their needs. Therefore we request and command your nobility to assist and support the religious brethren serving the Lord in the church of Blessed Peter of Münchmünster, and, if you know that you unjustly hold anything of their goods, to restore it to them. For it is exceedingly dangerous and contrary to the salvation of souls to apply to alien uses things granted to venerable churches [Col. 0567C] for the remission of sins or the repose of souls.

We also ask and impose upon you, for the remission of sins, that you do not permit those brethren or their household to be disturbed by anyone on the pretext of advocacy or by an unjust exaction, knowing that by such conduct you will render the Lord gracious toward yourself and gain the rewards of eternal recompense.

Given at the Lateran, on the sixth day before the Ides of December.

DI. To Henry, bishop of Winchester.—Concerning authority to hear the complaints of the monks of Westminster. (Year 1138–1142, December 9.)

[WILKINS, *Concilia Magnae Britanniae*, I, p. 418, from Cotton MS Vitellius A, XVII, fol. 17b.]

[Col. 0567D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, bishop of Winchester and legate of the Apostolic See, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Through our beloved son Osbert we have received a complaint on behalf of our sons, the monks of Saint Peter at Westminster, that the possessions and goods of the church of that monastery are taken from them and violently withheld by many persons in those regions. Since you exercise our authority in that land, so that you may administer justice to those suffering injury, especially ecclesiastical persons, through apostolic writings we command you to hear their complaints, cause due justice to be administered to them, [Col. 0568A] and permit no injury or annoyance to be inflicted upon them.

Given at the Lateran, on the fifth day before the Ides of December.

DII. To the convent of Westminster.—Concerning the canonization of King Edward. (Year 1138–1142, December 9.)

[WILKINS, ibid.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons G., abbot, and the brethren of Saint Peter at Westminster, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have gladly received the religious man Prior Osbert, sent by your brotherhood with your letters. Because of the merit of his excellence and outstanding manner of life, we commend him to you as our beloved son in a particular and special manner. His honorable importunity has so compelled us to satisfy your desire that, if we had had at hand sufficient testimony from bishops and abbots, he would already have brought back with him from the Roman Curia your king canonized in the catalogue of saints [Col. 0568B].

For this reason, after consulting our brother bishops and cardinals, we have deferred on this occasion the completion of your petition, because, since so great a feast ought to be celebrated for the honor and benefit of the whole kingdom, it ought likewise to be sought by the whole kingdom. It thus rests within your discretion, if you wish, to seek suitable testimony and to present it before us through instructed representatives of your monastery.

In these and other matters, according to God, we are willing gladly to hear your prayers and preserve unimpaired for you the rights [Col. 0568C] of your monastery. Hence we have commanded our venerable brother Henry, bishop of Winchester and legate of the Apostolic See, by apostolic writings, to render you full justice concerning those who unjustly withhold the churches, possessions, and goods of your monastery.

It is therefore your concern, beloved sons in the Lord, to live religiously in accordance with your profession and observe the Rule of blessed Benedict, so that the example of your good conduct may teach others to live well, and your mother, the holy Roman Church, may rejoice in your good works.

Given at the Lateran, on the fifth day before the Ides of December.

DIII. To archbishops, bishops, abbots, and priors. (Year 1138–1142, December 29.)

[Le PAIGE, *Bibliotheca Praemonstratensis*, p. 421.]

[Col. 0568D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brothers, archbishops and bishops, and beloved sons, abbots, provosts, and priors, to whom these letters shall come, greeting and apostolic blessing.

He does not seem inflamed by the love of brotherly charity who rashly presumes to inflict upon his neighbor what he does not wish inflicted upon himself. And the more anyone is adorned with higher rank and office, and the more he desires to be called and to be religious, the more carefully he ought to ensure that nothing irregular or [Col. 0569A] less than canonical is found in his actions; rather, his works should shine before people, and almighty God should be praised through his good endeavors.

For this reason we command and strictly enjoin your brotherhood by apostolic authority that you do not receive any of the lay brethren or other brethren of the Premonstratensian Order after they have made profession and promised obedience in their own house, without leave of their superior. If any such person, contrary to this our prohibition, should take refuge with you, restore that fugitive without objection or annoyance to his own abbot or superior. If you prove contemptuous, know that you will incur the indignation of the Apostolic See.

Given at the Lateran, on the fourth day before the Kalends of January.

DIV. He confirms to Abbess Heloise and the sisters of the Paraclete the goods granted by the priest Gundric. (Year 1138–1142, December 30.)

[*The Works of Abelard and Heloise*, 348.]

[Col. 0569B]

INNOCENT, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, HELOISE, abbess, and the nuns of the monastery of the Paraclete, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting readily to grant consent to religious desires, so that faithful devotion may obtain a swift result. Therefore, the more fragile the female sex is, the more we wish to extend paternal care and solicitude toward you, and beneficially provide, insofar as we are able according to God, for your peace and advantage [Col. 0569C].

Accordingly, we confirm to you by apostolic authority the place itself with all its appurtenances, which the priest Gundric, at the prayers and counsel of religious persons, reasonably granted to you, having constructed it on his paternal estate; and we strengthen that grant by this page of the present writing. But if anyone, knowingly, should rashly attempt to act against this page of our constitution, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to correct the offense by fitting satisfaction, let that person know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His apostles, blessed Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, on the third day before the Kalends of January.

DV. To D., parish priest of Massa, and all the chaplains of that parish. (Year 1139–1142.)

[BALUZ, *Miscellanea*, IV, 590.]

[Col. 0569D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son D., parish priest of Massa, and all chaplains of that parish, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We do not believe that you are unaware that we committed the church of Saint Pantaleon to our dearest sons J., prior, and the other brethren of the church of Saint Fridian. Therefore, by apostolic authority, we command and strictly enjoin you to admonish the people entrusted to you not to inflict any annoyance on the aforesaid brethren on that account, but rather to allow them to remain there peaceably [Col. 0570A].

Whoever should presume to oppose them in this matter, abstain from him as from an excommunicated person until he repents, and publicly denounce him in your churches. Furthermore, we summon the priests Signorectus and Roland—one of whom presumed to celebrate the office in the church of Saint Pantaleon, and the other in the church of Saint Anthony, contrary to our interdict—to appear before us on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of April, prepared to answer canonically concerning these matters.

Given at the Lateran, on the Ides of February.

DVI. To R[iboald], archbishop of Milan, and bishops Ar[dizzone of Como] and J[ohn of Lodi].—That people are not to be prohibited from receiving the monastic habit at the end of life or from burial in monasteries, unless excommunicated. (Year 1139–1142, April 23.)

[Aug. THEINER, *Disquisitiones criticae*, p. 366, from Vatican codex no. 1364, fol. 255.]

[Col. 0570B]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers R., archbishop of Milan, AR., bishop of Como, and J., bishop of Lodi, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It has come to our ears that, contrary to the privileges of the Roman Church, you are endeavoring to establish certain new and unheard-of regulations in your dioceses: namely, that henceforth no secular person may be buried in the cemeteries of monasteries, and that if anyone, overtaken by illness, should ask to become a monk, he is in no way to be received. We therefore command you and all [Col. 0570C] your clergy, through apostolic writings, to desist entirely from such presumption, and to permit free leave, according to the custom hitherto observed, to those who decide in life or death to enter religious life or be buried in monasteries—unless they are excommunicated.

Given at the Lateran, on the ninth day before the Kalends [uncertain: “Kalends?”] of May.

DVII. To A., archdeacon of Lucca. (Year 1141–1142, January 17.)

[BALUZ, *Miscellanea*, IV, 591.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son A., archdeacon of Lucca, greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0570D] We committed the church of Saint Savior of Mustolio, which is known to belong by right to blessed Peter, to our beloved sons Jer., prior, and the brethren of Saint Fridian; and we commanded the priests serving that church to render them obedience and reverence. Yet they are disobedient to us as rebels and contumacious persons, and scorn to obey those brethren in accordance with our command.

Therefore, by this present writing, we command and strictly enjoin you, on our behalf, rigorously to admonish those priests to render obedience and reverence to our aforesaid son Jer. until the coming Purification of blessed Mary. If they prove contemptuous, then remove them from ecclesiastical office and benefice [Col. 0571A], until they present themselves before us to make satisfaction for their contempt and disobedience.

Given at the Lateran, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of February.

DVIII. To R., prior, and the canons of Saint Angel. (Year 1141–1142, March 13.)

[BALUZ, ibid., p. 592.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to R., prior, and the canons of Saint Angelus in the Forum: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It displeases us that we are compelled to write to you so often concerning one and the same matter. For we remember that in another letter we commanded you, under injunction, not to harass our beloved sons, the canons of Saint Fridianus, concerning the church of Saint Savior at Mustolio, and to restrain your parishioners [Col. 0571B] from harassing them. As has been reported to us, you have neglected to carry this into effect; and although you dissemble and say that this is being done against your will, nevertheless your parishioners do not cease to harass them and to inflict serious wrongs upon them. Therefore we command and, in commanding, enjoin you again that, if you wish to retain the favor of Blessed Peter and of ourselves, you inflict no injury or violence upon the aforesaid brothers, nor permit it to be inflicted by your parishioners; taking diligent care lest you share the punishment of those whose wrongdoing you have consented to. For without doubt, he who neglects to correct what he is able to correct shares the guilt of the doer.

Given at the Lateran, 13 March.

DIX. To Arnald, Archbishop of Narbonne.—He signifies that he has pronounced a sentence of excommunication against the consuls of Montpellier, who, having expelled William, their lord, had withdrawn themselves from fidelity to him. (1142, 1 January.)

[D. BOUQUET, *Recueil*, XV, 406.]

[Col. 0571C]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother Arnald, Archbishop of Narbonne, and to his suffragans: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We do not believe that your prudence is unaware how the men of Montpellier, like faithless and treacherous persons, expelled our son William and withdrew themselves from his service and allegiance. [Col. 0571D] Therefore we, whose especial concern it is to restrain their wickedness by due punishment and not to fail the same son of ours in his just cause, have pronounced a sentence of excommunication against those who are called the consuls of that place and all others known to be leaders in so great a wickedness; and we have placed that place under interdict as regards divine offices, except for the baptism of children and the penances of the dying. Since anyone who knowingly associates with excommunicated persons incurs excommunication, by these present letters we command you to withdraw your parishioners from assisting them, and to strive strictly to compel them not to presume to hold any communion with them.

Given at the Lateran, 1 January.

DX. To G[William], bishop of Mende, and H[umbert], bishop of Le Puy, he writes concerning the men of Montpellier as in the preceding letter. (1142, January.)

[Only a notice of this letter survives in GARIET, *Series praesulum Magalonensium et Monspeliensium*, I, 182.]

[Col. 0572A]

DXI. He confirms the privileges of the monastery of Mortemer. (1142, 4 January.—Fragment.)

[*Neustria pia*, p. 779.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Adam, abbot of Mortemer, and his brethren, present and future, to be regularly appointed: perpetual greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0572B] “The desire which is shown to concern the profession of religion and the salvation of souls,” etc.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Gerard, priest-cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, 4 January, indiction 5, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1141, and in the twelfth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

DXII. Privilege for the abbey of Longpont. (1142, 5 January.)

[MULDRAC (Ant.), *Chronicle of the Abbey of Longpont*, p. 9.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to Hugh, abbot of Longpont, and his brethren, present and future, to be regularly appointed in perpetuity.

[Col. 0572C] Beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and of ourselves, and strengthen by the privilege of this present document, the monastery of Longpont of the Blessed Mother of God, in which you are devoted to divine service. We decree that whatever possessions and goods your monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by God’s favor, acquire through the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and inviolate for you and your successors. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this page of our enactment, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make fitting amends, [Col. 0572D] let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let him be subject to strict vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve what is just for that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina. I, Guy, unworthy priest of the Holy Roman Church. [Col. 0573A] I, Martin, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Stephen. I, Stantius, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Sabina. I, Rainerius, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Prisca. I, Ivo, priest-cardinal of Saint Lawrence in the title of Damasus. I, Gregory, cardinal-deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Otto, cardinal-deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Guy, deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Lumbald, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Gerard, priest-cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the Nones of January, indiction 5, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1141, and in the twelfth year of the pontificate of Lord [Col. 0573B] Pope Innocent II.

DXIII. Privilege for the church of Berchtesgaden. (1142, 8 January.)

[HUNDIUS, *Metropolis Salisburgensis*, II, p. 158.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Eberwin of the Church of Berchtesgaden and his brethren, present and future, to be regularly appointed in perpetuity.

A pious request ought to be fulfilled with an effect corresponding to the will expressed, so that both the sincerity of devotion may shine forth commendably and the benefit requested may undoubtedly obtain force. Yet we ought to give fuller charitable attention to the petitions of those whose foundations, established in religion, are known especially to belong to the right of the holy Roman [Col. 0573C] Church. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and, following the example of our predecessors of blessed memory, Paschal and Calixtus, Roman pontiffs, we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and of ourselves, and strengthen by the privilege of this present document, the aforesaid monastery of Blessed Peter, in which you are devoted to divine office. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by God’s favor, acquire through the grants of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and inviolate for you and your successors.

[Col. 0573D] Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: the woodland adjoining the cell; Niderheim, Sconenberc, Flozze, and the remainder which Count Berengar and his son Gebehard gave to that place; whatever you lawfully possess in the eastern region; Tetenstete and the other things which Engelwanus, Heinrich, and Bernhard of Mosa, Willehalmus of Huba, and their other neighbours reasonably conferred upon you; Rotehonen with its appurtenances; Hebnigen, together with the other things which Charles and his brothers likewise gave you; and also those things which Rudolph of Lungowe similarly conferred upon you.

We also decree that no person whatsoever may alter in your church the order of canonical life which you have professed according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine. [Col. 0574A] Nor shall any member of your profession, prompted by fickleness or under pretext of a stricter religious life, be free to leave the cloister without the permission of the provost or of the community. If anyone leaves, no bishop, abbot, or monk shall receive him without letters of authorization from the community, so long as, by the Lord’s grace, observance of the canonical order continues in your church.

You shall receive ecclesiastical sacraments from the diocesan bishop, provided that he enjoys the favor and communion of the Apostolic See and is willing to confer them freely and without corruption. Otherwise, for receiving the same sacraments, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what is requested.

[Col. 0574B] Moreover, we wholly forbid the advocacy of your place to be usurped, without the consent of the provost and brethren, whether by the heirs of its founders or by any other persons. If the person to whom that church has been entrusted proves burdensome or useless, and, after a second or third warning, does not amend, we grant you full freedom to expel him and appoint another suitable person in his place.

No cleric or layman whatsoever shall presume to exact tithes from you on the produce which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or on the increase of your animals. We also grant you henceforth, with due respect for the Archbishop of Salzburg, to retain, as you have hitherto retained with his permission, the cure of souls of the servants of that church—namely, those who serve within the cell or cultivate new lands about it—together with their tithes. [Col. 0574C] We decree that the settlement of the dispute which was between you and the canons of Bamberg, as it was reasonably concluded before our venerable brother C., Archbishop of Salzburg, and confirmed by his written instrument, shall remain ratified.

Upon the death of you, the present provost of that place, or upon your transfer to the governance of another church, or upon the death or transfer of any of your successors, no one shall be installed or set over that place through any stratagem of deceit or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the council, shall canonically provide to be elected in the fear of God and according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine.

We also grant that the burial-place of that establishment shall be free, so that no one may oppose the final wish and devotion of those who have resolved to be buried there, [Col. 0574D] unless they are excommunicated; the rights of the mother church nevertheless being preserved. We decree, therefore, that no one whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its goods or possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or oppress it with any undue exactions or troubles.
