Rather, let all things be preserved whole and be of every benefit to the uses of those for whose government and support they were granted, saving the canonical right of the Archbishop of Salzburg. As a sign of this protection received from the Apostolic See, you shall pay to us and our successors one gold bezant annually.

[Col. 0575A] If any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this page of our enactment, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should not correct his offense by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let him be subject to strict vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve what is just for that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good works and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. [Col. 0575B] I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Alberius, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed. I, Martin, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Stephen, have subscribed. I, Boetius, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Clement, have subscribed. I, Peter, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Pastor, have subscribed. I, Hubald, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Praxedes, have subscribed. I, Otto, cardinal-deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Vassallus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Eustace, have subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Gerard, priest-cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, 8 January, indiction 5, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation [Col. 0575C] 1141, and in the twelfth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

DXIV. The monastery of Reichersberg is received under the protection of the Apostolic See; all its goods are confirmed, and several privileges are granted to its monks and provost. (1142, 8 January.)

[COCQUELINES, II, 255.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Geroho, provost of the Church of Reichersberg, and his brethren, to be regularly appointed in perpetuity.

A pious request ought to be fulfilled by a corresponding effect, and it is fitting that we grant appropriate support to the just desires of petitioners. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, moved by the prayers of our venerable brother Conrad, Archbishop of Salzburg, we willingly admit your reasonable petitions; and we receive under the protection of the Apostolic See and of ourselves, and strengthen by the privilege of this present document, your monastery, situated in the diocese of Passau upon land of the church of Salzburg, in which you are devoted to divine office. First, we decree that in both your monastery and the monastery of nuns subject to you, the canonical order according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine shall be preserved inviolate for all time.

Furthermore, whatever possessions and goods the same church now justly and canonically possesses, [Col. 0576A] or may hereafter, by God’s favor, acquire through the grants of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and inviolate for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: the estate and parish of Reichersberg, with its tithe and parochial rights; the chapel of Saint Martin with its appurtenances; vineyards at Aschab; the village of Crovuat; and the other estates offered to Wenenhere, founder of that place; a salt-pan at Halla; and the other estates conferred on your church by the aforesaid Archbishop of Salzburg, our brother; Hostat, and the other estates offered by Ruopertus; the estates donated by Fredericus; the estates formerly belonging to Eglolf and Eberhard, with their tithes, [Col. 0576B] granted to you by the Bishop of Freising; the vineyards purchased [perhaps “acquired”] at Eremesa; and the things conferred by Duke Luitpold.

Certainly, no cleric or layman whatsoever shall presume to exact tithes from you on the produce which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or on the increase of your animals. You shall receive ecclesiastical sacraments from the diocesan bishop or from the Archbishop of Salzburg, provided that they enjoy the favor and communion of the Apostolic See and are willing to confer them freely and without corruption. Otherwise, for receiving the same sacraments, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what is requested.

And because your place is so established that the chief advocate of the Church of Salzburg is also advocate of that place, neither he nor any subadvocate of his may harass the same place with unjust burdens. [Col. 0576C] If he does so and, upon your complaint, does not make amends, then, by the counsel and assistance of the aforesaid archbishop, that advocacy shall be taken from the unsuitable holder and another appointed in his place.

Upon the death of you, the present provost of that place, or upon your transfer to the governance of another church, or upon the death or transfer of any of your successors, no one shall be installed or set over it through any stratagem of deceit or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the council, shall canonically provide to be elected in the fear of God and according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine.

We also grant that the burial-place of that establishment shall be free, [Col. 0576D] so that no one may oppose the final wish and devotion of those who have resolved to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated; the rights of the mother church nevertheless being preserved. We decree, therefore, that no one whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its goods or possessions, rashly retain what has been taken, diminish them, or oppress it with any undue exactions or troubles. Rather, let all things be preserved whole and be of every benefit to the uses of those for whose government and support they were granted, while the due rights of the Archbishop of Salzburg and Bishop of Passau are preserved.

If any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this page of our enactment, should rashly attempt to act against it, [Col. 0577A] and, having been warned a second or third time, should not correct his offense by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ; and let him be subject to strict vengeance at the last judgment.

We further forbid any member of your profession, prompted by fickleness or under pretext of a stricter religious life, to leave the cloister without the permission of the provost or community. If anyone leaves, no bishop, abbot, or monk shall receive him without letters of authorization from the community, so long as, by the Lord’s grace, observance of the canonical order flourishes in your church. If, after being summoned a second or third time, he refuses to return, the provost of that place may pronounce canonical sentence upon him. [Col. 0577B] But upon all who preserve what is just for that church, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good works and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal recompense. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina. I, Otto, cardinal-deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Martyrius, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Stephen. I, Boetius, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Clement. [Col. 0577C] I, Peter, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Pastor. I, Ubald, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Ubald, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul. I, Vassallo, cardinal-deacon of Saint Eustace. I, Peter, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Portico.

Given at the Lateran, 8 January, by the hand of Gerard, priest-cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, indiction 5.

DXV. He confirms the establishment of the Premonstratensian order at Vallis Secreta. (1142, 15 January.)

[HUGO, *Annales Praemonstratenses*, II, p. 643.]

[Col. 0577D] INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Godfrey, abbot of Vallis Secreta, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: perpetual greeting.

Whenever we are asked for something known to accord with religion and uprightness, it is fitting that we grant it with willing mind and give suitable support to the desires of petitioners. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, giving favorable assent to your just requests, we decree that the canonical order which you have professed, according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine and the institution of the brethren of Prémontré, shall be preserved inviolate in your church for all time.

Nor, after profession has been made there, may anyone, prompted by fickleness or under pretext of a more stringent religious life, transfer to other places without the permission of the abbot and the whole community. [Col. 0578A] If anyone does so, no person whatsoever may receive him without letters of authorization from the community. We also grant that the burial-place of that establishment shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and final wish of those who have resolved to be buried there, unless perhaps they are excommunicated; the rights of the mother church being preserved.

No one whatsoever, therefore, may rashly disturb that church, take away, retain, or diminish its goods or possessions, or oppress it with any troubles. If any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this page of our enactment, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to correct his offense [Col. 0578B] by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let him be subject to strict vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve what is just for that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good works and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina. [Col. 0578C] I, Ivo, priest-cardinal of Saint Lawrence in the title of Damasus. I, Peter, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Pastor. I, Goizo, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Hubald, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Hubald, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul. I, Gregory, cardinal-deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Otto, cardinal-deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Guy, cardinal-deacon of the Holy Roman Church. [Col. 0578D] I, Peter, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Portico.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Gerard, priest-cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, 15 January, indiction 4, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1141, and in the twelfth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

DXVI. Privilege for the monastery of Münchmünster. (1142, 23 January.)

[HUNDIUS, *Metropolis Salisburgensis*, II, p. 518.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son Richard, abbot of the monastery of Saint Peter situated in the place called Monasterium, and his brethren, present and future, to be regularly appointed in perpetuity.

[Col. 0579A] It is fitting for us to give assent to just vows and lend an ear to just petitions, since, though unworthy, we are, by the Lord’s ordering, placed as guardians and heralds of justice on the lofty watchtower of the princes of the apostles, Peter and Paul. Therefore, beloved son Richard, abbot in Christ, we grant assent to your petitions with the affection of due charity; and, receiving under the guardianship and protection of the Apostolic See the monastery of Blessed Peter over which, by God’s authorship, you preside, we strengthen it by the page of this present document. First, we decree that the monastic order according to the Rule of Blessed Benedict shall, by the Lord’s gift, be preserved there inviolate for all time.

[Col. 0579B] No member of your profession shall be free, prompted by fickleness or under pretext of a stricter religious life, to leave the cloister without the permission of the abbot or community. If anyone leaves, no bishop, abbot, or monk shall receive him without letters of authorization from the community, so long as, by the Lord’s grace, observance of the monastic order continues in your church.

Furthermore, whatever possessions and goods the same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by the Lord’s will, acquire through grants of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and inviolate for you and your successors. Among these [Col. 0579C] we have thought fit to record by their proper names two parts of the tithes and offerings from the two parishes, namely Attenhonem and Alantinchingen, which are known to belong to the aforesaid church.

We also grant that the burial-place of that establishment shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and final wish of those who have resolved to be buried there, unless perhaps they are excommunicated; the due rights of the mother church being preserved. No cleric or layman whatsoever shall presume to exact tithes from you on the produce which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or on the increase of your animals. We also forbid anyone, with rash presumption, to dare to disturb that abbey, its places, or persons belonging to it under pretext of advocacy, or to oppress them with undue exactions. [Col. 0579D] We also decree that in parochial churches belonging to your monastery you shall choose priests and present them to the bishop; if they are suitable and cannot canonically be rejected, the bishop shall commit to them the cure of souls, so that they shall answer to the bishop concerning the care of souls, but shall show you due subjection in temporal matters.

Upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed over it by any stratagem of deceit or violence. Rather, you may elect an abbot, by common counsel or the consent of the sounder part, according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict, without anyone’s opposition.

[Col. 0580A] We decree, therefore, that no one whatsoever may rashly disturb your aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or oppress it with any unjust vexations or undue exactions. Rather, let all things be preserved whole and be of every benefit to the uses of those for whose government and support they were granted, the canonical reverence due to the diocesan bishop being preserved. If any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this page of our enactment, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to correct his offense by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred [Col. 0580B] body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let him be subject to strict vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve their rights for that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good works and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

SAINT PETER, SAINT PAUL.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Gregory, cardinal-deacon of Saints Sergius and Achatius. I, Otto, cardinal-deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Guy, cardinal of Saints Cosmas and Damian. [Col. 0580C] I, Gerhard, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Dominica. I, Guy, cardinal-deacon of the Holy Roman Church. I, Martin, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Guy, unworthy priest of the Holy Roman Church. I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina. I, Guy, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Chrysogonus. I, Peter, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Pastor. I, Hubald, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Gerard, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman [Col. 0580D] Church, 23 February, indiction 6, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1141, and in the twelfth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

DXVII. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Peter at Rossleben. (1142, 25 January.)

[*Thuringia sacra*, p. 738.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son Peter, provost, and the brethren of the Church of Blessed Peter at Rostenleve, present and future, to be regularly appointed in perpetuity.

Whenever we are asked for something known to accord with religion and uprightness, it is fitting that we grant it with willing mind and give suitable support to the desires of petitioners. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and strengthen under the protection of Blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid church in which you are devoted to the Lord’s service. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same church now justly and canonically possesses, [Col. 0581A] or may hereafter, by God’s favor, acquire through grants of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and inviolate for you and your successors. We likewise confirm whatever Louis and his wife Matilda, with the consent of their heirs, have lawfully conferred upon that church.

Upon the death of you, the present provost of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed over it by any stratagem of deceit or violence; rather, you may elect, without anyone’s opposition, by common counsel or the counsel of the sounder part, according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Augustine. [Col. 0581B] We further decree that the canonical order according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine shall be preserved there inviolate for all time.

We also decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb your aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or oppress it with any vexations. Rather, let all things be preserved whole and be of every benefit to the uses of those for whose government and support they were granted. If any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this page of our enactment, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make fitting amends, let him be deprived of the dignity of power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; and let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer. [Col. 0581C] But upon all who preserve what is just for that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good works and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, N. I, Conrad, substitute bishop, N. [Col. 0581D] I, Gregory, cardinal-deacon of Saint George, Sergius, and Bacchus, N. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, N. I, Otto, cardinal-deacon, “scribe of the world” [read: of Saint George] at the Golden Veil, N. I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina, N. I, Guy, cardinal-deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, N. I, Martin, priest-cardinal of Saint Stephen, N. I, Guy, unworthy priest of the Holy Roman Church, N. [Col. 0582A] I, Stantius [Constantius], priest-cardinal of Saint Sabina, N. I, Guy, priest-cardinal of Saint Chrysogonus, N. I, Rainerius, priest-cardinal of Saint Prisca, N. I, Thomas, priest-cardinal of Saint . . . Paul, N. I, Cadalaus, cardinal-deacon of . . . in Dominica, N. I, Octavian, cardinal-deacon of Saint Nicholas in Carcere.

Given under—mo—[read: at the Lateran, by the hand of] Gerard, priest-cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church [Note: [Col. 0581D] The chronological notes are corrupt.], 25 February, indiction 5, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1142, and in the twelfth year of the pontificate of our lord Pope Innocent II.

DXVIII. To William, lord of Montpellier.—He signifies that he has commanded the bishops of the province of Narbonne to restrain Count Ildefonsus of Toulouse from bringing aid to William’s traitors in Montpellier, failing which Ildefonsus is to be excommunicated. (1142, 3 March.)

[DOM BOUQUET, *Recueil*, XV, p. 406.]

[Col. 0582B]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son, the illustrious man William of Montpellier: greeting and apostolic blessing.

As we remember having informed you in other letters, we grieve with paternal affection over your adversity, in which we willingly provide you, according to God, with help and counsel. Therefore we have commanded by our letters the venerable brothers, bishops of that land, [Col. 0582C] to admonish Ildefonsus, Count of Toulouse, to cease from aiding your traitors of Montpellier; and, if he proves contemptuous, to declare him publicly excommunicated and prohibit the celebration of divine offices in his land. [Note: [Col. 0581D] The excommunication of Ildefonsus, Count of Toulouse, is established by the letter of Hugh, Archbishop of Rouen, [Col. 0582D] cited by Acherius in the appendix to the *Works of Guibert of Nogent*, p. 688.] You will be able to learn from your messenger what has been done concerning the Bishop of Maguelone. But you, be strengthened in the Lord and in the might of his power, because he does not abandon those who hope in him, but brings them to the harbor of desired rest.

Given at the Lateran, 3 March.

DXIX. Confirmation of all the goods of the monastery of Saint Columban of Bobbio, of the Cassinese order, which is received under the protection of Blessed Peter. (1142, 8 March.)

[COCQUELINES, *Amplissima Collectio Bullarum, Privilegiorum ac Diplomatum Romanorum*, II, 258.]

[Col. 0582D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Oglerius, abbot of Saint Columban of Bobbio, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life in perpetuity.

The desire which pertains to the purpose of religion and the attainment of salvation ought to be granted by us with willing mind, and fitting support ought to be afforded to the desires of petitioners. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord [Col. 0583A], moved by the just prayers of your venerable brother the bishop, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, and strengthen by the safeguard of this present privilege, the church of Blessed Columban, in which you are devoted to divine service. We decree that whatever possessions and goods you now possess justly and canonically, or may hereafter be able to acquire, by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s favor, shall remain firm and inviolate for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to set out the following by their proper names:

the estate of Saint Martin, with its church and the castle called Petra-Carraria, with all its appurtenances; the estate of Saint Saviour, with its church and appurtenances; [Col. 0583B] the estate of the Cross, with its church and appurtenances; the estate of Garda, with its churches, jurisdiction, and all its appurtenances; the estate of Gravilia, with its church and appurtenances; the estate called Gomorga, with its church and appurtenances; the estate of Vignalis, with its church and appurtenances; the estate of Carelium, with its church and appurtenances; the parish of Saint Alban at Candubrium, with its appurtenances; the church of Saint Evasii at Quintinianum, with its appurtenances; the church of Saint George situated at Monte-Curto, with its appurtenances; the church of Ceresola, with its appurtenances; the church of Saint Anthony of Braida, with its tithes and appurtenances; the church of Saint Columban of Monte Claro, with its appurtenances; the church of Saint George of Montale, [Col. 0583C] with its appurtenances; the church of Saint Andrew of Travano, with its tithes and appurtenances; Saint Mary’s church in the cave, with its appurtenances; the church of the sick, with its appurtenances; the New Church, with its appurtenances; the church of Saint Lawrence, with its appurtenances; the church of Saint Bartholomew in Saxo, with its appurtenances; and half the market, the market of Saint Columban, and another market of Oliva, worth one hundred and ten Pavia solidi.

In the estate of Auraemala: the village of Stabulo; the village of Conio; the village of Cavana Nova; the tithe of Pradello Antonino; the village of Dusbagno; the village of Salso; the holding (*mansus*) of Guasco; the possession of Theodosius of Cigognis; the village of Riuturnum; Broidum and the meadow Donnicatum on [Col. 0583D] Mount Pennicis; the mount of Menningo; the village of Cerreto; the village of Cavana with Braida Donnica, Sapateli, and Roveretum; Mount Lenna; the village of Roncore; the village of Taidelli; Pratum-longum; the holding of Rugeli; Gambalata; Runchum de Grillo; Fraretum; Runchum de Pradilia; the holding of Barbuti; the holding of Petra Columba; the holding of Vaccaritia; the holding of Silva; the holding of Buzochi; the holding of Costaalta; the holding of Conflenti; the holding of Garda; the holding of Bonisenior of Cavello; the holdings of Uzoli Cazaritia; the holding of Lisignoli between Bobbio and the Trebbia; the holding of Motio; the holding of Gosino; the holding of Asino; the holding of Niblo; the holding of [Col. 0584A] Oniziis; the holding of Cerecesola; the holding of Albino; the holding of Curto; the holding of Buchia; the holding of Merconis of Canneto; the holding of Saint Desiderius; the holding of Guercho; the tithe of Sigisbert of Guita; the holding of Ponziprondo; the holding of Rusticus of Stavela; the holding of John Benedict of Caulo; the tithe of Lanfranc of Otono; the holding of Savonarius; the holding of Hugh Albert Dagatarius; the holding of Vallis Lauriculae; the holding of Pradello; the holding of Borellus of Sarto; the holding of Somenzarius; the holding of Sclavo; the holding of Maliolis; the holding of Quoquotum; the holding of Petroli and of John of Caniolo; one share at Lobi; one share at Palatium; and the rent from Corinello; the *braida* of Ponte; the *braida* beside the ditch of Batalia; the *braida* in the field of Tufini; the *braida* at Pigno; the *braida* [Col. 0584B] at Marzelasco; the meadow called Codognarium, with the vineyards attached to it; the vineyard within the city; and whatever mills the aforesaid Bishop Simon or his predecessors, or Aluisa, wife of Marquess Marcellus, together with her sons, may reasonably have granted you—all these likewise we confirm.

Moreover, from the produce of your labors, which you cultivate with your own hands and at your own expense, or from the increase of your animals, let no cleric or layman whatsoever presume to exact tithes from you. If, however, that episcopal see is vacant or has no Catholic bishop, you may receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars, and ecclesiastical ordinations of churches from whichever bishop you prefer.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it in any manner; but that all things shall be kept whole, to the benefit in every way of those for whose support and governance they were granted, saving the canonical justice of the supreme pontiff. If any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second and third time, should fail to amend the offense by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honor, know himself or herself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most holy body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, [Col. 0584D] and be subject to severe vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good works and find with the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

[Note: [Col. 0583] There is no chronological date. Margarinus, however, asserts that the diploma was issued on 8 March 1142; certainly with excessive precision and exactitude.]

### DXX. He undertakes the protection of the monastery of Gerbach [or Ingerbach] and confirms its goods and rights.  
*(1142, 11 March.)*

[Monumenta Boica, vol. X, p. 236.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons [Col. 0585A], BERON, provost, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life in the church of Gerbach, forever.

It accords with the clemency of the Apostolic See to love religious men and to foster their places with the safeguard of pious protection. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, moved by the prayers of our venerable brother Henry, bishop of Regensburg, we graciously admit your reasonable petitions; and we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, and strengthen by the safeguard of this present writing, the aforesaid church in which you are devoted to divine service. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that church now possesses justly and canonically, and may hereafter, by reasonable means and with God’s favor, acquire, shall remain firm and inviolate for you and your successors.

We also decree that the canonical order according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine shall be preserved there inviolate for all time. Upon the death of you, the present provost of the same place, or of any of your successors, no one may be placed over it by any cunning of deceit or by force, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, in the fear of God and according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine, shall canonically provide to be elected.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance [Col. 0585C] and support they were granted, saving the canonical justice of the diocesan bishop. If any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second and third time, should not make amends by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honor, know himself or herself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most holy body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and be subject to severe vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good works [Col. 0585D] and find with the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Gerard, presbyter-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Ides of March, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1141 from the Lord’s Incarnation, in the thirteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### DXXI. He undertakes the protection of the monastery of Saint Imer at Bellelay and confirms its possessions.  
*(1142, 14 March.)*

[HUGO, *Annals of Prémontré*, I, p. 216.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons [Col. 0586A], GERALD, abbot of Bellelay, and his brethren, present and future, regularly established forever.

Whenever that is requested of us which is recognized to accord with religion and uprightness, it is fitting that we grant it with willing mind and afford fitting support to the desires of petitioners. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, strengthening by the privilege of this present writing, the church of Blessed Imer in which you are devoted to divine service.

First, we decree that the canonical order according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine and the institution of the brethren of Prémontré shall be preserved there inviolate for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions and goods that church now possesses justly and canonically, or may hereafter, through the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, with God’s favor, acquire, shall remain firm and inviolate for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to set out the following by their proper names: the church of Saint Ursicinus of Nocriol with its appurtenances; the valley of Rursca with its appurtenances; the court of Boecourt with its appurtenances; and vineyards at Bielle.

Furthermore, from the produce of your labors which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or from the increase of your animals, let no cleric or layman whatsoever presume to exact tithes from you. We therefore decree [Col. 0586C] that no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid church of Bellelay, take away, retain, or diminish its possessions, or harass it with any molestations; but that all things shall be kept whole, to the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the canonical reverence due to the bishop of Basel. If any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second and third time, should not make amends by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power, know himself or herself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most holy [Col. 0586D] body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and be subject to severe vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good works and find with the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina. I, Octavius, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in Carcere.

The letter was issued [Note: [Col. 0585D] Read: “at the Lateran.”] through the hand of Gerard, presbyter-cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman [Col. 0587A] Church, on the second day before the Ides of March, in the fourth indiction, in the year 1141 from the Lord’s Incarnation, in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II. [Note: [Col. 0587D] Read “the twelfth year,” since Innocent II was elected pope on 23 February 1130.]

### DXXII. He undertakes the protection of the nunnery of Saint Lambert at Tulba, confirms its possessions, and establishes privileges.  
*(1142, 18 March.)*

[COCQUELINES, II, 252.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, the nuns professing the regular life in the church of Blessed Lambert the martyr at Tulba, present and future, forever.

The desire which is shown to pertain to the purpose of religion and [Col. 0587B] the salvation of souls ought to be granted by us with willing mind, and fitting support ought to be afforded to petitioners’ desires. Therefore, beloved daughters in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, strengthening by the privilege of this present writing, the aforesaid church in which you are devoted to divine service. First, we decree that the monastic order according to the Rule of Blessed Benedict shall be observed perpetually and inviolate.

Moreover, whatever possessions and goods the church now possesses justly and canonically, or may hereafter, through the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just [Col. 0587C] means, with God’s favor, acquire, shall remain firm and inviolate for you and your posterity. Among these we have thought fit to set out the following by their proper names: namely, the allod and benefice at Tulba, which Gerlac and his wife Regelinde, in devotion, gave to the monastery of Fulda together with many other goods of theirs; as it was afterward granted to you for religious reasons, together with certain other goods, by Conrad, abbot of that monastery of good memory, with the counsel of his brethren and of the aforesaid Gerlac; the allod of Evernide; the village of Luvris; five holdings and the demesne at Hamelemburch; seven holdings at Erdale; in another village of the same name, half a holding of one Latho; and whatever the aforesaid Gerlac and his wife possessed at Franchenborne [Col. 0587D] and Wolfchershlegere; the allod of Vostat, which the wife of Gerlac himself gave; the parish of that place; one village, Voestensasso; the tithe of the demesne lands of Hamelemburch and of the demesne of Thiebac.

We also forbid that anyone be set over that place by any cunning of deceit or by force, except one whom the sisters by common assent, or the sounder part of them, in the fear of God and according to the Rule of Blessed Benedict, shall provide to be elected. No provost, moreover, may be placed over it except one whom the abbess, with the common counsel [Col. 0588A] of the sisters, has chosen as suitable for herself.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be kept whole, to the benefit in every way of those for whose preservation and governance they were granted, saving the right and reverence of the monastery of Fulda. If any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second and third time, should not make amends by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honor, know himself or herself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most holy body [Col. 0588B] and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, and be subject to severe vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good works and find with the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed. I, Guido, unworthy priest of the Holy Roman Church, have subscribed. I, Guido, presbyter-cardinal of the title of Saint Cecilia, [Col. 0588C] have subscribed. I, Thomas, presbyter-cardinal of the title of Vestina, have subscribed. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Nicholas in Carcere, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Gerard, presbyter-cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of April, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1141 from the Lord’s Incarnation, in the thirteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II. [Note: [Col. 0587D] You see, reader, how many complications these chronological dates present here also—something it is surprising the reporter did not notice, though otherwise, as I have often been able to infer from his conversation, he was most learned. Change, therefore, if you wish, the tenth indiction to the fourth, and the thirteenth year of Innocent’s pontificate to the twelfth, so that they may agree with the year 1141.]

### DXXIII. Confirmation of the possessions of Grand-Selve.  
*(1142, 1 April.)*

[Gallia Christiana, XIII, Documents, 18.]

INNOCENT, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons BERTRAND, abbot of the monastery of Grand-Selve, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life in perpetuity (P. P. M.).

It accords with the clemency of apostolic governance to love religious persons and to fortify their places by pious protection. [Col. 0589A] For it is recognized as worthy and fitting to uprightness that we, who have been raised to the governance of churches, should both protect them from the malice of wicked persons and foster them by the patronage of the Apostolic See. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, strengthening by the safeguard of this present writing, the aforesaid monastery of the blessed Mother of God and ever-virgin Mary, situated in the diocese of Toulouse.

We decree that the monastic order according to the Rule of Blessed Benedict and the institution of the Cistercian brethren shall be preserved there inviolate for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now possesses justly and [Col. 0589B] canonically, or may hereafter, through the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, with God’s favor, acquire, shall remain firm and inviolate for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to set out the following by their proper names: namely, the place called Grand-Selve, with all that pertains to it, which lies within these four churches: Riclercella, Beaumont, Bolliacum, and Saint-Germain; the grange of Cobirac; the grange of Combaroger; and beyond the river Garonne, the grange of Baniols and the grange of Lasela; in another place under the castle of Caraman, the grange of Salet.

Moreover, in the district of Narbonne, the place of Fontfroide, with its tithes, first fruits, and all its appurtenances, which Aimeric, viscount of Narbonne, granted in perpetuity to the aforesaid abbot and brethren for the building of an abbey there, for the redemption of his soul. In the district of Périgueux, the place of Scenzalas, with tithes, first fruits, and all that pertains to it.

Furthermore, from the produce of your labors which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or from the increase of your animals, let no cleric or layman whatsoever presume to exact tithes from you. Upon the death of you, the present abbot of the same place, or of any of your successors, no one may be placed over it by any cunning of deceit or by force; rather, it shall be lawful for you, by common counsel or that of the sounder part, in the fear of God and according to the Rule of Blessed Benedict, to elect an abbot without anyone’s opposition. [Col. 0589D]

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be kept whole, to the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second and third time, should not make amends by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honor, know himself or herself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most holy body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ [Col. 0590A] the Redeemer, and be subject to severe vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good works and find with the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Gregory Gerard. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Guido, unworthy priest of the Holy Roman Church. [Col. 0590B] I, Gerard, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Domnica. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in Carcere. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of the Holy Roman Church. Guizo, presbyter-cardinal of the title of Saint Cecilia.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Gerard, presbyter-cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the Kalends of April, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1142 from the Lord’s Incarnation, in the thirteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Innocent II.

### DXXIV. Privilege for the church of Saint Lawrence at Viterbo.  
*(1142, 3 April.)*

[BUSSI, *History of the City of Viterbo*, I, p. 400.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son AZO, archpriest of the church of Saint Lawrence at Viterbo, and to his successors canonically appointed.

A petition of pious intention ought to be fulfilled by its effectual execution, so that the sincerity of devotion may be commendably made known and the requested benefit may undoubtedly acquire force. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Azo, archpriest, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, strengthening by the safeguard of this present writing, the aforesaid church over which, by God’s authorship, you are known to preside.

We decree that whatever [Col. 0590D] possessions and goods the same church now possesses justly and canonically, or may hereafter, through the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, with God’s favor, acquire, shall remain firm and inviolate for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to set out the following by their proper names: the church of Saint Blaise, the church of Saint Giles, and the church of Saint Bartholomew, with all their appurtenances. We likewise confirm to you the offerings of the living and whatever is granted or offered to those churches for the dead, as well as whatever you lawfully possess in other churches.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforementioned church, take away its possessions, [Col. 0591A] or harass it by any forms of vexation; but that all things shall be kept whole, to the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second and third time, should not make amends by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honor, know himself or herself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most holy body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and be subject to divine vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that church may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit [Col. 0591B] of good works and find with the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at the Lateran through the hands of Gerard, presbyter-cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Nones of April, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1142 from the Lord’s Incarnation, in the thirteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### DXXV. Privilege for the church of Saint Stephen at Toulouse.  
*(1142, 19 April.)*

[Gallia Christiana, XIII, Documents, p. 19.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother RAIMUND, bishop of Toulouse, and to his successors canonically appointed forever.

By the office of the apostolate entrusted to us by God, we ought to love our brethren both near and far, and to preserve their rights for the churches in which they are known to serve the Lord. Therefore, venerable brother Raimund, bishop, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, strengthening by the privilege of this present writing, the church of Toulouse of Blessed Stephen the protomartyr, over which, by God’s authorship, you are known to preside.

We decree that whatever possessions and goods you now possess justly and canonically, or may hereafter, by reasonable means and with God’s favor, acquire, shall remain firm and inviolate for you and your successors. Moreover, by apostolic authority we forbid any layman or cleric, upon the death of you or of your successors, to seize episcopal goods or dispose of ecclesiastical property; instead, they shall remain in the power of the steward and archdeacons for the use of the Church and the installation of a bishop. We also forbid anyone, without the counsel of you or your successors, or of the sounder part of the chapter of that church, to presume to sell, mortgage, or alienate those goods in any manner.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb that church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be kept whole, to the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and [Col. 0592A] support they were granted. If any ecclesiastical person in future, etc.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina. Himinarius, bishop of Tusculum. Guido, unworthy priest of the Holy Roman Church. Martin, presbyter-cardinal of the title of Saint Pastor. Goizo, presbyter-cardinal of the title of Saint Cecilia. Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. Gerald, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Domnica. [Col. 0592B] Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in Carcere. Peter, cardinal of Saint Mary in Portico. Nicholas, cardinal deacon of the Holy Roman Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Gerald, presbyter-cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of May, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1142 from the Incarnation, in the thirteenth year of the pontificate of Pope Innocent II.

### DXXVI. To the clergy and people of Toulouse.—He commends to them Bishop Raimund, who is returning from him, and commands them to give him help and counsel in recovering the alienated goods of the Church of Toulouse.  
*(1142, 19 April.)*

[D. BOUQUET, vol. XV, p. 406.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the clergy and people of Toulouse: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have received with due kindness our venerable brother Raimund, your bishop, when he came to us, and have carefully instructed him concerning matters belonging to the episcopal office. We therefore send him back to his own see with the favor of the Apostolic See and the support of our letters, and request, admonish, and command all of you to receive him kindly, love and honor him with special affection, and humbly render him obedience and reverence as your father [Col. 0592D] and bishop of your souls.

In recovering the goods and possessions of the Church of Toulouse which have been disposed of or alienated by evil administrators, and in preserving what is held, provide him help and counsel as good sons. For our part, we annul and judge void all sales, mortgages, or other alienations of episcopal goods or possessions made by anyone without that bishop’s consent. But if anyone should presume to be rebellious and disobedient, we shall, by the Lord’s authority, hold valid the sentence which he shall canonically pronounce against that person.

Given at the Lateran, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of May.

### DXXVII. He undertakes the protection of the church of Blessed Eusebius at Vercelli and confirms the possessions of its canons.  
*(1142, 25 April.)*

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, IV, 779.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ABRAHAM, archpriest, and the canons of the greater church of Vercelli, present and future, canonically appointed forever.

The principle of equity and justice persuades us to grant churches perpetual security in their goods and documents of unshaken force. For it is not fitting that clerics called to the Lord’s portion should be harassed by the perverse troubles of wicked persons and wearied by the reckless vexations of anyone; likewise, estates dedicated to the uses of the sacred mysteries of heaven ought not to suffer any oppressive demands of the powerful or any extraordinary burden.

Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, strengthening by the privilege of this present writing, the church of Blessed Eusebius at Vercelli, in which you are devoted to divine service. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that church now possesses justly and canonically, or may hereafter, through the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, with God’s favor, acquire, shall remain firm and inviolate for you and your successors, and through you for the same church forever. [Col. 0593C]

Among these we have thought fit to set out the following by their proper names: the estate of Caresiana; Villiacum; Mount Galliani with all its appurtenances; and Porto Servi. Moreover, we judge that the ancient and reasonable customs of that church shall remain valid.

Therefore no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it by vexations, saving the privileges—namely, the canonical reverence due to the Roman Church and to the bishop of Vercelli. If anyone should rashly attempt to act against these things, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honor, be cut off from the most holy body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, and be subject to vengeance at the last judgment. [Col. 0593D] Amen, amen.

Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. I, Martin, presbyter-cardinal of Saint Stephen. I, Guido, unworthy priest of the Holy Roman Church. I, Stamius, presbyter-cardinal of the title of Saint Sabina. I, Guido, presbyter-cardinal of Saint Chrysogonus. I, Ranerius, presbyter-cardinal of the title of Saint Prisca. I, Peter, presbyter-cardinal of the title of Pastor. I, Goizo, presbyter-cardinal of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Ubaldus, presbyter-cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul. I, Thomas, presbyter-cardinal of the title of Vestina. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. [Col. 0594A] I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Vassallus, cardinal deacon of Saint Eustace. I, Ubaldus, cardinal deacon in Via Lata. I, Gerard, deacon of Saint Mary in Domnica. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in Carcere. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of the Holy Roman Church. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of the Holy Roman Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Gerard, presbyter-cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Kalends of May, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1142 from the Lord’s Incarnation, [Col. 0594B] in the thirteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### DXXVIII. To Peter the Venerable, abbot of Cluny.—A manor in England given by King Stephen in place of the one hundred marks given by King Henry.  
*(1142, 19 May.)*

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 408.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son PETER, abbot of Cluny, and to his brethren, present and future, regularly established forever.

Being advanced, by God’s disposition, to the governance of the apostolic see, we are bound to grant assent to pious wishes and to incline our ears to just petitions. [Col. 0594C] For, just as no effect is to be granted to those who ask for unjust things, so the possession sought by those who petition lawfully and justly is not to be delayed. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, graciously assenting to your just requests, we confirm by apostolic authority to you, and through you to the monastery of Cluny, and strengthen by the page of this present writing, the manor of Letdecumba, as it was granted to you from his own domain, out of devotion, by the illustrious man Stephen, king of the English, together with the customs and liberties belonging to it and all its appurtenances, and as it was confirmed by his charter, namely in exchange for one hundred marks of silver which Henry, king of the English of good memory, Stephen’s predecessor, had granted to you to be paid annually from his treasury. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our confirmation, etc.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Martin, cardinal priest of the title of St Stephen, have subscribed. I, Statius, cardinal priest of the title of St Sabina, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of St Chrysogonus, have subscribed. I, Goizo, cardinal priest of the title of St Cecilia, have subscribed. [Col. 0595A] I, Hubald, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Rainerius, cardinal priest of the title of St Prisca, have subscribed. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of St George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Gerard, cardinal deacon of St Mary in Dominica, have subscr[ibed]. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of St Nicholas in Carcere, have subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of St Mary in Porticu, have subscribed.

Given at Tivoli, through the hand of Gerard, [Col. 0595B] cardinal priest and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of June [19 May], in the fifth indiction, in the year 1142 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the thirteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### DXXIX. Privilege for the Church of Ragusa. (Year 1142, 11 June.)

[Farlatus, *Illyricum sacrum*, vol. VI, p. 63.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother ANDREW, bishop of the city of Ragusa, and to his successors to be canonically appointed in perpetuity.

By the office of the apostolate entrusted to us, it is fitting that we provide with fatherly [Col. 0595C] care for our brothers both nearby and far away, etc. Therefore, graciously assenting with due kindness to your petitions, etc., we decree that whatever parishes . . . are to remain entire to you and your successors: namely, the kingdom of Zachlumia; the kingdom of Servilia; the kingdom of Tribunia; the cities of Kotor or Risan; Budva of the Avars; Ulcinj and Scutari; likewise Drivast and Polat, with their abbeys, churches, and parishes, etc. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, having been warned a second and third time and failing to make suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of authority and office; let that person know that he or she stands guilty before the divine judgment for the wrong committed; [Col. 0595D] let that person be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of the Lord, our Redeemer Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let that person be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that same church may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.

I, Albitius, etc.

Given at Tivoli, through the hand of Gerard, cardinal priest and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Ides of June [11 June], in the fifth indiction, in the year 1142 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the thirteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### DXXX. Privilege for the Church of St Mary of Stromberch. (Year 1142, 12 June.)

[Lacomblet, *Urkundenbuch*, I, p. 233.]

[Col. 0596A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons WALTHER, provost of the Church of St Mary of Stromberch, and HERMANN, and their other brethren, present and future, to be regularly appointed in perpetuity.

The care of the universal Church has been entrusted to us by God, the provider of all good things, so that we may love religious persons and endeavour by every means to advance religion pleasing to God. For no service is ever pleasingly rendered to God unless, proceeding from the root of charity, it has been [Col. 0596B] preserved in the purity of religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we mercifully assent to your just petitions; we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church, in which you are dedicated to divine service; and we fortify it with the privilege of this present writing, decreeing that the canonical order according to the Rule of blessed Augustine shall be inviolably maintained there for all time.

Moreover, whatever possessions and goods that church at present justly and canonically possesses, or may in future, with God’s favour, acquire by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. We likewise confirm the tithes of the entire hill upon which your church stands, and [Col. 0596C] of all newly cultivated lands that shall be cultivated within the boundary—namely, within the mark of the inhabitants of Winthere—and all else reasonably granted to you by Arnold, archbishop of Cologne. No one may presume to usurp the advocacy of that place, except one whom the brethren, by common consent or the counsel of the sounder part, shall see fit to elect according to the fear of God and the benefit of that place.

Indeed, no cleric or layperson whatsoever may presume to exact tithes from you on the produce of lands which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or on the sustenance of your animals. We also grant that the burial ground of that place shall be free, so that no one may obstruct any persons who determine to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated; yet the rights of the mother church are preserved. [Col. 0596D] We therefore decree that no person at all may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, seize its possessions, retain possessions seized, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; rather, all shall be preserved intact for the benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the canonical right of the archbishop of Cologne. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, after a second or third warning, does not make amends by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of authority and office and know that he or she stands guilty before divine judgment for the wrong committed; [Col. 0597A] let that person be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of the Lord, our Redeemer Jesus Christ, and at the last judgment be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve what is right for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of St Nicholas in Carcere, have subscribed.

Given at Tivoli, through the hand of Gerard, cardinal priest and [Col. 0597B] librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Ides of June [12 June], in the fifth indiction, in the year 1142 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the thirteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### DXXXI. To Henry, bishop of Moravia: he commends Guido the cardinal, sent as legate to these regions to correct the enormities of the clergy, asking Henry to support him with assistance and counsel. (Year 1142, 21 August.)

[Boczek, *Codex diplomaticus Moraviae*, I, 215, from a manuscript codex of the Olomouc archives, fourteenth century, no. CCCLXXIX; of the Church of Litovel, fifteenth century.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, bishop of Moravia, greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0597C] It is long since we learned that your brotherhood has been very diligent in uprooting vices and fostering virtues, and that you labour with particular earnestness to spread the religion of the Christian faith in those regions. Therefore, because of the great confidence which we have in your person, we earnestly commend to your affection our beloved son Guido, cardinal deacon, a prudent and honourable man, whom we are sending from our side to those regions for the correction of abuses. We ask you carefully to assist him and to furnish aid and counsel in those matters which you know concern the advancement of Christian religion and the correction of morals.

Given at the Lateran, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of September [21 August].

### DXXXII. He takes the monastery of Arnstein under protection and confirms its possessions and rights. (Year 1142, 30 September.)

[Hontheim, *Historia Trevirensis diplomatica*, I, 548.]

[Col. 0597D]

INNOCENT, etc., to his beloved sons GODEFRID, abbot of Arnstein, and his brethren, present and future, to be regularly appointed in perpetuity.

The care of the universal Church has been entrusted to us by God, the provider of all good things, so that we may love religious persons and endeavour by every means to advance religion pleasing to God. For no service is ever pleasingly rendered to God unless, proceeding from the root of charity, it has been preserved in the purity of religion. Therefore all lovers of the Christian faith ought [Col. 0598A] to cherish religious persons and carefully foster venerable places, together with persons dedicated to divine service, so that they may not be troubled by the molestations of evil people or worn down by burdensome exactions.

Accordingly, beloved sons in the Lord, we mercifully assent to your just petitions. We receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the Church of Arnstein of the Blessed Mother of God and ever-Virgin Mary and of the glorious confessor of Christ Nicholas, in which you are dedicated to divine service, and fortify it with the privilege of this present writing. First, we decree that the canonical order, according to the Rule of blessed Augustine and the institution of the brethren of Prémontré, shall be inviolably maintained there for all time. [Col. 0598B] No brother, after making profession, may dare, through any impulse of fickleness or under the pretext of a stricter religious life, to depart without permission from the abbot and the entire community; and no abbot or cleric may receive a departing brother without a common letter of surety.

Moreover, whatever possessions and goods you presently possess justly and canonically, whether through gift or grant of the illustrious man Louis and his wife Guda or through other faithful people of God, or may in future, with God’s favour, acquire by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors forever. Among these we have thought fit to specify in their own terms: the Church of St Margaret with its tithe; the church of Kirchdorff with its tithe and other [Col. 0598C] appurtenances, as these are known to have been reasonably granted to you by our brother Albero, archbishop of Trier; Clelebach with all its property, as it was granted to you by the aforesaid archbishop; Hattenhusen, Welderode, Gozenerode, Holdenruche, with all their appurtenances; vineyards and woods at Neven and Bremme, with every right and lordship, as the aforesaid Louis is known to have granted them to you; Bubenheim with its church and all its possessions; Wize and Berhernhem.

No cleric or layperson whatsoever may presume to demand tithes from you on the produce of lands which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or on the sustenance of your animals. On the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one may be set over it through any trickery, cunning, or violence; rather, you may elect an abbot, without anyone’s objection, by common counsel or by the sounder part of the counsel, according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Augustine. Further, no one may invade or usurp the advocacy of your place, except one whom the abbot and brethren shall provide to be elected according to God and the advantage of that place. We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, seize its possessions, retain possessions seized, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; rather, all shall be preserved entire for the benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the canonical right of the archbishop of Trier. [Col. 0599A] If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it and, after a second or third warning, does not make amends by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of authority and office; let that person know that he or she stands guilty before divine judgment for the wrong committed; let that person be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of the Lord, our Redeemer Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let that person be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve what is right for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. [Col. 0599B] I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of St George at the Golden Veil. I, Stannus, cardinal priest of the title of St Sabina. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of St Chrysogonus. I, Rainerius, cardinal priest of St Prisca. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of St Martha in Porticu.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Gerard, cardinal priest and librarian of the Holy Roman [Col. 0599C] Church, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of October [21 September; the date is inconsistent with the heading’s 30 September], in the fifth indiction, in the year 1142 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the thirteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### DXXXIII. At the request of Rudolf, bishop of Halberstadt, and Albert, bishop of Bamberg, he takes the Church of Kolbitz under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. (Year 1142, 30 September.)

[Beckmann, *History of Anhalt*, I, 469.]

### DXXXIV. He takes the monastery of St Mary of Varlar under protection and confirms its goods. (Year 1142, 27 October.)

[Hugo, *Annales Praemonstratenses*, II, p. 651.]

[Col. 0599D]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ALBERT, provost of the Church of St Mary of Varlar, and his brethren, present and future, in perpetuity.

A desire shown to pertain to the purpose of religion and the salvation of souls ought fittingly to be granted by us with a willing mind, and fitting support ought to be bestowed upon the desires of petitioners. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we mercifully assent to your just petitions. We receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church, in which you are dedicated to divine service, and fortify it with the privilege of this present [Col. 0600A] writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future, with God’s favour, acquire by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify in their own terms: Coesvilde, Asbecke, Lette, the tithe; at Lette, the holding of Adelheidis, *invariare* [uncertain reading].

On the death of you, the present provost of that place, or of any of your successors, no one may be set over it by the cunning of any fraudulent scheme or by insolence; rather, you may [Col. 0600B] elect a provost, without anyone’s objection, by common counsel or by the sounder part of the counsel, according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Augustine. Further, no one may invade or usurp the advocacy of your place, except one whom the provost and brethren unanimously determine should be elected according to God and the advantage of that place. We also decree that the burial ground of that place shall be free, so that no one may obstruct any who determine to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated; yet the right of the mother Church is preserved. No cleric or layperson whatsoever may presume to demand tithes from you on the produce of lands which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or on the sustenance of your beasts of burden and animals.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, seize its possessions, retain possessions seized, [Col. 0600C] diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; rather, all shall be preserved intact for the benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it and, after a second or third warning, does not make amends by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of authority and office; let that person know that he or she stands guilty before divine judgment for the wrong committed; let that person be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of the Lord, our Redeemer Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let that person be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve what is right for that place may there be the peace of our Lord [Col. 0600D] Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of St Nicholas in Carcere.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Gerard, cardinal priest and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the sixth day before the Kalends of November [27 October], in the sixth indiction, in the year 1142 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the thirteenth year of Lord Innocent II’s pontificate.

### DXXXV. He takes the monastery of Saints Sixtus and Sebastian of Chiemsee under protection and confirms its privileges and goods. (Year 1142, 29 October.)

[*Monumenta Boica*, II, p. 386.]

[Col. 0601A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons CONO, provost of Chiemsee, and his brethren, present and future, to be regularly appointed in perpetuity.

A desire shown to pertain to the purpose of religion and the salvation of souls ought fittingly to be granted by us with a willing mind, and fitting support ought to be bestowed upon the desires of petitioners. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Provost Cono, we mercifully assent to your just petitions. We receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the church of the blessed martyrs of Christ [Col. 0601B] Sixtus and Sebastian, in which you are dedicated to divine service, and fortify it with the privilege of this present writing. First, we decree that the canonical order according to the Rule of blessed Augustine shall be inviolably maintained there for all time.

Moreover, whatever possessions and goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may in future, with God’s favour, acquire by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. On the death of you, the present provost of that place, or of any of your successors, no one may be set over it by the cunning of any fraudulent scheme or by violence; rather, you may elect a provost, without anyone’s objection, by common counsel or by the sounder part of the counsel, according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Augustine. [Col. 0601C] No one may invade or usurp the advocacy of that place, except one who has been elected in agreement by the provost and brethren according to God and the benefit of that church. Moreover, we grant that the burial ground of that place shall be free, so that no one may obstruct any who determine to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated; yet the right of the mother church is preserved.
