For it is recognized as fitting and consonant with honour that, since we have been appointed to govern the churches, we should defend them against the malice of wicked men and fortify them by the aid of Saint Peter.

Accordingly, beloved sons in the Lord, moved by the petitions of our dearest brother the Bishop of Auxerre—through whose activity religious observance is known to have been established both in this new church and in many others—we suitably grant your reasonable requests and strengthen by the protection of the Apostolic See the Church of Blessed Mary, in which you devote yourselves to divine service. We decree that a canonical order according to the canonical Rule of blessed Augustine shall be established there. Whatever possessions or goods are now known to belong justly and canonically to the same church, or which you may hereafter acquire by grants of pontiffs, gifts of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other certain means, with the Lord’s help, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you in perpetuity.

Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: namely, the Church of Saint Martin of Bonorto, with the land around it, bounded by definite boundaries in the district of the province of Sens, which blessed Vigilius, martyr and bishop, is proved to have bestowed, together with other possessions, upon the Church of Blessed Mary.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any other vexations; but all shall be preserved whole, for the benefit in every respect of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, shall rashly presume to act against it and, having been warned a second or third time, shall fail to correct the offence by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honour, recognize himself or herself as guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and be subject at the last judgment to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve their rights to that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

DLXV. To Conrad, Archbishop of Salzburg.—After praising the canonical life, he forbids the brethren of Berchtesgaden to alter their institution. (1138–1143, 16 March.)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 427.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother CONRAD, Archbishop of Salzburg: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The divine Scripture teaches us much concerning the dignity and excellence of the life of canons; and much might be said, because the life of canons is an apostolic life. For the apostles, having despised all things, lived this life with the Lord; and after the Ascension, living this life with the multitude of believers, “of whom there was one soul and one heart” [Col. 0629A], they left it to posterity to be maintained by their example. The martyr and pontiff Urban took care to recall this in his decrees for the instruction of the faithful, saying: “We know that you are not unaware that the common life has hitherto flourished among good Christians, and still flourishes by God’s grace, especially among those who have been chosen for the Lord’s portion—that is, clerics—as is read in the Acts of the Apostles: ‘The multitude of believers had one heart and one soul.’” St. Jerome gave form to this life, ordered by the rules of Blessed Augustine, in his letters. Therefore, fortified by the authorities of these and others, we judge that it is of no less merit, with the Spirit of the Lord inspiring and sustaining, to observe the canonical life than, through the perseverance of that same Spirit, to keep monastic religion [Col. 0629B].

Accordingly, we recall that it was established by the decrees of our predecessors that no one professed in the canonical order, after placing a man over his head in God’s stead, should dare, through an impulse of fickleness or under pretext of a stricter religious life, to depart from the cloister without permission of the superior and congregation. Following in their footsteps, we forbid by apostolic authority the proposed attempt of certain brothers in the cloister of Berchtesgaden to alter their order through vain presumption; commanding that they should render what they have vowed to God, and strive, with the Lord’s help, faithfully to observe the Rule of Blessed Augustine which they have professed. If perhaps you find them lax and insufficiently fervent in observing it, we exhort your brotherhood [Col. 0629C], according to the wisdom given you by God, strictly to admonish them—as is your concern—to preserve their profession and order and to obey the commands of the Rule.

Given at the Lateran, the seventeenth day before the Kalends of April.

### DLXVI. To Hugh, Archdeacon of Arras.—He receives him under the protection of the Roman Church.  
*(A.D. 1138–1143, April 15.)*

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 404.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ HUGH, archdeacon of Arras, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The clemency of the Apostolic See, by the duty of its customary compassion, knows how more earnestly to love devoted and humble sons [Col. 0629D] and to cherish them under the safeguard of its protection. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, considering your devotion toward Blessed Peter and ourselves, we receive you as a special son of the Apostolic See; and we take your person, together with the ecclesiastical and temporal goods which you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter, by God’s favor, acquire by reasonable means, under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves, and fortify them by the protection of this writing. We decree that, should you perceive yourself oppressed in any matter, you may freely appeal to the Apostolic See. Let no person, however, presume rashly to disturb your person [Col. 0630A] or goods, or to harass you with any troubles. But whoever presumes to attempt this shall know that he has incurred the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, the seventeenth day before the Kalends of May.

### DLXVII. He commands the consuls of Piacenza not to allow the water of the stream of St. Sabinus, granted by emperors to the monks of St. Sabinus, to be diverted by citizens.  
*(A.D. 1138–1143, April 23.)*

[CAMP., *History of Piacenza*, I, p. 531.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the consuls of Piacenza, greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0630B] Our beloved son Lawrence, abbot of St. Sabinus, has complained to us that your fellow citizens are taking from them the water of the stream of St. Sabinus, which was granted to them by emperors and confirmed by our writing, and are diverting it from its proper course to their meadows and lands [lacuna]. Therefore, since it pertains to your office to correct the offences of subjects, by these present letters we command you to restrain your said fellow citizens strictly from such injury and to ensure that they are left in peaceful possession of the water itself.

Given at the Lateran, the ninth day before the Kalends of May.

### DLXVIII. To William, lord of Montpellier.—He assents to his pious wishes, since he desires to build a monastery for the use of the Cluniacs.  
*(A.D. 1138–1143, April 28.)*

[D. BOUQUET, *Recueil*, XV, 395.]

[Col. 0630C]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ WILLIAM of Montpellier, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The sacred and God-beloved monastery of Cluny ought fittingly to be cherished by illustrious princes. For there religious brothers, devoted to the service of God, render an acceptable service to God; and, pouring forth pure prayers to the Lord, they penetrate the heavens, join the depths to things above, unite earthly things with heavenly, and redeem the sins of Catholic men who place their hope in them. Everyone who deserves, by conferring a benefit, to become a participant in so blessed a brotherhood ought indeed to rejoice in the Lord. Therefore, desiring to provide for the advantage of the monastery and the salvation of you and the people of Montpellier, we give assent to your pious wishes and grant them permission to have a church at Montpellier in honor of God, in which the divine offices may be celebrated; and whoever may decide to be buried there shall have free faculty to do so, saving, of course, the right of the mother church. It is therefore your concern, beloved son in the Lord William, to bring your pious vow to effect and to accomplish effectively that the Cluniacs may have among you a church endowed with possessions and other goods.

> **Note:** [Col. 0629D] At Sauzet, on the bank of the River Lez, there remain traces of a church called Maurice of [Col. 0630D] Sauzet. William is said to have built it, according to the municipal records, Gariel reports.

Given at the Lateran, the fourth day before the Kalends of May.

### DLXIX. To the consuls of Lucca.  
*(A.D. 1138–1143, May 23.)*

[BALUZ., *Miscellanies*, IV, 590.]

[Col. 0631A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the consuls of Lucca.

Your whole community ought indeed to remember the many offences by which you have often offended the Lord, and to deserve from Him forgiveness for your misdeeds through fitting humility. Yet we learn that, conversely, you are acting among yourselves in the contrary way, since you permit the brothers of the Church of St. Fridianus—who are held worthy of great reverence because of their religious life and integrity—to be harassed concerning the administration of the Church of St. Pantaleon, which we entrusted to them to order and govern [Col. 0631B]. Therefore, by apostolic letters we command and enjoin you henceforth to permit no opposition or trouble to be inflicted upon those brothers in this matter; and, so that our grant may receive a completion pleasing to God, to give them counsel and aid, so that henceforth almighty God may there be served according to their administration.

Given at the Lateran, the tenth day before the Kalends of June.

### DLXX. He assures the canons of the Church of St. Alexander at Bergamo of the Church of Virgis.  
*(A.D. 1138–1143, September 23.)*

[LUPI, *Diplomatic Code of Bergamo*, II, 1019.]

[Col. 0631C]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons O., provost, and the canons of St. Alexander of Bergamo, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We received your messengers, namely our beloved sons J. and G., when they came to us, with due kindness; and we give thanks to your charity for the greetings conveyed to us through them. We wish you to know that we desire to love and support your persons and the Church of Blessed Alexander, and to preserve your rights unimpaired for you. Therefore, wishing to satisfy your petition, we grant you in perpetual possession the Church of Virgis, known to belong by right to Blessed Peter and entrusted to you, so that the church may remain secure under your governance [Col. 0631D] and may gladly render us its annual payment. It is therefore your concern to show yourselves such persons and to persevere in the service of that church in such a way that we may rejoice in your good works and consider you worthy of greater favor.

Given at the Lateran, the ninth day before the Kalends of October.

### DLXXI. To the Archbishop of Auch concerning the Abbey of St. Fremier.  
*(A.D. 1139–1143, January 30.)*

[*Gallia Christiana*, new edition, I, Instruments, 189.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother the Archbishop of AUCH [Col. 0632A], greeting and apostolic blessing.

The clemency of the Apostolic See customarily preserves for individual places and persons their dignity and right. Our beloved son M., abbot of St. Florentius, appearing before us, informed us that the Abbey of St. Fremier, situated in your archbishopric, has from ancient times belonged by right to St. Florentius; that the abbots established there made profession in the monastery of St. Florentius; and that they rendered obedience both to him and to his predecessors. Since that monastery, with all its appurtenances, belongs by right to Blessed Peter, we command and strictly enjoin you by these present letters that, if P., abbot of the said abbey, scorns to maintain his profession [Col. 0632B] and render the due and customary obedience to our said son the abbot, you shall without delay administer the justice due in his case.

Given at the Lateran, the third day before the Kalends of February.

### DLXXII. To Peter, Abbot, and the Monks of Cluny.—He restrains the Archbishop and clerics of Lyons, hostile to the Cluniacs and employing violence through sworn confederates. He sends Guy, cardinal deacon, to settle their disputes, etc.  
*(A.D. 1139–1143, May 17.)*

[D. BOUQUET, *Recueil*, XV, 396.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons PETER, abbot, and the monks of Cluny, greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0632C] We are greatly concerned for your peace and tranquillity. We have therefore, by request and command, imposed upon our venerable brother F., Archbishop of Lyons, the duty to cease from injuring and harassing you, and to make the clerics of Lyons desist.

> **Note:** [Col. 0631D] This was Falco, who became Archbishop of Lyons in 1139 and died in 1144.

Concerning those who laid violent hands upon monks or were parties to a sworn conspiracy or confederacy, we have decreed that they shall be subject to sentence of anathema until they make satisfaction to you. We likewise command that those things which the monastery of Cluny had held and which were taken away by the people of Lyons be restored. But if any dispute concerning these matters remains, it shall be settled before our son G[uy] [Col. 0632D], cardinal deacon and legate of the Apostolic See, whom we have sent especially on account of your cause.

> **Note:** [Col. 0631D] Guy, who held a judicial assembly at Uzès in 1139; see vol. XIV, p. 310.

We have also decreed that in the monastery of St. Raginbert (Saint-Rambert), because its brothers have hitherto lived too loosely and insufficiently religiously, religious observance shall be reformed through the brothers of Cluny. Nor shall the Church of Villefranche, known to have been granted to Cluny by the Archbishop of Lyons, be taken away.

> **Note:** [Col. 0632D] Concerning this Villefranche, Peter the Venerable wrote to the canons of Lyons, book IV, letter 6: [Col. 0633D] “I am therefore astonished, and I still lay before you a familiar complaint: that the pact of peace—to which we agreed, through the mediation of wise and religious persons, less than a year ago—has been broken, not indeed by all of you, but, as has been reported to me, by some among you; [Col. 0634D] and they even publicly forbade the lord Archbishop of Lyons to dedicate a cemetery at Villefranche according to the terms of the agreement. Whether this ought to have been done, you yourselves consider,” etc.

If any matters remain—which we do not wish to occur—that could not be settled in the presence of our legate, they shall, at a suitable time and with the Lord’s help, receive their due conclusion in our presence.

Given at the Lateran, the sixteenth day before the Kalends of June.

### DLXXIII. To the Abbot and Monks of Bec.  
*(A.D. 1140–1143, February 24.)*

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 420.]

[Col. 0633A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons LETARD, abbot, and the monks of the monastery of Bec, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Whenever something is asked of us that is known to accord with reason and propriety, it is fitting for us to grant it willingly and to give appropriate support to the petitioners’ wishes. Therefore, moved by the prayers of our venerable brother Rotrou, Bishop of Évreux, we confirm and fortify by the protection of this writing the Church of the Holy Trinity of Beaumont, with all that it now justly and canonically possesses through the gift of Roger of Beaumont, his son Robert, Count Waleran also [Col. 0633B], and other faithful people of God, or may hereafter, by the Lord’s aid, acquire by lawful means, as it was reasonably granted to you by our said brother with the consent of Count Waleran of Meulan. The prebends of the surviving canons who were instituted in that church before this time are reserved. If anyone, knowing this page of our constitution and confirmation, attempts to act against it, and, having been admonished a second or third time, does not correct his offence by suitable satisfaction, let him know that he shall incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

[Col. 0633C] Given at the Lateran, the sixth day before the Kalends of March.

### DLXXIV. To Pontius, Abbot of Vézelay.—He preserves the rights of Vézelay.  
*(A.D. 1140–1143, May 6.)*

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 403.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son PONTIUS, abbot of Vézelay, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We remember that by other letters we commanded you to answer Stephen, canon of Auxerre, concerning his complaint in the presence of our venerable brothers Geoffrey, Bishop of Langres, and Bernard, Abbot of Clairvaux, and firmly to observe whatever they should determine in the matter. But since you later informed us by letter and messenger that the Church of Vézelay has already held peacefully for thirty years and more the matter in dispute, and that, according to the ancient custom of your church, you are bound to answer no one in your court, we do not wish you to be troubled concerning this matter contrary to your church’s custom; nor do we wish what was decreed in this matter by Pope P. [Paschal], our predecessor of blessed memory, to be altered.

Given at the Lateran, the second day before the Nones of May.

### DLXXV. To Geoffrey, Bishop of Langres, and Bernard, Abbot of Clairvaux.—On the same matter.  
*(A.D. 1140–1143, May?)*

[MANSI, ibid., 403.]

[Col. 0634A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers GEOFFREY, Bishop of Langres, and BERNARD, Abbot of Clairvaux, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We remember that by apostolic letters we commanded you to hear and bring to a due conclusion the complaint of Stephen, canon of Auxerre, against our beloved son Pontius, abbot of Vézelay. But because the same abbot subsequently informed us by letter and messenger [Col. 0634B] that the Church of Vézelay has held peacefully for thirty years and more the matter in dispute, and that, according to the ancient custom of his church, etc., as in the preceding letter.

### DLXXVI. To Petronilla, Abbess, and the Nuns of Fontevraud.  
*(A.D. 1140–1143, July 1.)*

[PAVILLON, *Life of Robert of Arbrissel*, Preface, p. 627.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ PETRONILLA, abbess, and the sisters of Fontevraud, greeting.

Since our venerable brother Ulger, Bishop of Angers, informed us by his letters and messengers [Col. 0634C] that he wished, according to his conscience, to restore to you those things of which he had despoiled you, either personally or through his servants, but that you refused to receive them [lacuna]. We [lacuna] desire to impose a due conclusion upon this controversy after a long [lacuna]. By apostolic letters we commanded him to restore to you the mill and the other things of which he had despoiled you through [lacuna], saving his own right and that of Saints Sergius and Bacchus; after satisfaction had been made, we restored to him his episcopal office after seven days. Afterwards, however, the case itself [lacuna] our venerable brothers G., Bishop of Chartres, legate of the Apostolic See, H., Archbishop of Tours, and G., likewise Archbishop of Bordeaux [lacuna] an agreement [lacuna]. Since it is fitting that religious persons abstain from litigation and [lacuna], and since we desire diligently to attend to your peace and tranquillity [Col. 0634D] [lacuna] to preserve your right, we command you by apostolic letters that [lacuna] you may have [lacuna], so that this controversy, now debated for so long a time, may henceforth [lacuna] the Church of Angers may suffer some loss from contentions of this kind; praying that divine mercy may preserve you and grant you perseverance in His holy service.

Given at the Lateran, on the Kalends of July.

### DLXXVII. To Petronilla, Abbess of Fontevraud.—He consoles her, afflicted by injuries from Ulger, Bishop of Angers, and others; and declares that aid and justice are to be sought from Geoffrey, Bishop of Chartres, legate of the Apostolic See.  
*(A.D. 1140–1143, July 7.)*

[D. BOUQUET, *Recueil*, XV, 408.]

[Col. 0635A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ PETRONILLA, abbess, and the sisters of Fontevraud, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Ever since, though unworthy, we assumed by the Lord’s ordering the governance of God’s Church, we have loved and do love your persons and the place of Fontevraud with true charity in the Lord; and, so far as lies within our power, we desire to preserve your right for you whole and undiminished [Col. 0635B]. With paternal affection we grieve over the losses and injuries inflicted and being inflicted upon you and yours by Bishop Ulger and his people; and, as the Lord grants, we shall take care to relieve them. He himself, hardened in his obstinacy, remains in the city; what he expects or what he intends to do, we do not know. But we know that we have no intention whatever of altering what we have done concerning him or what we have decreed concerning your right. Indeed, unless he repents and carries our command in this matter into effect, we shall extend against him more severely the hands of Blessed Peter and our own.

Take courage, therefore, beloved daughters in the Lord, and amid temptations praise the Lord together with blessed Job. For it is written [Col. 0635C]: “The file proves iron, the furnace gold, and temptation proves the righteous.” Yet we hope in the Lord that by His grace He will provide you an issue together with the temptation and bring all evils to their desired end. We command and admonish our venerable brother Geoffrey, Bishop of Chartres, legate of the Apostolic See, to strive to help and support you both in this matter and in all others, and by every means according to God to labor for your peace and tranquillity. Those, moreover, who dared in sacrilegious fashion to demolish the houses of your witnesses and of others assisting you in the case—especially Bas. [Baslet], who came into our presence—to seize their possessions and goods, and to inflict many other losses and injuries, concerning which he has received their complaint, he shall strictly admonish to restore what they have taken and make reparation for the damage inflicted [Col. 0635D].

> **Note:** [Col. 0635D] The dispute concerned a certain small holding, according to the testimony of St. Bernard of Clairvaux, who in Letter 200 charges Ulger with the scandal arising from it: “How much is that cursed little holding worth, I ask, that it can any longer either obscure so manifest a truth or hinder so desired a correction?” And in Letter 340 to Pope Innocent: “Now broken by age, labors, and dangers, what breast would not be moved by the Bishop of Angers—unless it were that of one who has stripped himself of all compassion and every feeling of humanity? These considerations move me on behalf of that man, whose old age, if one deed alone be excepted, is rendered venerable both by his life and learning. Since we have not yet learned what has been concluded between him and the abbey, we presume to write nothing concerning a matter unknown to us. But if it is established that he has done what he promised, we believe that nothing remains except that he should be restored to the fullness of his favor and office.” Ulger nevertheless did not keep his promises, as we shall state in the letters of Pope Lucius II.

If, within forty days after his admonition, they scorn to comply and to prove themselves innocent in his presence in this matter, he shall pronounce sentence of excommunication upon them and ensure that it is firmly observed [Col. 0636A] until they make satisfaction. We pray that divine grace may preserve you and grant you perseverance in His holy service.

Given at the Lateran, on the Nones of July.

### DLXXVIII. To Peter the Venerable, Abbot of Cluny.—Confirmation of several churches in the Diocese of Troyes.  
*(A.D. 1140–1143, July 16.)*

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 415.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons PETER, abbot, and the monks of Cluny, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Those things which we know to have been reasonably granted to you and your brothers by bishops and rulers of God’s Churches out of regard for religion, we wish to preserve as our own and, by the authority of the Apostolic See in which we sit with the Lord presiding, to fortify so that they may be observed forever [Col. 0636B]. We therefore confirm and strengthen by the safeguard of this writing the grant made to your monastery and to you by our venerable brother Hatto, Bishop of Troyes, of the churches of St. Remigius, namely those of Plajotro, Bourbon, Lintis, Lintelles, and St. Silvester. Whoever knowingly attempts rashly to oppose this our confirmation shall know that he has incurred the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, the seventeenth day before the Kalends of August.

### DLXXIX. He writes to Samson, Archbishop of Reims, and Alvisus, Bishop of Arras, concerning Stephen, a fornicator and gambler.  
*(A.D. 1141–1143, March 10.)*

[BALUZ., *Miscellanies*, II, 165.]

[Col. 0636C]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers SAMSON, Archbishop of Reims, and ALVISUS, Bishop of Arras, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Although it is less blameworthy to acquit the guilty than to condemn the innocent, and although we wish to inflict injury on no one, nevertheless, because wickedness has increased among clerics as well as laypeople, discerning discipline must be applied. Therefore, if that Stephen concerning whom your brotherhood wrote to us appears to be a public fornicator and gambler [Col. 0636D], it pleases us that he be corrected so diligently that he himself may reform and others may not dare to commit the same enormity. But if he is innocent, he is not to be deprived of his ecclesiastical benefice.

Given at the Lateran, the sixth day before the Ides of March.

### DLXXX. To Henry [Humbert], Bishop of Autun.—He commends the monastery of Vézelay.  
*(A.D. 1141–1143.)*

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 402.]

[Col. 0637A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother H., Bishop of Autun, greeting and apostolic blessing.

As your brotherhood knows, the monastery of Vézelay, with all its appurtenances, belongs by right to Blessed Peter and pertains especially to his ownership and protection. You are therefore bound to defend and support that monastery and the brothers serving the Lord there, and to assist them in their needs. Accordingly, by these present letters [Col. 0637B] we command and strictly enjoin you not to presume in any way to oppress or harass our beloved P. [Pontius], the abbot, and his brothers; and, upon complaint received from them against any of your parishioners, to render them justice without delay. We furthermore restore to their offices and orders their clerics whom, it is said, you have suspended from orders contrary to the tenor of the privileges of the Apostolic See.

### DLXXXI. To William, Archbishop of Arles, Legate of the Apostolic See.—He orders the people of Montpellier, absolved by him but refusing to render justice to their lord, to be bound again by the bonds of excommunication.  
*(A.D. 1143, January 1.)*

[D. BOUQUET, *Recueil*, XV, 407.]

[Col. 0637C]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother WILLIAM, Archbishop of Arles, legate of the Apostolic See, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our beloved son William of Montpellier informed us by letter and messengers that the people of Montpellier, after sentence of excommunication had been pronounced against them and the place itself placed under interdict, offered into your hand to render justice to you, and confirmed this by oath, having provided pledges and sureties. On this basis, the sentence of excommunication having been relaxed, and a day and place having been appointed by your brotherhood for pursuing justice, they withdrew as faithless and perjured persons [Col. 0637D], and refused to render justice to their said lord. Since wrongdoing ought not to profit anyone, we command and strictly enjoin you by these present letters to renew the same sentence of excommunication against those called consuls of that place and against all known to be leaders in such great malice and wickedness; to place the place itself under interdict from the divine offices, except for the baptism of children and the penances of the dying; and strictly to compel your subjects to abstain from their communion and assistance. Those who are known to have sworn against the said lord, however, if they return without fraud to his fidelity and service, you shall absolve by our authority.

Given at the Lateran, on the Kalends of January.

### DLXXXII. To P[eter], Archbishop of Bourges.—He announces the excommunication of Stephen of Catiac, Rainald of Montfaucon, and their associates.  
*(A.D. 1143, January 10.)*

[RAYNAL, *History of Berry*, II, p. 529, from the charter collection of the monastery of St. Satyrius, p. 164.]

[Col. 0638A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother P[ETER], Archbishop of Bourges, and to his beloved sons the archdeacons and archpriests established throughout the territory of Bourges, obedient to Blessed Peter and ourselves, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The most grievous and devastating wickedness of arson has been forbidden in general councils by the authority of God and His blessed apostles Peter and Paul. No one is unaware how harmful it is to the people of God or how much injury it inflicts upon souls and bodies [Col. 0638B]. Therefore, in order to uproot so great an evil from God’s people, it has been decreed that, if anyone through evil intent, hatred, or vengeance sets a fire, causes one to be set, or knowingly gives counsel and aid to those setting it, he shall be excommunicated. If an arsonist dies, he shall be denied Christian burial; nor shall he be absolved unless he first makes compensation, according to his means, for the loss inflicted upon the person injured, swears that he will not set a fire again, and receives as penance the requirement to remain for one year at Jerusalem or in Spain in God’s service.

We therefore wish your whole body to know that we have pronounced sentence of excommunication against Stephen of Cratiac, Rainald of Montfaucon, and their other accomplices who sacrilegiously took part in the burning of the church and borough of St. Satyrius [Col. 0638C]. By these present letters we command and strictly enjoin you publicly to announce this same sentence throughout your parishes, firmly to observe it until they make satisfaction in the manner stated above, and likewise to ensure that it is observed by your subjects.

Given at the Lateran, the fourth day before the Ides of January.

### DLXXXIII. Privilege for the Monastery of St. Peter at Neustift.  
*(A.D. 1143, January 21.)*

[MEICHELBEK, *History of Freising*, p. 320.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons HERMANN, provost of the Church of St. Peter [Col. 0638D] of the New Place situated near the city of Freising, and his brothers, present and future, to be regularly appointed, forever.

It befits the clemency of apostolic governance to love religious persons and to fortify their places with pious protection. For it is recognized as worthy and consonant with propriety that we who have been raised to the governance of Churches should both protect them from the wickedness of evil persons and cherish them under the patronage of the Apostolic See. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and we take under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by this page of writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods you now justly and canonically possess [Col. 0639A], or may hereafter, by God’s favor, acquire through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Moreover, whatever our venerable brother Otto, Bishop of Freising, has granted you out of regard for religion and confirmed in his writing, we likewise confirm. We also establish that the canonical order, according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine and the institution of the brothers of Prémontré, shall be preserved inviolate forever in the same Church of Blessed Peter. During a general interdict of the city itself, you may celebrate the divine offices behind closed doors, excluding excommunicated and interdicted persons, without ringing bells and in a low voice [Col. 0639B]. No cleric or layperson whatsoever may presume to demand tithes from you for the produce of the labor which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or for the increase of your animals. We also grant that the burial-place of that church shall be free, so that none may obstruct the devotion and final wish of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated, the canonical right of the mother church being preserved.

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid Church, remove its possessions, retain things removed, diminish them, or harass it by any other vexations; but that all things granted for the governance and support of those for whose use they were given shall be preserved whole and be of benefit to them in every way. If anyone hereafter knowingly attempts rashly to act against this page of our constitution [Col. 0639C], and, having been warned a second or third time, does not correct his offence by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know that he is answerable before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject to strict vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve what is just for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action, and before the strict Judge find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. [Col. 0639D]  
I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed.  
I, Stephen, Bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed.  
I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of St. Nicholas in the Prison, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Gerard, cardinal priest and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of February, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1142 from the Incarnation of the Lord, and in the thirteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

### DLXXXIV. To the Canons of the Church of St. Fridianus at Lucca.  
*(A.D. 1143, February 9.)*

[BALUZ., *Miscellanies*, IV, 592.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 0640A] sons the canons of St. Fridianus, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We wish your charity to know that we received with due kindness our beloved son J., formerly your prior, when he came to us; and, as though by Blessed Peter’s own hands, in accordance with the petition of the clergy and people of the Church of Arezzo, we consecrated him bishop for them. Since grave losses commonly befall a flock without a pastor’s oversight, we exhort and command your whole body to be united and to have no schisms among you, but, after invoking the grace of the Holy Spirit, to elect as your father and prior a suitable, religious, and prudent person, through whose wisdom and diligence your church may, by the Lord’s favor [Col. 0640B], receive a welcome increase. For we have loved and do love you and your place with true charity in the Lord, and we desire, in all matters in which we can do so according to God, to support and aid you.

Given at the Lateran, the fifth day before the Ides of February.

### DLXXXV. Privilege for the Church of St. Mary of Reno.  
*(A.D. 1143, February 13.)*

[TROMBELLI, *Memoirs of St. Mary of Reno*, Appendix, p. 361.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GUIDO, prior of the Church of Blessed Mary of Reno, and his brothers, present and future, to be canonically appointed, forever.

The clemency of apostolic governance befits the loving of religious persons [Col. 0640C] and the strengthening of their communities by pious protection. For it is fitting, and is recognized as consonant with propriety, that we, who have been appointed to the governance of churches, should both defend them from the wickedness of evil persons and cherish them by the patronage of the Apostolic See. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we mercifully assent to your just requests, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid church in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the protection of this present document.

First, indeed, we decree that the canonical order according to the Rule of blessed Augustine be preserved there inviolate for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions and whatever goods you now possess justly and canonically [Col. 0640D], or may hereafter be able to acquire, God being gracious, through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. We further forbid any brother, after having made profession there, to dare to leave that cloister without the permission of the prior and of the whole congregation; and no one whatsoever shall receive one who departs without letters of authorization from the community. You shall have full liberty, without anyone’s objection, to receive for conversion clerics or free laymen living in the secular condition.

Moreover, concerning the produce of your labours, which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or concerning the increase of your animals, no cleric or layman whatsoever shall presume to exact tithes from you [Col. 0641A]. You shall receive holy oil, the consecration of altars or churches, and the ordination of clerics to be promoted to sacred orders from the diocesan bishop, provided that he is Catholic, possesses the favour and communion of the Apostolic See, and is willing to supply these things freely and without any improper exaction. Otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what is requested.

Upon the death of yourself, the present prior of that place, or of any one of your successors, no one shall be placed over it through any cunning of fraud or violence; rather, you may, by common counsel and equal consent, or by the counsel of the sounder part, in the fear of God and according to the Rule of blessed Augustine [Col. 0641B], elect a prior without anyone’s opposition. We also grant that the burial-place of that community shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and final wish of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated; the right of the mother church nevertheless being preserved.

Therefore we decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid church, or to take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all things shall be kept whole for the benefit, in every respect, of those for whose governance and support they were granted, the canonical right of the diocesan bishop nevertheless being preserved. If, therefore, in the future, any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it [Col. 0641C], after a second or third warning, unless he makes amends by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and office; let him know that he stands guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be separated from the most holy body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject, at the last judgment, to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good conduct and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.  
I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed.  
I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed.  
I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed.  
[Col. 0641D] I, Imar, bishop of Tusculum, have subscribed.  
I, Guido, unworthy priest of the Holy Roman Church, have subscribed.  
I, G.G., cardinal priest of the title of Calixtus, have subscribed.  
I, Rainerius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca, have subscribed.  
I, Goizo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia, have subscribed.  
I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed.  
I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.  
I, Humbald, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed.  
I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in Carcere, have subscribed.  
[Col. 0642A] I, Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Aquiro, have subscribed.  
I, Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Gerard, cardinal priest and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the Ides of February, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1142, indiction 11, in the thirteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## DLXXXVI. Privilege for the Church of Springiersbach.  
*(A.D. 1143, February 22.)*

[GUNTHER, *Codex diplomaticus Mosellensis*, I, 282.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons RICHARD, abbot of the Church of Springiersbach [Col. 0642B], and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

Whenever something is requested of us that is recognized as suited to religion and propriety, it is fitting that we grant it willingly and furnish suitable support to the petitioners’ desires. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, moved by the prayers of our venerable brother Albero, archbishop of Trier, we mercifully assent to your just requests. We confirm by apostolic authority, and strengthen by the page of this present document, the donation to you of the parochial church called Saint Peter’s on the Mountain, which is a mother church with five churches belonging to it in as many villages—namely Pünderich, Kaimt, Zell, Merl, and Krew—just as it was canonically made to you by the aforesaid our brother the archbishop, with the consent of his brethren [Col. 0642C], and confirmed by his document.

We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter be able to acquire, the Lord providing, through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Concerning the produce of your labours, which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or concerning the increase of your animals, no cleric or layman whatsoever shall presume to exact tithes from you.

Therefore we decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid church [Col. 0642D], or take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but all things shall be kept whole for the benefit, in every respect, of those for whose support and governance they were granted, the canonical right of the archbishop of Trier being preserved. If, therefore, in the future, any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, after a second or third warning, unless he makes amends by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power or office; let him know that he stands guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be separated from the most holy body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject at the last judgment to strict vengeance. [Col. 0643A] But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good conduct and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church.  
I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina.  
I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus.  
I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil.  
I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina.  
I, Imar, bishop of Tusculum.  
I, Geraud, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Dominio.  
[Col. 0643B] I, Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Agro.  
I, Guido, unworthy priest of the Holy Roman Church.  
I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Calixtus.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Gerard, cardinal priest and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the eighth day before the Kalends of March, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1143, in the fourteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## DLXXXVII. Privilege for the Monastery of Saint Columba at Sens.  
*(A.D. 1143, February 23.)*

[FLEUREAN, *Les antiquités d’Estampes*, p. 589.]

[Col. 0643C] INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons THEOBALD, abbot of the monastery of Saint Columba, situated in the suburb of Sens, and his brethren, present and future, to be appointed according to the rule: for perpetual remembrance.

It is fitting that we willingly grant a desire known to concern the religious purpose and the salvation of souls, and furnish suitable support to the petitioners’ wishes. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we mercifully assent to your just petitions; we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service; and we strengthen it by the protection of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods the same monastery now [Col. 0643D] justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter be able to acquire, God being gracious, through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these, we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The castle in which the monastery of Saint Columba was founded, and its boundaries from the Cross of Giraud as far as the crypts, entirely free from every customary due and exaction; the church of Saint Lupus of Sermasia, and the whole enclosure in which it was built; the chapel of Saint Mary of Cathiniac with its enclosure; the church of Saint Columba of Quadruvis; the church of Saint Benedict; the church of Saint Clement; the church of [Col. 0644A] Beiac; the church of the village of Patricius together with the church of Novavilla; the church of Grunno; the church of Cuisiac together with that at Euriac; the church of Saint Germanus; the church of Saint Lawrence together with the tithe of Pomerium; the church of Corlon; the church of Saint Martin of Sarmosia; the church of Closavilla; and the church of Maugeleart, with cemeteries, tithes, and their other appurtenances.

At [lacuna], an offering in the church of Saint Peter, on the feasts of that saint; in the church of Saint Stephen of Cathiniac, ten rent-paying solidi each year; the village of Sarmasia with all its appurtenances; the village of Grunni; the village of Patricius; the village of Misseriac with its meadows and pastures; the village of Cusiac; the village of Jovenciac; the village of Saint Germanus above the Orosa; the village called [Col. 0644B] Corloon; the land of Nangis with woods and its appurtenances; the lands of Bellomont above the Scauva, and beside the monks’ houses; and the enclosed property which you have on the summit of Braium Joviniacum and in their Castellanies. Five solidi in the mill of Clanesmeis; the land of Floriac; the lands of Broell with woods and men; the forest of the river Jeanna, from the place called Capetus as far as the village of Dulliac; from the wood of Saint Stephen adjoining the village of Nadiliac, two cartloads of wood every day; a plot within the city walls, from the canons’ cloister as far as the gate of Saint Desiderius, with all buildings situated in it.

The tithe beyond the bridge; free passage without toll for you and all yours through [lacuna]; the gift made by Eva, countess of Catiniac [Col. 0644C], with lands, woods, waters, and all appurtenances situated in the diocese of Troyes. The village of Regniac with the bridge of Saint Guinebaud; in the village of Moriniac, lands. The village of Sarmatia with its appurtenances, entirely free from every customary due and exaction.

Therefore we decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any molestations; but all things shall be kept whole for the benefit, in every respect, of those for whose governance and support they were granted, the canonical right of the diocesan bishop being preserved. If, therefore, in the future, any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it [Col. 0644D], after a second or third warning, unless he makes amends by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and office; let him know that he stands guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be separated from the body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject at the last judgment to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good conduct and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

SAINT PETER, ÷ SAINT PAUL.

I, Pope Innocent II.  
I, Boethius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement.  
[Col. 0645A] I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Chrysogonus.  
I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina.  
I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Sergius and Bacchus.  
I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia.  
I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina.  
I, Imar, bishop of Tusculum.  
I, Hubald, cardinal priest of Saint Praxedes.  
I, Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Domnica.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Gerard, cardinal priest and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Kalends of March, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1142, indiction 6, in the fourteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## DLXXXVIII. At the request of Conrad, Archbishop of Salzburg, he confirms the foundation of the Church of Seckau.  
*(A.D. 1143, March 12.)*

[PUSCH (Sigismund), *Diplomata sacra ducatus Styriae*, part I, p. 144.]

[Col. 0645B]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons WERNHER, provost of Seckau, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

Therefore, moved by the prayers of our venerable brother Chunrad, archbishop of Salzburg, we confirm by apostolic authority the transfer of your community from the place called Feistritz to the place called Seckau; and we receive that place with all its appurtenances under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, and strengthen it by the protection of this present document. [Col. 0645C] First, indeed, we decree that the canonical order according to the Rule of blessed Augustine shall be preserved there inviolate for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions and whatever goods you now justly possess, or may hereafter be able to acquire, God assisting, through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Upon the death of yourself, the present provost of that church, or of any one of your successors, no one shall be set over it through any cunning of fraud or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, in the fear of God and according to the Rule of blessed Augustine, shall judge ought to be elected. Therefore we decree [Col. 0645D] that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any other vexations; but that all things shall be kept whole for the benefit, in every respect, of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If, therefore, in the future, any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his offence by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and office; let him know that he stands guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be separated from the most holy body and blood of God and of Christ [Col. 0646A], our Redeemer; and let him be subject at the last judgment to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good conduct and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of [Gerard], etc., on the fourth day before the Ides of March, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1143, indiction 6, in the fourteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## DLXXXIX. To the Brethren of the Church of Saint Frigdianus at Lucca.  
*(A.D. 1143, March 13.)*

[BALUZE, *Miscellanea*, IV, 592.]

[Col. 0646B] INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons in the Lord, P., prior of Saint Frigdianus, and his brethren: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We rejoice and give thanks to almighty God, who makes people dwell in a house in unity, because, as you have informed us by letter and messenger, by common wish and equal consent you have elected a wise and honourable person as your prior. Therefore, by this present writing, we command, admonish, and exhort your entire community in the Lord to love and honour him as a father with special affection, and to render him, as the guardian of your souls, obedience and reverence devoutly and humbly.

You therefore, beloved son in the Lord, P., prior, should strive to administer the rule entrusted to you and the care of that church with such discretion and diligence [Col. 0646C] that the observance of the regular life may be preserved there for the honour of God and the salvation of souls, and that that church may increase, both temporally and spiritually, under your governance, the Lord granting it. For we wish to love with paternal affection your person and the church entrusted to you by God, and, according to God, to help and support it.

Given at the Lateran, on the third day before the Ides of March.

## DXC. Privilege for the Church of Saint Saviour at Casale.  
*(A.D. 1143, March 17.)*

[DE CONTI, *Notitie storiche di Casale*, I, p. 336.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son GIRARD, provost, and his brethren [Col. 0646D], present and future, living according to the rule in the church of Saint Evasio at Casale: in perpetuity.

A pious request should be brought to completion by the ensuing effect of the will, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth commendably and the requested benefit may undoubtedly acquire force. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, granting your petitions our favourable assent with due kindness, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid church, in which you are devoted to divine service, and, after the example of our predecessor of good memory Pope Calixtus, strengthen it by the protection of this present document.

First, indeed, we decree that the canonical order according to [Col. 0647A] the Rule of blessed Augustine be preserved there inviolate for all time; and we forbid anyone, after making profession, to hold property of his own or to leave the cloister without permission of the provost or congregation. Moreover, whatever possessions and whatever goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter be able to acquire, the Lord providing, through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these, we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

In Casale itself: the church of Saint Mary, and the church of Saint Stephen, with the hospital built there and all their appurtenances; [Col. 0647B] all churches situated in the district of Casale, with all appurtenances. At Paciliano: the church of Saint Germanus and the church of Saint Michael of Castagneto. In the place of Saint George: the churches of Saint Martin, Saint Mary, Saint Hilary, Saint Vitalis, and Saint Peter. At Cinagium: the church of Saints Cosmas and Damian, with four manses and the whole tithe of the entire place. At Rodolasco: the church of Saint Michael with its appurtenances. At Torcello: the churches of Saint Clement and Saint Nicholas. In Casale: three manses of land which you cultivate with your own oxen; six jugera of vineyard for your own labour; the holding of Brisca; the holding of Framinia; the holding of Officianus; the holding of Ambrose of Ticino; the holding of the sons of Gisi; the holding of Hilary; the holding of Adam of Lugano; the holding of Spatea Caldaria; the holding of Henry Scinea; the holding [Col. 0647C] of Setaciarius; the holding of Casatexta; the holding of Obert Risulianus; the holding of Quiricus Baldea; the holding of Rodulfus Qualea; together with first-fruits and a third of the tithes of the entire place of Casale; the whole tithe of the lands of the household of Saint Evasio; and the whole tithe of the Braidae of the bishop. The village of Luventino with tithes and all its appurtenances. At Saint Gregory: thirteen manses; a sixteenth part of Torcello with all appurtenances. At Monteclo: three manses; at Mirabello: five manses. In the dependency of the cell: seven manses; at Sannatia: five manses; at Paciliano: five manses; in the village of Borrani: one manse; at Luno: one manse; at Agelio: one manse; at Ozano: one manse; at Occimiano: one manse; at Frassinetto: one and a half manses.

Furthermore, we wholly forbid [Col. 0647D] any knight or any secular person whatsoever to presume to take tithes from the goods of that church or from the peasants belonging to the parishes of that church; rather, in accordance with the canonical sanctions, they shall be assigned for the use of you or of your church. Moreover, no bishop or provost shall hinder you from receiving for conversion secular clerics under your provost. You shall receive chrism, holy oil, the consecration of altars or churches, and the ordination of clerics who are to be promoted to sacred orders from the diocesan bishop, provided he is Catholic, possesses the favour and communion of the Apostolic See, and is willing to provide these things freely [Col. 0648A] and without any improper exaction. Otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what is requested.

Upon the death of yourself, the present provost of that place, or of any one of your successors, no one shall be placed over it through any cunning of fraud or violence; rather, you may, by common counsel or by the sounder part of the counsel, in the fear of God and according to the Rule of blessed Augustine, elect a provost without anyone’s opposition. Therefore we decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid church, invade the houses of your cloister, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations. Nor shall any provost have authority to grant the church’s estates in fief to secular persons [Col. 0648B], or alienate them by any contrivance. Rather, all things shall be kept whole for the benefit, in every respect, of those for whose governance and support they were granted, the canonical right and reverence due to the diocesan bishop being preserved.

If, therefore, in the future, any ecclesiastical or secular person whatsoever, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, after a second or third warning, unless he makes amends by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and office; let him know that he stands guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be separated from the most holy body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject, at the last judgment, to strict vengeance [Col. 0648C]. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good conduct and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church.

I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Gerard, cardinal priest and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of April, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1142.

## DXCI. Privilege for the Monastery of Saint Martin of the Fields.  
*(Fragment.—A.D. 1143, March 23.)*

[*Bibliotheca Cluniacensis*, col. 603.]

[Col. 0648D] INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ THEOBALD, prior of the monastery of Saint Martin of the Fields, and his successors, etc.

[lacuna] Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Theobald, prior, assenting to your petitions, we strengthen by the authority of this decree the monastery of Saint Martin, over which, by the Lord’s appointment, you preside under the institution of our venerable brother Peter, abbot of Cluny, etc.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Gerard, cardinal priest and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the tenth day before the Kalends of April, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1141, indiction 6, in the fourteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## DXCII. Privilege for Weingarten Abbey.  
*(A.D. 1143, April 9.)*

[HESS, *Prodromus Monum. Guelf.*, p. 52.]

[Col. 0649A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GEBEHARD, abbot of Weingarten Monastery, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

It is fitting to grant ready assent to religious desires, so that the devotion of the faithful may obtain a swift result. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, favourably assenting to your petitions, we receive under the right and protection of the chief of the apostles, and strengthen by the patronage of the Apostolic See, the aforesaid monastery [Col. 0649B], which was offered to blessed Peter by the illustrious man of good memory, Welf, founder of that place, following the example of our predecessors Urban and Paschal, pontiffs of Rome of blessed memory. We decree that whatever goods and whatever possessions the aforesaid monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter be able to acquire, the Lord providing, through grants of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other reasonable means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Therefore we decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the same monastery [Col. 0649C], or take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any other vexations; but all things shall be kept whole for the benefit, in every respect, of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If, therefore, in the future, any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his offence by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and office; let him know that he stands guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be separated from the most holy body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject at the last judgment to strict vengeance. But upon all [Col. 0649D] who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good conduct and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Innocent, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Gerard, cardinal priest and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Ides of April, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1143, indiction 6, in the fourteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## DXCIII. To Conrad, Archbishop of Salzburg—Ordering him to restore Ulrich and his daughter, with certain estates, from the monks of Admont to Benediktbeuern Monastery.  
*(A.D. 1143, April 12.)*

[MEICHELBECK, *Chronicon Benedictoburanum*, p. 92.]

[Col. 0650A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to CONRAD, archbishop of Salzburg: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We wish your brotherhood to know that the brethren of the monastery of Beuern have complained by letter and messenger that a certain nobleman, named Ulrich, vowed and offered himself and his only daughter, together with their estates, to God in their monastery, in your presence and in that of our venerable brother Hildebold, bishop of Gurk [Col. 0650B]. Afterwards, when persecution came upon that place, the aforesaid Ulrich, taking his daughter and fleeing the persecution, transferred himself to Admont Monastery in your diocese; and there he presumed, altogether unlawfully, to offer his daughter with the estates.

Therefore, by this present writing, we direct and, in directing, command you: if you establish that the matter is so, cause Ulrich himself and his daughter, with the estates offered, to be restored in their entirety to the aforesaid brethren of Beuern. For he had no authority, without the permission of the abbot and the whole congregation, to transfer or offer to another monastery what he had offered to God in that monastery.

Given at the Lateran, on the fourth day before the Ides of April.

## DXCIV. Privilege for the Monastery of Saint Mary of Castiglione.  
*(A.D. 1143, April 13.)*

[AFFO, *Storia della cittadi Parma*, Appendix II, p. 352, from the Vatican Archive.]

[Col. 0650C]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ALBERT, abbot of the monastery of Saint Mary of Castiglione, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

It is fitting that we willingly grant a desire known to concern the religious purpose and the salvation of souls, and furnish suitable support to the petitioners’ desires. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we mercifully assent to your just requests [Col. 0650D]; and, because the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, belongs by right to blessed Peter, we receive it under the right and protection of that chief of the apostles, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods the same monastery justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter be able to acquire, the Lord providing, through grants of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these, we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The church of Saint Saviour of the duke’s basilica, with all its appurtenances; the church of Saint Remigius of Palude; the church of Saint Eusebius of Grani; the cell of Saint Benedict [Col. 0651A] of Guasco, with all its appurtenances; the church of Saint Mary of Charity, situated in the suburb of Mantua; the church of the castle of Zuoni; the church of Tassarolo; whatever you possess in the counties of Luni and Genoa; in the county of Modena, in the place called Solaria and Erbaria; and in the abbey of Saint Mary of Corsica called Pladellu, with all its appurtenances; and in the court called Marrairegia, in the court of Rupta, in Castelnuovo, in the estate of Albini, and of Saint Andrew.

Upon the death of yourself, the present abbot of that place, or of any one of your successors, no one shall be placed over it through any cunning of fraud or violence, except one whom the brethren, by common consent or by the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, shall elect in the fear of God and according to the Rule of blessed Benedict; and the person elected shall be blessed by the Roman pontiff. [Col. 0651B] You shall receive chrism, holy oil, the consecration of altars or churches, and the ordination of your monks or canons to be promoted to sacred orders from whichever Catholic bishops you prefer. We forbid any bishop, without the abbot’s consent, to celebrate public masses in the same monastery, or to hold any station, synod, or ordination there; and thus we decree that your monastery shall remain free from every yoke or jurisdiction of any person.

Therefore we decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those otherwise taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but all things shall be kept whole [Col. 0651C] for the benefit, in every respect, of those for whose support and governance they were granted. If, therefore, in the future, any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, after a second or third warning, unless he makes amends by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and office; let him know that he stands guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be separated from the most holy body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject at the last judgment to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good [Col. 0651D] conduct and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Gerard, cardinal priest and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the Ides of April, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1143, indiction 6, in the fourteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## DXCV. Privilege for the Canonry of Saint Peter at Faenza.  
*(A.D. 1143, April 26.)*

[TONDUZZI, *History of Faenza*, p. 186.]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the canons of the Church of Faenza: Farolf [Col. 0652A], archdeacon; Peter, archpriest; and their brethren, present and future, canonically appointed: in perpetuity.

The effect ought to follow a pious request, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth commendably and the benefit sought may undoubtedly acquire strength. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, graciously granting due and favorable assent to your just petitions, we take under the protection of the same prince of the apostles and of ourselves the church of Blessed Peter the Apostle, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the safeguard of this present privilege. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the aforesaid church now holds by any right whatsoever, or may hereafter, by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, obtain through the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and inviolate for you and your successors. We have judged that these should be expressly named: the parish church of Saint Peter in Lacuna, with all its appurtenances; half of the parish church of Saint Andrew in Panigale, with all its appurtenances; the church of Saint Christopher the Martyr outside the castle of Quartuli; the church of Saint Andrew in Casanaula; the church of Saint Mary in Merlasco; moreover, Greater and Lesser Arcuatum, Greater and Lesser Fermelinum with their appurtenances—namely Fabriati Murena, adjoining them together with the Greater Field, and Taulis of Villanova; two holdings (*mansi*) in Cicutino, four in Cicutino, four in Pegulino, two in Morino; the place called Gargugnanus; the place called Curilianus; the place called Mons; the place called Tistitus; two holdings in Varano; whatever you possess in Fuscarino, Pigna, and Pitriolo, and in any places, villages, estates, lands, waters, or watercourses.

[Col. 0652C] We also establish for you and your successors forever the ancient customs, honors, and dignities of your church: those in tithes, first-fruits, wills, offerings of both living persons and the dead, the anciently customary processions and payments of the parish churches of your bishopric, and all dues, prebends, or revenues, just as you or your successors, by the ancient usage of your church, held and possessed them from the day of the death of Paul, the venerable bishop of the same church of blessed memory, until the time of James, his successor. We confirm by the authority of the apostolic see forever to your church alone and to its priests the oil for the sick and their anointings throughout your entire parish district; and, under threat of deprivation of office and excommunication, we command that none of the chaplains retain it for himself or administer it without the permission of the mother church.

[Col. 0652D] We further command that an archdeacon and archpriest shall always be appointed canonically in your church; and whatever is granted to them by the authority of the sacred canons, we confirm by the authority of this present privilege.

[Col. 0653A] We establish as valid, and order to be preserved inviolate for you and your successors, those charitable allowances of food which you have customarily received from the monastery of Saint Mary Outside the Gate and the monastery of Saint Hippolytus, or from your bishop at the Nativity of the Lord and at the Resurrection, whether you have made the customary processions to the said monasteries or, through an excusable impediment, omitted them.

[Col. 0653A] We also grant that burial in your aforesaid church shall be wholly free. No one shall have authority, without your permission, to receive the bodies of those who have decided to be buried there, or of those known to belong to your cemetery through the customary burial-right of kinship or family, unless perhaps, while still living, they have undertaken some religious vocation. If anyone, whether layman or cleric, should rashly presume to receive or bury such persons, he shall be subject to ecclesiastical punishment until he has made fitting satisfaction; and no one shall presume to celebrate the funeral rites for those deceased persons.

[Col. 0653B] Moreover, we decree that, without the consent of you or your successors, no new church or oratory shall be built or consecrated within the boundaries of the bishopric of Faenza. If one should nevertheless be built or consecrated, you shall, by apostolic authority, forbid the celebration of divine offices therein. Nor may any archpriest or bishop despoil any cleric of the mother church of his office or benefice without canonical judgment. We have also judged it right to add by this present decree that you and your successors shall enjoy complete immunity from every imposition of tribute, in ecclesiastical as well as secular matters, in common affairs as well as private ones.

[Col. 0653C] Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, remove its possessions, retain those removed, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; rather, all shall be preserved intact for the benefit in every respect of those for whose support and governance they have been granted. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing the tenor of this decree, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, after a second or third warning, fail to correct the offense by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honor, acknowledge himself or herself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed,

[Col. 0653D] be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer, and be subject at the last judgment to the severe vengeance of the supreme Judge. But upon all who preserve inviolate the things confirmed by this present privilege may there be the peace and grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Gerard, priest-cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the sixth day before the Kalends of May, in the year 1143 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the fourteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent II.

## DXCVI. Privilege for the Church of Saint Lawrence, Florence.  
*(A.D. 1143, May 1.)*

[LAMI, *Ecclesiae Florent. Monum.*, III, 1779.]

[Col. 0654A]

INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons PETER, prior of Saint Lawrence in the city of Florence, and his brethren, both present and future, forever.

The principle of equity and justice urges us to confer upon churches perpetual stability and safeguards of unshaken strength. For it is not fitting that clerics called to the Lord’s portion should be harassed by the perverse troubles of evil men and wearied by anyone’s rash vexations.
