In this month is the Nativity of Saint Mary, which is celebrated with the greatest solemnity by the pontiff at Saint Adrian’s, where the collect is held, as at the Purification and Annunciation of Saint Mary.

74. On the Exaltation of the Holy Cross, the station is at the Lateran. The collect is held at Saint Mary Major, where the stational cross, the school, regional clergy, and acolytes assemble with the cross of Saint John and its canons, and with the cross of Saint Mary and its canons. The *primicerius* with [Col. 0760B] the school sings the collect; the regional subdeacon bears the stational cross before the singers, and they proceed in procession to the Lateran. The *primicerius* with the school first sings the antiphon, “But it is fitting that we glory.” Then the canons of Saint Mary, arriving at the field beside the Fullery, await there with all the people the pontiff and the holy objects from the palace.

> [Note: [Col. 0760D] That is, the relics, as is understood from what follows. In two manuscripts these words, “and the holy objects from the palace,” are likewise absent.]

The pontiff, vested and barefoot, descends from the palace with the other orders. In the procession the cardinals carry holy objects—namely, wood of the Lord’s cross, the sandals of Jesus Christ, and his circumcision—to the basilica of the Savior, where the station is held. There the pontiff sings Mass; when it has been sung, all depart joyfully with the blessing.

75. On the first Sunday of October the book [Col. 0760C] of Maccabees is appointed until the first Sunday of November. In the middle of October, on the following Sundays at morning praises, when “Bless, all works of the Lord, the Lord” is said, these antiphons are sung: “While they endure,” “I see three men,” and the others found in the Antiphonary. On the first Sunday of November Daniel the prophet is appointed and is read on Sundays until the Advent of the Lord. During the weeks Ezekiel and the Twelve Prophets are read.

76. On the feast of Saint Andrew, the lord pontiff with all the schools must be at Saint Andrew’s in the Vatican, and there solemnly celebrate Vespers and Vigils, as on the feast of Saint Peter. [Col. 0760D] But he is to perform Matins at his brother’s [church], that is, at the altar of Saint Peter. In the morning Mass is sung over the altar of blessed Andrew, so that all the people may depart joyfully with the blessing. The prefect, with the assistance of the tenth, illuminates the church and provides a meal for the curia. Thanks be to God.

### Addition from the Vallicellian codex

These are the feasts on which the lord pontiff must be crowned: namely, on the feast of the Holy Four Crowned Martyrs; on the feast of Saint Martin, where the title of Equitius is said; on the feast of Saint Clement; on Advent Sunday; on the Sunday of [Col. 0761A] Jerusalem; on Gaudete Sunday; on the feast of the Lord; on the feast of Saint Stephen; on Epiphany; on Laetare Jerusalem Sunday; at Easter; on Monday at Saint Peter’s; on the Sunday “I am the Good Shepherd”; at the Ascension; at Pentecost; on the feast of Saint Peter; on his anniversary; and on the feast of Saint Sylvester.

These are the nocturnal stations of Saint Peter: Gaudete Sunday, Epiphany, the Ascension of the Lord, Pentecost, the feast of Saint Peter and its octave, and the feast of Saint Andrew. At each of these stations, the schools of the palace—namely, the cardinals, deacons, subdeacons, regional singers, and acolytes—must receive five solidi of denarii from the altar of Saint Peter for the supper allowance; the archdeacon, eighteen denarii; for those who sing, [Col. 0761B] sixty [denarii]; the canons, twelve solidi; and, at Mass, one half of the altar revenue between them and the chaplains of the lord pope [Col. 0762A] until the end. If the lord pontiff is absent and a cardinal alone comes to sing Mass, the aforesaid schools receive the whole half of the altar revenue at whatever station it may be. The cardinal who sings Mass receives a third part of the offering; but if he has another cardinal as companion, this is not done: rather, the offering, as customary, is divided jointly among the schools.

These are the daytime stations of Saint Peter: on all Ember Saturdays; on Quinquagesima Sunday; Passion Sunday; Monday after Easter; the Sunday “I am the Good Shepherd”; at the Greater Litanies; on the Dedication; and on the Chair of Saint Peter. At each of these stations they receive five solidi and the offering. But the lord pontiff receives twenty solidi at the nocturnal stations, [Col. 0762B] when the hanging lamps are lit; and at the daytime stations, when the candles are lit.

> [Note: [Col. 0761] They call it by another name *pharum*, that is, a circular lamp with a fixed number of lamps or candles.]

[Col. 0761]

## APPENDIX

Diploma of Pope John XIX—

> [Note: [Col. 0761] For us, John XX, whose third year coincides with the year 1026, the third indiction having begun in September.]

—by which he grants the bishop of Silva Candida authority to celebrate divine offices on specified days in the church of Saint Peter in the Vatican.

**JOHN**, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son **PETER**, by the grace of God bishop of the Church of Silva Candida, and through you to that same venerable bishopric and to your successors forever.

“It is fitting for apostolic governance . . .” It is extant among the letters and diplomas of John XIX, *Patrologia*, vol. CXLI, col. 1125, no. 4.

## IN THE YEAR OF THE LORD 1144. CELESTINE II, ROMAN PONTIFF

[Col. 0761]

## HISTORICAL NOTICE

*(MANSI, Councils, vol. XXI, col. 591.)*

[Col. 0761C] Celestine II, a Tuscan by nation, formerly called Guido, formerly cardinal priest of the title of Saint Mark, was, according to the constitution of his predecessor Innocent, by which the people were altogether excluded from the election of the pontiff, the first, according to the testimony of Onuphrius, to be created pontiff without any votes of the people, because of the civil war threatening from the Romans, who were striving to restore the senate. He was created [Col. 0762C] pontiff in the time of Emperor Conrad, in the year of the Lord 1143, on the day when Innocent II had departed this life. Peter, abbot of Cluny, wrote him a letter, extant in Papirius Masson, which states that, having been lawfully elected, at the beginning of his pontificate he found all things peaceful at Rome. William, treasurer of the church of York, [Col. 0763A] a man then of bad character, twice intruded into the see of York, condemned and expelled by Innocent, he ordained and consecrated bishop of the church of York by fraud; and, when Saint Bernard made grave complaint concerning this matter, he defended him. Having held the pontificate, according to Ursperg, for five months and thirteen days, and according to Otto of Freising for almost six months, he died [Col. 0764A] in the year of the Lord 1144 and was buried at Rome in the Constantinian basilica. The Vatican codex on the Lives of the Pontiffs has the following:

> “He held an ordination during the month of December, in which he created seven deacons, priests in various places, and bishops in various places . . . . He died at the Palladium on the eighth day before the Ides of March, and was buried in the Lateran church.”

[Col. 0763]

## DIPLOMATIC NOTICE

*(Philipp JAFFÉ, Registers of the Roman Pontiffs, p. 605.)*

+ Celestine II employed this motto: **“May peace be in thy strength and abundance in thy towers”** (5, 8, 10, 26, 27, 30, 32, 37, 39).

Bishop of Santa Rufina: Theodwin, from 26 Nov. 1143 to 24 Feb. 1144. Bishop of Sabina: Conrad, from 19 Oct. 1143 to 6 Mar. 1144. Bishop of Tusculum: Imar, from 23 Dec. 1143 to 6 Mar. 1144. Cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia: Aribert, from 12 Feb. 1144 to 26 Feb. 1144. Cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia: Goizo, from 30 Dec. 1143 to 6 Mar. 1144. Cardinal priest of the title of Saint Callistus: Gregory, from 19 Oct. 1143 to 19 Feb. 1144. Cardinal priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus: Guido, from 9 Dec. 1143 to 6 Mar. 1144. Cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cyriacus: Nicholas, from 23 Dec. 1143 to 6 Mar. 1144. Cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul: Hubald, from 23 Dec. 1143 to 19 Feb. 1144. Cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Damaso: Guido, from 10 Jan. 1144 to 26 Feb. 1144. Cardinal priest of the title of Saint Mark: Gilibert, from 23 Dec. 1143 to 23 Feb. 1144. Cardinal priest of the title of Saint Pastor: Peter, from 9 Dec. 1143 to 10 Jan. 1144. Cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes: Hubald, from 1 Dec. 1143 to 6 Mar. 1144. Cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca: Rainerius, from 22 Nov. 1143 to 6 Mar. 1144. Cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina: Manfred, from 10 Jan. 1144 to 6 Mar. 1144. Cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill: Rainerius, from 23 Dec. 1143 to 19 Feb. 1144. Cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna: Peter, from 19 Oct. 1143 to 24 Feb. 1144. Cardinal priest of the title of Saint Vestina: Thomas, from 19 Oct. 1143 to 6 Mar. 1144. Cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian: John Paparo, from 19 Feb. 1144 to 6 Mar. 1144. Cardinal deacon of Saint Angel: Gregory, from 30 Dec. 1143 to 19 Feb. 1144. Cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian: Guido, from 17 Feb. 1144 to 6 Mar. 1144. Cardinal deacon of Saint Eustace near the temple of Agrippa: Astald, from 10 Jan. 1144 to 24 Feb. 1144. Cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil: Otto, from 19 Oct. 1143 to 24 Feb. 1144. Cardinal deacon of Saint Lucy in the Septizodium: Rodolph, from 10 Jan. 1144 to 26 Feb. 1144. Cardinal deacon of Saint Lucy in Orphea: Hugh, on 19 Feb. 1144. Cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Aquiro: Peter, from 9 Dec. 1143 to 19 Feb. 1144. Cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Dominica: Gerard, from 1 Dec. 1143 to 6 Mar. 1144. Cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico: Peter, from 19 Oct. 1143 to 19 Feb. 1144. Cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata: Ubald, from 19 Oct. 1143 to 9 Dec. 1143. Cardinal deacon of Saint Mary the New: John, from 10 Jan. 1144 to 6 Mar. 1144. Cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison: Octavian, from 23 Nov. 1143 to 19 Feb. 1144. Cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus: Gregory, from 19 Oct. 1143 to 19 Feb. 1144.

Guido, altar minister in the Roman Church, on 17 and 24 Feb. 1144.

The bulls were issued through the hand of Gerard, cardinal priest and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, from 19 Oct. 1143 to 6 Mar. 1144.

[Col. 0765]

# LETTERS AND PRIVILEGES OF CELESTINE II, ROMAN PONTIFF

## I. Privilege for the Church of Saint Marianus of Gubbio  
*(Year 1143, 19 October.)*

*[UGHELLI, Sacred Italy, I, 637.]*

[Col. 0765A]

**CELESTINE**, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons **BENEDICT**, provost, and his brethren serving the Lord in the church of the episcopal see of Blessed Marianus in the city of Gubbio, both present and future, forever.

It is fitting that we readily grant a desire shown to concern the religious purpose and the salvation of souls, and afford suitable support to the requests of petitioners. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we mercifully grant assent to your requests and strengthen by the document of apostolic privilege the church of Blessed Marianus, [Col. 0765B] in which you are devoted to divine service. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that place now possesses canonically, or may hereafter acquire, by grant of pontiffs, gift of kings or princes, offering of the faithful, or other just means, by the Lord’s provision, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you forever. Among these we have thought fit to state expressly: the parish church of Saint John of Civitate; the parish church of Saint Mary Serrata; the parish church of Fisciano; the parish church of Saint Mary of Glodiano with the parish church of Saint Donatus and Saint Virianus; the parish church of Saint Gervasius; the estate of Lavari, with all the other churches and goods belonging to the aforesaid church; the chapel of Saint Bartholomew; the chapel [Col. 0765C] of the Holy Cross; the chapel of Saint Verecundus; the chapel of Saint Angel; the chapel of Saint George; the chapel of Saint Sabinus; the chapel of Saint Angel; the chapel of Saint Christopher; the chapel of the Savior; the chapel of Saint Mary of Mediano; the chapel of Saint Bartholomew of Castro Venale; the chapel of Saint Mary and the chapel of Saint George of Cortiva; the chapel of Saint Mary; the chapel of Saint Margaret with all their appurtenances; the castle of Mount Julian with its estate; the castle of Galgata with its estate; the castle of the valley of Marcula with its estate; the castle of Algnanir; and the castle of Agelli.

We further prohibit anyone, within the ancient boundaries of the greater or baptismal church, from presuming to build a church without your permission, or from demanding tithes or offerings from people dwelling within those same boundaries, or compelling them to transfer for burial [Col. 0765D] elsewhere. Rather, according to the Apostle, since you sow spiritual things for them, you may reap their temporal things with no one hindering you. We also grant you free authority to receive clerics or free lay persons [Col. 0766A] who wish to convert from secular dress and live religiously in your church. We decree also that burial in that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and final wish of those who decide to be buried there, unless they happen to be excommunicated, without prejudice to the right of the mother church. We therefore decree, etc. Amen.

Place + of the seal.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Callistus. I, Thomas, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna. [Col. 0766B] I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, . . . Bald, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Nicholas, deacon of the Holy Roman Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Gerard, cardinal priest and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of November, indiction VII, in the year 1143 of the Incarnation of the Lord, in the first year of the pontificate of the lord Pope Celestine.

## II. He informs the Cluniacs of his election and requests their prayers. He remits to them the offense of the bishop of Clermont.  
*(Year 1143, 6 November.)*

*[MANSI, Councils, XXI, 592.]*

[Col. 0766C]

**CELESTINE**, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons **PETER**, abbot, and the monks of Cluny: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Recognizing that your charity is concerned for the state of the holy Roman Church, your mother, we have taken care to make known to you what has happened concerning us. We therefore make known to your love that, after our lord Pope Innocent of blessed memory died on the eighth day before the Kalends of October and was buried in the Lateran church amid a very great gathering of the Roman clergy and people, the cardinal priests and deacons, together with our brethren the bishops and subdeacons, while the Roman clergy and people acclaimed, and in part requested it, on the third day in that same church, by unanimous vote and equal consent, [Col. 0766D] concordantly elected me, unworthy and altogether unequal to so great an office, by some judgment of God unknown to me, as Roman pontiff.

But I, considering [Col. 0767A] that my weakness could not attain to the height of the apostolic see, preferred to decline this burden, lest I should collapse in the pastoral government through an administration unequal to it. Yet because it is not possible to resist the judgment of the Lord who ordains, I obediently followed what the merciful hand governing me willed to accomplish concerning me. Therefore, submitting my neck to the disposition of the divine counsel, I recognize myself to be pressed by so great a weight that I may say, not in the spirit of prophecy but from experience: “I am bent down and humbled utterly” (Psalm CXVIII [119]). For burdens of business weigh me down so greatly that my mind can scarcely at times be raised to heavenly things. I am tossed by many waves of affairs; and, after the leisure of peace which I remember having before this office, I am afflicted by such storms of a tumultuous life [Col. 0767B] that I may rightly say: “I came into the depth of the sea, and the tempest has overwhelmed me” (Psalm LXVIII [69]).

Therefore, dearest brothers—

> [Note: [Col. 0767D] The pontiff ought to have said, “dearest sons.” HARD.]

—I beseech you through the almighty Lord to assist me, as I grow weary beneath this burden of pastoral care, by the intercessions of your prayers; that with all effort and full desire you may implore the mercy of that same almighty God, so that, as I labor amid the waves of the sea, he may stretch forth to me the right hand of his majesty and grant that I may so preside over his little ship that, with the burden of the ship entrusted to me, under his guidance I may reach the harbor of eternal rest.

For our part, we wish to love and cherish the monastery of Cluny as the special possession of Blessed Peter, in the manner of our predecessors, and to preserve its rights for it.

[Col. 0767C] As for the bishop of Clermont, who, having been summoned by our predecessor Pope Innocent of good memory for the recent feast of Blessed Luke, did not come and offered no canonical excuse: for love of you we bear this patiently for the present.

Given at the Lateran, on the eighth day before the Ides of November.

## III. To Alvisus, bishop of Arras. He reserves to himself a certain marriage case.  
*(Year 1143, 6 November.)*

*[MANSI, ibid., col. 595.]*

**CELESTINE**, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable [Col. 0767D] brother **ALVISUS**, bishop of Arras: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have received the letters sent by your brotherhood and have carefully considered what they contained concerning the consanguinity between the son of our most beloved son Stephen, illustrious count of Blois, and the daughter of the noble man Theodoric, count of Flanders. But because we find the bishops of Gaul lukewarm in justice and in observing the commands of the apostolic see, and because that same our son, Count . . . [lacuna] was treated by them altogether disorderly and contrary to justice in the matrimonial case of R. of Péronne, we have thought it right to reserve the case itself for the judgment of the apostolic see. [Col. 0768A] But if you yourself, or anyone else, should wish to proceed canonically in the case, present yourselves before us on the next Sunday, on which is sung, “These are the days,” etc., so that, in the presence of both parties, we may carefully investigate the case and determine concerning it what canonical equity shall prescribe.

Given at the Lateran, on the eighth day before the Ides of November.

## IV. To A., provost, and the canons of Rosate.  
*(Year 1143, 6 November.)*

*[GIULINI, Memoirs of the History of Milan, vol. V, p. 578.]*

**CELESTINE**, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons A., provost, and the canons of Rosate, [Col. 0768B] greeting and apostolic blessing.

It has been established by the apostolic see that religious persons are not to be compelled to pay tithes from the produce which they cultivate with their own hands or at their own expense, or from the sustenance of their animals. Yet a complaint has reached our ears to the contrary: that you demand tithes from the nuns of Saint Mary of Montano and extort them from them by force. Since, therefore, no one may depart from what is established by the apostolic see without danger to his own standing, we command you by this present writing not to presume in any way to exact tithes from those same nuns; but if you believe that you have any right there, show it in our presence.

[Col. 0768C] Given at the Lateran, on the eighth day before the Ides of November.

## V. Privilege confirming the church of Saint John of Monza.  
*(Year 1143, 23 November.)*

*[FRIZI, Historical Memoirs of Monza, vol. II, p. 56.]*

**CELESTINE**, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons in Christ **UBRANDUS**, archpriest of Monza, and his brethren, both present and those to be canonically appointed in the future, forever.

A devout petition ought to be brought to completion with a corresponding effect, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth commendably and the benefit sought may acquire unquestioned force. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, [Col. 0768D] we graciously assent to your just requests; and, following the example of our predecessors of blessed memory, Calixtus and Innocent, Roman pontiffs, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and fortify by the privilege of this present document, the church of Blessed John at Monza, in which you are devoted to divine service. We decree that whatever possessions or goods that same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s bounty, shall remain secure and unimpaired.

Among these we have thought fit to specify in their own terms [Col. 0769A]: namely, the church itself of Saint John the Baptist with all its chapels, etc.; the church of Saint John of Varena; of Saint Mary of Sara; of Saint Peter of Sirone; etc.; at Coliate, the church of Saint Carpophorus, etc.; of Saint Mary of Teneblaco and Saint Mary of Sundri; likewise, confirmation of the election of the abbess of Cremella, as it was reasonably granted to you and confirmed by his document by our venerable brother Robald, archbishop of Milan. We likewise confirm to you the right and reasonable customs which you possess in the same church of Saint Peter of Remella. Moreover, by apostolic authority we confirm to you and your successors those feudal benefices which our venerable brother Jordan, archbishop of Milan, granted to your church in the aforementioned churches for the common support of the brethren. We further prohibit anyone within your parish from presuming to build a church or chapel without your consent, without prejudice to the authority of the Roman pontiff, etc.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make suitable amends by adequate satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour; let that person know that he or she stands guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let that person be excluded from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and at the last judgment let that person be subject to severe vengeance. [Col. 0769C] But upon all who preserve the just rights of your church may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.

In the circle:

**MAY THERE BE PEACE IN YOUR STRENGTH, AND ABUNDANCE IN YOUR TOWERS.**

In the monogram:

Fare well.

I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, [Col. 0769D] have subscribed. I, Thomas, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina, have subscribed. I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in Carcere, have subscribed. I, Rainerius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Gerard, cardinal priest and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the ninth day before the Kalends of December, in the seventh indiction, in the year 1143 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Celestine II.

## VI. Privilege for the church of Oberzell near Würzburg. (1143, 24 November.)

[HUGO, *Annals of Prémontré*, I, Preface, p. 385.]

[Col. 0770A]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons CONRAD, provost of Zell, and his brethren, present and future, regularly appointed, in perpetuity.

A devout petition ought to be brought to completion with a corresponding effect, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth commendably and the benefit sought may acquire unquestioned force. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests and receive the aforesaid place, in which you are devoted to divine service, [Col. 0770B] under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and fortify it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions or goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter acquire by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, by God’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors.

We further enact that the canonical order, according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine and the institution of the brethren of Prémontré, shall be preserved there inviolate for all time. Nor may any brother, after making profession, leave that cloister without the permission of the provost and the whole congregation; and no one shall dare to retain a departing brother without a letter of assurance from the community. We also confirm the exchange which you reasonably made with the bishop of Würzburg concerning the place called Zell, and by apostolic authority forbid anyone to presume to usurp the advocacy of that place. We likewise confirm to you the tithe from Mosa, as it was granted to you by the bishop.

We decree, therefore, that no person at all may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, remove its possessions, retain what has been removed, diminish them, or harass it with any other vexations; but that all things be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose support and governance they were granted. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical [Col. 0770D] or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make suitable amends by adequate satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour; let that person know that he or she stands guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let that person be excluded from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and at the last judgment let that person be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve their rights for that same place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Gerard, cardinal priest and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, [Col. 0771A] on the eighth day before the Kalends of December, in the sixth indiction, in the year 1143 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Celestine II.

## VII. Privilege for the cathedral church of Augsburg. (1143, 26 November.)

[*Monumenta Boica*, XXXIII, I, p. 714.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons SIGEFRID, provost, and the other canons of the cathedral church of Augsburg, present and future, canonically appointed, in perpetuity.

The authority of the apostolic see entrusted to us exhorts us to grant the protection of guardianship to places and persons which duly seek its aid with devotion. For, just as no effect should be granted to those who ask for unjust things, so the petition of those who seek what is lawful and just ought not to be delayed. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and fortify by the privilege of this present document, the church of Augsburg of the blessed Mother of God and ever-Virgin Mary, in which you are devoted to divine service. We decree that whatever possessions or goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter acquire by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, [Col. 0771C] through God’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to specify in their own terms: Strubingen, Gisenhusen, Aitingen; likewise Aitingen, Muron, Sigelbach, Gershoven, Lanchwate, Biberbach, Mardingen, Altheim, Lebezzingen, Ecke, Flinhusen, Regnibolthesoven, Almintingen, and the vineyards of Powele in Bozon. Furthermore, we likewise confirm to you the ecclesiastical dignities and all the prelations which you have reasonably held hitherto in that church.

We decree, therefore, that no person at all may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, remove its possessions, retain what has been removed, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance [Col. 0771D] and support they were granted, without prejudice to the canonical right of your bishop. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make suitable amends by adequate satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour; let that person know that he or she stands guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let that person be excluded from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and at the last judgment let that person be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve what is just for that same place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge [Col. 0772A] may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Theodewin, bishop of Santa Rufina, have subscribed. I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Hubald, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in Carcere Tulliano, have subscribed. [Col. 0772B] I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Calixtus, have subscribed. I, Thomas, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina, have subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Gerard, cardinal priest and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the sixth day before the Kalends of December, in the seventh indiction, in the year 1143 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Celestine II.

## VIII. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Martin of Ahusen. (1143, 26 November.)

[PETRI, *Suevian Church*, p. 91.]

[Col. 0772C]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the monks of Saint Martin of Ahusen, present and future, regularly appointed, in perpetuity, etc.

A desire shown to pertain to the religious purpose and the salvation of souls should fittingly be granted by us with a willing mind, and suitable support should be supplied to the desires of petitioners. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, moved by the prayers of our venerable brother Walter, bishop of Augsburg, we graciously assent to your just requests. We receive under the protection of that chief of the apostles and ourselves, and fortify by the privilege of this present document, the aforesaid monastery, which was built on its own allodial land by Manegold, count palatine, a man of distinguished memory, and by his sons—namely, our aforesaid brother Walter, now bishop of Augsburg, Adelbert, and Odalric—and offered to blessed Peter with all its appurtenances. We decree that whatever possessions, tithes, or other goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through God’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors.

We confirm by apostolic authority the exchange reasonably made, with the assent of both parties, concerning the place in which the monastery itself is situated, with the church of Saint Peter of Totingen, [Col. 0773A] to whose parish it belonged. You may freely choose by common counsel an advocate whom you know to be useful for the defence of that monastery; should he prove useless, you may remove him and appoint another whom you judge more useful. When the abbot then holding office dies, no one shall be set over you through any deceitful contrivance or violence; rather, you may elect an abbot, by common counsel or that of the sounder part, according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict, without anyone’s contradiction.

You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and the ordinations of monks to be promoted to sacred orders from the diocesan bishop, provided he is Catholic, enjoys the favour and communion of the apostolic see, and is willing to supply these to you freely and without any improper exaction. Otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what is requested. We also grant that burial in that place shall be free, so that no one may prevent any who have decided to be buried there—unless perhaps they are excommunicated—without prejudice, nevertheless, to the right of the mother church. As a sign of this liberty received from the apostolic see, you shall pay one gold coin each year to us and our successors.

We decree, therefore, that no person at all may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, remove its possessions, retain what has been removed, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, without prejudice to the authority of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make suitable amends by adequate satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour; let that person know that he or she stands guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let that person be excluded from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and at the last judgment [Col. 0773D] let that person be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve what is just for that same place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Theodewin, bishop of Santa Rufina, have subscribed. I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed. I, [name omitted], cardinal priest of the title of Saint Calixtus, have subscribed. I, Thomas, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina, have subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna, have subscribed. [Col. 0774A] I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Hubald, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in Carcere Tulliano, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Gerard, cardinal priest and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the sixth day before the Kalends of December, in the seventh indiction, in the year 1143 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Celestine II.

## IX. Privilege for the monastery of Thenol. (1143, 29 November.)

[HUGO, *Annals of Prémontré*, II, p. 582.]

[Col. 0774B]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his most beloved son WALFRID, abbot of the church of Thelon, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

A desire shown to pertain to the religious purpose and the salvation of souls should fittingly be granted by us with a willing mind, and suitable support should be supplied to the desires of petitioners. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests and receive the aforesaid church, in which you are devoted to divine service, under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and fortify it by the privilege of this present document. [Col. 0774C] We decree that whatever possessions or goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s provision, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify in their own terms: namely, the place itself of Thenol and the whole tithe of that territory, with its due liberty [lacuna].

We further enact that the canonical order according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine and the institutions of the brethren of Prémontré shall be observed there inviolate for all time. Nor may any brother, after making profession in that place, leave that cloister without the permission of the abbot and the whole congregation; and no one shall dare to retain a departing brother without a letter of assurance from the community. We decree, therefore, that no person at all may lawfully rashly disturb that same church, remove its possessions, retain what has been removed, diminish them, or harass it with any other vexations; but that all things be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose support and governance they were granted. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make suitable amends by adequate satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour; [Col. 0775A] let that person know that he or she stands guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let that person be excluded from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and at the last judgment let that person be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that same place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of the Church of Sabina. I, Alberic, bishop of the Church of Ostia. I, Rayner, cardinal priest of Saint Prisca.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of [lacuna], cardinal priest and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the third [Col. 0775B] day before the Kalends of December, in the sixth indiction, in the year 1143 of the Lord’s Incarnation.

## X. Privilege for the church of Saint Alexander of Bergamo. (1143, 1 December.)

[LUPI, *Bergamo Diplomatic Codex*, II, no. 1043.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons OBERTO, provost, and the brethren of the church of Saint Alexander of Bergamo, present and future, canonically appointed, for perpetual remembrance.

The order of justice and reason counsels that those who desire their own commands to be observed by successors should preserve the will and enactments of their predecessor. Therefore we, [Col. 0775C] who, though unworthy, have succeeded our predecessor of happy memory, Pope Innocent, in the governance of the apostolic see, wishing to preserve his will and enactment, confirm and judge to remain valid the sentence promulgated by him between you and the canons of Saint Vincent. Namely: whenever the canons of Saint Alexander meet the canons of Saint Vincent at solemnities and funeral rites, or elsewhere, the provost of Saint Alexander shall hold the first place on the left side of the choir. The chaplains of the churches of Saint Saviour, Saint Agatha, Saint John, Saint Grata, and Saint Vigilius shall come to the church of Saint Alexander for the principal masses on Sundays and major feasts. Offenders from the parish of Saint Alexander shall receive penance in the presence of the provost or one of the priests of that church. Likewise, we enact that priests who swear fealty to Blessed Vincent shall also swear it to Blessed Alexander. One of the priests of Saint Alexander shall carry the reliquary; at the transfer of the church, however, two priests of Saint Alexander shall carry the shrine with two priests of Saint Vincent. At the scrutinies on Maundy Thursday, at baptism, and at other solemnities, they shall assemble according to custom. When the canons of Saint Vincent come to the church of Saint Alexander, they shall be honourably received, both in the ringing of bells and in other matters as is customary, and shall occupy the entire choir as they have been accustomed to do.

Furthermore, whatever possessions or goods [Col. 0776A] that same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through God’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify in their own terms: the churches of Licina, Lemene, and Saint Faustinus; of Villa; of Gromole; and of Virgil, without prejudice to the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. We also confirm the grant of tithes canonically made to the provost of your church by Adelbert, bishop of Bergamo of good memory, as is contained in the documents of that bishop and of the canons of the blessed martyrs Alexander and Vincent, so that those tithes may remain permanently for the use of the brethren. Moreover, we strengthen by apostolic authority the good usages and reasonable customs confirmed to you by our predecessors of pious memory, Popes Innocent and Honorius.

We decree, therefore, that henceforth no person at all may disturb the church of Blessed Alexander of Bergamo concerning this our confirmation, or under any pretext infringe or alter it. Rather, all things shall be preserved whole for you in perpetuity, as they are known to have been established by the sanction of this present document. Should anyone, however, rashly attempt to oppose this our confirmation, then, having been warned a second or third time, if he does not make amends by adequate satisfaction, let him suffer the loss of his power and honour and be subject to excommunication. Amen, amen.
