I, Gerard, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Dominica, have subscribed. I, Gisilbert, cardinal deacon of the Holy Roman Church, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of the Holy Roman Church, have subscribed. I, Nicholas, cardinal deacon of the Holy Roman Church, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Gerard, cardinal priest and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the Kalends of December, in the sixth indiction, in the year 1145 of the Lord’s Incarnation, [Col. 0777A] in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Celestine II.

## XI. He informs G[regory], bishop of Bergamo, of the preceding confirmation of privileges. (1143, December.)

[LUPI, *Bergamo Diplomatic Codex*, II, no. 1047.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother G[REGORY], bishop of Bergamo, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We wish your brotherhood to know that we have confirmed by the authority of the apostolic see the sentence of Blessed Vincent and Alexander promulgated by our predecessor of blessed memory, Pope Innocent. Therefore, by these present letters, we command your brotherhood [Col. 0777B] to observe, and to cause to be observed, what our same predecessor enjoined upon you concerning interdicted priests and the other matters pertaining to observance of this sentence.

## XII. Privilege for the monastery of Saints Saviour and Quiricus. (1143, 5 December.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, III, p. 711.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son ALBERT, abbot of the monastery of Saint Saviour and Blessed Quiricus of Populonia, and to his successors regularly appointed, in perpetuity.

The authority of our office exhorts us to love with paternal affection religious persons and places entrusted to their governance, and, with the Lord’s help, to take care that provision is made beneficially for their peace. Accordingly, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Albert, we have thought fit graciously to assent to your reasonable petitions; and we receive under the guardianship and protection of blessed Peter, and fortify by the privilege of the apostolic see, the monastery of our Lord Jesus Christ the Saviour and Saint Quiricus, over which, by God’s appointment, you are known to preside. We decree that whatever possessions or goods that monastery now justly and lawfully possesses, or may hereafter acquire by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s provision, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to record by their own names [Col. 0777D]: namely, all that land which extends from the *acala* of Saint Ambrose to the hill of Scultatorius, as you appear to have peacefully possessed it hitherto, with woods, vineyards, cultivated and uncultivated lands; the hill of the destroyed city which was anciently called Populonia, with all its appurtenances situated there; the church of Saint Christopher, with all its appurtenances, situated at Livellino; the church of Saint Blaise, situated at Laborcone, with all its appurtenances; in Corsica, the church of Saint Nicholas at Monario, with all its appurtenances and buildings; the fishpond of Lifred; Falconaia; Franciola; Castellone with all its appurtenances; the mill [Col. 0778A] of Guidalto; la Cosella; Fabricianum; Saline; and Caldanella. We likewise confirm to you the tithes of your possessions, as you have hitherto possessed them peacefully.

Moreover, for the liberty and reverence of that place, we grant by this decree that you may approach whichever bishop you prefer for the ordinations of your clerics or monks who are to be promoted to sacred orders, provided that he is Catholic, enjoys the favour of the apostolic see, and freely and without improper exaction grants what is requested. We likewise enact that, upon the death of an abbot, no other shall be appointed there by any authority of deceitful intrusion, except one whom the brethren of that monastery have elected by common consent according to the fear of God, especially if a suitable person can be found from that same congregation. But if no one fit for this office can be found among them, they shall seek from elsewhere a father and master for themselves.

We decree, therefore, that no person at all may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, remove its possessions, retain what has been removed, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If anyone, therefore, etc. Amen.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Theodewin, bishop of Santa Rufina, have subscribed. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, [Col. 0778C] have subscribed. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Ubald, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Gerard, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church and librarian, on the Nones of December, in the sixth indiction, in the year 1143 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Celestine II.

## XIII. Privilege for the monastery of Prémontré. (1143, 6 December.)

[HUGO, *Annals of Prémontré*, I, p. 14.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons HUGH, abbot of Prémontré, and his [Col. 0778D] brethren, present and future, regularly appointed, in perpetuity.

It is fitting to apostolic dignity to grant assent to just requests and to hear the prayers of religious persons with gracious ears; nor is there any doubt that, if we kindly support the petitions of God’s servants, we find the merciful Lord favorable to our own needs, so that, just as by divine providence we are called fathers among God’s people, we may also deserve, through the effective fulfillment of our work, to preside beneficially over the faithful. Therefore, although we ought generally to provide for all ecclesiastical persons, we ought nevertheless to be solicitous with more devoted care for those whom we know to aspire with greater zeal to the service of almighty God and to shine forth in a stricter religious observance and uprightness of conduct.

With this indeed [Col. 0779A] in view, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Hugh, we grant with due kindness our assent to the prayers of your devotion; and we fortify by the present document of privilege the Church of Prémontré, over which, by God’s appointment, you are known to preside, together with all its appurtenances. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that venerable place now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future acquire, God favoring it, by grant of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and inviolate for you and your successors.

Among these we have judged the following to be expressly named: namely, the precinct of the valley of Prémontré itself, as it is contained in your documents and defined by fixed boundaries, free from every exaction, whether of land-tax, tithe, or rent; likewise the estate of Fontenelles, with its fishpond and two parts of the mills lying below it, and its other appurtenances; the estate of Penencourt, with vineyards and its other appurtenances; the estate of Merliu, with its vineyards; the estate of Roseries, with its dependencies and appurtenances; the estate of Vercigny, with its appurtenances; the estate of Souppy, with the mills lying below it on the river called the Aisne, and its other appurtenances and dependencies. Two thirds of the tithe of Crépy; one third of the tithe of Chavus. At Valavergni, ten measures of wine from the tithe of that same village; the tithe together with the land-tax of Vrevin; and the land-taxes of Concivilla, except for two [Col. 0779C] measures which must be paid from them to the church of Blessed Mary of Nogent.

Also a fishpond and mill beside that same village, as Ingelrannus, son of Thomas of Marla, had held them in his own demesne in the aforesaid two villages; rents from Poilly; the mill of Rochis; the mill of Proisel; the mill of Achery; the mill of Cortun; the mill of Cenceny; wine-dues from Bourguignon; land at Carenni; two parts of the mill of Aquila; vineyards at Broiencourt, Ursignicourt, Brummout, Lizy, Valavrigny, Montarcenne, and Montbavin; vineyards at Concy-Castel and Coucivilla; wine-dues and vineyards at Novavilla in the diocese of Soissons, in the suburb of the city; an estate and site, a winepress, and vineyards. At Pomerias, wine-dues; rents in money from the castle of Brana [Col. 0779D] and the village of Branella; the estate of Bucy, with vineyards and its other dependencies. The mill of Rupibus, which lies beneath that same village; the estate of Clamecy, with winepress, vineyards, and other dependencies. At Sorny, two winepresses, vineyards, and other revenues; the estate of Tenselva, with its dependencies; the estate of Luilly and half a mill, with its other dependencies. At Bethencourt, wine-dues and other revenues; at Pinon, a certain rent, one third of the small tithe from the courtyard, one sixth of a certain mill, and the tithe which Josbert held there. The chapel and estate of Rosel, with mill, fishpond, winepress, vineyards, and all its dependencies.

On the hill of Trosly, one estate, and another in the valley, with lands, vineyards, [Col. 0780A] and other dependencies; and part of the village with its appurtenances, which Andrew of Baldimento granted you, as he held it in his own demesne; and certain other things offered by other faithful servants of God; the estate of Biucy, with its dependencies; the estate of Attechi and two thirds of the tithe, vineyards with their other appurtenances. At Cauny, a rent and wine-dues; in the village called Pont-Saint-Médard, a certain portion of the tithe. At Margival, half a mill; half the chestnut-groves of Vausaillon.

In the diocese of Noyon, the altar and estate of Bonolio with its dependencies; the estate of Bolmont; the estate of Calveni; the allod of Germainnes; the estate of Montisel; the estate of Thory; the estate of Landricourt; and in the suburb of Noyon, land, vineyards, and meadows, an estate [Col. 0780B] with what pertains to it; the mills of Despeville, and one half of the tithe of that same village; two thirds of the tithe of Destoily; one sixth of the tithe of Duri; the mills of Offois, and two thirds of the tithe of that same village; one third of the tithe of Grecy; half the site of a certain mill at Dinisa and half the tithe of that same village; two thirds of the tithe of Saint Radegund; two thirds of the tithe of Calveni; one third of the tithe of Caullaincourt; two thirds of the tithe of Gricourt; three portions of half the tithe of Leherwes; one third of the tithe of Lancy; the tithe of Kivres; land at Omencourt; land of Liencourt and Curcy; three jugera at Greum; the free chapel [Col. 0780C] of St Nicholas at Saint-Quentin; the estate of the allods with its appurtenances; the estate of Voiana with its appurtenances; the estate of Hanapiis, held in allod, together with its tithe; two thirds of the tithe of Bechincourt; two thirds of the tithe of Cartigny; the entire tithe of Falvi, except the small tithe; one fourth of that of Aldeni; the mills of Escauly, with their appurtenances; the mills of Hamel; the site of a certain mill at Pieton.

We have also recognized, on grounds of humanity, and by this decree, to remain in force forever, establish, that the sisters who, through the labor of our brother of blessed memory Norbert, archbishop of Magdeburg, and through your exhortation, have entered the service of almighty God and offered themselves to the Lord, shall now and always, without anyone’s opposition, receive from the goods of your church what is necessary for their temporal support—goods of which no small part is known to have come to that place through them. [Col. 0780D]

Likewise we decree that you shall not be compelled to pay tithes to anyone from the produce which you gather by your own hands and at your own expense; nor may any bishop, on any pretext, prohibit divine offices in your church. If, however, a general interdict is imposed in the diocese, you shall nevertheless celebrate divine offices behind closed doors, excluding the excommunicated.

Moreover, you shall receive the institution of canons, the consecration of altars or churches, and the other ecclesiastical sacraments from the bishop of Laon, provided that he is Catholic and enjoys the favor and communion of the Apostolic See; otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what is requested. If any nobleman determines to be buried there, no one may oppose his devotion and last will, unless he is excommunicated, while the rights of the mother church remain intact.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all shall be preserved whole for the benefit and support of those for whose governance and maintenance they were granted, to be of use to them in every way. If anyone, moreover, knowingly presumes with rash boldness to act against this our constitution, after a second or third warning, unless [Col. 0781B] he corrects his presumption by fitting amendment, let him be subject to excommunication. But those who preserve these provisions shall obtain the grace of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Leodeninus, bishop of Santa Rufina. I, Thomas, cardinal priest, etc., etc.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Gerard, cardinal priest and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the eighth day before the Ides of December [6 December], in the seventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1143, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Celestine II.

XIV. The pope commands archbishops and bishops not to hinder the annual assemblies of the abbots and provosts of Prémontré. (1143, 6 December.)

[LEPAIGE, *Biblioth. Praem.*, 422.]

[Col. 0781C]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable archbishops and bishops to whom these letters shall come: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is our desire that religion pleasing to God may spread, and that those measures established by reasonable provision for its observance may be strengthened in their stability. For then our service will be acceptable to God, if the beneficial institution, rigor, and order of holy places are preserved in purity of religious observance. We do not think that your brotherhood is unaware that the Order of the brothers of Prémontré has already, by God’s grace, grown throughout diverse regions of the world, and that their good conduct and religious observance have encouraged very many persons to live well. Therefore we, who, though unworthy, preside by the Lord’s ordering over the governance of the Apostolic See, desire to love and cherish these brothers and their houses, and to provide for their needs.

For the observance of this order it has been established that the abbots or provosts of the Order of Prémontré shall assemble at Prémontré [Col. 0782A] once each year, so that, by the common counsel of the brothers, what needs correction in that order may be corrected, and what ought to be established for the honor of God may reasonably be established. Therefore, by these present letters, we command you not in any way to prevent those abbots or provosts dwelling in your dioceses from coming to that assembly. Indeed, compel strictly those unwilling to go. Bind with the bond of excommunication those who have apostatized from the same order and departed, without the permission of their superior and of the whole congregation, from the places where they are known to have made profession, if, after warning, they disdain to return; and proclaim them excommunicated throughout your parishes.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Gerard, cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman [Col. 0782B] Church, on the eighth day before the Ides of December [6 December], in the tenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1143, in the first year of our pontificate.

XV. To Arnald, archbishop of Narbonne, and his suffragans.—They are to warn their parishioners not to give shelter to Aimonius and his accomplices, rebels against William, lord of Montpellier; otherwise they are to be excommunicated. (1143, 8 December.)

[DOM BOUQUET, *Recueil*, vol. XV, p. 409.]

[Col. 0782C] CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brothers A[rnald], archbishop of Narbonne, and his suffragans: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our beloved son William of Montpellier, as we do not believe you are unaware, has by God’s grace recovered his town, and the greater part of the inhabitants of that town has returned to his allegiance. Now, however, as we have learned, certain traitors to him—namely Aimonius [Note: [Col. 0781D] The Aymonii were said to be hostile to William because he had entrusted the vicariate authority in his absence to persons bound to him by no tie of blood; and they pressed this contention all the more obstinately because they seemed to be supported by the greater authority of leading men, especially Count Ildefonsus of Toulouse and certain other magnates.] and some of his accomplices—dwelling in your dioceses, are plotting to disturb the peace and wage war. Since traitors and violators of peace must be restrained by ecclesiastical justice, by these present letters we command you strictly to warn your parishioners not to presume to harbor them against that same their lord. If they refuse to obey your warnings and presume, after your warning, to harbor them, prohibit the celebration of divine offices in the places where they have been received, except for the baptism of children and the penance of the dying; admonish your parishioners also to desist from aiding them, and, if they prove contemptuous, exclude them from the thresholds of the church.

Given at the Lateran, on the sixth day before the Ides of December [8 December].

XVI. To Hugh, archbishop of Tours.—He is to appear before the Apostolic See to answer the bishop of Dol, who complained that he had been despoiled of the bishopric of Alet. (1143, 10 December.)

[MARTÈNE, *Thes. Anecd.*, III, 887.]

[Col. 0783A]

Our predecessor Pope Innocent of blessed memory, on account of the complaint of our brother, the archbishop of Dol, summoned you to appear before him on the past feast of St Luke, so that you might demonstrate the right of your church concerning the subjection which you exact from him, and answer him concerning the bishopric of Alet, which he asserts that you hold and of which he complains that he was despoiled without reason or judgment. He indeed appeared before us on that same date; but you [Col. 0783B] neither came nor offered a canonical excuse. Although this ought to have been punished by a severe penalty against you, nevertheless, out of the clemency of the Apostolic See and at the prayers of our brothers who interceded for you, we have for the present borne it patiently; and by these present letters we command you to appear before us on the coming Kalends of May [1 May], prepared to demonstrate the right concerning the aforesaid subjection of your church and to answer him concerning the aforesaid bishopric.

Given at the Lateran, on the fourth day before the Ides of December [10 December].

XVII. To William, lord of Montpellier.—The pope rejoices that the town of Montpellier, wrongfully taken from him by its inhabitants, has been restored to him. (1143, 10 December.)

[D. BOUQUET, *Recueil*, XV, 410.]

[Col. 0783C]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son WILLIAM of Montpellier: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We rejoice with paternal affection that you have, by God’s grace, recovered the town of Montpellier, wrongfully taken from you by your inhabitants, [Note: [Col. 0783D] With Genoese assistance William had recovered the town of Montpellier, as is recorded in the Genoese Annals of Caffaro.] and we give thanks to almighty God. For, following the example of our predecessors, we desire to love and cherish your person and, as the duty of our office requires, to restrain your assailants by due punishment. Since, therefore, beloved son in the Lord, there is no authority except from God, we admonish and exhort your belovedness in the Lord always to look to [Col. 0783D] Him and to endeavor to govern in justice and equity the people entrusted to you by God, so that God may thereby be honored and your mother, the holy Roman Church, may rejoice in your good deeds.

Given at the Lateran, on the sixth day before the Ides of December [8 December].

XVIII. To Peter, abbot of Saint-Gilles.—He commands him, in the pope’s name, to lay the first stone in the foundation of the chapel which William, lord of Montpellier, intended to build in his new castle at Montpellier; and, after accepting the gift of the chapel, to establish an annual payment to the Roman Church. (1143, 10 December.)

[D. BOUQUET, *ibid.*]

[Col. 0784A]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son P[eter], abbot of Saint-Gilles: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our beloved son William of Montpellier has informed us through his messengers that in the castle which he has newly begun to build at Montpellier he intends to construct a chapel in honor of God. Since the vows of the faithful should be promoted by our efforts, by these present letters we command you to go to that place, receive for the use of the Holy Roman Church the donation of the site on which the chapel is to be built, and [Col. 0784B] establish there a suitable annual payment to be rendered to us and our successors, as you determine to be expedient. Afterwards, once the site has been marked out according to custom, lay the first stone in the foundation there by our authority, taking diligent care that the same William endow the clerics who will serve that chapel from his goods sufficiently for them to be able to live honorably and serve God.

Given at the Lateran, on the fourth day before the Ides of December [10 December].

XIX. He takes the church of St Mary at Halberstadt under protection and confirms the possessions of its canons. (1143, 23 December.)

[It exists in the royal archive at Berlin, according to JAFFÉ, *Regesta Rom. pont.*, p. 607.]

XX. To the archbishop, clergy, and people of Liège. He confirms the sentence of excommunication pronounced by them against those attacking the monastery of Stavelot, and exhorts them to ensure the restoration of goods alienated by Poppo II, etc. (1143, 28 December.)

[MARTÈNE, *Ampl. Collect.*, II, 117.]

[Col. 0784C]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother Ad. [Note: [Col. 0784D] Adalbero II of that name, son of the count of Guelders, who was elected bishop of Liège in 1136 from being primicerius at Metz, and held office until 1146.] bishop, and to the beloved sons, the clergy and people of Liège: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is pleasing to us that, as the Apostle teaches, bearing one another’s burdens, you assist our beloved son Wibald, abbot of Stavelot, as we have learned from his own report, together with the monastery entrusted to him, against its attackers, and that you have issued against them, as sacrilegious persons, a sentence of due punishment. We therefore, whose special duty it is to correct evil deeds and confirm good ones, confirm by apostolic authority the sentence of excommunication canonically pronounced against them and decree that it shall remain valid.

Concerning others, however, who retain against the will of the abbot the *joariae*, *majoriae*, and *villicationes*—that is, administrative offices of judicial, mayoral, and estate-management authority—as well as benefices which they received from Poppo the Second, abbot, whose alienations [Col. 0785A] and transfers have been annulled by the judgment of kings, and who are not yet subject to the same sentence: we command you strictly to admonish them to surrender these same offices and goods freely into the abbot’s hand. If they prove contemptuous, bind them with the bond of anathema.

And you, brother bishop, likewise admonish Henry of Roche to restore whole the house of Erhebert [Note: [Col. 0785D] He is elsewhere called Erchembert.]—brother of the aforesaid abbot—which he destroyed during the truce, namely in the days of the sacred Passion, together with the things he took from the abbey’s goods. If within forty days after your warning he neglects to do so, pronounce the canonical sentence against him; and neither he nor the others mentioned above shall be absolved until they make worthy satisfaction to that abbot. With regard to the priests of Longia and Wellin, and others who, as we have learned, presume to communicate with the aforesaid excommunicated persons, administer justice.

Given at the Lateran, on the fifth day before the Kalends of January [28 December].

XXI. Privilege granted to Abbot Wibald.—He receives the monastery of Stavelot under the protection of the Apostolic See and confirms its various privileges and immunities. (1143, 30 December.)

[MARTÈNE, *ibid.*]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Wibald, abbot of Stavelot, and his brothers, both present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

[Col. 0785C] It accords with the clemency of apostolic governance to love religious persons and fortify their places with pious protection. For it is recognized as worthy and becoming to our office that we, who have been raised to the governance of churches, should both defend them from the malice of wicked persons and cherish them by the patronage of the Apostolic See. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Wibald, graciously granting our favorable assent to your just petitions, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the monastery of Stavelot, over which, by God’s appointment, you are known to preside, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and canonically [Col. 0785D] possesses, or may in future, God favoring it, acquire by grant of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and inviolate for you and your successors.

Among these we have judged the following to be expressly named: namely, Malmedy, which, as it is known to have been from the beginning of its foundation, shall always remain subject to the house of Stavelot as a cell to a monastery; the monks of that place shall make their profession at Stavelot and be blessed and ordained wherever the abbot shall provide; nor shall the abbot of Stavelot for the time being be compelled, on account of that place, to promise obedience to the archbishop of Cologne or to receive from him the care of souls. [Col. 0786A]

The castle called Longia, with the prohibition that no advocate may presume to appropriate anything there for himself, but that it shall remain at all times under the abbot’s disposal; the church at Sprimont, Herram, Turnines, Hosammont, Oiseis, Praisdis, Aldendhorph, Amblavia, Tumbis, and Clotena; the village of Germiniacum and two mills on the river Suppia; the village of Turnines; the village of Sprimont; Lukesenges; Vilippes; Tavernou; Husenebarch; and the village of Bacen, which the free man Godefridus gave you.

We likewise confirm to you the appointments to the churches and their tithes, as you have held them hitherto. We decree that in the parish churches which you hold no bishop shall install a priest without the abbot’s consent; rather, in accordance with the decree of our predecessor Pope Urban of blessed memory, bishops shall, with the abbot’s consent, entrust parochial care to a priest, so that such priests shall render account to the bishop for the care of the people, but shall show to the abbot due subjection in temporal matters belonging to the monastery. [Col. 0786B]

We also prohibit anyone in the possessions of that monastery from holding by hereditary succession or feudal right any *joaria*, *majoria*, or *villicatio*—judicial, mayoral, or estate-management office—but it shall remain in the abbot’s power to appoint and, when he judges it expedient, to change such officers. Nor may anyone presume to infringe the security and liberty in the circuit of the monastery within the league, as reasonably granted by kings or emperors.

That monastery shall not have a third advocate, but, according to ancient custom, only two. The first shall receive the advocacy with the *bannum*—the authority of command and jurisdiction—from the hands of kings or emperors; the second, having received his benefice from the hand of the first advocate, shall receive the *bannum* from kings or emperors. Nor may they impose lodging, hold courts, exact forced contributions, or impose exactions upon possessions or persons belonging to the monastery; nor take palfreys; nor exact *freda*, redemptions, or the customary dues commonly called “dead-hand” dues. Rather, as is contained in the writings of kings and emperors, these matters shall belong to the abbot’s right and ordering. When ministeriales assemble for the monastery’s feast days, they shall demand no service or meal beyond what [Col. 0786D] the abbot reasonably provides for them.

Furthermore, by apostolic authority we add and forbid that the abbey itself be given to anyone as a benefice or in exchange, that it ever be governed by a layman, or that an abbot for the time being give any of its possessions or goods to anyone as a fief or pledge, or make any exchange whatsoever or any alienation of them without the common counsel of the chapter. Upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed over it by any artifice of deceit or violence; but you may, by common counsel or by the counsel of the sounder part, in accordance with the fear of God and the Rule of St Benedict, elect an abbot without anyone’s opposition. [Col. 0787A]

You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars and churches, the abbot’s blessing, and the ordination of monks who are to be promoted to holy orders from the diocesan bishop, provided he is Catholic, enjoys the favor and communion of the Apostolic See, and is willing to supply these things to you freely and without any improper exaction. Otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what is requested. Moreover, the abbot presiding over that place for the time being shall be compelled to attend the synod of no bishop except the diocesan. Priests and clerics serving in your churches shall render to you the due and customary services without any objection.

We also grant that the burial-place of that house shall be free, so that no one may oppose anyone who determines to be buried there, unless that person is excommunicated, while the rights of the mother church nevertheless remain intact. We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all shall be preserved whole for the use, in every respect beneficial, of those for whose governance and support they exist, while the right of its ancient liberty remains intact. If, in future, any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this document of our constitution, attempts rashly to violate it, after a second or third warning, unless [Col. 0787C] he makes fitting satisfaction, let him lose the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and our Lord, Redeemer Jesus Christ; and at the final judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who observe justice toward that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Theodewin, bishop of Santa Rufina. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. [Col. 0787D] I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of St Chrysogonus. I, Goizo, cardinal priest of the title of St Cecilia. I, Thomas, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Gerard, cardinal deacon of St Mary in Domnica. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of St Nicholas in Carcere Tulliano. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of St Angelo.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Gerard, cardinal priest and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, [Col. 0788A] on the third day before the Kalends of January [30 December], in the seventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1143, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Celestine II.

XXII. Privilege for the church of Aix. (1143–44.)

[PITTON, *Annales de l’Eglise d’Aix*, p. 130.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons BERTRAND, provost of Aix, and his brothers, both present and future, entering canonically, etc.

We receive the church of Aix under the protection of the blessed apostles and our own, together with whatever possessions and goods that church now [Col. 0788B] justly and canonically possesses. Among these we have judged the following to be expressly named: the territory of Ratmont, which Guy, then archbishop and provost, gave to your church and to the canons serving God there, and which is bounded by the following limits: on the north, by the public road leading to St Honoratus (Saint-Honorat de Roquefavour); on the east, by the stream descending through the valley of Marseille (*lou Plan d’Aguilles*) and flowing into the river called the Arc; on the south, by that same river Arc; on the west, where the water runs downward and divides it from the territory of St Honoratus; etc.

XXIII. Privilege for the monastery of Rott. (1144, 2 January.)

[*Monumenta Boica*, I, p. 358.]

[Col. 0788C]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brothers C[onrad], archbishop of Salzburg, HENRY, bishop of Regensburg, and R., bishop of Passau: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We believe that your brotherhood knows that the monastery of Rott, together with all its goods, belongs by right to blessed Peter and is known especially to pertain to his possession and protection. Therefore, the more especially you know it and the brothers serving the Lord there to belong to the right of the Apostolic See and to remain under its protection and defense, the more earnestly you ought to aid and support them. Accordingly, by these present [Col. 0788D] letters we command you, for reverence for blessed Peter and for us, to love, honor, aid, support, and defend from the assaults of wicked persons our beloved son B., abbot of that place, his brothers, and their houses. Concerning your parishioners of whom they complain to you, administer full justice to them without delay or pretext.

Given at the Lateran, on the fourth day before the Nones of January [2 January].

XXIV. He entrusts Walter, bishop of Augsburg, with the protection of the monastery of Rott against the widow of Count Otto. (1144, 2 January.)

[*Monumenta Boica*, I, p. 359.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable [Col. 0789A] brother WALTER, bishop of Augsburg: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our beloved son Berticus, abbot of the monastery of Rott, appearing before the Apostolic See, complained in our presence that G., widow of Count Otto, and Sigfrid, your ministerial, were violently taking away and unjustly retaining certain possessions belonging by right to the monastery entrusted to him. Since that monastery, together with all its goods, belongs by right to blessed Peter and is known especially to pertain to his possession and protection, by these present letters we command you strictly to admonish the aforesaid invaders to restore the goods of that monastery to the aforementioned abbot and brothers and leave them in peace. If they disdain to do so, [Col. 0789B] restrain them by ecclesiastical censure.

Given at the Lateran, on the fourth day before the Nones of January [2 January].

XXV. To Folmar, abbot of Hirsau, and Adam, abbot of Eberbach. (1144, 2 January.)

[*Codex Laureshamensis*, I, 241.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons FOLMAR, abbot of Hirsau, and ADAM, abbot at Eberbach: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Baldemar, abbot of Lorsch Abbey, came before the Apostolic See, asserting that he had been canonically elected to it and complaining that he had been despoiled of it in his absence and without judgment; he requested restoration. But, through the testimony of our venerable brother Theodewin, bishop of Santa Rufina, and the letters of many discerning men, we learned that Baldemar had refused to appear at Lorsch for the examination of his case and to answer the charges; that he had been transferred from the rule of the abbey of Bleidenstadt to Lorsch without the authority of the Roman Church; and that we had removed from him the abbey to which he had unlawfully passed and suspended him from the other which he had previously held.

Moreover, since that brother who has been installed in the governance of Lorsch Abbey has been accused before us of the crime [Col. 0789D] of simony, and since we cannot and ought not to pass over so great a crime without examination, we command you by these present letters: if persons appear who canonically accuse him of simony, summon both parties before you at a suitable place and time, hear the case diligently, and bring it to a canonical conclusion. Otherwise, let that brother purge himself of so grave a charge by the fifth hand of religious persons. Do not delay to inform us of what you have done in this matter, and likewise of the election, the method of election, and the suitability of the person, so that, once the truth has been more fully known, we may, with God as author, do what must be done for God’s honor.

Given at the Lateran, on the fourth day before the Nones of January [2 January].

XXVI. Privilege for the church of the Holy Sepulchre at Jerusalem. (1144, 10 January.)

[ROZIÈRE, *Cartulaire du Saint-Sépulcre*, 29.]

[Col. 0790A]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons PETER, prior, and the brothers of the Holy Sepulchre of Jerusalem, both present and future, canonically appointed, in perpetuity.

If the gentleness and generosity of the holy Roman Church ought to furnish timely assistance to all Christians, it is all the more fitting that it should bestow this upon those who lead the religious life and appear to cleave more closely to almighty God. Since, therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, you have resolved to live according to the Rule of blessed Augustine [Col. 0790B], and, worshipping in the place where the Lord’s feet stood, you serve regularly at his glorious tomb, in which he rested bodily for three days, and at the other most holy places where the Redeemer of the world endured for our salvation bonds, scourges, the disgrace of the cross, wounds, and death, we judge you worthy of greater goodwill and favor and desire to cherish you with paternal affection. Accordingly, graciously assenting to your requests, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the most holy church of the Holy Sepulchre—where, devoted to divine offices, you continually recall with the faith of eyewitnesses the Lord’s Passion and the triumph of the most victorious cross—as well as your persons, [Col. 0790C] and strengthen them by this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that church now canonically possesses; whatever has been justly bestowed upon that place by men of distinguished memory—namely Duke Godfrey and both Kings Baldwin—as well as by Arnulf and the other patriarchs; and whatever shall hereafter reasonably be granted by patriarchs or other faithful of God, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you.

Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: namely, one half of the offerings of the Holy Sepulchre; all offerings of the Lord’s Cross; and all offerings of the altars situated in the church of the Holy Sepulchre, as they were reasonably granted to you by gift of the patriarchs; [Col. 0790D] all houses, shops, and ovens of the city of Jerusalem, except two—those, namely, of the Hospital and of the church of Saint Mary of the Latins—as they were lawfully granted to you by gift of Duke Godfrey, his brother King Baldwin, and other good men; the villages which you possess in the territory of Jerusalem, namely Mahumeria with its appurtenances, Sabaiet, Cafareab, Calandria, Armotia, Ramitta, Beteligel, Bethsuri, and Aessens, with their appurtenances; in the territory of Ramla, the village of Gith with all its appurtenances; in the territory of Caesarea, the castle of Feniculi with its appurtenances; in the territory of Tyre, the village of Derina with its appurtenances; the garden which you have between the wall and the outer wall of the city of Tyre; the garden, mills, [Col. 0791A] and other possessions which you have within and around Antioch; the church of Quarantine with its appurtenances; the church of Saint Peter at Jaffa with its appurtenances; the church of the Holy Sepulchre at Acre, with the land and house which Lambert Hals gave you, and its other appurtenances; in the territory of the same city, the church of Saint Mary of Mimas with its appurtenances; the church of Saint Mary in the city of Tyre with its appurtenances; the church of the Holy Sepulchre on Mount Peregrine with its appurtenances; the church of Saint George in the mountains with its appurtenances; the church of the Holy Sepulchre in the city of Brindisi with its appurtenances; the church of the Holy Sepulchre at Barletta with its appurtenances; the church [Col. 0791B] which you have in the city of Venosa by gift of Nicholas, bishop of that city, with its appurtenances; the church of the Holy Sepulchre near the city of Troy with its appurtenances; the church of Saint Theodore the Martyr before the gate of the city of Benevento, with its appurtenances; the castle of Cerret with its appurtenances, which the nobleman Albert, count of Blandat, gave to the church of the Holy Sepulchre; and the church which you have in the diocese of Constance, in the village called Kendorf.

We therefore decree that absolutely no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain possessions taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be kept whole for the benefit, in every way, of those for whose government and support they were granted, without prejudice to the reverence due to the Apostolic See and the canonical rights of the patriarch of Jerusalem and of the bishops in whose parishes your churches are situated. [Col. 0791C] If in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of rank and office, and recognize himself or herself as answerable before divine judgment for the wrong committed; let that person be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer, and be subject at the last judgment to severe punishment. But upon all who preserve what is right for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit [Col. 0791D] of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.  
I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed.  
I, Theodevinus, bishop of Santa Rufina, have subscribed.  
I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed.  
I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed.  
I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum, have subscribed.  
I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Calixtus, have subscribed.  
[Col. 0792A] I, Goizo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia, have subscribed.  
I, Hubald, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes, have subscribed.  
I, Humbald, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed.  
I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed.  
I, Octo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.  
I, Ottavianus, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Gerard, cardinal priest of the holy Roman Church and librarian, on the fourth day before the Ides of January, in the seventh indiction, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation [Col. 0792B], in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Celestine II.

### XXVII. To the brethren of the church of Lucca, heirs of Almeric, of blessed memory, chancellor of the Holy Roman Church and cardinal deacon of the church of Blessed Mary Nova: he grants the privilege that cardinal deacons of the church of Blessed Mary Nova shall henceforth be chosen from their number.  
*(A.D. 1144, January 10.)*

[Bullarium Lateranense, 122.]

### XXVIII. Privilege for the church of the Holy Sepulchre at Jerusalem.  
*(A.D. 1144, January 10.)*

[ROZIÈRE, *Cartulary of the Holy Sepulchre*, 27.]

[Col. 0792C]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons PETER, prior, and the brethren of the Holy Sepulchre of Jerusalem, present and future, canonically appointed, forever.

Whenever our assent is expected in certain agreements, reason requires that what is done be confirmed by us, for the security of the parties, lest it fall into doubt. Our beloved son Fulk, illustrious king of Jerusalem, and his wife Melisende, queen, desire that men or women of the monastic religious life be established in the church of Saint Lazarus, situated at Bethany; and they humbly request that this be strengthened by the authority of the Apostolic See, both in their own letters and in those of our venerable brother William, patriarch of Jerusalem, as well as of the archbishops and bishops of that land. [Col. 0792D] Therefore we, whose special concern it is to assent to just wishes, graciously granting our favorable assent to their devout desires, decree that in the same church of Blessed Lazarus, according to the petition and ordinance of our aforesaid brother the patriarch and of the aforementioned king and queen, men or women of monastic profession shall be established for the honor and service of God, and that the monastic order shall be preserved there inviolably for all time.

We also confirm by apostolic authority, and judge it to remain valid, the exchange concerning the village of Thecua, as the aforesaid king freely granted it to you, and concerning the villages which you in like manner freely granted him for the support of the religious persons to be established in that church, [Col. 0793A] as it was concluded between you and that king and confirmed in writing on both sides. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of rank and office, and recognize himself or herself as answerable before divine judgment for the wrong committed; let that person be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer, and be subject at the last judgment to severe punishment. But upon those who observe it may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit [Col. 0793B] of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.  
I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed.  
I, Theodovinus, bishop of Santa Rufina, have subscribed.  
I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed.  
I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed.  
I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum, have subscribed.  
I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Calixtus, have subscribed.  
I, Goizo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint [Col. 0793C] Cecilia, have subscribed.  
I, Hubald, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes, have subscribed.  
I, Humbald, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed.  
I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed.  
I, Octo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.  
I, Octavianus, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Gerald, cardinal priest of the holy Roman Church and librarian, on the fourth day before the Ides of January, in the seventh indiction, in the year 1143 of the Lord’s Incarnation [Col. 0793D], in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Celestine II.

### XXIX. To Peter, prior, and the canons of the Holy Sepulchre at Jerusalem—He grants them a church in the city of Rome.  
*(A.D. 1144, January 12.)*

[ROZIÈRE, *ibid.*, p. 76.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons P[ETER], prior, and the canons of the Holy Sepulchre: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have received with due kindness your brethren, our beloved sons L. . . and G. . . , together with the letters sent by your brotherhood to our predecessor of blessed memory, Pope Innocent, [Col. 0794A] and have granted their just requests. For we love the holy Church of Jerusalem and your persons with true charity in the Lord, and wish to honor and exalt you in all matters in which we can do so according to God. Therefore, in consideration of your honor and religious character, we have judged it fitting to grant you a church in the city of Rome, where you may serve the Lord and, when you come to the curia on the affairs of your Church, have honorable lodging.

It concerns you, therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, that, the more closely you behold the glorious Sepulchre of our Lord Jesus Christ and the other places which he deigned to visit in bodily presence, the more devout you should be in his service, and that you should strive in every respect to please him, so that after the passage from this life you may deserve to receive the fruit of everlasting recompense from the Lord Jesus Christ, the rewarder of all good things. [Col. 0794B] We commend to your affection the aforesaid brethren, who have conducted themselves honorably among us and have worked faithfully in the affairs entrusted to them, asking that, for love of us, you may hold them dearer among your dear ones. May divine grace preserve you as you pray for us, and absolve you from all sins.

Given at the Lateran, on the second day before the Ides of January.

### XXX. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Bertin at Sithiu.  
*(A.D. 1144, January 19.)*

[Collection of Cartularies, III, 314.]

[Col. 0794C]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son LEO, abbot of Saint Bertin, and to his successors regularly appointed forever.

The order of justice and reason counsels that one who wishes his own commands to be observed by successors should undoubtedly preserve the will and ordinances of his predecessor. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Leo, we confirm and decree to remain valid the settlement of the controversy long debated between you and our beloved son Peter, abbot of Cluny, concerning the subjection which that abbot claimed for himself in your monastery. This settlement was made by our predecessor of blessed memory, Pope Innocent, in our presence and with the assent of his other brethren, [Col. 0794D] and was confirmed by the authority of his written instrument. Since the privileges which the Cluniacs asserted that they held from the Apostolic See concerning this matter were annulled by that aforesaid predecessor of ours, justice so requiring, we, following his example, absolve you, your successors and brethren, and the monastery of Saint Bertin from this suit and from subjection to the Cluniacs. We decree that the same monastery, restored to its own liberty, shall remain forever under the authority and protection of the Roman Church alone, saving the right of the church or bishop of Thérouanne.

We decree that whatever possessions and goods that place now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, God favoring, by grants of popes, gifts of kings, generosity of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. [Col. 0795A] Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: in the parish of Thérouanne, the church of Saint Margaret, the churches of Saint John and Saint Martin, the church of Harbela, the church of Peternesse, and the church of Turbessem, as anciently free from every episcopal due; the church of Broburg with its chapels; also two sheaves of tithe from newly cultivated land wherever it may accrue throughout the whole parish of Broburg, which extends to the boundaries of neighboring parishes; the church of Arkes with that village; the church of Poperinghem with that village; the church of Steenkerka; the church of Brusele; the church of Scales; the church of Boveringhem with their villages; the villages of Aldenfort, Ostresela, and Rokestor, with the land which the Church bought from Arnulf of Vuenti and the other adjoining lands; the allod which Clarembald gave in the village of Eustinghem; the church of Coeka; the church of Helcin with their villages; and what you possess in the church of Valnas by gift of John, bishop of Thérouanne, of blessed memory; the church of Locanes and Acquina; the church of Hunela with that village; and the altar of Merchem, which the venerable Bishop John granted you.

In the parish of Noyon: the estate of Caneta, that is, Calmunt. In that of Tournai: the church of Rokeshem, the church of [Col. 0795C] Edingehem, that of Vestkerke, and the tithe of Claneskerke; the church of Hildingehem, the church of Lisnega, the church of Snelgekerke, the church of Erningehem, and the church of Bovenkerke. In the parish of Arras: the church of Verkin, the church of Salomes, and the church of Hautay. In the territory of Furnes: the forty-pound sheepfold which Charles gave for the soul of Count Baldwin, and the land of Buri, which your church is known to possess in the district of Beauvais. In the parish of Cologne: the church of Frekene and the church of Gildestorp, with their appurtenances.

Of these we command that no assessment be exacted by bishops or their ministers on any pretext, saving the bishops’ annual revenues. We also confirm the church of Coclers, which Baldric, bishop of the church of Tournai, granted to Abbot Lambert of blessed memory and his successors to administer, free from every exaction, together with the altar of Rusleta, except for ten solidi in coin, paid yearly from Rusleta to the bishop; [Col. 0795D] and the entire space of the precinct which lies on every side between your basilica and the middle course of the river Agnion, with the fisheries of Mera and Grath, Mardic and Stranguer, and Laugha, and with adjoining cultivated or uncultivated lands, as you have possessed them from ancient times. Again, in the parish of Thérouanne: the church of Osclara, the church of Vuarnestim, the church of Saint Mary called Eggafrid’s Chapel, and the church of Haveskerke.

Following also in the footsteps of our aforesaid predecessor, we confirm by apostolic authority and strengthen by this present written document the agreement reasonably made and confirmed by his instrument between Lambert, your predecessor, beloved son in the Lord Abbot Leo, and Everard, son of Odbert of Helcin, concerning the altar of that village and its chapels, in the presence of John, bishop of Thérouanne of blessed memory, and his clerics. [Col. 0796A] Moreover, the same monastery shall henceforth possess peacefully and without anyone’s objection, according to the terms of that agreement, Saint Martin’s meadow, the *femedir* [term uncertain] of the priest Peter, and Albert’s cleared land, which were granted to Everard only for his lifetime in order to preserve the agreement.

We absolutely forbid the bishop to impose public lodging-quarters in that monastery, and forbid that bishop to come there frequently unless summoned by the abbot and brethren. On your death, you who are now abbot of the same place, no one may be placed over it by any trick of intrigue or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, shall elect according to the fear of God and the Rule of Saint Benedict. Likewise, at the monastery of Saint Silvin at Alciacum, according to ancient custom, a suitable and religious person from your community shall always be selected and established as abbot.

We also decree that, according to the decree of Pope Urban of blessed memory, you shall appoint priests in the parish churches which you hold, with the counsel of the bishops, to whom the bishops commit the care of the parish with your assent. [Col. 0796C] Such priests shall render account to the bishops for the care of the people, but shall show you due subjection concerning temporal affairs belonging to the monastery. We further enact that within your parishes no one shall presume to build a church or monastery without your assent, while in all things the authority of the Apostolic See remains reserved.

As an acknowledgment of this liberty received from the Roman Church, you shall pay one ounce of gold every year to us and our successors. We therefore decree that absolutely no person may rashly disturb that monastery in respect of this our grant and confirmation, take away its possessions, retain possessions taken away, diminish them, etc. “As above in the privilege of Innocent [Col. 0796D], to the end.”

“I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.

“Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Gerard, cardinal priest of the holy Roman Church and librarian, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of February, in the seventh indiction, in the year 1143 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Celestine II.

“LET PEACE BE IN YOUR STRENGTH, AND ABUNDANCE IN YOUR TOWERS. SAINT PETER. SAINT PAUL.”

### XXXI. To Gerhoh, provost of Reichersberg—He consoles him for the many things he suffers from adversaries and invites him to come to him.  
*(A.D. 1144, January 27.)*

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 593.]

[Col. 0797A]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son GERHOH, provost of Reichersberg: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We sympathize with you in paternal affection concerning the troubles and distresses which, as we have learned from the testimony of our beloved son G., cardinal deacon, you endure in defense of truth and justice; and in all matters in which we can do so according to God, we willingly offer you aid and counsel. You ought to show the greater patience in these things because it is more certain that your diligence endures these persecutions in defense of justice. [Col. 0797B] For you know that it is neither new nor unusual that, according to the Apostle, those who wish to live piously in Christ suffer persecution from the ungodly and unlike-minded; and the Lord consoles them in the Gospel, promising them eternal blessedness: “Blessed,” he says, “are those who suffer persecution for the sake of righteousness.”

Nevertheless, in discharge of our duty we wish to oppose your rivals and restrain them by ecclesiastical censure. Therefore by this present writing we command you to present yourself before us on the next Sunday, on which is read, “I am the good shepherd,” so that, having learned the case more fully from you yourself, we may provide for your peace and tranquility [Col. 0797C] and give you timely assistance as to a beloved son.

### XXXII. Privilege for the nunnery of Saint Hilary.  
*(A.D. 1144, February 8.)*

[LAMI, *Delights of Learning*, 1737, p. 209.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters AGNES, abbess of the monastery of Saint Hilary situated in the diocese of Fiesole, . . . . and to its present and future members, professing the regular life, forever.

The care of the universal Church has been entrusted to us by God, the provider of all good things, in order that we may love religious persons and strive by every means to promote religion pleasing to God; [Col. 0797D] for no service is ever acceptable to God unless, proceeding from the root of charity, it is preserved in the purity of religious life. Therefore, beloved daughters in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that all castles, estates, rights, courts, churches, vineyards, cultivated and uncultivated lands with their appurtenances—whatever the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, God favoring, by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means—shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors.

We further decree that the monastery itself shall remain forever in the same estate and governance of holy nuns—that is, women—daily advancing in religious life, as from its beginning here . . . . [Col. 0798A] Following also in the footsteps of our predecessor Pope Alexander of blessed memory, we grant and confirm to you by apostolic authority the whole tithes from cultivated and uncultivated lands and your other property, for the use of the poor and pilgrims. You shall receive the consecration of altars or churches, and the ordination of your clerics who are to be promoted to sacred orders, from the diocesan bishop, provided that he is Catholic, enjoys the favor and communion of the Apostolic See, and is willing to provide these things freely and without any improper exaction. Otherwise you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what is requested.

We therefore decree that absolutely no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain possessions taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be kept whole, to benefit in every way you and others for whose government and support they were granted, the authority of the Apostolic See being reserved in all things. [Col. 0798C] If in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of rank and office, and recognize himself or herself as answerable before divine judgment for the wrong committed; let that person be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer, and be subject at the last judgment to severe punishment. But upon all who preserve what is right for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

In the circle:

LET PEACE BE IN YOUR STRENGTH, AND ABUNDANCE IN YOUR TOWERS.

[Col. 0798D] In the center of the circle:

SAINT PETER, SAINT PAUL, POPE CELESTINE II.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church.  
I, Gibi, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Mary in Trastevere.  
I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Damaso.  
I, Octavianus, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison.  
I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna.  
I, John.  
I, Guizzo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia.  
[Col. 0799A] I, Thomas, cardinal priest of Saint Vestina.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Gerard, cardinal priest and librarian of the holy Roman Church, on the sixth day before the Ides of February, in the seventh indiction, in the year 1143 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Celestine II.

### XXXIII. Privilege for the monastery of Mount Saint John.  
*(A.D. 1144, February 12.)*

[MIRAEUS, *Diplomatic Works*, III, 722.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons [Note: [Col. 0799D] In the year 1136 Walter of Gymmenich, dean of the collegiate church of Saint Gereon at Cologne, together with his brother Hubert, founded an abbey of Premonstratensians on Mount Saint John, near Eyckam in the diocese of Liège, now called Maseyca or Mosacum. The first religious were sent here by Blessed Andrew, first abbot of Averbode, and Giselbert, previously prior of Averbode, was appointed first abbot. Pope Celestine II confirmed this foundation in 1143 by the bull just cited, and Count Louis of Loon did so in 1155 (*diploma in Miraeus*, p. 700). Yet after this Giselbert, the names of no later abbots are found. Indeed, this recent plantation was, as it were, from its very cradle grievously exposed to the attacks and raids of hostile persons. Before 1162 it was destroyed and burned by Siger, a kinsman of the founder, as appears from the following diploma of Henry, bishop of Liège. Finally, it was burned again about 1226 and utterly perished, the abbot returning with his religious to Averbode. Some ruins of this abbey may still be seen, as well as the chapel of Saint John the Baptist built out of its ruins. Of its property nothing remains except a village with a few *bonaria* of land. These documents were kindly communicated by the Reverend and most esteemed Lord Braunman, canon of the abbey of Averbode and formerly president of the Premonstratensian college at Louvain.] GISELBERT, abbot of the church of Mount Saint John, and his brethren, present and [Col. 0799B] future, who profess the regular life, forever.

It accords with the clemency of apostolic governance to love religious persons and to unite their places to itself in pious protection. For it is recognized as worthy and consonant with propriety that we, who have been raised to the governance of the Churches, should both protect them from the malice of wicked people and cherish them by the patronage of the Apostolic See.

Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the church of the blessed apostles John and James, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, [Col. 0799C] God favoring, by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: namely, the place itself, with the entire wood and the adjoining lands, as Walter, canon of Saint Gereon, and his brother Hubert granted them to you in pious devotion. We also decree that no cleric or layperson whatsoever shall exact tithes from you from the newly cultivated lands which you till with your own hands and at your own expense.

We further provide that the aforesaid church shall not cease from divine office on account of a general interdict of the parish, but rather that, with the doors closed and excommunicated and interdicted persons excluded, you may celebrate the divine offices in a low voice. We also forbid any brother, after making profession there, to leave that cloister without permission of the abbot and the whole [Col. 0800A] community; and no one may dare retain a departing brother without the common safeguard of letters. We grant that the burial-ground of that place shall be free: whoever decides to be buried there may be so buried, unless he or she is excommunicated; no one may obstruct it, provided always that the right of the mother church is preserved.

We therefore decree that absolutely no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain or diminish possessions taken away, or harass it with any vexations; but that its goods shall be kept whole, to benefit in every way those for whose government and support they were granted, without prejudice to the canonical right of the diocesan bishop and to the authority of the Apostolic See. As an acknowledgment of this protection received from the Apostolic See, you shall pay every year to us and our successors one gold denarius in the coinage of Cologne. [Col. 0800B] If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of rank and recognize himself or herself as answerable before divine judgment for the wrong committed; let that person be excluded from the most holy body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, and be subject at the last judgment to severe punishment. But upon all who preserve what is right for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, and may they find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

[Col. 0800C] Pope Celestine II.  
I, Amadeus, bishop of Sabina.  
I, Theodoric, bishop of Santa Rufina.  
I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia.  
I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum.  
I, Peter, bishop of Albano.  
I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus.  
I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna.  
Aubert, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Gerard, cardinal priest and librarian of the holy Roman Church, [Col. 0800D] on the sixth day before the Ides of February, in the seventh indiction, in the year 1143 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Celestine II.

### XXXIV. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Saviour at Florence.  
*(A.D. 1144, February 15.)*

[MITTARELLI, *Camaldolese Annals*, III, 281.]

[Col. 0801A]

Pope Celestine II receives under his own protection and that of blessed Peter the monastery of Saint Saviour near Florence, decreeing that the same monastery shall hold unimpaired, by papal authority, whatever possessions or goods it has or shall have in perpetuity, by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means. He decreed that certain goods should be specified by their proper names: namely, the tithes which that monastery had possessed without challenge for forty years; likewise, the right which it has in the church of Saint Christopher; likewise, that it should have free burial for those who, by devotion or final wish, choose to be buried there, while preserving the right of the mother church. All the cardinals subscribed.

Given at the Lateran in the year of the Lord 1143, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of March, in the first year of his pontificate.

### XXXV. To the clergy and people of Prato—That they obey Bishop A[tto] of Pistoia.  
*(A.D. 1144, February 17.)*

[ZACHARIA, *Medieval Anecdotes*, 212.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the clergy and people of Prato: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0801C] It is evident that obedience is the stability and foundation of all virtues, and that a person is shown to be unfaithful by its absence, even if he or she appears faithful. Therefore, by apostolic writing we command you humbly to render to our venerable brother A., bishop of Pistoia, a discerning and religious man, due obedience and reverence without any contradiction, as to your own shepherd and bishop of your souls. You shall do him no injury concerning the possessions and revenues of his Church, nor permit others to do so.

Given at the Lateran, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of March.

### XXXVI. Privilege for the Church of Pistoia.  
*(A.D. 1144, February 17.)*

[ZACHARIA, *ibid.*, p. 229.]

[Col. 0801D]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother ATTO, bishop of Pistoia, and to his successors canonically promoted forever.

The Church of Pistoia, through the generosity of the Lord, author of all good things, has from long past times in the regions of Tuscany possessed this special prerogative: that it has shone under the governance of wise and discerning pastors, and through their diligence has received growth pleasing to the Lord both in temporal and spiritual affairs. We likewise rejoice with due gladness because the providence of the heavenly dispensation has appointed you, venerable brother Bishop Atto, a man indeed wise and proved in religious life, pastor of that same place, and divine mercy has called you to govern and instruct its people by doctrine and by the example of your life. Therefore, the more religious your person is, and the more devoted the aforesaid Church of Pistoia, over which you preside by God’s appointment, has been to blessed Peter, the more gratefully the necessity laid upon us by the office of the apostolate obliges us to fortify by the authority of an apostolic privilege that Church committed to you by the Lord, and to preserve for it its right unimpaired and entire.

Following the example of our predecessors of blessed memory, Popes Paschal and Innocent, bishops of Rome, we therefore decree by this present enactment that all things which the same Church now possesses justly and lawfully, or may in future acquire through the grant of pontiffs, [Col. 0802B] the generosity of kings, etc. The parish church at Villiano; the parish church of St. Quiricus; the parish church of Spanareclo; the parish church of Saturnana; the parish church of Brandelio; the parish church of Calloria, with all chapels and tithes rightfully belonging to them; the parish church of Vinaciano; the parish church of Seiano; the parish church of St. Paul; the parish church of St. Hippolytus; the parish church of Ajolo; the parish church of St. Justus; the parish church of Colonica, with its people, tithes, and other appurtenances rightfully belonging to it; and, in Prato, the parish church of St. Stephen.

Therefore let absolutely no one, as below in the bull of Eugenius III, 3 Ides of December, 1152. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Teruderinus, bishop of St. Rufina, have subscribed. [Col. 0802D] I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of St. Lawrence in Damaso. I, Rainerius, cardinal priest of the title of St. Stephen, have subscribed.
