### XXXVII. Privilege for the Church of St. Mary of Undersford. (1144, February 18.)

[Monum. Boic., X, p. 238.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons RICHARD, provost of the church of St. Mary of Undinesdorf, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity. [Col. 0803B]

A desire shown to concern the profession of religion and the salvation of souls ought fittingly to be granted by us with willing mind, and suitable assistance ought to be bestowed upon the desires of those who ask. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, and protect by the patronage of this writing the aforesaid church, founded on his own allod by the noble man Otto, Count Palatine, and offered to blessed Peter under a payment of one bezant to be rendered annually to us and our successors. First, indeed, we decree that the canonical order according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine shall be preserved there inviolably for all time.

Moreover, whatever possessions or goods that church now possesses justly and canonically, or may hereafter acquire, God favouring it, through grants of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. [Col. 0803C] You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and the ordination of clerics to be promoted to sacred orders from the diocesan bishop, provided that he is Catholic, enjoys the favour and communion of the Apostolic See, and is willing to supply these things to you freely and without any improper exaction. Otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer. By apostolic authority we also grant freedom of burial to the aforesaid church.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; rather, all things shall be kept whole for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make suitable amends, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the last judgment let him be subject to severe vengeance. [Col. 0804A] But upon all who preserve what is just for that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good works and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Gerard, cardinal priest and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of March, in the seventh indiction, in the year 1143 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Celestine II.

### XXXVIII. Privilege for the Church of Stromberg. (1144, February 19.)

[LACOMBLET, *Urkundenbuch*, I, p. 348.]

[Col. 0804B] CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons WALTHER, provost of the church of St. Mary of Stromberch, and his brethren, present and future, to be regularly established, in perpetuity.

It accords with the mercy of apostolic governance to love religious persons and to fortify their places with pious protection. For it is recognized as worthy and consonant with propriety that we, who have been assumed to the governance of churches, should both protect them from the malice of wicked people and cherish them under the patronage of the Apostolic See. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the aforesaid church, in which you are dedicated to divine service; and we strengthen it by the privilege of this writing. We decree that the canonical order according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine shall be preserved there inviolably for all time.

Moreover, whatever possessions or goods that church now possesses justly and canonically, or may hereafter acquire, God favouring it, through grants of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: the estate at Steintelberch with its appurtenances; the estate at Mechitinheim with its appurtenances; whatever you rightfully possess in cultivated or uncultivated lands, vineyards, meadows, woods, pastures, mills, or [Col. 0804D] other goods; also the tithes of the whole mountain upon which your church stands, and of all newly cultivated lands worked within its boundary—that is, within the mark of the people living at Winthere. We likewise confirm everything else that has been granted to you by Arnold, archbishop of Cologne, with reasonable foresight.

Certainly, no cleric or layperson whatsoever may presume to demand tithes from you upon the produce which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or upon the sustenance of your animals. Your advocate shall demand nothing from you and shall impose no levy upon your goods or possessions; rather, he shall be content with the one gold penny of Cologne currency which, according to the agreement made between you and him at the dedication of your church, is to be paid to him annually by you. You may also, during a general interdict of that bishopric, celebrate divine offices in a low voice behind closed doors, with excommunicated and interdicted persons excluded. We further grant that burial in that place be free; and no one may hinder those who have chosen to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated, while the rights of the mother church are nevertheless preserved. As a sign of the protection received from the Apostolic See, you shall pay to us and our successors each year two book-clasps.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; rather, all things shall be kept whole for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the canonical right of the archbishop of Cologne and the reverence due to the Apostolic See. [Col. 0805B] If in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make suitable amends, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the last judgment let him be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve what is just for that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good works and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

### XXXIX. He settles the controversy of the monks of Vivo and Camaldoli. (1144, February 23.)

[MITTARELLI, *Annales Camaldulenses*, III, appendix, p. 406.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons BONO, prior of Vivo, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

By the administration of the Apostolic See entrusted to us by God, we are compelled to remove the scandals of religious brethren and to provide for their peace and tranquillity. Therefore, after hearing the arguments on both sides and carefully investigating, with the counsel of our brethren, we have decided that the controversy long disputed between you and the religious brethren of Camaldoli is to be settled in the following manner. Since it is recognized that the place itself has flourished in religious life almost from the beginning of its foundation through the brethren of Camaldoli, we decree, in order that the bond of charity may be preserved among you, that the prior to be appointed in that place at any time shall be elected from that congregation by the brethren of the same place, according to the Rule of St. Benedict, if a suitable man is found there. The person elected shall, within forty days, promise the prior of Camaldoli obedience in the observance of the order, with all humility. But if—God forbid!—a suitable man cannot be found there, [Col. 0807A] he shall be elected by the brethren of Vivo from the Congregation of Camaldoli, as stated above, according to the Rule.

Whenever the prior and Camaldolese brethren come to Vivo, they shall be received as brethren in common in choir, refectory, and dormitory; and the prior shall hold the first place both in chapter and elsewhere, shall correct with reasonable foresight what needs correction in the order, and shall establish what must be established. The prior of Vivo, moreover, shall go to the annual chapter of the Camaldolese brethren and shall be honoured there and elsewhere as one of the senior priors of that congregation. If he and his brethren should at any time come to Camaldoli, they shall be treated in common within the monastery, both in choir and elsewhere. Notices of deceased brethren shall be received on both sides according to the custom of the Camaldolese Congregation, and offices shall be celebrated for them.

If in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our decree, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make suitable amends, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord, the Redeemer; and at the last judgment let him be subject to severe vengeance. But upon those who observe these provisions may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruits of good works and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

[Col. 0807C] **LET THERE BE PEACE IN YOUR + STRENGTH, SAINT PETER, + SAINT PAUL, CELESTINE + POPE II, AND ABUNDANCE + IN YOUR TOWERS.**

### XL. He receives the monastery of Ensdorf under protection, confirms its goods, and establishes its rights. (1144, February 24.)

[RIED, *Codex diplomaticus*, I, 207.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons THIEDOIN, abbot of the Church of Ensdorf, and his brethren, present and future, [Col. 0808B] professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

A desire shown to concern the profession of religion and the salvation of souls ought fittingly to be granted by us with willing mind, and suitable assistance ought to be bestowed upon the desires of those who ask. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the aforesaid church, in which you are dedicated to divine service; and we strengthen it by the privilege of this writing. We decree that whatever possessions or goods that church now possesses justly and canonically, or may hereafter acquire, God favouring it, through grants of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors.

We prohibit any brother, after making profession there, from leaving that cloister without the permission of the abbot and the entire community; and no one may dare retain one who departs without a letter of authorization from the community. The abbot serving at the time shall freely administer the goods of the monastery with the common counsel of the brethren, and shall reasonably correct what requires correction there. So that you may devote yourselves more freely to divine service, we prohibit any advocate from holding a court within the circuit of your wall unless invited by the abbot. We further decree that burial in that place be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who have chosen to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated, while the rights of the mother church are nevertheless preserved. [Col. 0808D]

Certainly, no one whatsoever may demand from you tithes on produce that you cultivate with your own hands and at your own expense. We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or burden it with any annoyances; rather, all things shall be kept whole for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the canonical right of the diocesan bishop and the authority of the Apostolic See. If in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make suitable amends, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the last judgment let him be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve what is just for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good works and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen. [Col. 0809A]

### XLI. To the canons of St. Alexander of Bergamo. (1144, February 24.)

[LUPI, *Codex diplomaticus Bergomensis*, II, 1047.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the canons of St. Alexander of Bergamo, [Col. 0809D] greetings and apostolic blessing.

We grieve with paternal concern over the dispute conducted between you and the canons of St. Vincent, and we willingly intend to devote ourselves to restoring peace and concord among you. Therefore, by this present writing we command that on the next Sunday upon which “The Good Shepherd” is read, two of the wiser and more discerning among you come into our presence and bring with them the ancient and modern privileges of your church, especially those of our predecessor Pope Innocent of good memory, so that, after the privileges have been examined and the arguments of both parties heard, we may then establish, with the Lord’s help, what ought to be settled between you. Furthermore, we command you by way of request to bear patiently the fact that, on this occasion, we have restored the priestly office to priests under interdict. [Col. 0810A]

Given at the Lateran, on the sixth day before the Kalends of March.

### XLII. He confirms to the monastery of Cluny the church of St. Vincent, granted by Berengarius, bishop of Salamanca. (1144, February 24.)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 594.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons PETER, abbot of Cluny, and his brethren, greetings and apostolic blessing.

Although by the office of the apostolate enjoined upon us by God we are debtors to all the children of the Catholic Church, it is fitting that we should give ourselves with a more earnest zeal of charity to you who adhere more especially to the Holy Roman Church. Therefore, wishing to provide with paternal care for you as special sons of blessed Peter, we confirm by this page of our present writing the church of St. Vincent of Salamanca, which our brother Berengarius, bishop of that city, canonically granted to you with the assent of the prior of that place and of our dearest son A., king of Spain. If anyone, knowing this page of our confirmation, should attempt to act against it, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul. [Col. 0810B]

Given at the Lateran, on 6 March.

### XLIII. Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary of Bonosolatio. (1144, February 26.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, III, 104.]

[Col. 0810C]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons LANFRANC, abbot of St. Mary of Bonosolatio, and his brethren, present and future, to be regularly established, in perpetuity.

Since without the true worship of Religion, etc., down to “shall remain.” Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: namely, the tithes which you have hitherto possessed canonically; what you possess on Mount Caroso and in the estate of that same castle; at the rock of Mensola; in the estate at Aquaricu; and whatever you possess in the valley of Carza. [Col. 0810D] Upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it through any stratagem of intrusion or through violence. Rather, you shall be free, without anyone’s opposition, to elect an abbot by common counsel, or by the counsel of the sounder party, according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict. You shall also have the faculty and permission, without anyone’s opposition, to receive for conversion clerics or free laymen living in the secular state.

We further grant that burial in that place be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who have chosen to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated, while the rights of the mother church are nevertheless preserved. As a token of the protection received from the Apostolic See, you shall pay annually to us and our successors twelve denarii of Luccan currency. We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb that monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or burden it with any annoyances; rather, all things shall be kept whole for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the canonical right of the diocesan bishop and the authority of the Apostolic See. If in future anyone, etc. But upon all, etc. Amen. [Col. 0811A]

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Peter, bishop of Albano. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of St. Cecilia. [Col. 0811B] I, Ubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of St. Praxedes. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of St. Lawrence in Damaso. I, Manfredus, cardinal priest of the title of St. Sabina. I, Aribertus, cardinal priest of the title of St. Anastasia. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Rodulphus, cardinal deacon of the title of St. Lucy in Septasalis. I, John, cardinal deacon of St. Mary the New.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Gerard, cardinal priest and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Kalends of March, in the tenth indiction; in the year 1192 of the Lord’s Incarnation. [Note: [Col. 0811D] The chronological marks are corrupt.] In the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Celestine II. [Col. 0811C]

### XLIV. To the archbishop of Toledo—That he restore certain parishes to Bishop A. (1144, February 26.)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 594.]

Our beloved son G., cardinal deacon and legate of the Apostolic See, as we have learned from him himself, commanded our brother, the bishop of Astorga, on various occasions to restore without any condition the parishes of Tepolis and Caldellis to our venerable brother M., bishop of Ourense. Yet he not only failed entirely to carry out that command, but also celebrated divine offices in those same churches after they had been placed under interdict by that same our son because of contempt and disobedience. But since we have learned that he has entered upon the way of all flesh, we command you by this present writing to cause those same parishes to be fully restored to the aforesaid bishop within forty days after receiving this writing, in accordance with the command of that same our son. Once the restoration has been made, when the Church of Astorga has by God’s grace obtained a Catholic pastor, if it believes that it possesses any right in those same churches, the case of both parties shall be heard in your presence at a suitable place and time, and shall be concluded with due settlement. If anyone should rashly attempt to obstruct that restoration, cause the interdict which the aforesaid our son, the cardinal, imposed upon those same churches to be firmly observed. [Col. 0812A]

Given at the Lateran, on the fourth day before the Kalends of March.

### XLV. Privilege for the Monastery of Michelsfeld. (1144, February 28.)

[USSERMANN, *Episcopatus Bambergensis, Probationes*, 93.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ADELBERTO, abbot of the church of Michelsfeld, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

It is fitting to grant ready assent to religious desires, so that faithful devotion may obtain a swift result. [Col. 0812B] Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the aforesaid church, in which you are dedicated to divine service; and we strengthen it by the privilege of this writing. We decree that whatever possessions or goods that church now possesses justly and canonically, or may hereafter acquire, God favouring it, through grants of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors.

We prohibit any brother, after making profession there, from leaving that cloister without the permission of the abbot and the entire community; and no one may dare retain one who departs without a letter of authorization from the community. The abbot serving at the time shall freely administer the goods of the monastery with the common counsel of the brethren, and shall reasonably correct what requires correction there. [Col. 0812C]

So that you may devote yourselves more freely to divine service, we prohibit any advocate from holding a court within the circuit of your wall unless invited by the abbot. We further decree that burial in that place be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who have chosen to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated, while the rights of the mother church are nevertheless preserved. Certainly, no one whatsoever may demand from you tithes on produce which you cultivate with your own hands within the appurtenances of your cell. We prohibit the holding within the wall of your cloister of dances or secular noise by which your repose might be disturbed or the observance of the rule broken. We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb that same church, etc. [Col. 0812D]

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Gerard, cardinal priest and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Kalends of March, in the seventh indiction, in the year 1143 of the Lord’s Incarnation. [Note: [Col. 0812D] Correct to 1144; for in the preceding year, at that month, he was not yet pope.] In the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope CELESTINE II.

### XLVI. To Conrad, archbishop of Salzburg. (1144, March 1.)

[MOICHELBEK, *Chronicon Benedictoburanum*, p. 93.]

[Col. 0813A]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother CONRAD, archbishop of Salzburg, greetings and apostolic blessing.

We have received the complaint of the brethren of Benediktbeuern that a certain man named Oudalricus, together with his only daughter and all that he possessed, offered himself to their monastery. But afterward, having broken his vow, he departed from them and transferred himself to the community of Admont. As we have learned from the letters of our venerable brother Gwalter, bishop of Augsburg, this case was heard in your court and, although suitable witnesses were produced, was not settled by your fraternity—a matter at which we are surprised. Since [Col. 0813B] it was not settled by your fraternity—a matter at which we are surprised. Since we desire that justice be rendered to each person, we command your fraternity by this present writing to summon both parties into your presence, hear the case carefully, and endeavour to bring it to its due conclusion with impartial equity.

Given at the Lateran, on the Kalends of March.

### XLVII. Privilege for the Church of Lille. (1144, March 3.)

[MIRAEI, *Opera diplomatica*, IV, 15.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons DESIDERIUS, provost of the Church of Lille, and the canons, present and future, canonically established in perpetuity, greetings and apostolic [Col. 0813C] blessing.

The authority of the apostolic see entrusted to us . . . Beloved sons in the Lord, inclining to the prayers of our venerable brethren Simon, bishop of Noyon, and Milo, bishop of Thérouanne, and likewise of the noble man Theodoric, count of Flanders, we graciously admit your reasonable petitions, and receive under the protection of the same prince of the apostles and of ourselves the Church of Lille, founded in honour of Blessed Peter; and we strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods the church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, [Col. 0813D] or by other just means, with God’s favour acquire, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have judged it proper to set forth the following by their proper names: on the same island, the altar of Saint Stephen with two parts of the tithe; the altar of Saint Maurice; and the altar of the Holy Saviour; the altar of Leschin, with two parts of the tithe; the altar of Werwhie with two parts of the tithe; the altar of Anaspia with two parts of the tithe; the altar of Werleghehem with two parts of the tithe; the altar of Fleis; the altar of Marca, called that of Saint Amand; the altar of Wenesbrechies; the altar of Perenchies; the altar of Long-prato; the altar of Quesnois; the altar of Lombersart; the altar of Ulmo; the altar of Segedin; the altar of Primeca; the altar of Campingehem; the altar [Col. 0814A] of Rumh; the altar of Haluwin and Buibesca; the altar of Lauba; the altar of Huila; the altar of Maclines; and the altar of Ghides. Two parts of the tithe of Dehuliesmons, two parts of the tithe of Wasemes, two parts of the tithe of Rollers, and the tenth part of all the revenues of the count of Flanders belonging to the island. In the diocese of Thérouanne, the altar of Flambertenges; the altar of Drawa nultra. In the diocese of Arras, the altar of Moncellis.

We further prohibit the parishioners of your island, so long as they are willing to administer ecclesiastical justice within their own parish, as they are known to have done from ancient times, from being compelled to go outside that parish. Let the canons of the same church reside within their [Col. 0814B] cloister, as is just and established by ancient custom.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away or retain its possessions once taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all shall be preserved intact, wholly available for the benefit of those uses for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the canonical right of the diocesan bishop and the authority of the apostolic see. . . . .

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Thirteen cardinals also subscribed.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Gerard, cardinal-priest and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Nones of March, in the seventh indiction, in the year 1143 from the Incarnation of the Lord, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord [Col. 0814C] Pope Celestine II.

## XLVIII. Privilege for the Church of Saint Mary Magdalene.  
*(A.D. 1144, March 4.)*

*[Mémoires et documents inédits de la Franche-Comté, II, 317.]*

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, etc. . . .

We confirm the liberty and safe-conduct within the city granted by Hugh of Salins, of blessed memory, archbishop of Besançon, to your cloister and the houses adjoining it, as is contained in the charter of that same archbishop. We also confirm the possessions bestowed by that same brother, namely: the holding of the armourer, the chapel with its oven and appurtenances; the street at [Col. 0814D] the eastern end of your church, between the holding of Sibo and Varnerius and the holding of Odo on the western side; the street extending from the gate on the southern side of the same city to your refectory; the land from the Gate of the Arsenals to the dormitory of the canons, whether occupied by houses or vineyards or vacant; the wood which lies near the city . . . . the church of Saint James at Besançon within the arenas, with its appurtenances; the holding of Remigius above the Dubium; the holding of Constantine near the mill in the district of Baptens; a share of the mill of Baptens; the revenues called Monaydae at the winepress of Naal; the fodder-right from your land, which you won in litigation against Hubald of Albans; the land of your church, whether occupied by vineyards or houses or vacant; three solidi of annual rent at the general court [Col. 0815A] by gift of Stephen the viscount; the tithes of your parish, as you have hitherto canonically possessed them; and we decree that the ancient and reasonable customs of that church shall remain valid.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Gerard, cardinal-priest and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Nones of March, in the seventh indiction, in the year 1143 from the Incarnation of the Lord, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Celestine II.

## XLIX. Privilege for the Church of Fiesole.  
*(A.D. 1144, March 6.)*

*[UGHELLI, Italia sacra, III, 242.]*

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother JONATHAS, bishop of Fiesole, and to his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity. [Col. 0815B]

By the office of the apostolate committed to us by God, it befits us to provide with fatherly care for our brethren, both those nearby and those far away, and to preserve to the churches known to serve the Lord their respective rights, so that, just as by God’s ordering we are called Fathers in name, so also we may prove ourselves such in deed. For this reason, beloved brother in the Lord, we graciously admit your reasonable petitions, receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves the Church of Fiesole, over which by God’s gift you are known to preside, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter, by reasonable means and with God’s [Col. 0815C] favour, acquire, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors, and through you for the Church of Fiesole. Among these we have judged it proper to specify the following by their proper names: the monastery of Saint Bartholomew, situated at Fiesole; the monastery of Saint Martin at Maiano; the monastery of Saint Gaudentius at the foot of the Alps; the parish church of Saint Peter of Romena; the parish church of Blessed Peter of Cascina; the parish church of Saint John of Caprilia; and the parish church of Saint Leoninus in Collina. We likewise confirm all the other parish churches and churches known to belong by right to the Church of Fiesole, together with castles, estates, and other possessions, as they were specifically confirmed to you in the privilege of our predecessor Pope Innocent of blessed memory. Nor may anyone presume, without your assent, to appropriate to himself the appointment of the aforesaid monasteries [Col. 0815D] and baptismal churches subject to the Church of Fiesole. In the chapels of your parish churches, however, let the parish priests have free administration and due obedience, without anyone’s contradiction, as was granted to them through the privilege of Pope Paschal of happy memory, saving the due reverence of their own bishop. We confirm to you, according to the statutes of the canons, a share of the tithes, offerings, bequests, and other ecclesiastical revenues throughout your bishopric. We forbid any church to be built in the same bishopric, or any church already built to be subjected to anyone without your permission, while nevertheless preserving in all things the right and authority of the Roman see.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb that church, take away or retain its possessions once taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all shall be preserved intact for you and your brethren, wholly available for the benefit of those uses for whose governance and support they were granted. If anyone therefore, etc. But upon all, etc. Amen.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed. I, Imar, bishop of Tusculum, have subscribed. I, Peter, bishop of Albano, have subscribed. I, Raynerius, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Prisca, [Col. 0816B] have subscribed. I, Gozzo, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Cecilia, have subscribed. I, Thomas, cardinal-priest of the title of Vestina, have subscribed. I, Nicholas, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Cyriacus, have subscribed. I, Manfred, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Sabina, have subscribed. I, Guido, deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Gerard, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Domnica, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary the New, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Gerard, cardinal-priest and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Nones of March, in the sixth indiction, in the year 1143 from the Incarnation of the Lord, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Celestine II, etc.

## L. Privilege for the Church of Ferrara.  
*(A.D. 1144, March 6.)*

*[COCQUELINES, II, 265.]*

[Col. 0816C]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother GRYPHO, bishop of Ferrara, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

By the Lord’s ordering, we are seen to have been placed upon the throne of the apostolic see in order that we may care for all churches, assign to each its right, and especially preserve whole and inviolate the rights of those which belong to Blessed Peter. Therefore, following the example of our predecessor Pope Innocent of blessed memory, and in accordance with the tenor of the privileges, we have decreed that the bishop of Ferrara shall be elected [Col. 0816D] by our cardinals and consecrated by the bishop of the Roman see; and by this decree we establish that the Church of Ferrara shall remain under the right and dominion of the apostolic see. Therefore, while you, clergy and people of Ferrara, remain steadfast, following the example of our predecessors of happy memory—Vitalian, Hadrian, Leo, Benedict, John, Alexander, Paschal, and Innocent, Roman pontiffs—we confirm to the holy Church of Ferrara, as a daughter of the apostolic see, the estates and patrimonies of that mother: namely, the great estate called Ferrara, formerly Babylonian, with its twelve dependent estates; and we subject to it eleven other, smaller estates of ours, with all obedience and service: namely, the estate and riverbank of Palatiolum with its twelve dependent estates; [Col. 0817A] Constantiacus with its twelve dependent estates; likewise the estate of Quartisiana with its twelve dependent estates; the whole and entire estate of Donoro with its twelve dependent estates; also the estate of Carulum; the estate of Salerta with its twenty-four dependent estates; the estates of Senetica and Castilione, likewise with their dependent estates; and in the same manner the estate called Fermignana with all its dependent estates. These aforesaid estates, with everything belonging to their rights, we give and convey, by this charter of donation and transfer, out of the dominion, right, and power of this holy Roman Church to the holy Church of Ferrara. Henceforth it shall be lawful for you, dearest brother Bishop Grypho, and for your successors, to appoint and consecrate churches, with clerics, priests, and deacons, in each estate. We wholly decree that the Church of Ferrara, with its whole parish, shall be preserved perpetually in the right, dominion, and privilege of our holy Roman Church of Blessed Peter, whose patrimony it is, and shall always be under our election, appointment, and consecration; so that whoever is elected, appointed, and consecrated there by us may enjoy the full integrity of its honour and authority.

The boundaries and limits of the county of Ferrara are these: on the east, on one side of the River Po; on the other, our estates of Fiscalia and Veteraria. From Veteraria to the ditch of Bossonis, they cross the River Sandalo as far as Bucciletum; through Bucciletum they cross the River Gabiana by Luduria; they encircle the settlement of Marazam and Madrariam, reaching Maletum; from Maletum they proceed alongside Argile Anxianum, through marshes and fisheries, as far as Vitrica; they come to the ditch of Burana, and by the ditch of Burana emerge into the Po, and descend westward as far as Ulmo Formosa, which is the fixed boundary between Romagna and Lombardy. On the other side of the river, the boundaries likewise begin in the east at the hill of Sine, which is the boundary between our county of Ferrara and our other county of Comacchio; they extend through marshes and fisheries as far as the ditch of Silvulae, encircle the estate of Corneto and Longano, which belongs to our county of Ferrara; thence they descend westward through marshes and fisheries to the River Tartaro, and follow that River Tartaro [Col. 0817D] to the River Po.

Certainly, we abolish bad and evil customs imposed upon the inhabitants of the great estate of Ferrara, except that, as they have been accustomed, each free person shall annually give, through their representative, one Venetian penny of the head-tax to support our holy Roman Church. Of the rent, tribute, and toll from the riverbank and river, we grant one half as a benefaction for the common benefit and the improvement or restoration of the said great estate, and reserve the other half to ourselves. Likewise, we retain one half of the market toll and remit the other half to our aforesaid bishop. [Col. 0818A] We likewise retain the general court under the dominion and power of the holy Roman Church, so that justice may be administered before our representative once a year, and observed by all for three days. We exact no levy, fodrum, small or unjust service, payment, or custom; but, out of fear and love of God, we have remitted all such burdens to all inhabitants of the aforesaid great estate of our holy Church of Saint George, and we subject the other smaller estates, as has been said above, with all their services.

Furthermore, whatever churches and possessions, and whatever goods, you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter by reasonable means and with God’s favour acquire, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors, and through you for the Church of Ferrara. Among these we have judged it proper to specify the following by their proper names: the parish church of Saint George beyond the Po; the parish church of Saint Mary of the Po; the parish church of Saint George of Tamara; the parish church of Saint Mary of Gabiano; the parish church of Saint Mary of Vicoventia; the parish church of Saint Peter of Cupario; the parish church of Saint Stephen of Formignana; the parish church of Saint Apollinaris of Frisicallo; the parish church of Saint Martin of Rupina; the parish church of Saint Mary of Vicobariono; [Col. 0818B] the parish church of Saint Mary of Septempolicinio; the parish church of Saint Stephen of Caligo; the parish church of Saint Donatus of Peduvio; the parish church of Saint Antoninus of Picazolio; the parish church of Saint George of Trecenta; the parish church of Saint Mary of Cinisello; and the parish church of Saint Michael of Bregantio, with their chapels and appurtenances—saving in all things the authority of the apostolic see.

If any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowingly contravening this document of our constitution, should rashly presume either to diminish the Church of Ferrara in respect of the things stated above, or to take away from the holy apostolic see its rights in them, as set forth above, he shall pay to that same holy apostolic see one hundred pounds of the finest gold as a penalty and settlement. Unless he correct what he has wickedly presumed by fitting satisfaction, let him lose the dignity of his authority and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the last judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. [Col. 0818D] But upon all who observe what is just toward the same churches, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Guido, cardinal-priest of Saint Chrysogonus. I, Rainerius, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Prisca. I, Goizo, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Thomas, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Vestina. I, Ubaldus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Gilibertus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Mark. [Col. 0819A] I, Nicholas, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Cyriacus. I, Manfred, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Sabina. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Theodewicus, bishop of Saint Rufina. I, Albert, bishop of Ostia. I, Imar, bishop of Tusculum. I, Peter, bishop of Albano. I, George, deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Gerard, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Domnica. [Col. 0820A] I, John, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary the New. I, John Paparo, cardinal-deacon of Saint Adrian.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Gerard, cardinal-priest and librarian of the holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Nones of May, in the seventh indiction, in the year 1144 from the Incarnation of the Lord, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Celestine II.

# IN THE YEAR OF THE LORD 1145: POPE LUCIUS II

[Col. 0819]

## NOTICE

*(MANSI, Councils, vol. XXI, col. 607)*

[Col. 0819B] Lucius, whose name had been Gerard, was born at Bologna, of Albert, a citizen of Bologna, from the Caccianimica family. In the judgment of Otto of Freising, he was a man worthy of the priestly office because of his gentleness and humility. From being cardinal of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, he became pontiff in the year of the Lord 1144, in the time of Emperor Conrad. Baronius records the following concerning him from a Vatican manuscript:

> “This man was from the province of Emilia, a native of Bologna, son of Viseus. He was received by Lord Pope Honorius into the title of Holy Cross and made librarian of the Roman Church. Like a good shepherd, he greatly and abundantly increased his church, both in buildings and possessions, making it rich from being most poor. He reformed the fabric of that church from top to bottom for the better [Col. 0819C], built anew the cloister with all its offices, and, by God’s aid, established there a community of regular canons.”

Because of his learning and the merits of his life, Pope Innocent bound this distinguished man more closely to himself after the death of Chancellor Haimeric, made him chancellor of the apostolic see, and at his own death entrusted to him the goods of the Church, as to its principal and worthiest member. As a prudent and strong man, having taken counsel with the faithful of the Church, he compelled the senators, who had ascended the Capitol against the prohibition of his predecessor Pope Innocent, to renounce the senate. The truce which he made in war with Roger, king of Sicily, is indicated by his letter to Peter of Cluny. “Having suffered a grievous persecution from the citizens,” says Freising in Book VII, chapter 31, “he sends humble letters to King Conrad, containing both an account of his own oppression [Col. 0819D] and thanks to God for the king’s safety and prosperity, and inviting him to the protection of the Roman Church.” And shortly after reciting a fragment of the letter mentioned, he says: “They did not fear to afflict the soul of the righteous man from day to day.” Worn down by daily torments and by weariness of life, he died within a year of his pontificate, on the fifth day before the Kalends of March, having sat for eleven months and fourteen days.

In the Vatican codex entitled *On the Privileges of the Roman Church*, Baronius says that among the deeds of Lucius it is asserted, concerning the occasion of his death, that when he was attempting to drive the Romans, stirred up to revolutionary designs, from the Capitol, he was struck by an uncertain blow of a stone, fell ill as a result, and departed this life. In the time of this pontiff, [Col. 0820C] Alfonso, duke of Portugal, out of devotion toward his duchy, made it tributary to the Roman Church, at an annual payment of four ounces of gold. Thus Innocent III states in Letter 100 of Book I of his letters. And so, while the Romans rebelled against and opposed the Roman Church, distant princes revered it and voluntarily submitted themselves to it.

In the days of this pontiff, Otto of Freising writes in *The Deeds of Frederick*, Book I, chapters 27 and 28, Arnold, otherwise Arnaldus, a man wearing the habit of religion but by no means observing it—as became clear from his teaching—entered the city of Rome. Wishing, out of envy of ecclesiastical honour, to renew the senatorial dignity and equestrian order after the pattern of the ancients, he stirred up almost the whole City, and especially the people, [Col. 0820D] against their pontiff. On this matter they sent letters to Emperor Conrad, which Otto himself reports in the place mentioned above. The followers of this Arnold [Col. 0821A] are called Arnoldists, heretics. Only a few Romans, and those of the more obscure sort, attached themselves to them, and they are called Roman Arnoldists. By the machinations of these men, with Arnold as author and counsellor, occurred the events narrated from Otto of Freising in the *Life of Eugenius III*.

[Col. 0821]

## DIPLOMATIC NOTICE

# LETTERS AND PRIVILEGES OF POPE LUCIUS II

## I. Privilege for the Monastery of Saint Columbanus at Bobbio.  
*(A.D. 1144, March 15.)*

*[UGHELLI, Italia sacra, IV, 977.]*

[Col. 0823A]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons OGLERIUS, abbot of Saint Columbanus at Bobbio, and his brethren both present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

A devout petition ought to be fulfilled by the effect of a favourable decision, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth worthily and the benefit requested may undoubtedly acquire strength. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions; we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves the church of Blessed Columbanus, in which you are devoted to divine service, [Col. 0823B] and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter, by grants of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, with God’s favour acquire, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have judged it proper to specify the following by their proper names: the estate of Saint Martin with its church, and the castle called Petra Carana with its appurtenances; the estate of the Holy Saviour with its church and appurtenances; the estate of the Cross with its church and appurtenances; the estate of Garda, with its churches, jurisdiction, and appurtenances; the estate of Carelli with its church and appurtenances; the estate of Gravilia with its church [Col. 0823C] and appurtenances; the estate called Comorga, with its church, jurisdiction, and appurtenances; the parish church of Saint Alban in Candiubrio with its tithes and appurtenances; the church of Saint Mary at Monte Lungo with its appurtenances; the church of Saint Symphorianus in the estate of Neblani with its tithes and appurtenances; the estate of Saint Martin in the Purple Valley with its tithes and appurtenances; the church of Saint Evasii at Quintiano with its tithes and appurtenances; the church of Saint Peter at Masi with its tithes and appurtenances; the church of Saint George, situated at Monte Acuto, with its tithes and appurtenances; the church of Saint Thomas at Romano with its tithes and appurtenances; the church of Ceresola with its appurtenances; the church of Saint Antoninus of Braida with its appurtenances; [Col. 0823D] the church of Saint George of Montale with its appurtenances; the church of Saint Andrew at Travano with its tithes and appurtenances; the church of Saint Mary in Spelunca with its appurtenances; the New Church [Col. 0824A] with its appurtenances; the church of Saint Bartholomew in Sarto with its appurtenances and half the market; the church of Saint Desiderius with its appurtenances; and the church of Saint Lawrence with its appurtenances.

The market of Saint Columbanus and another market at Oliva; a rent of ten Pavia solidi in the estate of Oremale; the estate of Stabulo; the estate of Cavatina Nova; the tithe of Bradello Antonino; the estate of Busbagno; the estate of Salse; the holding of Gavone; the possession of Tedisius of Cicogni; the estate of Riuturni; Brodium; Pratum Donicatum on Monte Penice; Monte Merconico; the estate of Cereto; the estate of Cavanna with Braida Dominica, Sapetelli, and Roveretum; Monte Cesina; the estate of Roncore; the estate of Faidelli; Pratum Longum; the holding of Rugoli Gambalata; [Col. 0824B] the broken field of Grillo; the field of Pradalia; the holding of Barbutus; the holding of Petra Columba; the holding of Juncaritia; the holding of Silva; the holding of Buzavil; the holding of Costalda; the holding of Conflenti; the holding of Gorda; the holding of the good lord of Caulo; the holdings of Violi; Casaria; the holding of Lisignoli between Bobbio and Trebbia; the holding of Mocio; the holding of Goslino; the holding of Cisino; the holding of Hiblo; the holding of Guizi; the holding of Corezala; the holding of Albino; the holding of Cucco; the holding of Bivis; the holding of Marconis of Caneto; the holding of Saint Desiderius; the holding of Guerro; the tenth part of Giselbertus of Gurra; the holding of Ponzipiodo; the holding of Rusticus of Stavella; the holding of John Benedict of Caulo; the tenth part of Lanfranc of Otto; [Col. 0824C] the holding of Savonarius; the holding of Hugh and Albert of Degathani; the holding in the valley of Lovariola; the holding of Pradelle of Sarto; the holding of Semerzarius; the holding of Pradelle; the holding of Borellus of Sarto; the holding of Semerzarius; the holding of Solario; the holding of Maliollo; the holding of Cojorum; the holding of Petrochus and John of Coniolo; one share at Liobe; one share in the field of John; one share in Parratio; and the rent from Cornulo.

The meadow-land of Ponte; the meadow-land beside the ditch of Batalia; the meadow-land in Campo Fasiani; the meadow-land at Pegni; the meadow-land at Marcelasco. The meadow called Codugnar, with the vineyards adjoining it. A vineyard within the city, and mills. We likewise confirm whatever our venerable brother Simeon, your bishop, or his predecessors, or Aluisa, [Col. 0824D] wife of Marquis Malaspina, with her sons, have reasonably granted to you.

Certainly, no cleric or layman whatsoever may presume to exact tithes from you on the produce of your labours which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or on the increase of your animals. On the death of yourself, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one may be put in charge there by any stratagem of fraud or by force. Rather, it shall be lawful for you, by common counsel or by the counsel of the sounder part, in the fear of God and according to the Rule of Blessed Benedict, to elect an abbot without anyone’s opposition. If the same episcopal see should become vacant or lack a Catholic bishop, it shall be lawful for you to receive chrism, holy oil, the consecration of altars or churches, and the ordination of clerics from whichever bishop you prefer.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away or retain its possessions once taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all shall be preserved intact for the benefit of those uses for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the canonical right of the bishop and the authority of the apostolic see. If any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowingly contravening this document of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he makes fitting satisfaction and amendment, let him lose the dignity of his authority and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the last judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. [Col. 0825C] But upon all who preserve what is just toward the same place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Peter, bishop of Albano, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Callistus, have subscribed. I, Gezo, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Susanna, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal-deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Otto, cardinal-deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. [Col. 0825D] I, Guido, cardinal-deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Baron, chaplain and writer of the sacred palace, on the Ides of March, in the seventh indiction, in the year 1144 from the Incarnation of the Lord, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius II.

## II. Privilege confirming all the goods and rights of the holy Church of Ferrara, which is declared to be and to remain, with all its appurtenances, under the perpetual right of the apostolic see.  
*(A.D. 1144, March 15.)*

*[SAVIOLI, Annali Bolognesi, I, II, 203.]*

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother GRYPHO, bishop of the Church of Ferrara, [Col. 0826A] and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

Established by the Lord in the chair of the Apostolic See for this purpose, we plainly recognize that we ought to exercise care for all churches and preserve intact the right belonging to each, especially to those which belong by right to Blessed Peter. Therefore, following the example of our predecessors of blessed memory, Popes Innocent and Celestine, in accordance with the tenor of their privileges, we decree that the bishop of Ferrara shall be elected by our cardinals and consecrated by the bishop of the Roman See; and we ordain by decree that the Church of Ferrara shall remain under the right and lordship of the Apostolic See. Accordingly, for you, Bishop Gripho, most dear brother, and for the clergy and people of Ferrara persevering in fidelity to Blessed Peter, [Col. 0826B] following the example of our predecessors of good memory, the Roman pontiffs Vitalian, Hadrian, Leo, Benedict, John, Alexander, Paschal, Innocent, and Celestine, we confirm to the holy Church of Ferrara, as a daughter of the Apostolic See, the estates and patrimonies of that same mother: namely, the Babylonian estate, called Ferrara, with its twelve estates; to which we subject eleven other, smaller estates of ours, with every obedience and service: that is, the riverside estate of Palatiolum with twelve estates; likewise the Quartisian estate with twelve estates; and the whole and undivided estate of Donorio with its twelve estates; likewise the people’s estate with twelve estates; also the estate of Curulum; and the estate of Saleta with its twenty-four [Col. 0826C] estates; and in like manner the estate called Formignana, with all its estates.

These aforesaid estates, with all that pertains to them, we give and convey from the lordship, right, and power of this holy Roman Church to the holy Church of Ferrara by this charter of donation, so that henceforth it shall be lawful both for you, most dear brother Bishop Gripho, and for your successors, to appoint and consecrate in each estate churches with clerics, priests, and deacons. We ordain in every respect that the entire parish of the Church of Ferrara shall be kept forever in the right, lordship, and privilege of our holy Roman Church of Blessed Peter, whose patrimony it is, and shall always be subject to our election and consecration; and whatever [Col. 0826D] bishop is elected, ordained, and consecrated shall enjoy the full integrity of this honor and authority.

The boundaries and limits of the county of Ferrara are as follows: on the east, on one side of the River Po, from our fiscal and Veteraria estate, they pass as far as the Bossonis ditch, cross the River Sancti as far as Bucilletum, cross the River Gabiana, go through Ludria, encompass Villamagna, and, reaching Madraria, go as far as Maletum; from Maletum they proceed by Anxian Argile, through marshes and fisheries as far as Vitrica; they come to the Burana ditch, pass through the Burana ditch into the Po, and descend westward as far as Ulmus Formosa, which is the fixed boundary between Romagna and Lombardy. On the other side of the river, the boundaries similarly begin on the east at the hill of Fine, which [Col. 0827A] is the boundary between our county of Ferrara and our other county of Comacchio; they extend through marshes and fisheries as far as the ditch of the little wood, encompass the estates of Cornetum and Longanum, which belong to our county of Ferrara, and thence descend westward through marshes and fisheries to the River Tartaro, proceeding as far as the River Po.

Moreover, we remove evil and wrongful customs from the inhabitants of the greater estate of Ferrara, provided nevertheless that, as they have been accustomed, each free person shall annually give, through their messenger, a single Venetian denarius for the head-tax of the Massarii in aid of the holy Roman Church. Of the revenues from dues, tribute, and toll from the riverbank and river, we grant one half, as a blessing, for the common benefit and improvement [Col. 0827B] or restoration of the aforesaid greater estate, and reserve the other half to ourselves. Likewise, of the market toll we reserve one half to ourselves and remit the other half to the aforesaid bishop.

We likewise retain the general court under the lordship and authority of our holy Roman Church, so that justice shall be administered before our messenger once a year and observed by all for three days. We exact no levy or fodrum, no wrongful or unjust service, payment, or custom; but, out of fear of God and love for our aforesaid holy Church of Blessed George, we spare all inhabitants of that estate, and subject the other smaller estates with all their services, as is written above.

Furthermore, whatever churches and possessions, and whatever goods, you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter, by reasonable means and with God’s favor, acquire, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors, and through you to the Church of Ferrara. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their own names: the parish church of Saint George beyond the Po; the parish church of Saint Mary of Gabiana; the parish church of Saint Mary of Vicoventia; the parish church of Saint Martin opposite the Po; the parish church of Saint Gregory of Tomara; the parish church of Saint Peter of Cupario; the parish church of Saint Stephen of Formignana; the parish church of Saint Apollinaris of Trissicallium; the parish church of Saint Martin of Rupina; [Col. 0827D] the parish church of Saint Mary in the village of Bariono; the parish church of Saint Mary of Seven Policino; the parish church of Saint Stephen of Caligo; the parish church of Saint Donatus of Pedurio; the parish church of Saint Antoninus of Ficarolio; the parish church of Saint George of Trecenta; the parish church of Saint Mary of Cinisello; the parish church of Saint Michael of Bragantio, with its chapels and their appurtenances; and the church of Saint Romanus of Tartaro—while in all matters the authority of the Apostolic See remains reserved.

If any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this charter of our ordinance, should rashly attempt to act against it, or presume either to diminish the Church of Ferrara in the matters written above or to take away from the holy Apostolic See its rights therein, as set forth above, let that person pay, by way of penalty, one hundred pounds of the finest gold to that same holy Apostolic See; and [Col. 0828A] unless the wrongful presumption is corrected by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honor, recognize himself or herself as guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most holy Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, and at the final judgment be subject to severe vengeance.

But upon all who preserve what is just for the same churches, may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ rest, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the severe Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Callixtus. I, Goizo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. [Col. 0828B] I, Thomas, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina. I, Ubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Guilibertus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Mary. I, Nicholas, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cyriacus. I, Manfredus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina. I, Gerard, bishop of Sabina. I, Theodewinus of Saint Rufina. I, Albert, bishop of Ostia. I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina. I, Incarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Peter, bishop of Albano. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of the title of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint George at the Golden Veil. [Col. 0828C] I, Guido, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Mary in Dominica. I, Guido, minister of the altar in the Roman Church. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Gr., unworthy deacon of the holy Roman Church. I, John, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Hadrian. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Michael the Archangel. I, John, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary the New. I, Hugh, deacon of the Roman Church of the title of Saint Lucy in Orphea. I, Astaldus, cardinal deacon of Saint Eustace.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Baro, chaplain and scribe, on the Ides of March, in the seventh indiction, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord [Col. 0828D] Pope Lucius II.

## III. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Peter of Perugia.  
*(Year 1144, March 15.)*

[Margarini, *Bullarium Casinense*, II, 106.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Bernard, abbot of the monastery of Saint Peter situated beside the city of Perugia, and his brethren, present and future, to be regularly promoted, forever.

It is fitting that we readily grant a desire shown to pertain to the purpose of religion and the salvation of souls, and extend suitable assistance to the wishes of petitioners. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and, following in the footsteps of our predecessors, strengthen by the privilege of the Apostolic See especially the monastery in which you are devoted to divine service. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same place now justly and lawfully possesses, or may in future, with God’s favor, acquire by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors, in churches, cells, courts, parish churches, monasteries, estates, and rural holdings. Among them we have thought fit to specify the following by name: namely, the parish churches of Saint Constantius, Saint Rufinus, Saint Martin, and Saint John; the parish church of Saint Martyrius; the church of Saint Benedict at Agellione, with its [Col. 0829B] appurtenances; the church of Saint Justin with its court; the churches of Saint Andrew and Saint Angel of Alliano, with their appurtenances; the churches of Saint Mary in Cicciano and Saint Clement; the court of Casale; the court of Petroniano; whatever belongs to you from the court and church of Saint Donatus in Civitella; and also the land of Hugh, nephew of Berno of Monte Nigro.

We also confirm to you by the protection of the Apostolic See the churches of Saints Apollinaris, Blasius, and Montanus, with their appurtenances, saving the annual rent owed to the Church of Farfa. We further confirm the three estates situated in the county of Perugia: one called Pusulo, another Filoncio, and another called Casalina, with churches, houses, vineyards, fields, gardens, mountains, cultivated and uncultivated lands, and all their appurtenances; the monastery [Col. 0829C] of Saint Angel in the county of Assisi, in the place called Limisano, with cells, chapels, and all that pertains to it; the church of Saint Archangel situated near Lake Perugia; the monastery of Saint Saviour in Pothale; the monastery of Saint Peter in Plojano, with all their appurtenances; the church of Saint Sylvester in Morcella; the church of Saint Donatus; the right which you have in Agello; the church of Saint Mary in Poggio, with its appurtenances; the church of Saint Paul in Monticello; and the church of Saint Peter of Petroniano with its court.

You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and the ordinations of monks who are to be advanced to sacred orders, as well as of clerics belonging to that monastery, from the diocesan [Col. 0829D] bishop, provided that he is Catholic and willing to provide these freely and without wrongful exaction. Otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what you have requested.

Upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed over it through any craft of intrigue or violence, except one whom the brethren, by common consent—or the sounder part of their counsel—have elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict, to be consecrated by the Roman pontiff. We strictly prohibit public masses being celebrated in the same monastery by a bishop, or stations or any ordinations being held, apart from the will of the abbot and brethren, lest any occasion for popular gatherings be given in the retreats of the servants of God. [Col. 0830A] Nor shall any bishop, without the consent of the Roman pontiff, have power to burden, place under interdict, excommunicate, or impose new exactions upon that monastery or its cells. Nor may any secular magnate extort fodrum or any other service from the same monastery or its appurtenances, while the right and lordship of the holy Roman Church are of course reserved.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb that church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, appropriate for personal use things unjustly given, or harass it with reckless vexations. Rather, let all things be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical [Col. 0830B] or secular person in future, knowing this charter of our ordinance, should rashly attempt to act against it, and after a second or third warning fails to make suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honor, recognize himself or herself as guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most holy Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and at the final judgment be subject to severe vengeance.

But upon all who preserve what is just for that same place, may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ rest, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the severe Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. [Col. 0830C] I, Gregory, cardinal priest of Saint Callixtus, have subscribed. I, Goizo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Baro, chaplain and scribe, on the Ides of March, in the seventh indiction, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius II.

## IV. Privilege for the nunnery of the Holy Trinity of the Paraclete.  
*(Year 1144, March 15.)*

[Abelard, *Works*, ed. Cousin, p. 719. Paris, 1849, quarto.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, Heloise, prioress, and the other sisters in the oratory of the Holy Trinity, devoted to divine service, present and future, forever. [Col. 0830D]

Whenever a request is made of us that is recognized as consonant with reason, it is fitting that we grant it willingly and afford appropriate assistance to petitioners’ desires. Therefore, beloved daughters in the Lord, assenting to your just petitions, we receive under the protection of the Apostolic See the monastery of the Holy Trinity, in which you devote yourselves to divine service, and strengthen it by this charter. We decree that whatever possessions or goods you now justly and lawfully possess, or may in future, by grants of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, obtain with the Lord’s help, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you forever. [Col. 0831A]

Moreover, we grant you the right to possess without any opposition the tithes of your labors, which you cultivate at your own expense, and of annual produce. Therefore no one may lawfully rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; rather, let all these things be preserved intact, to be of perpetual benefit to your use. As a token of this liberty received from the Roman Church, you shall pay six coins annually to the Lateran palace.

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this charter of our ordinance, should rashly attempt to act against it and, after a second or third warning, fails to make suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity [Col. 0831B] of office and honor, be cut off from the most holy Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and at the final judgment be subject to severe vengeance. But those who preserve it, through the merits of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul, may obtain the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ and the rewards of eternal blessedness. Amen.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Barrocius, chaplain and scribe, on the Ides of March, in the seventh indiction, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius II.

## V. Privilege for the Church of Cremona.  
*(Year 1144, March 17.)*

[Ughelli, *Italia sacra*, IV, 602.]

[Col. 0831C]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother Obert, bishop of Cremona, and his successors canonically appointed, forever.

Just as no effect should be granted to those who make unjust requests, so the petition of those who desire what is lawful ought not to be delayed. Therefore, beloved brother in Christ, Bishop Obert, graciously assenting to your petitions, for the perpetual security of the holy Church of Cremona, we confirm by Apostolic authority all possessions and goods which that Church now justly possesses or may hereafter, through the Lord’s bounty, justly and canonically acquire. Among all these, the following seemed first to us to require express specification. [Col. 0831D]

Namely, whatever jurisdiction over toll, riverbank dues, and port dues belonging to the city of Cremona pertains to public authority, both from the county of that city itself and from the portion of the court of Sexpilas; also the riverbanks and fisheries from Vulpariolo to the source of the Adda, with mills and with the customary payment from every ship, as is contained in the decree and in your records; likewise the payments made by all ships coming to Cremona for purposes of trade, whether Venetian or other ships, and jurisdiction over all transactions conducted on the aforesaid riverbank.

The jurisdiction of the city within and without, for a distance of five miles. Also the altar of Saint Himerius, the canonry, and [“dest...” uncertain; lacuna], which the canons have been accustomed to receive from the bishop’s hand as a benefice; horses, transport-services, labor-services, jurisdictions, embassies, military expeditions, journeys, the market, [Col. 0832A] and the other matters contained in the aforesaid decree; and the matters concerning the abbot and monastery of Saint Lawrence, as are justly contained in your privileges and imperial decrees.

Furthermore, the churches of Saint Saviour; Saint Martin of Morengo; Saint Andrew of Brugnano; Saint Mary of Rumano; and the churches of Farinate, Vailate, Saint Stephen of Aufoningo, Fontanella, the castle of Sancini, Saint Bassianus, Saint Peter in Curte, Saint John in the old castle, Saint Michael in Burgo, Saint Sirus, Questro, Alfiano, Lake Obscuro, Scandolaria, Clavatone, the castle of Vivariolo, Via Cava, Saint Mary, Commessajo, Dufno, Corrigia Viridis, Pangoneta, Ciconiaria, [Col. 0832B] the church of Saint Margaret, and Citanova, saving the fixed rent of the monastery of Saint Peter.

In the church of Saint Paul of Citanova, the episcopal right, as was established through our brother Indicus by command of our predecessor Pope Celestine of good memory. Likewise all parish churches, with chapels and baptismal churches and their appurtenances, which you now possess peacefully and canonically. From all churches that are in your bishopric, obedience, synodal dues, and the other things according to the due custom of the churches of the bishop of Cremona.

Also the court called Barianum, and Maleum, Crotta, Montodanum, Rivaltella, Monterione, Jovisalta, Fornovum, Sencinum, Platena, and Mocianica, with their castles, villages, and appurtenances; the castle of Rivigingo [Col. 0832C] with its entire integrity; and shares in the courts of Gabiano, Vidalasco, Ternolasco, public lands within and without, and likewise at Azanello and Fontanella. Whatever has been justly acquired, or is to be acquired, for the aforesaid Church through the diligence of your prudence, we confirm by this present charter of our Apostolic sanction.

We decree that enfeoffments made within your bishopric by priests, archpriests, or your abbots out of the goods of churches, without the counsel or consent of you and your predecessors, are void; and we strictly prohibit such enfeoffments from being made henceforth. We judge that the agreement made between you and the canons of the greater Church of Cremona by our predecessor Pope Calixtus of good memory, and confirmed by his written instrument, shall remain valid: namely, that no one shall be appointed canon in the greater Church except with the assent and will of the bishop, who, as he is head of the church, so his will and judgment ought to come first. The canons shall promise and maintain obedience to the bishop into his hand. When the bishop dines at the canons’ table, he shall come with one cleric and one servant, or with two clerics, and shall be honored as bishop. From the altar of Saint Himerius he shall receive every offering except food-offerings laid at the foot of the altar, which shall be reserved at the disposal of the canons, and except half of the wax and incense offered there, which shall be reserved for the service of the church. The bishop shall appoint the archdeacon, the cantor, and the other principal persons [Col. 0833A] with the consent of the canons. He shall possess peacefully and quietly the church of Saint Michael and the lands and possessions which he proves by suitable witnesses belong properly to the bishopric. And because the canons gave the house in which they formerly lived for enlargement of the church, they shall nevertheless retain the house in which they now live—although it belonged by right to the bishop—for the use and cohabitation of their common life henceforth, in concord and charity; and they may receive guests into it whenever they wish, while in all matters the authority of the holy Roman Church is reserved.

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this charter of our ordinance, should rashly attempt to act against it and, after a second [Col. 0833B] or third warning, fails to make suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honor, be cut off from the most holy Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and at the final judgment be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve what is just for that same Church, may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ rest, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the severe Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Theodinus, bishop of Saint Rufina. I, Stephen, bishop of Palestrina. [Col. 0833C] I, Peter, bishop of Albano.
