I, G.G., cardinal priest of the title of Saint Callixtus. I, Gio., cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Thomas, cardinal priest of Saint Vestina. I, Hubaldus, cardinal priest of Saint Praxedes. I, Manfredus, cardinal priest of Saint Sabina. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, John, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary the New.

Given at the Lateran through the hands of the chaplain and scribe, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of April, in the seventh indiction, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius II.

## VI. Privilege for the monastery of Saint John of Parma, of the Cassinese order.  
*(Year 1144, March 17.)*

[Margarini, *Bullarium Casinense*, II, 161.]

[Col. 0833D]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Guido, abbot of the monastery of Saint John situated in the city of Parma, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, forever.

Since without the observance of true religion neither the unity of charity can endure nor service acceptable to God be offered, it is fitting for Apostolic authority to cherish religious persons and support with the protection of the Apostolic See the places in which they devote themselves to divine offices. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your reasonable [Col. 0834A] petitions; and, following the footsteps of our predecessors of blessed memory, the Roman pontiffs Paschal and Innocent, we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves, and strengthen by this charter, the church of Saint John, in which you are devoted to divine service. We decree that whatever possessions and goods it now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by grants of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, obtain with God’s favor, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their own names:

In the same bishopric of Parma: the church of Saint Stephen, which is in Burgo; the church [Col. 0834B] of Saint Michael of Arao; the church of Saint Stephen of Torano; the church of Saint Salvinus with its court; the church of Saint Lawrence of Ramusello; the castle of Ramuselli with its church; the castle of Saint Vitalis with its church and court; the church of Gainaco; the church of Saint Sylvester of Inehela; the church of Saint Saviour of Sanguineo with its castle and court; two parts of the court of Sacca, and whatever you justly hold in the church of the same place; the church of Saint Justina; the churches of Saint Prosper and Saint Anastasius in the same city; the church of Saint James at the bridgehead; the church of Saint Peter of the borough of Saint Domninus; the church of Provinciano; the church of Casa Dei, with all their [Col. 0834C] appurtenances; the church of Saint Matthew of Callio; the church of Saint Melanus, with half the borough and four houses; the church of Paterno, with its castle and court; the church of Saint Michael of Filino; and whatever you justly possess in the church of Saint George of Pratis.

In the bishopric of Reggio, the church of Saint Michael; in the bishopric of Luni, the church of Saint Justina and the church of Cavallaria; in the bishopric of Pistoia, the monastery of Saint Bartholomew, with the church of Saint Mary in the borough and the church of Saint Mary outside the gate; the church of Saint Bartholomew of Travallio; the church of Saint Domninus of Impolis, with its court and all its appurtenances; the church of Saint Mary of Capiciano; and the church of Saint Michael of Valle Nebulae, with [Col. 0834D] all their appurtenances. We likewise confirm to you the tithes granted to your monastery by the discretion of the bishops of Parma.

We prohibit tithes from being demanded of you on labor cultivated by your own hands or at your own expense, or on the increase of your animals. We grant permission to every free person who wishes to come to you and take the religious habit. We also grant that burial in that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and final will of any persons who have chosen burial there, unless they happen to be excommunicated, while the right of the mother church remains reserved.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the same monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with reckless vexations; rather, let all things be kept intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the canonical right of the diocesan bishop and the authority of the Apostolic See. If any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowingly [Col. 0835A] attempts to act rashly against this charter of our ordinance and, after a second or third warning, does not make suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honor, recognize himself or herself as guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most holy Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and at the final judgment be subject to severe vengeance.

But upon all who preserve what is just for that same place, may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ rest, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the severe Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Baro, chaplain and scribe, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of April, in the seventh indiction, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius II.

## VII. Privilege for the Church of Olivolo, or Castello (Venice).  
*(Year 1144, March 21.)*

[Ughelli, *Italia sacra*, V, 1241.]

[Col. 0835C]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother John, bishop of the Church of Olivolo, or Castello, and to his successors canonically appointed, forever.

It is equitable and reasonable that the holy Roman Church, which is the head and teacher of all churches, established by the Lord, should, like a loving mother, exercise care and concern and protect them from the injuries of wicked people by prudent vigilance. Therefore we, who, though unworthy, sit by the Lord’s disposition in the place of Blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, are bound by the office of apostleship entrusted to us by God to love our brother bishops with due kindness and preserve for the churches committed to them their rights. [Col. 0835D]

Accordingly, with this purpose of charity, venerable brother Bishop John, we graciously assent to your reasonable petitions and have judged that the Church of Olivolo, over which you preside by God’s authority, should be fortified by the privilege of the Apostolic See. For it is established by the decrees of holy pontiffs that no one may usurp another’s boundaries, presume to judge or excommunicate another’s parishioners; that no primate, metropolitan, or any other bishop whatsoever may enter another’s city or approach a possession which does not belong to him and lies in another bishop’s parish, for the purpose of making any disposition, ordination, or judgment there, unless called by the person whose right it is known to be. [Col. 0836A]

Therefore, by this charter, we forbid and, in forbidding, decree that in the Church of Olivolo—also called Castello—or in its diocese, no patriarch or fellow-provincial bishop may presume, without permission from you or your successors, to perform consecrations or blessings of churches, clerics, or nuns. Nor may anyone there make chrism, confirm children with chrism, or pronounce excommunications or absolutions. We also add that no general assembly of bishops shall be held indiscriminately in the same parish without your consent, except a provincial council of Grado; and they too shall arrange it with the knowledge of your charity, nor shall they remain there beyond the limits set by the canons except in a more serious necessity. [Col. 0836B]

Furthermore, without your permission none of them shall dare to ordain or retain the clerics of your church, whether there or elsewhere; to judge any of your parishioners; to appoint their own clerics in your church; or to impose penances for public crimes. Moreover, both the church of Blessed Mark and the other churches and clerics of churches within the same parish shall remain under your obedience and authority. The disobedient shall be restrained at the discretion of your power according to the sanctions of the holy canons.

Concerning the monasteries of Saints Hilary, George, Nicholas, the Holy Cross, Zacharias, Lawrence, Erasmus, and Servulus, we decree that the same obedience shall continue to be rendered to you as your predecessors are known to have possessed. Moreover, abbots established in your parish shall by no means presume to celebrate public masses in churches not their own. [Col. 0836C] We also decree that those who reside continually in your parish, and to whom you administer spiritual ministrations, both they themselves and their households, shall pay tithes to you without contradiction from anyone. But we prohibit any bishop or abbot from daring, without consulting you, to impose public penance upon them, whether healthy or sick, except perhaps in the urgent circumstance of death.

Adding these provisions, we decree that whatever possessions or goods the same Church now justly and lawfully possesses, or may in future, with the Lord’s assistance, canonically acquire, shall remain secure and inviolate to you and your successors forever. [Col. 0836D]

If anyone hereafter rashly attempts to oppose this ordinance of ours and, after a second or third warning, does not correct the matter by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honor, recognize himself or herself as guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most holy Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and at the final judgment be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that same Church, may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ rest, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the severe Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

[Col. 0837A] I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church, etc. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, etc. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, etc. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum, etc. I, S.S., cardinal priest of the title of Callixtus, etc. I, Gilibertus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Mark. I, Rainerius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Manfredus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Gerard, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Dominica. I, Gregory, unworthy deacon of the holy Roman Church, wrote this. Rodulphus, cardinal deacon of Saint Lucy in Septasolis.

[Col. 0837B] Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Baro, chaplain and scribe, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of April, indiction VII, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Pope Lucius II.

## VIII. Privilege for the Abbey of Admont. Year 1144, March 21.

[PEZ, *Thesaurus Anecdotorum*, III, III, 663.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son GOTEFRID, abbot of the monastery called Admont, situated in the diocese of Salzburg, and to his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, forever.

[Col. 0837C] Since, by reason of the apostolic office laid upon us by God, we are debtors to all churches and ecclesiastical persons, we ought nevertheless to cherish with more paternal affection those who, having set aside secular affairs, have bound themselves more closely to the service of almighty God. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your reasonable petitions; and we receive under the guardianship and protection of the Apostolic See, and strengthen by the authority of this present document, the aforesaid monastery of Admont, in which you are devoted to divine service. It is known to have been founded in his diocese by Gebehard, archbishop of Salzburg, of happy memory, and endowed with many goods.

Moreover, whatever possessions or goods [Col. 0837D] have been bestowed by the aforesaid Archbishop Gebehard, or by his successor Archbishop Tyemo, or by other faithful servants of God, in tithes or donations of other lands, or may hereafter be offered—in lands, vineyards, or any other possessions—and whatever the same abbey has acquired or may acquire by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, we confirm to you by the authority of this present document. Among these we have thought it proper to specify the following by their proper names: the estate given by Bishop Gebehard in the forest called Frizewalt, on both sides of the river, from Horgeprukke as far as Schratengaste, with its tithes and all appurtenances; the estate which you received from Otto at Chatse by exchange; the tithes canonically granted to you by Bishop Gebehard; the estate at Elsindorf, with its church and appurtenances; and, at Halle near the monastery, whatever Bishops Gebehard, Tiemo, and Chunrad granted you there.

[Col. 0838A] No bishop, not even the abbot himself, nor any other person, shall have authority to grant the goods of that abbey to anyone as a fief or benefice without the consent of the better and more discerning brethren, nor to alienate them in any other way. We likewise forbid any brother, after making profession, to leave the cloister without the permission of the abbot and the whole congregation; and no one shall dare to retain a brother who departs without the common authorization of letters.

We decree that the burial-place [Col. 0838B] of that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the final wishes of any who resolve to be buried there, provided they are not excommunicated, while preserving the rights of the mother church. No opposition of any bishop or provost shall prevent you from receiving laypeople or secular clerics for conversion.

Furthermore, we strengthen by apostolic privilege for you the hospice built at Friesach by our venerable brother Chunrad and bestowed upon the abbey of Admont, together with the old and new tithes at Mothnizze and all other things—whether pastures, woods, lands, serfs, or things obtained by exchange or reasonable donation. Upon the death [Col. 0838C] of yourself, now abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it by any trickery or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the council, shall judge ought to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict.

Let no person whatsoever presume to disturb that abbey, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with reckless vexations. Rather, let everything remain intact and serve in every respect the purposes for which it was granted: the governance and support of those concerned, saving the canonical reverence due to the archbishop of Salzburg. He, however, shall in no way be permitted to impose upon it any vexation or custom harmful to the peace of regular religious.

[Col. 0838D] If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing the contents of this document of our decree, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make worthy amends by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and office; let him or her know that he or she stands guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him or her be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of the Lord, our Redeemer Jesus Christ; and let him or her be subject, at the final judgment, to severe punishment. But may all who preserve the rights of the same place have the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find with the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

[Col. 0839A] I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Chunrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Theodewinus, bishop of Santa Rufina, have subscribed. I, Ymerus, bishop of Tusculum, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal-priest of the title of Calixtus, have subscribed. I, Gwido, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus, have subscribed. I, Rainerus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal-deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Otto, cardinal-deacon of Saint George at the [Col. 0839B] Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Gebehardus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Domnica, have subscribed. I, Peter, deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Baro, chaplain and scribe, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of April, indiction VII, in the year 1143 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Pope Lucius.

## IX. Privilege for the convent of Remiremont. Year 1144, March 22.

[Gallia Christiana XIII, *Instrumenta*, 499.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in [Col. 0839C] Christ, Judith, abbess of the monastery of Remiremont, and her sisters, present and future, professing the regular life . . . [lacuna]

M. . . . [lacuna] Although, by the office laid upon us, we ought to have care for all churches, we ought nevertheless to be especially solicitous for those churches which belong in a particular way to the right of blessed Peter, and diligently to provide for their peace and welfare. Therefore, beloved daughters in the Lord, graciously assenting to your reasonable petitions, we receive under the guardianship and protection of the Apostolic See, and strengthen by the privilege of this present document, the monastery of Remiremont, in which you are devoted to divine service.

For we decree that the same abbey shall always remain under the special jurisdiction of the Apostolic See, in accordance with the venerable decrees of our predecessors. Whatever the same monastery now justly and lawfully possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by grants of popes, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, with the Lord’s assistance, shall remain firm and undiminished to you and your successors. Among these we have thought it proper to specify the following by their proper names: the territory held by the monastery of Remiremont at Adacei; the revenues from Madesmei, which William of Arches relinquished; the estate of Guoherii; Candary Point; Landricurt; Basonicurt; Guillonvillart; the lands of Madesmei; the holding in the city of Toul formerly held by Hugh of Gundricurt; the vineyards which you possess at Barro; [Col. 0840A] and the land which you possess in the territory of Toul.

Moreover, lest access be open to popular assemblies within the nuns’ enclosure, we forbid any bishop to celebrate public masses there or to dispose of the affairs of that place, unless invited to do so by the abbess of that place or by the convent of sisters. But you shall receive chrism, holy oil, the consecration of altars and churches, and the ordination of clerics to be advanced to sacred orders, from whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, provided that he enjoys the favor and communion of the Apostolic See. If, when requested, a bishop should visit the monastery, he shall not be allowed to appropriate for himself anything, great or small, whether ornaments, vessels, or any other goods. Nor do we permit archbishops, archdeacons, the diocesan bishop himself, or any person whatever to exercise authority in that monastery.

[Col. 0840B] We also forbid anyone within one league of the monastery to attack any person or that person’s property. Upon the death of yourself, now abbess of that place, or of any of those who shall succeed you, no one shall be placed there by any device of fraud or violence, except one whom they have elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict. The woman elected shall be presented to the Roman pontiff to receive the mysteries of blessing; and if she should perhaps depart from the regular path, she shall be subject to the correction of the Apostolic See. A bishop, however, shall not presume, without the permission of the Roman pontiff, to exercise any disciplinary action against her.

As a sign of the liberties received from the Roman Church, within the period of four years you shall pay to us and to our successors, together with a pallium called Rustrolino, a white horse. We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away or retain its possessions once taken, diminish them, or harass it with reckless vexations. Rather, let everything remain intact and serve in every respect the welfare of those for whose governance and support it was granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See.

If, therefore, any archbishop or bishop, emperor or king, prince or margrave, count, viscount, judge, or any ecclesiastical [Col. 0840D] or secular person, knowing the contents of this document of our decree, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to correct the matter by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power or office, and let him or her . . . stand under judgment . . . and be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of the Lord, our Redeemer Jesus; and let him or her be subject, at the final judgment, to severe punishment. But may all who preserve the rights of the venerable place have the peace of the Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find with the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Theodeurinus, bishop of Santa Rufina. [Col. 0841A] I, Alberius, bishop of Ostia. I, Gregory, cardinal-deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Otto, cardinal-deacon of Sabellium at the Golden Veil. I, Guido, cardinal-deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Gerard, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Damme. I, Thomas, cardinal-priest of Saint Vessina. I, Imarys, bishop of Tusculum. I, Theobald, cardinal-priest of Saint Praxedes. I, Numerius, cardinal-priest of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Gilibertus, cardinal-priest of Saint Mark.

[Col. 0841B] Given at the Lateran through the hand of Baro, chaplain and scribe, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of April, indiction VII, in the year 1148 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Pope Lucius.

## X. To Albero of Trier, Humbert of Besançon, archbishops, etc. (Year 1144, March 22.)

[GRAVIER, *Histoire de Saint-Dié*, Notes, p. 348.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brethren [ALBERO], archbishop of Trier; HU. [HUMBERT], archbishop of Besançon; L. [STEPHEN], bishop of Metz; HEN., bishop of Toul; A., bishop of Verdun; and G., bishop of Langres; and to the beloved sons, the abbots of Bellocampo and Belloprato: greeting and apostolic [Col. 0841C] blessing.

Our predecessor Pope Innocent, of good memory, bound Simon, duke of Lorraine, with the bond of excommunication on account of the injuries and damages which he inflicted upon the Church of Remiremont; and he forbade the celebration of divine offices in the church of Saint Deodatus, where Simon was buried. Now, however, honorable and discerning persons of that land have informed us that this sentence of excommunication was in no way announced to him; that, having made confession in communion with the Church and received penance, he ended his life; and that he was buried as a Christian in the aforesaid church by you, brother bishop of Toul, and by many discerning and religious men.

But Duke Matthew, [Col. 0841D] his son, succeeding to his father’s same wickedness, persecutes that same church. By plunder, robbery, novel exactions, and many burdens laid upon both clerics and laypeople, he despoils and devastates the goods and possessions of that church, although in the presence of our dearest son Conrad, illustrious king of the Romans, he made peace with the abbess and nuns of the aforesaid church and confirmed it in writing at the monastery of Remiremont. Therefore, by our predecessor Pope Innocent, of good memory, he has been bound with the bond of excommunication, and his land has been placed under interdict from divine offices, except for the baptism of children and the penances of the dying.

Since the same abbess, coming to the Apostolic See through many hardships, has tearfully set before us her own miseries and those of her sisters, we compassionately regard the desolation [Col. 0842A] of that church and the hardships of the abbess herself with paternal affection; and, in matters in which we can act according to God, we willingly devote our efforts to their peace and tranquility. Therefore, by this present letter, we command you to assemble at the church of Saint Deodatus on the second day before the Nones of June. If the aforesaid duke firmly promises, into your hands, that he will observe the peace and concord made between himself and the Church of Remiremont through the intervention of our dearest son Conrad, illustrious king of the Romans, and confirmed by his written instrument; and if he makes satisfaction for the damages and injuries inflicted upon that church after the concord was made, then absolve both him from the sentence of excommunication and his land from the interdict.

Concerning the other matters, if it is established with certainty [Col. 0842B] that excommunication was not announced to his father Simon, and that, while alive, he communicated with the Church; or if you learn through suitable witnesses that at the end, having received penance and made confession, he ended his life, then let him have ecclesiastical burial, and let that church no longer cease from divine offices on this account. But if the aforesaid Duke Matthew refuses to observe the concord made or to restore what he afterwards took from the aforesaid church, or should presume even to violate it in intention, then both he and his under-advocates and officials, through whom he exercises his tyranny over the goods of that church, and their lands, shall remain subject to the aforesaid sentence of excommunication and interdict.

But if you, brother A[lbero], archbishop of Trier, are unable to be present, [Col. 0842C] you other brethren shall bring the matter, as it has been written above, to its execution.

Given at the Lateran, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of April.

## XI. To Gervasius, abbot of Saint Germanus at Auxerre—concerning the dispute with the abbot of Vézelay. (Year 1144, March 22.)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 613.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son, the abbot of Saint Germanus at Auxerre: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our beloved son Pontius, abbot of Vézelay, [Col. 0842D] appearing before us, complained that in a certain wood held in common by you and him, you caused his men to be seized and handed over to the servants of the count of Nevers for imprisonment. When he demanded them from you and could not obtain them, he provided sureties for their release and surrendered the book of the Gospels. Since this is known to have been done contrary to religion and the bond of fraternal charity, we command you by this present letter, without delay, to restore to him the book of the Gospels which was so improperly received and to release his sureties.

Afterwards, if you believe that you have any right against him, obtain before the venerable brother Godefrid, bishop of Langres, whatever justice shall decree. Also restore to Guibert, your servant, those things which you took from him because of his ill will.

[Col. 0843A] Given at the Lateran, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of April.

## XII. He receives certain churches of the monastery of Marseille under protection, and confirms the agreement made by Abbot Peter with Bishop Ademarus of Rodez, of blessed memory. (Year 1144, March 29.)

[BALUZE, *Miscellanea*, Lucian edition, vol. III, p. 70.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son PETER, abbot of Marseille, and to his successors regularly appointed, forever.

It is recognized as equitable and reasonable that we, who have been assumed to the governance of churches, should protect them from the malice of wicked [Col. 0843B] people and, with the Lord’s help, diligently provide for their peace and welfare. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Peter, we graciously assent to your just petitions. We receive under the protection of the Apostolic See, and confirm to you, your successors, and, through you, to the monastery of Marseille by the authority of this present privilege, the churches which you canonically possess: namely, the church of Saint Amantius, situated in the suburb of Rodez, and the church of Saint Austremonius of Sales, with their chapels and all things belonging to those churches.

Moreover, we strengthen by apostolic authority the agreement reasonably made and confirmed in writing between you and our venerable brother Ademarus, bishop of that city, of blessed memory, by the will and agreement of both parties; and we decree that it shall remain ratified and unshaken forever in future times. Nor shall anyone be permitted to pronounce a sentence of interdict against the aforesaid church of Saint Amantius so long as you, your successors, or your brethren, having been summoned by the Apostolic See concerning accusations made against them, are prepared to render and receive justice before the Roman pontiff.

[Col. 0843C] We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may harass you or your successors concerning these matters, or inflict upon you on their account any opposition or molestation. If, however, any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing the contents of this document of our decree, should attempt to act against it and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to correct this presumption by suitable satisfaction, let that person incur the loss of dignity of power and office, be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of the Lord, our Redeemer Jesus Christ, and be subject at the final judgment to severe punishment. But those who preserve these things shall obtain the favor of almighty God, of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul, and of ourselves. Amen, amen.

[Col. 0843D] Given at the Lateran through the hand of Baro, chaplain and scribe, on the fourth day before the Kalends of April, indiction VII, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Pope Lucius II.

## XIII. To Raimund, bishop of Maguelonne—he commands him to pronounce a canonical sentence against the count of Melgueil and others as sacrilegious persons, unless they restore to the monastery of Saint Theofredus what Bernard, formerly count of Melgueil, had left to that monastery by testament. (Year 1144, March 29.)

[Dom BOUQUET, *Recueil*, XV, 411.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother R[AIMUND], bishop of Maguelonne: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is sacrilege and contrary to law if anyone attempts, out of a wicked inclination to personal gain, to retain what has been left to venerable places.

[Note: [Col. 0843D] Berengarius-Raimundi, count of Provence or Arles, who, having taken in marriage Beatrice, the daughter and sole heiress of Bernard, count of Mergoriensis—of Mauguio or Melgueil—was also called count of Melgueil [Col. 0844D].]

A report has therefore reached our ears that the count of Melgueil and certain other parishioners under your jurisdiction violently take away from the monastery of Saint Theofredus what Bernard, formerly count of Melgueil, left to it by testament.

[Note: [Col. 0844D] Saint-Chaffre, the distinguished monastery of the Order of Saint Benedict in the diocese of Le Puy, also called Calmilium and Calmiciacum.]

Therefore, by this present letter, we command you diligently to warn the aforesaid count and others who hold the same testament that they should restore, with all things taken away, to our sons B. (Beraldo), the abbot, and his brethren, and leave in peace, what he left to the aforesaid monastery for the redemption of his soul. If they scorn to comply within forty days after your warning, pronounce against them a canonical sentence as against sacrilegious persons, and cause it to be observed until they repent.

[Col. 0844C] Given at the Lateran, on the fourth day before the Kalends of April.

## XIV. To Peter of Bourges, Arnald of Narbonne, Raimund of Arles, Pontius of Aix, and William of Embrun, archbishops: he commands them to ensure that goods taken from the monastery of Marseille are restored. (Year 1144, March 30.)

[*L’Antiquité de Marseille*, I, 460.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brethren P., archbishop of Bourges; A., archbishop of Narbonne; R., archbishop of Arles; P., archbishop of Aix; G., archbishop of Embrun; and to their suffragans: greeting and apostolic blessing.

P., abbot of Marseille, laid before us a grave complaint that parishioners under your jurisdiction violently take away the goods of [Col. 0844D] his church, etc. But you, established as patrons of justice and bound to oppose evildoers by punishing them sternly, allow this to pass in silence, etc. By this present letter we command you strictly to warn those same evildoers to restore in full to our aforesaid son, the abbot, what has been taken away; henceforth to cease harassing him; and to make worthy satisfaction for such great offenses. If they prove contemptuous, administer justice against them as against sacrilegious persons, and against their lands.

Given at the Lateran, on the third day before the Kalends of April.

## XV. He confirms the privileges of Patriarch Henry of Grado and the possessions of the Church. (Year 1144, March 31.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, V, 1121.]

[Col. 0845A]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother HENRY, patriarch of Grado, and to his successors regularly appointed, forever.

From the apostolic office entrusted to us by God, we ought to provide with paternal care for our brethren both near at hand and far away, and to preserve to churches in which they are known to serve the Lord their due rights; so that, just as by God’s ordering we are called fathers in name, we may likewise be proved such in deed. For this reason, venerable [Col. 0845B] brother Henry, patriarch, we graciously assent to your petitions. We receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and strengthen by the protection of this present document, the Church of Grado, over which by God’s will you are known to preside.

Therefore, following the authority of our predecessors Pelagius, Alexander, Urban, and Innocent, and especially preserving the tenor of that constitution which our predecessor Pope Leo IX established and confirmed both by synodal judgment and by the text of a privilege, we grant to you and to your successors canonically appointed the patriarchal dignity; and we confirm that the governance of the Church of Grado shall be exercised within those boundaries only which are known to have been assigned to that Church by the aforesaid our predecessors.

We also grant that a cross may be borne before you, except when you are in Rome or in the presence or company of the Roman pontiff. Furthermore, from the generosity of the Apostolic See, we bestow upon your fraternity the pallium—that is, the fullness of the pontifical office—which you shall remember to use within your church in celebrating the solemnities of Mass on the days when your predecessors are unquestionably known to have used it: namely, at the Nativity of the Lord, Epiphany, Hypapante, the three feasts of Saint Mary, the Lord’s Supper, Holy Saturday, the Resurrection of the Lord, the Ascension, Pentecost, the Nativity of Saint John the Baptist, and the feasts of all the apostles; likewise on the feasts of Saint Mark, Saint Stephen the Protomartyr, Saint Lawrence, and Saint Martin; at the solemnity of All Saints; and at the principal [Col. 0845D] feasts of your church; also at the consecrations of churches, bishops, and other clerics, and on the anniversary day of your own consecration.

We also decree that whatever goods or possessions the Church of Grado now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by just means, shall remain firm and undiminished to you and your successors. We freely confirm to you and your successors the revenues in Constantinople, Istria, and Venice that were justly granted by bishops, abbots, doges, judges, and the people of Venice to your predecessors Dominic and John Gradenicus, their successors, and the Church of Grado, as their written instruments attest; and likewise the churches given to the Church of Grado by religious persons, established in the parishes of that province, together [Col. 0846A] with all things in those churches known to belong to your jurisdiction.

Accordingly, beloved brother in Christ, the greater the prerogative by which you are known to be exalted, the more earnestly you must take care that, in correcting your subjects, reason may prevail with you more than power. Let the good find you a gentle corrector and the wicked a merciful one. Love persons; pursue vices. Otherwise, if you should perhaps choose to act differently, correction may turn into cruelty, and you may lose those whom you desire to amend. You must cut away a wound in such a manner that you do not ulcerate what is sound; lest, if you apply the blade more deeply than the matter requires, it harm the one whom you hasten to help, and thus one evil be engendered from another—so that the good may have, through love, something to avoid, and the wicked may have, through fear, something to love.

[Col. 0846B] We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid Church, take away or diminish its possessions or revenues, or harass it with any vexations or molestations. Rather, let all things remain intact and serve in every respect the purposes for which they were granted: the governance and support of those concerned—always preserving in all things the authority of the Apostolic See.

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing the contents of this document of our decree, should rashly attempt to act against it and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make amends through suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and office; let him or her know that he or she stands guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him or her be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of the Lord, our Redeemer Jesus Christ; and let him or her be subject at the final judgment to severe punishment. But may all who preserve the rights of that place have the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find with the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

[Col. 0846C] I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Theoderinus, bishop of Santa Rufina, have subscribed. I, Albericus, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Ymarus, bishop of Tusculum, have subscribed. I, Peter, bishop of Albano, have subscribed. [Col. 0846D] I, Guido, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus, have subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal-priest of the title of Pastor, have subscribed. I, Thomas, cardinal-priest of the title of Vestina, have subscribed. I, Hubaldus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Praxedes, have subscribed. I, Rainerius, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill, have subscribed. I, Manfredus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Sabina, have subscribed. I, Geraldus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Domnica, have subscribed. I, Guido, unworthy minister of the altar in the Roman Church, have subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Gr., unworthy deacon of the Holy Roman Church, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary Nova, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal-deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. [Col. 0847A] I, Otto, cardinal-deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal-deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Hugh, deacon of the Roman Church at Saint Lucy in Horphea, have subscribed. I, Astaldus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Eustace near the Temple of Agrippa, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Baro, chaplain and scribe, on the second day before the Kalends of April, indiction VII, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Pope Lucius II.

## XVI. At the request of Bishop Albero, he confirms the possessions and diocesan boundaries of the Church of Reggio. (Year 1144, April 2.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, II, 295.]

[Col. 0847B]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother ALBERO, bishop of Reggio, and to his successors canonically appointed, forever.

From the office of the apostolate entrusted to us by God, it is fitting that we provide with paternal care for our brethren both nearby and far away, and preserve for churches in which they are known to serve the Lord their due right, so that, just as by God’s ordering we are called fathers in name, so we may likewise be proved such in deed. Therefore, venerable brother Bishop Albero, we graciously grant your petitions, receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves the Church of Reggio, over which by God’s authority you are known to preside, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. [Col. 0847C] We decree that whatever possessions and goods it now justly and canonically holds, or may in future be able, with God’s favour, reasonably to acquire, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors, and through you to that same Church. We have thought fit to specify these in their proper names: [lacuna] the canonry of St. Prosper; the chapel of St. John of the City; the chapel of St. James; the canonry of St. Germinian; the chapel of St. Stephen; and the other chapels of the same city; the monastery of St. Thomas; the monastery of St. Raphael; the parish church of Menotio; the chapel of St. James on the island of Bibio, with the other chapels belonging to it; the parish church of Thoano; the chapel of the Hospital at the bridge of Cavola, with its possessions and the other chapels of that parish; the parish church of [Col. 0847D] St. Vitalis, with its chapels and everything belonging to it by right; the parish church of Campiola; the chapel of St. Venantius of Busana; the chapel of Valesneria; the chapel of St. Vitus, with the other chapels of that parish; the parish church of Baisio with its other chapels; the parish church of the castle of Ariano with its chapels; the parish church of St. Eleuchadius with its chapels; the parish church of Albineto with its chapels; the parish church of Pojanello with its chapels; the parish church of Lecolo with its chapels; the parish church of Caviliano; the chapel of Jano; the chapel of Rezola; the chapel of St. Prosper of Graxiano with the other chapels of that parish; the parish church of Bibiano; the chapels of Bibianello with the other chapels of that parish; the parish church of Mutilena; the chapels of [Col. 0848A] Curviaco with the other chapels of that parish; the parish church of Rivalta with its chapels; the parish church of Foliano with its chapels; the parish church of Arceto with its chapels; the parish church of Banio with its chapels; the parish church of Herberia with its chapels; the parish church of Prato, with the chapel of St. Martin of Rio and its other chapels; the parish church of Bagniolo with its chapels; the parish church of Campo Rotondo, with the chapel of Corrigia and its other chapels; the parish church of Corte Nuova; the parish church of Nuvolaria with its chapels; the churches of Campagniola; the parish church of Fabrica, with the chapel of Razolo and its other chapels; the parish church of St. Zeno with its chapels; the parish church of St. Mary of Novis with its chapels; the church of Gorgatela; the parish church of St. Stephen, with the chapel of St. Possidonius and its other chapels; the parish church of Quarantula with its chapels; [Col. 0848B] the parish church of St. Martin in Spina, with its chapels of Gavella and Manziana; the parish church of Cutiano, with the chapel of Mulla and its other chapels; the church of Gonzaga; the parish church of Villula with its chapels; the parish church of Pigognaga with its chapels; the parish church of Bondeno de Ronculis with its chapels; the parish church of Bondeno Arduini with its chapels; the parish church of Suzaria with its chapels; the church of Loco Bello; the Church of Polesino; the church of Zitola; the parish church of Luzaria, with the chapel of Sacca and its other chapels; the parish church of Guardistalla with its chapels; the monastery of Marola; the monastery of Canusio.

By the authority also of this decree, we ordain that the entire boundaries of the bishopric of Reggio shall henceforth be preserved peacefully and wholly intact for you and your successors. [Col. 0848C] Following in the footsteps of our predecessor Pope Urban of blessed memory, we decree that, in parish churches held by monks within your bishopric, they shall install priests with your consent. If these are suitable, they shall receive from you the care of souls; they shall render account to you concerning the pastoral care of the people, but shall show the monks due subjection in temporal matters, the authority of the Apostolic See being preserved in all things.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowingly, should rashly attempt to violate this page of our constitution, and after a second or third warning does not make amendment by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of his or her power and honour; let such a person know that he or she stands guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let that person be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let that person be subject to severe vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that same Church may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen. Amen. Amen.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal of SS. Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of St. Sixtus, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal priest of St. Chrysogonus, have subscribed. I, Ymarus, bishop of Tusculum, have subscribed. [Col. 0849A] I, Peter, bishop of Albano, have subscribed. I, Thomas, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina, have subscribed. I, Ubaldus, of the title of St. Praxedes, have subscribed. I, Manfredus, cardinal priest of the title of St. Sabina, have subscribed. I, Nicholas, cardinal priest of the title of St. Cyriacus, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of SS. Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Rodulphus, cardinal deacon of St. Lucy in Setasolis, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal deacon of St. Adrian, have subscribed. I, Gr., deacon of the Holy Roman Church, have subscribed. I, Hugh, deacon of the Roman Church at St. Lucy in Horfia, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Bobo, chaplain and scribe, on the fourth day before the Nones of April, in the seventh indiction, in the year of the Incarnation of the Lord 1144, [Col. 0849B] in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius II.

## XVII. Privilege for the monastery of St. Trudpert. (1144, April 3.)

[HERRGOTT, *Genealogy of the Habsburgs*, II, 169.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons EVERARD, abbot of the monastery of the martyr St. Trudpert, situated in the Black Forest, and to his brethren both present and future, to be regularly appointed in succession, in perpetuity.

The care of the universal Church has been entrusted to us by God, the provider of all good things, so that we may love religious persons and strive in every way to promote religion pleasing to God. For no service is rendered acceptable to God unless, proceeding from the root of charity, it is kept pure by religious observance. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, moved by the prayers of our venerable brother Theodewin, bishop of St. Rufina, we graciously grant your just petitions. We receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. [Col. 0849C] We decree that whatever possessions or goods this monastery now justly and canonically holds, or may in future be able, with God’s favour, to obtain by grant of popes, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, [Col. 0849D] or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors.

We have thought fit to specify these in their proper names: namely, whatever Othpertus, Rampertus, Lutfredus, and their successors granted to you and the same monastery: that is, the valley itself in which the monastery was built, with its boundaries, namely from Mount Samba as far as Mezzenbach, together with mountains, hills, meadows, pastures, woods, valleys, cultivated and uncultivated land, on both sides of the mountains, wholly and throughout; together with the tithes in Mortunowa and Kippenhein; the church with its tithe; the church in Sunthoven with its tithe; the estates of Bonbach with its church; Berghusen with its church; Krossingen with its church and tithe; [Col. 0850A] Tonsol with its church and tithe; Gruonre with its church; Loiffen with its church; Wilare; Eberingen; Zesinkoven; Buchingen; Muriclmigen with its church; Ichihein; Smihein; Wittilunbach; and the care of souls of the settlers living from Mount Brizzenberg to Mezzinbach, as you have hitherto canonically held it by grant of the bishops of Constance.

On the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be imposed or put in charge there by any craft of deception or by force. Rather, it shall be lawful for you, by common counsel or by the sounder part of the counsel, according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict, and without anyone’s opposition, to elect an abbot. Likewise, we confirm to you the valley of Bellinowa with its tithe and the aforesaid properties.

We decree, therefore, [Col. 0850B] that no person whatsoever may presume to exact from the abbot or brethren any undue rent or service, or rashly disturb the same monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations. Rather, all things shall be kept whole for the benefit in every respect of those for whose governance they were granted, the canonical right of the diocesan bishop and the authority of the Apostolic See being preserved.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts rashly to violate this page of our constitution, and after a second or third warning does not make amendment by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of his or her power and honour; let such a person know that he or she stands guilty before the divine judgment [Col. 0850C] for the iniquity committed; let that person be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let that person be subject to severe vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the just rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Baron, chaplain and scribe, on the third day before the Nones of April, in the seventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1144, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius II.

## XVIII. Privilege for the monastery of St. Zeno (at Reichenhall). (1144, April 5.)

[*Monumenta Boica*, III, 530.]

[Col. 0850D]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons LAUZON, provost of Hall, and his brethren, both present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

It is fitting that we readily grant a request shown to concern the purpose of religious life and the salvation of souls, and give suitable support to the desires of petitioners. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously grant your just petitions. We receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church at Hall, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege [Col. 0851A] of this present writing. We decree that in the same church the canonical order, according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine, shall be preserved inviolate for all time, as our venerable brother Chunrad, archbishop of Salzburg, ordained and confirmed by his writing.

Moreover, whatever possessions or goods the same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, with God’s favour, acquire by grants of popes, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. We have thought fit to specify these in their proper names: the chapel of St. Mary Muna; the chapel of St. George; the chapel of St. Martin None; the chapel of St. Valentine of Morzols; [Col. 0851B] the chapel in Plajen Castle; the chapel in Halla Castle; the water at the spring of Halla, given by Ebo; the water given by Sigboto, Unchen, Oteheim, and Unehine; the estate given by Heinricus and Papo Nuzboum; one fourth part of the salt tithe.

Indeed, no cleric or layperson whatsoever may presume to demand from you a tithe of the produce which you cultivate by your own hands or resources, or of the fodder of your animals. We also forbid that anyone of your profession, moved by any impulse of fickleness or under the pretext of a stricter religious observance, may leave the cloister without the permission of the provost or community. If anyone does leave, no bishop, abbot, or monk shall receive that person without a guarantee in a common letter, [Col. 0851C] so long as, by the Lord’s favour, the order of canons continues in force in your church. But if, when called a second or third time, that person scorns to return, it shall be lawful for the provost of that place to pronounce canonical sentence against him.

On the death of you, the present provost of that place, or upon your transfer to the governance of another church, or on the death of any of your successors, no one shall be imposed or put in charge there by any craft of deception or by force, except one whom the brethren, by common consent or by the sounder part of their counsel, according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Augustine, shall canonically provide to be elected.

We also grant that burial in that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the last will and devotion of those who have resolved to be buried there, [Col. 0851D] unless they are excommunicated, while the right of their mother church remains intact. We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its goods or possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any undue exactions or molestations. Rather, all things shall be preserved whole for the benefit in every respect of those for whose governance and support they were granted, with the canonical right of the archbishop of Salzburg of course preserved.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts rashly to violate this page of our constitution, and after a second or third warning does not correct his or her offence by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of his or her power and honour; let such a person know that he or she stands guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let that person be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let that person be subject to severe vengeance at the last judgment. [Col. 0852A] But upon all who preserve that place’s rights may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal recompense.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Baron, chaplain and scribe, on the Nones of April, in the seventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1144, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius II.

## XIX. To Pontius, abbot of Vézelay.—Against the killers of Abbot Artald. (1144, April 8.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 614.]

[Col. 0852B]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons PONTIUS, abbot of Vézelay, and his brethren: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our predecessor Paschal of happy memory, as we have learned from his writings, commanded bishops throughout Gaul that the killers of Abbot Artald of Vézelay—because they had so wickedly slain their lord, priest, and abbot—should be driven into exile according to a fitting measure of penance; and, if they would not obey, that they should be subjected to excommunication. He also prohibited any abbot or provost of Vézelay ever [Col. 0852C] from having authority to receive those same murderers to dwell in that monastery.

Therefore, confirming his command in this matter, we prohibit by apostolic authority that neither they nor their heirs may henceforth presume to disturb that monastery. We expressly include Stephen, clerk of Auxerre, who, when he had brought you, beloved son and abbot in the Lord, into litigation on this matter before our venerable brethren Geoffrey, bishop of Langres, and Bernard, abbot of Clairvaux, was, as we have learned, defeated in the suit by their judgment. And we forbid that any abbot or provost may hereafter be permitted to receive them to dwell in the borough of Vézelay.

[Col. 0852D]

Given at the Lateran, on the sixth day before the Ides of April.

## XX. Bull for the monastery of Pontlevoy. (1144, April 15.)

[*Gallia Christiana*, VIII, Documents, 424.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons FULCHER, abbot of the monastery of St. Mary of Pontlevoy, and his brethren, both present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetual remembrance.

It is fitting that we readily grant a desire shown to concern the purpose of religious life and the salvation of souls, and give suitable support to the desires of petitioners. Therefore, beloved [Col. 0853A] sons in the Lord, moved by the prayers of our venerable brother Geoffrey, bishop of Chartres, we graciously grant your just petitions. We receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions or goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter, with God’s favour, acquire by grants of popes, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors.

We have thought fit to specify these in their proper names: in the bishopric of Chartres, the place of Pontlevoy itself with its appurtenances; the church [Col. 0853B] of St. Peter of Pontlevoy. At Montcalve, the churches of St. Nicholas and St. Martin; the church of Taniac; the church of Cembineio; the church of Oscampo; the church of Castenet; the church of the seat of St. Mundricius; the church of Fulgery; the church of Fenis; the church of St. Gervasius beyond the Loire; the church of Vinolio; the church of St. Deodatus; the church of Mont-Levald; the church of Muisdia; the church of Braceolis; the church of Torno. At Blois, the church of St. John; the church of St. Gervasius; the church of Vilerbo; the church of St. Betharius; the church of St. John of Floriac; the church of Octinvilla; the church of Columba; the church of Orioro; the church of Meso. Near the castle of La Ferté-Villeneuil, the church of St. Peter and the church [Col. 0853C] of St. Martin; the church of St. Marcellus of Ceretto. Near Châteaudun, the church of St. Valerian. Near Basoche, the church of St. John. In the district of Rennes, the church of St. Peter and St. John of Igneio; the church of St. Leonard of Fulgery; the church of St. Martin of Cussa; the cell of St. Martin of Lustris; the church of Peregrina. In England, the church of St. Mary of Luministro; the chapel of Roxitunga; the chapel of Palingis; the chapel of Warmacan; the church of Pingis; the church of Sordis. In the district of Orléans, the church of Pruneriis; the church of Gii; the church of Soemo; the church of Maes; the church of Chalziac; the church of Thaisiis; the church of Lorgis; the church of [Col. 0853D] St. Romanus; the church of St. Mary of Fontanis. In the archbishopric of Tours, the church of St. Denis in Atrio; St. Martin’s; the church of St. Cyricus beyond the Loire; the church of St. Thomas; the church of Poilly; the church of Nantolio; the church of St. George; the church of St. Martin of Pressiniac; the church of Vernolio. In the bishopric of Bourges, the church of St. Mary of Valentiac; the church of St. Hilary of Château-Vieux; the church of St. Martin of Sigiac. In the district of Sées, the church of St. Hilary; the church of St. Peter of Basochis.

It shall also be lawful for you to choose priests in your churches. If they are suitable, they shall receive the care of souls from the bishops freely and without any improper demand; they shall render account to the bishops concerning the care of the people, but [Col. 0854A] shall show you due subjection in temporal matters.

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations. Rather, all things shall be preserved whole for the benefit in every respect of those for whose governance and support they were granted, with the canonical right of the diocesan bishop and the authority of the Apostolic See preserved. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts rashly to violate this page of our constitution, and after a second or third warning does not make amendment by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of his or her power and honour; let such a person know that he or she stands guilty before the divine [Col. 0854B] judgment for the iniquity committed; let that person be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let that person be subject to severe vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, GG., cardinal priest of the title of Calixtus. I, Birido, cardinal priest of the title of St. Chrysogonus. I, Rainerius, cardinal priest of the title of St. Prisca. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of the Shepherd. [Col. 0854C] I, Hubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of St. Praxedes. I, Manfridus, cardinal priest of the title of St. Sabina. I, Guiddo, cardinal priest of St. Lawrence in Damaso. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Albericus, bishop of Ostia. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of SS. Sergius and Bacchus. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Portico. I, Peter, bishop of Albano. [Col. 0854D] I, John, cardinal deacon of St. Adrian. I, GG., cardinal deacon of St. Angelo. I, Artaldus, cardinal deacon of St. Eustace beside the Temple of Agrippa.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Baron, chaplain and scribe, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of May, in the seventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1144, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Lucius II.

## XXI. Privilege for the Church of SS. Peter and Ursus at Aosta (in the province of Tarentaise). (1144, April 15.)

[*Monumenta Historiae Patriae*, Charters, I, 785.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ARNALD, prior, and the brethren in the church of SS. Peter and Ursus at Aosta, [Col. 0855A] professing the canonical life, both present and future, in perpetuity.

The care of the universal Church has been entrusted to us by God, the provider of all good things, so that we may love religious persons and strive in every way to promote religion pleasing to God. For no service is ever rendered acceptable to God unless, proceeding from the root of charity, it is kept pure by religious observance. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously grant your reasonable petitions and strengthen by the privilege of the Apostolic See the church of SS. Peter and Ursus, in which you devote yourselves to divine service. We decree that all [Col. 0855B] things which you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter, with the Lord’s aid, acquire by grants of popes, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall be preserved whole and unimpaired to that church.

We also decree that burial in that place shall be free, so that, while the right of the mother church remains intact, no one may oppose the devotion and final wish of those who have resolved to be buried there, unless perhaps they are excommunicated. On the death of you, the present prior of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be imposed or put in charge there by any craft of deception or by force, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Augustine, shall determine should be elected. [Col. 0855C]

We decree, therefore, that neither the mother church nor any person whatsoever may rashly disturb your church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, demand from you anything other than what has been established of old, or harass you by any molestations. Rather, all things shall be preserved whole to you for the benefit in every respect of those for whose support and governance they were granted, with the canonical right and reverence due to the diocesan bishop, and the authority of the Apostolic See, of course preserved.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts rashly to violate this page of our constitution, and after a second or third warning does not correct his or her offence by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of his or her power and honour; let such a person know that he or she stands guilty before the divine judgment [Col. 0855D] for the iniquity committed; let that person be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let that person be subject to severe vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve their rights for that church may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen. Amen. Amen.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Calixtus, have subscribed. [Col. 0856A] I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of St. Chrysogonus, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of SS. Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Baron, chaplain and scribe, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of May, in the seventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1144, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius II.

## XXII. Privilege for the Hermitage of Fonte Avellana. (1144, April 24.)

[NITTARELLI, *Camaldolese Annals*, IX, 27.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons in Christ SAVINUS, prior of the Hermitage of the Church of the Holy Cross of Fonte Avellana, and the brethren, both present [Col. 0856B] and future, professing the regular life, in perpetual remembrance.

The care of the universal Church has been entrusted to us by God, the provider of all good things, so that we may love religious persons and strive in every way to promote religion pleasing to God. For no service is ever rendered more acceptable to God unless, proceeding from the root of charity, it is kept pure by religious observance. Therefore, all lovers of the Christian faith ought to cherish religious life and foster with greater attentiveness venerable places together with the persons devoted to divine service within them, so that they may not be disturbed by the molestations of wicked people or harassed by oppressive and untimely exactions.

Therefore, beloved sons in Christ, we graciously grant your just petitions. We receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid place, in which [Col. 0856C] you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions or goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter, with God’s favour, acquire by grants of popes, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors.

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb that place, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations. Rather, all things shall be preserved whole for the benefit in every respect of those for whose governance and support they were granted, with the authority of the Apostolic See preserved in all things. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts rashly to violate this page of our constitution, and after a second or third warning does not make amendment by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of his or her power and honour; let such a person know that he or she stands guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let that person be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; [Col. 0856D] and let that person be subject to severe vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the just rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

[Col. 0857A] I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Baron, chaplain and scribe, on the eighth day before the Kalends of May, in the seventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1144, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius II.

## XXIII. He confirms the judgment pronounced by Innocent II concerning the dispute between the canons of St. Vincent and St. Alexander of Bergamo. (1144, April 30.)

[LUPI, *Diplomatic Codex of Bergamo*, II, 1050.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons OBERTO, provost, and the brethren of the Church of St. Alexander at Bergamo, both present and future, canonically appointed in succession, in perpetual remembrance.

[Col. 0857B] The order of justice and reason recommends that those who wish their commands to be kept by their successors should preserve the will and enactments of their predecessors. Therefore we, although unworthy successors in the governance of the Apostolic See to our predecessor Pope Innocent of happy memory, wishing to preserve his will and enactment, confirm and decree to remain valid the judgment which he pronounced between you and the canons of St. Vincent, and which his successor Pope Celestine of good memory confirmed.

That is: whenever the canons of St. Alexander meet with the canons of St. Vincent at solemnities and funeral offices, whether in the church of St. Vincent or elsewhere, the provost of St. Alexander shall occupy the first place on the left side of the choir. [Col. 0857C] The chaplains of the churches of St. Saviour, St. Agatha, St. John, St. Grata, and St. Vigilius shall come to the church of St. Alexander on Sundays and principal feast days for the major masses. Criminals from the parish of St. Alexander shall receive penance in the presence of the provost or one of the priests of the same church. We likewise decree that priests who swear fidelity to Blessed Vincent shall also swear it to Blessed Alexander; each of the priests of St. Alexander shall carry the reliquary. At the translation of the church, two priests of St. Alexander shall carry the ark together with two priests of St. Vincent. At the scrutinies on the Lord’s Supper, at baptism, and at other solemnities, they shall assemble according to the customary practice. [Col. 0857D] When the canons of St. Vincent come to the church of St. Alexander, they shall be honourably received, both in ringing the bells and in other matters as custom requires, and they shall occupy the whole choir as they have been accustomed to do.

Moreover, whatever possessions or goods the same church now justly and canonically holds, or may hereafter, with God’s favour, acquire by grants of popes, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. We have thought fit to specify these in their proper names: the churches of Licina, Lomene, and St. Faustinus; of Villa, Gromole, and Virgis; the church of St. Martin in Bergamo; the church of St. Mary Magdalene; the church of St. [Col. 0858A] Lawrence of Zaunio.

We also confirm the grant of tithes canonically made to the provost of your church by Adelbert, bishop of Bergamo of good memory, as it is contained in the writings of the same bishop and of the canons of the blessed martyrs Alexander and Vincent, so that these tithes may accrue perpetually to the use of the brethren. Further, we strengthen by apostolic authority the good usages and praiseworthy customs confirmed to you by our predecessors of pious memory, Popes Honorius, Innocent, and Celestine.

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid Church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any other molestations. Rather, all things shall be preserved whole [Col. 0858B] for the benefit in every respect of those for whose governance and support they were granted, with the canonical right of the diocesan bishop and the authority of the Apostolic See preserved. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts rashly to violate this page of our constitution, and after a second or third warning does not make amendment by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of his or her power and honour; let such a person know that he or she stands guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let that person be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let that person be subject to severe vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the just rights of that place [Col. 0858C] may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen. Amen. Amen.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Theodewin, bishop of Santa Rufina, have subscribed. I, Alberius, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of St Callistus, have subscribed. I, Guy, cardinal priest of the title of St Chrysogonus, have subscribed. I, Aribert, cardinal priest of the title of St [Col. 0858D] Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Rainerius, cardinal priest of the title of St Prisca, have subscribed. I, Hubald, cardinal priest of the title of St Praxedes, have subscribed. I, Guy, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Lawrence and Damasus, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Addo, cardinal deacon of St George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Guy, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Gerard, cardinal deacon of St Mary in Domnica, have subscribed. [Col. 0859A] I, Guy, unworthy minister of the altar in the Roman Church, have subscribed. I, Hugh, deacon of the Roman Church at St Lucy in Horphea, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal deacon of St Mary the New, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Baro, chaplain and scribe, on the second day before the Kalends of May [30 April], in the seventh indiction, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of lord Pope Lucius II.

## XXIV. To Gregory, bishop of Bergamo: he announces what he has decreed concerning the dispute between the canons of St Vincent and St Alexander.  
*(30 April 1144.)*

[LUPI, *Codex diplomaticus Bergomensis*, II, 1051.]

[Col. 0859B]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother G[REGORY], bishop of Bergamo: greeting and the apostolic blessing.

The canons of the blessed martyrs Vincent and Alexander, at the appointed term set for them by our predecessor Pope Celestine of blessed memory concerning the dispute long conducted between them, presented themselves before us. Having heard their arguments and carefully examined the documents of each party, by the counsel of our brethren we commanded that, on the vigil and feast of Victor, and during the Gregorian Litanies when they make processions, the canons of St Alexander themselves shall henceforth receive the canons of Blessed [Col. 0859C] Vincent peacefully and without any opposition, with bells rung, incense, and holy water.
