All other matters, however—just as they were defined or settled by the privilege of our predecessor Pope Innocent of blessed memory, by his letters, or by the judgment of our venerable brother Robald, archbishop of Milan—such as the place in choir and at table, the receiving of the clerics’ pledges of fidelity, the carrying out and bringing back of the reliquary containing relics, and the rest, shall be observed inviolably by both sides. Thus the provost of the church of Blessed Alexander shall hold the first place in choir and at table on the left-hand side; and the pledges of fidelity of the clerics shall be received jointly by both parties.

Since it is your duty to observe inviolably what is established by the Apostolic See, we command you by these present letters to observe firmly this judgment promulgated by us, and also to cause it to be observed by the parties themselves; likewise, you are to uphold firmly what, as we have learned, you reasonably promulgated in synod concerning the penances of offenders.

Given at the Lateran, on the second day before the Kalends of May [30 April].

## XXV. To the canons of the church of St Alexander of Bergamo, he signifies the same.  
*(30 April 1144.)*

[ibid., p. 1053.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons OBERTO, provost, and the brethren of St Alexander of the [Col. 0860A] Church of Bergamo: greeting and the apostolic blessing.

Concerning the dispute long carried on between you and the canons of Blessed Vincent, our predecessor Pope Celestine of blessed memory summoned you and them to the Apostolic See. But, as it pleased God, he meanwhile entered upon the way of all flesh. We, who, though unworthy, by the Lord’s disposition succeeded him in the governance of the Apostolic See, carefully heard you and them when, at the term fixed for you by him, you appeared before us; and we diligently examined the complaints of both sides, both personally and through our brethren.

Having therefore heard the arguments of both parties and carefully examined the documents of both parties, by counsel of the community of our brethren we commanded [Col. 0860B] that on the vigil of St Viator and during the Gregorian Litanies, when they make processions, the canons of St Alexander themselves shall henceforth receive the canons of Blessed Vincent peacefully and without any opposition, with bells rung, incense, and holy water.

All other matters, however—just as they were defined or settled by the privilege of our predecessor Pope Innocent of blessed memory, by his letters, or by the judgment of our venerable brother Robald, archbishop of Milan—such as the place in choir and at table, and the other matters, shall be observed inviolably by both sides. Thus the provost of the church of Blessed Alexander shall hold the first place in choir and at table on the left-hand side; and the pledges of fidelity of the clerics [Col. 0860C] shall be received jointly by both parties.

If in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this text of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second and third time, should not correct his offence by suitable satisfaction, let him forfeit the dignity of his honour and office and be subject, at the final judgment, to strict vengeance.

Given at the Lateran, on the second day before the Kalends of May [30 April].

## XXVI. To Alfonso, king of Portugal, who had made his kingdom tributary to the Roman Church.  
*(1 May 1144.)*

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 616.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ A., illustrious duke of Portugal: greeting [Col. 0860D] and the apostolic blessing.

We greatly rejoice in your devotion, beloved son in the Lord, because you recognize yourself as one of those sheep whom our Lord Jesus Christ entrusted to Peter’s keeping. Since, being intent upon the conquest of the pagans and occupied with many secular affairs, you could not visit the thresholds of the apostles, through the hand of our beloved son G., cardinal deacon and then legate of the Apostolic See in those regions, you performed homage with commendable devotion to our predecessor Pope Innocent of happy memory. You offered to Blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, the land entrusted to you by God, and humbly committed both your person and that land to his [Col. 0861A] protection. Afterwards, both by your letters and through our venerable brother I., archbishop of Braga, you likewise promised us that both you and your heirs would pay each year to the Roman pontiff four ounces of gold from that land.

Therefore we, who, although unworthy, are seen to sit in the place of Blessed Peter, receive both you and your sons and successors, with his help, among the heirs of that prince of the apostles, so that you may remain under his blessing and protection, for your souls as well as your bodies; defended through it from the attack of visible and invisible enemies, you may by the Lord’s bounty be able to return to the heavenly kingdoms.

Given at the Lateran, on the Kalends of May [1 May].

## XXVII. General apostolic confirmation concerning the possessions of the Church of Lichfield, without prejudice to the canonical right of the bishop of Coventry.  
*(4 May 1144.)*

[*Monasticon Anglicanum*, vol. III, p. 232.]

[Col. 0861B]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the canons of the Church of Lichfield, present and future, in perpetuity.

It befits the mercy of the Apostolic See to extend the aid of maternal protection to all who seek its patronage, so that, just as by the Lord’s disposition we are called fathers among God’s people, so too we may be proved such by the performance of our works. For this reason, beloved sons in the Lord, we grant your desires with paternal kindness; and, following the example of our predecessor Pope Innocent, we strengthen the church of Lichfield, in [Col. 0861C] which you are engaged in divine service, by the text of this present document. We establish that the churches, tithes, and whatever possessions and goods the aforesaid church now justly and canonically holds, or may in future obtain, God favouring, by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means—and likewise whatever our venerable brother Roger, bishop of Coventry, has bestowed upon you, in churches, tithes, lands, and other possessions, or shall in future, God favouring, bestow—shall remain firm and unimpaired to you in perpetuity.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb [Col. 0861D] that same church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any molestations; but that all things shall be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, without prejudice to the canonical right of the bishop of Coventry and the authority of the Apostolic See. If anyone should presume with rash audacity to attempt this, let him incur the indignation of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul, and be subject to excommunication. But those who preserve these things shall obtain the blessing and grace of those same apostles and of us. Amen, amen.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Baro, chaplain and scribe, on the fourth day before the Nones of May [4 May], in the seventh indiction, [Col. 0862A] in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of lord Pope Lucius II.

## XXVIII. To Roger, bishop of Coventry, and the Church of Lichfield, he confirms certain churches.  
*(4 May 1144.)*

[*Monasticon Anglicanum*, III, 235.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother ROGER, bishop of Coventry, and his successors canonically promoted, and also to the Church of Lichfield, in perpetuity.

The authority of our office exhorts us, etc., to act toward our neighbours after the example of our predecessor Pope Innocent of blessed memory by the present document, etc.; moreover, [Col. 0862B] the churches of Stafford and Penkridge, the church of Wolverhampton, with all their appurtenances, belonging to you, Roger, etc., without prejudice in all things to the authority of the Apostolic See. If therefore anyone, etc.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Baro, chaplain and scribe, on the fourth day before the Nones of May [4 May], in the seventh indiction, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of lord Pope Lucius II.

## XXIX. To Roger, bishop of Coventry, he grants certain privileges.  
*(4 May 1144.)*

[*Monasticon Anglicanum*, III, 232.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable [Col. 0862C] brother ROGER, bishop of Coventry, and his successors canonically promoted, in perpetuity.

From the charge laid upon us by God, etc. . . . assuredly his own, to Prior Laurence and the monks of the same place, etc. Following the example of Pope Innocent, our predecessor of happy memory, we confirm by the text of this present document, etc., without prejudice in all things to the authority of the Apostolic See. But if anyone, etc.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Baro, chaplain and scribe, on the fourth day before the Nones of May [4 May], in the seventh indiction, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of lord Pope Lucius II.

## XXX. Bull confirming all rights and privileges of the monastery of St Mary of Castellione.  
*(10 May 1144.)*

[MURATORI, *Antiquitates Italicae*, V, 819.]

[Col. 0862D]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ALBERT, abbot of the monastery of St Mary of Castellione, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

It befits us willingly to grant a request which is known to concern the purpose of religion and the salvation of souls, and to extend fitting assistance to the desires of petitioners. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests and receive the aforesaid monastery, which belongs by right to Blessed Peter, wherein you are devoted to divine service, into the right and protection [Col. 0863A] of that prince of the apostles; and we strengthen it by the privilege of this present document. We establish that whatever possessions and goods the same monastery justly and canonically possesses, or may in future acquire, God granting, by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: the church of St Saviour of *Basilica ducis*, with all its appurtenances; the church of St Remigius of *Palude*; the church of St Eusebius of Gavi; the cell of St Benedict of Guasto, with all its appurtenances; the church of St Mary of Charity, situated in the suburb of Mantnano; the church of Castello. [Col. 0863B] [Lacuna.] The church of Tasajalo; whatever you possess in the counties of Luni and Genoa, in the county of Modena, namely in the places called Solaria and Herbaria; and in the abbey of St Mary of Corsica, called Plaidelii, with all its appurtenances; and in the court called Marca Regia; in the court of Rupta; at Castello Novo; Casale Albini; and St Andrew.

When you, the present abbot of that place, or any of your successors, die, let no one be placed over it by any artifice of subreption or force, except one whom the brethren, by common consent or by the consent of the sounder part of the brethren, elect according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict. The person elected shall be blessed by the Roman pontiff. You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars and churches, and ordinations of your monks or canons who are to be promoted to sacred orders, from whichever Catholic bishops you prefer. We forbid any bishop, without the abbot’s consent, to celebrate public masses in that monastery, or to hold a station, synod, or any ordination there; [Col. 0863C] and we decree that your monastery shall remain free from every yoke or jurisdiction of any person.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved wholly intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, without prejudice in all respects to the authority of the Apostolic See. If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this text of our confirmation, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second and third time, should not make amends by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ; and let him be subject, at the final judgment, to strict vengeance. But to all who preserve the rights of that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action, [Col. 0863D] and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

[Col. 0864A] I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, . . . [lacuna] . . . I, Guy, cardinal priest of the title of St Chrysogonus, have subscribed. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Thomas, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina, have subscribed. I, P. . . . [lacuna] . . . *manus*, bishop of Tusculum, have subscribed. I, Manfred, cardinal priest of the title of St Sabina, have subscribed. I, Aribert, cardinal priest of St Anastasia, have subscribed. [Col. 0864B] I, Odo, cardinal deacon of St George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Wido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal deacon of St Adrian, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal deacon of St Mary the New, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Baro, chaplain and scribe, on the sixth day before the Ides of May [10 May], in the seventh indiction, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of lord Pope Lucius.

A cord hangs without a lead seal.

## XXXI. Privilege for the nunnery of Fontevraud.  
*(10 May 1144.)*

[PAVILLON, *Vie de Robert d’Arbrissel*, Proofs, p. 628.]

[Col. 0864C]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ P[ETRONILLA], abbess of the monastery of Fontevraud, and the sisters there devoted to divine service, present and future, in perpetuity.

It befits the mercy of apostolic governance to cherish religious persons and to fortify their places by pious protection. Therefore, the more fragile the female sex is, the more we wish to extend to you paternal care and solicitude, and to defend the rights of your monastery against the assaults of evil men. Accordingly, beloved daughters in the Lord, we graciously assent to your reasonable petitions, and, following in the footsteps of our predecessors, receive under the right and protection of Blessed Peter the monastery [Col. 0864D] of St Mary of Fontevraud, which particularly belongs to the guardianship of the Apostolic See and in which you are engaged in divine service; and we strengthen it by the privilege of this present document.

For we establish that whatever goods and possessions the aforesaid monastery now justly and lawfully possesses, or may hereafter acquire through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain whole and unimpaired for ever to you and your successors. Furthermore, if any one of the faithful, moved by devotion, bestows upon you a place in which you wish to construct an oratory, then, at your request, the archbishops and bishops in whose parish that place lies shall provide you without molestation, as required by the episcopal office, with holy water and the other ecclesiastical sacraments.

Just as we decree that you are free from every exaction, so we also ordain that priests subject to the parishes to which they are known to belong, while serving you without disturbance, shall devote themselves to your service. We further establish that the same archbishop and bishop shall diligently protect and defend you, and shall not allow any injury or molestation to be brought against you regarding possessions which you can prove, through two or three suitable witnesses, to have been lawfully donated to and possessed by you. If anyone should presume to attempt this, they shall, as required by the episcopal office, administer full justice against that person. [Col. 0865B]

Since you lead a religious life and ought to live from the alms and beneficence of others, we establish that no one may presume to exact or receive tithes from you on the produce which you cultivate at your own expense or on the increase of your animals. Moreover, on account of the greater renown for religion which by God’s grace spreads far and wide from your place, we command by the authority of the Apostolic See that free persons who, for the salvation of their souls, vow to persevere in the service of God and of the Church, either at your monastery or in places belonging to it, shall persevere in that good intention and faithfully serve the sisters in accordance with the disposition of the abbess of that place, for the goods of God, as was established by the judgment of Robert of Arbrissel, priest of distinguished religious devotion and blessed memory. [Col. 0865C] If it should happen otherwise, we enjoin upon the diocesan bishop that he compel them, as violators of their vow, to return to their former religious purpose, punishing by fitting correction what was rashly done.

We decree that the burial place of that monastery shall be entirely free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and final wish of those who have decided to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated, without prejudice to the right of the mother church. We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those [Col. 0865D] for whose governance and support they were granted.

If in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this text of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second and third time, should not make amends by suitable satisfaction, let that person forfeit the dignity of power and honour; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, [Col. 0866A] our Redeemer; and let him be subject, at the final judgment, to strict vengeance. But to all who preserve the rights of that place, may there be peace from God and our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Baro, chaplain and scribe, on the sixth day before the Ides of May [10 May], in the seventh indiction, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of lord Pope Lucius II.

## XXXII. Privilege for the Church of Tours.  
*(Fragment—10 May 1144.)*

[LAUNOII, *Opera*, III, II, 64.]

[Col. 0866B] Pope Lucius II, in the year 1144, in his diploma issued at the Lateran on the sixth day before the Ides of May [10 May], in the seventh indiction and the first year of his pontificate, says as follows: “Moreover, let the liberty and immunity, honours and benefices bestowed upon that same Church of Blessed Martin by the writings of our predecessors, the Roman pontiffs Adeodatus, Leo, Hadrian, Sergius, Gregory, Urban, Paschal, Callistus, Honorius, and Innocent, or by those of the archbishops of Tours Crotpert, Ibbo, and Herard, be preserved to you whole and inviolate.”

## XXXIII. Bull to Humbert of Prangins.  
*(11 May 1144.)*

[*Mémoires et documents de la Société d’histoire de Genève*, II, II, 32.]

[Col. 0866C]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ HUMBERT of Pringins.

[Note: [Col. 0865D] Pringins, a château and village situated on a slope above Lake Geneva, near Nyon, canton of Vaud. The Prangins family referred to here was a noble family which, in that capacity, had the right to sit in the former Estates of the Pays de Vaud. (See Muller, *History of Switzerland*, book I, chapter 10; *Documents relating to the history of the Pays de Vaud*, by the [Col. 0866D] Baron de Grenus, Geneva, 1817, p. 62.)]

Greeting and the apostolic blessing.

We greatly rejoice in your devotion, beloved son in the Lord, because you recognize yourself as one of those sheep whom our Lord Jesus Christ entrusted to the keeping of Blessed Peter; you have reverently visited his thresholds and committed your person and land to the protection of that prince of the apostles. For in the presence of us and our brethren, having performed homage to Blessed Peter and to us, you promised that both you and your heirs would pay yearly one Byzantine [*bisantium*] [Note: [Col. 0866D] *Bisantium*, *besant*: a gold coin so called because the emperors had the first such coins struck at Constantinople, or Byzantium. The use of this coin spread through Italy, France, Germany, and elsewhere. There were also white, or silver, besants.] from [Col. 0866D] your land to the Roman pontiff.

And therefore we, who, although unworthy, are seen to sit in the place of Blessed Peter, receive both you and your sons and successors, with his help, among the heirs of that prince of the apostles, so that you may remain always under his blessing and protection, both in soul and body, and through it may attain the heavenly kingdoms by the Lord’s bounty.

Given at the Lateran, on the fifth day before the Ides of May [11 May].

## XXXIV. Privilege for the church of Bologna.  
*(13 May 1144.)*

[SAVIOLI, *Annali Bolognesi*, I, II, 206.]

[Col. 0867A]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved brother in Christ HENRY, bishop of the church of Bologna, and his successors canonically appointed.

If we desire to attain the heavenly kingdoms, we must labour with unwearied zeal; rather, insofar as we can, with God’s help, we should strive diligently to hasten, so that we may in every way support and restore to better condition the churches which our Lord also acquired by his own blood. Since Christ, the Son of God, entrusted them by divine, heavenly aid to Peter the keeper of the keys, [Col. 0867B] we must for this reason raise them to the most eminent condition. For we most certainly believe that the more zealously we foster the exaltation of churches, the more worthily we enjoy the bounty of him through whose spiritual care the Catholic and Apostolic Church is ruled and governed, in which, by God’s ordinance, we perform the office of the apostles.

Therefore we wish it to be known to all that our most reverend brother Henry, bishop of Bologna, having come to Rome to visit the thresholds of the apostles, showed us the charters, investitures, and confirmations made by our predecessors—that is, the apostolic pontiffs Agapetus, Pelagius, and Gregory VII—concerning the property of his church. . . . Inclining favourably to his petitions, we grant and confirm to his church, without prejudice in all respects to the right and privilege of the Roman Church, [Col. 0867C] the monastery of St Michael the Archangel, situated on the paternal estate, with all its property and appurtenances; and we grant the estate of Brento, with male and female serfs and all its appurtenances. We also bestow the monastery of St Mary, situated in the district called Monte Palense, which Emperor Jovinian gave to the Church of Bologna, with the estate held there; the place called Aurelia, with the hills situated around the aforesaid monastery; and the other estates called Bombiana, with their hamlets and appurtenances, and the mountain called Cavallorum.

We likewise grant the port called Galliana, with bank-toll and customs duty, marshes, fisheries, woods, and all things known to belong to it; and two estates, one called Curta Major and the other Curta Minor, situated within the parish called Boida. Moreover, we give the monastery of St Anastasius, founded on the Petriculo estate, with port, customs duty, and bank-toll; with woods and hunting rights, marshes and fishing rights, and all things which appear to belong to the estate called Petriculosum and to the aforesaid monastery. We also give the estate called Gellula, beside the river called Savena, with olive groves, vineyards, fields, woods, hunting rights, household servants, tenant farmers, and all its appurtenances; and, not far from there, the entire estate of Venetiae, also called Sociorum, belonging to those estates; and the estate at Panigale, which contains [Col. 0868A] three landed and vineyard estates, called by these names: Candidatis, Pulsia, and Grisiribili. We also grant the monastery of St Prosper, situated in the aforesaid place called Panigale; the estate called Cumo with all its appurtenances; the monastery of St Martin at Pojo, with its estate and all its appurtenances; the monastery of St Peter in Strada; the monastery of St Mary with all its appurtenances; the monastery of St Peter, with the estate called Nucifatico and all its property; and the monastery of St Martin in Casalicchio with all its appurtenances.

We further bestow upon your charity the port in the city of Bologna commonly called St Peter’s, and the road called the Salt Road, with its road-toll and every payment customarily rendered from ancient times by those persons accustomed to travel there or return by the aforesaid routes. We also admonish them to endeavour to pay the aforesaid revenues at the appointed time without negligence. We likewise grant the monastery of St Mary called Major, with all its appurtenances, together with the house called Solariata within the city of Bologna, which belongs to that monastery; the monastery of St Columbanus the Confessor with all its property; the monastery of Saints Gervasius and Protasius with all its property; the monastery of St Andrew the Apostle, situated before the gate of St Peter, with all its property; and the monastery of St John the Evangelist, founded on the mountain called Oliveti, with all its appurtenances. [Col. 0868B]

Likewise we grant the monastery of St Stephen called Jerusalem, which the most holy bishop Lord Petronius built for the use of that church, together with the market of St John the Baptist held there. We further confirm and establish the estate called Millonis, with port, bank-toll, customs duty, and market; woods, hunting rights, marshes and fishing rights; male and female serfs, tenant farmers, and all things belonging to it.

Likewise we grant all estates and possessions, monasteries and parish churches, baptismal churches and all other churches, castles, villages, abbots, monks, priests, deacons, educated and uneducated clerics, male and female servants of God and deaconesses, servants of either sex, and all persons living upon the land of the aforesaid Church [Col. 0868D] of Bologna, to be under the authority and protection of you and your successors within the boundaries and confines of the whole diocese of Bologna, as from the river called Gaibana and the stream called Sablosculus, together with the road called Ungarista, as far as . . . [lacuna] . . . and the place called Cutte, and the river called Leo, and the other called Muza.

Likewise we grant to the aforesaid church the estate called Maxumasticum, with its property, possessions, and all appurtenances. We decree that all the things read above, which the aforesaid church truly and justly holds or shall hereafter acquire, shall be reserved in perpetuity both for you and for all who shall succeed in the rank and office which you hold, or for those whose interest it may be.

But if any person, whether king, priest, judge, or layman, knowing the text of this our constitution, should attempt to act against it . . . [lacuna] . . . let him forfeit the dignity of his honour; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; and unless he restores what has been wrongly taken away by another or laments unlawful acts by worthy penance, let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer, [Col. 0869A] and let him be subject, at the final judgment, to strict vengeance. But to all who preserve the rights of that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church. [Col. 0869B] I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of St Callistus. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Pastor. I, Thomas, cardinal priest of the title of St Justina. I, Raynerius, cardinal priest of the title of St Prisca. I, Guy, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Lawrence and Damasus. I, Nicholas, cardinal priest of the title of St Cyriacus. I, Aribert, cardinal priest of the title of St Anastasia. I, Manfred, cardinal priest of the title of St Sabina. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Theodorinus, bishop of Santa Rufina. [Col. 0869C] I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. I, Aymar, bishop of Tusculum. I, Peter, bishop of Albano. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of St George at the Golden Veil. I, Gerald, cardinal deacon of St Mary in Domnica. I, Guy, unworthy minister of the altar in the Roman Church. I, Rodulph, cardinal deacon of St Lucy in the Seven Solia. I, John, cardinal deacon of St Adrian.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Baro, chaplain and [Col. 0869D] scribe, on the third day before the Ides of May [13 May], in the seventh indiction, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of lord Pope Lucius II.

## XXXV. He receives the church of St Mary of Ardennes into protection and confirms its property.  
*(13 May 1144.)*

[*Neustria Pia*, p. 704.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GISLEBERT, prior of the church of St Mary of Ardena, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life in perpetuity: greeting and the apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0870A] The care of the universal Church has been entrusted to us by the Lord, the provider of all good things, for this purpose: that we may love religious persons and strive by every means to promote religion pleasing to God. For no service is ever rendered acceptable to God unless, proceeding from the root of charity, it is preserved by the purity of religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid church, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods the same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by the grant of pontiffs, the gifts of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, by God’s favor, acquire, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following in their proper terms:

The church of St. Germanus of Alba Herba. The whole tithe from Oelard’s own demesne at Hermenville. One acre of land from the fief of William Crassus, before the well of Ardena. One field of land from Bitot, from Odard’s fief. One acre of land from Bitot. Two acres of land and three virgates in the long *varenda* [enclosed pasture?]. One field of land at Buruni, from Aiulf’s fief. Two acres of land between Caen and Ardena, from the fief of Geoffrey of the Castle. Two fields of land above St. Germanus, from the fief of Henry, son of Herbert. Nine acres of land at Ardena. Five strips of land, [Col. 0870C] between St. Germanus and the infirmary. Five strips on the other side of the road. The whole tithe from the demesne of Adam of Francavilla. One prebend at Bayeux, of ten denarii, from the king’s alms; another at Caen, of seven denarii. One house at Caen, free and exempt from all market dues. Another house in the borough of the abbess at Caen. Two houses in the borough of the abbot at Caen, in the new settlement. Three acres of land at La Perella, and everything that Hasculph held at Lucerne from his own demesne (except a portion of the wood of Curba Fossa), and two arpents of vineyard at Suligneium. The whole tithe of Gripum, both in the mills and waters and in all the revenues of the village. One fishery at Boleium. All the land of Gislebert, son of [Col. 0870D] Adam, from his own demesne at Lucerne. One acre of land in *carum* [uncertain], from the fief of Ralph, son of Ralph. Two measures of grain, one of which was given by William, son of Roger, and the other by Richard Chalus.

We likewise decree that the canonical order, according to the Rule of blessed Augustine and the institution of the Premonstratensian brethren, shall be inviolably maintained there for all time. We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all things shall be kept whole, to be of every benefit for the uses of those for whose governance and support they were granted, without prejudice to the canonical right of the diocesan bishop [Col. 0871A] and the authority of the Apostolic See. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been admonished a second or third time, should fail to make fitting satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honor, know himself or herself guilty before the divine judgment of the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and Redeemer Jesus Christ, and be subject at the last judgment to severe punishment. But upon all who preserve what is right for the same place, may there be the peace of our Lord Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church. [Col. 0871B] I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. I, Ismar, bishop of Tusculum. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Calixtus. I, Thomas, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina. I, Gilibert, cardinal priest of the title of St. Mark. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Lawrence and Damasus. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Gerard, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in [Col. 0871C] Dominica. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of St. Angelo.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Baron, chaplain and scribe, on the third Ides of May, in the seventh indiction, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius II.

### XXXVI. To Raymond, Archbishop of Toledo.—He confirms the primacy of the Church of Toledo. (Year 1144, May 13.)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 609.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother RAYMOND, Archbishop of Toledo, and to his successors canonically appointed forever.

[Col. 0871D] The most holy Roman and Apostolic Church was established by the Lord Jesus Christ himself, Savior of all, as the head and pivot of all Churches. It is therefore not fitting that the members should dissent from the head, but that they should obey the exalted reason and heavenly providence of the head. The discerning governance of the head, moreover, joining together the dutiful actions of the individual members, distinctly preserves for each the right and order established by nature, and, without envy, preserves in social charity for all noble persons the dignity of their own comeliness. Moved by this reasoning, therefore, we wish to preserve the honor of the noble and renowned Church of Toledo, the own and special daughter of the Apostolic See. Accordingly, venerable brother Raymond, whom we love with true charity in Christ, [Col. 0872A] we have judged it right to assent, with the affection of paternal kindness, to your reasonable requests.

By the page of this present privilege, therefore, we decree by apostolic authority that you shall hold the dignity of primacy throughout all the kingdoms of Spain. You shall accordingly use the pallium granted to your charity by the Apostolic See in the celebration of Masses only on the chief feasts: namely, on the three days at the Nativity of the Lord; at Epiphany; at Hypopanton [Hypapante, the Presentation]; on Maundy Thursday; on Holy Saturday; on the three days of Easter; at the Ascension; at Pentecost; on the feasts of Saint Mary, of Saint Michael, and of Saint John the Baptist; on all feasts of the apostles and of those martyrs whose relics rest in your church; on the feasts of Saint Martin and Saint Ildefonsus, confessors; [Col. 0872B] and on the Commemoration of All Saints; at consecrations of churches, bishops, and clergy; on the anniversary of your own consecration; and on the feasts of Saint Isidore and Leander.

All the prelates of the Spanish kingdoms shall acknowledge you as primate, and shall refer to you any matter arising among them that deserves inquiry. Nevertheless, in all things the authority of the Roman Church is reserved. Furthermore, retaining your person in more special favor, we decree that any cause concerning you, should one arise, shall be decided by the judgment of the Roman pontiff alone. We strengthen the Church of Toledo by the stability of this present privilege, confirming to it the parish of Complutum with its boundaries, and also all churches which it is known to have possessed of ancient right. Moreover, we decree that the episcopal sees which you now [Col. 0872C] justly and peaceably possess shall be subject to that Church of Toledo as their metropolis. As for the remaining sees that were subject to it in ancient times, when almighty God in the mercy of his condescension restores them to Christian power, we decree by the authority of this decree that they shall be restored to their proper head.

Moreover, we subject to your jurisdiction the dioceses of those cities which, through Saracen invasion, have lost their own metropolitans, on the condition that, so long as they are without their own metropolitans, they shall be subject to you as to their proper metropolitan. But if any metropolitan sees are restored to their own condition, let each diocese be restored to its own metropolitan, so that under the governance of its proper shepherd it may glory in the bestowal of the divine benefit. [Col. 0872D] If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, etc.

Given at the Lateran through the hands of Baron, chaplain and scribe, on the third Ides of May, in the seventh indiction, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius II.

### XXXVII. To the archbishops and bishops established throughout Spain.—On the same matter. (Year 1144, May 13.)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 610.]

The clemency of the Apostolic See is accustomed to preserve for individual churches and ecclesiastical persons their dignity and right. Therefore we, whose particular concern it is [Col. 0873A] to have care for all churches, kindly received our venerable brother, the most reverend Archbishop of Toledo, when he came to us; and, having examined the privileges of our predecessors, confirmed to him the dignity of primacy throughout all the kingdoms of Spain, in accordance with the tenor of those privileges. Therefore, sending him back to his own see with the favor of the Apostolic See and the support of our letters, we command and direct all of you: that you take care to render to him, as your primate, canonical obedience and due reverence without any contradiction. For it is fitting that one who rejoices to preside over many subjects should by no means blush to be subject to his own superiors.

[Col. 0873B] Given at the Lateran, on the third Ides of May.

### XXXVIII. Privilege for the monastery of St. Bartholomew at Neuburg. (Year 1144, May 14.)

[*Codex Laureshamensis diplomaticus*, I, 239.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons MARQUARD, provost of the church of St. Bartholomew the Apostle of Nova Civitas, and his brethren, both present and future, professing the regular life, forever.

The care of the universal Church has been entrusted to us by God, the provider of all good things, for this purpose: that we may love religious persons and strive by every means to promote religion pleasing to God. For no service is ever rendered acceptable to God unless, proceeding from the root of charity, it is preserved by the purity of religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid church, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods the same church justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, through the grant of pontiffs, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, by God’s favor, acquire, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. No one, moreover, may presume to usurp the advocacy of this place there; [Col. 0873D] rather, the abbot of Lorsch shall defend the same church with its appurtenances, in the capacity of advocate, from the attacks of evil men. You shall also have free power to bury your pilgrims or guests who decide to be buried there, provided that they have not been excommunicated.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all things shall be kept whole, to be of every benefit for the uses of those for whose governance and support they were granted, without prejudice to the canonical right of the diocesan bishop and the authority of the Apostolic See. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing this page of our constitution, [Col. 0874A] should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been admonished a second or third time, should fail to make fitting satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honor, know himself or herself guilty before the divine judgment of the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ, and be subject at the last judgment to severe punishment. But upon all who preserve what is right for the same place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

SHOW US, O LORD, YOUR MERCY.

Fare well.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. [Col. 0874B] I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Theodewin, bishop of St. Rufina, have subscribed. I, Gerhard, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Dominica, have subscribed. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of St. Nicholas in Carcere Tulliano, have subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Pastor, have subscribed. [Col. 0874C] I, Peter, bishop of Albano, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Baron, chaplain and scribe, on the second Ides of May, in the seventh indiction, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius II.

### XXXIX. To Bernard, bishop of St. David’s (Menevia). (Year 1144, May 14.)

[WARTHON, *Anglia Sacra*, II, 549.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother BERNARD, bishop of St. David’s: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have received the letters of your brotherhood with due kindness, and have carefully considered what they contain concerning the dignity of your Church, both in those letters themselves and in the others sent to the Apostolic See on this matter. But since, owing to sins and the overflowing malice of evil men, the dignity of that Church was, long ago, alienated from it and transferred to other Churches, we have no settled counsel at present as to what should be decreed concerning it. By God’s grace, indeed, we intend shortly to send our legates into those regions on Church affairs; through them you shall take care to establish this cause by the testimony of old men and by authentic documents of your Church. Once the truth has been more fully learned through them, we shall, after more mature deliberation, decree what ought to be established for the honor of God.

Given at the Lateran, on the second Ides of May.

### XL. Bull confirming the judgment of Pope Urban II concerning the subjection of the Church of Dol to the Church of Tours. (Year 1144, May 15.)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 619.]

[Col. 0875A]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HUGH, Archbishop of Tours, and to his successors canonically appointed forever.

Matters decided by the truth of judgment ought to be entrusted to the record of letters, lest they may thereafter be disturbed by the opposition of evil men. Our predecessor Pope Innocent, of happy memory, committed to our venerable brother Geoffrey, bishop of Chartres and then legate of the Apostolic See, for investigation and settlement, the controversy long disputed between the pastors of the Church of Tours and that of Dol concerning the precedence of Tours and the subjection of Dol. When this case had been treated in his presence at many places in Gaul and had not yet been brought to its proper conclusion, the Archbishop of Dol came, in our presence, before that same predecessor of ours, complaining that he had often been burdened by the delay of the case and had incurred many expenses on that account. He therefore humbly asked that our same predecessor should recall the case to his own presence and bring it to a proper conclusion. Assenting to his petition, he directed you by apostolic letters, venerable brother Hugh, Archbishop of Tours, [Col. 0875C] commanding you to appear before the apostolic presence prepared to show the right of your church in this matter.

In the meantime, when he had entered, by divine judgment, upon the way of all flesh, you, brother Archbishop, and the Archbishop of Dol both appeared before us for the resolution of this controversy. Since you had produced many arguments, documents, and proofs concerning the right of your church, there was finally produced in the midst the privilege of Pope Urban, our predecessor of blessed memory. It clearly contained that, after many examinations and reconsiderations of this matter in his own presence and also in that of the legates of the Apostolic See, and after careful examination of the writings of the Roman pontiffs Nicholas, John, Leo IX, and Gregory VII, and after all matters on both sides had been fully considered with diligent examination, that pope, by the common judgment of his brother bishops and many clerics of the Roman Church, decreed and confirmed by the protection of his writing that both the bishop of Dol and all other bishops of Brittany thereafter should acknowledge the Church of Tours as their metropolitan and render it due reverence; and that, after the death of Roland, who then presided over the Church of Dol, no bishop of Dol should at any later time aspire to use the pallium.

To this the bishop of Dol replied nothing supported by reason, nor could he defend his side by the authority of any Roman pontiff. Having therefore taken counsel, since, though unworthy, we have been placed by the Lord’s ordering in the seat of justice and neither can nor ought to depart from the way of truth, [Col. 0876A] we, following the footsteps of the same predecessor, in the assembly of our brethren Conrad of Sabina, Imer of Tusculum, bishops of our see; Raymond, Archbishop of Toledo; Henry of Winchester, Ulger of Angers, John of Aleth, Nigel of Ely, and Philip of Bayeux, bishops; Gregory of St. Mary in Trastevere, Peter of St. Pudentiana, Thomas of St. Vitalis, Gilbert of St. Mark, and Guido of St. Lawrence in Damaso, cardinal priests; Gregory of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, Odo of St. George at the Velum Aureum, Guido of Saints Cosmas and Damian, and Octavian of St. Nicholas in Carcere, cardinal deacons; Peter of Cluny, Atmeric of St. Julian of Tours, and Berneris of Nucaria, abbots; Peter, prior of St. Mary of Charity; the noble Romans Cencius Frangipane and his nephew Cencius, Leo son of Peter Leo, and Peter Uguition; and many others, clerics as well as laymen—have confirmed the same judgment by the authority of the Apostolic See granted us by God. By our own hand, through the staff, we invested both you and the Church of Tours with the obedience of those bishops.

In accordance with the tenor of that judgment, we command that both the bishop of Dol and all the bishops of Lower Brittany thereafter shall be subject to the Church of Tours as their own metropolitan and shall humbly render it due obedience and reverence. This moderation, however, is to be observed: our brother Geoffrey, bishop of Dol, shall have the pallium and be subject only to the Roman pontiff for as long as he presides over the same church; but after him no bishop of Dol may presume to aspire to the use of the pallium. Rather, as has already been said, he shall acknowledge the Church of Tours as his own metropolitan and reverently obey it.

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing the judgment of this our determination, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been admonished a second or third time, should fail to make fitting satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honor, know himself or herself guilty before the divine judgment of the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ, and be subject at the last judgment [Col. 0876D] to severe punishment. But upon those who observe it may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

ST. PETER. ST. PAUL.

Pope Lucius II. (Place of the monogram.)

SHOW US, O LORD, YOUR MERCY.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Theodewin, bishop of St. Rufina, have subscribed. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Imar, bishop of Tusculum, have subscribed. [Col. 0877A] I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Pastor, have subscribed. I, Thomas, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina, have subscribed. I, Gilbert, cardinal priest of the title of St. Mark, have subscribed. I, Ranier, cardinal priest of the title of St. Stephen on the Caelian Hill, have subscribed. I, Manfred, cardinal priest of the title of St. Sabina, have subscribed. I, Aribert, cardinal priest of the title of St. Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of St. Nicholas in [Col. 0877B] Carcere Tulliano, have subscribed. I, Guido, unworthy minister of the altar in the Roman Church, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal deacon of St. Adrian, have subscribed. I, Gregory, deacon of St. Angelo, have subscribed. I, Hugh, deacon of the Roman Church at St. Lucy in Horphea, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Baron, chaplain and scribe, on the Ides of May, in the seventh indiction, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius II.

### XLI. To the bishops of Saint-Brieuc and Tréguier.—He absolves them from the obedience promised to the bishop and Church of Dol. (Year 1114, May 15.)

[MARTÈNE, *Thesaurus*, III, 890.]

[Col. 0877C]

We have thought fit briefly to inform your brotherhood how the controversy, long disputed between their pastors concerning the precedence of the Church of Tours and that of Dol, was decided according to judicial order in our presence. Having heard the arguments of both parties and examined the privileges of the Roman pontiffs, especially that of Pope Urban, which clearly contained that, after many examinations and reconsiderations in his own presence and also that of his legates, that pope judged that both the bishop of Dol and the other bishops of Lower Brittany should acknowledge the Church of Tours as their own metropolitan and render it due [Col. 0877D] reverence, and that after Roland’s death no bishop of Dol should aspire to use the pallium: therefore, having taken the counsel of our brethren and following the footsteps of the same predecessor of ours, we confirmed the same judgment by the authority of the Apostolic See and invested our venerable brother Hugh, Archbishop of Tours, by our own hand and through the staff, with the obedience of those bishops.

Accordingly, absolving you by the authority granted to us by God from disobedience and fealty to the Church of Dol and to its bishop [reading: “to the Church of Dol and to the bishop himself”], we command you through apostolic letters and enjoin you under obedience to render obedience and reverence to the same archbishop and the Church of Tours. But if you presume to be contemptuous, we shall, with the Lord as author, hold ratified the judgment which he shall pronounce against you in canonical equity.

[Col. 0878A] Given at the Lateran, on the Ides of May.

### XLII. Bull for the Church of St. Martin of Tours. (Year 1144, May 15.)

[*Défense des priviléges de Saint-Martin de Tours*, p. 17.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the canons of the church of Blessed Martin of Tours, both present and future, canonically appointed forever.

Although by the authority and benevolence of the Apostolic See we stand as debtors to all Churches and ecclesiastical persons, it is nevertheless fitting that we provide with more zealous care for those persons known to adhere more especially to the holy Roman Church. Accordingly, beloved sons in the Lord, assenting to your just requests, we have judged that the church of Blessed Martin of Tours, in which you devote yourselves to divine office and which is known especially to belong by right and property to the holy Roman Church, ought to be fortified by the protection of the Apostolic See and strengthened by the protection of this present writing. We decree, therefore, that whatever possessions and whatever goods are now seen justly and lawfully to belong to that church, or which you may hereafter, by the grants of pontiffs, the gifts of princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s assistance, acquire, shall remain secure [Col. 0878C] and unimpaired for you. Among them we have added the following to be recorded by their proper names: the borough of Saint Peter the Maid, with its appurtenances, granted to you by our dearest son Louis, illustrious and glorious king of the Franks; the church of St. Paul of Cormariacum; the church of St. Mary of Bellomonte; and the church of St. Cosmas with its appurtenances. Furthermore, may the liberty and immunity, honors and benefices conferred upon the same Church of your Blessed Martin by the writings of our predecessors, the Roman pontiffs Adeodatus, Leo, Adrian, Sergius, Gregory, Urban, Paschal, Calixtus, Honorius, and Innocent, or by the Archbishops of Tours Crotbert, Ivo, and Airard, be preserved for you whole and inviolate.

Your cloister shall remain wholly free as far as the buttresses of the wall, as it is known to have remained hitherto. The priests residing within the church’s precinct in your cells and oratories, in the church of St. Venantius, and in the church of St. Peter called “of Cardonet,” shall henceforth retain the freedom in which they have remained in times past. You shall receive chrism, holy oil, and the ordinations of canons to be promoted to sacred orders from the Archbishop of Tours, provided he enjoys the favor and communion of the Apostolic See and is willing to provide them freely and without wrongdoing; otherwise, you shall receive them from any Catholic bishop. If one of your canons is also a canon of churches belonging to the archbishop’s right, the archbishop shall not have the power to excommunicate him after the benefice has been renounced.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church of Blessed Martin, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it by any molestations; but that all things shall be kept whole, to be beneficial for the uses of those for whose support and governance they were granted, with the authority of the Apostolic See reserved in all things. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been admonished a second or third time, should fail to make fitting satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honor, know himself or herself guilty before the divine judgment of the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord and Redeemer, and be subject at the last judgment to severe punishment. But upon all who preserve what is right for the same place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

SHOW US, O LORD, YOUR MERCY.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. I, Imar, bishop of Tusculum. I, Peter, bishop of Albano. I, Guilbert, cardinal priest of the title of St. Mark. [Col. 0879C] I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Calixtus. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Pastor. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Lawrence and Damasus. I, Rainer, cardinal priest of the title of St. Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Manfred, cardinal priest of the title of St. Sabina. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, John, cardinal deacon of St. Adrian. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of St. Angelo. [Col. 0879D] I, Astaud, cardinal deacon of St. Eustace beside the temple of Agrippa.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Baron, chaplain and scribe, on the sixth Ides of May, in the seventh indiction, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius II.

### XLIII. To Geoffrey, Count of Brittany, and Henry, his brother.—That they should not hinder the bishops of Brittany from being subject to the Church of Tours. (Year 1144, May 18.)

[MARTÈNE, *Thesaurus*, III, 890.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons in Christ, GAUFR. [Geoffrey], illustrious Count of Brittany, and HENR., his brother, and to the barons established throughout the bishoprics of Dol, Saint-Brieuc, [Col. 0880A] and Tréguier: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We wish all of you to know that our brother G. [Geoffrey], bishop of Dol, complained before our predecessor Pope Innocent, of happy memory, in our presence, concerning the case disputed in various places in Gaul between himself and our venerable brother Hu. [Hugh], Archbishop of Tours, about the precedence of the Church of Tours and the subjection of Dol: he complained that he had been greatly burdened and had incurred heavy expenses. Our same predecessor, sympathizing with his labors and expenses, summoned the aforesaid brother Hu., archbishop, to the Apostolic See at his request, in order that, with both parties present, he might hear the case and impose a proper conclusion.

When he had meanwhile entered, by divine judgment, upon the way of all flesh, we, who, though unworthy, have succeeded him by the Lord’s ordering, had both parties appear before us and decided the same controversy in this manner. Having heard the arguments of both parties and examined the privileges of the Roman pontiffs, especially that of Pope Urban, which clearly contained that, after many examinations and reconsiderations in his own presence and in that of the legates of the Apostolic See, he judged that both the bishop of Dol and also the bishops of Lower Brittany should acknowledge the Church of Tours as their own metropolitan and render it due reverence, and that after Roland’s death no bishop of Dol should aspire to use the pallium: when the bishop of Dol [Col. 0880C] had nothing to answer to this that was supported by reason, nor could defend his side through authentic privileges of the Roman pontiffs, we took counsel with our brethren, followed the footsteps of the same predecessor of ours, confirmed the same judgment by the authority of the Apostolic See, and invested our venerable brother Hu., archbishop, by our own hand and through the staff, with the obedience of those bishops.

Since it is the duty of good princes to preserve the ordinances of the holy Roman Church, we command your nobility through apostolic writings, and enjoin this upon you for the remission of sins: that you in no way hinder the same judgment promulgated by us under the compulsion of justice, but patiently allow them to obey reverently the said archbishop and the Church of Tours as their own metropolitan. For no injury is done to anyone when due honor and reverence are rendered to individual churches and ecclesiastical persons. If anyone presumes to oppose that archbishop in this matter, we shall, with the Lord as author, hold ratified the judgment which he shall pronounce against that person in canonical equity.

[Col. 0880D] Given at the Lateran, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of June.

### XLIV. Privilege for the Premonstratensian Order. (Year 1144, May 19.)

[LE PAIGE, *Bibliotheca Praemonstratensis*, p. 625.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons HUGH, abbot of Prémontré, and the co-abbots, [Col. 0881A] provosts, priors, and all brethren of the Premonstratensian Order, both present and future, regularly appointed forever.

To the abundant fruits which the sacred Premonstratensian Order, planted by heavenly institution in the field of the Church Militant, has hitherto produced and does not cease continually to produce, we direct the gaze of our consideration; and, weighing with attentive meditation that the Lord has granted it such great increase that it has already stretched forth its branches from sea to sea, we are bound by the care of the apostolic office to be found attentive and watchful concerning the growth of such a religious order. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, assenting to your reasonable requests, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, after the example of our predecessor Pope Innocent II of happy memory, your persons and the churches in which you are devoted to the divine service, [Col. 0881B] and strengthen them by the privilege of the present writing; decreeing that whatever possessions and goods your churches now justly and lawfully possess, or may hereafter reasonably acquire by grants of pontiffs, the generosity of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors.

Moreover, by apostolic authority and by the tenor of these presents, we grant that you shall be obliged to pay to no one the small tithes of vegetables, fruits, and meadows, but shall henceforth possess them freely, as you are known to have possessed them until now. We strictly forbid [Col. 0881C] archbishops or bishops in whose dioceses the possessions of your monasteries lie to dare, without judgment and just cause, to take from you those things which their predecessors reasonably bestowed upon your monasteries and confirmed by their writings.

Furthermore, we decree that alms which any of the faithful are known lawfully to have granted you through the hands of their bishops, and which those same bishops subsequently confirmed under their seals, shall remain whole and unimpaired to your monasteries, as you now possess them. We further forbid, following the example of our predecessor Celestine II of happy memory, archbishops, bishops, abbots, or provosts of your Order residing in their dioceses to prevent members of your Order from attending the general chapter of the Order [Col. 0881D]; indeed, they shall strictly compel those unwilling to go.

No brother who has promised stability and obedience in a place shall dare to depart, and no one shall dare to retain one who departs except with letters of commendation. In order that the integrity of your Order may be inviolably observed in both superiors and subjects, we decree that, if any abbot or provost of your churches departs from the governance of your Order and from the custom of the monastery of Prémontré, the father abbot shall admonish him twice or three times concerning his correction. If he appears incorrigible, the diocesan bishop, in the presence and upon the testimony of the father abbot and of two abbots of the same Order, shall without any delay depose the transgressor against his Order. The bishop shall send the deposed man back to the church [Col. 0882A] from which he came, and immediately appoint another suitable person in his place by the canonical election of the brethren.

Therefore let it be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb your persons or churches, or to take away their possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass them by wanton vexations; but let all things be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of those for whose support and governance they were granted. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second and third time, does not make suitable amends by satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour, and know himself or herself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let that person be cut off from the most holy body and [Col. 0882B] blood of God and of our Lord, Redeemer Jesus Christ, and be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve the just rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Baron, chaplain and scribe, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of June [19 May], in the seventh indiction, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius II.

### XLV. Privilege for the Church of Saint Martin of Laon. (1144, 19 May)

*[Ibid., p. 451.]*

[Col. 0882C]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GUATTERUS, abbot, and the canons of the church of Blessed Martin situated in the suburb of Laon, and to their successors devoted to divine service, forever.

Since without the worship of true religion neither the unity of charity can endure nor service pleasing to God be rendered, it befits apostolic authority to love religious persons and to foster religious places with the protection of the Apostolic See. For whenever something is requested of us which is recognized as consonant with reason, it becomes us willingly to grant it and to extend suitable support to the petitioners’ desires. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, assenting to your reasonable petitions, [Col. 0882D] we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves, after the example of Pope Innocent, our predecessor of happy memory, the church of Saint Martin, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of the present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and lawfully possesses, or may hereafter reasonably acquire by grants of pontiffs, the generosity of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors.

Among these, we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: namely, the allods of Diona, Conerchis, and Boelio; the mills of Fossa and Bartels; the allods of Taron de Planeto, Magniviler, Remicurt, [Col. 0883A] and Floricurt, with the tithes of those same allods; the whole territory of Salmuncei with woods, meadows, jurisdiction, and district, as it was granted to you by our venerable brother Stephen, bishop of Metz; the lands which you possess at Rokignicurt, Pirrehs, Pomeret, and Mozokis, with its mill; two-thirds of the tithe of Cilis, together with the tithe of the cultivated lands; the land of Aveins with its tithe; the cultivated field of Monstrata; the lands which you have at Vercigniac, Burcis, and Makigni, with mill, oven, and meadows; the allods of Vorgia; two-thirds of the tithe of Monte-Cavillo; the mill of Alneto; two-thirds of the tithe of Camulgia; the mill of Auvil; part of the tithe of Pusello and the lands which you hold there and at Athies; the mills of Anisi, Clari, Comportet, Destoneles, [Col. 0883B] Folia, and the mill called Becheralum; the vineyards which you possess on the hill of Laon, at Tiriniac, Vorgia, Jovia, Brueria, Sirivalla, Monte-Cavillo, Orgivalla, Camulgia, Capriniac, Monte Artelli, Trubercourt, Cryptis, Mons, and Philains.

Certainly, no cleric or layperson whatsoever shall presume to exact tithes from you on the produce which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or on the fodder of your animals. In order that the integrity of your Order may be inviolably observed in both superiors and subjects, we decree that, if any of the abbots who have proceeded from your church departs from the order and custom of the monastery of Saint Martin of Laon, the abbot of the said monastery shall admonish him twice [Col. 0883C] or three times concerning his correction. If he appears incorrigible, the diocesan bishop, in the presence and upon the testimony of the abbot of Saint Martin and of two abbots of the same Order, shall without delay depose the transgressor against his Order. The bishop shall send the deposed person back to the church of Blessed Martin and immediately appoint another suitable person in his place by the canonical election of the brethren.

We also grant that the burial-place of the same house shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who have resolved to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated, without prejudice to the right of parish priests. Therefore let it be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, [Col. 0883D] diminish them, or harass it by wanton vexations; but let all things be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of those for whose support and governance they were granted, saving the canonical justice of the diocesan bishop and the authority of the Apostolic See. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second and third time, does not make suitable amends by satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour, and know himself or herself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let that person be cut off from the most holy body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, and be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve their rights in that place [Col. 0884A] may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Baron, chaplain and scribe, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of June [19 May], in the seventh indiction, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius II.

### XLV bis. Privilege for the Church of Saint Peter of Faenza. (1144, 20 May)

*[MITARELLI, Additions concerning Faenza, p. 431.]*

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons FARULF, archdeacon of the Church of Faenza, [Col. 0884B] PETER, archpriest, and their brethren now present and to be canonically appointed in that same church in the future, forever.

By the Lord’s bounty we have been raised to the watchtower of apostolic dignity so that we may provide with fatherly care for the welfare and peace of churches, and preserve for each its just rights, ratified and unimpaired. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we assent to your just petitions and receive under the protection of the chief of the apostles himself and of ourselves the church of Blessed Peter, in which you are devoted to divine service; and we strengthen it by the protection of the present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically [Col. 0884C] possesses, or may hereafter, God being favourable, acquire by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, or offerings of the faithful, shall remain whole and unimpaired to you and your successors. We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no one whatsoever, etc.

**“Show us, O Lord, your mercy.”**

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church.  
I, Theodegrinus, bishop of Saint Rufina.  
I, Icmarus, bishop of Tusculum.  
I, Peter, bishop of Albano.  
I, Rainerius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca.  
I, Rainerius, cardinal priest of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill.  
I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Calixtus.  
I, Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Aquiro.  
[Col. 0884D] I, Ugo, cardinal deacon of the Holy Roman Church.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Baron, chaplain and keeper of the archives, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of June [20 May], in the seventh indiction, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius II.

### LXVI. Privileges for the Church of Rimini. (1144, 21 May)

*[UGHELLI, Sacred Italy, II, 422.]*

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother RAYNERIUS, bishop of Rimini, and to his successors to be canonically promoted, forever.

Placed by the Lord’s disposition upon the exalted watchtower of the Apostolic See, we are bound by the office entrusted to us to love our brethren the bishops [Col. 0885A] and to preserve for the churches committed to them by God their just rights. Therefore, adhering to the footsteps of our predecessors, the Roman pontiffs, we grant assent to your petitions, dearest brother Raynerius, bishop in Christ; and, strengthening the holy Church of Rimini, over which by God’s will you preside, with the privileges of the Holy Roman Church, we confirm to you and to your lawful successors, for the stability and peace of that place, its monasteries, parish churches, churches, courts, estates, halls, castles, hamlets, vineyards, lands, woods, marshes, cultivated and uncultivated properties, with their tithes and tenants, male and female servants, *aldiones* [a dependent legal class], and everything else that belongs to it justly and lawfully by the grant of any of the faithful or by any acquisition, and likewise whatever it holds from our Holy Roman Church. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names, namely:

[Col. 0885B]

Within the city of Rimini: the churches of Saint Michael the Archangel, Saint Innocentia, Saint Mary in Tribio, and of the holy martyrs Cosmas and Damian, called Holy Cross; of Saint Agnes, Saint Genesius, Saint Euphemia; the church of Saint John the Evangelist; Saint Martin; Saint Sylvester; Saint Vitalis; and Saint Lawrence situated above the Gallic Gate, with all their appurtenances.

Outside the city: the monastery of Saint Peter, with the oratory of Saint Maurus; the church of Saints Andrew and Donatus; the church of Saint John the Baptist, called “outside the gate,” together with the ruined church of Saint Stephen adjoining it; the church of Saint Apollinaris [Col. 0885C] and the monastery of Saint Gaudentius, with the oratory of Saint Victor and all their appurtenances; the church of Saints John and Paul; the church of Saint Gregory within the same city in the suburb; the church of Saint Mary Major; the parish church of Saint Angel “in Salute”; the parish church of Saints John and Peter, called “in Corpedo”; the churches of Saint Maurus, Saint Martin, Saint Christopher, and Saint Mary, and whatever right you have in the monastery of Saint Theonistus within that parish; the parish church of Saints Paul and Stephen; the church of Saint Prosper; the church of Saint Peter; the church of Saint Mary in Cento; the church of Saint Mary in Vernano; and Saint John in Frelioli, situated within that parish; the parish church of Saint John in Galilee; the church of Saint Christopher in Flanignano; the church of Saint Lawrence in the castle of Sulani; the church of Saint Paul in the court [Col. 0885D] of that same castle; the church of Saint Margaret in the castle with Curseto; and the church of Saint Andrew; the church of Saint Christopher in the castle of Scortigato and of Saint Vicinus; the parish church of Saint Archangel, called “in Acerbolo”; the church of Saint Mary in Camerano; Saint John in Cento; Saint Andrew in Gallia; Saint Mary New; Saint Mary in Ceola; Saint Bartholomew in Tribio, situated within that parish; the parish church of Saints Vitus and Modestus; the churches of Saint Justina and Saint Juvenalis within that parish; the parish church of Saint Martin, called “in Burdundo,” or “Burdunchio”; the parish church of Saint Lawrence, called “on Mount Appadiano”; the churches of Saint Christina; Saint Martin, called “in Viginti”; Saint Mary in Virgilano; Saint Mary in Paterno; and whatever right it has in the church of Saint Hermes situated within that parish;
