[Col. 0886A] the parish church of Saint John in New Bulgaria; the church of Saint Apollinaris, which lies in the wilderness; the church of Saint Martin, called “in Cerreto”; the church of Saint Peter in the castle of Veraculi; and whatever right it has in the churches of Saint Andrew, Saint Blasius, and Saint Vitus in Gualdo, situated within that parish; the parish church of Saint John in Cella Jovis; and the parish church of Saint Innocentia; the parish church of Saint Lawrence in Strata; the parish church of Saint Gregory in the castle of Conce, with the oratory of Saint Stephen situated beside that parish church; Saint Erasmus; the church of Saint Andrew; the parish church of Saint Sabinus; the church of Saint John in Pasciano; the parish church of Inferni, called that of Saint Columba; the churches of Saint Donatus and Saint Martin; Saint Mary in Uria; Saint Peter, called Accorti; and Saint Peter in Laureto, situated within that parish; the parish church of Saint Lawrence in Barcola.

We confirm to you and your successors the aforesaid monasteries and all the churches situated in the county of Rimini, with their appurtenances. We also confirm to the same Church of Rimini the Gate of Saint Donatus, called that of Saint Andrew; the entire half of the Gallic Gate, called Saint Peter; the whole portico by which one goes to the sea; and the portico by which entry is made to the episcopal palace; the entire half of the shore of the sea, together with half of its jurisdiction belonging to the banks of the shore, whether over Jews or Christians; and also the seashore extending from the streamlet to the river called Maricula. [Col. 0886C]

Moreover, following in the footsteps of our predecessors, as it has been established by them, so we likewise establish henceforth to remain forever: the Church of Rimini shall be subject to no other metropolis except the holy and apostolic Roman Church alone, and its bishop shall at all times be consecrated only by the Roman pontiff. For the aforesaid properties belonging by right to the Holy Roman Church, which the Church of Rimini possesses, you and your successors shall pay annually to the Lateran Palace thirty denarii as a pension. We entrust to you and to your successors, and confirm by the page of the present writing, the parish church of Saint Paternianus with its tithes and other appurtenances, together with those things belonging by right to blessed Peter on the estate of Arginaria, subject to an annual payment to us and our successors of twenty-four Lucchese denarii. [Col. 0886D]

We therefore decree, etc.; if anyone therefore, etc.; but upon all, etc.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church.  
I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina.  
I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum.  
I, Peter, bishop of Albano.  
I, Raynerius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca.  
I, Thomas, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Baron, subdeacon of the Holy Roman Church, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of June [21 May], in the seventh indiction, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius II.

### XLVII. To G., Count of Nevers—That he restore what he took from Vézelay. (1144, 22 May)

*[MANSI, Councils, XXI, 614.]*

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ G., count of Nevers, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It belongs to your nobility to love and protect venerable places together with the persons devoted in them to divine service, and to preserve their just rights. Therefore, by apostolic letters we command your nobility, and enjoin this upon you for the remission of your sins, [Col. 0887B] that you restore to the aforesaid place the ancient road which you are said to have taken away from Vézelay and diverted elsewhere.

Given on the ninth day before the Kalends of June [24 May].

### XLVIII. He confirms to the monastery of Cluny the manor of Lecdecumba. (1144, 22 May)

*[Bullarium Cluniacense, 52.]*

[Col. 0887C]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son PETER, abbot of Cluny, and to his brethren now present and to be regularly appointed in the future, forever.

Since without the worship of true religion neither the unity of charity can endure nor service pleasing to God be rendered, it befits apostolic authority to love religious persons and to foster with the protection of the Apostolic See religious places—especially those which belong by right to blessed Peter and pertain in a special manner to the Roman Church—and to preserve their rights unimpaired. Therefore, beloved sons, adhering to the footsteps of Pope Innocent, our predecessor of happy memory, we grant favourable assent to your just petitions and, by apostolic authority, confirm to you and through you to the monastery of Cluny the manor of Lecdecumba, as it was granted to you from his own domain, out of devotion, by the illustrious man Stephen, king of the English, with the customs and liberties pertaining to it and all its appurtenances, and confirmed by his charter, in exchange for the one hundred marks of silver which Henry, king of the English of good memory, Stephen’s predecessor, had granted you annually from his treasury. [Col. 0887D] We strengthen this confirmation by the page of the present writing.

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing this page of our confirmation, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second and third time, does not make suitable amends by satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour, and know himself or herself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let that person be cut off from the most holy body and blood of God and of our Lord, our Redeemer Jesus Christ, and be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance. But upon those who observe it may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church.  
I, Theodewinus, bishop of Saint Rufina.  
I, Rainerius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca.  
I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum.  
[Col. 0888B] I, Thomas, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina.  
I, Peter, bishop of Albano.

[Col. 0888C] I, Rodulphus, cardinal deacon of Saint Lucy in Septa Solis.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Baron, subdeacon of the Holy Roman Church, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of June [22 May], in the seventh indiction, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius II.

### XLIX. To Peter, Abbot of Cluny—Privilege of Cluny. (1144, 22 May)

*[MANSI, Councils, XXI, 610.]*

[Col. 0888D]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his dearest son in Christ PETER, abbot of Cluny, and to his successors regularly appointed, forever.

The monastery of Cluny, of blessed Peter—a mirror of monastic religion in modern times and, in the regions of Gaul, an example—was offered into the proper jurisdiction of the Apostolic See from the very beginning of its foundation. Accordingly, our fathers of holy memory—John XI; likewise John XIX; Agapetus II; Benedict VI; likewise Benedict VII; Leo VII and IX; Gregory VI and VII; Alexander II; Stephen; Victor [Col. 0889A] III; Urban II; Paschal II; Gelasius II; Calixtus II; and Honorius II, pontiffs of the Roman Church—endowed that place with the prerogative of singular affection and liberty, and fortified everything belonging to it by the enactments of their privileges.

For it was established that all churches, cemeteries, monks, clerics, and all laypeople dwelling within the boundaries—which run from the stream of Salnay, etc.—should remain under the jurisdiction and protection of the Apostolic See alone. Nor are the priests or parishioners of the place of Cluny itself to be compelled to attend the synod or assembly of anyone except the Roman pontiff and the abbot of Cluny.

For the ordination of the abbot, monks, or clerics dwelling within the aforesaid boundaries; for the preparation of chrism; and for the consecration of holy oil, churches, altars, and cemeteries, the monastery of Cluny may summon whichever bishop it prefers. No person whatsoever, apart from the Roman pontiff and a legate sent for this purpose, may excommunicate or place under interdict Cluniac monks dwelling anywhere. [Col. 0889B]

We confirm by the page of the present decree the boundaries of the immunity of your place established by our aforesaid predecessor Pope Urban: namely, that no person, of whatever condition or power, may presume within the limits of those boundaries to make an invasion, seize plunder, commit robbery, or perpetrate homicide. Thus, the boundaries of the sacred ban are these, etc.

In the abbeys that, together with their abbots, have been given to the governance of the monastery of Cluny—namely Saint Martial, etc.—no abbot whatsoever shall be elected without the counsel of the abbot of Cluny. Furthermore, we add that in all priories and cells now subject to your governance without their own abbot, no one shall ever presume in future times to appoint an abbot. Rather, both those priories and cells, and all other possessions in whatever places, with which the Church of Cluny was invested at the time of the Council of Auvergne celebrated by the aforesaid Pope Urban, and concerning which no dispute was then raised, shall always be preserved in peace and quiet both to you and to your successors. [Col. 0889C]

No bishop shall have authority to impose any burden upon you or to cause you trouble concerning your altars, churches, or tithes; rather, as you have possessed some of these in part and some in their entirety by their permission, so you shall possess them in the future. You may lawfully possess, for your own governance and that of the poor, the tithes of your churches which are held by laypeople, if reverence for religion can, according to God, withdraw them from their power.

You shall henceforth possess more peacefully, without any opposition from bishops or episcopal officials, the tithes of your labour—concerning which bishops have been accustomed to trouble both you and other men of the monastic profession—namely those of the lands called *dominicaturae*, cultivated at your expense by the dependants of your monasteries and cells, and which you distribute among your pilgrims, brethren, and poor. [Col. 0889D]

All churches situated anywhere, your chapels, and cemeteries shall be free and exempt from every exaction, except the customary *parata* due to the bishop and his jurisdiction over priests who have offended against the dignity of their order. You and your brethren may also choose priests for your churches, provided that they receive the care of souls from bishops or their vicars without payment. If, God forbid, they refuse through perversity to confer it, then the priests shall obtain from the benevolence of the Apostolic See permission to celebrate the offices. If diocesan bishops refuse freely to perform consecrations of churches or altars, you may receive them from any Catholic bishop.

Nor shall brethren of your cells wherever situated suffer suspension of divine offices on account of any interdict or excommunication. Rather, both the monks themselves and their servants, and those who have devoted themselves to the monastic profession, shall celebrate the offices of divine worship and perform the duties of burial with the doors of the churches closed and diocesan officials not admitted. [Col. 0890B]

Furthermore, whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, God being favourable, acquire by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these, we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: in Burgundy, the church, etc.

We forbid anyone to presume, within the parishes belonging by right to the monastery of Cluny, to build a church or chapel without the assent of the abbot of Cluny, saving in all things the authority of the Apostolic See. Therefore we decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but let all things be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing this page of our grant, etc. [Col. 0890C]

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.  
I, Theodewinus, bishop of Saint Rufina, have subscribed.  
I, Rainerius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca, have subscribed.  
[Col. 0890D] I, Thomas, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina, have subscribed.  
I, Gillebertus, of the title of Saint Mary, have subscribed.  
I, Maurus, bishop of Tusculum, have subscribed.  
I, Peter, bishop of Albano, have subscribed.  
I, Rainerius, priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill, have subscribed.  
I, Manfredus, cardinal priest of Saint Sabina, have subscribed.  
I, Aubertus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia, have subscribed.  
I, Hugo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed.  
[Col. 0891A] I, Octavianus, cardinal deacon, have subscribed.  
I, Guido, unworthy minister of the altar in the Roman Church, have subscribed.  
I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Angel, have subscribed.  
I, Astaldus, cardinal deacon of Saint Eustachius beside the temple of Agapitus [probably an OCR or textual variant for Agrippa], have subscribed.  
I, John, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary New, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Baron, subdeacon of the Church, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of June [22 May], in the seventh indiction, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius.

### L. To the Bishops of Gaul—He forbids churches or chapels to be built in parishes belonging to the monastery of Cluny. (1144, 22 May)

*[Dom BOUQUET, Collection, XV, 413.]*

[Col. 0891B]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to all venerable brethren, bishops established throughout Gaul, greeting and apostolic blessing.

According to canonical enactment, bishops must ensure in every way that older churches do not lose their rights or tithes on account of new ones, but that dues are always paid to the older churches. Therefore, since it is fitting that we provide for the needs of the religious brethren of Cluny, we command you by apostolic letters that, in parishes belonging to the monastery of Cluny, no one may presume to build a church or chapel without the consent [Col. 0891C] of the abbot of Cluny, saving in all things the authority of the Apostolic See.

Given . . . . . on the eleventh day before the Kalends of June [22 May].

### LI. Privilege for the Monastery of Saint Bertin at Sithiu. (1144, 26 May)

*[Collection of Cartularies, III, 319.]*

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons LEO, abbot of Saint Bertin, and his brethren now present and to be regularly appointed in the future, forever.

We acknowledge that, by the Lord’s ordering, we have been promoted to the service of the Apostolic See for this purpose: that we ought effectively to assist its children when they seek aid, and, insofar as the Lord grants, to defend and protect those obedient to it. Hence we ought to extend the hand of protection to venerable places and to provide more diligently for the peace of God’s servants. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the monastery of Saint Bertin, in which you are devoted to divine service; and we strengthen it by the privilege of the present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God being favourable, acquire, shall remain secure [Col. 0892A] and unimpaired to you and your successors.

Among these, we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: in the diocese of Arras, the altar-rights of Anesin, Werkin, and Barli; in the diocese of Tournai, the altar-right of Runbeke, free from the *personatus* [parochial incumbency], while preserving episcopal revenues; in the diocese of Thérouanne, the altar-right of Vuiserna with the same village, the tithe in the church of Saint Martin, the tithe at Longuenesse, the tithe at Saint Michael, and the tithe at Tilleke.

Therefore we decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but let all things be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the canonical justice of the diocesan bishop and the authority of the Apostolic See. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, etc., to the end as above in the other privileges. [Col. 0892B]

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Baron, subdeacon of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Kalends of June [26 May], in the seventh indiction, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius II.

Around the circumference of the seal is written: **“Show us, O Lord, [Col. 0892C] your mercy.”**

### LII. To Alvisus, Bishop of Arras. (1144, 29 May)

*[BALUZE, Miscellanies, Luc. ed., II, 167.]*

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother ALVISUS, bishop of Arras, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The bearer of this letter, as we have learned, is a young man of good repute and trained in literary learning, and he can serve the Church of Arras honorably. Therefore, since he has for some time conducted himself well with our venerable brother Imar, bishop of Tusculum, by these present letters we command your charity, requesting that, for reverence toward blessed Peter and ourselves, you grant him a prebend in that same Church. [Col. 0892D]

Given at the Lateran, 29 May.

LIII. Privilege for the monastery of Faremoutiers. (Year 1144, 30 May.)

[PETIT, *The Penitential of Theodore*, II, p. 676.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ RISSENDA, abbess of the monastery of Faremoutiers, and her sisters, present and future, for ever.

Whenever that is requested of us which is recognized as fitting religion and propriety, it is right that we grant it with a willing spirit and afford suitable assistance to the desires of those making the request. Therefore, beloved daughters in the Lord, moved by the prayers of our venerable brother Alberic, bishop of Ostia, we graciously assent to your just petitions. We receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing; decreeing that whatsoever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, God being favorable, acquire through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or by other means, shall remain firm and inviolate to you and your successors.

Moreover, the agreement reasonably made between you and our venerable brother, the bishop of Meaux, by our venerable brothers Geoffrey, bishop of Châlons, and Hugh, bishop of Auxerre, at the command of our predecessor of happy memory, Pope Innocent, and confirmed by that same predecessor, we confirm by this present writing and decree that it be observed by both parties. [Col. 0893A–B]

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, seize its possessions, retain those seized, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things be preserved whole, to be of every benefit for the uses of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the canonical right of the diocesan bishop and the authority of the Apostolic See. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should not make amendment by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of his or her power and honor; let him or her know that he or she stands guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him or her be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let him or her be subject to strict vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve what is right for the same place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen. [Col. 0893C]

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. [Col. 0893D] I, Theodewin, bishop of Santa Rufina, have subscribed. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Incarus, bishop of Tusculum, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Calixtus, have subscribed. I, Thomas, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina, have subscribed. I, Gilbert, cardinal priest of the title of St. Mark, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Lawrence and Damasus, have subscribed. I, Bb., cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Guiso, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal deacon of St. Adrian, have subscribed. I, Radulf, cardinal deacon of St. Lucy in the Septizonium, have subscribed.

[Col. 0894A] Given at the Lateran through the hand of Baro, subdeacon of the holy Roman Church, 30 May, in the seventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1144, in the first year of the pontificate of the lord Pope Lucius II.

LIV. He undertakes the protection of the church of St. Peter at Faenza and confirms the possessions and privileges of its canons, at the request of Alberic, bishop of Ostia. (Year 1144, 1 June.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, II, 495.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons FAROLF, archdeacon of the Church of Faenza, PETER, archpriest, and their brethren, present and future, to be appointed in their place in the same Church, for ever.

By the Lord’s gift we have been raised to the watchtower of apostolic dignity so that, with fatherly solicitude, we may provide for the welfare and peace of the Churches and preserve for each its own right, confirmed and inviolate. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, graciously assenting to your just petitions, we receive the church of blessed Peter, in which you are devoted to divine service, under the protection of the same Prince of the Apostles and of ourselves, and fortify it by the protection of this present writing.

We decree that whatsoever possessions and goods the aforesaid Church now possesses by whatever right, or may hereafter, by the Lord’s favor, acquire through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other reasonable means, shall remain firm and inviolate to you and your successors. Among these we have judged the following to be expressly named: the parish church of St. Peter in Lacuna, with all appurtenances belonging to it; half of the parish church of St. Andrew in Panigale, with all its appurtenances; the church of St. Christopher the martyr; the so-called castle of Quartulli; the church of St. Andrew in Casanaula; and the church of St. Mary in Morlascho. [Col. 0894B–C]

Further, Greater and Lesser Arcuatum; Greater and Lesser Fermilinum with their appurtenances, namely Fabriati, Morena with the great field adjoining it, and Taulis of Villanova; two manses in Licutino; four in Pegalino; two in Amerino; the place called Gargugnanus; the place called Curiglianus; the place called Mons; the place called Tillitus; two manses in Varano; whatever you possess in Fustarini, Pigna, Pitriolo, and in whatsoever places, villages, or estates, lands or waters, or watercourses.

We also confirm to you and your successors for ever the ancient customs, honors, and dignities of your Church in tithes, first-fruits, wills, offerings of both living and dead persons, the anciently customary rights of the parish churches of your bishopric, processions and pensions, and all payments, prebends, or revenues, just as you or your predecessors, by the ancient usage of your Church, had, held, and possessed them from the death of Paul of good memory, venerable bishop of that Church, until the time of his successor James. [Col. 0894D–0895A]

Moreover, by the authority of the Apostolic See, we confirm for ever to your Church and its priests alone the oil for the sick and their anointings from your whole parish. We command, under threat of deprivation of their office and excommunication, that no chaplain retain these for himself or perform such an office without the permission of the mother church. We further command that an archdeacon and an archpriest shall always be maintained in your Church according to canonical constitution. Whatever is granted to them by the authority of the sacred canons, we confirm by the authority of this present privilege.

We also decree that the charitable food-gifts which you have customarily received annually from the monasteries of St. Mary Outside the Gate and St. Hippolytus, and from your bishop at the Nativity and Resurrection of the Lord—whether you have made the customary processions at the said monasteries or have omitted them through an excusable hindrance—shall remain valid and inviolate for you and your successors. [Col. 0895A–B]

We further decree that this shall remain valid and unshaken for your Church for all time: in all ecclesiastical affairs or contracts known to pertain to the diocese of the bishopric of Faenza, no one whatsoever shall have authority to establish or reform, judge, or dispose of anything without the counsel and consent of you and your successors.

We also grant that burial in that Church shall be wholly free; and no one may presume, without your permission, to receive the bodies of those who have chosen to be buried there, or of those known to belong to your cemetery through the customary burial-place of their family or kinship, unless perhaps while still living they have adopted some religious profession. Whoever rashly presumes to receive or bury them, whether cleric or layperson, shall be subject to ecclesiastical punishment until making fitting satisfaction. [Col. 0895B–C]

In addition, we decree that no new church or oratory shall be built or consecrated within the boundaries of the bishopric of Faenza without the assent of you or your successors. If any are built or consecrated otherwise, you shall, by apostolic authority, prohibit the celebration of divine offices in them. Likewise, by apostolic authority, we forbid anyone of your bishopric whom you have canonically placed under interdict or excommunicated to presume, on the pretext of any privilege or authority, to resist or contradict you; rather, let him obey your command without contradiction. Under a general interdict of your city, no church placed under interdict may openly celebrate divine office.

Nor may any archbishop or bishop despoil a cleric of the mother church of office or benefice without canonical judgment. We have also judged it proper to add to this decree that you and your successors shall enjoy complete immunity from every tributary exaction, whether ecclesiastical or secular, communal or private. Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever, etc. If anyone therefore, etc. But upon all, etc. Amen. [Col. 0895C–0896A]

Given at the Lateran, 1 June, in the first year.

LIV bis. He confirms the privileges of the monastery of Tournus. (Year 1144, 7 June.)

[JUENIN, *History of the Royal Abbey of Tournus*, Proofs, p. 147.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ PETER, abbot of Tournus, and to his successors to be regularly appointed, for ever.

It is fitting for us to grant assent to just vows and lend our ears to just petitions, since, although unworthy heralds of justice, we are, by the Lord’s ordering, set in the exalted watchtower of the apostles Peter and Paul. Therefore, graciously assenting to your petitions, we extend to the monastery of Tournus, over which, by God’s authorship, you preside, the protection of the Apostolic See, following the example of our predecessors of happy memory, Paschal, Calixtus, and Innocent II, Roman pontiffs. By this page of our present decree we confirm to you and your successors those places which the industry either of your predecessors or of your own zeal has reasonably acquired or lawfully recovered, or which have been granted to that monastery through the liberality of ancient princes or bishops.

Namely, in the diocese of Clermont: the monastery of St. Pourçain, with the churches of Besson, Quintiniacum, Polines, Celsiacum, Travallium, Fellinia, Mont-Aureux, Sustris, Charel, Liriniacum, Martiliacum, Monfanc, Boiacum, Barbariacum, Vernei, Villena, Lupiacum, Paredo, Brialis, Varinnas, Voroz, and St. Lupus; the churches of Bésiacum, Nuilliacum, Capelz, Branciacum, and Floriacum, with the chapel of Cavarocca; the church of Salviliis and that of Libiacum; the church of St. Nicholas and the church of Vernolium. [Col. 0896B–C]

In the diocese of Chalon: Pristiacum, Aguliacum, the church of Baldreas, the church of St. Andrew, Lambras, Manciacum; the church in the village of Ginniacum, and that of Ver; the church of St. Martin of Griviliacum, and that of Cusiriacum.

In the diocese of Lyons: the church of St. Andrew of Baljiacum, Vasliacum, Brienna, Juvenciacum; the church of St. James of Grassiacum, and that of St. Benignus; the church of Cabrosium; the church of Cavannis; Bisiacum; the church of St. Mary of Soliniacum; St. Martin of Butella; the church of St. Andrew, commonly called Pannos; the church of Mont Raculf; the church of Sasiriacum; the church of Peroniacum; the chapel of Château Corgenon; the church of St. Lydius, commonly called Olives; Lovincum; and Silviniacum. [Col. 0896C–D]

In the diocese of Mâcon: Ulchistriacum, Villare, Plotas, Belniacum, the church of Li. Douziacum, the cell of St. Romanus, St. Maurice, St. Symphorian, St. Mary of Chapelle-Reverias, and St. Peter of Romaniscas; the church of Aziacum and that of Fisiacum; St. Julian of Lonciacum; and St. Vitalis of Lenna.

In the diocese of Bourges: the church of Saciacum.

In the diocese of Autun: the church of Pariniacum with its chapel; the church of Petraficta, with the chapel of St. Justus.

In the diocese of Nantes: the monastery of St. Philibert; the church of St. Vitalis of Raas; the church of Machicol; St. Martin of Paciacum; St. Liucinius; the church of Limoziveria; St. Columbarius; the churches of Corcoiacum; the churches of Mores Mansiones, Legiacum, and Tolvei; and the churches of Monasteriis. [Col. 0896D–0897A]

In the diocese of Poitiers: the island of Herum; the churches of Bellovidere with its cemetery; the cell of St. Mary of Laudun; the church of St. Nicholas; St. Peter; the churches of Basilicis and Holy Cross; the churches of Berniziacum and Aziacum; Maciacum; Taziacum; the church of Madernas; the churches of Bernazai, Mount St. Leodegarius, and Estivalibus.

In the diocese of Tours: Pontiacum, Verniolum, Corcoriacum.

In the diocese of Angers: the cell of Cunaldus with its appurtenances; the churches of Doadicastrum, St. Denis, St. Peter, St. John, and St. Leodegarius; the church of St. Lawrence; the village of Landrum; Terenciacum; the churches of Varinas; and St. Mary of Tanays with its chapel.

In the diocese of Geneva: the church of Perois.

In the diocese of Le Puy: the monastery of St. Philibert; the church of St. Peter of Salitas; St. Felix of Laudons; St. Mary of Pratalias; St. Martin of Cocornensis; the chapel of St. Philibert; St. Cyricus; St. Maurice of Amblavensis; St. Vincent; the chapel in Château Syroi; St. Mary of Basac; the chapel of Château Rocos; St. Julian of Caspiniacum; the chapel of Château Mercolio; and the church of St. Quintin. [Col. 0897A–B]

In the diocese of Die: the church of Château Grainan; St. Vincent; St. Romanus; and the church of Torrites.

In the diocese of Tricastin: the church of Vallis Nympharum; St. Martin; St. Mary; St. Peter; St. Romanus; the chapel of St. Michael of Gaba; the church of Eleemosyna; and St. Mary of Grainan.

In the diocese of Orange: the church of Dosera; St. Mary; St. Benedict; St. Christopher; and St. Saturninus.

In the diocese of Vaison: the church of St. Germanus; St. Peter of Falco; and St. Mary of Purpureae.

In the diocese of Vienne: the cell of St. Agnes of Mota; St. Martin of Aziacum with its cemetery; St. Veranus of Rivas; the church of Fai; St. John of Château Miron; the church of Villanova; the chapel of St. Michael of Albon; the church of St. Saturninus with its parish; the cell of St. Philibert of Minniacum; the church of St. Romanus; St. Andrew; and the church of St. Ferreolus.

In the diocese of Besançon: St. Cornelius, St. Desiderius, and the church of Azzon. [Col. 0897B–C]

Whatever else you may hereafter, by God’s gift, justly acquire shall remain firm and inviolate to you and your successors. Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb that monastery, seize its possessions, retain those seized, diminish them, or harass them with rash vexations; but that all things be preserved whole, to be of every benefit for the uses of those for whose governance and support they were granted.

Furthermore, we add that the same place, in which rest the bodies of blessed Valerian the martyr and St. Philibert the confessor, shall be preserved for ever free from every yoke of secular power. Nor may a bishop of any diocese disturb that place on the pretext of excommunication, absolution, or any other act of administration, or impose crosses or any new exactions upon the borough or the other possessions of the monastery. [Col. 0897C–0898A]

We forbid public masses to be celebrated in the same monastery, or a station to be held there by a bishop, apart from the will of the abbot and brethren. We also confirm all else that has been confirmed by the privileges of John of reverend memory and of the aforesaid Roman pontiffs. Further, out of reverence for blessed Mary ever Virgin, by whose name your place is distinguished, we permit the abbot or brethren, at the Annunciation of our Lord and Savior, to pronounce the Angelic Hymn during the solemnities of the Mass.

Upon the death of you, now abbot of the same place, or of any of your successors, no one may be set over it through any trickery or violence of intrusion, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall elect according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict, to be consecrated by the bishop of the Apostolic See or his legate because of the difficulty of travel. [Col. 0898A–B]

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should not make amendment by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of his or her power and honor; let him or her know that he or she stands guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him or her be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let him or her be subject to strict vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve what is right for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen. [Col. 0898B–C]

In the monogram:

SHOW US, O LORD, YOUR MERCY.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Peter, bishop of Albano. I, Thomas, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Lawrence and Damasus. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Portico. I, John, cardinal deacon of St. Mary the New.

Given at Ceprano through the hand of Baro, subdeacon of the holy Roman [Col. 0898D] Church, 7 June, in the seventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1144, in the first year of the pontificate of the lord Pope Lucius II.

LV. He commands Gregory, bishop of Bergamo, to compel the priests of his bishopric to render fealty to the churches of St. Vincent and St. Alexander. (Year 1144, 16 June.)

[LUPI, *Diplomatic Codex of Bergamo*, II, 1053.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother G[REGORY], bishop of Bergamo, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We believe that your brotherhood knows what was established by our predecessor Pope Innocent, of good memory, concerning the fealties to be rendered by the priests of your bishopric to the churches of St. Vincent and St. Alexander, and afterward confirmed by us. Therefore, by these present letters we command you strictly to admonish those priests ordained after that constitution to render fealty to both churches. If any prove resistant, restrain them by canonical censure. [Col. 0899A]

Given at Ceprano, 16 June.

LVI. To the bishops of Arras and Cambrai—That they are to hear a matrimonial case and lift the excommunication incurred on that account. (Year 1144, 16 June.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 618.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers ALVISUS, bishop of Arras, and NICHOLAS, bishop of Cambrai, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The nobleman Ebrard of Britolio, returning from Jerusalem by way of us, informed us that he had presumed to unite himself with a certain kinswoman of his, namely the daughter of Thomas of Marna, contrary to the prohibition of the bishop and Church of Beauvais; because of this presumption he himself was bound by the same bishop with the bond of excommunication, and his land was placed under interdict as regards divine offices. At length, however, he left her and, as he asserts, contracted a lawful marriage with another woman.

When he was journeying toward Jerusalem, he was ready, in the presence both of our predecessor of happy memory and of ourselves, to produce witnesses in support of this assertion. But our predecessor refused to receive them in the absence of the other party, and committed the case itself to your discretion for investigation and decision. Following in his footsteps, we command you by apostolic letters that within forty days after receiving the present writing you summon both him and the same woman, namely Thomas’s daughter, before you, and investigate the case carefully on both sides. [Col. 0899B–C]

If consanguinity between them is proved by suitable witnesses, and it is established that he married her contrary to the prohibition of the bishop and Church of Beauvais, and that on this account his land was placed under interdict and he was excommunicated, absolve him entirely from the complaint of that same woman, and do not in future impede, on that account, the marriage which he contracted with the other woman. But if either of you cannot be present because some necessity arises, the other, associating with himself prudent and wise men, shall nevertheless hear the case and decide it in the manner stated above. [Col. 0899C–D]

Given 16 June.

LVII. To the bishops of Arras and Thérouanne—That they are to ensure reparation for losses inflicted on Walter of Verdon while he was travelling to Jerusalem. (Year 1144, 17 June.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 617.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers ALVISUS, bishop of Arras, and MILO, bishop of Thérouanne, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The nobleman Walter of Verdon, returning from Jerusalem by way of us, complained that, after he had undertaken the journey to Jerusalem, your parishioners plundered his land and inflicted very great losses upon him. Therefore, since the possessions and goods of those who travel to Jerusalem out of devotion stand under the protection of the holy Church of God, we command you by apostolic letters diligently to admonish those of your parishioners concerning whom he complained to us, that they restore in full the losses subsequently inflicted upon him. If they prove contemptuous, restrain them by canonical censure. [Col. 0900A–B]

Given at Ceprano, 17 June.

LVIII. Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary of Fontevivo. (Year 1144, 28 June.)

[AFFO, *History of Parma*, II, p. 357.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons VIVIAN, abbot of Fontevivo, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, for ever.

It accords with the mercy of apostolic governance to love religious persons and fortify their places with pious protection. For it is recognized as worthy and consistent with propriety that we who have been appointed to the governance of Churches should both protect them from the malice of evil men and foster them by the patronage of the Apostolic See. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, graciously assenting to your just petitions, we receive the monastery of blessed Mary, Mother of God and ever Virgin, of Fontevivo, situated in the diocese of Parma, in which you are devoted to divine service, under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing.

We decree that whatsoever possessions and goods the same place now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, God being favorable, acquire through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and inviolate to you and your successors. Among these, the following have seemed proper to name expressly: by the gift of our venerable brother Lanfranc, bishop of Parma, the church of St. Mary of Fontevivo with all its appurtenances, together with the tithes of the same place, granted to you by the aforesaid bishop out of devotion and with the consent of his canons; and the lands and possessions justly conferred upon your monastery by laypersons. [Col. 0900B–D]

Since, moreover, you live a common life and should be supported by the alms and beneficence of others, we decree that no one may dare demand tithes from you on the produce which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or on the sustenance of your animals. We forbid, as was established through the reasonable provision of our venerable aforesaid brother, the bishop of Parma, that from the river Taro to the stream Batibovis, and from the road of the stream Scamnus to the boundary of Cornalet and Maressius, any new church be built or any secular dwelling whatever be erected. [Col. 0900D–0901A]

Therefore no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, seize its possessions, retain those seized, diminish them, or harass it generally or by any molestations; but that all things be preserved whole, to be of every benefit for the uses of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See. If indeed any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should not make amendment by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of his or her power and honor; let him or her know that he or she stands guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him or her be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let him or her be subject to strict vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen. [Col. 0901A–B]

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Rainerius, cardinal priest of the title of St. Prisca, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. [Col. 0901C] I, Thomas, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina, have subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of St. Matthias in Portico, have subscribed. I, Hugh, cardinal priest of the title of St. Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed. I, Aribert, cardinal priest of the title of St. Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of St. Marcellus, have subscribed. I, Ubald, cardinal priest of Holy Cross, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Baro, subdeacon of the holy Roman Church, 28 June, in the seventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1144, in the first year of the pontificate of the lord Pope Lucius II.

LIX. To the clergy and people of Ravenna. (Year 1144, 6 July.)

[RUBEI, *History of Ravenna*, p. 329.]

[Col. 0901D]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the clergy and people of Ravenna, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We wish it to be known to all of you that we have graciously received our venerable brother M., canonically and unanimously elected by you; and, invoking the grace of the Holy Spirit, we have consecrated him as your archbishop with our own hands, as though with the hands of blessed Peter. Sending him back to his own see with the favor of the Apostolic See and under the protection of our letters, we command you by apostolic writings to receive him kindly, love and honor him with special affection, and humbly render to him obedience and reverence as to your own pastor and bishop of your souls.

Moreover, in recovering the possessions and goods of the Church of Ravenna, your mother, and retaining those which it possesses, give him aid and counsel as good sons. For our part, because of his learning and uprightness, we desire to love and honor him, and the Church of Ravenna as a special daughter of the Apostolic See, according to God, and to preserve its rights for it. Hence we command our venerable brother A., bishop of Piacenza, by apostolic letters, that according to the tenor of the privileges of the Church of Ravenna and ancient custom, he render due obedience and reverence to that bishop and to the Church of Ravenna. [Col. 0902A]

Given at the Lateran, 6 July.

LX. He summons Henry, bishop of Olomouc, to Rome concerning certain ecclesiastical affairs. (Year 1144, 10 July.)

[BOCZEK, *Diplomatic Codex of Moravia*, I, 320.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, bishop of Olomouc, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have received the letters of your brotherhood with due kindness, and we are grateful that, from reading them, we understand that you rejoice at our elevation, although that elevation and dignity of office bring us no rest or tranquility of mind, but at times increase for us cares and anxieties, labors also and tribulations. We loved your person with sincere affection before this office, and now we desire to love you more affectionately and to honor you in those matters in which, according to God, we can do so.

It is therefore incumbent upon you so praiseworthily to exercise yourself in matters belonging to your office and diligently to attend to the honor and exaltation of your mother, the holy Roman Church, that God may thereby be honored and that the same Roman Church may rejoice in your devotion. Furthermore, because in certain ecclesiastical affairs we need the counsel of your discretion, we command you by these present letters to present yourself to us as soon as possible. [Col. 0902B–D]

Given at the Lateran, 10 July.

LXI. To Otto, bishop of Lucca, and G., cardinal deacon. (Year 1144, 10 July.)

[BALUZE, *Miscellanies*, Lucan edition, IV, 593.]

Lucius, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers O., bishop of Lucca, and G., cardinal deacon of the holy Roman Church, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The prior of St. Angelo in Folo, appearing before us, excused himself merely by word of mouth, saying that he had inflicted no injury upon our brethren of St. Fridianus concerning the church of St. Savior. But since we were hindered by many and diverse affairs and could not apply attentive diligence to the case itself, we commanded him orally, under obedience, that he and his brethren should observe without challenge what our predecessors of good memory, Innocent and Celestine, had commanded concerning this matter, and what he himself had confirmed by oath in the hand of our beloved son G., cardinal priest of Saints Lawrence and Damasus, inviolably.

By this letter of apostolic blessing, however, we command you to regard as excommunicated those who threw stones at that same church of St. Savior or made an assault upon it, until they have made satisfaction for so great a sacrilege. But if the aforesaid prior, his brethren, or parishioners should presume to harass the brethren of St. Fridianus concerning that same church of St. Savior, we forbid the celebration of divine offices in the church of St. Angelo itself. [Col. 0903A–B]

Given at the Lateran, 10 July.

LXII. He again summons Henry, bishop of Olomouc, to Rome. (Year 1144, 20 August.)

[BOCZEK, *Diplomatic Codex of Moravia*, I, 231.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, bishop of Olomouc, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have received with due kindness the letters of your brotherhood and have carefully considered what they contained. Therefore, as we commanded you in other letters, we command you again to present yourself to us as soon as you can. Then, once the truth has been more fully learned through you, both concerning the matters which you reported to us and others about which we wish to speak with you, we shall, with the Lord as author, determine what is to be determined. [Col. 0903B–C]

Given at Rome, 20 August.

LXIII. Privilege for the Church of the Holy Sepulchre at Jerusalem. (Year 1144, 14 September.)

[ROZIÈRE, *Cartulary of the Holy Sepulchre*, p. 33.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons in Christ PETER, prior, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life in the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, for ever.

If the meekness and liberality of the holy Roman Church ought to furnish fitting assistance to all Christians, it is still more fitting that these be bestowed more generously upon those who lead the religious life and seem to cling more closely to almighty God. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, since you have resolved to live according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine, and, worshipping in the place where the Lord’s feet stood, you serve under rule at his glorious tomb—in which he rested bodily for three days—and at the other most sacred places in which the Redeemer of the world endured for our salvation bonds, scourges, the disgrace of the cross, wounds, and death, we judge you worthy of greater goodwill and favor and wish to cherish you with paternal affection.

Accordingly, granting due and kindly assent to your petitions, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the most holy Church of the Holy Sepulchre, in which, devoted to divine service, you continually commemorate with the faith of eyewitnesses the Lord’s Passion and the triumph of the most victorious cross; and we strengthen it by the authority of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that church now canonically possesses, whatever has been justly bestowed upon that place by men of distinguished memory—namely Duke Godfrey, both Baldwins, and King Fulk, likewise Arnulf and the other patriarchs—or shall hereafter be reasonably bestowed by patriarchs or other faithful of God, shall remain secure and inviolate for you.

Among these we have thought fit to state expressly: namely, one half of all offerings made at the Lord’s Sepulchre; likewise the offerings of the Cross, except on the day of Holy Preparation alone [Good Friday], or if the patriarch has taken it with him for some necessity; the tithes of the city of Jerusalem and of adjacent places, excepting the tithes of the *funda*; and one half of the benefice given by the king in exchange for the bishopric of Bethlehem, as all these matters are set out in the charter of concession and confirmation of Arnulf, patriarch of blessed memory; likewise, by concession of that same patriarch, the church of St Peter at Jaffa, with the full integrity of its honor and dignity.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb that church, or to take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with reckless vexations; but that all things be preserved intact and applied in every way to the benefit of those for whose support and governance they were granted, saving the reverence and authority of the holy Roman Church and the patriarchal dignity. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second and third time, should fail to make suitable amends by satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity perpetrated; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord, the Redeemer Jesus Christ; and let him be subject to severe vengeance at the final judgment. But upon all who preserve what is right for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Theodwin, bishop of Santa Rufina, have subscribed. I, Peter, bishop of Albano, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Calixtus, have subscribed. [Col. 0905A] I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Lawrence and Damasus, have subscribed. I, Aribert, cardinal priest of the title of St Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of St Marcellus, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of St Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of St Angelo, have subscribed. I, Astaldus, cardinal deacon of St Eustace [Col. 0905B] beside the Temple of Agrippa, have subscribed. I, Berard, cardinal deacon of the holy Roman Church, have subscribed.

Given at Rome, through the hand of Baro, subdeacon of the holy Roman Church, on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of October [14 September], in the eighth indiction, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius II.

### LXIV. To Peter, Abbot of Cluny.—Concerning his illness and the truce concluded with the King of Sicily. (1144, 22 September.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 608.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son PETER, abbot of Cluny, greetings and apostolic [Col. 0905C] blessing.

We have received the letters of your love with due kindness, and we have gladly granted your requests, which seemed reasonable to us and to our brethren. Knowing that you are concerned about our condition, we wish you to know that almighty God has visited us by his grace: he has chastened us severely, but has not delivered us over to death. Through his mercy we are recovering, and we hope shortly to regain our former health. We agreed to meet with the King of Sicily; and, since we could not make a firm peace with him to the honor of God and his Church, nevertheless, compelled by the pressure of his violence, we concluded a truce with him.

Moreover, we are pleased that, as you indicated in your letters, you should send us thirteen of your brethren as soon as you can; for we shall, with the Lord’s help, take care to receive them honorably and establish them to the honor of God and of the Church of Cluny. May divine grace preserve your holy congregation as it prays for us, and absolve it from all sins.

Given at the Lateran, on the tenth day before the Kalends of October [22 September].

### LXV. He receives the monastery of St Mary of Évron under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges, at the request of Hugh, Archbishop of Tours. (1144, 4 November.)

[Institut des provinces de France, 2nd series, *Instrumenta*, vol. I, p. LXXIX. First cartulary of Évron.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 0906A] sons GEOFFREY, abbot of the monastery of Évron, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

It is fitting for us willingly to grant a desire shown to concern the religious purpose and the salvation of souls, and to furnish suitable support for the wishes of petitioners. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, inclined by the prayers of our venerable brother Hugh, Archbishop of Tours, your metropolitan, and likewise of the religious men Garnier, abbot, and the brethren of Marmoutier, we graciously assent to your just requests. We receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the Church of Évron of the Blessed Mother of God and ever-virgin Mary, in which you are dedicated to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document.

We decree that whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by God’s favor, through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and inviolate for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to state expressly: the church of St Martin situated in the borough of Évron, with all its appurtenances; the church of St Vigor of Nigeul; the church of St Martin of Mont-Sûr; the church of St George of Gesnes; the church of St Peter of Chaalon; the church of Bazouges of Mont-Pinson; the church of St Mary of Bédée; the church [Col. 0906C] of St Gervais of Champ-Genestoux; the church of St Nicholas of Trahant; the church of St Peter of Issé; the church of St Martin of Castris; the church of St Martin of Cures; the church of St Martin of Lunayo; the church of St Denis of Orques; and the church of St Susanna.

In the aforesaid churches, [we confirm] the customary dues called *circades*, and the episcopal share from synods, canonically granted to you by the bishops of Le Mans. The monastery itself with the adjoining borough; the church of St Martin of the Fields situated in that same borough; the church of St Peter of Tortiac; the church of St Leodegar of Viviers; the church of St Peter of Vultériac; the church of St Ceneratus; the church of Champ-Aion; the chapel [Col. 0906D] of Tilliac; the church of St Suppitius of Vegia; the church of St Leodegar; the church of St Sixtus of the Chapel; the church of St Gervais of Breiac; the church of St Paduinus of the Fields; the church of St Gemma; the church of St Martin of Araone; the church of St Fronto of Mézengiac; the church of St Christopher; the church of St Mary of Cambiac; the church of St Peter situated in that same village; the church of St Germanus of Hatevella; the chapel of St Audoin; the chapel of St Treicius; the chapel of St Gerald; the chapel of St Mary of Barben; the church of St Cyprian of Baconeria; the church of Andoliac; the church of Intramis; the church of Ruilliac; the church of Frumenteries; the church of St Martin of Agniculus; the church [Col. 0907A] of St Martin of the Wood; the church of St Symphorian of Martigniac; the chapel of St Martin of Cahors; the chapel of St Vigor of Mengniac; the church of the Two Avals; the church of St Audoin; the church of St Mary of the Chapel; the chapel of St Mary of Lynceium; the church of St Mary of Chimiriac (otherwise Chimeriac); the church of Moolay; the church of St Peter of Chama; and the church of St Stephen of Thorigniac. Your right in the church of Neuvillette; the tithes which you have in the parish of Parenay, in the parish of Amenay, in the parish of Tannay, in the parish of Courcité, in the parish of Parennis, in the parish of Cigné, and, in the parish of St John upon the Arve, the chapel of St Mary in Campo Divino.

[Col. 0907B] We have also ordained that the priests serving your parish churches, according to the decree concerning the care of the people issued by our predecessor Pope Urban of blessed memory, shall render account to the bishop for the care of the people, but shall show you the due subjection in temporal matters.

Furthermore, since new churches or chapels ought not to be constructed to the detriment of ancient churches, we forbid anyone to presume to build a new church or chapel within your parishes.

We entirely abolish that evil custom by which archdeacons or clerics, upon the installation of the abbot of your monastery, exact one hundred solidi from you; and, by apostolic authority, we forbid anyone henceforth to dare either to give or exact them. Upon the death of yourself, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it by any cunning of usurpation or violence; but it shall be lawful for you, by common counsel, or by the counsel of the sounder part, according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict, to elect an abbot without anyone’s contradiction.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all things be preserved intact and applied in every way to the benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the apostolic see and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make suitable amends by satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity perpetrated; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject to severe vengeance at the final judgment. But upon all who preserve what is right for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen.

[Col. 0908A] Given at the Lateran through the hand of Baro, subdeacon of the holy Roman Church, on the second Nones of November [4 November], in the seventh indiction, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius II.

### LXVI. Bull confirming the monastery of St Mary of Roggenburg. (1144, 7 November.)

[HUGO, *Annals of Prémontré*, II, 435.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son GERUNG, provost of Roggenburg, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

[Col. 0908B] It accords with the height of apostolic governance to love religious persons and to fortify their places with pious protection. For it is recognized as worthy and consonant with propriety that we, who have been raised to the governance of churches, should protect them from the wickedness of evil men and cherish them by the patronage of the apostolic see. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, inclined by the prayers of our venerable brethren Walter, bishop of Augsburg, and Conrad, bishop of Chur, we graciously assent to your just requests. We receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the Church at Roggenburg of the Blessed Mother of God and ever-virgin Mary and of St Augustine, in which you are dedicated to divine service, and strengthen it by the protection of this present document.

We decree that whatever possessions and goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter acquire, by God’s favor, through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and inviolate for you and your successors. We add also that the canonical order which is known to have been established in that place according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine and the institution of the Premonstratensians shall be maintained there forever. Nor may any brother, after making profession there, leave the cloister without the permission of his superior; and no bishop or abbot may dare to receive or retain one who has departed.

Moreover, no cleric or layman whatsoever shall presume to exact tithes from you on the produce which you gather by your own labor and at your own expense, or on the increase of your animals. Upon the death of yourself, the present provost of that place, no one shall be set over it by any cunning of usurpation or violence, except one whom the brethren, or the sounder part of the brethren, according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Augustine, shall provide to be elected.

It shall further be lawful for you, in the parish churches which you hold, to appoint priests from among your brethren or from others. If they are suitable, the bishops shall, with your consent, commit the care of the parish to them, so that such priests shall render account to the bishop for the care of the people, but shall show you due subjection in temporal matters. As a token that the same place has been offered to blessed Peter by our aforesaid brother Bishop Conrad and his brothers, namely Sigefrid and Berthold, and remains under his protection, it shall pay yearly to us and our successors one gold bezant.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all things be preserved intact and applied in every way to the benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the apostolic see and the canonical reverence due to the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make suitable amends by satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity perpetrated; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject to severe vengeance at the final judgment. But upon all who preserve that place’s rights may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal priest, have subscribed. [Col. 0909C] I, Theodoguido, bishop of Silva Candida, have subscribed. I, Guido, unworthy minister of the altar in the Roman Church, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Baro, subdeacon of the holy Roman Church, on the seventh Ides of November [7 November], in the seventh indiction, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Pope Lucius II.

### LXVII. He receives the monastery of Stavelot under his protection and confirms its privileges. (1144, 10 November.)

[MARTENE, *Amplified Collection*, II, 121.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 0909D] sons WIBALD, abbot of Stavelot, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity. “It accords with the clemency of apostolic governance to love religious persons and to fortify their places with pious protection,” etc., as in the privilege of Pope Celestine II, no. 21 of this volume, col. 785.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Theodwin, bishop of Santa Rufina. I, Peter, bishop of Albano. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Calixtus. I, Giselbert, cardinal priest of the title of St Mark. [Col. 0910A] I, Ubald, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross. I, Hugh, priest of the holy Roman Church, of the title of St Lawrence in Lucina. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of St Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Guido, unworthy minister of the altar in the Roman Church. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of St Mary in Portico. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of St Angelo. [Col. 0910B] I, John, cardinal deacon of St Mary the New. I, Gerard, cardinal deacon of the holy Roman Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Baro, subdeacon of the holy Roman Church, on the fourth Ides of November [10 November], in the eighth indiction, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius II.

### LXVIII. To St Bernard, Abbot of Clairvaux.—That he admonish the Count of Nevers not to exact anything unlawful from the men of Vézelay. (1144, 19 November.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 614.]

[Col. 0910C]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his dearest son in Christ BERNARD, abbot of Clairvaux, greetings and apostolic blessing.

We do not think your love is unaware that the monastery of Vézelay belongs by right to blessed Peter and pertains particularly to his ownership and protection. But now, as we have learned, Count G. of Nevers, contrary to justice and the authority of the apostolic see, violently demands of our beloved son Pons, abbot of that place, that in every complaint involving his own person and his men he answer in the count’s court. [Col. 0910D] Neither the abbot himself nor his predecessors is known to have done this hitherto.

Therefore, by these apostolic letters, we command you diligently to admonish the same count on our behalf that, out of reverence for blessed Peter, to whose right the monastery is recognized to belong, he desist from such exaction; or else, in the presence of our venerable brethren A., bishop of Ostia, and I., bishop of Tusculum, legates of the apostolic see, receive from the same abbot, in accordance with the tenor of the privileges of the apostolic see, whatever justice shall dictate. If he refuses to accept this, we cannot permit that monastery to be oppressed so unjustly; and, with the Lord’s help, we shall do what belongs to our office.

Given at the Lateran, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of December [19 November].

### LXIX. He confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of All Saints of Bari. (1144, 25 November.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, VII, 620.]

[Col. 0911A]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons NICHOLAS, abbot of the venerable monastery called All Saints, in the place of Cuti in the suburb of Bari, and his brethren, present and future, to be regularly appointed, in perpetuity.

It is fitting for us willingly to grant a desire shown to concern the religious purpose and the salvation of souls, and to furnish suitable support for the wishes of petitioners. Therefore, beloved [Col. 0911B] son in Christ Nicholas, abbot, whom by God’s grace we have blessed as abbot, we strengthen by the privilege of the apostolic see the monastery of All Saints over which, by the Lord’s authority, you preside, following the example of our predecessor Pope Calixtus of happy memory.

We likewise confirm by the page of this present document every provision for peace and liberty which Ursus and Elias, bishops of the Church of Bari of good memory, granted to that monastery, and which our lord predecessor Pope Paschal of holy memory confirmed: namely, that the place itself, with all things justly belonging to it, shall remain free from the lordship or oppression of any person; that no bishop of the Church of Bari, nor any other reckless person—God forbid!—shall dare to impose excommunication upon that monastery; and that no one shall inflict upon its persons or goods any injury or litigation in any manner contrary to justice.

Let him grant ordinations of clerics and consecrations of churches freely, setting aside wicked practice and every exaction. We entirely forbid public masses to be celebrated there by the bishop without the will of the abbot and brethren, lest any occasion for popular gatherings be given in the retreats of God’s servants. Upon the death of yourself, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it by any cunning of usurpation or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict, shall provide to be elected. If any more serious case should arise for him, he shall be free [Col. 0911D] to appeal to the hearing of the apostolic see.

Furthermore, whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by God’s favor, through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and inviolate for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to state expressly: the church of St Nicholas of Pazzar; the church of St Lawrence of Anto; the convent of girls of St Procopius of Sao; the church of the holy apostles Simon and Jude outside the walls; and the church of St Sebastian, with all their appurtenances.

[Col. 0912A] We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all things be preserved intact and applied in every way to the benefit of those for whose support and governance they were granted, saving in all respects the right and authority of the holy Roman Church. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it and, having been warned a second or third time, should ultimately fail to make suitable amends by satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity perpetrated; let him be cut off from the most sacred body of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, [Col. 0912B] our Redeemer; and let him be subject to severe vengeance at the judgment. But upon all who preserve what is right for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Theodwin, bishop of Silva Candida. I, Peter, bishop of Albano. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of St Mary in Portico. I, Guido, unworthy minister of the altar in the Roman Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Boso, subdeacon of the holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Kalends of December [25 November], [Col. 0912C] in the eighth indiction, in the year 1144 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius II.

### LXX. Bull for the abbey of St Apollinaris in Classe. (1144, 29 November.)

[*Annals of Camaldoli*, III, 411.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons HENRY, abbot of the monastery of St Apollinaris in Classe, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

The care of the universal Church has been entrusted to us by God, the provider of all good things, for this purpose: that we should love religious persons and strive by every means to spread religion pleasing to God. [Col. 0912D] For no apostolic service is ever pleasingly rendered to God unless, proceeding from the root of charity, it is preserved by purity of religion. Therefore all lovers of the Christian faith ought to cherish religion and diligently support venerable places along with the persons dedicated to divine service in them, so that they may not be troubled by any molestations of wicked men or wearied by importunate burdens.

Therefore, beloved son in the Lord Henry, abbot, we graciously assent to your just requests and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery, over which, by God’s authority, you are known to preside; and we strengthen it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same [Col. 0913A] monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by God’s favor, through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and inviolate for you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to state expressly: in the March, five cells, one of which is built in honor of St Mary, together with the castle founded there called Frasta, with chapels, villages, and all things pertaining to it; another in honor of St Martin, likewise with the castle subject to it, chapels, villages, and all things pertaining to it; a third in honor of St Apollinaris at Rotundo, with all things pertaining to it; a fourth in honor of St Vitus, with all things adjoining it. [Col. 0913B] Likewise, two castles and the island called Collese, with chapels, villages, and all things pertaining to it. In the city of Fano, the church of St Apollinaris with all things belonging to it. In the county of Senigallia, the church of St Mary in Scot, with its appurtenances. Whatever else you possess in the counties of Fermo, Pesaro, Rimini, Ravenna, Faenza, Cornelium, Populium, Liviense, Sarsina, Montefeltro, and Gubbio, with their goods and possessions. [lacuna] As has been decreed by our predecessors, the Roman pontiffs, and confirmed by their writings, you shall pay yearly to us and our successors one gold solidus as census.
